hirado_castle.highlight_en: Land of Nanban trade and Xavier's missionary work. The symbol of Hirado Island, where the sea, church, and castle coexist
hirado_castle.text_en: Hirado Castle is located on Hirado Island, Nagasaki Prefecture, and is a sea castle that was the residence of the Matsuura clan, the lord of the Hirado domain, during the Edo period. Hirado once prospered as a base for trade with Portugal, the Netherlands, and England, and Francisco Xavier visited there in 1550 to carry out missionary activities. Hirado was the center of trade with Europe until the Dutch trading post was moved to Dejima in 1641 after the Shimabara Rebellion. The castle was completed in 1718, and the unique view of the church between the sea and the castle is known as a landscape unique to Hirado. The current castle tower was restored in 1962, but the stone walls and moat remain as they were back then, and the view overlooking the port is spectacular.

hirado_xavier_church.name: 平戸ザビエル記念教会
hirado_xavier_church.kana: ひらどざびえるきねんきょうかい
hirado_xavier_church.text: 平戸ザビエル記念教会は、フランシスコ・ザビエルが1550年に平戸を訪れて布教したことを記念して建てられた聖公会の教会です。現在の建物は1931年に建てられたゴシック様式の聖堂で、平戸城を背景に市街地の高台に建つ姿は平戸を代表する景観のひとつです。ザビエルは平戸での布教で多くの信者を獲得し、平戸は九州のキリスト教布教の重要拠点となりました。平戸の信者たちはその後の弾圧期にも信仰を守り続け、「隠れキリシタン」の伝統が明治まで続きました。教会の近くにある「ザビエル記念碑」とともに、日本へのキリスト教伝来の歴史を今に伝えています。
hirado_xavier_church.highlight: ザビエルが1550年に布教した地に建つゴシック教会。平戸城との共演が絶景
hirado_xavier_church.highlight_en: A Gothic church built on the site of Xavier's missionary mission in 1550. Spectacular view with Hirado Castle
hirado_xavier_church.text_en: Hirado Xavier Memorial Church is an Anglican church built to commemorate Francis Xavier's missionary visit to Hirado in 1550. The current building is a Gothic-style cathedral built in 1931, and its appearance on a hill above the city with Hirado Castle in the background is one of the most representative views of Hirado. Xavier gained many followers through his missionary work in Hirado, and Hirado became an important base for Christian missionary work in Kyushu. The believers in Hirado continued to maintain their faith even during the subsequent period of oppression, and the tradition of ``hidden Christians'' continued until the Meiji period. Along with the "Xavier Monument" near the church, it tells the story of the introduction of Christianity to Japan.

goto_dozan_church.name: 堂崎天主堂
goto_dozan_church.kana: どうざきてんしゅどう
goto_dozan_church.text: 堂崎天主堂は五島列島・福江島に1908年に完成したレンガ造りのゴシック様式教会で、五島列島最古の教会建築のひとつです。五島列島には江戸時代に長崎の潜伏キリシタンが移住し、弾圧下でも信仰を守り続けた「五島キリシタン」の歴史があります。明治政府の禁教令が解除された後、フランス人宣教師ペルー神父らの尽力でこの地に教会が建てられました。堂内はキリシタン弾圧の歴史を伝える資料館となっており、迫害を受けながらも信仰を守った人々の遺物や証言が展示されています。五島列島の教会群は「長崎と天草地方の潜伏キリシタン関連遺産」としてユネスコ世界遺産に登録されています。
goto_dozan_church.highlight: 五島最古のレンガ教会。200年以上の弾圧に耐えた潜伏キリシタンの信仰の証
goto_dozan_church.highlight_en: The oldest brick church in Goto. Evidence of the faith of Hidden Christians who withstood over 200 years of oppression
goto_dozan_church.text_en: Dozaki Cathedral is a brick Gothic style church completed in 1908 on Fukue Island in the Goto Islands, and is one of the oldest church buildings in the Goto Islands. Hidden Christians from Nagasaki immigrated to the Goto Islands during the Edo period, and there is a history of ``Goto Christians'' who continued to protect their faith even under oppression. After the Meiji government's ban on Christianity was lifted, a church was built in this area through the efforts of French missionary Father Peru. The inside of the hall is a museum that tells the history of the oppression of Christians, displaying relics and testimonies of people who kept their faith despite persecution. The churches of the Goto Islands are registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site as "Hidden Christian Sites in the Nagasaki and Amakusa Region."

kashiragashima_church.name: 頭ケ島天主堂
kashiragashima_church.kana: かしらがしまてんしゅどう
kashiragashima_church.text: 頭ケ島天主堂は五島列島の上五島・頭ケ島に1919年に完成した石造りの教会で、信者自らが近くの砂岩を切り出して建てた珍しい石造建築です。島の人口のほぼ全員がカトリック信者であるこの小さな島に、長い時間をかけて手作りされた天主堂は、潜伏キリシタンの子孫たちの篤い信仰心を物語っています。ユネスコ世界遺産「長崎と天草地方の潜伏キリシタン関連遺産」の構成資産のひとつで、国の重要文化財にも指定されています。周囲を緑豊かな自然に囲まれた石造りの白い教会は、五島の教会群の中でも特に美しいとされており、遠方からも多くの巡礼者や観光客が訪れます。
kashiragashima_church.highlight: 島民全員カトリック信者の島に立つ石造教会。世界遺産・信者自らが石を切り出して建設
kashiragashima_church.highlight_en: A stone church standing on an island where all the islanders are Catholic. World Heritage Site: Constructed by believers themselves by cutting stones
kashiragashima_church.text_en: Togashima Cathedral is a stone church completed in 1919 on Kamigoto and Togashima in the Goto Islands, and is a rare stone structure built by the believers themselves by cutting out nearby sandstone. On this small island, where almost all of the island's population is Catholic, the cathedral, which was hand-built over a long period of time, testifies to the deep faith of the descendants of the Hidden Christians. It is one of the constituent assets of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Hidden Christian Sites in the Nagasaki and Amakusa Region" and has been designated as an important national cultural property. The white stone church, surrounded by lush nature, is said to be one of the most beautiful churches in Goto, and is visited by many pilgrims and tourists from far and wide.

tsushima_kaneda_castle.name: 金田城跡
tsushima_kaneda_castle.text: 金田城（かなたのき）は対馬の南部、城山（きやま）に築かれた古代山城で、663年の「白村江の戦い」で唐・新羅連合軍に敗れた後、大和朝廷が西日本防衛のために築いた朝鮮式山城のひとつです。朝鮮半島の技術者が建設に関わったとされ、急峻な山の地形を活かして石塁が巡らされています。対馬は古代から朝鮮半島との交流の窓口であり、元寇（文永・弘安の役）の際には最初に元軍の攻撃を受けた地でもあります。城跡からは対馬海峡を一望でき、古代の人々が朝鮮半島の動向を監視した様子が想像されます。国の特別史跡に指定されており、石塁が山の稜線に沿って残る景観は圧倒的です。
tsushima_kaneda_castle.highlight: 白村江の戦い後に築かれた古代朝鮮式山城。日本防衛の最前線・対馬の国特別史跡
tsushima_kaneda_castle.highlight_en: An ancient Korean-style mountain fortress built after the Battle of Hakuchogang. The front line of Japan's defense, Tsushima National Special Historic Site
tsushima_kaneda_castle.text_en: Kanata Castle is an ancient mountain castle built on Mt. Kiyama in the southern part of Tsushima. It is one of the Korean-style mountain castles built by the Yamato court to defend western Japan after it was defeated by the Tang and Silla allied forces at the Battle of Hakusonko in 663. Engineers from the Korean peninsula are said to have been involved in its construction, and the stone forts are built to take advantage of the steep mountain topography. Tsushima has been a gateway for exchange with the Korean Peninsula since ancient times, and was also the first area attacked by the Yuan army during the Mongol Invasion (Bun'ei-Koan War). The castle ruins offer a panoramic view of the Tsushima Strait, and you can imagine how people in ancient times monitored developments on the Korean Peninsula. It has been designated as a special historic site of the country, and the sight of the stone walls remaining along the ridgeline of the mountain is overwhelming.

izuhara_banshoin.name: 万松院
izuhara_banshoin.text: 万松院は対馬藩主・宗（そう）氏の菩提寺として1615年に創建された曹洞宗の寺院で、厳原（いずはら）の城下町に位置します。宗氏は鎌倉時代以来、対馬の支配者として朝鮮王朝との外交・貿易を一手に取り仕切り、室町・江戸時代を通じて日朝関係の橋渡し役を担いました。境内には宗氏歴代藩主の廟所があり、高さ2.5メートルの石燈籠が100基以上並ぶ参道は「対馬三名跡」のひとつとされています。朝鮮通信使に関する資料も所蔵されており、日朝外交の歴史を伝える重要な史跡です。対馬が日本と朝鮮半島をつなぐ架け橋として果たした役割を今に伝えています。
izuhara_banshoin.highlight: 対馬藩主・宗氏の菩提寺。日朝外交を700年担った宗氏ゆかりの廟所に100基の石燈籠
izuhara_banshoin.highlight_en: The family temple of Souji, the lord of Tsushima. 100 stone lanterns at the mausoleum of the Mune clan, who were responsible for Japan-North Korea diplomacy for 700 years
izuhara_banshoin.text_en: Manshoin is a Soto sect temple built in 1615 as the family temple of the Sou clan, the lord of Tsushima, and is located in the castle town of Izuhara. As the ruler of Tsushima since the Kamakura period, the Sou family was in charge of diplomacy and trade with the Korean dynasty, and served as a bridge between Japan and North Korea throughout the Muromachi and Edo periods. There is a mausoleum for successive feudal lords of the Sou clan within the precincts, and the approach, lined with over 100 stone lanterns 2.5 meters high, is considered one of the ``Three Famous Sites of Tsushima.'' It also houses materials related to the Korean envoys, and is an important historical site that tells the history of Japan-Korea diplomacy. It still conveys the role that Tsushima played as a bridge connecting Japan and the Korean Peninsula.

nagasaki_bugyosho.name: 長崎歴史文化博物館（旧長崎奉行所）
nagasaki_bugyosho.kana: ながさきれきしぶんかはくぶつかん
nagasaki_bugyosho.text: 長崎歴史文化博物館は、旧長崎奉行所西役所跡に建てられた長崎の歴史と文化を総合的に展示する博物館です。長崎奉行所は江戸幕府が出島の管理・外国貿易の監督・キリシタン取り締まりを行う目的で設置した直轄機関で、長崎の対外政策の中心を担いました。館内には約4万8千点の資料が収蔵されており、オランダ・中国・ポルトガルとの交易品や、出島に関する絵図、長崎奉行の記録文書など、長崎の国際都市としての歴史を示す資料が豊富に展示されています。復元された奉行所の建物では、江戸時代の役所の姿を体感することができます。長崎の歴史を学ぶうえで欠かせない拠点施設です。
nagasaki_bugyosho.highlight: 旧長崎奉行所跡の博物館。鎖国下で対外交易・キリシタン監視を担った江戸幕府の出先機関
nagasaki_bugyosho.name_en: Nagasaki Museum of History and Culture (formerly Nagasaki Magistrate's Office)
nagasaki_bugyosho.highlight_en: A museum on the site of the former Nagasaki Magistrate's Office. A branch office of the Edo Shogunate that was responsible for foreign trade and monitoring of Christians during the period of national isolation.
nagasaki_bugyosho.text_en: The Nagasaki Museum of History and Culture is a museum that comprehensively displays the history and culture of Nagasaki, built on the site of the former Nagasaki Magistrate's Office West Office. The Nagasaki Magistrate's Office was established by the Edo Shogunate to manage Dejima, supervise foreign trade, and crack down on Christians, and played a central role in Nagasaki's foreign policy. Approximately 48,000 items are stored in the museum, including trade goods with the Netherlands, China, and Portugal, pictures of Dejima, records of the Nagasaki magistrate, and a wealth of other materials showing Nagasaki's history as an international city. In the restored magistrate's office building, you can experience what a government office looked like in the Edo period. This is an indispensable base facility for learning about the history of Nagasaki.

matsuura_museum.name: 松浦史料博物館
matsuura_museum.kana: まつうらしりょうはくぶつかん
matsuura_museum.text: 松浦史料博物館は平戸藩主・松浦家が代々収集・所蔵してきた文化財を公開する博物館で、平戸城のすぐ隣に位置します。松浦氏は平安時代末期から平戸を拠点とした海洋豪族で、南北朝時代には倭寇の棟梁としても知られました。戦国時代以降は南蛮貿易の窓口として繁栄し、フランシスコ・ザビエルやオランダ・イギリスの商館を受け入れた平戸藩の歴史を伝える資料が充実しています。所蔵品には江戸時代の絵画・刀剣・南蛮貿易の関連資料・朝鮮通信使に関する文書などが含まれており、平戸と世界をつないだ国際交流の歴史を示しています。歴代藩主が住んだ鶴ヶ峯邸（旧藩主邸）も隣接しており、武家文化の雰囲気を体感できます。
matsuura_museum.highlight: 平戸藩主・松浦氏が収集した南蛮貿易・倭寇関連の至宝。海洋豪族700年の歴史
matsuura_museum.highlight_en: Treasures related to Nanban trade and Wakou, collected by the Matsuura clan, the lord of Hirado. 700 years of history of the maritime powers
matsuura_museum.text_en: The Matsuura Historical Materials Museum is a museum that displays cultural assets that have been collected and kept by the Matsuura family, the lords of the Hirado domain, for generations, and is located right next to Hirado Castle. The Matsuura clan was a powerful maritime clan that had been based in Hirado since the end of the Heian period, and was also known as the leader of the Japanese pirates during the Nanbokucho period. After the Sengoku period, the Hirado domain prospered as a gateway for trade between the South and the South, and there is a wealth of materials that tell the history of the Hirado domain, which hosted Francis Xavier and trading posts from the Netherlands and England. The collection includes paintings and swords from the Edo period, materials related to the Nanban trade, and documents related to Korean envoys, showing the history of international exchange that connected Hirado with the world. The Tsurugamine residence (former lord's residence), where successive feudal lords lived, is also adjacent, allowing you to experience the atmosphere of samurai culture.

dazaifu_tenmangu.name: 太宰府天満宮
dazaifu_tenmangu.kana: だざいふてんまんぐう

transit.name: 西鉄太宰府線「太宰府駅」

dazaifu_tenmangu.text: 太宰府天満宮は、学問・文化・芸術の神として崇敬される菅原道真公を祀る神社で、全国約12,000社の天満宮・天神社の総本社です。道真は894年に遣唐使廃止を建議した名臣ですが、藤原時平の策略により901年に大宰府に左遷され、翌々年に903年に当地で没しました。その後都では相次いで天変地異や貴族の急死が起こり、道真の怨霊によるものとして恐れられました。道真を神として祀ることで怨霊を鎮め、やがて学問の神として全国に信仰が広まりました。現在の社殿は1591年に小早川隆景が再建したもので、国の重要文化財です。境内の飛梅は道真が愛でた梅が都から飛んできたとの伝説を持ち、毎年早春に白い花を咲かせます。
dazaifu_tenmangu.highlight: 全国12,000社の総本社。左遷された菅原道真が没した地に立つ学問の神
dazaifu_tenmangu.highlight_en: Headquarters of 12,000 companies nationwide. The god of learning stands on the site where the demoted Michizane Sugawara died.
dazaifu_tenmangu.text_en: Dazaifu Tenmangu is a shrine dedicated to Sugawara no Michizane, who is revered as the god of learning, culture, and art, and is the headquarters of approximately 12,000 Tenmangu shrines and shrines nationwide. Michizane was a famous vassal who proposed the abolition of envoys to Tang China in 894, but due to Fujiwara Tokihira's strategy, he was demoted to Dazaifu in 901 and died there in 903, two years later. After that, a series of natural disasters and sudden deaths of nobles occurred in the capital, and these were feared as being caused by Michizane's vengeful ghost. By worshiping Michizane as a god, vengeful spirits were appeased, and soon his faith as the god of learning spread throughout the country. The current shrine building was rebuilt in 1591 by Takakage Kobayakawa and is an important cultural property of the country. The flying plum blossoms on the grounds have a legend that the plum blossoms that Michizane admired were flown from the capital, and the white flowers bloom in early spring every year.

dazaifu_ruins.name: 大宰府政庁跡
dazaifu_ruins.kana: だざいふせいちょうあと

transit.name: 西鉄太宰府線「太宰府駅」

dazaifu_ruins.text: 大宰府政庁跡は、奈良〜平安時代にかけて九州を統括した最高地方行政機関「大宰府」の中枢を担った役所の跡地です。大宰府は7世紀後半に設置され、外交・防衛・九州諸国の統治を担い、「遠の朝廷（とおのみかど）」とも称されました。外交使節の応接もここで行われ、唐・新羅・渤海などとの外交の窓口でもありました。政庁の建物は整然と配置された官衙建築群から成り、現在は礎石のみが草原に残っています。大伴旅人・山上憶良・菅原道真ら名だたる歌人・文人が大宰府に赴任し、多くの秀歌を詠んでいます。「令和」の元号の典拠となった万葉集の「梅花の歌」の序文は、旅人の邸宅での宴で詠まれた歌に基づいています。
dazaifu_ruins.highlight: 奈良・平安時代の九州の都「遠の朝廷」。令和の元号典拠・梅花の歌の舞台
dazaifu_ruins.highlight_en: The Tono Imperial Court was the capital of Kyushu during the Nara and Heian periods. The origin of the era name of Reiwa, the stage of the song of plum blossoms
dazaifu_ruins.text_en: The Dazaifu Government Office Site is the site of the government office that served as the center of Dazaifu, the highest local administrative body that supervised Kyushu from the Nara to Heian periods. Dazaifu was established in the latter half of the 7th century and was responsible for foreign affairs, defense, and governance of the Kyushu countries, and was also called the ``Toonomikado''. Diplomatic missions were also received here, and it was also the point of contact for diplomacy with countries such as Tang, Silla, and Balhae. The government building consists of a group of government buildings arranged in an orderly manner, and today only the foundation stones remain on the grassland. Famous poets and writers such as Otomo Tabito, Yamagami Okura, and Sugawara Michizane were assigned to Dazaifu and wrote many beautiful poems. The preface to the Manyoshu's ``Uta of Plum Blossoms,'' which served as the basis for the era name ``Reiwa,'' is based on a poem recited at a banquet at a traveler's residence.

mizuki_wall.name: 水城跡
mizuki_wall.text: 水城は663年の白村江の戦いで唐・新羅連合軍に敗れた後、大和朝廷が翌664年に築いた防衛施設です。博多湾からの外敵の侵攻を食い止めるため、北部九州の要衝に全長約1.2キロメートル、高さ約13メートルの土塁を築き、その前面に幅約60メートルの堀を設けました。当時の日本が直面した最大の脅威に対応するため、天智天皇が命じて急ピッチで建設されました。現代的に言えば「防衛線」の役割を果たしたわけです。1,350年以上経った現在も土塁の一部が良好な状態で残っており、国の特別史跡に指定されています。この水城と大野城・基肄城を組み合わせた古代防衛ラインは、当時の国家的危機感を今に伝えています。
mizuki_wall.highlight: 白村江敗戦翌年に築いた古代の防衛土塁。全長1.2kmが1,350年後の今も残る
mizuki_wall.highlight_en: An ancient defensive earthwork built in the year after the defeat of Shiramura. The total length of 1.2 km still remains 1,350 years later.
mizuki_wall.text_en: Mizuki is a defense facility built by the Yamato court in 664, the following year, after it was defeated by the Tang and Silla allied forces at the Battle of Hakusonko in 663. In order to stop the invasion of foreign enemies from Hakata Bay, an earthwork approximately 1.2 kilometers long and 13 meters high was built at a key strategic point in northern Kyushu, and a moat approximately 60 meters wide was placed in front of it. It was constructed at a rapid pace ordered by Emperor Tenji in response to the greatest threat facing Japan at the time. In modern terms, it served as a ``line of defense.'' More than 1,350 years later, some of the earthworks still remain in good condition and have been designated as a national special historic site. The ancient defense line that combined Mizuki, Ono Castle, and Motosuke Castle still conveys the sense of national crisis at the time.

fukuoka_castle.name: 福岡城跡

transit.name: 福岡市営地下鉄「大濠公園駅」

fukuoka_castle.text: 福岡城は関ヶ原の戦いで功績を挙げた黒田長政が1601年から7年をかけて築いた平山城で、筑前52万石の居城です。黒田長政の父・黒田孝高（官兵衛）が計画に深く関わったとされており、その知略が随所に活かされた堅固な縄張りが特徴です。城の規模は九州最大級で、47棟もの多聞櫓や天守台を備えていましたが、天守が実際に建てられたかどうかは現在も歴史家の間で議論が続いています。明治維新後に廃城となり、建物のほとんどが失われましたが、石垣は今も良好な状態で残っています。現在は舞鶴公園として整備され、隣接する大濠公園とともに福岡市民の憩いの場となっています。春の桜の名所としても人気です。
fukuoka_castle.highlight: 黒田長政・官兵衛父子が築いた九州最大級の城。47棟の多聞櫓と謎の天守
fukuoka_castle.highlight_en: One of the largest castles in Kyushu built by father and son Kuroda Nagamasa and Kanbei. 47 Tamon Yagura towers and mysterious castle towers
fukuoka_castle.text_en: Fukuoka Castle is a Hirayama castle built over seven years starting in 1601 by Kuroda Nagamasa, who achieved great success in the Battle of Sekigahara, and is the residence of Chikuzen's 520,000 koku. It is said that Nagamasa Kuroda's father, Yoshitaka Kuroda (Kanbei), was deeply involved in the planning, and his wisdom was put to good use in many areas, making for a solid territory. The castle was one of the largest in Kyushu, with 47 towers and a castle tower, but historians still debate whether or not the castle tower was actually built. After the Meiji Restoration, the castle was abandoned and most of the buildings were lost, but the stone walls are still in good condition. Currently, it is maintained as Maizuru Park, and along with the adjacent Ohori Park, it is a place of relaxation for Fukuoka citizens. It is also a popular spot for cherry blossom viewing in spring.

kushida_shrine.name: 櫛田神社

transit.name: 福岡市営地下鉄「祇園駅」

kushida_shrine.text: 櫛田神社は博多の総鎮守として古くから市民に「お櫛田さん」と親しまれている神社で、757年の創建と伝わります。全国的に有名な「博多祇園山笠」の起点として知られており、毎年7月に行われる山笠は770年以上の歴史を持つ博多の夏の風物詩です。クライマックスの「追い山」では、重さ約1トンの「舁き山笠（かきやま））」を男衆が担いで博多の街を疾走し、その速さを競います。境内には豪華絢爛な「飾り山笠」が常設展示されており、迫力ある博多の伝統文化を年中体感できます。また境内には「不老長寿の水」と呼ばれる霊水が湧いており、博多っ子の信仰を集めています。
kushida_shrine.highlight: 博多総鎮守。770年以上の歴史を持つ博多祇園山笠の起点
kushida_shrine.highlight_en: Hakata general guardian. The starting point of Hakata Gion Yamakasa, which has a history of over 770 years
kushida_shrine.text_en: Kushida Shrine is said to have been founded in 757 and has been affectionately known as ``Okushida-san'' by the citizens since ancient times as the general guardian of Hakata. It is known as the starting point of the nationally famous "Hakata Gion Yamakasa", and the Yamakasa festival, which is held every July, is a summer tradition in Hakata with a history of over 770 years. In the climax, ``Oiyama,'' men run through the streets of Hakata carrying ``Kakiyamakasa,'' which weigh approximately 1 ton, competing to see how fast they can run. Inside the precincts, gorgeous ``Kazari Yamakasa'' are permanently displayed, allowing you to experience the powerful traditional culture of Hakata all year round. In addition, a sacred water called ``Water of Eternal Youth and Longevity'' gushes within the shrine grounds, and it is worshiped by Hakata residents.

shofukuji_hakata.name: 聖福寺

transit.name: 福岡市営地下鉄「祇園駅」

shofukuji_hakata.text: 聖福寺は1195年に栄西（えいさい）禅師が創建した日本最古の禅寺です。栄西は二度にわたって宋に渡り、臨済宗の禅を日本に伝えるとともに、茶の種を持ち帰って日本の喫茶文化の基盤を作った人物でもあります。後鳥羽上皇から「扶桑最初禅窟（ふそうさいしょのぜんくつ）」という称号を賜った、日本禅宗の発祥地です。境内は鎌倉時代の伽藍配置を保ちながら静かな佇まいを見せており、木々に囲まれた境内は都市の中の別世界のような空間です。現在の建物は江戸時代以降に再建されたものですが、境内全体が国の史跡に指定されています。博多の豊かな禅文化と茶文化の原点がここにあります。
shofukuji_hakata.highlight: 1195年創建・日本最古の禅寺。茶を日本に伝えた栄西が開いた「日本禅宗の発祥地」
shofukuji_hakata.highlight_en: Founded in 1195, Japan's oldest Zen temple. ``The birthplace of Japanese Zen Buddhism'' opened by Eisai, who introduced tea to Japan.
shofukuji_hakata.text_en: Shofukuji is Japan's oldest Zen temple, founded in 1195 by Zen Master Eisai. Eisai traveled to the Sung Dynasty twice and brought the Zen of the Rinzai sect to Japan, as well as bringing back tea seeds and creating the foundation of Japan's cafe culture. It is the birthplace of Japanese Zen Buddhism, and was given the title of ``Fuso's First Zen Cave'' by the retired Emperor Go-Toba. The precincts maintain the layout of a temple from the Kamakura period, but have a quiet appearance, and the precincts surrounded by trees are like a space in another world within the city. The current building was rebuilt after the Edo period, but the entire precinct is designated as a national historic site. This is the origin of Hakata's rich Zen culture and tea culture.

tochoji_hakata.name: 東長寺

transit.name: 福岡市営地下鉄「祇園駅」

tochoji_hakata.text: 東長寺は806年に弘法大師・空海が唐から帰国後に最初に創建したとされる真言宗の寺院で、日本最初の密教寺院として知られています。空海は唐での修行を終えて九州に戻った際、博多に立ち寄りこの地で護摩供養を行い寺を創建したと伝わります。境内にある「福岡大仏」は高さ10.8メートルで、木造坐像としては日本最大級を誇ります。1992年に完成したこの大仏の内部は「地獄・極楽めぐり」として公開されており、暗闇の中を歩きながら仏教の世界観を体感できます。また境内には六角形の「六角堂」があり、その中には福岡藩主・黒田家の墓所があります。博多の歴史的な寺町エリアの中心的な存在です。
tochoji_hakata.highlight: 空海が806年に創建・日本最初の密教寺院。日本最大級の木造大仏が境内に
tochoji_hakata.highlight_en: Founded by Kukai in 806, Japan's first esoteric Buddhist temple. Japan's largest wooden Buddha statue is on the grounds
tochoji_hakata.text_en: Tochoji Temple is said to have been the first temple of the Shingon sect built by Kobo Daishi Kukai after his return from the Tang Dynasty in 806, and is known as Japan's first esoteric Buddhist temple. It is said that when Kukai returned to Kyushu after completing his training in the Tang Dynasty, he stopped by Hakata, held a Goma memorial service, and founded a temple here. The Fukuoka Great Buddha, located within the temple grounds, is 10.8 meters high and is one of the largest wooden seated statues in Japan. The interior of this Great Buddha, completed in 1992, is open to the public as part of the ``Hell and Paradise Tour,'' where you can experience the worldview of Buddhism while walking through the darkness. There is also a hexagonal ``Rokkaku-do'' within the precincts, which contains the graves of the Kuroda family, the lords of Fukuoka. It is the center of Hakata's historic temple town area.

genko_boruei.name: 元寇防塁跡
genko_boruei.kana: げんこうぼうるいあと
genko_boruei.text: 元寇防塁は1281年の弘安の役に備えて、鎌倉幕府が博多湾沿岸に築いた石積みの防塁です。1274年の文永の役で元・高麗連合軍の集団戦法と火薬兵器「てつはう」に苦しんだ幕府は、博多湾岸約20キロメートルにわたって高さ2〜3メートルの石塁を構築しました。弘安の役では14万の大軍が来襲しましたが、防塁によって上陸を阻まれ、さらに暴風雨（神風）によって元軍は壊滅しました。この防塁は九州の御家人たちが動員されて短期間で建設した土木工事の偉業でもあります。今津や生の松原など数か所に石塁が現存しており、国の史跡に指定されています。「神風」の伝説を生んだ元寇の歴史的現場です。
genko_boruei.highlight: 14万の元軍を食い止めた石の防衛線。「神風」伝説を生んだ元寇の現場
genko_boruei.highlight_en: A stone defense line that stopped the 140,000 Yuan army. The site of the Mongol invasion that gave birth to the “kamikaze” legend
genko_boruei.text_en: The Mongol Invasion Fort was a stone wall built by the Kamakura Shogunate on the coast of Hakata Bay in preparation for the Battle of Koan in 1281. During the Bun'ei War in 1274, the shogunate, which suffered from the mass tactics and gunpowder weapons of the former Goryeo allied forces, constructed stone forts 2 to 3 meters high along a 20-kilometer stretch of Hakata Bay. During the Battle of Koan, a large army of 140,000 troops attacked, but they were prevented from landing by fortifications, and the Yuan army was annihilated by a rainstorm (kamikaze). This fortification is also a feat of civil engineering work, constructed in a short period of time by the vassals of Kyushu. Stone embankments still exist in several places, including Imazu and Nama Matsubara, and are designated as national historic sites. This is the historical site of the Mongol invasion, which gave rise to the legend of "kamikaze."

shikano_island.name: 志賀島（金印発見地）
shikano_island.text: 志賀島は博多湾に浮かぶ島（実際には砂州で陸続き）で、1784年に甚兵衛という農民が水田の溝から発見した「漢委奴国王印」の金印で世界的に有名です。この金印は中国の歴史書「後漢書」に記された、西暦57年に後漢の光武帝が倭の奴国王に与えた印綬と同一のものと考えられており、日本と中国の外交関係を示す最古の物証のひとつです。純金製で一辺2.3センチメートルのこの小さな印は現在、福岡市博物館に所蔵されており、国宝に指定されています。島内には「漢委奴国王金印発見之処」の碑が建てられています。島の周囲は玄界灘の荒波が打ち寄せる絶景で、万葉集にも詠まれた歴史ある地です。
shikano_island.highlight: 西暦57年の国宝・金印の発見地。中国皇帝から倭の王への外交の証が眠っていた島
shikano_island.name_en: Shika Island (place where the gold seal was discovered)
shikano_island.highlight_en: The place where the national treasure, the gold seal, was discovered in 57 AD. The island where the proof of diplomacy from the Emperor of China to the King of Wa was buried
shikano_island.text_en: Shikajima is an island floating in Hakata Bay (actually connected to the land by a sandbar), and is world-famous for the gold seal of the ``Kan-Kai Koku-in'' that was discovered in a ditch in a rice field by a farmer named Jinbe in 1784. This gold seal is thought to be the same as the seal given by Emperor Guangwu of Later Han to King Na of Wa in 57 AD, as recorded in the Chinese history book ``Book of Later Han,'' and is one of the oldest physical evidences of diplomatic relations between Japan and China. This small seal, made of pure gold and measuring 2.3 centimeters on each side, is currently housed in the Fukuoka City Museum and has been designated as a national treasure. A monument has been erected on the island that says ``The place where the golden seal was discovered by the King of the Han Dynasty.'' The island is surrounded by a spectacular view of the rough waves of the Genkai Sea, and is a historical place that was even mentioned in the Manyoshu.

munakata_taisha.name: 宗像大社
munakata_taisha.text: 宗像大社は宗像三女神（田心姫神・湍津姫神・市杵島姫神）を祀る神社で、沖ノ島の沖津宮・大島の中津宮・田島の辺津宮の三宮から成ります。古代から「海の道」の守り神として、大陸との外交・交易を行う船人たちの信仰を集めてきました。沖ノ島は「海の正倉院」とも呼ばれ、4世紀から9世紀にかけて大陸との交流で奉納された金銅製の馬具・ガラス器・銅鏡など約8万点が発見されており、その全てが国宝に指定されています。島全体が御神体とされ、今も女人禁制・持ち出し禁止が守られています。2017年に「『神宿る島』宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群」としてユネスコ世界遺産に登録されました。
munakata_taisha.highlight: 世界遺産「神宿る島」沖ノ島。8万点すべて国宝・女人禁制が今も続く海の正倉院
munakata_taisha.highlight_en: Okinoshima, a world heritage site where the gods dwell. All 80,000 items are national treasures; Shosoin by the Sea is still prohibited to women.
munakata_taisha.text_en: Munakata Taisha is a shrine that enshrines the three goddesses of Munakata (Tashin Himekami, Taketsu Himekami, and Ichikishima Himekami), and consists of three shrines: Okitsu Shrine on Okinoshima, Nakatsu Shrine on Oshima, and Hetsu Shrine on Tajima. Since ancient times, it has been worshiped by sailors who conduct diplomacy and trade with the continent as a guardian deity of the ``sea roads''. Okinoshima is also known as the ``Shosoin of the Sea,'' and about 80,000 items have been discovered, including gilt bronze harnesses, glassware, and bronze mirrors, which were dedicated during exchanges with the mainland from the 4th to the 9th century, all of which have been designated as national treasures. The entire island is considered a sacred object, and to this day, women are not allowed to enter or take it out. In 2017, it was registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site as ``Munakata/Okinoshima Island, the island where the gods dwell, and related heritage sites.''

akizuki_castle.name: 秋月城跡
akizuki_castle.text: 秋月は福岡県朝倉市に位置し、「九州の小京都」と称される美しい城下町です。中世には秋月氏が支配し、江戸時代には福岡藩から分かれた秋月藩（2万5千石）の陣屋町として栄えました。城跡には大手門の「黒門」と長屋門が現存しており、石垣と石畳の旧城下町の通りが往時の雰囲気を保っています。特に春の桜の季節には、黒門と桜のコントラストが絶景を生み出し「日本さくら名所100選」に選ばれています。1876年には西南戦争に呼応して「秋月の乱」が起き、秋月藩の旧士族が反乱を起こしましたが、翌日には鎮圧されました。乱を起こした旧士族の処刑地「野鳥の森」も歴史の証人として残っています。
akizuki_castle.highlight: 九州の小京都。黒門と桜の絶景で知られ、西南戦争では「秋月の乱」の舞台に
akizuki_castle.highlight_en: Little Kyoto in Kyushu. Known for its Kuromon gate and spectacular view of cherry blossoms, it was the scene of the Akizuki Rebellion during the Seinan Rebellion.
akizuki_castle.text_en: Akizuki is located in Asakura City, Fukuoka Prefecture, and is a beautiful castle town known as the "Little Kyoto of Kyushu." In the Middle Ages, it was ruled by the Akizuki clan, and during the Edo period it flourished as the Jinyacho of the Akizuki clan (25,000 koku), which was separated from the Fukuoka clan. At the castle ruins, the Otemon (Kuromon) and Nagayamon (Otemon) still exist, and the stone walls and cobblestone streets of the old castle town retain the atmosphere of yesteryear. Especially during the spring cherry blossom season, the contrast between Kuromon and the cherry blossoms creates a spectacular view, and it has been selected as one of Japan's top 100 cherry blossom viewing spots. In 1876, the Akizuki Rebellion broke out in response to the Seinan Rebellion, in which the former samurai clan of the Akizuki clan rebelled, but it was suppressed the next day. The Wild Bird Forest, the execution site for the former samurai who caused the rebellion, also remains as a witness to history.

yanagawa.name: 柳川城下町
yanagawa.kana: やながわじょうかまち

transit.name: 西鉄天神大牟田線「西鉄柳川駅」

yanagawa.text: 柳川は福岡県南部に位置する水郷の城下町で、縦横に走る掘割（どぼり）を川下りするどんこ舟が名物です。戦国時代には蒲池氏・田中氏が支配し、関ヶ原の戦いで西軍として戦いながら最後に東軍に寝返り所領を守った立花宗茂が藩主となりました。宗茂は江戸時代を通じて柳川藩を統治し、今も市民から慕われています。掘割は城の防衛施設として造られたものが今も生活用水路として機能しており、江戸時代の水利システムが現代に生きています。詩人・北原白秋の出身地でもあり、「からたちの花」など多くの名詩がこの水郷の風景から生まれました。城跡・御花（旧立花家別邸）・白秋記念館が柳川の歴史と文化を伝えています。
yanagawa.highlight: 掘割に囲まれた水郷の城下町。立花宗茂が治め、北原白秋が詩作した情緒ある町
yanagawa.highlight_en: A castle town in Suigo surrounded by moat. An atmospheric town ruled by Muneshige Tachibana and where Hakushu Kitahara wrote poetry.
yanagawa.text_en: Yanagawa is a water village castle town located in the southern part of Fukuoka Prefecture, and is famous for its donko-bune (donko-bune) boats that travel down the river through dobori (dobori) that run vertically and horizontally. During the Sengoku period, it was ruled by the Kamachi and Tanaka clans, and Muneshige Tachibana, who fought for the western army during the Battle of Sekigahara, but defected to the eastern army to protect his territory, became the lord of the domain. Muneshige ruled the Yanagawa domain throughout the Edo period and is still admired by the citizens. The moat was built as a defense facility for the castle, but it still functions as a waterway for daily life, and the water use system of the Edo period is still alive today. It is also the birthplace of the poet Hakushu Kitahara, and many famous poems such as ``Karatachi no Hana'' were born from the scenery of this water village. The castle ruins, Ohana (former Tachibana family villa), and Hakushu Memorial Hall convey the history and culture of Yanagawa.

kokura_castle.name: 小倉城
kokura_castle.text: 小倉城は1602年に細川忠興が築いた平城で、天守は大入母屋破風の「唐造り」と呼ばれる特殊な建築様式が特徴で、最上階が4層目より広くなっています。細川氏の後は小笠原氏が15万石の城主となり、明治維新まで小倉藩の中心として機能しました。1837年に隣接する火事が飛び火して天守が焼失し、以降再建されないまま廃城を迎えましたが、1959年に復元されました。宮本武蔵と佐々木小次郎が巌流島で決闘した際（1612年）、武蔵は小倉城下に向かう途中だったとも伝わります。城の東側には松本清張記念館があり、北九州出身の社会派作家・松本清張の業績を伝えています。
kokura_castle.highlight: 唐造りの特殊天守・細川忠興が築く。巌流島決闘にも縁があり、松本清張の故郷
kokura_castle.highlight_en: A special Kara-zukuri castle tower built by Tadaoki Hosokawa. It is also connected to the Ganryujima Duel and is the hometown of Seicho Matsumoto.
kokura_castle.text_en: Kokura Castle is a flat castle built by Tadaoki Hosokawa in 1602, and the castle tower is characterized by a special architectural style called ``Karazukuri'' with large gables, and the top floor is wider than the fourth floor. After the Hosokawa clan, the Ogasawara clan became the lord of the castle with a 150,000 koku (koku), and it functioned as the center of the Kokura domain until the Meiji Restoration. In 1837, the castle tower was destroyed by a fire that spread adjacent to the castle, and the castle was abandoned without being rebuilt, but it was restored in 1959. It is said that Musashi was on his way to Kokura Castle when Miyamoto Musashi and Sasaki Kojiro dueled on Ganryujima in 1612. On the east side of the castle is the Matsumoto Seicho Memorial Hall, which tells the story of the achievements of Matsumoto Seicho, a socialist writer from Kitakyushu.

yahata_seitetsu.name: 官営八幡製鐵所
yahata_seitetsu.kana: かんえいやはたせいてつしょ

transit.name: JR鹿児島本線「スペースワールド駅」

yahata_seitetsu.text: 官営八幡製鐵所は1901年に操業を開始した日本初の本格的な近代製鉄所で、日本の産業革命を象徴する施設です。清国（現中国）からの賠償金を元手に建設され、ドイツ・クルップ社の技術を導入して設立されました。当初は技術的な困難から操業が難航しましたが、改良を重ねて軌道に乗り、日露戦争の鉄砲・艦船用の鉄鋼を供給するなど、日本の近代化・軍事力強化に決定的な役割を果たしました。製鐵所の発展に伴い労働者が集まって北九州工業地帯が形成され、「近代日本の産業の礎」として機能しました。旧本事務所・修繕工場などが現存しており、2015年に「明治日本の産業革命遺産」としてユネスコ世界遺産に登録されました。
yahata_seitetsu.highlight: 1901年操業・日本初の近代製鉄所。日本産業革命の象徴・ユネスコ世界遺産
yahata_seitetsu.highlight_en: Started operation in 1901, Japan's first modern steelworks. A symbol of the Japanese Industrial Revolution and a UNESCO World Heritage Site
yahata_seitetsu.text_en: The government-run Yawata Steel Works is Japan's first full-scale modern steelworks, which began operations in 1901, and is a symbol of Japan's industrial revolution. It was built using reparations from the Qing Dynasty (present-day China) and was established using technology from Germany's Krupp Company. Initially, operations were difficult due to technical difficulties, but after repeated improvements, the plant got back on track and played a decisive role in modernizing Japan and strengthening its military power, supplying steel for guns and ships used in the Russo-Japanese War. With the development of the steel works, workers gathered together to form the Kitakyushu Industrial Zone, which functioned as the "foundation of modern Japanese industry." The former main office and repair factory still exist, and in 2015 it was registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site as a "Site of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution."

itoshima_ito_koku.name: 伊都国歴史博物館
itoshima_ito_koku.kana: いとこくれきしはくぶつかん
itoshima_ito_koku.text: 糸島市に位置する伊都国歴史博物館は、弥生時代に栄えた強国「伊都国」の歴史と出土品を展示する博物館です。伊都国は中国の歴史書「魏志倭人伝」に「一大率（いちだいそつ）」が置かれた重要な拠点として記され、邪馬台国への道筋の要所とされています。糸島市内には多くの弥生時代の王墓が発掘されており、中でも「三雲南小路遺跡」や「井原鑓溝遺跡」からは、中国皇帝から贈られた前漢鏡・金銅製品・ガラス製品など極めて豪華な副葬品が出土しています。これらの出土品は当時の伊都国王が中国と直接外交を行っていたことを示しており、弥生時代の日本と東アジアとの交流を考えるうえで第一級の資料です。
itoshima_ito_koku.highlight: 魏志倭人伝に記された伊都国の王墓。中国皇帝から贈られた前漢鏡が眠る弥生の王都
itoshima_ito_koku.highlight_en: The royal tomb of Ito Province, which is described in the history of Wajin. The royal capital of Yayoi where the former Han mirror, a gift from the Chinese emperor, rests.
itoshima_ito_koku.text_en: The Ito Province Museum of History, located in Itoshima City, is a museum that displays the history and excavated artifacts of Ito Province, a powerful nation that flourished during the Yayoi period. Ito Province is described in the Chinese history book ``Gishi Wajinden'' as an important base with ``Ichidaisotsu,'' and is considered to be a key point on the route to Yamataikoku. Many royal tombs from the Yayoi period have been excavated in Itoshima City, and among them, the Mikumo Minamikoji Ruins and the Ibara Yarigou Ruins have unearthed extremely luxurious burial goods such as mirrors from the Former Han Dynasty, gilt bronze products, and glass products that were gifts from Chinese emperors. These excavated items show that the King of Ito at the time was engaged in direct diplomacy with China, and are first-class materials when considering exchanges between Japan and East Asia during the Yayoi period.

ono_castle.name: 大野城跡

transit.name: 西鉄天神大牟田線「都府楼前駅」

ono_castle.text: 大野城は663年の白村江の戦い敗北後、大和朝廷が朝鮮半島の技術者（百済の役人）を招いて664年に築いた古代山城です。四王寺山（標高410メートル）の山頂に石垣と土塁を巡らせた広大な城郭で、大宰府政庁の背後を守る防衛拠点として機能しました。百済から亡命してきた技術者が建設に携わったとされる「朝鮮式山城」で、対馬の金田城・壱岐の城跡と並ぶ古代防衛ラインの要です。山中には礎石が残る政庁跡・倉庫群跡が多数確認されており、城の規模の大きさを物語っています。国の特別史跡に指定されており、現在は市民の登山・ハイキングの場としても親しまれています。
ono_castle.highlight: 白村江敗戦後に百済技術者が築いた古代山城。大宰府を背後から守る飛鳥時代の要塞
ono_castle.highlight_en: An ancient mountain fortress built by Baekje engineers after the defeat of Hakuchogang. A fortress from the Asuka period that protected Dazaifu from behind.
ono_castle.text_en: Ono Castle is an ancient mountain castle built in 664 by the Yamato court, which invited engineers from the Korean peninsula (Baekje officials) after the defeat at the Battle of Hakusonko in 663. It is a vast castle surrounded by stone walls and earthworks on the summit of Mt. Shioji (410 meters above sea level), and functioned as a defensive base to protect the rear of the Dazaifu Government Office. This ``Korean-style mountain castle'' is said to have been constructed by engineers who defected from Baekje, and is a key part of the ancient defense line along with Kaneda Castle in Tsushima and the castle ruins in Iki. Many ruins of government buildings and warehouses with their foundation stones have been found in the mountains, testifying to the scale of the castle. It has been designated as a national special historic site, and is now a popular mountain climbing and hiking spot for local residents.

fukuoka_museum.name: 福岡市博物館（金印）
fukuoka_museum.kana: ふくおかしはくぶつかん

transit.name: 福岡市営地下鉄「西新駅」

fukuoka_museum.text: 福岡市博物館は、国宝「漢委奴国王印」（金印）の常設展示で知られる博物館です。1784年に志賀島で発見されたこの金印は、中国の歴史書「後漢書」に記された西暦57年に後漢の光武帝が倭の奴国王に賜ったものと同一視されており、日本と中国の外交関係を示す最古の遺物のひとつです。純金製で重さ約108グラム、一辺2.3センチメートルの小さな印ですが、その歴史的重要性は計り知れません。博物館内では金印のほか、博多の歴史・南蛮貿易・元寇に関する資料も充実しており、福岡の歴史を俯瞰して学べます。館内は無料で入れる常設展示エリアもあり、地域の歴史文化の拠点として機能しています。
fukuoka_museum.highlight: 西暦57年・国宝「漢委奴国王印」を常設展示。日中外交最古の証・金印をここで見られる
fukuoka_museum.highlight_en: A.D. 57, the national treasure "Kan-Kan-no-King Seal" is on permanent display. You can see the gold seal, the oldest proof of Sino-Japanese diplomacy, here.
fukuoka_museum.text_en: Fukuoka City Museum is a museum known for its permanent exhibition of the National Treasure, ``Kan-Kyoku King Seal'' (Golden Seal). This gold seal, discovered on Shika Island in 1784, is thought to be the same as the one given by Emperor Guangwu of the Later Han Dynasty to King Yao of Wa in 57 AD, as recorded in the Chinese history book ``Book of the Later Hans.'' It is one of the oldest artifacts showing diplomatic relations between Japan and China. Although it is a small mark made of pure gold, weighing approximately 108 grams and measuring 2.3 centimeters on each side, its historical importance is immeasurable. In addition to the gold seal, the museum also has a wealth of materials related to Hakata's history, Nanban trade, and Mongol invasions, allowing you to learn about Fukuoka's history from a bird's-eye view. The museum also has a permanent exhibition area that can be entered free of charge, and functions as a base for local history and culture.

nanzoin.name: 南蔵院

transit.name: JR篠栗線「城戸南蔵院前駅」

nanzoin.text: 南蔵院は福岡県篠栗町にある真言宗の寺院で、四国八十八か所霊場を模した「篠栗四国八十八か所霊場」の総本寺です。境内に安置されている「釈迦涅槃像」は全長41メートル・高さ11メートル・重さ約300トンで、ブロンズ（青銅）製の涅槃像としては世界最大です。1995年に建立されたこの巨大涅槃像は、ミャンマー・タイ・スリランカの仏教国から仏舎利（仏陀の遺骨）が贈られたことを縁に造立されました。像内には仏舎利が安置されており、参拝者は胎内を参拝することができます。住職がジャンボ宝くじで1等・前後賞を同時に当選したというエピソードでも知られ、「金運の寺」として多くの参拝者が訪れます。
nanzoin.highlight: 世界最大のブロンズ涅槃像（全長41m）。仏舎利を安置する篠栗四国の総本寺
nanzoin.highlight_en: The world's largest bronze reclining statue (41m long). The main temple of Sasaguri Shikoku where the Buddha's ashes are enshrined
nanzoin.text_en: Nanzoin is a Shingon sect temple located in Sasaguri Town, Fukuoka Prefecture, and is the main temple of the ``Sasaguri Shikoku 88 Sacred Sites'', which are modeled after the 88 Sacred Sites of Shikoku. The ``Shakya Nirvana Statue'' enshrined within the shrine grounds is 41 meters long, 11 meters high, and weighs approximately 300 tons, making it the world's largest bronze reclining statue. This gigantic reclining statue was erected in 1995 after receiving Buddha's ashes from the Buddhist countries of Myanmar, Thailand, and Sri Lanka. Buddha's ashes are enshrined inside the statue, and worshipers can worship inside the statue. It is also known for the story of the chief priest winning the first and second prizes at the same time in the Jumbo Lottery, and many people visit the temple as a ``temple of financial fortune.''

jotenji_hakata.name: 承天寺

transit.name: 福岡市営地下鉄「祇園駅」

jotenji_hakata.text: 承天寺は1241年に聖一国師（円爾）が宋から帰国後に創建した臨済宗の寺院です。円爾は宋での修行中に製粉・製麺技術を学んで持ち帰り、博多にうどん・そば・饅頭などの製法を伝えたとされており、境内には「饂飩蕎麦発祥之地」「饅頭発祥の碑」が建てられています。また円爾は博多の商人と協力して博多の大洪水に備えた「博多堀川」の掘削を進言するなど、都市整備にも貢献しました。境内の庭園「洗濤庭」は石組みと白砂によるシンプルな枯山水庭園で、鎌倉時代の美意識を今に伝えています。博多が宋との貿易を通じて日本の食文化・精神文化の革新に果たした役割を体感できる場所です。
jotenji_hakata.highlight: うどん・そば・饅頭の発祥地。宋から製麺技術を伝えた円爾が1241年に創建
jotenji_hakata.highlight_en: The birthplace of udon, soba, and manju. Founded in 1241 by En'er, who brought noodle-making techniques from the Song Dynasty.
jotenji_hakata.text_en: Jotenji is a Rinzai sect temple founded in 1241 by Shoichi Kokushi (En'er) after returning from the Song Dynasty. It is said that Enji learned flour-milling and noodle-making techniques during his training in the Song Dynasty and brought them back to Hakata, where he introduced the methods of making udon, soba, and manju.There are monuments erected within the temple grounds, such as ``The birthplace of udon and soba'' and ``The birthplace of manju.'' Enji also contributed to urban development, working with Hakata merchants to recommend the excavation of the Hakata Hori River in preparation for a major flood in Hakata. The garden on the grounds, ``Saito-tei'', is a simple dry landscape garden with stonework and white sand, and it still conveys the aesthetic sense of the Kamakura period. This is a place where you can experience the role Hakata played in revolutionizing Japan's food and spiritual culture through trade with the Song Dynasty.

sumiyoshi_shrine_hakata.name: 住吉神社（博多）

transit.name: 福岡市営地下鉄「唐人町駅」

sumiyoshi_shrine_hakata.text: 博多の住吉神社は大阪・住吉大社、下関・住吉神社とともに「日本三大住吉」のひとつに数えられる古社です。底筒男神・中筒男神・表筒男神の住吉三神と神功皇后を祀り、航海・交通の守護神として古代から海人族や船乗りの厚い信仰を集めてきました。創建は約1,800年前と伝わり、神功皇后が三韓征伐から凱旋の折にこの地に神を祀ったのが起源とされています。古代から博多は大陸貿易の玄関口であり、住吉神社は航海の安全を祈る場として機能しました。現在の本殿は1623年に黒田長政が再建したもので、国の重要文化財に指定されています。境内は市街地の中に静かな空間を形成しており、地域の氏神として今も博多市民に親しまれています。
sumiyoshi_shrine_hakata.highlight: 日本三大住吉のひとつ。神功皇后創建・1,800年の歴史を持つ航海の守護神
sumiyoshi_shrine_hakata.highlight_en: One of Japan's three major Sumiyoshi. Founded by Empress Jingu, the guardian deity of navigation with a history of 1,800 years.
sumiyoshi_shrine_hakata.text_en: Sumiyoshi Shrine in Hakata is an old shrine that is counted as one of Japan's three major Sumiyoshi shrines, along with Osaka Sumiyoshi Taisha and Shimonoseki Sumiyoshi Shrine. It enshrines the three deities of Sumiyoshi, the Sokotsutsu, Nakazutsu, and Omotestutsu deities, and Empress Jingu, and has been worshiped by the Kaijin tribe and sailors since ancient times as the guardian deity of navigation and transportation. It is said to have been founded about 1,800 years ago, and it is said that Empress Jingu enshrined a god here during her triumphant return from the Sanhan Conquest. Since ancient times, Hakata has been the gateway to continental trade, and Sumiyoshi Shrine has functioned as a place to pray for safe voyages. The current main shrine was rebuilt by Kuroda Nagamasa in 1623 and is designated as a national important cultural property. The shrine grounds form a quiet space within the city, and are still loved by Hakata citizens as the local deity.

tsurumaru_castle.name: 鶴丸城跡（鹿児島城）
tsurumaru_castle.text: 鶴丸城（鹿児島城）は1601年に島津家18代・家久が築いた城で、天守を持たない「武家屋敷の集合体」のような構造が特徴的な平城です。島津氏はあえて天守を設けず「天守は不要、城下全体を城とする」という考え方を採りました。幕末には薩摩藩政治の中心として機能し、藩校「造士館」や演武館が置かれ、西郷隆盛・大久保利通・小松帯刀ら明治維新の志士たちを輩出しました。1877年の西南戦争では激しい戦闘の末に焼失しました。現在は「黎明館」（鹿児島県歴史・美術センター）が建てられており、鹿児島の歴史・民俗・美術資料を収蔵・展示しています。2020年には薩摩藩が造った御楼門が145年ぶりに復元され、往時の威容を取り戻しました。
tsurumaru_castle.highlight: 天守なき薩摩の城。西郷・大久保を生んだ政治の中心・御楼門が145年ぶりに復元
tsurumaru_castle.highlight_en: A castle in Satsuma without a castle tower. The Goroumon Gate, the political center that gave birth to Saigo and Okubo, has been restored for the first time in 145 years.
tsurumaru_castle.text_en: Tsurumaru Castle (Kagoshima Castle) was built in 1601 by Iehisa, the 18th generation of the Shimazu clan, and is a flat castle with a structure that resembles a collection of samurai residences without a castle tower. The Shimazu clan did not intentionally install a castle tower, instead adopting the idea that ``a castle tower is unnecessary, and the entire castle grounds should be treated as a castle.'' At the end of the Edo period, it functioned as the center of politics for the Satsuma domain, and the domain schools ``Zoshikan'' and Enbukan were located here, and it produced patriots of the Meiji Restoration such as Saigo Takamori, Okubo Toshimichi, and Komatsu Tateto. It was burnt down after a fierce battle during the Satsuma Rebellion in 1877. Currently, "Reimeikan" (Kagoshima Prefectural History and Art Center) is being built, and it stores and displays Kagoshima's history, folklore, and art materials. In 2020, the Goroumon gate built by the Satsuma clan was restored for the first time in 145 years, returning it to its former grandeur.

sengan_en.name: 仙巌園・尚古集成館
sengan_en.kana: せんがんえん・しょうこしゅうせいかん
sengan_en.text: 仙巌園は1658年に島津家19代・光久が造営した池泉回遊式の大名庭園で、桜島を借景に錦江湾を池に見立てた雄大な景観が特徴です。隣接する尚古集成館は幕末に島津斉彬が建設した日本最初期の洋式工場群の一部で、現存する日本最古の石造洋風建築です。斉彬は「集成館事業」として反射炉・ガラス工場・紡績機械・蒸気船の建造など最先端産業を推進し、日本の近代化を率先した名君として知られています。2015年に「明治日本の産業革命遺産」としてユネスコ世界遺産に登録されました。西郷隆盛・大久保利通ら薩摩の志士たちが斉彬の薫陶を受け、明治維新の推進力となっていったのもこの地の周辺です。
sengan_en.highlight: 桜島を借景にした大名庭園と日本最古の洋式工場。世界遺産・斉彬の近代化の拠点
sengan_en.highlight_en: A feudal lord garden with Sakurajima as its backdrop and Japan's oldest Western-style factory. Base of modernization of World Heritage Site Nariaki
sengan_en.text_en: Sengan-en is a feudal lord's garden built in 1658 by Mitsuhisa, the 19th generation of the Shimazu family, with a pond strolling around it.It is characterized by a magnificent landscape with Sakurajima in the background and Kinko Bay as a pond. The adjacent Shoko Shuseikan is part of Japan's earliest Western-style factory complex, built by Nariakira Shimazu at the end of the Edo period, and is the oldest remaining stone Western-style building in Japan. Nariakira promoted cutting-edge industries such as the construction of reverberatory furnaces, glass factories, spinning machines, and steamships under the Shuseikan project, and is known as a master who led Japan's modernization. In 2015, it was registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site as a "Site of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution." It was around this area that Saigo Takamori, Okubo Toshimichi, and other Satsuma patriots received Nariakira's tutelage and became the driving force behind the Meiji Restoration.

shiroyama_kagoshima.name: 城山（西郷隆盛終焉の地）
shiroyama_kagoshima.text: 城山は鹿児島市街地を一望できる標高107メートルの丘で、1877年の西南戦争最終決戦の地です。新政府軍に追い詰められた西郷隆盛は約200名の残兵とともに城山に籠城し、9月24日の総攻撃で洞窟から出た直後に銃弾を受けて絶命しました。享年49歳でした。「敬天愛人」を信条とした西郷の最期は今も多くの人の心を打ちます。城山には当時西郷らが潜んだとされる洞窟が残っており、見学することができます。山頂の展望台からは眼下に鹿児島市街地、錦江湾越しに桜島の雄姿を一望でき、西郷が最後に見た故郷の景色を追体験できます。山全体が亜熱帯植物の天然林に覆われた国の天然記念物でもあります。
shiroyama_kagoshima.highlight: 西郷隆盛が49歳で散った西南戦争終焉の地。山頂から桜島と錦江湾の絶景を望む
shiroyama_kagoshima.name_en: Shiroyama (the place where Saigo Takamori died)
shiroyama_kagoshima.highlight_en: The place where Saigo Takamori died at the age of 49 at the end of the Seinan War. Enjoy spectacular views of Sakurajima and Kinko Bay from the mountaintop
shiroyama_kagoshima.text_en: Shiroyama is a 107 meter high hill overlooking the city of Kagoshima, and was the site of the final battle of the Seinan War in 1877. Cornered by the new government forces, Takamori Saigo holed up in Shiroyama with about 200 remaining soldiers, and was killed by a bullet just after emerging from the cave during an all-out attack on September 24th. He passed away at the age of 49. The last moments of Saigo, who believed in ``respect for heaven and love,'' still touch the hearts of many people today. The cave where Saigo and his friends are said to have hid at the time still remains in Shiroyama, and you can tour it. From the observation deck at the top of the mountain, you can see Kagoshima city below and the majesty of Sakurajima across Kinko Bay, allowing you to relive the last view of Saigo's hometown. The entire mountain is covered in a natural forest of subtropical plants and is a national natural monument.

nanshu_cemetery.name: 南洲墓地・南洲神社
nanshu_cemetery.kana: なんしゅうぼち・なんしゅうじんじゃ
nanshu_cemetery.text: 南洲墓地は1877年の西南戦争で戦死した薩摩軍の将兵を埋葬した墓地で、西郷隆盛の墓を中心に2,023名の墓が並んでいます。西郷の墓は正面中央に位置し、多くの参拝者が訪れます。隣接する南洲神社は1879年に薩摩軍戦没者の霊を慰めるために建立され、西郷隆盛を主祭神として祀っています。「南洲」は西郷の号です。敵将である西郷を称えた山形県酒田市の旧庄内藩士たちが、戊辰戦争で敗れたにもかかわらず西郷の寛大な処置に感謝して創建に協力したという逸話は有名です。墓地内には「敬天愛人」と刻まれた石碑が立ち、西郷の信条を今に伝えています。
nanshu_cemetery.highlight: 西郷隆盛と2,023名の薩摩軍将兵が眠る。敵であった旧庄内藩士が神社創建に協力
nanshu_cemetery.highlight_en: Takamori Saigo and 2,023 soldiers of the Satsuma army are buried here. Former enemy samurai of the Shonai clan cooperated in the construction of the shrine.
nanshu_cemetery.text_en: Nanshu Cemetery is a cemetery where the soldiers of the Satsuma army who died in the Seinan War of 1877 were buried, and there are 2,023 graves lined up, including the grave of Takamori Saigo. Saigo's tomb is located in the front center and is visited by many worshipers. The adjacent Nanshu Shrine was built in 1879 to console the spirits of the Satsuma army's fallen soldiers, and enshrines Saigo Takamori as its main deity. ``Nanshu'' is the name of Saigo. There is a well-known anecdote that the former Shonai feudal retainers of Sakata City, Yamagata Prefecture, who praised the enemy general Saigo, cooperated in the construction of the shrine in gratitude for Saigo's generous treatment even though they were defeated in the Boshin War. Inside the cemetery, there is a stone monument inscribed with the words ``Respect for Heaven and Love,'' which conveys Saigo's beliefs to this day.

chiran_peace.name: 知覧特攻平和会館
chiran_peace.kana: ちらんとっこうへいわかいかん

transit.name: 指宿スカイライン知覧IC

chiran_peace.text: 知覧特攻平和会館は第二次世界大戦末期の1945年、沖縄戦に向けて鹿児島・知覧基地から飛び立った特別攻撃隊（特攻隊）の若者たちの遺品・遺書・写真を保存・展示する平和祈念館です。知覧は「陸軍特攻の聖地」と呼ばれ、ここから1,036名の若者が沖縄の海に散りました。展示されている遺書や手紙には、祖国・家族への思いが切々と綴られており、平均年齢20歳前後の若者たちが死と向き合いながら書いた言葉は今も見る者の心を揺さぶります。零戦など実物の特攻機も展示されています。年間50万人以上が訪れる九州を代表する平和学習の場で、戦争の悲惨さと平和の尊さを後世に伝えています。
chiran_peace.highlight: 1,036名の若者が旅立った特攻の聖地。平均20歳の遺書が語りかける戦争の真実
chiran_peace.highlight_en: A sacred place for special attacks where 1,036 young people departed. The truth about war told by suicide notes written by an average 20-year-old
chiran_peace.text_en: The Chiran Special Attack Peace Museum is a peace memorial hall that preserves and exhibits the belongings, wills, and photographs of the young men of the Special Attack Force (Kamikaze Unit) who took off from the Chiran base in Kagoshima in preparation for the Battle of Okinawa in 1945 at the end of World War II. Chiran was called the ``sacred place for army special attacks,'' and from here 1,036 young men were dispersed to the seas of Okinawa. The wills and letters on display earnestly express their feelings for their homeland and family, and the words written by young people, with an average age of around 20 years old, as they faced death still move the hearts of those who see them. Actual special attack aircraft such as the Zero Fighter are also on display. It is Kyushu's leading peace learning venue, visited by more than 500,000 people a year, and conveys the misery of war and the preciousness of peace to future generations.

chiran_bukeyashiki.name: 知覧武家屋敷群
chiran_bukeyashiki.kana: ちらんぶけやしきぐん

transit.name: 指宿スカイライン知覧IC

chiran_bukeyashiki.text: 知覧武家屋敷群は薩摩藩の外城制度（とじょうせいど）のもと、藩内各地に設けられた「麓（ふもと）」と呼ばれる武士集落のひとつです。薩摩藩は城下以外にも武士が居住する武家集落を各地に設け、軍事的な分散配置と農村支配を実現しました。知覧の武家屋敷群は石垣と生垣が整然と並ぶ美しい景観を保ち、「薩摩の小京都」と称されています。7つの庭園が国の名勝に指定されており、沖縄・中国の影響を受けた琉球式の庭園様式と日本庭園の様式が混在した独特の美しさが特徴です。九州で最も保存状態の良い武家屋敷群のひとつとして、多くの観光客が訪れます。
chiran_bukeyashiki.highlight: 薩摩の小京都。国名勝7庭園を持つ、九州最高の武家屋敷群の景観
chiran_bukeyashiki.highlight_en: Little Kyoto of Satsuma. A view of the best samurai residences in Kyushu with 7 scenic gardens
chiran_bukeyashiki.text_en: The Chiran Samurai Residences are one of the samurai villages called ``Fumoto'' that were established throughout the Satsuma domain under the Satsuma domain's outer castle system. In addition to the castle grounds, the Satsuma Domain established samurai villages in various locations where samurai lived, achieving military decentralization and control over rural areas. The samurai residences in Chiran maintain a beautiful landscape with neatly lined stone walls and hedges, and are known as ``Little Kyoto of Satsuma.'' Seven of its gardens have been designated as National Places of Scenic Beauty, and are characterized by their unique beauty, which is a mixture of Ryukyu style gardens influenced by Okinawa and China, and Japanese garden styles. As one of the best-preserved samurai residences in Kyushu, it is visited by many tourists.

kirishima_jingu.name: 霧島神宮
kirishima_jingu.text: 霧島神宮は天孫降臨神話の主役・瓊瓊杵尊（ににぎのみこと）を主祭神として祀る神社で、創建は6世紀頃とされています。日本神話において天照大神の孫・ニニギが降り立ったとされる高千穂峰（標高1,574m）のふもとに鎮座し、「南九州の総鎮守」として崇敬を集めてきました。現在の社殿は1715年に島津吉貴が造営したもので、権現造りの本殿は国宝に指定されています。境内の杉並木は樹齢数百年を誇り、独特の神聖な雰囲気を醸し出しています。坂本龍馬がお龍（りょう）と新婚旅行でこの地を訪れたことでも知られており、日本初の新婚旅行の地として観光PRにも使われています。
kirishima_jingu.highlight: 天孫降臨神話の地・高千穂峰ふもとの国宝社殿。坂本龍馬が日本初の新婚旅行で訪問
kirishima_jingu.highlight_en: A national treasure shrine at the foot of Mt. Takachiho, the mythical place of the descent of the descendants of the Tenson. Ryoma Sakamoto visits Japan for his first honeymoon
kirishima_jingu.text_en: Kirishima Shrine is a shrine that enshrines Ninigi no Mikoto, the protagonist of the myth of the descent of the descendants of the Tenson, as its main deity, and is said to have been founded around the 6th century. It is enshrined at the foot of Mt. Takachiho (1,574m above sea level), where Ninigi, the grandson of Amaterasu Omikami, is said to have descended in Japanese mythology, and has been revered as the ``general guardian of southern Kyushu.'' The current shrine building was built by Yoshiki Shimazu in 1715, and the Gongen-zukuri main shrine is designated as a national treasure. The cedar trees on the grounds are hundreds of years old, creating a unique sacred atmosphere. It is also known that Ryoma Sakamoto visited this place on his honeymoon with Ryo, and it is also used in tourism PR as Japan's first honeymoon destination.

sakurajima_history.name: 桜島

transit.name: 鹿児島港からフェリー

sakurajima_history.text: 桜島は鹿児島湾（錦江湾）に浮かぶ活火山で、薩摩藩・鹿児島のシンボルです。元は島でしたが、1914年（大正3年）の大噴火「大正大噴火」で大量の溶岩が流出し、対岸の大隅半島と陸続きになりました。この噴火は史上最大規模のひとつで、溶岩は約35平方キロメートルを覆い、島の外周が約2倍になりました。埋没した鳥居の一部が今も地中に残り、噴火の壮絶さを物語っています。現在も南岳・昭和火口が活発に噴火を続けており、世界でも有数の「生きた火山」です。周辺では火山灰が農業に活用されており、特産の「桜島大根」（世界最大の大根）は火山灰土壌で育ちます。
sakurajima_history.highlight: 1914年大噴火で陸続きに。今も噴火する活火山に埋まった鳥居が噴火の凄まじさを伝える
sakurajima_history.highlight_en: In 1914, a large eruption led to the land being connected. A torii gate buried under an active volcano that is still erupting conveys the ferocity of the eruption.
sakurajima_history.text_en: Sakurajima is an active volcano floating in Kagoshima Bay (Kinko Bay) and is a symbol of the Satsuma Domain and Kagoshima. It was originally an island, but in 1914 (Taisho 3), a large amount of lava flowed out during the Taisho eruption, and it became connected to the Osumi Peninsula on the opposite shore. This eruption was one of the largest in history, with lava covering an area of ​​approximately 35 square kilometers, approximately doubling the circumference of the island. Part of the buried torii still remains underground, testifying to the ferocity of the eruption. The Minamidake/Showa crater continues to actively erupt, making it one of the world's leading "living volcanoes." In the surrounding area, volcanic ash is used for agriculture, and the specialty ``Sakurajima radish'' (the world's largest radish) grows in volcanic ash soil.

tanegashima_teppo.name: 種子島（鉄砲伝来の地）

transit.name: 鹿児島港からフェリー約3時間

tanegashima_teppo.text: 種子島は1543年にポルトガル人を乗せた中国船が漂着し、日本に初めて鉄砲（火縄銃）が伝来した島として世界史的に重要な場所です。漂着したポルトガル人商人から鉄砲2丁を購入した島主・種子島時尭は、早速刀鍛冶に鉄砲の複製を命じ、翌年には量産に成功しました。この鉄砲の伝来は日本の戦国時代の戦術を根本から変え、長篠の戦い（1575年）での織田信長による鉄砲足軽の大規模運用など、戦国史に決定的な影響を与えました。島内の「種子島開発総合センター鉄砲館」では鉄砲伝来の歴史を詳しく学べます。現代では「種子島宇宙センター」が立地し、古代の鉄砲伝来と現代のロケット打ち上げが共存するユニークな島です。
tanegashima_teppo.highlight: 1543年・日本に鉄砲が初上陸した島。戦国時代の戦術を変えた歴史的転換点
tanegashima_teppo.highlight_en: 1543 - The island where the first guns landed in Japan. Historical turning point that changed tactics during the Sengoku period
tanegashima_teppo.text_en: Tanegashima is an important place in world history, as it is the island where a Chinese ship carrying Portuguese people washed ashore in 1543, and where the first firearms (matchlock guns) were introduced to Japan. The island's owner, Tokitaka Tanegashima, who purchased two guns from a Portuguese merchant who had washed ashore, immediately ordered a swordsmith to duplicate the guns, and the following year they succeeded in mass producing them. The introduction of this gun fundamentally changed Japan's tactics during the Sengoku period, and had a decisive influence on the history of the Sengoku period, such as Oda Nobunaga's large-scale use of gun ashigaru at the Battle of Nagashino (1575). At the Tanegashima Development Center Gun Museum on the island, you can learn more about the history of the introduction of guns. Today, the Tanegashima Space Center is located on this unique island where ancient firearms and modern rocket launches coexist.

yakushima_jomon.name: 屋久島（縄文杉）

transit.name: 鹿児島港からフェリー約4時間

yakushima_jomon.text: 屋久島は鹿児島県南方の離島で、島の90パーセント以上が森林に覆われ、1993年に日本初のユネスコ世界自然遺産に登録されました。島のシンボル「縄文杉」は推定樹齢2,170〜7,200年とされ（研究により諸説あり）、幹周16.4メートル・高さ25.3メートルの巨木で、屋久島の神秘性を象徴する存在です。屋久島では「一ヶ月に35日雨が降る」と言われるほどの多雨環境が屋久杉の巨大化をもたらしました。宮崎駿監督のアニメ映画「もののけ姫」の舞台のモデルになったとされる原生林は、苔むした幻想的な景観で訪れる者を魅了します。江戸時代には屋久杉が薩摩藩の重要な財源として大量に伐採されましたが、今は厳重に保護されています。
yakushima_jomon.highlight: 樹齢数千年の縄文杉が立つ日本初の世界自然遺産。「もののけ姫」の舞台モデルの原生林
yakushima_jomon.highlight_en: Japan's first world natural heritage site with Jomon cedar trees that are several thousand years old. The primeval forest that served as the stage model for “Princess Mononoke”
yakushima_jomon.text_en: Yakushima is a remote island in the southern part of Kagoshima Prefecture, with more than 90% of the island covered in forest, and was registered as Japan's first UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site in 1993. The island's symbol, the Jomon Cedar, is estimated to be between 2,170 and 7,200 years old (there are various theories based on research), and is a gigantic tree with a trunk circumference of 16.4 meters and a height of 25.3 meters, symbolizing the mystique of Yakushima. Yakushima's rainy environment, where it is said that it rains 35 days a month, has caused the Yakusugi to grow in size. The primeval forest, which is said to have been the setting for Hayao Miyazaki's animated film ``Princess Mononoke,'' fascinates visitors with its magical, moss-covered landscape. During the Edo period, large quantities of Yakusugi were felled as an important source of revenue for the Satsuma domain, but now they are strictly protected.

amami_saigo.name: 奄美大島（西郷隆盛流刑地）
amami_saigo.text: 奄美大島は鹿児島県南方の離島で、独自の自然・文化・歴史を持ちます。島は江戸時代に薩摩藩の直轄領として砂糖の専売制度が敷かれ、島民は苛酷な搾取に苦しみました。西郷隆盛は1859年に安政の大獄に連座して奄美大島に流刑となり、島に3年間滞在しました。この時期に島の女性・愛加那（あいかな）と結婚し、子どもも授かっています。西郷はこの島での生活を通じて民衆の苦しみを実感し、後の政治思想に影響を受けたとも言われています。2021年には「奄美大島、徳之島、沖縄島北部及び西表島」としてユネスコ世界自然遺産に登録され、希少な生態系が評価されました。大島紬をはじめとする独自文化も魅力です。
amami_saigo.highlight: 西郷隆盛が流刑中に妻・愛加那と出会った島。2021年に世界自然遺産登録
amami_saigo.highlight_en: The island where Saigo Takamori met his wife Aikana while in exile. Registered as a World Natural Heritage Site in 2021
amami_saigo.text_en: Amami Oshima is a remote island in the south of Kagoshima Prefecture, with its own unique nature, culture, and history. During the Edo period, the island was placed under the direct control of the Satsuma domain and a sugar monopoly system was established, and the islanders suffered from severe exploitation. Takamori Saigo was exiled to Amami Oshima in 1859 as part of the Great Prison of Ansei and stayed on the island for three years. During this period, he married a woman from the island, Aika, and they had a child together. It is said that Saigo experienced the suffering of the people through his life on this island and was influenced by his later political ideas. In 2021, "Amami Oshima, Tokunoshima, Northern Okinawa Island, and Iriomote Island" were registered as UNESCO World Natural Heritage Sites, and their rare ecosystems were recognized. Its unique culture, including Oshima Tsumugi, is also attractive.

bonotsu_port.name: 坊津

transit.name: 鹿児島市内からバス約2時間

bonotsu_port.text: 坊津は薩摩半島南西端に位置する天然の良港で、古代から「日本三津（みつ）」のひとつとして博多・難波とともに数えられた国際的な港湾都市です。奈良・平安時代には遣唐使船の発着港として機能し、鑑真和上も753年に日本への渡航を試みた際に坊津に関わりがあったとされています。中世には中国・琉球との密貿易が盛んに行われ、薩摩藩の貿易の窓口として栄えました。フランシスコ・ザビエルも1549年にここから日本に上陸し、鹿児島に向かったと伝わります。江戸時代には密貿易の取り締まりが厳しくなりましたが、薩摩藩が公認する形で琉球を通じた中国との貿易が続けられました。
bonotsu_port.highlight: 古代の遣唐使港・ザビエル上陸の地。日本三津のひとつとして栄えた国際貿易港
bonotsu_port.highlight_en: An ancient port for envoys to China and the place where Xavier landed. An international trading port that flourished as one of Japan's three major cities
bonotsu_port.text_en: Bozu is a good natural port located at the southwestern tip of the Satsuma Peninsula, and is an international port city that has been counted as one of the ``Three Mitsu'' of Japan since ancient times, along with Hakata and Namba. During the Nara and Heian periods, it functioned as a port for envoys sent to Tang China, and it is said that Ganjin Wajo was also connected to Bozu when he attempted to travel to Japan in 753. In the Middle Ages, smuggling trade with China and the Ryukyus flourished, and it flourished as a trade gateway for the Satsuma domain. It is said that Francisco Xavier also landed in Japan from here in 1549 and headed for Kagoshima. During the Edo period, the crackdown on smuggling became stricter, but trade with China through the Ryukyus continued with official approval from the Satsuma domain.

izumi_bukeyashiki.name: 出水麓武家屋敷群
izumi_bukeyashiki.kana: いずみふもとぶけやしきぐん
izumi_bukeyashiki.text: 出水麓武家屋敷群は薩摩藩の外城制度により整備された武士集落「麓」のうち、最大・最高の保存状態を誇るものとして知られています。薩摩藩は藩内各地に武士を分散居住させる独自の制度を採っており、出水は薩摩・肥後両藩の国境に位置する軍事的要衝だったため、特に重武装の武士集落が置かれました。石垣と白壁の武家屋敷が碁盤の目状に並ぶ美しい街並みは国の重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に選定されています。薩摩の武士道「郷中教育（ごじゅうきょういく）」はこの麓で行われた厳格な若者教育制度で、薩摩藩士の強さの源でもありました。毎年10月には約15,000羽の鶴が飛来し、武家屋敷の景観と鶴の渡来地が共存する独特の風景を生み出します。
izumi_bukeyashiki.highlight: 薩摩最大・最良の武家屋敷群。「郷中教育」で鍛えられた薩摩武士道の里
izumi_bukeyashiki.highlight_en: The largest and best group of samurai residences in Satsuma. The village of Satsuma Bushido, trained through “Gonchu education”
izumi_bukeyashiki.text_en: The Izumizuroku Samurai Residences are known as the largest and best-preserved samurai settlements built under the Satsuma clan's outer castle system. The Satsuma domain had a unique system in which samurai were dispersed throughout the domain, and since Izumi was a military strategic point located on the border between the Satsuma and Higo domains, a particularly heavily armed samurai village was located there. The beautiful townscape, with its stone walls and white-walled samurai residences lined up in a grid pattern, has been designated as a nationally important preservation district for groups of traditional buildings. The Bushido of Satsuma, ``gojukyōiku,'' was a strict youth education system carried out at the foot of this mountain, and was the source of the strength of the Satsuma samurai. Approximately 15,000 cranes fly to the area every October, creating a unique landscape where samurai residences and crane migration sites coexist.

kagoshima_spinning.name: 旧鹿児島紡績所跡
kagoshima_spinning.kana: きゅうかごしまぼうせきじょあと
kagoshima_spinning.text: 旧鹿児島紡績所は1867年に薩摩藩が建設した日本初の洋式紡績工場です。島津斉彬が推進した「集成館事業」の一環として、英国から機械・技術者を招いて建設されました。建設には1865年に薩摩藩がイギリスに密航留学させた「薩摩藩英国留学生」の成果も活かされています。工場は「日本で初めて洋式機械によって綿糸が生産された場所」として近代工業史上重要な意義を持ちます。現存する「異人館」はフランス人技術者の住居として建てられたもので、2015年に「明治日本の産業革命遺産」の構成資産としてユネスコ世界遺産に登録されました。幕末に薩摩藩が如何に早く近代化に取り組んでいたかを物語る証拠です。
kagoshima_spinning.highlight: 1867年・日本初の洋式紡績工場。薩摩の密航留学生の成果が結実した世界遺産
kagoshima_spinning.highlight_en: 1867 - Japan's first Western-style spinning factory. A world heritage site born from the achievements of stowaway students from Satsuma
kagoshima_spinning.text_en: The former Kagoshima Spinning Mill was built by the Satsuma clan in 1867 and was Japan's first Western-style spinning factory. It was constructed by inviting mechanics and engineers from England as part of the Shuseikan project promoted by Shimazu Nariakira. The construction also utilized the achievements of the ``Satsuma Clan British Students'' who were smuggled to England by the Satsuma Clan in 1865 to study abroad. The factory has an important significance in the history of modern industry as ``the first place in Japan where cotton yarn was produced using Western-style machinery.'' The existing "Ijinkan" was built as a residence for a French engineer, and was registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2015 as a component of the "Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution." This is evidence of how quickly the Satsuma clan was modernizing at the end of the Edo period.

sekiya_sosui.name: 関吉の疎水溝
sekiya_sosui.kana: せきよしのそすいこう
sekiya_sosui.text: 関吉の疎水溝は島津斉彬が集成館事業のために水力確保を目的として19世紀中頃に築いた用水路で、稲荷川上流から仙巌園・集成館一帯まで約6キロメートルにわたって水を引いています。近代産業に必要な水力を山から引いてくる技術的に高度な施設で、水車動力を使った反射炉・工場の稼働を支えました。素朴な石積みの水路が今も水を流しており、160年以上前の土木技術の高さを実感できます。2015年に「明治日本の産業革命遺産」の構成資産としてユネスコ世界遺産に登録されました。付近の自然の中を歩きながら、幕末の産業革命の礎となった水路の歴史に思いを馳せることができます。
sekiya_sosui.highlight: 斉彬の集成館に水力を供給した用水路。今も水が流れる世界遺産の産業インフラ
sekiya_sosui.highlight_en: An irrigation canal that supplied water power to Nariakira's Shuseikan. World heritage industrial infrastructure with water still flowing through it
sekiya_sosui.text_en: The Sekiyoshi water canal is an irrigation canal built by Shimazu Nariakira in the mid-19th century to secure water power for the Shuseikan project, and it draws water for approximately 6 kilometers from the upper reaches of the Inari River to the Senganen and Shuseikan areas. It was a technologically advanced facility that drew the water power necessary for modern industry from the mountains, and supported the operation of reverberatory furnaces and factories using water wheel power. Water still flows through the rustic stone canals, and you can experience the high level of civil engineering technology used over 160 years ago. In 2015, it was registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site as a component of the "Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution." While walking through the nearby nature, you can think about the history of the waterway that became the foundation of the industrial revolution at the end of the Edo period.

terayama_charcoal.name: 寺山炭窯跡
terayama_charcoal.kana: てらやますみがまあと
terayama_charcoal.text: 寺山炭窯跡は島津斉彬が集成館事業の燃料供給のために1858年頃に築いた木炭製造施設の跡地です。反射炉や溶鉱炉の燃料として大量の木炭が必要だったため、仙巌園・集成館から吉野台地の山中に炭窯を設けました。花崗岩を積み上げた炭窯は直径約4メートル・深さ約3メートルで、内部の石積みが良好な状態で残っています。人里離れた山中に静かに佇むこの炭窯跡は、150年前の産業革命の現場が自然の中にそのまま保存された貴重な遺構です。2015年に「明治日本の産業革命遺産」の構成資産としてユネスコ世界遺産に登録されました。
terayama_charcoal.highlight: 斉彬の工場に木炭を供給した炭窯。山中にひっそり残る世界遺産の産業遺構
terayama_charcoal.highlight_en: A charcoal kiln that supplied charcoal to Nariakira's factory. World heritage industrial remains hidden in the mountains
terayama_charcoal.text_en: The Terayama charcoal kiln site is the site of a charcoal manufacturing facility built by Nariakira Shimazu around 1858 to supply fuel for the Shuseikan project. Since large amounts of charcoal were needed as fuel for reverberatory furnaces and blast furnaces, a charcoal kiln was built in the mountains of Yoshino Plateau from Senganen and Shuseikan. The charcoal kiln is made of stacked granite and is about 4 meters in diameter and 3 meters deep, and the stonework inside is still in good condition. This charcoal kiln site, located quietly in a remote mountain, is a valuable relic of the industrial revolution 150 years ago, preserved in its natural setting. In 2015, it was registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site as a component of the "Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution."

satsuma_students.name: 薩摩藩英国留学生記念館
satsuma_students.kana: さつまはんえいこくりゅうがくせいきねんかん

transit.name: JR鹿児島本線「神村学園前駅」

satsuma_students.text: 薩摩藩英国留学生記念館（いちき串木野市）は、1865年に薩英戦争での敗北から西洋技術の重要性を痛感した薩摩藩が幕府の禁を犯して密かにイギリスへ派遣した19名の留学生を顕彰する施設です。長沢鼎・五代友厚・寺島宗則・森有礼ら、後に明治政府の要人となる若者たちがグラスゴーやロンドンで最先端の技術・文化・制度を学び、帰国後の日本近代化を主導しました。五代友厚は大阪経済界の発展に尽力し、長沢鼎はアメリカでワイナリーを創設して「ぶどう王」と呼ばれました。この密航留学は維新のエネルギーの源のひとつであり、「薩摩スチューデント」として日英交流史に刻まれています。
satsuma_students.highlight: 幕府の禁を犯した19名の密航留学。五代友厚ら明治の立役者を育てた薩摩の先見性
satsuma_students.name_en: Satsuma Domain British Student Memorial Hall
satsuma_students.highlight_en: 19 stowaway students who violated the Shogunate's ban. The foresight of Satsuma, which nurtured leading figures of the Meiji period such as Godai Tomoatsu
satsuma_students.text_en: The Satsuma Clan British Students Memorial Hall (Ichikikushikino City) is a facility that honors the 19 students who were secretly sent to England in 1865 by the Satsuma Clan, who realized the importance of Western technology after their defeat in the Anglo-Satsuma War and violated the Shogunate's ban. Young people who would later become key figures in the Meiji government, such as Kanae Nagasawa, Tomoatsu Godai, Munenori Terajima, and Arinori Mori, studied cutting-edge technology, culture, and systems in Glasgow and London, and led the modernization of Japan after returning to Japan. Tomoatsu Godai worked hard to develop the Osaka business community, and Kanae Nagasawa founded a winery in America and was known as the "Grape King." This stowaway study abroad was one of the sources of energy for the Meiji Restoration, and is etched in the history of Japan-UK exchanges as the ``Satsuma Student''.

nitta_shrine.name: 新田神社
nitta_shrine.text: 新田神社は薩摩国一宮（いちのみや）として、薩摩・大隅両国の総鎮守を担ってきた古社です。祭神は天津日高彦穂穂出見尊（山幸彦）で、神話では竜宮から帰還した後にこの地に鎮座したとされています。標高約60メートルの亀山の山頂に鎮座しており、麓から続く参道と山上の社殿が独特の景観を形成しています。薩摩藩主・島津家の崇敬を受け、代々の藩主が社殿の造営・修理を行いました。「神亀山」と呼ばれる自然の丘全体が聖域とされており、境内には樹齢数百年の楠の巨木が茂っています。薩摩の一宮として、古代から島津氏の精神的支柱として機能してきた由緒ある神社です。
nitta_shrine.highlight: 薩摩国一宮・山幸彦を祀る古社。島津家が代々崇敬した薩摩の精神的守護神
nitta_shrine.highlight_en: An old shrine dedicated to Yamasachihiko of Ichinomiya, Satsuma Province. The spiritual guardian deity of Satsuma, revered by the Shimazu family for generations.
nitta_shrine.text_en: Nitta Shrine is an old shrine that served as the Ichinomiya of Satsuma Province and was responsible for the overall guardianship of both Satsuma and Osumi Provinces. The enshrined deity is Amatsu Hidaka Hikoho Demikoto (Yamasachihiko), who is said to have been enshrined here after returning from the Dragon Palace. It is located on the summit of Kameyama, approximately 60 meters above sea level, and the approach that leads from the foot of the mountain and the shrine building on the mountain form a unique landscape. It was revered by the Shimazu family, the lords of the Satsuma domain, and successive generations of lords built and repaired the shrine. The entire natural hill called ``Kamikameyama'' is considered a sacred area, and within the precincts there are huge camphor trees that are hundreds of years old. As the Ichinomiya shrine of Satsuma, it is a historic shrine that has functioned as the spiritual pillar of the Shimazu clan since ancient times.

kagoshima_jingu.name: 鹿児島神宮
kagoshima_jingu.text: 鹿児島神宮は大隅国一宮として、古代から大隅地方の総鎮守を担ってきた格式高い神社です。祭神は天津日高彦火火出見尊（山幸彦）・豊玉比売命（豊玉姫）などで、神話の世界と深く結びついています。創建は神代とも言われ、欽明天皇の時代（6世紀）に現在地に遷座したとの伝承があります。境内の大楠は樹齢800年以上といわれる巨木で、国の天然記念物に指定されています。毎年9月には「浜下り（はまおり）」と呼ばれる伝統神事が行われ、神輿が海岸まで渡御します。また「初午祭（はつうまさい）」で行われる「お田植え踊り」は国の重要無形民俗文化財で、農耕の豊穣を祈る古式ゆかしい祭礼です。
kagoshima_jingu.highlight: 大隅国一宮。樹齢800年の大楠と「お田植え踊り」（国重要無形民俗文化財）
kagoshima_jingu.highlight_en: Ichinomiya, Osumi Province. 800-year-old camphor tree and “rice planting dance” (National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)
kagoshima_jingu.text_en: Kagoshima Shrine is a highly prestigious shrine that has been the main guardian of the Osumi region since ancient times. The deities enshrined include Amatsu Hidakahiko Hidemison (Yamasachihiko) and Toyotama Hime no Mikoto (Toyota Hime), and are deeply connected to the world of mythology. It is said to have been founded in the age of the gods, and legend has it that it was moved to its current location during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century). The large camphor tree in the temple grounds is said to be over 800 years old and has been designated as a national natural monument. Every September, a traditional ritual called ``Hamaori'' is held, in which a mikoshi (portable shrine) is carried to the shore. In addition, the ``Rice Planting Dance'' held during the ``Hatsuumasai'' is a nationally designated Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property, and is an ancient festival that prays for a bountiful agricultural harvest.

ibusuki_hasimuregawa.name: 橋牟礼川遺跡（指宿）
ibusuki_hasimuregawa.text: 橋牟礼川遺跡は鹿児島県指宿市に位置する縄文時代後期〜弥生時代の遺跡で、縄文土器と弥生土器が同一地層から出土した「縄文・弥生文化の移行」を示す重要遺跡として国の史跡に指定されています。1920年代にその重要性が認識され、日本の先史時代研究に大きな影響を与えました。遺跡周辺では薩摩半島の南端に位置することから、南方との海上交流を示す遺物も出土しており、縄文時代の海洋文化の広がりを物語っています。指宿市考古博物館「時遊館COCCOはしむれ」では出土品を展示しており、縄文から弥生への文化変遷を学べます。指宿は「砂むし温泉」でも有名で、歴史と温泉を組み合わせた観光地として人気があります。
ibusuki_hasimuregawa.highlight: 縄文・弥生土器が同一地層から出土した国史跡。縄文から弥生への文化移行を示す証拠
ibusuki_hasimuregawa.highlight_en: A national historic site where Jomon and Yayoi pottery was excavated from the same stratum. Evidence of cultural transition from Jomon to Yayoi
ibusuki_hasimuregawa.text_en: The Hashimure River ruins are located in Ibusuki City, Kagoshima Prefecture, and are ruins dating from the late Jomon period to the Yayoi period, and are designated as a national historic site as important ruins that demonstrate the ``transition of Jomon-Yayoi culture,'' where Jomon pottery and Yayoi pottery were excavated from the same stratum. Its importance was recognized in the 1920s, and it had a major impact on Japanese prehistoric research. Because the site is located at the southern tip of the Satsuma Peninsula, artifacts that indicate maritime exchange with the south have been unearthed, testifying to the spread of maritime culture during the Jomon period. The Ibusuki City Archeology Museum ``Jiyukan COCCO Hashimure'' exhibits excavated artifacts and allows you to learn about the cultural transition from Jomon to Yayoi. Ibusuki is also famous for its "sand bath" and is a popular tourist destination that combines history and hot springs.

takachiho_gorge.name: 高千穂峡

transit.name: 高千穂バスセンターからバス

takachiho_gorge.text: 高千穂峡は宮崎県高千穂町を流れる五ヶ瀬川が阿蘇山の火山活動で形成した溶岩台地を浸食して作り出した峡谷で、国の名勝・天然記念物に指定されています。柱状節理の断崖が最大100メートルの高さで連続する景観は圧巻で、真名井の滝（まないのたき）は落差17メートルを誇り、日本の滝百選にも選ばれています。この地は天照大神が天岩戸に隠れた際の舞台とされる高天原（たかまがはら）の地と伝わり、日本神話と深く結びついています。ボート遊びができる遊歩道も整備されており、四季折々の自然美を楽しめます。特に紅葉の季節は滝と断崖が色づき、幻想的な景色を呈します。神話の里・高千穂の自然と歴史が融合した宮崎を代表する観光地です。
takachiho_gorge.highlight: 日本神話ゆかりの峡谷。柱状節理の断崖と真名井の滝が織りなす絶景（名勝・天然記念物）
takachiho_gorge.highlight_en: A gorge associated with Japanese mythology. Spectacular scenery created by columnar joint cliffs and Manai Falls (scenic beauty and natural monument)
takachiho_gorge.text_en: Takachiho Gorge is a gorge created by the Gokase River, which flows through Takachiho Town, Miyazaki Prefecture, eroding the lava plateau formed by the volcanic activity of Mt. Aso, and is designated as a national scenic spot and natural monument. The scenery of continuous columnar joint cliffs up to 100 meters high is a sight to behold, and Manai Falls boasts a drop of 17 meters and has been selected as one of Japan's top 100 waterfalls. This area is said to be Takamagahara, the place where Amaterasu Omikami hid in Amanoiwato, and is deeply connected to Japanese mythology. There is also a promenade where you can go boating, and enjoy the natural beauty of each season. Especially during the autumn foliage season, the waterfalls and cliffs change color, creating a fantastic scenery. It is a tourist destination representing Miyazaki that combines the nature and history of the mythical village of Takachiho.

amanoiwato_shrine.name: 天岩戸神社
amanoiwato_shrine.kana: あまのいわとじんじゃ

transit.name: 高千穂バスセンターからバス

amanoiwato_shrine.text: 天岩戸神社は天照大神（あまてらすおおみかみ）が隠れたとされる天岩戸（あまのいわと）を御神体とする神社で、西本宮・東本宮の二社から成ります。西本宮の本殿の裏手には岩戸川を挟んで実際の岩窟があり、神職の案内でのみ見学できます。岩戸川の対岸には、八百万の神々が天照大神を招き出すために集まったとされる「天安河原（あまのやすかわら）」があり、無数の積み石が積まれた洞窟は神秘的な雰囲気を持ちます。日本神話最大のクライマックスとも言える「岩戸隠れ」の舞台として、全国から参拝者が訪れます。周辺は高千穂の神話の里として整備されており、高千穂神社と合わせて訪れる参拝者が多い神話スポットです。
amanoiwato_shrine.highlight: 天照大神が隠れた岩窟を御神体とする神社。天安河原の積み石群が神秘的
amanoiwato_shrine.highlight_en: A shrine whose object of worship is a rock cave where Amaterasu Omikami hid. The mysterious piled stones of Tenyasu River
amanoiwato_shrine.text_en: Amanoiwato Shrine is a shrine whose object of worship is Amanoiwato, where Amaterasu Omikami is said to have hidden, and consists of two shrines: the Nishihongu Shrine and the Higashihongu Shrine. Behind the main shrine of Nishihongu, there is an actual rock cave across the Iwato River, which can only be visited with the guidance of a Shinto priest. On the other side of the Iwato River is Amanoyasu Kawara, where 8 million gods are said to have gathered to invite Amaterasu Omikami, and the cave with countless piles of stones has a mystical atmosphere. It is the setting for Iwatogakure, which can be said to be the climax of Japanese mythology, and is visited by worshipers from all over the country. The surrounding area has been developed as a mythical village of Takachiho, and it is a mythological spot that many people visit together with Takachiho Shrine.

takachiho_shrine.name: 高千穂神社

transit.name: 高千穂バスセンターから徒歩

takachiho_shrine.text: 高千穂神社は創建1900年余の歴史を持つ高千穂郷八十八社の総社で、国の重要文化財に指定された本殿は室町時代に造営されたものです。祭神は三毛入野命（みけぬのみこと）ほか神話に登場する神々で、高千穂の地を開拓した神として崇敬を集めています。境内には樹齢800年を超える夫婦杉があり、縁結びや夫婦円満のご利益で知られています。毎晩行われる「高千穂神楽（たかちほかぐら）」の奉納は国の重要無形民俗文化財で、岩戸神楽を起源とする33番の演目を夜通し奉納する伝統が1000年以上続いています。観光用として毎夜20時から1時間の夜神楽公演も行われており、日本神話の世界を体感できます。
takachiho_shrine.highlight: 創建1900年余の高千穂郷総社。毎夜奉納の高千穂神楽（国重要無形民俗文化財）
takachiho_shrine.highlight_en: Takachihogo Soja Shrine was founded over 1900 years ago. Takachiho Kagura dedicated every night (National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)
takachiho_shrine.text_en: Takachiho Shrine is the main shrine of the 88 shrines in Takachiho-go, which has a history of over 1,900 years.The main shrine, designated as a national important cultural property, was built during the Muromachi period. The deities enshrined are Mikenu no Mikoto and other gods who appear in mythology, and are revered as the gods who pioneered the land of Takachiho. There is a couple cedar tree in the precincts that is over 800 years old and is known for its blessings on matchmaking and marital harmony. The nightly dedication of Takachiho Kagura is a National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property, and the tradition of offering No. 33 throughout the night, which originated from Iwato Kagura, has continued for over 1,000 years. For sightseeing, night kagura performances are held every night from 8:00 pm for one hour, allowing you to experience the world of Japanese mythology.

miyazaki_jingu.name: 宮崎神宮
miyazaki_jingu.text: 宮崎神宮は初代天皇・神武天皇（じんむてんのう）を御祭神とする神社で、宮崎を代表する格式高い宮です。神武天皇はこの日向（ひゅうが）の地から東征を開始し、大和（やまと）で初代天皇として即位したとされており、宮崎は「神武天皇お膝元の地」として特別な意義を持ちます。広大な社叢に囲まれた荘厳な境内には、本殿・拝殿ほか多くの社殿が並び、明治時代に官幣大社として整備されました。毎年10月に行われる「神武さま（じんぶさま）」と親しまれる例大祭は宮崎最大の祭りで、神幸行列が市内を練り歩きます。日本建国の始まりの地として、全国から参拝者が訪れる宮崎の精神的シンボルです。
miyazaki_jingu.highlight: 初代天皇・神武天皇を祀る宮崎の総鎮守。東征出発の地として「日本建国の始まり」を体感
miyazaki_jingu.highlight_en: The general guardian of Miyazaki, where the first emperor, Emperor Jimmu, is enshrined. Experience the “beginning of the founding of Japan” as the starting point for the Eastern Expedition
miyazaki_jingu.text_en: Miyazaki Jingu is a shrine that enshrines the first emperor, Emperor Jinmu, and is one of the most prestigious shrines in Miyazaki. It is said that Emperor Jimmu began his eastern expedition from this land in Hyuga and ascended the throne as the first emperor in Yamato, and Miyazaki has a special significance as the ``place of Emperor Jimmu''. Surrounded by a vast shrine complex, the majestic precincts are lined with the main shrine, worship hall, and many other shrine buildings, and was developed as a Kanpei Taisha during the Meiji period. The annual festival affectionately known as "Jinbusama" is held every October and is Miyazaki's largest festival, with a procession of gods paraded through the city. As the birthplace of Japan's founding, it is a spiritual symbol of Miyazaki, which is visited by worshipers from all over the country.
