udo_shrine.name: 鵜戸神宮

transit.name: 宮崎駅からバス約1時間

udo_shrine.text: 鵜戸神宮は日向灘（ひゅうがなだ）に面した断崖絶壁の岩窟内に社殿が鎮座する珍しい形式の神社で、日本でも数少ない「下り参道」の神社として知られています。祭神は彦波瀲武鸕鷀草葺不合尊（ひこなぎさたけうがやふきあえずのみこと）で、神武天皇の父神にあたります。岩窟内に鎮座する朱塗りの社殿と、荒波打ち寄せる日向灘の景色が対照的な絶景を生み出しています。境内には亀石と呼ばれる岩があり、窪みに男性は左手、女性は右手で「運玉（うんだま）」と呼ばれる素焼きの丸い玉を投げ入れると願いが叶うとされます。太平洋を見渡す断崖の神社として、自然の雄大さと神聖さが融合した宮崎屈指のパワースポットです。
udo_shrine.highlight: 断崖絶壁の岩窟に鎮座する珍しい神社。運玉投げと日向灘の絶景が有名
udo_shrine.highlight_en: A rare shrine located in a rock cave on a cliff. Famous for its undama toss and the spectacular view of the Hyuga Sea.
udo_shrine.text_en: Udo Shrine is an unusual type of shrine, with its shrine building enshrined inside a rock cave on a cliff facing the Hyuga-nada Sea, and is known as one of the few shrines in Japan with a descending approach. The enshrined deity is Hikonagi Satake Ugaya Fukiaezu no Mikoto, who is the father god of Emperor Jimmu. The vermilion-painted shrine building nestled inside a rock cave and the view of Hyuga-nada Sea with rough waves create a spectacular contrasting view. There is a rock called Kameishi in the temple grounds, and it is said that if men throw a round unglazed ball called an undama into the hollow with their left hand (men) and right hand (women), their wishes will come true. As a shrine on a cliff overlooking the Pacific Ocean, it is one of Miyazaki's best power spots, where the majesty of nature and sacredness are fused.

aoshima_shrine.name: 青島神社
aoshima_shrine.text: 青島神社は周囲1.5キロの小島・青島全体が境内となっており、島そのものが国の特別天然記念物「亜熱帯性植物群落」に指定されています。島の周囲を取り囲む「鬼の洗濯板（おにのせんたくいた）」と呼ばれる奇岩群は波状岩（はじょうがん）と呼ばれる地質現象で、遠い昔の海底が隆起して形成されたものです。祭神は山幸彦（やまさちひこ）と豊玉姫（とよたまひめ）の夫婦神で、縁結び・安産のご利益で知られています。かつて一般人の立ち入りが禁じられた「禁足地（きんそくち）」であり、神聖な島として崇められてきました。宮崎のシンボル的存在として、青い海と亜熱帯植物に囲まれた神秘的な雰囲気が魅力の神社です。
aoshima_shrine.highlight: 亜熱帯植物に囲まれた島全体が境内の神社。「鬼の洗濯板」の奇岩群が見事（特別天然記念物）
aoshima_shrine.highlight_en: The entire island is a shrine surrounded by subtropical plants. The strangely shaped rocks of “Oni no Washita” are spectacular (Special Natural Monument)
aoshima_shrine.text_en: Aoshima Shrine's precincts cover the entirety of Aoshima, a small island with a circumference of 1.5 km, and the island itself has been designated as a special natural monument of the country as a ``subtropical plant community.'' The strange rock formations surrounding the island, known as Oni no Sentakuita, are a geological phenomenon known as wavy rocks, and were formed when the ocean floor rose up a long time ago. The deities enshrined are the married deities of Yamasachihiko and Toyotamahime, who are known for their blessings on matchmaking and safe childbirth. It was once a ``forbidden place'' where the general public was prohibited from entering, and was revered as a sacred island. As a symbol of Miyazaki, this shrine has a mysterious atmosphere surrounded by the blue sea and subtropical plants.

saito_kofun.name: 西都原古墳群
saito_kofun.kana: さいとばるこふんぐん
saito_kofun.text: 西都原古墳群は宮崎県西都市に広がる国内最大級の古墳群で、319基の古墳が国の特別史跡に指定されています。3世紀から7世紀にかけて造られた前方後円墳・円墳・方墳が丘陵地帯に密集しており、その規模と保存状態の良さから「日向の古代王国」の中心地として重要視されています。最大の古墳は全長219メートルの男狭穂塚（おさほづか）と全長180メートルの女狭穂塚（めさほづか）で、神武天皇の祖先にあたる神々の御陵と伝承されています。昭和初期の発掘調査以降、学術的な研究が進められており、隣接する「西都原考古博物館」では出土品の展示と古代日向の歴史を学べます。春の桜と菜の花が古墳を彩る景色は「さいとばる桜まつり」として親しまれています。
saito_kofun.highlight: 国内最大級319基の古墳群（国特別史跡）。「日向の古代王国」の中心地として3〜7世紀の謎を伝える
saito_kofun.highlight_en: A group of 319 ancient tombs, one of the largest in Japan (national special historic site). Conveying the mysteries of the 3rd to 7th centuries as the center of the "Ancient Kingdom of Hyuga"
saito_kofun.text_en: The Saitobaru Tumulus Cluster is one of the largest tumulus clusters in Japan, located in Saito City, Miyazaki Prefecture, and 319 tumuli have been designated as a special national historic site. Keyhole-shaped, round, and rectangular tombs built between the 3rd and 7th centuries are concentrated on a hilly area, and due to their size and well-preserved condition, they are regarded as important as the center of the ``Ancient Kingdom of Hyuga.'' The largest burial mounds are Osahozuka, which is 219 meters long, and Mesahozuka, which is 180 meters long, and is said to be the mausoleum of the gods who were the ancestors of Emperor Jinmu. Academic research has been underway since excavations in the early Showa period, and at the adjacent Saitobaru Archaeological Museum, you can see excavated artifacts on display and learn about the history of ancient Hyuga. The scenery of spring cherry blossoms and rape blossoms decorating the ancient tomb is popularly known as the Saitobaru Cherry Blossom Festival.

obi_castle.name: 飫肥城下町
obi_castle.text: 飫肥城下町は「九州の小京都」と称される宮崎県日南市の城下町で、江戸時代を通じて飫肥藩伊東氏5万1000石の城下として栄えました。大手門から続く石垣と白壁の武家屋敷群・商家が現在も保存されており、国の重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に選定されています。飫肥城は16世紀に伊東氏と島津氏が激しく争った要衝で、慶長5年（1600年）の関ヶ原の戦い後に伊東氏が安堵されて明治維新まで統治しました。城跡には大手門・松尾丸などが復元され、伊東家歴代の功績を伝える「旧本丸歴史館」も整備されています。名物の「飫肥天（おびてん）」（魚のすり身揚げ）や「厚焼き玉子」など、城下町グルメも人気を集めています。
obi_castle.highlight: 「九州の小京都」と称される江戸城下町（国重要伝統的建造物群保存地区）。石垣と白壁の武家屋敷群
obi_castle.highlight_en: Edo Castle Town (National Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings) is known as the "Little Kyoto of Kyushu." Samurai residences with stone walls and white walls
obi_castle.text_en: Obi Castle Town is a castle town in Nichinan City, Miyazaki Prefecture, known as the ``Little Kyoto of Kyushu.'' Throughout the Edo period, it prospered as the castle town of the Ito clan of the Obi Domain, which owned 51,000 koku. A group of samurai residences and merchant houses with stone walls and white walls that continue from the Otemon Gate are still preserved today, and have been selected as a nationally important preservation district for groups of traditional buildings. Obi Castle was a strategic point where the Ito clan and Shimazu clan fought fiercely in the 16th century, and after the Battle of Sekigahara in 1600, the Ito clan was relieved and ruled until the Meiji Restoration. The castle ruins include the Otemon Gate and Matsuo Maru, which have been restored, and the ``Old Honmaru History Museum,'' which tells about the achievements of successive generations of the Ito family, has also been maintained. Castle town gourmet foods such as the famous "Obiten" (fried minced fish) and "Atsuyaki omelet" are also gaining popularity.

hyuga_misaki.name: 馬ヶ背・日向岬
hyuga_misaki.kana: うまがせ・ひゅうがみさき
hyuga_misaki.text: 馬ヶ背は宮崎県日向市の日向岬にある断崖絶壁で、柱状節理の玄武岩が高さ70メートルにわたって垂直に切り立つ景観は「九州東海岸最大の断崖」と称されます。断崖の上に設けられた展望台からは太平洋の大海原が一望でき、柱状節理の岩壁が波に洗われる雄大な光景が広がります。近隣の「クルスの海」は2つの海食洞が十字（クルス＝ポルトガル語で十字）形に繋がっており、16世紀のキリスト教伝来との関連が伝えられています。日向市は日本書紀・古事記にも登場する日向（ひゅうが）の国の中心地であり、神武天皇東征の出発地・日向の国の歴史を今に伝える地域です。荒波と断崖の絶景は宮崎の自然美を代表する景勝地です。
hyuga_misaki.highlight: 高さ70メートルの柱状節理断崖「九州東海岸最大の断崖」。クルスの海の十字型海食洞も見事
hyuga_misaki.highlight_en: A columnar joint cliff with a height of 70 meters, "the largest cliff on the east coast of Kyushu". The cross-shaped sea caves in the Cruz Sea are also spectacular.
hyuga_misaki.text_en: Umagase is a sheer cliff located at Cape Hyuga, Hyuga City, Miyazaki Prefecture.The columnar jointed basalt cliffs rise vertically to a height of 70 meters, and it is said to be the ``largest cliff on the east coast of Kyushu.'' From the observation deck built on top of the cliff, you can see a panoramic view of the Pacific Ocean, and the magnificent sight of the columnar jointed rock walls being washed by the waves. The nearby "Sea of ​​Cruz" has two sea caves connected in the shape of a cross (cruz = cross in Portuguese), and is said to be connected to the introduction of Christianity in the 16th century. Hyuga City is the center of the country of Hyuga, which also appears in the Nihon Shoki and Kojiki, and is an area that still tells the history of the country of Hyuga, the starting point of Emperor Jimmu's eastern expedition. The spectacular view of the rough waves and cliffs is a scenic spot that represents the natural beauty of Miyazaki.

nobeoka_castle.name: 延岡城跡
nobeoka_castle.text: 延岡城は慶長8年（1603年）に高橋元種（たかはしもとたね）が築城した平山城で、後に有馬氏が入封し「千人殺し」の石垣で知られます。この石垣は積み上げた石が抜けると一度に千人が圧死するほどの規模という意味合いで命名された巨大な野面積みの石垣で、高さ22メートルを誇ります。城山公園として整備された現在の城跡には三の丸・二の丸・本丸の石垣が残り、天守台からは五ヶ瀬川と日向灘が一望できます。江戸時代の延岡は日向国北部の中心として内藤氏が7万石の城下町を形成し、商工業が発達しました。城下の商人文化を今に伝える「延岡大師祭（おおしまつり）」は毎年4月に開催される県内最大級の祭りです。
nobeoka_castle.highlight: 「千人殺し」と呼ばれる高さ22メートルの壮大な石垣が圧巻。五ヶ瀬川と日向灘を一望
nobeoka_castle.highlight_en: The majestic 22-meter-high stone wall, known as the ``thousand killers,'' is a sight to behold. A panoramic view of the Gokase River and the Hyuga-nada Sea
nobeoka_castle.text_en: Nobeoka Castle is a Hirayama castle built by Motane Takahashi in 1603, and later occupied by the Arima clan, and is known for its stone walls that were said to have killed a thousand people. This stone wall is 22 meters high and has the appearance of a huge field area, and was named because of the scale of the stone wall, which could crush 1,000 people to death if it fell through. The stone walls of Sannomaru, Ninomaru, and Honmaru remain at the current castle ruins, which have been developed as Shiroyama Park, and you can see the Gokase River and Hyuga-nada Sea from the castle tower. During the Edo period, Nobeoka was the center of northern Hyuga Province, where the Naito clan built a castle town with a capital of 70,000 koku, and commerce and industry developed. The Nobeoka Daishi Festival (Oshima Festival) is one of the prefecture's largest festivals, and is held every April, preserving the merchant culture of the castle area.

miyakonojo_shimazu.name: 都城島津伝承館
miyakonojo_shimazu.kana: みやこのじょうしまづでんしょうかん
miyakonojo_shimazu.text: 都城島津伝承館は島津氏発祥の地・都城にある歴史資料館で、宮崎県都城市が運営しています。島津氏の始祖・島津忠久（しまづただひさ）は鎌倉時代初期に薩摩・大隅・日向三国の守護に任じられ、都城はその所領の一つとして発展しました。都城島津家は薩摩の本家・島津宗家から分かれた支藩で、江戸時代を通じて独自の武家文化を育みました。伝承館では都城島津家の甲冑・刀剣・古文書などの文化財を展示しており、島津一族の歴史と宮崎の武家文化を学べます。都城は「都城大弓（みやこのじょうおおゆみ）」の産地としても名高く、国内生産シェアの約80%を占める伝統工芸品として知られています。
miyakonojo_shimazu.highlight: 島津氏発祥の地・都城の歴史資料館。鎌倉時代から続く都城島津家の甲冑・刀剣を展示
miyakonojo_shimazu.highlight_en: A historical museum in Miyakonojo, the birthplace of the Shimazu clan. Exhibits the armor and swords of the Miyakonojo Shimazu family that have been around since the Kamakura period
miyakonojo_shimazu.text_en: Miyakonojo Shimazu Denshokan is a historical museum located in Miyakonojo, the birthplace of the Shimazu clan, and is operated by Miyakonojo City, Miyazaki Prefecture. Tadahisa Shimazu, the founder of the Shimazu clan, was appointed the guardian of the three provinces of Satsuma, Osumi, and Hyuga in the early Kamakura period, and Miyakonojo developed as one of his territories. The Miyakonojo Shimazu family was a branch domain that branched off from the main family of Satsuma, the Shimazu family, and cultivated a unique samurai culture throughout the Edo period. The folklore museum exhibits cultural assets such as armor, swords, and ancient documents from the Miyakonojo Shimazu clan, allowing you to learn about the history of the Shimazu clan and the samurai culture of Miyazaki. Miyakonojo is also famous as the production area for the Miyakonojo Great Bow, a traditional craft that accounts for approximately 80% of the domestic production share.

kushima_toi.name: 都井岬
kushima_toi.text: 都井岬は宮崎県串間市の太平洋に突き出た岬で、岬全体が国の天然記念物「都井岬の野生馬（御崎馬）」の生息地として保護されています。御崎馬（みさきうま）は江戸時代初期に薩摩藩が放牧した馬が野生化したもので、現在約100頭が岬の草原を自由に闊歩しています。日本在来馬の一種として貴重な存在であり、人間を恐れず間近で観察できることが大きな魅力です。岬の灯台（都井岬灯台）からは日向灘の大海原と馬の群れが同時に眺められ、他では見られない独特の景観が広がります。春には桜と野生馬、夏には緑の草原と海の青さのコントラストが美しく、宮崎の秘境的な観光スポットとして人気を集めています。
kushima_toi.highlight: 江戸時代から野生化した「御崎馬」約100頭が草原を闊歩（国天然記念物）。灯台からの絶景も必見
kushima_toi.highlight_en: Approximately 100 Misaki horses, which have become wild since the Edo period, roam the grasslands (a national natural monument). The spectacular view from the lighthouse is also a must-see
kushima_toi.text_en: Cape Toi is a cape that juts out into the Pacific Ocean in Kushima City, Miyazaki Prefecture, and the entire cape is protected as the habitat of the national natural monument, the Cape Toi Wild Horse (Misaki Horse). Misaki horses are wild horses that were grazed by the Satsuma clan in the early Edo period, and currently about 100 of them roam freely on the grasslands of the cape. They are a valuable species of horse native to Japan, and their great appeal is that they are not afraid of humans and can be observed up close. From the lighthouse on the cape (Cape Toimisaki Lighthouse), you can see the vast ocean of the Hyuga Sea and the herd of horses at the same time, creating a unique landscape that cannot be seen anywhere else. The beautiful contrast between cherry blossoms and wild horses in the spring, and the green grassland and blue sea in the summer has made it popular as an unexplored tourist spot in Miyazaki.

heguri_shrine.name: 江田神社・みそぎ池
heguri_shrine.kana: えだじんじゃ・みそぎいけ
heguri_shrine.text: 江田神社はイザナギノミコトが黄泉の国（死者の世界）から戻り、禊（みそぎ）を行ったとされる「みそぎ池」に隣接する古社です。日本神話において禊（みそぎ）は最も重要な清めの儀式の一つで、この場所でイザナギが禊を行ったことで天照大神・月読命・スサノオの三貴神が誕生したとされます。神社の境内には江戸時代に整備された「みそぎ池」が現存しており、日本神話の重要な場面の舞台として全国の神話ファンや参拝者が訪れます。境内は緑豊かな鎮守の森に囲まれており、静寂な雰囲気の中で神話の世界に思いを馳せることができます。宮崎市内からアクセスしやすく、神武天皇ゆかりの宮崎神宮と合わせて「神話巡り」として訪れる人が多い神社です。
heguri_shrine.highlight: イザナギが禊を行い三貴神が誕生した場所。「みそぎ池」が現存する日本神話最重要スポットの一つ
heguri_shrine.highlight_en: The place where Izanagi performed purification and the Three Noble Gods were born. "Misogi Pond" is one of the most important spots in Japanese mythology that still exists.
heguri_shrine.text_en: Eda Shrine is an old shrine adjacent to Misogi Pond, where Izanagi no Mikoto is said to have returned from the land of the dead (the world of the dead) and performed misogi. In Japanese mythology, misogi is one of the most important purification rituals, and it is said that when Izanagi performed purification at this place, the three noble gods Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, and Susanoo were born. The Misogi Pond, which was maintained in the Edo period, still exists within the grounds of the shrine, and is visited by myth fans and worshipers from all over the country as it is the setting for important scenes in Japanese mythology. The precincts are surrounded by a lush green guardian forest, allowing you to imagine the world of mythology in a tranquil atmosphere. It is easily accessible from Miyazaki City, and many people visit this shrine along with Miyazaki Shrine, which is connected to Emperor Jimmu, as part of their ``mythology tour''.

tsuma_shrine.name: 都萬神社

transit.name: 西都市バスセンターから徒歩

tsuma_shrine.text: 都萬神社は日向国一宮（ひゅうがのくにいちのみや）として古代から格式高い神社で、祭神は木花開耶姫命（このはなさくやひめのみこと）です。木花開耶姫は富士山の神・浅間大社の主祭神としても有名で、その美しさと豊穣・安産のご利益で知られています。境内は西都原古墳群に隣接しており、古代の日向国の政治・宗教の中心地として機能していたと考えられています。延喜式（えんぎしき）に記された式内社（しきないしゃ）であり、平安時代から国家の重要な神社として位置付けられていました。西都市の桜の名所としても知られており、春には境内が桜の花に彩られます。古墳群と一宮を合わせて訪れることで、日向古代王国の歴史を深く体感できます。
tsuma_shrine.highlight: 日向国一宮・木花開耶姫を祀る古社。隣接する西都原古墳群と合わせて古代日向の歴史を体感
tsuma_shrine.highlight_en: An old shrine dedicated to Konohana Sayahime of Ichinomiya, Hyuga Province. Experience the history of ancient Hyuga with the adjacent Saitobaru Tumulus Group
tsuma_shrine.text_en: Tsuman Shrine has been a high-class shrine since ancient times as Hyuga no Kuni Ichinomiya, and its enshrined deity is Konohanasakuyahime no Mikoto. Konohana Sayahime is also famous as the deity of Mt. Fuji and the main enshrined deity of Sengen Taisha Shrine, and is known for her beauty and blessings for fertility and safe childbirth. The precincts are adjacent to the Saitobaru Tumulus Group, and are thought to have functioned as the political and religious center of the ancient Hyuga country. It is a Shikinaisha shrine written in the Engishiki, and has been positioned as an important shrine of the nation since the Heian period. It is also known as a famous cherry blossom viewing spot in Saito City, and the precincts are decorated with cherry blossoms in spring. By visiting the ancient tombs and Ichinomiya together, you can deeply experience the history of the ancient kingdom of Hyuga.

ebino_kogen.name: えびの高原

transit.name: えびのICからバスまたはタクシー

ebino_kogen.text: えびの高原は宮崎県えびの市に位置する霧島山系の高原で、標高約1200メートルに広がる火山性の高原景観が特徴です。霧島・錦江湾国立公園に含まれ、韓国岳（からくにだけ・1700メートル）をはじめとする霧島連山の登山基地となっています。高原には硫黄山・不動池・六観音御池・白紫池など複数の火口湖が点在し、コバルトブルーの湖面と草原が織り成す景色は「霧島の宝石」とも呼ばれます。古来、霧島山は神が降臨した山として崇敬され、ニニギノミコト（瓊瓊杵尊）が天孫降臨した「高千穂の峰」としての伝承を持ちます。秋にはノリウツギやススキが高原を彩り、冬には霧氷や積雪が見られ四季折々の絶景が楽しめます。
ebino_kogen.highlight: 霧島連山に広がる標高1200mの高原。天孫降臨の地・霧島山を望む火口湖群「霧島の宝石」
ebino_kogen.highlight_en: A plateau at an altitude of 1200m that spreads across the Kirishima Mountain Range. ``The Jewel of Kirishima'' is a group of crater lakes overlooking Mt. Kirishima, the place where the descendants of the gods descended.
ebino_kogen.text_en: Ebino Plateau is a plateau in the Kirishima Mountains located in Ebino City, Miyazaki Prefecture, and is characterized by a volcanic plateau landscape that stretches approximately 1,200 meters above sea level. It is included in the Kirishima-Kinkowan National Park and serves as a climbing base for the Kirishima Mountain Range, including Mt. Karakuni (1,700 meters). The plateau is dotted with multiple crater lakes, including Mt. Ioyama, Fudoike, Rokukannon Oike, and Byakushiike, and the scenery of the cobalt blue lake surface and grassland is also called the ``Jewel of Kirishima.'' Since ancient times, Mt. Kirishima has been revered as the mountain where the gods descended, and there is a legend that it is the ``Takachiho peak'' where Ninigi no Mikoto (Kioni no Mikoto) descended. In autumn, the plateau is colored by Noritsugi and pampas grass, and in winter, you can see hoarfrost and snowfall, so you can enjoy the spectacular scenery in each season.

nango_baekje.name: 南郷・百済の里
nango_baekje.kana: なんごう・くだらのさと
nango_baekje.text: 南郷百済の里は宮崎県美郷町南郷区にあり、朝鮮半島の百済（くだら）王国滅亡（660年）の際に日向の国に亡命した百済王族・禎嘉王（ていかおう）と神助（じんじょ）親子を祀る「西の正倉院」や百済王伝説を伝える地域です。禎嘉王は唐・新羅の連合軍に攻められた百済から逃れ、海を渡って日向の南郷に上陸したとされ、現地の人々に温かく迎えられたと伝わります。毎年10月には「百済の里秋まつり」が開催され、韓国の芸能団も参加する日韓交流の場となっています。「西の正倉院」には百済王族ゆかりの宝物が収蔵されており、日本と朝鮮半島の古代交流の証として貴重な史料を展示しています。アジア最東端に残る百済文化の遺産として、学術的にも高い評価を受けています。
nango_baekje.highlight: 660年・百済滅亡で亡命した百済王族を祀る地。「西の正倉院」が日韓古代交流の証を収蔵
nango_baekje.highlight_en: A place to enshrine the Baekje royal family who went into exile after the fall of Baekje in 660. “Western Shosoin” houses evidence of ancient exchanges between Japan and Korea
nango_baekje.text_en: Nango Baekje no Sato is located in Nango Ward, Misato Town, Miyazaki Prefecture, and is an area where the legend of the King of Baekje is told, as well as the ``West Shosoin'', which enshrines Teikaou and Jinjo, a father and son of the Baekje royal family who defected to Hyuga Province during the fall of the Kudara Kingdom on the Korean Peninsula (660). It is said that King Teika fled Baekje, which was attacked by the combined forces of Tang and Silla, crossed the sea and landed in Nango, Hyuga, where he was warmly welcomed by the local people. The Baekje no Sato Autumn Festival is held every October, and has become a venue for Japan-Korea exchanges, with Korean entertainment groups also participating. The West Shosoin Temple houses treasures related to the Baekje royal family, and valuable historical materials are on display as evidence of ancient exchanges between Japan and the Korean Peninsula. It has been highly evaluated academically as a heritage of Baekje culture that remains at the easternmost tip of Asia.

heiwadai_park.name: 平和台公園・八紘一宇の塔
heiwadai_park.kana: へいわだいこうえん・はっこういちうのとう
heiwadai_park.text: 平和台公園にそびえる「八紘一宇の塔（はっこういちうのとう）」は、昭和15年（1940年）に皇紀2600年を記念して建設された高さ36.4メートルの石塔です。「八紘一宇」とは「八紘（世界）を一つの家（宇）とする」という意味で、当初は日本の対外膨張主義のスローガンとして用いられました。終戦後GHQにより「平和の塔」と改称され、現在は平和のシンボルとして親しまれています。塔身には全国から集められた戦地や内地の石が埋め込まれており、四隅には武人像が据えられています。宮崎市街と日向灘を見渡せる丘の上に立つ巨大な石塔は、近代日本の歴史の複雑さを今に伝える歴史的建造物です。塔の周辺は「こどもの国」として整備された公園になっています。
heiwadai_park.highlight: 皇紀2600年記念に建設された高さ36.4mの石塔。近代日本の歴史の複雑さを象徴する「平和の塔」
heiwadai_park.highlight_en: A 36.4m tall stone pagoda built to commemorate the 2600th anniversary of the Imperial era. The ``Peace Tower'' symbolizes the complexity of modern Japanese history.
heiwadai_park.text_en: The Hakko Ichiu Tower towering over Heiwadai Park is a 36.4 meter tall stone pagoda built in 1940 to commemorate the 2600th anniversary of the Imperial era. ``Hakko Ichiu'' means ``to make Hakko (the world) one home (u),'' and was originally used as a slogan for Japan's overseas expansionism. After the war, it was renamed "Peace Tower" by GHQ and is now a familiar symbol of peace. The pagoda's body is filled with stones from battlefields and inland areas collected from all over the country, and statues of warriors are placed in the four corners. The huge stone pagoda that stands on top of a hill overlooking Miyazaki city and the Hyuga Sea is a historical building that conveys the complexity of modern Japan's history. The area around the tower is a park maintained as a ``Kodomo no Kuni'' (Kodomo no Kuni).

hososhima_port.name: 細島・古代の港
hososhima_port.kana: ほそしま・こだいのみなと
hososhima_port.text: 細島（ほそしま）は宮崎県日向市の東端に位置する港町で、古代から「ひゅうが」の海上交通の要衝として機能してきました。古事記・日本書紀には「吾平津媛（あひらつひめ）の故地」として登場し、神武天皇の妃の出身地とされています。江戸時代には日向国の重要な商業港として繁栄し、大坂・上方と結ぶ「北前船（きたまえぶね）」の寄港地として商業的に発展しました。細島灯台（1873年建設）は九州最古の洋式灯台の一つであり、明治時代の近代化を象徴する建造物として今も現役で機能しています。「細島商人」と呼ばれた商人たちが活躍した江戸時代の繁栄の跡が、古い商家や倉庫建築に残っています。日向国の海上交流の歴史を伝える宮崎の知られざる歴史港湾都市です。
hososhima_port.highlight: 古代から江戸時代まで日向国の要衝だった港町。九州最古級の洋式灯台（1873年）が現役稼働
hososhima_port.highlight_en: A port town that was a key hub in Hyuga Province from ancient times to the Edo period. The oldest Western-style lighthouse in Kyushu (built in 1873) is in active operation.
hososhima_port.text_en: Hososhima is a port town located at the eastern end of Hyuga City, Miyazaki Prefecture, and has functioned as a key point for maritime transportation since ancient times. It appears in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki as ``the birthplace of Ahiratsuhime,'' and is said to be the birthplace of Emperor Jimmu's wife. During the Edo period, it flourished as an important commercial port in Hyuga Province, and developed commercially as a port of call for the Kitamaebune, which connected Osaka and Kamigata. Hososhima Lighthouse (built in 1873) is one of the oldest Western-style lighthouses in Kyushu, and is still functioning today as a symbol of modernization during the Meiji era. Traces of the prosperity of the Edo period, when merchants known as "Hososhima merchants" were active, can be seen in the old merchant houses and warehouse buildings. This is a little-known historical port city in Miyazaki that tells the history of maritime exchanges in Hyuga country.

sadowara_castle.name: 佐土原城跡
sadowara_castle.text: 佐土原城は室町時代後期から江戸時代まで存在した山城で、戦国時代には島津氏の日向国支配の重要拠点として機能しました。島津氏の庶流・佐土原島津家の居城として江戸時代には1万石の小藩として存続しました。織田信長・豊臣秀吉の時代にこの地を統治した島津以久（しまづもちひさ）は、朝鮮出兵（文禄・慶長の役）にも参加した武将です。城跡は現在公園として整備されており、本丸跡から復元された「鶴松館（つるまつかん）」は佐土原島津家の歴史を伝える資料館になっています。近隣の「佐土原人形」は江戸時代に島津家の庇護を受けて発展した伝統工芸品で、宮崎を代表する郷土玩具として知られています。
sadowara_castle.highlight: 島津氏の日向支配の拠点・佐土原島津家の居城跡。江戸時代の「佐土原人形」の産地としても有名
sadowara_castle.highlight_en: The ruins of the castle of the Sadowara Shimazu family, the base of the Shimazu clan's control over Hyuga. Famous as the production area for "Sadowara dolls" from the Edo period
sadowara_castle.text_en: Sadowara Castle was a mountain castle that existed from the late Muromachi period to the Edo period, and during the Sengoku period it functioned as an important base for the Shimazu clan's control of Hyuga Province. It was the residence of the Sadowara Shimazu family, an offshoot of the Shimazu clan, and continued as a small domain of 10,000 koku during the Edo period. Shimazu Mochihisa, who ruled this area during the era of Oda Nobunaga and Toyotomi Hideyoshi, was a military commander who also participated in the invasion of Korea (Bunroku and Keicho War). The castle ruins are currently being maintained as a park, and the ``Tsurumatsukan'', which was restored from the main castle ruins, is now a museum that tells the history of the Sadowara Shimazu family. The nearby "Sadowara dolls" are a traditional craft that developed under the patronage of the Shimazu family during the Edo period, and are known as Miyazaki's representative local toys.

kirishima_higashi.name: 霧島東神社
kirishima_higashi.kana: きりしまひがしじんじゃ

transit.name: 高原駅からタクシー約15分

kirishima_higashi.text: 霧島東神社は宮崎県高原町に鎮座する古社で、天孫降臨（てんそんこうりん）の神・ニニギノミコト（瓊瓊杵尊）を主祭神とします。霧島山の東麓に位置し、霧島六社（きりしまろくしゃ）の一つとして古代から崇敬を集めてきました。創建は6世紀頃と伝わり、霧島山を御神体として仰ぐ山岳信仰の神社です。鎌倉時代には源頼朝からの崇敬を受け、江戸時代には薩摩藩主・島津家の庇護のもとで社殿が整備されました。境内には樹齢数百年の杉の巨木が立ち並び、霧島の霊気に包まれた神秘的な雰囲気を持ちます。霧島山を背景に広がる荘厳な景色は、天孫降臨の伝説の舞台に相応しい神聖な空間を形成しています。隣県・鹿児島の霧島神宮と合わせて「霧島詣で」として参拝する信者も多い古社です。
kirishima_higashi.highlight: 天孫降臨の神・ニニギノミコトを祀る霧島六社の一社。霧島山を御神体とする古代山岳信仰の神社
kirishima_higashi.highlight_en: One of Kirishima's six shrines that enshrines Ninigi no Mikoto, the god of the descendants of heaven. An ancient mountain worshiping shrine whose deity is Mt. Kirishima.
kirishima_higashi.text_en: Kirishima Higashi Shrine is an old shrine located in Takahara Town, Miyazaki Prefecture, and its main deity is Ninigi-no-Mikoto, the god of the descent of the descendants of the descendants of the descendants of heaven. Located at the eastern foot of Mt. Kirishima, it has been revered since ancient times as one of the six Kirishima shrines. It is said to have been founded around the 6th century, and is a mountain worshiping shrine that worships Mt. Kirishima as its object of worship. In the Kamakura period, it was revered by Minamoto no Yoritomo, and in the Edo period, the shrine was built under the patronage of the Shimazu family, the lords of the Satsuma domain. The grounds are lined with huge cedar trees that are hundreds of years old, giving it a mystical atmosphere filled with the spirit of Kirishima. The majestic scenery with Mt. Kirishima in the background forms a sacred space suitable for the legendary setting of the descendants of the gods. It is an old shrine that many believers visit together with Kirishima Shrine in the neighboring prefecture of Kagoshima on a ``Kirishima pilgrimage''.

yoshinogari.name: 吉野ヶ里遺跡
yoshinogari.era: 弥生時代（紀元前5世紀〜3世紀）

transit.name: JR長崎本線「吉野ヶ里公園駅」

yoshinogari.text: 吉野ヶ里遺跡は佐賀県神埼市・吉野ヶ里町にまたがる国内最大規模の弥生時代の環濠集落跡で、国の特別史跡に指定されています。紀元前5世紀頃から7世紀にわたって人々が生活した痕跡が残り、最盛期には約5000人が居住していたと推定されています。2重・3重に巡らされた環濠（かんごう）・城柵（きさく）と、見張り台・物見やぐらが防衛拠点としての集落の姿を今に伝えます。日本書紀・魏志倭人伝に登場する「邪馬台国（やまたいこく）」との関連性を示す遺物が多数発見されており、古代史研究において重要な位置を占めています。復元整備された弥生人の住居・高床式倉庫・祭殿などが広大な公園内に立ち並び、弥生時代の集落生活を体感できます。
yoshinogari.highlight: 国内最大の弥生時代環濠集落（国特別史跡）。邪馬台国との関連が指摘される古代史の宝庫
yoshinogari.highlight_en: The largest Yayoi era moated village in Japan (national special historic site). A treasure trove of ancient history that has been linked to Yamataikoku
yoshinogari.text_en: The Yoshinogari ruins are the largest Yayoi period moated settlement site in Japan, spanning Kanzaki City and Yoshinogari Town, Saga Prefecture, and are designated as a special national historic site. There are traces of people living there from around the 5th century BC to the 7th century, and it is estimated that about 5,000 people lived there at its peak. The double and triple moats and castle fences, as well as the lookout tower and watchtower, give us a glimpse of the village as a defense base. Many artifacts have been discovered that show a connection to Yamataikoku, which appears in the Nihon Shoki and Gishi Wajinden, and it occupies an important place in ancient history research. Restored Yayoi residences, elevated warehouses, and shrines are lined up in the vast park, allowing you to experience village life in the Yayoi period.

saga_castle.name: 佐賀城本丸歴史館
saga_castle.kana: さがじょうほんまるれきしかん
saga_castle.text: 佐賀城は慶長12年（1607年）に佐賀藩初代藩主・鍋島直茂（なべしまなおしげ）が築城した城で、36万石の城下として発展しました。本丸御殿の一部が復元・整備された「佐賀城本丸歴史館」は、鍋島藩の歴史と幕末佐賀藩の近代化を学べる施設です。佐賀藩は幕末に国内初の洋式船・蒸気船の建造や反射炉の設置など積極的な西洋技術の導入を進め、「七賢人（ななけんじん）」と呼ばれる維新の志士を多数輩出しました。大隈重信・江藤新平・島義勇など、明治維新後の日本の政治・制度設計に大きな影響を与えた人物たちが佐賀から生まれています。武士道の書「葉隠（はがくれ）」の精神を受け継ぐ佐賀藩の独自の文化は、近代日本の礎となりました。
saga_castle.highlight: 36万石の鍋島藩の城。大隈重信ら「七賢人」を輩出した幕末近代化の先進藩の歴史を学べる
saga_castle.highlight_en: The castle of the Nabeshima clan, worth 360,000 koku. Learn about the history of the advanced modernizing domain at the end of the Edo period, which produced Shigenobu Okuma and other "Seven Sages"
saga_castle.text_en: Saga Castle was built in 1607 by Nabeshima Naoshige, the first lord of the Saga domain, and developed into a castle with an estate of 360,000 koku. The Saga Castle Honmaru History Museum, where part of the Honmaru Palace has been restored and maintained, is a facility where you can learn about the history of the Nabeshima clan and the modernization of the Saga clan at the end of the Edo period. At the end of the Edo period, the Saga Domain actively introduced Western technology, such as building Japan's first Western-style ships and steamships and installing reverberatory furnaces, and produced many Meiji Restoration patriots known as the ``Seven Wise Men.'' Saga is home to many people who had a great influence on Japan's politics and institutional design after the Meiji Restoration, such as Shigenobu Okuma, Shinpei Eto, and Yoshiyu Shima. The unique culture of the Saga domain, which inherited the spirit of the Bushido calligraphy Hagakure, became the foundation of modern Japan.

karatsu_castle.name: 唐津城
karatsu_castle.text: 唐津城は慶長7年（1602年）に寺沢広高（てらざわひろたか）が関ヶ原の戦いの論功行賞として唐津藩12万石を与えられ、慶長13年（1608年）に完成した平山城です。舞鶴城（まいづるじょう）とも呼ばれ、海に突き出た丘陵に建つ天守閣と、海岸線に続く「虹の松原（にじのまつばら）」が一体となった景観は「唐津城のハマボウ」として名高く、日本百名城の一つに選定されています。現在の天守は昭和41年（1966年）に復元されたもので、内部は歴代藩主の遺品・甲冑・陶磁器などを展示する資料館になっています。唐津は対馬（つしま）・壱岐（いき）へのゲートウェイとして古代から大陸交易の拠点であり、「玄界灘（げんかいなだ）の表玄関」として繁栄しました。
karatsu_castle.highlight: 「舞鶴城」の別名を持つ海城。虹の松原と一体の絶景（日本百名城）、大陸交易の拠点として栄えた
karatsu_castle.highlight_en: Kaijo is also known as "Maizuru Castle". Spectacular scenery with rainbow pine forest (one of Japan's top 100 castles), prospered as a base for continental trade
karatsu_castle.text_en: Karatsu Castle is a Hirayama Castle that was completed in 1608, after being awarded 120,000 koku by the Karatsu domain to Hirotaka Terazawa in 1602 as an award for his deeds during the Battle of Sekigahara. Also known as Maizuru Castle, the castle tower built on a hill that juts out into the sea, and the rainbow pine forest that stretches along the coastline combine to create a landscape that is famous as the ``Hamabou of Karatsu Castle'' and has been selected as one of Japan's 100 Famous Castles. The current castle tower was restored in 1966, and the interior is now a museum displaying the belongings, armor, and ceramics of successive feudal lords. Karatsu has been a hub for continental trade since ancient times as a gateway to Tsushima and Iki, and flourished as the ``main entrance to the Genkai Sea.''

nagoya_castle_saga.name: 名護屋城跡
nagoya_castle_saga.text: 名護屋城は豊臣秀吉が文禄・慶長の役（1592〜1598年）の朝鮮出兵拠点として肥前（佐賀）の松浦半島先端に築いた城です。わずか5ヶ月という超短期間で完成した城は大坂城に次ぐ規模を誇り、最盛期には20万人以上の兵士と全国の大名が集結しました。秀吉はここに約3年間逗留し、当時の城下は「西の大坂」とも呼ばれる繁栄を誇りました。秀吉の死後は解体され、現在は石垣が広大な範囲で残るのみですが、国の特別史跡に指定されています。隣接する「佐賀県立名護屋城博物館」では出兵の経緯と当時の日明朝（日本・明・朝鮮）の交流を詳細に展示しており、日韓の歴史的関係を学ぶ上で重要な施設となっています。
nagoya_castle_saga.highlight: 豊臣秀吉が朝鮮出兵のために5ヶ月で築いた超巨大城（国特別史跡）。最大20万人が集結した「西の大坂」
nagoya_castle_saga.highlight_en: A gigantic castle (national special historic site) built by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in five months to send troops to Korea. “Osaka of the West” where up to 200,000 people gathered
nagoya_castle_saga.text_en: Nagoya Castle was built by Toyotomi Hideyoshi at the tip of the Matsuura Peninsula in Hizen (Saga) as a base for dispatching troops to Korea during the Bunroku-Keicho War (1592-1598). The castle, which was completed in an extremely short period of just five months, was the second largest castle after Osaka Castle, and at its peak attracted over 200,000 soldiers and feudal lords from all over the country. Hideyoshi stayed here for about three years, and at that time the castle town was so prosperous that it was also called the ``Osaka of the West.'' It was dismantled after Hideyoshi's death, and now only a vast area of ​​stone walls remains, but it has been designated as a special national historic site. The adjacent Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum exhibits detailed information on the history of the dispatch of troops and the exchanges between Japan and the Ming Dynasty (Japan, Ming, and Korea) at the time, making it an important facility for learning about the historical relationship between Japan and Korea.

arita_porcelain_town.name: 有田・磁器発祥の地
arita_porcelain_town.kana: ありた・じきはっしょうのち
arita_porcelain_town.text: 有田は日本における磁器（じき）発祥の地として知られ、慶長17年（1612年）頃に朝鮮人陶工・李参平（りさんぺい）が泉山（いずみやま）で磁器原料の白磁鉱を発見し、日本初の磁器を焼いたことで始まりました。江戸時代には佐賀藩（鍋島藩）の保護のもとで磁器生産が発展し、17世紀後半には長崎・出島を通じてヨーロッパへ輸出される「伊万里焼（いまりやき）」として世界に名を馳せました。ヨーロッパの名窯・マイセンやデルフト陶器に多大な影響を与えた有田焼は、現在も400年の伝統を受け継ぐ日本を代表する陶磁器です。有田の町並みは江戸時代の陶磁器商の蔵屋敷が並ぶ「内山地区」が国の重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に選定されています。
arita_porcelain_town.highlight: 1612年に日本初の磁器が誕生した地。ヨーロッパの陶磁器文化に革命をもたらした伊万里焼の故郷
arita_porcelain_town.highlight_en: The place where Japan's first porcelain was born in 1612. The birthplace of Imari ware, which revolutionized European ceramic culture.
arita_porcelain_town.text_en: Arita is known as the birthplace of porcelain in Japan, and it began around 1612 when Korean potter Ri Sanpei discovered white porcelain, a raw material for porcelain, in Izumiyama and fired Japan's first porcelain. During the Edo period, porcelain production developed under the protection of the Saga domain (Nabeshima domain), and in the late 17th century, it gained worldwide fame as "Imari ware," which was exported to Europe via Nagasaki and Dejima. Arita ware, which had a great influence on the famous European kilns Meissen and Delft pottery, is a representative ceramic of Japan that continues to carry on a 400-year-old tradition. The Uchiyama district of Arita, which is lined with warehouses of ceramic merchants from the Edo period, has been selected as a nationally important preservation district for groups of traditional buildings.

yobuko_asaichi.name: 呼子の朝市と海の歴史
yobuko_asaichi.kana: よぶこのあさいちとうみのれきし
yobuko_asaichi.text: 呼子（よぶこ）は佐賀県唐津市の松浦半島北端に位置する小さな漁港の町で、「日本三大朝市」の一つとして全国に名が知れています。江戸時代から玄界灘の豊かな海産物の集積地として栄え、特に壱岐（いき）・対馬（つしま）との海上交易の要衝として機能してきました。呼子のイカは新鮮さと品質の高さで特に名高く、活き造りの透明なイカの姿が名物となっています。朝市通りには毎朝地元の漁師や農家が新鮮な海産物・農産物を並べ、その歴史は100年以上続いています。近隣の加部島（かべじま）には「田島神社（たじまじんじゃ）」があり、対馬・壱岐とともに「玄界三島」の航海安全の守護神として古代から崇敬されてきました。
yobuko_asaichi.highlight: 日本三大朝市の一つ・呼子。江戸時代から壱岐・対馬との海上交易で栄えた玄界灘の要衝
yobuko_asaichi.name_en: Yobuko morning market and history of the sea
yobuko_asaichi.highlight_en: Yobuko is one of Japan's three major morning markets. A strategic point in the Genkai Sea that has prospered through maritime trade with Iki and Tsushima since the Edo period.
yobuko_asaichi.text_en: Yobuko is a small fishing port town located at the northern tip of the Matsuura Peninsula in Karatsu City, Saga Prefecture, and is known throughout the country as one of Japan's three major morning markets. Since the Edo period, the area has prospered as a gathering place for the rich seafood of the Genkai Sea, and has functioned as a key point for maritime trade, especially with Iki and Tsushima. Yobuko's squid is particularly famous for its freshness and high quality, and its transparent live squid is a specialty. Local fishermen and farmers display fresh seafood and agricultural products on Morning Market Street every morning, and this has been going on for over 100 years. Nearby Kabe Island is home to Tajima Shrine, which has been revered since ancient times as the guardian deity of the Genkai Three Islands, along with Tsushima and Iki.

yutoku_inari.name: 祐徳稲荷神社
yutoku_inari.kana: ゆうとくいなりじんじゃ
yutoku_inari.text: 祐徳稲荷神社は伏見稲荷・笠間稲荷と並ぶ「日本三大稲荷」の一社で、年間300万人以上が参拝する九州を代表する神社です。貞享4年（1687年）に鹿島藩主・鍋島直朝の夫人・惟宗院（いそうのいん）が創建し、稲荷大神・大宮売大神・猿田彦大神を主祭神として衣食住・産業の守護神として信仰されています。断崖絶壁に建てられた朱塗りの楼門・拝殿・本殿が重なり合い、京都の清水寺を思わせる懸造り（かけづくり）の建築様式が壮観です。奥の院まで続く稲荷山には無数の鳥居と石燈籠が並び、山全体が神域となっています。商売繁盛・五穀豊穣・縁結びなどのご利益で知られ、佐賀を代表する聖地として古くから多くの参拝者が訪れます。
yutoku_inari.highlight: 日本三大稲荷の一社。断崖に建つ朱塗りの懸造り社殿が壮観。年間300万人が参拝する九州最大の稲荷社
yutoku_inari.highlight_en: One of Japan's three major Inari companies. The vermilion-painted hanging structure of the shrine built on the cliff is spectacular. The largest Inari shrine in Kyushu, visited by 3 million people a year
yutoku_inari.text_en: Yutoku Inari Shrine is one of Japan's three major Inari shrines, along with Fushimi Inari and Kasama Inari, and is one of Kyushu's most representative shrines, visited by more than 3 million people a year. It was founded in 1687 by Isouin, the wife of Nabeshima Naotomo, the lord of the Kashima domain, and is worshiped as the guardian deity of food, clothing, shelter, and industry, with Inari Okami, Omiya Uri Okami, and Sarutahiko Okami as the main deities. Built on a cliff, the vermilion-painted tower gate, worship hall, and main hall overlap, creating a spectacular Kake-zukuri architectural style reminiscent of Kiyomizu-dera Temple in Kyoto. Inariyama, which extends all the way to Okunoin Temple, is lined with countless torii gates and stone lanterns, making the entire mountain a sacred area. It is known for its blessings such as prosperous business, good harvest, and matchmaking, and has been visited by many worshipers since ancient times as a sacred place representative of Saga.

nijino_matsubara.name: 虹の松原
nijino_matsubara.text: 虹の松原は唐津湾に沿って約5キロにわたって続く松林で、三保の松原（静岡）・気比の松原（福井）と並ぶ「日本三大松原」の一つとして国の特別名勝に指定されています。慶長12年（1607年）に唐津藩初代藩主・寺沢広高が防砂・防風を目的として植林を命じたのが始まりで、以来400年以上にわたって守り続けられてきました。約100万本のクロマツが密生する松林の中には散策路が整備されており、海と松と唐津城が一体となった景観は国内でも有数の美しさを誇ります。「虹の松原」の名は、松原越しに見える玄界灘の虹のように美しい浜辺の様子から名付けられたとされています。地元では松原の保全活動が盛んで、市民・観光客が一体となって美しい松原を守り続けています。
nijino_matsubara.highlight: 日本三大松原（国特別名勝）。寺沢広高が植えさせた約100万本のクロマツが400年後も唐津湾を彩る
nijino_matsubara.highlight_en: Japan's three major pine pine fields (National Special Place of Scenic Beauty). Approximately 1 million Japanese black pines planted by Hirotaka Terasawa still decorate Karatsu Bay 400 years later.
nijino_matsubara.text_en: Niji-no-Matsubara is a pine forest that stretches for approximately 5 kilometers along Karatsu Bay, and has been designated as a special scenic spot by the country as one of Japan's three major pine forests, along with Miho-no-Matsubara (Shizuoka) and Kehi-no-Matsubara (Fukui). It began in 1607 when Hirotaka Terasawa, the first lord of the Karatsu domain, ordered the planting of trees for the purpose of sand and wind protection, and the trees have been protected for more than 400 years. There is a walking path in the pine forest where about 1 million Japanese black pines grow densely, and the scenery where the sea, pine trees, and Karatsu Castle come together is one of the most beautiful in Japan. It is said that the name ``Niji no Matsubara'' comes from the beautiful rainbow-like appearance of the beach in the Genkai Sea that can be seen beyond the pine bar. Local efforts to preserve the pine forest are active, and citizens and tourists alike continue to work together to protect the beautiful pine forest.

takeo_onsen.name: 武雄温泉楼門
takeo_onsen.kana: たけおおんせんろうもん
takeo_onsen.text: 武雄温泉は1300年以上の歴史を持つ古湯で、奈良時代の「肥前国風土記（ひぜんのくにふどき）」にも記載されている由緒ある温泉地です。温泉のシンボルである朱塗りの楼門（ろうもん）は大正4年（1915年）に辰野金吾（たつのきんご）設計により建設されたもので、国の重要文化財に指定されています。辰野金吾は東京駅や日本銀行本店の設計者として有名で、武雄温泉楼門はその代表作の一つです。楼門をくぐった先には温泉本館があり、江戸時代からの歴史ある湯船で入浴できます。江戸時代には長崎街道（ながさきかいどう）の宿場町として栄え、オランダ商館長や伊能忠敬なども逗留した記録が残っています。九州で最も歴史的背景を持つ温泉地の一つとして、文化財と温泉を合わせて楽しめます。
takeo_onsen.highlight: 辰野金吾（東京駅設計者）設計の朱塗り楼門（国重要文化財）。1300年の歴史を持つ長崎街道の古湯
takeo_onsen.highlight_en: Vermilion-painted tower gate (National Important Cultural Property) designed by Kingo Tatsuno (designer of Tokyo Station). An old hot spring on the Nagasaki Kaido road with a history of 1300 years
takeo_onsen.text_en: Takeo Onsen is an old hot spring with a history of more than 1,300 years, and is a historic hot spring area that is even mentioned in the Nara period's Hizen no Kuni Fudoki. The red-painted tower gate, the symbol of the hot springs, was built in 1915 and designed by Tatsuno Kingo, and has been designated as a national important cultural property. Kingo Tatsuno is famous as the designer of Tokyo Station and the Bank of Japan head office, and the Takeo Onsen Tower Gate is one of his masterpieces. Beyond the tower gate is the main hot spring building, where you can take a bath in a historic bathtub dating back to the Edo period. During the Edo period, it prospered as a post town on the Nagasaki Highway, and there are records that the head of a Dutch trading post and Tadataka Ino stayed here. As one of the hot spring areas with the most historical background in Kyushu, you can enjoy both cultural assets and hot springs.

taku_seibyo.name: 多久聖廟
taku_seibyo.text: 多久聖廟は孔子（こうし）を祀る廟（びょう）で、宝永5年（1708年）に多久藩3代藩主・多久茂文（たくしげふみ）が建立しました。孔子廟としては長崎の聖堂・東京の湯島聖堂と並んで「日本三大聖廟」の一つとされ、国の重要文化財に指定されています。多久藩は鍋島藩の支藩として儒学を重視し、藩士の教育に力を注いだことで知られます。毎年4月と10月に行われる「釈菜（せきさい）」は孔子を祀る礼楽の儀式で、中国・韓国でも行われる国際的な儀式が日本でも継承されています。こぢんまりとした廟ながら、均整のとれた唐様建築の美しさは格別で、庭園とともに静寂な雰囲気の中で儒学の精神に触れることができます。
taku_seibyo.highlight: 日本三大聖廟の一つ（国重要文化財）。1708年建立の孔子廟で今も「釈菜」の儀式が継承される
taku_seibyo.highlight_en: One of Japan's three major sacred shrines (National Important Cultural Property). The ritual of ``Shaku-na'' is still practiced at the Confucius temple built in 1708.
taku_seibyo.text_en: Taku Seibyo is a shrine dedicated to Confucius, and was built in 1708 by Shigefumi Taku, the third lord of the Taku domain. As a Confucian temple, it is considered one of Japan's three great sacred temples, along with the cathedral in Nagasaki and the Yushima Cathedral in Tokyo, and is designated as an important cultural property of the country. As a branch domain of the Nabeshima domain, the Taku domain is known for its emphasis on Confucianism and its efforts in educating the domain's samurai. Sekisai, which is held in April and October every year, is a ritual to honor Confucius, an international ceremony that is also held in China and Korea, and has been inherited in Japan. Although it is a small temple, the beauty of the well-proportioned Chinese architecture is exceptional, and you can experience the spirit of Confucianism in a quiet atmosphere along with the garden.

okawachiyama.name: 大川内山・鍋島焼の秘窯の里
okawachiyama.kana: おおかわちやま・なべしまやきのひかまのさと
okawachiyama.text: 大川内山（おおかわちやま）は伊万里市の山間に位置する鍋島藩（佐賀藩）の「御用窯（ごようがま）」が置かれた地で、「秘窯の里（ひかまのさと）」として知られます。延宝3年（1675年）、佐賀藩は将軍家や諸大名への献上品として最高品質の磁器「鍋島焼（なべしまやき）」を焼くため、この三方を山に囲まれた地に御用窯を集約しました。製法の秘密を守るため外部との往来を厳しく制限し、藩の最高技術者のみが入ることを許された「禁断の村」でした。鍋島焼は精巧な絵付けと完璧な品質管理で日本磁器の最高峰として評価され、現在は「伊万里・鍋島焼会館」で展示・販売されています。今も多くの窯元が営業する山あいの集落には、江戸時代の風情が色濃く残っています。
okawachiyama.highlight: 佐賀藩が最高機密として守った「鍋島焼」の御用窯の里。製法秘匿のため外部と隔絶された幻の陶器の村
okawachiyama.name_en: Okawachiyama, the secret kiln village of Nabeshima ware
okawachiyama.highlight_en: This is the home of the official kiln for Nabeshima-yaki, which was kept as a top secret by the Saga clan. A phantom pottery village isolated from the outside world to keep its manufacturing methods secret.
okawachiyama.text_en: Okawachiyama is located in the mountains of Imari City and is the site of the Goyogama kiln of the Nabeshima clan (Saga clan), and is known as the ``Hikama no Sato'' (secret kiln village). In 1675, the Saga domain concentrated its official kilns in this area, surrounded by mountains on three sides, in order to fire the highest quality porcelain called "Nabeshimayaki" as gifts to the shoguns and various feudal lords. It was a ``forbidden village'' where only the domain's top engineers were allowed to enter, with access to outsiders strictly restricted to protect the secrets of the manufacturing process. Nabeshima-yaki is acclaimed as the pinnacle of Japanese porcelain due to its elaborate painting and perfect quality control, and is currently on display and sold at the Imari Nabeshima-yaki Hall. The mountain village, where many potteries still operate today, retains a strong atmosphere from the Edo period.

nanatsugama.name: 七ツ釜
nanatsugama.text: 七ツ釜は唐津市北部の玄界灘沿岸に発達した海食洞（かいしょくどう）の総称で、国の天然記念物に指定されています。玄武岩の柱状節理（ちゅうじょうせつり）が波浪の侵食を受けて形成された複数の洞窟が並ぶ景観は独特で、洞窟の形が釜に似ていることから「七ツ釜」と名付けられました。最大の洞窟は高さ約6メートル・幅約7メートル・奥行き110メートルに及び、観光船で内部に入ることができます。玄界灘の荒波が打ち寄せる絶壁には、柱状節理の岩が整然と並ぶ「屏風岩（びょうぶいわ）」なども見られます。近世には唐津藩の松浦地方支配の重要拠点として機能した玄海地区の自然と歴史が融合した景勝地です。日本書紀にも玄界灘を舞台とした神話の記述があり、古代から交易の舞台となった海域の神秘を感じられます。
nanatsugama.highlight: 玄武岩の柱状節理が波に侵食されて生まれた海食洞群（国天然記念物）。観光船で洞窟内部に入れる
nanatsugama.highlight_en: A group of sea caves (national natural monument) created by the erosion of basalt columnar joints by waves. Enter the cave by sightseeing boat
nanatsugama.text_en: Nanatsugama is the general name for the sea caves that developed along the coast of the Genkai Sea in the northern part of Karatsu City, and is designated as a national natural monument. The landscape is unique, with multiple caves lined up, formed by the erosion of basalt columnar joints by waves.The caves were named ``Nanatsugama'' (Nanatsugama) because the shape of the caves resembles a cauldron. The largest cave is approximately 6 meters high, 7 meters wide, and 110 meters deep, and can be entered by sightseeing boat. On the cliffs where the rough waves of the Genkai Sea crash, you can also see ``Byobuiwa,'' which are columns of rocks with columnar joints lined up in an orderly manner. It is a scenic spot that combines the nature and history of the Genkai district, which served as an important base for the Karatsu clan's control of the Matsuura region in early modern times. There are also descriptions of myths set in the Genkai Sea in the Nihon Shoki, and you can feel the mystery of the sea area, which has been a stage of trade since ancient times.

hamanourano_tanada.name: 浜野浦の棚田
hamanourano_tanada.text: 浜野浦の棚田は佐賀県玄海町の海岸沿いの急斜面に広がる棚田群で、283枚の小さな田が海に向かって段々と続く景観は「日本の棚田百選」に選ばれています。田植えが終わった5〜6月の夕暮れ時、水を張った田んぼに夕日が映り込む光景は「鏡の棚田」とも称され、国内有数の絶景として写真愛好家が全国から訪れます。佐賀・長崎の玄界灘沿岸は古来、大陸との交流の最前線として栄え、周辺には縄文・弥生時代の遺跡も多く残ります。棚田農業は急傾斜地での食料確保という先人の知恵と労苦の結晶であり、現在も地元農家が伝統の農法を守り続けています。棚田の保全活動を通じた地域コミュニティの絆は、農業文化の継承という観点から高く評価されています。
hamanourano_tanada.highlight: 283枚の田が海へ続く棚田（日本の棚田百選）。夕日が水面に映り込む「鏡の棚田」の絶景
hamanourano_tanada.highlight_en: A terraced rice field with 283 rice paddies extending out to the sea (Japan's top 100 rice terraces). Spectacular view of the ``Mirror Rice Terraces'' where the setting sun is reflected on the water surface
hamanourano_tanada.text_en: The rice terraces of Hamanoura are a group of rice terraces that spread out on a steep slope along the coast in Genkai-cho, Saga Prefecture, and the landscape of 283 small rice fields cascading toward the sea has been selected as one of Japan's ``Top 100 Rice Terraces.'' At dusk in May or June after rice planting is finished, the sight of the setting sun reflecting on the rice fields filled with water is also known as the ``Mirror Rice Terraces,'' and is considered one of the most spectacular views in Japan, attracting photography enthusiasts from all over the country. The Genkai Sea coast of Saga and Nagasaki has flourished as a front line of exchange with the continent since ancient times, and many ruins from the Jomon and Yayoi periods remain in the surrounding area. Terraced rice farming is the result of the wisdom and hard work of our ancestors in securing food on steep slopes, and local farmers continue to adhere to traditional farming methods today. The bonds between local communities through rice terrace conservation activities are highly valued from the perspective of passing on agricultural culture.

ureshino_onsen.name: 嬉野温泉
ureshino_onsen.era: 江戸時代（長崎街道沿い）

transit.name: 武雄温泉駅からバス約30分

ureshino_onsen.text: 嬉野温泉は「日本三大美肌の湯」の一つとして知られる佐賀県嬉野市の温泉地で、泉質は重曹泉（炭酸水素ナトリウム泉）で肌が滑らかになる美人の湯として名高いです。温泉の歴史は奈良時代の「肥前国風土記」に記述があるほど古く、江戸時代には長崎街道（ながさきかいどう）の宿場町「嶋原宿（しまばらじゅく）」として栄えました。シーボルトやケンペルなどの長崎出島のオランダ商館員も参勤交代の行列とともにこの宿場を通過し、記録を残しています。嬉野茶（うれしのちゃ）は全国有数の銘茶産地としても知られ、温泉と茶の両方で名を馳せる地域です。明治・大正時代の温泉旅館建築が残る温泉街は、昔ながらの湯の町の雰囲気を今に伝えています。
ureshino_onsen.highlight: 日本三大美肌の湯の一つ。長崎街道の宿場町として栄え、シーボルトも滞在した1300年の歴史を誇る
ureshino_onsen.highlight_en: One of Japan's three major hot springs for beautiful skin. It flourished as a post town on the Nagasaki Highway, and boasts a 1,300-year history where Siebold stayed there.
ureshino_onsen.text_en: Ureshino Onsen is a hot spring area in Ureshino City, Saga Prefecture, known as one of Japan's three major hot springs for beautiful skin.The spring quality is sodium bicarbonate (sodium hydrogen carbonate spring), and it is famous as a beauty hot spring that makes your skin smooth. The history of hot springs is so old that it is mentioned in the Nara period's ``Hizen Province Fudoki,'' and during the Edo period it flourished as a post town called ``Shimabarajuku'' on the Nagasaki Highway. Members of the Dutch trading post in Dejima, Nagasaki, such as Siebold and Kaempfer, passed through this post station along with their sankin kotai procession and left records. Ureshinocha is known as one of the leading tea producing areas in Japan, and is famous for both its hot springs and tea. The hot spring town retains the architecture of hot spring inns from the Meiji and Taisho eras, and still retains the atmosphere of a traditional hot spring town.

mifuneyama_rakuen.name: 御船山楽園
mifuneyama_rakuen.text: 御船山楽園は武雄市の御船山の断崖を借景とした約15万坪（約50万平方メートル）の広大な日本庭園で、弘化2年（1845年）に武雄領主・鍋島茂義（なべしまもちよし）がわずか3年で造り上げた名園です。御船山の切り立った岩壁を背景に、池・築山・茶室が配された回遊式庭園は幕末の名園として「日本の歴史公園100選」に選ばれています。春の大楠（天然記念物・樹齢3000年）と桜、夏の新緑、秋の紅葉、冬の枯山水と、四季折々に異なる表情を見せる庭園は多くの文人・墨客に愛されてきました。近年ではアート集団・チームラボのデジタルアート展示「武雄」でも知られ、伝統とデジタルの融合した幻想的な夜の庭園体験として国際的に注目されています。
mifuneyama_rakuen.highlight: 1845年に武雄領主が3年で造り上げた15万坪の名園（日本の歴史公園100選）。樹齢3000年の大楠が圧巻
mifuneyama_rakuen.highlight_en: This famous garden of 150,000 tsubo (150,000 tsubo) was built in 1845 by the feudal lord of Takeo in three years (one of Japan's top 100 historical parks). The 3,000-year-old large camphor tree is the highlight
mifuneyama_rakuen.text_en: Mifuneyama Rakuen is a vast Japanese garden of approximately 150,000 tsubo (approximately 500,000 square meters) with the cliffs of Mifuneyama in Takeo City as its backdrop.It is a famous garden built in 1845 by Shigeyoshi Nabeshima, the lord of Takeo, in just three years. With the steep rock walls of Mifuneyama in the background, the strolling garden with a pond, rockery mountain, and tea room has been selected as one of Japan's top 100 historical parks as a famous garden from the end of the Edo period. The garden has been loved by many literary figures and artists, with its different expressions throughout the four seasons: large camphor tree (natural monument, 3000 years old) and cherry blossoms in spring, fresh greenery in summer, autumn leaves, and dry landscape landscape in winter. In recent years, it has also become known for the digital art exhibition ``Takeo'' by the art group teamLab, which is attracting international attention as a fantastic nighttime garden experience that fuses tradition and digital.

hagakure_saga.name: 葉隠れゆかりの地・佐賀
hagakure_saga.kana: はがくれゆかりのち・さが
hagakure_saga.text: 「葉隠（はがくれ）」は佐賀藩士・山本常朝（やまもとつねとも）が口述し、田代陣基（たしろつらもと）が書き記した武士道の書で、「武士道とは死ぬことと見つけたり」の一節で世界に知られています。享保元年（1716年）頃に成立し、全11巻からなる書物は鍋島藩の武士としての生き方・心得・主君への忠誠を説いています。太平洋戦争中は特攻隊の精神的支柱として利用された歴史もあり、日本人の死生観・武士道精神を論じる際に必ず引用される古典です。山本常朝の墓は佐賀市内の金立山（きんりゅうざん）麓にあり、毎年法要が行われています。佐賀市には葉隠を紹介する「肥前さが幕末維新博覧会」の展示施設があり、武士道の精神と佐賀の誇りを伝え続けています。
hagakure_saga.highlight: 「武士道とは死ぬことと見つけたり」の葉隠ゆかりの地。世界に影響を与えた佐賀藩の武士道精神
hagakure_saga.name_en: Saga, a place related to Hagakure
hagakure_saga.highlight_en: A place related to Hagakure, who said, ``Bushido is about dying and finding something.'' The Bushido spirit of the Saga clan influenced the world
hagakure_saga.text_en: ``Hagakure'' is a book on Bushido that was dictated by Tsunetomo Yamamoto, a samurai of the Saga domain, and written by Jinki Tashiro, and is known around the world for the passage ``Bushido is about dying and finding something.'' Compiled around the first year of Kyoho (1716), this 11-volume book explains the way of life, knowledge, and loyalty to the lord as a samurai of the Nabeshima clan. It has a history of being used as a spiritual support for special attack units during the Pacific War, and is a classic that is always cited when discussing the Japanese view of life and death and the Bushido spirit. Tsunetomo Yamamoto's grave is located at the foot of Mt. Kinryuzan in Saga City, and a memorial service is held every year. Saga City has an exhibition facility for the ``Hizen Saga Bakumatsu Meiji Restoration Exhibition'' that introduces Hagakure and continues to convey the spirit of Bushido and the pride of Saga.

karatsu_kunchi.name: 唐津くんち
karatsu_kunchi.text: 唐津くんちは毎年11月2〜4日に行われる唐津神社の秋季例大祭で、国の重要無形民俗文化財に指定されています。文政2年（1819年）に始まった「曳山（ひきやま）行事」では、江戸・明治期に制作された14台の巨大な漆塗りの曳山（山車）が町を練り歩きます。刀町の「赤獅子」・中町の「青獅子」・木綿町の「亀と浦島太郎」など、各町内が誇る曳山は最大で高さ7メートル・重さ5トンにも及ぶ豪華絢爛な山車です。「エンヤ！エンヤ！」の掛け声とともに石畳の旧城下町を練り歩く14台の曳山は圧巻で、3日間で約50万人の観客が訪れます。曳山は「唐津曳山展示場」に常設展示されており、祭り以外の時期でも見学可能です。
karatsu_kunchi.highlight: 国重要無形民俗文化財。漆塗りの巨大曳山14台が唐津城下を練り歩く200年の伝統祭礼
karatsu_kunchi.highlight_en: Nationally important intangible folk cultural property. A 200-year-old traditional festival in which 14 giant lacquered floats parade through Karatsu Castle.
karatsu_kunchi.text_en: Karatsu Kunchi is the annual autumn festival of Karatsu Shrine held from November 2nd to 4th every year, and has been designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property. During the Hikiyama Festival, which began in 1819, 14 giant lacquered floats made during the Edo and Meiji periods are paraded through the town. The floats that each town is proud of, such as Katanacho's ``Red Lion,'' Nakamachi's ``Blue Lion'' and Motomachi's ``Kame to Urashima Taro,'' are gorgeous floats that can reach up to 7 meters in height and weigh 5 tons. The 14 floats parading through the cobblestone old castle town with chants of "Enya! Enya!" are a sight to behold, and approximately 500,000 people visit over the three days. The Hikiyama floats are on permanent display at the Karatsu Hikiyama Exhibition Hall, and can be viewed even outside of the festival.

hizen_koku_cho.name: 肥前国庁跡
hizen_koku_cho.kana: ひぜんこくちょうあと
hizen_koku_cho.text: 肥前国庁跡は奈良・平安時代に肥前国（現在の佐賀・長崎両県）を治めた国府（こくふ）の所在地で、国の史跡に指定されています。7世紀後半から11世紀頃まで機能した国府は、中央政府の命令を地方に伝達する行政機関として重要な役割を担いました。発掘調査により、国庁の中心部である前殿（まえでん）・後殿（うしろでん）・脇殿（わきでん）の構造が明らかになり、礎石が整備・公開されています。周辺には田道間守（たじまのもり）を祀る許乃波奈佐久神社など、古代の神社・寺院が今も残ります。奈良時代の肥前国は西海道（さいかいどう）の要衝として、遣唐使の寄港地・大宰府への中継地として重要な位置を占めていました。古代の佐賀の政治的中心地を実感できる貴重な遺跡です。
hizen_koku_cho.highlight: 奈良〜平安時代の肥前国の政治中心地（国史跡）。発掘復元された国庁の礎石が当時の行政の規模を伝える
hizen_koku_cho.highlight_en: The political center of Hizen Province during the Nara and Heian periods (national historic site). The excavated and restored foundation stone of the national government building conveys the scale of government at the time.
hizen_koku_cho.text_en: The Hizen National Government Office Ruins is the location of the Kokufu that ruled Hizen Province (present-day Saga and Nagasaki prefectures) during the Nara and Heian periods, and is designated as a national historic site. The Kokufu, which functioned from the latter half of the 7th century to around the 11th century, played an important role as an administrative organ that transmitted the orders of the central government to local areas. Excavation research has revealed the structure of the front hall (Maeden), back hall (Ushiroden), and side hall (Wakiden), which are the central part of the national government building, and the foundation stones have been prepared and opened to the public. Ancient shrines and temples still remain in the area, including Konohanasaku Shrine, which is dedicated to Tajima no Mori. During the Nara period, Hizen Province occupied an important position as a strategic point on the Saikaido Road and as a transit point for Dazaifu, a port of call for envoys envoys to China. This is a valuable ruin where you can experience the political center of ancient Saga.

saga_nabeshima_blast.name: 佐賀藩反射炉跡
saga_nabeshima_blast.kana: さがはんはんしゃろあと
saga_nabeshima_blast.text: 佐賀藩反射炉跡は嘉永3年（1850年）に佐賀藩が日本で初めて建設した近代的製鉄炉の跡地です。反射炉（はんしゃろ）は西洋の技術を基に開発した大砲鋳造用の高温炉で、佐賀藩はオランダの技術書「王立陸軍砲工学校教程」を参考に独力で建造しました。建造から2年で完成した50ポンドモルチール砲（臼砲）は国内最大の大砲として幕府を驚かせ、後に大浦海岸に設置された台場に配備されました。この技術革新が佐賀藩の軍事力を飛躍的に向上させ、幕末の佐賀藩が維新政府成立に大きな影響力を持つ一因となりました。現在は碑と石積みの一部が残り、佐賀県の「幕末維新期の近代化遺産」として整備されています。明治日本の産業革命遺産の一環として世界文化遺産の構成資産にも選ばれています。
saga_nabeshima_blast.highlight: 1850年・日本初の近代製鉄炉（世界文化遺産構成資産）。オランダ技術書を独力で解読して実現した幕末の技術革命
saga_nabeshima_blast.highlight_en: 1850: Japan's first modern iron making furnace (World Cultural Heritage Site). The technological revolution at the end of the Edo period was achieved by independently deciphering Dutch technical books.
saga_nabeshima_blast.text_en: The Saga Domain Reverberatory Furnace Ruins is the site of Japan's first modern iron-making furnace built by the Saga Domain in 1850. A reverberatory furnace (reverberatory furnace) is a high-temperature furnace for cannon casting developed based on Western technology, and the Saga clan built it on their own with reference to the Dutch technical book ``Royal Army Artillery School Curriculum''. The 50-pound mortar gun, which was completed within two years of construction, surprised the Shogunate as the largest cannon in Japan, and was later deployed on a platform installed on the Oura coast. This technological innovation dramatically improved the military power of the Saga domain, and was one of the reasons why the Saga domain had a great influence on the establishment of the Meiji Restoration government at the end of the Edo period. Today, the monument and some of the stonework remain, and are being maintained as Saga Prefecture's ``modernization heritage from the end of the Edo period and the Meiji Restoration period.'' It has been selected as a component of the World Cultural Heritage Site as part of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution heritage sites.

kabe_island_tajima.name: 加部島・田島神社
kabe_island_tajima.kana: かべじま・たじまじんじゃ
kabe_island_tajima.text: 加部島は呼子の北に浮かぶ周囲16キロの小島で、島内にある田島神社（たじまじんじゃ）は古代から玄界灘を渡る船人の守護神として崇敬されてきました。延喜式（えんぎしき）に記された「名神大社（みょうじんたいしゃ）」の一つで、主祭神は田心姫神（たごりひめのかみ）ほか三女神です。古代の海上交通の要衝であった玄界灘において、壱岐・対馬とともに大陸との交易を守護する神社として、大陸から渡来する文化・物品の受け口として機能してきました。島を渡る「呼子大橋（よぶこおおはし）」は全長728メートルの吊り橋で、玄界灘の島と橋の景観が美しいです。加部島は「風の見える丘公園」からの展望も素晴らしく、対馬暖流の恩恵を受けた豊かな海洋生態系が今も維持されています。
kabe_island_tajima.highlight: 玄界灘を渡る古代からの航海守護神・田島神社。延喜式の名神大社として壱岐・対馬とともに海上交易を守護
kabe_island_tajima.highlight_en: Tajima Shrine has been a guardian deity for navigation across the Genkai Sea since ancient times. As a famous Engi-style shrine, it protects maritime trade along with Iki and Tsushima.
kabe_island_tajima.text_en: Kabejima is a small island with a circumference of 16 km north of Yobuko, and Tajima Shrine on the island has been revered since ancient times as the guardian deity of boaters crossing the Genkai Sea. It is one of the ``Myojin Taisha'' mentioned in the Engishiki, and the main deities enshrined are Tagorihimenokami and three other goddesses. In the Genkai Sea, which was a key point for maritime transportation in ancient times, it served as a shrine that protected trade with the continent along with Iki and Tsushima, and functioned as a reception point for culture and goods coming from the continent. Yobuko Ohashi Bridge, which crosses the island, is a suspension bridge with a total length of 728 meters, and the scenery of the island and the bridge in the Genkai Sea is beautiful. The view of Kabe Island from ``Kaze no Mieru Oka Park'' is spectacular, and the rich marine ecosystem that benefits from the Tsushima Warm Current is still maintained.

kitsuki_castle.name: 杵築城と武家屋敷群
kitsuki_castle.kana: きつきじょうとぶけやしきぐん
kitsuki_castle.text: 杵築城は応永元年（1394年）に木付頼直が築いたとされ、三方を川・海に囲まれた独特の地形に建つ「水城」として知られています。三の丸・北台・南台の武家屋敷地区が台地の上に位置し、その中間の低地に商人町が挟まれた「サンドイッチ型城下町」という珍しい構造が特徴です。石畳の坂道と白壁の武家屋敷が続く町並みは国の重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に選定されており、江戸時代の武家・商家の文化が色濃く残っています。大原邸・磯矢邸など江戸時代の武家屋敷が内部公開されており、実際に暮らしの様子を体感できます。松平（能見）氏3万2000石の城下町として江戸時代を通じて存続し、「九州の小京都」と呼ばれる落ち着いた雰囲気が魅力です。
kitsuki_castle.highlight: 「サンドイッチ型城下町」（国重要伝統的建造物群保存地区）。石畳と白壁の武家屋敷群が九州の小京都の風情
kitsuki_castle.highlight_en: "Sandwich-shaped castle town" (National Important Traditional Buildings Preservation District). A cluster of samurai residences with stone pavement and white walls gives the atmosphere of Kyushu's Little Kyoto.
kitsuki_castle.text_en: Kitsuki Castle is said to have been built by Yorinao Kitsuke in 1394, and is known as a ``water castle'' due to its unique topography, surrounded by rivers and the sea on three sides. The Sannomaru, Kitadai, and Minamidai samurai estates are located on a plateau, and the merchant town is sandwiched between the plateaus, making it unique as a ``sandwich-type castle town.'' The townscape of stone-paved slopes and white-walled samurai residences has been designated as a nationally important preservation district for groups of traditional buildings, and the culture of the samurai and merchant families of the Edo period remains strongly intact. The interiors of samurai residences from the Edo period, such as the Ohara residence and Isoya residence, are open to the public, allowing you to experience what life was really like. It remained a castle town built by the Matsudaira (Nomi) family of 32,000 koku throughout the Edo period, and is known for its calm atmosphere as the "Little Kyoto of Kyushu."

fukuzawa_yukichi.name: 福沢諭吉旧居（中津）
fukuzawa_yukichi.kana: ふくざわゆきちきゅうきょ
fukuzawa_yukichi.text: 福沢諭吉は天保5年（1835年）に中津藩士の子として大坂で生まれ、幼少期から青年時代を中津で過ごした近代日本最大の啓蒙思想家・教育者です。「天は人の上に人を造らず人の下に人を造らず」の言葉で始まる『学問のすすめ』（1872〜76年）は当時の日本人に近代的な人間平等観と実学の重要性を説き、明治の近代化を精神的に支えました。慶應義塾（現・慶應義塾大学）の創設者として日本の高等教育の基盤を築き、現在の一万円札の肖像にもなっています。中津市内に残る「福沢諭吉旧居」は江戸時代の武家屋敷で、諭吉が少年時代を過ごした生家として保存・公開されています。隣接する「福沢諭吉記念館」では直筆の手紙・著作・遺品など多数の資料を展示しており、諭吉の生涯と思想を詳しく学べます。
fukuzawa_yukichi.highlight: 『学問のすすめ』の著者・福沢諭吉が少年時代を過ごした旧居。一万円札の人物ゆかりの地・中津
fukuzawa_yukichi.highlight_en: This is the former residence of Yukichi Fukuzawa, the author of ``Advice of Learning'', where he spent his childhood. Nakatsu, the place associated with the person on the 10,000 yen bill
fukuzawa_yukichi.text_en: Yukichi Fukuzawa was born in Osaka in 1835 as the son of a samurai of the Nakatsu clan, and spent his childhood and youth in Nakatsu, becoming the greatest Enlightenment thinker and educator in modern Japan. The book ``Advice of Learning'' (1872-1876), which begins with the words ``Heaven does not create people above people nor create people below people,'' explained to the Japanese people of the time the importance of a modern view of human equality and practical learning, and spiritually supported the modernization of the Meiji period. As the founder of Keio Gijuku (now Keio University), he laid the foundation for higher education in Japan, and his portrait is on the current 10,000 yen bill. The former residence of Yukichi Fukuzawa, which remains in Nakatsu City, is a samurai residence from the Edo period that has been preserved and opened to the public as the birthplace where Yukichi spent his childhood. The adjacent Fukuzawa Yukichi Memorial Museum exhibits a large number of materials, including handwritten letters, writings, and personal effects, allowing you to learn more about Yukichi's life and thoughts.

hita_mameda.name: 日田・豆田町（江戸の天領）
hita_mameda.text: 日田は江戸時代に幕府直轄地（天領）として九州全体の代官所が置かれた重要な行政都市で、九州の政治・経済の中心として栄えました。豆田町は日田の旧市街で、国の重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に選定された商家・蔵屋敷の町並みが約300メートルにわたって続いています。江戸時代に設けられた私塾「咸宜園（かんぎえん）」は広瀬淡窓が開き、高野長英・大村益次郎ら全国から3000名以上の学者・志士を輩出した日本最大規模の私塾として知られています。三隈川の清流と盆地の自然に囲まれた日田は「水郷日田」とも称され、アユ漁と日田杉の産地としても名高い地域です。毎年5月・10月の「日田祇園祭」では国指定重要無形民俗文化財の山鉾が巡行します。
hita_mameda.highlight: 江戸時代の幕府天領・九州の政治中枢。3000人超を輩出した最大私塾「咸宜園」がある商家町（国重要伝統的建造物群保存地区）
hita_mameda.highlight_en: The shogunate's domain and the political center of Kyushu during the Edo period. A merchant town where Kangien, the largest private school that has produced over 3,000 students, is located (Nationally Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings)
hita_mameda.text_en: Hita was an important administrative city during the Edo period as a territory under the direct control of the Shogunate (Tenryo), where the magistrate offices for all of Kyushu were located, and flourished as the political and economic center of Kyushu. Mameda-cho is the old town of Hita, and the townscape of merchant houses and storehouses, which has been selected as a nationally important preservation district for groups of traditional buildings, stretches for approximately 300 meters. Kangien, a private school founded in the Edo period, is known as the largest private school in Japan, having produced more than 3,000 scholars and patriots from all over the country, including Nagahide Takano and Masujiro Omura. Surrounded by the clear waters of the Mikuma River and the nature of the basin, Hita is also known as ``Suigo Hita'' and is a famous area for sweetfish fishing and Hita cedar production. At the Hita Gion Festival held in May and October every year, yamahoko floats, which are designated as important intangible folk cultural properties by the country, are paraded.

beppu_onsen_hist.name: 別府温泉・鉄輪の歴史
beppu_onsen_hist.kana: べっぷおんせん・かんなわのれきし
beppu_onsen_hist.text: 別府温泉は日本最大の源泉数と湧出量を誇る世界的な温泉都市で、8つの温泉地区「別府八湯」から成ります。温泉の歴史は奈良時代以前に遡り、行基菩薩が温泉を整備したとの伝承が残ります。鎌倉時代には一遍上人が鉄輪地区を訪れ、温泉による療養を広めたとされており、鉄輪温泉は700年以上の歴史を持つ温泉街として現在も多くの共同浴場が現役で機能しています。明治以降に鉄道が開通すると観光客が急増し、大正・昭和期に「東洋のナポリ」と称される国際的な温泉保養地として発展しました。地獄めぐりと呼ばれる高温・高圧の源泉群は「坊主地獄」「血の池地獄」など個性豊かな8ヶ所が国の名勝に指定されています。
beppu_onsen_hist.highlight: 日本最大の源泉数・湧出量の世界的温泉都市。700年の歴史を持つ鉄輪温泉と「地獄めぐり」（国名勝）
beppu_onsen_hist.highlight_en: A world-class hot spring city with the largest number of hot springs and the largest amount of spring water in Japan. Kannawa Onsen with 700 years of history and “Hell Tour” (National Scenic Place)
beppu_onsen_hist.text_en: Beppu Onsen is a world-class hot spring city that boasts the largest number of hot springs and the largest amount of water in Japan, and consists of eight hot spring districts called ``Beppu Hatto''. The history of hot springs dates back to before the Nara period, and legend has it that Gyoki Bodhisattva maintained the hot springs. It is said that during the Kamakura period, Ippen Shonin visited the Kannawa area and spread the idea of ​​hot springs for healing, and Kannawa Onsen is a hot spring town with a history of over 700 years, with many public baths still functioning today. After the Meiji era, the number of tourists increased rapidly when the railway opened, and during the Taisho and Showa periods it developed into an international hot spring resort called the "Naples of the East." Eight of the high temperature and high pressure hot springs known as Jigoku Meguri have been designated as national scenic spots, including ``Bozu Jigoku'' and ``Chinoike Jigoku''.

yufuin_hist.name: 湯布院・由布院の歴史
yufuin_hist.kana: ゆふいん・ゆふいんのれきし
yufuin_hist.text: 湯布院は大分県由布市に位置する温泉地で、由布岳（1583m）を背景にした盆地の景観と静かな温泉宿が特徴です。温泉の歴史は江戸時代以前に遡り、湯の坪街道沿いに旅館・工芸品店が並ぶ現在の温泉街の原型は明治時代に形成されました。昭和40年代以降、地域住民が主導した「潤いのあるまちづくり」運動によって大型ホテル開発を抑制し、自然と共存する温泉地として独自のブランドを確立しました。由布院映画祭・音楽祭などの文化事業を地域全体で育て、「文化観光」の先駆けとして全国から注目されています。由布岳は古来から山岳信仰の対象として崇敬され、山麓には由布神社が鎮座しています。
yufuin_hist.highlight: 由布岳を背景にした温泉盆地。昭和40年代から住民主導で育てた文化観光の先駆け・由布院ブランドの原点
yufuin_hist.highlight_en: A hot spring basin with Mt. Yufu in the background. The origin of the Yufuin brand, a pioneer of cultural tourism that has been developed by residents since the 1960s.
yufuin_hist.text_en: Yufuin is a hot spring resort located in Yufu City, Oita Prefecture, and is characterized by the scenery of a basin with Mt. Yufu (1583m) in the background and quiet hot spring inns. The history of hot springs dates back to before the Edo period, and the prototype of the current hot spring town, where inns and craft shops line Yunotsubo Kaido, was formed during the Meiji period. Since the 1960s, a movement to create a thriving community led by local residents has curtailed the development of large hotels and established a unique brand as a hot spring resort that coexists with nature. The area fosters cultural projects such as the Yufuin Film Festival and music festival throughout the region, and is attracting attention from all over the country as a pioneer in "cultural tourism." Mt. Yufu has been revered as an object of mountain worship since ancient times, and Yufu Shrine is located at the foot of the mountain.

harajiri_falls.name: 原尻の滝（東洋のナイアガラ）
harajiri_falls.era: 自然史（阿蘇火砕流台地）

transit.name: 豊後竹田駅からバス約20分

harajiri_falls.text: 原尻の滝は大分県豊後大野市緒方町を流れる緒方川に懸かる幅120メートル・落差20メートルの大瀑布で、「東洋のナイアガラ」の異名を持つ壮観な滝です。国の名勝・天然記念物に指定されており、日本の滝百選にも選ばれています。この滝は阿蘇カルデラの大噴火（約9万年前）によって噴出した溶岩・火砕流が台地を形成し、河川がその台地を侵食して生まれた地質学的に貴重な景観です。周囲にはつり橋・遊歩道が整備されており、馬蹄形の断崖から落下する滝の迫力を間近で体感できます。豊後大野市は原尻の滝を含む「竹田ASO・くじゅうユネスコ世界ジオパーク」の一角を担っており、火山地質と歴史が融合する地域として注目されています。
harajiri_falls.highlight: 幅120m・落差20mの「東洋のナイアガラ」（国名勝・天然記念物・日本の滝百選）。阿蘇火砕流台地が生み出した大瀑布
harajiri_falls.highlight_en: ``Niagara of the East'' (National Place of Scenic Beauty, Natural Monument, Top 100 Waterfalls in Japan) with a width of 120m and a drop of 20m. A large waterfall created by the Aso pyroclastic flow plateau
harajiri_falls.text_en: Harajiri Falls is a large waterfall with a width of 120 meters and a drop of 20 meters that spans the Ogata River that flows through Ogata-cho, Bungo-Ono City, Oita Prefecture, and is a spectacular waterfall that is nicknamed the "Niagara of the East." It has been designated as a national scenic beauty and natural monument, and has been selected as one of Japan's top 100 waterfalls. This waterfall is a geologically valuable landscape that was created when the lava and pyroclastic flow erupted from the Aso Caldera eruption (approximately 90,000 years ago) formed a plateau, and the river eroded the plateau. There are suspension bridges and promenades in the surrounding area, allowing you to experience the power of the waterfall falling from the horseshoe-shaped cliff up close. Bungo-Ono City is part of the Takeda ASO Kuju UNESCO Global Geopark, which includes Harajiri Falls, and is attracting attention as an area that combines volcanic geology and history.

saiki_castle.name: 佐伯城跡・三の丸屋敷
saiki_castle.kana: さいきじょうあと・さんのまるやしき
saiki_castle.text: 佐伯城は慶長11年（1606年）に佐伯藩初代藩主・毛利高政が築いた山城です。「鶴屋城」とも呼ばれ、標高144メートルの山頂に本丸を持ちます。現在は本丸の石垣と三の丸屋敷が残っており、三の丸屋敷は江戸時代の面影を伝える貴重な建築物です。毛利家は毛利元就の子孫で、関ヶ原以後に豊後へ転封された大名として佐伯2万石を支配し、明治維新まで統治しました。城下の佐伯藩文化は独自の武士道と産業（くじら・海産物）で発展し、江戸後期には独自の自然哲学「玄語」を著した蘭学者・三浦梅園を輩出しています。
saiki_castle.highlight: 毛利高政（毛利元就の孫）が築いた山城。蘭学者・三浦梅園を輩出した佐伯2万石の城跡
saiki_castle.highlight_en: A mountain castle built by Takamasa Mori (grandson of Motonari Mori). The ruins of Saiki's 20,000-koku castle, which produced the Dutch scholar Miura Umezono.
saiki_castle.text_en: Saiki Castle is a mountain castle built in 1606 by Mori Takamasa, the first lord of the Saeki domain. Also known as "Tsuruya Castle", it has its main castle on the top of a mountain at an altitude of 144 meters. Today, the stone walls of the main enclosure and the Sannomaru mansion remain, and the Sannomaru mansion is a valuable building that conveys the essence of the Edo period. The Mori family is a descendant of Motonari Mori, and as a daimyo transferred to Bungo after Sekigahara, they controlled 20,000 koku of Saiki, and ruled until the Meiji Restoration. The culture of the Saeki clan in the castle town developed with its own Bushido and industry (whales and seafood), and in the late Edo period produced Miura Baien, a Dutch scholar who wrote his own natural philosophy, ``Gengo.''

hiji_castle.name: 日出城跡（鯛城）
hiji_castle.kana: ひじじょうあと・たいじょう
hiji_castle.text: 日出城は慶長7年（1602年）に日出藩初代藩主・木下延俊が豊後別府湾に突き出た崖の上に築いた海城です。別府湾を一望する絶壁の直下ではマダイが生息しており、釣り上げた鯛が城内に直接届いたという逸話から「鯛城」の愛称で親しまれています。木下氏は豊臣秀吉の正室・北政所の甥の系統で、外様大名でありながら幕末まで日出2万5000石を維持しました。城跡には石垣・堀跡が残り、天守台からは別府湾と由布岳の絶景が広がります。木下家が藩を通じて育んだ儒学・蘭学の文化が現在も地域に息づいており、城下の風情が今も感じられる小さな城下町です。
hiji_castle.highlight: 崖下でマダイが釣れた「鯛城」の異名を持つ海城。秀吉正室の縁戚・木下氏が幕末まで治めた日出藩の城跡
hiji_castle.highlight_en: Kaijo is also known as ``Taijo'' where you can catch red sea bream at the bottom of the cliff. The castle ruins of the Hiji clan, which was ruled by the Kinoshita clan, a relative of Hideyoshi's legal wife, until the end of the Edo period.
hiji_castle.text_en: Hiji Castle is a sea castle built in 1602 by Nobutoshi Kinoshita, the first lord of the Hiji domain, on a cliff jutting out into Bungo-Beppu Bay. Red sea bream live just below the cliff overlooking Beppu Bay, and the castle is nicknamed ``Tai Castle'' because of the anecdote that the sea bream they caught were delivered directly to the castle grounds. The Kinoshita clan is descended from the nephew of Toyotomi Hideyoshi's legal wife, Kita Mandokoro, and although he was a Tozama daimyo, he maintained a net worth of 25,000 koku in Hiji until the end of the Edo period. Ruins of stone walls and moats remain at the castle ruins, and from the castle tower you can enjoy a spectacular view of Beppu Bay and Mt. Yufu. The culture of Confucianism and Dutch studies that the Kinoshita family fostered through their domain is still alive in the area, and it is a small castle town where you can still feel the atmosphere of a castle town.

nata_shrine.name: 奈多宮（宇佐の海の古社）
nata_shrine.text: 奈多宮は大分県宇佐市の国東半島東端の海岸に鎮座する古社で、正式名称は「奈多八幡神社」です。宇佐神宮の母宮または放生会の神として古代から崇敬されており、宇佐・香春・宮地嶽の「三所八幡」として豊前・豊後の要地を結ぶ信仰圏の一端を担っています。海に面した境内から見える別府湾・国東半島の景色は格別で、社叢の原始林も貴重な自然遺産です。古代より舟を祀る海神信仰と八幡信仰が融合した独特の神社として、漁師・航海者の信仰を集めてきました。国東半島の六郷満山文化の影響を受けた周辺の寺院・神社と合わせて、古代日本の神仏習合文化を学べる場所として注目されています。
nata_shrine.highlight: 宇佐神宮の母宮とされる海辺の古社。豊後三所八幡の一角として古代の海上信仰と八幡信仰が融合
nata_shrine.highlight_en: An old seaside shrine that is said to be the mother shrine of Usa Jingu. As part of Bungo Sansho Hachiman, ancient maritime beliefs and Hachiman beliefs are fused.
nata_shrine.text_en: Nata Shrine is an old shrine located on the coast of the eastern tip of the Kunisaki Peninsula in Usa City, Oita Prefecture, and its official name is ``Nata Hachiman Shrine.'' It has been revered since ancient times as the mother shrine of Usa Shrine or the deity of the Hojokai, and as the "Sansho Hachiman" of Usa, Kaharu, and Miyajidake, it plays a part in the religious area that connects the important areas of Buzen and Bungo. The view of Beppu Bay and Kunisaki Peninsula from the precincts facing the sea is exceptional, and the virgin forest of the shrine is also a valuable natural heritage. Since ancient times, it has attracted the faith of fishermen and voyagers as a unique shrine that combines the belief in the sea god that enshrines boats and the belief in Hachiman. Together with the surrounding temples and shrines that were influenced by the Rokugo-Manzan culture of the Kunisaki Peninsula, it is attracting attention as a place where you can learn about ancient Japan's syncretistic culture of Shinto and Buddhism.

funai_xavier.name: ザビエル府内訪問の地（大分市）
funai_xavier.kana: ざびえるふないほうもんのち
funai_xavier.text: フランシスコ・ザビエルは天文20年（1551年）に豊後国の府内（現・大分市）を訪れ、大友宗麟の保護のもとでキリスト教の布教活動を行いました。ザビエルは大友氏の城下・府内に病院・学校を設立し、西洋の医学・文化を日本に伝えた最初の宣教師として歴史的に重要な人物です。大友宗麟（洗礼名フランシスコ）はキリスト教に深く傾倒し、ポルトガルとの南蛮貿易を積極的に展開して府内を西洋文化が花開く「南蛮文化の都」へと発展させました。府内には「ザビエル上陸記念碑」や城址公園にキリスト教伝来を記念するモニュメントが設置されています。16世紀の日本で最も国際色豊かな都市の一つであった府内の歴史は、大分が「日本のキリスト教発祥地のひとつ」として位置付けられる根拠となっています。
funai_xavier.highlight: 1551年・ザビエルが大友宗麟の保護で布教した「南蛮文化の都」府内。日本のキリスト教・西洋医学伝来の拠点
funai_xavier.name_en: Place of visit to Xavier Funai (Oita City)
funai_xavier.highlight_en: In 1551, Xavier spread the word in Funai, the ``capital of Nanban culture'' under the protection of Sorin Otomo. Base of the introduction of Christianity and Western medicine in Japan
funai_xavier.text_en: Francisco Xavier visited Funai (present-day Oita City) in Bungo Province in 1551 and carried out Christian missionary work under the protection of Sorin Otomo. Xavier established a hospital and school in the Otomo clan's castle town and prefecture, and is a historically important figure as the first missionary to introduce Western medicine and culture to Japan. Sorin Otomo (baptized as Francisco) was deeply devoted to Christianity and actively expanded trade with Portugal to develop Nanban culture into a ``capital of Nanban culture'' where Western culture flourished. In the prefecture, there are monuments commemorating the introduction of Christianity, such as the ``Xavier Landing Monument'' and the castle ruins park. Funai's history as one of Japan's most cosmopolitan cities in the 16th century is the basis for Oita's position as "one of the birthplaces of Christianity in Japan."

tenjinyama_kofun.name: 亀塚古墳（大分県最大の前方後円墳）
tenjinyama_kofun.text: 亀塚古墳は大分市横尾に位置する前方後円墳で、墳丘長約170メートル・高さ約20メートルと大分県内最大規模の古墳として国の史跡に指定されています。4〜5世紀に築造されたと推定されており、豊後国の古代首長墓として当時の政治権力の大きさを示しています。出土品には鏡・玉類・武器・馬具などが含まれ、大和政権との密接な関係を示す副葬品も発見されています。「亀塚古墳展示館」では出土品の展示と古墳の構造を学べ、整備された公園内では前方後円墳の形を実際に歩いて感じることができます。豊後国の古代史において亀塚古墳は「豊後の王」の権力を示す最重要の遺跡として評価されており、宇佐地方の古墳群と合わせて豊後の古代王国の全体像を解明する鍵となっています。
tenjinyama_kofun.highlight: 大分県最大の前方後円墳（国史跡）。4〜5世紀に築かれた豊後の古代首長墓。大和政権との関係を示す副葬品が出土
tenjinyama_kofun.name_en: Kamezuka Tumulus (Oita Prefecture's largest keyhole-shaped tumulus)
tenjinyama_kofun.highlight_en: The largest keyhole-shaped tumulus in Oita Prefecture (national historic site). An ancient chieftain's tomb in Bungo built between the 4th and 5th centuries. Grave goods showing ties to the Yamato government were discovered
tenjinyama_kofun.text_en: Kamezuka Kofun is a keyhole-shaped tumulus located in Yokoo, Oita City, and is designated as a national historic site as the largest kofun in Oita Prefecture, with a length of about 170 meters and a height of about 20 meters. It is estimated that it was built between the 4th and 5th centuries, and as an ancient chieftain's tomb of Bungo Province, it shows the extent of political power at the time. The excavated items include mirrors, jewels, weapons, horse harnesses, etc., and grave goods indicating a close relationship with the Yamato regime have also been discovered. At the Kamezuka Tumulus Exhibition Hall, you can see excavated artifacts and learn about the structure of the tumulus, and in the well-maintained park you can actually walk and feel the shape of the keyhole-shaped tumulus. In the ancient history of Bungo Province, the Kamezuka Tumulus is regarded as the most important ruin that shows the power of the ``King of Bungo'', and together with the tombs in the Usa region, it is the key to elucidating the entire picture of the ancient kingdom of Bungo.

rokugo_manzan.name: 六郷満山・国東半島の仏の里
rokugo_manzan.kana: ろくごうまんざん・くにさきはんとうのほとけのさと
rokugo_manzan.text: 六郷満山は国東半島に展開する独自の神仏習合文化で、養老2年（718年）に仁聞菩薩が宇佐神宮を本地として28の寺院・65の庵を創建したことに始まると伝えられています。「六郷」とは半島を6つの郷に分けた地区区分で、「満山」は全山を意味し、半島全体が一大霊場を形成しています。山岳修行「峯入り」は現在も毎年行われており、修験道の伝統を今に伝える貴重な文化です。国東半島には富貴寺・両子寺・熊野磨崖仏など多数の重要文化財が点在しており、石仏・石塔・磨崖仏が半島全体に分布しています。「鬼会」と呼ばれる独特の修行儀式は国の重要無形民俗文化財に指定されており、奈良・平安時代からの宗教文化が生きた形で継承されています。
rokugo_manzan.highlight: 718年に始まった国東半島独自の神仏習合文化。半島全体が霊場で今も峯入り修行が続く日本唯一の仏教文化圏
rokugo_manzan.highlight_en: Kunisaki Peninsula's unique syncretistic culture of Shinto and Buddhism began in 718. The entire peninsula is a sacred place, and it is Japan's only Buddhist cultural area where the practice of entering the mountain still continues.
rokugo_manzan.text_en: Rokugo Manzan is a unique syncretistic culture of Shintoism and Buddhism that developed on the Kunisaki Peninsula, and it is said to have started in 718 when Ninmon Bosatsu established 28 temples and 65 hermitages with Usa Jingu as his home base. ``Rokugo'' is a district division that divides the peninsula into six villages, and ``Manzan'' means all mountains, and the entire peninsula forms one large sacred site. The mountain training "Mineiri" is still held every year, and is a valuable culture that passes down the tradition of Shugendo to the present day. Kunisaki Peninsula is dotted with many important cultural properties such as Fukiji Temple, Futagoji Temple, Kumano Magaibutsu, and stone Buddhas, stone pagodas, and Magaibutsu are distributed throughout the peninsula. The unique training ritual called "Oni-e" has been designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property, and is a living form of religious culture that has been passed down since the Nara and Heian periods.

kusu_morijinja.name: 玖珠・森藩と久留島氏陣屋
kusu_morijinja.kana: くす・もりはんとくるしまうじじんや
