kusu_morijinja.text: 玖珠郡の森藩は正保2年（1645年）に久留島通清が1万石の大名として立藩した小藩で、明治維新まで続いた大分の小藩の一つです。久留島氏は伊予国来島水軍の末裔で、関ヶ原の戦いで西軍に属したため改易となり、のちに久留島通清が復封されて豊後・玖珠を治めました。玖珠盆地は阿蘇山の火砕流が固まったメサ（卓状台地）が侵食された独特の景観「伐株山」を有しています。また「日本のアンデルセン」と称された久留島武彦ゆかりの地としても有名で、明治〜大正時代に多くの童話・おとぎ話を全国に広めました。豊後森機関庫は昭和初期の扇形機関庫として現存し、国の登録有形文化財に指定されています。
kusu_morijinja.highlight: 来島水軍の末裔・久留島氏が治めた小藩。「日本のアンデルセン」久留島武彦を輩出した玖珠盆地の歴史
kusu_morijinja.name_en: Kusu Mori domain and Kurushima clan jinya
kusu_morijinja.highlight_en: A small domain ruled by the Kurushima clan, descendants of the Kurushima Navy. The history of the Kusu Basin, which produced Takehiko Kurushima, the “Andersen of Japan”
kusu_morijinja.text_en: The Mori Domain in Kusu District was established in 1645 by Michiyo Kurushima as a daimyo with 10,000 koku, and was one of the small domains in Oita that continued until the Meiji Restoration. The Kurushima clan is a descendant of the Kurushima navy in Iyo Province, and was relegated to the Western Army at the Battle of Sekigahara, and was later re-established as Kurushima Michikiyo, who ruled Bungo and Kusu. The Kusu Basin has a unique landscape called ``Kutshuyama,'' which is an eroded mesa (tableland) formed by the solidified pyroclastic flow of Mt. Aso. It is also famous as the birthplace of Takehiko Kurushima, who was known as ``Japan's Hans Christian Andersen'' and popularized many fairy tales and fairy tales throughout the country during the Meiji and Taisho periods. The Bungomori Engine Depot is a fan-shaped engine depot from the early Showa period that still exists and is designated as a registered tangible cultural property of the country.

kuju_sangaku.name: 久住山と山岳信仰
kuju_sangaku.kana: くじゅうさんとさんがくしんこう

transit.name: 豊後竹田駅からバス約60分

kuju_sangaku.text: 久住山（1786m）を中心とする九重連山は大分・熊本両県にまたがる九州最高峰の山岳地帯で、古代から修験道の霊場として崇敬されてきました。山麓の豊後大野・竹田地区には鎌倉時代以降に開山された寺院が点在しています。九重連山では毎年夏に「山開き」が行われ、現在も登山者が久住山頂の神社に参拝する慣習が続いています。坊がつるは九州最大の湿原として知られ、その独特の生態系と山岳の景観は「ラムサール条約湿地」にも登録されています。豊後大野市の「原尻の滝」と合わせてユネスコ世界ジオパークに認定されており、地質・歴史・文化が一体となった地域として世界から注目されています。秋には紅葉が連山を彩り、九州随一の山岳景観が広がります。
kuju_sangaku.highlight: 九州最高峰・久住山（1786m）の山岳地帯。古代から修験道の霊場として崇敬され、坊がつる湿原はラムサール登録
kuju_sangaku.highlight_en: A mountainous area with Kyushu's highest peak, Mt. Kuju (1786m). Revered as a sacred site for Shugendo since ancient times, Bogatsuru Wetland has been registered as a Ramsar site.
kuju_sangaku.text_en: The Kokonoe Mountain Range, centered on Mt. Kuju (1786m), is the highest mountain range in Kyushu, spanning both Oita and Kumamoto prefectures, and has been revered as a sacred site for Shugendo since ancient times. The Bungo-Ono and Takeda areas at the foot of the mountain are dotted with temples that were built after the Kamakura period. A ``mountain opening ceremony'' is held every summer in the Kokonoe Mountains, and the custom of climbers visiting the shrine at the summit of Mt. Kuju continues today. Bogatsuru is known as the largest wetland in Kyushu, and its unique ecosystem and mountain scenery have been registered as a Ramsar wetland. Together with Harajiri Falls in Bungo-Ono City, it has been certified as a UNESCO Global Geopark, and is attracting attention from around the world as a region that combines geology, history, and culture. In autumn, the mountains are colored with autumn leaves, creating one of the best mountain scenery in Kyushu.

bungo_ono_ruins.name: 緒方・南北朝の戦跡と豊後大野の歴史
bungo_ono_ruins.kana: おがた・なんぼくちょうのせんせきとぶんごおおののれきし
bungo_ono_ruins.text: 大野郡緒方は大分県豊後大野市に位置する地域で、南北朝時代（14世紀）に大野地方を支配した緒方氏・大友氏らの争いの舞台となった歴史的な地域です。緒方三郎惟義は平安末期の武将で、源頼朝の挙兵を支援した豊後の有力武士として知られており、緒方一族は九州武士団として南北朝期まで大きな勢力を誇りました。緒方盆地には「緒方城跡」の石垣が残り、中世の山城の姿をとどめています。豊後大野市は阿蘇火砕流台地「竹田ASO・くじゅうユネスコ世界ジオパーク」の中心地でもあり、地質的な奇景と中世の歴史が重なるユニークな地域です。周辺には「沈堕の滝」など豊かな自然遺産も点在しています。
bungo_ono_ruins.highlight: 平安末期の豊後武士・緒方三郎惟義の本拠地。南北朝の激戦を経た中世山城跡とユネスコジオパークの火砕流台地が共存
bungo_ono_ruins.name_en: Battle ruins of Ogata and Nanbokucho and the history of Bungo-Ono
bungo_ono_ruins.highlight_en: The home base of Saburo Ogata, a Bungo samurai from the late Heian period. The remains of a medieval mountain castle that was the site of a fierce battle between the Northern and Southern Courts coexist with the pyroclastic flow plateau of the UNESCO Geopark.
bungo_ono_ruins.text_en: Ogata, Ono District is an area located in Bungo Ono City, Oita Prefecture, and is a historical area that was the scene of a conflict between the Ogata and Otomo clans who ruled the Ono region during the Nanbokucho period (14th century). Saburo Ogata was a military commander at the end of the Heian period, and was known as a powerful samurai of Bungo who supported Minamoto no Yoritomo in raising an army, and the Ogata clan boasted great power as the Kyushu samurai group until the period of the Northern and Southern Courts. The stone walls of the Ogata Castle Ruins remain in the Ogata Basin, preserving the appearance of a medieval mountain castle. Bungo-Ono City is also the center of the Aso Pyroclastic Flow Plateau "Takeda ASO Kuju UNESCO Global Geopark," and is a unique area where geological wonders and medieval history overlap. There are also rich natural heritage sites scattered around the area, such as the Chinda Falls.

himeshima_history.name: 姫島の歴史と黒曜石文化
himeshima_history.kana: ひめしまのれきしとこくようせきぶんか

transit.name: 国見港からフェリー約20分

himeshima_history.text: 姫島は大分県東国東郡の島で、周囲約17キロの小島ながら日本有数の黒曜石の産地として縄文時代から石器の原料として採掘・交易されてきました。姫島産の黒曜石は遠く四国・中国地方の縄文遺跡からも出土しており、古代の海上交易ネットワークの重要な結節点として機能していたことが分かります。島の鎮守「比売語曽神社」は古代の女神・比売語曽神を祀り、古事記・日本書紀にも名が出る古社です。島には「姫島七不思議」と呼ばれる伝説が伝わり、神秘的な自然現象・伝説が島の各所に残っています。毎年8月に行われる「姫島盆踊り」は国の重要無形民俗文化財で、「キツネ踊り」など独特の演目が有名です。
himeshima_history.highlight: 縄文時代の黒曜石交易の重要拠点。四国・中国地方に流通した黒曜石が出土し古代の海上ネットワークを証明する離島
himeshima_history.highlight_en: An important base for obsidian trade during the Jomon period. A remote island where obsidian distributed in the Shikoku and Chugoku regions has been unearthed, proving an ancient maritime network
himeshima_history.text_en: Himejima is an island in Higashi-Kunisaki District, Oita Prefecture, and although it is a small island with a circumference of approximately 17 km, it is one of Japan's leading producers of obsidian, and has been mined and traded as a raw material for stone tools since the Jomon period. Obsidian from Himeshima has also been unearthed from Jomon ruins in the distant Shikoku and Chugoku regions, indicating that it functioned as an important node in ancient maritime trade networks. Himegoso Shrine, the island's guardian deity, is an ancient shrine that enshrines the ancient goddess Himegoso, whose name is also mentioned in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki. A legend known as the ``Seven Wonders of Himejima'' has been passed down on the island, and mysterious natural phenomena and legends remain in various parts of the island. The ``Himejima Bon Odori'' held every August is a nationally designated Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property, and is famous for its unique performances such as the ``Fox Dance.''

usa_mirokuji.name: 弥勒寺跡・宇佐の古代仏教
usa_mirokuji.kana: みろくじあと・うさのこだいぶっきょう
usa_mirokuji.text: 弥勒寺跡は大分県宇佐市に残る奈良時代の大寺院跡で、宇佐神宮と密接に関わった「宇佐の古代仏教」の中心地です。神護景雲3年（769年）に発生した「宇佐八幡神託事件」は、宇佐神宮が道鏡を天皇位に就けようとする画策に対して「道鏡を皇位につけるな」との神託を発したとされる事件で、日本古代政治史の重要な転換点となりました。弥勒寺は宇佐神宮の神宮寺として機能し、神仏習合の観点から宇佐の宗教複合体の核心を担っていました。発掘調査によって七堂伽藍の礎石が確認されており、奈良時代の大規模寺院の姿が明らかになっています。宇佐市内には古代条里制の痕跡が残る水田地帯があり、奈良時代の豊前・豊後の農村景観を今に伝えています。
usa_mirokuji.highlight: 宇佐神宮の神宮寺・弥勒寺の遺跡。「道鏡皇位事件」（769年）の舞台となった古代政治史の重要地点
usa_mirokuji.name_en: Ruins of Mirokuji Temple/Ancient Buddhism in Usa
usa_mirokuji.highlight_en: Ruins of Mirokuji, a shrine temple in Usa Jingu. An important point in ancient political history that was the setting for the Dokyo Imperial Throne Incident (769)
usa_mirokuji.text_en: The Mirokuji Temple ruins are the remains of a large temple from the Nara period in Usa City, Oita Prefecture, and are the center of ``Ancient Buddhism in Usa,'' which was closely related to Usa Jingu. The ``Usa Hachiman Oracle Incident'' that occurred in the third year of Jingo Keiun (769) was an important turning point in ancient Japanese political history, as it was said that Usa Jingu Shrine issued an oracle ordering ``Dokyo not to be placed on the throne'' in response to a plot to place Dokyo on the throne. Mirokuji Temple functioned as the shrine temple of Usa Jingu, and was the core of Usa's religious complex from the perspective of syncretism of Shinto and Buddhism. Excavations have confirmed the foundation stones of Shichido Garan, revealing the appearance of a large-scale temple from the Nara period. There is a paddy field area in Usa City where traces of the ancient Jori system remain, and the rural landscape of Buzen and Bungo during the Nara period has been preserved to this day.

yamakuni_history.name: 山国川・青の洞門と耶馬渓
yamakuni_history.kana: やまくにがわ・あおのどうもんとやばけい
yamakuni_history.text: 青の洞門は大分県中津市本耶馬渓町を流れる山国川の断崖に掘られたトンネルで、禅海和尚が延享4年（1747年）から30年以上かけて鑿と槌だけで独力で掘り続けた全長142メートルのトンネルです。禅海和尚は人々が険しい岩壁の崖道で命を落とすのを嘆き、托鉢で資金を集めながら一人で岩を掘り続け、約30年で完成させました。この偉業は菊池寛の小説「恩讐の彼方に」の題材となり、全国に広まりました。山国川の耶馬渓は奇岩絶壁が連続する景勝地として国の名勝に指定されており、紅葉の名所として秋には全国から多くの観光客が訪れます。江戸時代から水運の要衝として機能した山国川流域の歴史と自然が融合した地域です。
yamakuni_history.highlight: 禅海和尚が30年かけて独力で掘った全長142mのトンネル（小説「恩讐の彼方に」の舞台）。耶馬渓の奇岩絶壁（国名勝）
yamakuni_history.name_en: Yamakuni River, Blue Cave and Yabakei
yamakuni_history.highlight_en: A tunnel with a total length of 142m that was dug by monk Zenkai over a period of 30 years (the setting for the novel ``Beyond Benevolence'').耶馬渓の奇岩絶壁（国名勝）
yamakuni_history.text_en: The Blue Cave is a tunnel dug into the cliff of the Yamakuni River that flows through Honyabakei-cho, Nakatsu City, Oita Prefecture.It is a tunnel with a total length of 142 meters that the monk Zenkai continued to dig by himself for more than 30 years starting in 1747 using only a chisel and a mallet. Monk Zenkai lamented that people were losing their lives on the steep rocky cliffs, so he continued to dig into the rock by himself, collecting funds through alms, and completed the work in about 30 years.この偉業は菊池寛の小説「恩讐の彼方に」の題材となり、全国に広まりました。 Yabakei on the Yamakuni River has been designated as a national scenic spot with a series of strangely shaped cliffs, and is a famous spot for autumn leaves, attracting many tourists from all over the country in the fall.江戸時代から水運の要衝として機能した山国川流域の歴史と自然が融合した地域です。

bungotakada_manyo.name: 豊後高田・六郷満山の入口
bungotakada_manyo.kana: ぶんごたかだ・ろくごうまんざんのいりぐち
bungotakada_manyo.text: 豊後高田市は国東半島の北西に位置し、六郷満山文化の中心地の一つとして中世から栄えた地域です。天念寺の「川中不動」は川の中の岩に刻まれた磨崖仏として独特の景観を持ち、毎年2月の「修正鬼会」は国の重要無形民俗文化財として六郷満山随一の迫力ある宗教行事です。周辺には「高山寺」など平安時代創建の古刹が点在し、石仏・磨崖仏が各所に残っています。また富貴寺の国宝大堂は平安時代の九州最古の木造建築として、全国から研究者・参拝者が訪れます。市内の「昭和の町」は昭和期の商店街を整備した観光エリアですが、その基盤となる歴史は千年以上続く六郷満山の仏教文化に根ざしています。
bungotakada_manyo.highlight: 六郷満山文化の拠点・豊後高田。川中岩に刻まれた天念寺「川中不動」と修正鬼会（国重要無形民俗文化財）
bungotakada_manyo.highlight_en: Bungotakada is a hub of Rokugo Manzan culture. Tennenji Temple “Kawanaka Fudo” carved into Kawanaka Rock and Shushu Onikai (National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)
bungotakada_manyo.text_en: Bungotakada City is located in the northwest of the Kunisaki Peninsula, and is an area that has prospered since the Middle Ages as one of the centers of Rokugo-Manzan culture. Tennen-ji Temple's Kawanakafudo has a unique landscape as a carved stone Buddha carved into a rock in the middle of a river, and the annual Shusho Oni Festival held in February is one of the most powerful religious events in Rokugo Manzan, designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property. The surrounding area is dotted with ancient temples built in the Heian period, such as Kozanji Temple, and stone Buddhas and carved Buddha statues remain in various places. The National Treasure Hall of Fukiji Temple is the oldest wooden building in Kyushu from the Heian period, and is visited by researchers and worshipers from all over the country. The city's "Showa-no-machi" is a tourist area built from the Showa era shopping street, but its foundational history is rooted in the Buddhist culture of Rokugo Manzan, which has continued for more than a thousand years.

taketa_jokamachi.name: 竹田城下町・荒城の月ゆかりの地
taketa_jokamachi.kana: たけたじょうかまち・こうじょうのつきゆかりのち
taketa_jokamachi.text: 竹田市は岡城の城下として栄えた歴史都市で、明治時代の音楽家・滝廉太郎が少年時代を過ごした地として「荒城の月」の舞台として全国に知られています。荒城の月は岡城の廃墟の姿から着想を得た唱歌で、明治34年（1901年）に発表されて以来、日本を代表する名曲の一つとして歌い継がれています。竹田市内には江戸時代の武家屋敷・商家が残る城下町の面影があり、「瀧廉太郎記念館」では作曲家の生涯と作品を学べます。周囲を山に囲まれた盆地の竹田は、旧城下の石畳・白壁・武家屋敷と豊かな自然が融合した「大分の小京都」として人気です。また豊後国の切支丹大名・大友宗麟の本拠地でもあったこの地には、キリシタン文化の痕跡も残っています。
taketa_jokamachi.highlight: 「荒城の月」の滝廉太郎が少年時代を過ごした城下町。岡城の廃墟から生まれた名曲のふるさとを歩く
taketa_jokamachi.name_en: Takeda castle town, the place associated with Kojo no Tsuki
taketa_jokamachi.highlight_en: A castle town where Rentaro Taki from "Kojo no Tsuki" spent his childhood. Walk through the hometown of famous songs born from the ruins of Oka Castle
taketa_jokamachi.text_en: Takeda City is a historical city that flourished as the castle town of Oka Castle, and is known throughout the country as the place where Meiji era musician Rentaro Taki spent his childhood and as the setting for ``Kojo no Tsuki.'' Kojo no Tsuki is a song inspired by the sight of the ruins of Oka Castle, and since its release in 1901, it has been sung as one of Japan's most famous songs. Takeda City has the vestiges of a castle town where samurai residences and merchant houses from the Edo period remain, and you can learn about the composer's life and works at the Taki Rentaro Memorial Museum. Takeda, a basin surrounded by mountains, is popular as ``Oita's Little Kyoto,'' where the stone pavements, white walls, and samurai residences of the former castle town are fused with rich nature. Traces of Christian culture remain in this area, which was also the home base of Otomo Sourin, the Kirishitan daimyo of Bungo Province.

iwatoyama_kofun.name: 岩戸山古墳

transit.name: バス「岩戸山古墳前」（西鉄バス）

iwatoyama_kofun.highlight: 磐井の乱の主役・筑紫君磐井の墓。九州最大級の前方後円墳
iwatoyama_kofun.text: 岩戸山古墳は、527年に勃発した「磐井の乱」の首謀者・筑紫君磐井の墓と伝えられる大型前方後円墳です。墳丘の長さは約135メートルと九州最大級を誇ります。磐井の乱は、ヤマト王権が新羅征討のために徴兵しようとした北部九州の豪族・磐井が反乱を起こした事件です。大和朝廷は物部麁鹿火を派遣し、翌528年に磐井を討ち取りました。この乱はヤマト王権が九州を直接支配下に置く大きな転換点となりました。古墳の周囲には石人・石馬が配置されており、独自の葬送文化を示しています。
iwatoyama_kofun.highlight_en: The grave of Tsukushi-kun Iwai, the main character of the Iwai Rebellion. One of the largest keyhole-shaped tumuli in Kyushu
iwatoyama_kofun.text_en: Iwatoyama Tumulus is a large keyhole-shaped tumulus that is said to be the tomb of Iwai, the leader of the Iwai Rebellion that broke out in 527. The length of the mound is approximately 135 meters, making it one of the largest in Kyushu. The Iwai Rebellion was an incident in which the Iwai clan, a powerful clan in northern Kyushu, rebelled when the Yamato monarchy attempted to conscript troops to conquer Silla. The Yamato court dispatched Mononobe Karikabi and defeated Iwai in the following year, 528. This rebellion was a major turning point when the Yamato monarchy put Kyushu under direct control. Stone men and stone horses are placed around the tomb, indicating a unique funerary culture.

kora_taisha.name: 高良大社
kora_taisha.highlight: 筑後国一之宮。高良山に鎮座する古代から続く大社
kora_taisha.text: 高良大社は、久留米市の高良山（312m）山頂近くに鎮座する筑後国一之宮で、全国に約450社ある高良神社の総本社です。祭神の高良玉垂命は詳細が謎に包まれており、古代の有力氏族との関係が研究されています。社殿は江戸時代初期に久留米藩主・有馬頼利が再建したもので、国の重要文化財に指定されています。高良山は古くから神聖な山として崇められ、山全体に多くの神社・仏堂が点在していました。筑後川流域を一望する展望台からは、筑紫平野の雄大な景観を楽しめます。
kora_taisha.highlight_en: Chikugo Province Ichinomiya. A shrine that has existed since ancient times on Mt. Kora
kora_taisha.text_en: Kora Taisha Shrine is the main shrine of Chikugo Province, located near the summit of Mt. Kora (312m) in Kurume City, and is the headquarters of the approximately 450 Kora Shrines nationwide. The details of the enshrined deity, Takara Tamada, are shrouded in mystery, and the relationship with the powerful clans of ancient times is being studied. The shrine building was rebuilt by Yoritoshi Arima, the lord of the Kurume domain, in the early Edo period, and has been designated as a national important cultural property. Mt. Takara has been revered as a sacred mountain since ancient times, and there were many shrines and Buddhist temples scattered throughout the mountain. From the observation deck overlooking the Chikugo River basin, you can enjoy the magnificent scenery of the Chikushi Plain.

korokan_ato.name: 鴻臚館跡
korokan_ato.highlight: 遣唐使や外国使節をもてなした国際外交施設の跡
korokan_ato.text: 鴻臚館は、奈良〜平安時代に外国使節の接待や遣唐使の出発拠点として機能した国営の迎賓館です。7世紀後半から11世紀頃まで使われ、福岡（博多）・難波・京都の三か所に置かれていました。博多の鴻臚館は最も重要で、渤海・新羅・唐の使節が滞在し、日本からの使者もここから出発しました。現在の福岡城跡（平和台球場跡）の発掘調査で遺構が確認されており、出土品は当時の日本と東アジアの活発な交流を示しています。鴻臚館跡展示館では発掘された遺構をそのまま見学できます。
korokan_ato.highlight_en: The remains of an international diplomatic facility that hosted envoys and foreign envoys to Tang China.
korokan_ato.text_en: Korokan is a state-run guest house that served as a base for entertaining foreign envoys and as a departure base for envoys sent to Tang Dynasty during the Nara to Heian periods. It was used from the late 7th century to the 11th century, and was placed in three locations: Fukuoka (Hakata), Namba, and Kyoto. Korokan in Hakata is the most important, where envoys from Balhae, Silla, and Tang stayed, and envoys from Japan also departed from here. Remains have been confirmed during excavations of the current Fukuoka Castle ruins (Heiwadai Stadium ruins), and the excavated items show the active exchange between Japan and East Asia at the time. At the Korokan Ruins Exhibition Hall, you can see the excavated remains as they are.

hikosan_jingu.name: 英彦山神宮
hikosan_jingu.highlight: 九州最大の修験道の霊山。最盛期は3000人の修験者が暮らした
hikosan_jingu.text: 英彦山は、奈良時代から続く修験道の霊山で、出羽の羽黒山・紀伊の大峰山と並ぶ日本三大修験山の一つです。最盛期の江戸時代には3000人以上の修験者（山伏）が英彦山に住み、独自の宗教王国を形成していました。祭神は天忍穂耳命で、「彦山」の名は「日の子の山」に由来するとも言われます。1871年の神仏分離令・修験道廃止令により急激に衰退しましたが、現在も石段や坊跡が山中に残り、往時の壮大さを物語っています。英彦山スロープカーを利用して参拝できます。
hikosan_jingu.highlight_en: The largest sacred mountain for Shugendo in Kyushu. At its peak, 3,000 ascetics lived here.
hikosan_jingu.text_en: Mt. Hiko is a sacred mountain for Shugendo that has continued since the Nara period, and is one of the three major Shugendo mountains in Japan, along with Mt. Haguro in Dewa and Mt. Omine in Kii. At its peak in the Edo period, more than 3,000 Shugenja (Yamabushi) lived on Mt. Hiko, forming their own religious kingdom. The enshrined deity is Tennin Homi no Mikoto, and it is said that the name ``Hikoyama'' comes from ``Hiko-no-yama''. Although it rapidly declined in 1871 due to the Separation of Shinto and Buddhism Order and the Abolition of Shugendo, the stone steps and ruins of the temple still remain in the mountains, testifying to the grandeur of the past. You can visit the shrine using the Mt. Hiko slope car.

tatarawa_peace_museum.name: 大刀洗平和記念館
tatarawa_peace_museum.kana: たちあらいへいわきねんかん
tatarawa_peace_museum.highlight: 旧陸軍大刀洗飛行場跡。零戦の実機が展示される平和記念館
tatarawa_peace_museum.text: 大刀洗は、大正〜昭和初期に東洋最大規模を誇った旧陸軍の飛行場があった地です。第一次世界大戦後の1919年に開設され、航空部隊の一大拠点として栄えました。太平洋戦争末期の1945年3月・6月には米軍の大規模な空襲を受け、多くの命が失われました。また、特攻隊員たちが知覧などへ飛び立つ前の中継地点ともなりました。現在の大刀洗平和記念館には、実際に飛行した零式艦上戦闘機（零戦）の実機が展示されており、当時の歴史を生々しく伝えています。
tatarawa_peace_museum.highlight_en: Former Army Tachiarai Air Base ruins. Peace Memorial Museum where actual Zero Fighter aircraft are displayed
tatarawa_peace_museum.text_en: Tachiarai is the site of a former military airfield that boasted the largest scale in the East during the Taisho and early Showa periods. It was opened in 1919 after World War I and prospered as a major base for aviation units. In March and June 1945, during the final stages of the Pacific War, many lives were lost due to large-scale air raids by the U.S. military. It also served as a staging point for suicide bombers before flying off to Chiran and other destinations. The current Tachiarai Peace Memorial Museum displays an actual Zero fighter jet that actually flew, vividly conveying the history of the time.

iwaya_castle_fukuoka.name: 岩屋城跡
iwaya_castle_fukuoka.highlight: 高橋紹運763名が島津軍2万に50日間抵抗した壮絶な籠城戦の地
iwaya_castle_fukuoka.text: 岩屋城は、大友氏の重臣・高橋紹運が守った山城です。1586年、島津義久の北上作戦において、島津軍約2万が岩屋城を包囲しました。紹運はわずか763名の兵で50日以上にわたって籠城を続け、城兵全員が戦死するまで一歩も退きませんでした。この壮絶な抵抗により島津軍は大きな損害を受け、北上の勢いが鈍化。豊臣秀吉の九州征伐に繋がる時間稼ぎとなりました。紹運の息子・立花宗茂はその後九州随一の名将として知られることになります。現在は岩屋城公園として整備されています。
iwaya_castle_fukuoka.highlight_en: The site of a fierce siege battle in which 763 men, Shoun Takahashi, resisted the 20,000 Shimadzu army for 50 days.
iwaya_castle_fukuoka.text_en: Iwaya Castle is a mountain castle protected by Shōun Takahashi, a senior vassal of the Otomo clan. In 1586, during Shimazu Yoshihisa's northern campaign, approximately 20,000 Shimazu troops besieged Iwaya Castle. Shoun remained in siege for more than 50 days with only 763 soldiers, and did not retreat one step until all of the castle's soldiers were killed in battle. This fierce resistance caused the Shimazu army to suffer heavy losses, and its movement northward slowed. It bought time for Toyotomi Hideyoshi's conquest of Kyushu. Shoun's son Muneshige Tachibana later became known as the most famous general in Kyushu. Currently, it is maintained as Iwaya Castle Park.

okinoshima_heritage.name: 沖ノ島（宗像大社沖津宮）
okinoshima_heritage.kana: おきのしまむなかたたいしゃおきつみや

transit.name: 神湊港から船（年1回の神事のみ上陸可）

okinoshima_heritage.highlight: 神宿る禁断の島。4〜9世紀の奉献品8万点が世界遺産に
okinoshima_heritage.text: 沖ノ島は、福岡県宗像市の玄界灘に浮かぶ孤島で、宗像大社の沖津宮が鎮座します。古代から「神宿る島」として崇められ、4〜9世紀に行われた国家的祭祀の奉献品が約8万点発見されました。金製指輪・ガラス製品・中国や朝鮮半島からの舶来品など、当時の日本と東アジアの交流を示す貴重な品々です。島全体が御神体とされており、現在も女人禁制・上陸は年1回の神事参拝者のみという厳格なルールが守られています。2017年に「神宿る島・宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群」として世界遺産に登録されました。
okinoshima_heritage.highlight_en: A forbidden island where a god dwells. 80,000 votive objects from the 4th to 9th centuries become world heritage sites
okinoshima_heritage.text_en: Okinoshima is a solitary island floating in the Genkai Sea in Munakata City, Fukuoka Prefecture, where Okitsu-miya, Munakata Taisha Shrine, is located. It has been revered as the "island where the gods dwell" since ancient times, and about 80,000 offerings from national rituals held from the 4th to 9th centuries have been discovered. These are valuable items that demonstrate the exchange between Japan and East Asia at the time, including gold rings, glassware, and imported items from China and the Korean Peninsula. The entire island is considered a sacred object, and strict rules are still followed, such as no women allowed on the island and only those who come ashore to worship once a year. In 2017, it was registered as a World Heritage Site as the ``Islands inhabited by the Gods, Munakata, Okinoshima, and Related Sites''.

hakata_machiya.name: 博多町家ふるさと館
hakata_machiya.kana: はかたまちやふるさとかん
hakata_machiya.highlight: 明治・大正期の博多商人の暮らしを再現。博多織・博多人形の実演も
hakata_machiya.text: 博多町家ふるさと館は、明治・大正時代に建てられた町家を移築・保存した施設です。博多は古くから大陸との貿易で栄えた商人の町で、「博多商人」は日本の商業史に大きな足跡を残しました。町家の造りには「博多格子」と呼ばれる独特の意匠が施され、狭い間口に奥行きのある「うなぎの寝床」型の構造が特徴です。館内では博多織の実演や博多人形の製作見学ができ、博多どんたく・博多祇園山笠などの祭り文化についても学べます。博多の「町衆」文化が凝縮された施設です。
hakata_machiya.highlight_en: Recreates the life of Hakata merchants during the Meiji and Taisho periods. Demonstration of Hakataori and Hakata dolls
hakata_machiya.text_en: Hakata Machiya Furusatokan is a facility that relocated and preserved the townhouses built during the Meiji and Taisho eras. Hakata has long been a merchant town that has prospered through trade with the continent, and the ``Hakata merchants'' left a huge footprint in Japan's commercial history. The machiya is built with a unique design called ``Hakata lattice,'' and features an ``eel bed'' type structure with a narrow frontage and depth. Inside the museum, you can see demonstrations of Hakata-ori and the production of Hakata dolls, and learn about festival culture such as Hakata Dontaku and Hakata Gion Yamakasa. This facility is a condensation of Hakata's "townsman" culture.

chikuzen_kokubunji.name: 筑前国分寺跡
chikuzen_kokubunji.kana: ちくぜんこくぶんじあと
chikuzen_kokubunji.highlight: 聖武天皇の詔で建てられた筑前の国分寺。七重塔の礎石が残る
chikuzen_kokubunji.text: 筑前国分寺は、741年に聖武天皇が「国分寺建立の詔」を発し、全国60余か国に建てられた国立寺院の一つです。大宰府の官人や商人・庶民の信仰の中心として機能しました。七重塔の礎石が現存しており、往時の壮大な伽藍の規模を偲ぶことができます。近隣には大宰府政庁跡・水城跡・大宰府天満宮が集中しており、古代の大宰府がいかに重要な政治・文化の拠点であったかがわかります。現在も礎石公園として保存・整備されており、無料で見学できます。
chikuzen_kokubunji.highlight_en: Kokubunji Temple in Chikuzen was built by Emperor Shomu's edict. The foundation stone of the seven-storied pagoda remains
chikuzen_kokubunji.text_en: Chikuzen Kokubunji is one of the national temples built in over 60 countries around the country after Emperor Shomu issued an edict to establish Kokubunji in 741. It functioned as a center of worship for Dazaifu's government officials, merchants, and common people. The foundation stones of the seven-storied pagoda still exist, giving us a reminder of the grand scale of the temple in the past. The Dazaifu Government Office Ruins, Mizuki Ruins, and Dazaifu Tenmangu Shrine are located nearby, and you can see how important Dazaifu was as a political and cultural base in ancient times. It is still preserved and maintained as Foundation Stone Park and can be visited for free.

shikanoumi_shrine.name: 志賀海神社
shikanoumi_shrine.highlight: 全国の綿津見神社の総本社。海人族・阿曇族が祀る古社
shikanoumi_shrine.text: 志賀海神社は、玄界灘に浮かぶ志賀島に鎮座する古社で、全国の綿津見神社（海神を祀る神社）の総本社です。海人族の阿曇氏（安曇氏）が代々神職を務め、海の神・綿津見三神を祀っています。阿曇族は古代日本を代表する航海民族で、大陸との交流に重要な役割を果たしました。志賀島は1784年に農民が金印「漢委奴国王」を発見した場所としても有名です。4月と11月に行われる「歩射祭（おしゃさい）」は、国の重要無形民俗文化財に指定されています。
shikanoumi_shrine.highlight_en: Headquarters of Watatsumi Shrines nationwide. An old shrine enshrined by the Kaijin and Azumi tribes
shikanoumi_shrine.text_en: Shikaumi Shrine is an ancient shrine located on Shika Island in the Genkai Sea, and is the headquarters of all Watatsumi Shrines (shrines dedicated to the sea god) nationwide. The Azumi clan (Azumi clan) of the Umajin tribe have served as Shinto priests for generations, and enshrine the three Watatsumi gods, the gods of the sea. The Azumi tribe was a seafaring tribe representing ancient Japan, and played an important role in communicating with the continent. Shikajima is also famous as the place where a farmer discovered the gold seal ``Kan-Kai-no-King'' in 1784. The Oshasai, held in April and November, has been designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property.

ogi_castle_saga.name: 小城城跡・牛尾神社
ogi_castle_saga.kana: おぎじょうあとうしおじんじゃ
ogi_castle_saga.highlight: 佐賀藩の支藩・小城藩3万石の居城跡。桜の名所としても名高い
ogi_castle_saga.text: 小城城は、江戸時代に佐賀藩（鍋島家）の支藩として成立した小城藩の居城です。1607年頃に築かれ、小城鍋島家が3万石を治めました。城は小城の背後にそびえる山に築かれた山城で、現在は石垣と土塁の一部が残ります。城址一帯は桜の名所として知られ、春には多くの花見客が訪れます。麓の牛尾神社は小城藩主の崇敬を受けた神社で、菊の節句の行事が今も行われています。小城市内には「小城羊羹」で知られる老舗和菓子店が軒を連ね、江戸時代の面影を今に伝えます。
ogi_castle_saga.highlight_en: The ruins of a 30,000 koku castle owned by the Ogi domain, a branch domain of the Saga domain. Also famous as a cherry blossom viewing spot
ogi_castle_saga.text_en: Ogi Castle is the residence of the Ogi clan, which was established as a branch domain of the Saga clan (Nabeshima family) during the Edo period. It was built around 1607, and the Ogi Nabeshima family ruled over 30,000 koku. The castle was built on the mountain that rises behind the small castle, and today only some of the stone walls and earthworks remain. The area around the castle ruins is known as a famous cherry blossom viewing spot, and many visitors visit in spring to view the cherry blossoms. Ushio Shrine at the foot of the mountain is a shrine that was revered by the lord of the Ogi domain, and events for the Chrysanthemum Festival are still held today. Ogi City is lined with long-established Japanese confectionery shops known for ``Ogi Yokan'', which still retains the atmosphere of the Edo period.

imari_port_saga.name: 伊万里港・伊万里津の歴史
imari_port_saga.kana: いまりこういまりつのれきし
imari_port_saga.highlight: 有田焼を世界に運んだ港。「伊万里焼」の名はこの積出港に由来する
imari_port_saga.text: 伊万里港（伊万里津）は、江戸時代に有田・波佐見で生産された磁器を積み出した重要な港です。有田で焼かれた磁器は陸路で伊万里まで運ばれ、ここから長崎・出島を経てオランダ東インド会社の船でヨーロッパへと輸出されました。そのため欧州では有田焼のことを「伊万里焼（Imari）」と呼ぶ習慣が生まれました。17世紀後半のヨーロッパでは日本の磁器が王侯貴族の間で空前のブームとなり、マイセンなどのヨーロッパ磁器産業誕生の直接的な刺激となりました。伊万里市の「鍋島藩窯公園」では当時の窯跡を見学できます。
imari_port_saga.name_en: History of Imari Port and Imaritsu
imari_port_saga.highlight_en: The port that transported Arita ware to the world. The name "Imari ware" comes from this shipping port.
imari_port_saga.text_en: Imari Port (Imaritsu) is an important port where porcelain produced in Arita and Hasami was shipped during the Edo period. Porcelain fired in Arita was transported overland to Imari, and from there it was exported to Europe via ships of the Dutch East India Company via Nagasaki and Dejima. For this reason, in Europe a custom was born to call Arita ware "Imari". In Europe in the late 17th century, Japanese porcelain became an unprecedented boom among the royalty and aristocracy, directly stimulating the birth of the European porcelain industry such as Meissen. At Nabeshima Hangama Park in Imari City, you can see the remains of the kiln from that time.

kinryu_shrine_saga.name: 金立神社

transit.name: バス「金立公園前」（昭和バス）

kinryu_shrine_saga.highlight: 神功皇后伝説と徐福伝説が交差する古社。金立山に鎮座する
kinryu_shrine_saga.text: 金立神社は、佐賀市の金立山に鎮座する古社で、神功皇后が三韓征伐の際に立ち寄ったという伝説を持ちます。また、中国の秦の始皇帝の命を受けて不老不死の薬を求めて渡来したとされる徐福が、この地に居住したという伝説も残っており、境内には徐福を祀る祠があります。神功皇后は『古事記』『日本書紀』に記された伝説的な人物で、九州各地に彼女にまつわる伝説が残っています。金立山ハイキングコースを通じて上社・下社の両社を参拝でき、佐賀平野を一望できます。
kinryu_shrine_saga.highlight_en: An old shrine where the legend of Empress Jingu and the legend of Jofuku intersect. Enshrined on Mt. Kintate
kinryu_shrine_saga.text_en: Kindate Shrine is an ancient shrine located on Mt. Kindate in Saga City, and there is a legend that Empress Jingu stopped by during her conquest of the Three Koreas. There is also a legend that Xu Fu, who is said to have come to the temple on the orders of China's Qin Shihuang in search of the elixir of life, resided in this area, and there is a shrine dedicated to Xu Fu on the grounds. Empress Jingu is a legendary figure written in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, and there are legends surrounding her throughout Kyushu. You can visit both Kami-sha and Shimo-sha shrines through the Mt. Kintate hiking course, and enjoy a panoramic view of the Saga plains.

matsura_navy_history.name: 松浦水軍の里（鷹島）
matsura_navy_history.kana: まつらすいぐんのさとたかしま

transit.name: バス「鷹島」（松浦市コミュニティバス）

matsura_navy_history.highlight: 元寇で蒙古軍が壊滅した鷹島。海底に沈んだ元の軍船が眠る
matsura_navy_history.text: 松浦水軍（松浦党）は、北部九州の玄界灘を拠点とした海上武士団です。平安末期から戦国時代にかけて活躍し、倭寇の主力としても知られています。1281年の弘安の役（元寇）では、鷹島沖に約14万の蒙古・高麗連合軍が集結しましたが、暴風雨（神風）によって艦隊が壊滅。鷹島海底には今も多数の元の軍船が沈んでいます。水中考古学の調査によって船体や武器が引き揚げられており、鷹島海底遺跡は国の史跡に指定されています。鷹島歴史民俗資料館で出土品を見学できます。
matsura_navy_history.highlight_en: Takashima, where the Mongolian army was destroyed by the Mongol invasion. The original military ship that sank to the bottom of the ocean lies dormant.
matsura_navy_history.text_en: The Matsuura Suigun (Matsuura Party) was a maritime samurai group based in the Genkai Sea in northern Kyushu. They were active from the end of the Heian period to the Sengoku period, and were also known as the main force of the Japanese pirates. During the Battle of Koan (Mongol Invasion) in 1281, approximately 140,000 Mongolian and Goryeo combined forces gathered off the coast of Takashima, but the fleet was destroyed by a rainstorm (kamikaze). Many of the original warships are still sunk on the Takashima seabed. The hull and weapons have been salvaged through underwater archeological surveys, and the Takashima underwater ruins have been designated as a national historic site. You can view excavated items at the Takashima History and Folklore Museum.

saga_seven_sages.name: 佐賀の七賢人ゆかりの地
saga_seven_sages.kana: さがのしちけんじんゆかりのち
saga_seven_sages.highlight: 副島種臣・江藤新平ら明治維新を支えた「佐賀の七賢人」の出身地
saga_seven_sages.text: 「佐賀の七賢人」とは、幕末〜明治維新期に活躍した佐賀藩出身の7人の偉人を指します。大隈重信（早稲田大学創設・内閣総理大臣）、副島種臣（外務卿）、江藤新平（司法卿・佐賀の乱首謀者）、大木喬任（文部卿）、島義勇（開拓使判官・札幌建設）、佐野常民（日本赤十字社創設）、鍋島直正（佐賀藩近代化の藩主）の7名です。佐賀藩は幕末に均田制改革と西洋技術導入で先進的な藩として知られ、明治政府の中枢に多数の人材を輩出しました。佐賀市内には各人の記念碑・旧居跡が点在しています。
saga_seven_sages.name_en: Places related to the Seven Sages of Saga
saga_seven_sages.highlight_en: Taneomi Soejima and Shinpei Eto Birthplace of the "Seven Sages of Saga" who supported the Meiji Restoration
saga_seven_sages.text_en: The ``Seven Sages of Saga'' refer to seven great figures from the Saga domain who were active from the end of the Edo period to the Meiji Restoration period. The seven members were Shigenobu Okuma (founder of Waseda University and Prime Minister), Taneomi Soejima (Minister of Foreign Affairs), Shinpei Eto (Minister of Justice and mastermind of the Saga Rebellion), Takato Oki (Minister of Education), Yoshiyu Shima (Chief Development Officer and Sapporo Construction), Tsunetami Sano (founder of the Japanese Red Cross Society), and Namasa Nabeshima (lord of the Saga domain for modernization). The Saga domain was known as an advanced domain at the end of the Edo period due to its reform of the Hitota system and the introduction of Western technology, and produced many people who were central to the Meiji government. Saga City is dotted with monuments and ruins of their former residences.

mitsuse_ancient_road.name: 三瀬峠（古代の肥前越え）
mitsuse_ancient_road.kana: みつせとうげこだいのひぜんごえ
mitsuse_ancient_road.highlight: 佐賀と長崎を結ぶ古道。長崎街道の脇道として人・文化・物資が行き交った
mitsuse_ancient_road.text: 三瀬峠は、佐賀平野と背振山地を越えて長崎方面へ向かう峠道です。古代には大陸文化が長崎・平戸方面から九州内陸部へ伝わる経路の一つであり、中世以降は長崎街道の脇街道として商人・旅人・キリシタン宣教師・大名行列が往来しました。江戸時代には長崎から輸入された砂糖・オランダ製品がこの峠を越えて佐賀へ運ばれ、「三瀬越え」として知られていました。明治以降は峠の役割が低下しましたが、現在も三瀬村には古道の石畳や茶屋跡が残り、ハイキングコースとして親しまれています。
mitsuse_ancient_road.name_en: Mise Pass (crossing the ancient Hizen Pass)
mitsuse_ancient_road.highlight_en: An ancient road that connects Saga and Nagasaki. As a side street of the Nagasaki Kaido, people, culture, and goods came and went.
mitsuse_ancient_road.text_en: Mise Pass is a mountain pass that crosses the Saga Plain and the Sefuri Mountains towards Nagasaki. In ancient times, it was one of the routes by which continental culture was transmitted from Nagasaki and Hirado to the interior of Kyushu, and since the Middle Ages, merchants, travelers, Christian missionaries, and processions of feudal lords came and went as a side road to the Nagasaki Highway. During the Edo period, sugar and Dutch products imported from Nagasaki were transported across this pass to Saga, and it was known as ``Mise-goe''. Although the role of the mountain pass declined after the Meiji period, the stone pavement of the old road and the ruins of a tea house still remain in Mise Village, making it a popular hiking course.

hizen_stone_bridges.name: 肥前の石橋群
hizen_stone_bridges.kana: ひぜんのいしばしぐん
hizen_stone_bridges.highlight: 佐賀・長崎県境に残る江戸期の石橋群。肥前の石工技術の結晶
hizen_stone_bridges.text: 肥前地方（佐賀・長崎）には江戸時代に建設された石橋が数多く残っています。これらの石橋は「肥後の石工」と呼ばれる熊本出身の職人集団が技術を持ち込み、九州各地に広めたものです。嬉野市・鹿島市周辺の河川には今も美しい石造アーチ橋が現存しており、中でも塩田川流域の「石橋の郷」は複数の江戸期石橋が連続して残る貴重な景観を保っています。石橋建設には当時最先端の土木技術が用いられており、数百年を経た今も現役で使われているものもあります。
hizen_stone_bridges.highlight_en: A group of stone bridges from the Edo period that remain on the border between Saga and Nagasaki prefectures. The crystallization of Hizen's stonemasonry technology
hizen_stone_bridges.text_en: Many stone bridges built during the Edo period remain in the Hizen region (Saga and Nagasaki). These stone bridges were created by a group of craftsmen from Kumamoto called ``Higo Stonemasons'' who brought their techniques and spread them throughout Kyushu. Beautiful stone arch bridges still exist on the rivers around Ureshino City and Kashima City, and in particular, ``Ishibashi no Sato'' in the Shiota River basin preserves a valuable landscape with several Edo-era stone bridges remaining in a row. The most advanced civil engineering techniques of the time were used to construct the stone bridges, and some of them are still in use today, hundreds of years later.

saga_chikoken.name: 徴古館
saga_chikoken.highlight: 鍋島家が設立した日本最古の私設博物館。佐賀藩の歴史資料を収蔵
saga_chikoken.text: 徴古館は、旧佐賀藩主・鍋島家が1927年（昭和2年）に設立した博物館で、日本最古の私設博物館の一つです。「徴古」とは古いものを集め考証するという意味です。佐賀藩に伝わる武具・調度品・古文書・茶道具などが収蔵されており、鍋島家の歴史と佐賀藩の文化を詳しく知ることができます。隣接する佐賀城本丸歴史館と合わせて見学することで、江戸時代の佐賀藩政の全体像を理解できます。建物自体も昭和初期の洋風建築として価値が高く、国の登録有形文化財に指定されています。
saga_chikoken.highlight_en: Japan's oldest private museum established by the Nabeshima family. Contains historical materials of the Saga Domain
saga_chikoken.text_en: Chokokan is a museum established in 1927 by the Nabeshima family, former lords of the Saga domain, and is one of the oldest private museums in Japan. ``Choko'' means to collect old things and examine them. The museum houses weapons, furniture, old documents, tea utensils, etc. that have been passed down through the Saga clan, allowing you to learn more about the history of the Nabeshima family and the culture of the Saga clan. By visiting this site along with the adjacent Saga Castle Honmaru History Museum, you can get a comprehensive understanding of the Saga domain government during the Edo period. The building itself is highly valuable as a Western-style building from the early Showa period, and has been designated as a nationally registered tangible cultural property.

tara_mountain_religion.name: 多良山系の山岳信仰
tara_mountain_religion.kana: たらさんけいのさんがくしんこう
tara_mountain_religion.highlight: 佐賀・長崎県境の霊峰。経ヶ岳を中心に古代から続く神仏習合の聖地
tara_mountain_religion.text: 多良山系は、佐賀県と長崎県にまたがる山地で、最高峰の経ヶ岳（1,076m）を中心に古代から山岳信仰の場として崇められてきました。山中には多良岳修験道の拠点となった「金泉寺」が今も残り、役行者が開いたとされる霊地が各所に点在しています。江戸時代には肥前の大名や庶民の信仰を集め、霊山への参詣が盛んに行われました。神仏習合時代の石仏・石塔が山中に残り、廃仏毀釈後も地元の人々によって守られてきました。現在は多良山系の自然公園としてトレッキングが楽しめます。
tara_mountain_religion.name_en: Mountain worship of the Tara mountain range
tara_mountain_religion.highlight_en: A sacred mountain on the border of Saga and Nagasaki prefectures. A sacred place of syncretism of Shinto and Buddhism that has continued since ancient times, centered on Mt. Kyogadake.
tara_mountain_religion.text_en: The Tara Mountain Range is a mountainous area that straddles Saga and Nagasaki prefectures, and has been revered as a place of mountain worship since ancient times, with its highest peak, Kyogadake (1,076m). Kinsen-ji Temple, the base of Mt. Taradake Shugendo, still remains in the mountains, and there are spiritual sites scattered throughout the area that are said to have been founded by En no Gyoja. During the Edo period, it attracted the faith of the feudal lords and common people of Hizen, and pilgrimages to the sacred mountain were actively held. Stone Buddhas and stone pagodas from the period of syncretization of Shinto and Buddhism remain in the mountains, and have been protected by local people even after the abolition of Buddhism. Nowadays, you can enjoy trekking as a natural park in the Tara Mountains.

kawakamikyo_history.name: 川上峡（熊の川温泉）の歴史
kawakamikyo_history.kana: かわかみきょうくまのかわおんせんのれきし
kawakamikyo_history.highlight: 「肥前の嵐山」と称される峡谷美。佐賀藩の奥座敷として栄えた温泉地
kawakamikyo_history.text: 川上峡は、嘉瀬川の清流が刻んだ渓谷で、桜・紅葉の名所として「肥前の嵐山」と呼ばれます。渓谷沿いには熊の川温泉が湧き、江戸時代から佐賀藩士や庶民の湯治場として利用されてきました。明治時代には西洋医学の観点からも炭酸水素塩泉の効能が注目され、近代的な温泉地として発展しました。川上峡は大正時代の観光開発で観光船（どんこ舟）による川下りが始まり、現在も続けられています。春の桜シーズンには渓谷両岸の桜が水面に映り、幻想的な景観を楽しめます。
kawakamikyo_history.highlight_en: The beauty of the gorge is known as ``Hizen's Arashiyama.'' A hot spring area that flourished as the inner quarters of the Saga clan
kawakamikyo_history.text_en: Kawakami Gorge is a valley carved by the clear waters of the Kasegawa River, and is known as ``Hizen's Arashiyama'' as a famous spot for viewing cherry blossoms and autumn leaves. Kumanogawa Onsen springs up along the valley, and has been used as a spa for Saga feudal samurai and common people since the Edo period. During the Meiji period, the efficacy of hydrogen carbonate springs attracted attention from the perspective of Western medicine, and the area developed into a modern hot spring resort. Kawakami Gorge was developed for tourism during the Taisho era, and sightseeing boats (donko boats) began to be used to travel down the river, and this continues to this day. During the spring cherry blossom season, the cherry blossoms on both banks of the valley are reflected in the water, creating a fantastic scenery.

tsushima_shimizuyama.name: 清水山城跡
tsushima_shimizuyama.kana: しみずやまじょうあと

transit.name: バス「厳原」（対馬島内バス）

tsushima_shimizuyama.highlight: 文禄・慶長の役（朝鮮出兵）で築かれた対馬の山城。三段の石垣が壮観
tsushima_shimizuyama.text: 清水山城は、1591年の文禄の役に備えて豊臣秀吉の命により対馬の宗義智が築いた山城です。標高約200メートルの山頂に三の丸・二の丸・本丸が段状に配置され、総石垣造りの堅固な城でした。文禄・慶長の役（1592〜1598年）において、対馬は朝鮮半島への出兵の中継基地となり、多くの兵や物資がここを経由しました。宗氏は対馬と朝鮮の間で外交・貿易を担う特殊な立場にあり、戦後も朝鮮との国交回復に尽力しました。現在も見事な石垣が山上に残り、見晴らしも抜群です。
tsushima_shimizuyama.highlight_en: A mountain castle in Tsushima built during the Bunroku and Keicho wars (the dispatch of troops to Korea). The three-tiered stone wall is spectacular
tsushima_shimizuyama.text_en: Shimizuyama Castle is a mountain castle built by Mune Yoshitomo of Tsushima on the orders of Toyotomi Hideyoshi in preparation for the Bunroku War in 1591. It was a strong castle built entirely of stone walls, with Sannomaru, Ninomaru, and Honmaru arranged in steps on the mountaintop at an altitude of about 200 meters. During the Bunroku-Keicho War (1592-1598), Tsushima became a relay base for dispatching troops to the Korean Peninsula, and many soldiers and supplies passed through here. Mr. So was in a unique position in charge of diplomacy and trade between Tsushima and Korea, and even after the war he worked hard to restore diplomatic relations with Korea. Today, the beautiful stone wall still remains on the mountain, and the view is outstanding.

ikitsuki_hidden_christian.name: 生月島・隠れキリシタンの里
ikitsuki_hidden_christian.kana: いきつきしまかくれきりしたんのさと

transit.name: バス「生月大橋」（西肥バス）

ikitsuki_hidden_christian.highlight: 200年以上の禁教下で独自の信仰を守り続けた隠れキリシタンの島
ikitsuki_hidden_christian.text: 生月島（長崎県平戸市）は、江戸時代の禁教令下で独自のキリシタン信仰を守り続けた「隠れキリシタン」の島として知られます。16世紀にフランシスコ・ザビエルやガスパール・ヴィレラらが布教し、島の大部分の住民がキリスト教に改宗しました。しかし江戸幕府の禁教令（1614年〜）により表向きは仏教・神道に改宗しながら、「オラショ」と呼ばれるラテン語の祈りや独自の聖像を密かに伝えました。明治の禁教解禁後も「かくれ」の信仰形態を守り続けた人々がおり、その信仰は世界遺産関連遺産にも登録されています。
ikitsuki_hidden_christian.highlight_en: An island of hidden Christians who continued to maintain their unique faith despite the ban on Christianity for over 200 years.
ikitsuki_hidden_christian.text_en: Ikitsuki Island (Hirado City, Nagasaki Prefecture) is known as the island of "hidden Christians" who continued to maintain their unique Christian faith under the ban on Christianity during the Edo period. In the 16th century, Francis Xavier and Gaspar Villera spread the word, and most of the island's inhabitants converted to Christianity. However, due to the Edo shogunate's ban on Christianity (from 1614), while ostensibly converting to Buddhism and Shinto, they secretly passed on the Latin prayers called ``orasho'' and their own sacred images. Even after the ban on Christianity was lifted in the Meiji period, there were people who continued to adhere to the "Kakure" form of faith, and their faith has been registered as a World Heritage Site.

fukuejima_castle_nagasaki.name: 福江城跡（石田城）
fukuejima_castle_nagasaki.kana: ふくえじょうあとやつしろじょう

transit.name: 長崎港からフェリー約3時間

fukuejima_castle_nagasaki.highlight: 日本最後の海城。幕末の異国船対策で幕府が築城を許可した
fukuejima_castle_nagasaki.text: 福江城（石田城）は、五島列島の福江島にあった城で、1863年に完成した日本で最後に築かれた城の一つです。五島藩主・五島盛成が外国船の侵入に備えるため幕府の許可を得て築城しましたが、完成の翌年に大政奉還が行われ、実戦に使われることはありませんでした。城は海に面した「海城」で、城壁が直接海に接する珍しい構造を持ちます。明治後に陸軍の施設として使用され、現在は五島高等学校の敷地となっています。石垣と堀が残り、桜の名所でもあります。五島氏は中世から五島を支配した海の豪族で、倭寇との関係も深い氏族でした。
fukuejima_castle_nagasaki.highlight_en: Japan's last sea castle. At the end of the Edo period, the Shogunate allowed the construction of castles as a countermeasure against foreign ships.
fukuejima_castle_nagasaki.text_en: Fukue Castle (Ishida Castle) was a castle located on Fukue Island in the Goto Islands, and was one of the last castles built in Japan, completed in 1863. Morinari Goto, the lord of the Goto domain, built the castle with permission from the shogunate in order to protect against intrusion by foreign ships, but the castle was restored to power the year after its completion and was never used in actual combat. The castle is a "sea castle" facing the sea, and has an unusual structure where the castle walls directly touch the sea. After the Meiji period, it was used as an army facility and is currently the site of Goto High School. The stone walls and moat remain, and it is also a famous spot for cherry blossom viewing. The Goto clan was a powerful maritime clan that had ruled Goto since the Middle Ages, and had close ties to the Wakō (Japanese pirates).

unzen_martyrs.name: 雲仙地獄（キリシタン殉教地）
unzen_martyrs.kana: うんぜんじごくきりしたんじゅんきょうち
unzen_martyrs.highlight: 江戸初期、多数のキリシタンが熱湯責めにされた凄惨な殉教の地
unzen_martyrs.text: 雲仙地獄は、長崎県雲仙市に広がる活火山の噴気地帯で、1627〜1629年にキリシタン弾圧のため多くのキリシタンが熱湯や硫黄ガスで処刑された場所です。この拷問は「雲仙責め」と呼ばれ、100℃近い熱湯の中に信徒を少しずつ沈めるという凄惨なものでした。宣教師コルネリウス・ハスケルら外国人宣教師を含む多くの殉教者が出ました。小説家・遠藤周作の名作『沈黙』もこの時代のキリシタン弾圧を題材にしています。現在は観光地として整備されていますが、殉教碑が建てられ、犠牲者の記憶を伝えています。
unzen_martyrs.highlight_en: A place of horrific martyrdom where many Christians were tortured with boiling water in the early Edo period.
unzen_martyrs.text_en: Unzen Jigoku is a fumarolic area of ​​an active volcano located in Unzen City, Nagasaki Prefecture, and is the place where many Christians were executed with boiling water and sulfur gas during the oppression of Christians from 1627 to 1629. This torture was called ``Unzen Torture,'' and it was a gruesome process in which the believers were gradually submerged in boiling water of nearly 100 degrees Celsius. There were many martyrs, including foreign missionaries such as missionary Cornelius Haskell. Novelist Shusaku Endo's masterpiece ``Silence'' also deals with the oppression of Christians during this period. Although it is currently being developed as a tourist destination, a martyrdom monument has been erected to commemorate the victims.

nagasaki_tojin_yashiki.name: 唐人屋敷跡

transit.name: 路面電車「新地中華街」駅

nagasaki_tojin_yashiki.highlight: 出島のオランダ人と並ぶ存在。中国人商人が集住した長崎の異空間
nagasaki_tojin_yashiki.text: 唐人屋敷は、1689年に幕府が中国人商人を管理するために長崎に設置した居住地です。出島のオランダ商館と並ぶ鎖国時代の対外貿易の窓口でした。最盛期には2000人もの中国人が居住し、土神堂・観音堂・天后堂・福建会館など多くの廟が建てられました。現在も土神堂と観音堂は当時の建物が残っており、中国式の建築様式が独特の雰囲気を醸し出しています。長崎の「ちゃんぽん」「皿うどん」などの食文化や、長崎くんちの「龍踊り」などは唐人屋敷を介した中国文化の影響を強く受けています。
nagasaki_tojin_yashiki.highlight_en: An existence comparable to the Dutch of Dejima. A different space in Nagasaki where Chinese merchants lived together
nagasaki_tojin_yashiki.text_en: Tojin Yashiki is a residential area established in Nagasaki by the Shogunate in 1689 to control Chinese merchants. Along with the Dutch trading post on Dejima, it was a gateway for foreign trade during the period of national isolation. At its peak, as many as 2,000 Chinese lived there, and many temples were built, including the Tushen Hall, Guan Yin Hall, Tianhou Hall, and the Fujian Hall. Today, the original buildings of Toshindo and Kannondo still remain, and the Chinese architectural style creates a unique atmosphere. Nagasaki's food culture, such as ``Champon'' and ``Sara Udon,'' as well as Nagasaki Kunchi's ``Dragon Dance,'' are strongly influenced by Chinese culture through Tojin Yashiki.

omura_castle_ruins.name: 大村城跡（玖島城）
omura_castle_ruins.kana: おおむらじょうあとくしまじょう
omura_castle_ruins.highlight: 日本初のキリシタン大名・大村純忠の地。桜の名所としても名高い
omura_castle_ruins.text: 大村城（玖島城）は、大村湾に面した水城で、戦国時代の大村藩主・大村純忠が整備した城です。大村純忠は1563年に洗礼を受けた日本初のキリシタン大名として知られ、領内でのキリスト教布教を積極的に許可しました。純忠は1580年に長崎港をイエズス会に寄進するという大胆な決断も行っています。江戸時代には大村藩の政庁として機能し、石垣が今も大村公園として残っています。桜の名所として有名で、日本さくら名所100選にも選ばれています。大村市は長崎空港の所在地でもあります。
omura_castle_ruins.highlight_en: The land of Japan's first Christian daimyo, Sumitada Omura. Also famous as a cherry blossom viewing spot
omura_castle_ruins.text_en: Omura Castle (Kushima Castle) is a water castle facing Omura Bay, and was built by Sumitada Omura, the lord of the Omura domain during the Sengoku period. Sumitada Omura is known as Japan's first Christian daimyo who was baptized in 1563, and actively allowed Christianity to be spread within his territory. Sumitada also made the bold decision to donate Nagasaki Port to the Society of Jesus in 1580. During the Edo period, it functioned as the government office of the Omura domain, and the stone walls still remain as Omura Park. It is famous as a cherry blossom viewing spot and has been selected as one of Japan's top 100 cherry blossom viewing spots. Omura City is also the location of Nagasaki Airport.

sasebo_kujukushima_hist.name: 九十九島と海の歴史
sasebo_kujukushima_hist.kana: くじゅうくしまとうみのれきし
sasebo_kujukushima_hist.highlight: リアス式海岸に浮かぶ208の島々。中世には松浦水軍・倭寇の根拠地
sasebo_kujukushima_hist.text: 九十九島は、長崎県北部の佐世保市から平戸市にかけて広がるリアス式海岸に点在する208の島々です（「九十九」は「無数に多い」という意味）。中世にはこの複雑な海域を熟知した松浦水軍（倭寇）の絶好の根拠地となり、大陸との交易・抗争に活躍しました。近代には佐世保が海軍の拠点となり、九十九島周辺の海は軍事的に重要な水域となりました。太平洋戦争末期には特攻艇「震洋」の基地も置かれました。現在は西海国立公園として保護されており、遊覧船やカヤックで島々を巡ることができます。
sasebo_kujukushima_hist.name_en: History of Kujukushima and the sea
sasebo_kujukushima_hist.highlight_en: 208 islands floating on the ria coast. In the Middle Ages, it was the base of the Matsuura Navy and Wakō.
sasebo_kujukushima_hist.text_en: Kujukushima is a group of 208 islands dotted along the ria coastline that stretches from Sasebo City to Hirado City in northern Nagasaki Prefecture (``kujuku'' means ``infinitely many''). In the Middle Ages, it became a perfect base for the Matsuura Navy (Wakou), who were well versed in this complex sea area, and were active in trade and conflict with the continent. In modern times, Sasebo became a naval base, and the sea around Kujukushima became an important military area. At the end of the Pacific War, it was also the base for the special attack boat "Shinyo". It is now protected as Saikai National Park, and you can tour the islands by sightseeing boat or kayak.

goto_hidden_christian.name: 五島・頭ヶ島天主堂周辺の隠れキリシタン
goto_hidden_christian.kana: ごとうかしらがしまてんしゅどうしゅうへんのかくれきりしたん
goto_hidden_christian.highlight: 禁教期に五島へ移住した外海のキリシタン集落。珊瑚礁石の天主堂が圧巻
goto_hidden_christian.text: 五島列島は、長崎県の外海地方（現西彼杵郡外海町）から移住してきた隠れキリシタンの子孫が多く暮らす地域です。18世紀末〜19世紀初頭、人口増加と耕地不足に悩む外海の農民が五島藩の招きを受けてこの地に移住しました。禁教下での移住であったため、信仰は秘密裏に守り続けられました。明治の禁教解禁後、各地に天主堂が建てられ、頭ヶ島天主堂は珊瑚礁の石で建てられた珍しい教会として世界遺産（長崎と天草地方の潜伏キリシタン関連遺産）に登録されています。
goto_hidden_christian.name_en: Hidden Christians around Goto and Kashiragashima Cathedral
goto_hidden_christian.highlight_en: A Christian village in Sotome that migrated to Goto during the period when Christianity was prohibited. The coral reef stone cathedral is a masterpiece
goto_hidden_christian.text_en: The Goto Islands is an area where many descendants of Hidden Christians who immigrated from the Sotome region of Nagasaki Prefecture (currently Sotome Town, Nishisonogi District) live. From the end of the 18th century to the beginning of the 19th century, farmers from Sotome, who were suffering from population growth and lack of arable land, moved to this area at the invitation of the Goto clan. Because they migrated under a ban on religion, their faith was kept secret. After the ban on Christianity was lifted in the Meiji period, cathedrals were built in various places, and Kashiragashima Cathedral is registered as a World Heritage Site (Hidden Christian Sites in the Nagasaki and Amakusa Regions) as a rare church built with coral reef stone.

nagasaki_mitsubishi_shipyard.name: 三菱長崎造船所史跡
nagasaki_mitsubishi_shipyard.kana: みつびしながさきぞうせんじょしせき
nagasaki_mitsubishi_shipyard.highlight: 明治の近代化を象徴する造船所。世界遺産「明治日本の産業革命遺産」の一部
nagasaki_mitsubishi_shipyard.text: 三菱長崎造船所は、1857年に幕府が設立した「長崎鎔鉄所」を起源とし、明治時代に岩崎弥太郎が創業した三菱が引き継いで発展させた造船所です。日本の近代造船業の発祥地の一つであり、国産初の大型蒸気客船や軍艦を次々と建造しました。太平洋戦争中は戦艦「武蔵」もここで建造されています。「ジャイアントカンチレバークレーン」（1909年製）をはじめとする複数の史跡が「明治日本の産業革命遺産」として世界遺産に登録されています。史跡ミュージアム「三菱重工長崎造船所 第三ドック」では往時の設備を見学できます。
nagasaki_mitsubishi_shipyard.highlight_en: A shipyard that symbolizes the modernization of the Meiji era. Part of the World Heritage Site “Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution”
nagasaki_mitsubishi_shipyard.text_en: The Mitsubishi Nagasaki Shipyard is a shipyard that originated from the Nagasaki Tsuba Tetsujo, which was established by the Shogunate in 1857, and was taken over and developed by Mitsubishi, which was founded by Yataro Iwasaki in the Meiji era. It is one of the birthplaces of Japan's modern shipbuilding industry, and built many of the first domestically produced large steam passenger ships and warships. The battleship Musashi was also built here during the Pacific War. Several historical sites, including the "Giant Cantilever Crane" (built in 1909), are registered as World Heritage Sites as "Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution." At the historical site museum ``Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Nagasaki Shipyard & Machinery Works Third Dock,'' you can see the equipment of yesteryear.

shimabara_bukeyashiki.name: 島原武家屋敷群
shimabara_bukeyashiki.kana: しまばらぶけやしきぐん
shimabara_bukeyashiki.highlight: 島原城下に残る江戸期の武家屋敷。清水が流れる水路が今も現役
shimabara_bukeyashiki.text: 島原の武家屋敷群は、島原城の城下町として整備された江戸時代の武士の住まいが現存する貴重な地区です。屋敷の前には清水が流れる水路が設けられており、今もその水路が現役で使われています。島原は1637〜1638年の島原・天草一揆（島原の乱）の舞台となった地で、乱後は松平家が藩主として入り、厳格な藩政が続きました。武家屋敷の一部は内部を公開しており、当時の生活様式を垣間見ることができます。島原城とともに城下町の雰囲気が良く保存されており、散策が楽しめます。
shimabara_bukeyashiki.highlight_en: A samurai residence from the Edo period that remains in Shimabara Castle. The canal where fresh water flows is still in use today.
shimabara_bukeyashiki.text_en: The samurai residences in Shimabara are a valuable area where the residences of samurai from the Edo period, which was developed as a castle town for Shimabara Castle, still exist. In front of the mansion, there was a waterway through which fresh water flows, and this waterway is still in use today. Shimabara was the site of the Shimabara-Amakusa Uprising (Shimabara Rebellion) of 1637-1638. After the rebellion, the Matsudaira family became the feudal lords and a strict feudal government continued. Some of the samurai residences are open to the public, allowing you to get a glimpse of the lifestyle of the time. Along with Shimabara Castle, the atmosphere of the castle town has been well preserved and you can enjoy a walk.

reigando_musashi.name: 霊巌洞（宮本武蔵・五輪書の地）
reigando_musashi.kana: れいがんどうみやもとむさしごりんのしょのち
reigando_musashi.highlight: 宮本武蔵が兵法書『五輪書』を著した岩窟。晩年の武蔵が悟りを開いた地
reigando_musashi.text: 霊巌洞は、熊本市西区の金峰山中腹にある岩窟で、剣豪・宮本武蔵が晩年を過ごし、不朽の兵法書『五輪書』を著した地として知られます。武蔵は1640年頃に細川忠利の招きで熊本に来て以来、この地に籠もって修行と執筆に励みました。1645年に完成した『五輪書』は、地・水・火・風・空の五巻からなり、武道のみならず経営・戦略論として現代でも世界的に読まれています。洞窟内には武蔵の像が安置されており、霊巌洞入口には羅漢像が立ち並ぶ「五百羅漢」も見どころです。武蔵はこの執筆を終えた2週間後に没しました。
reigando_musashi.name_en: Reigan Cave (Land of Miyamoto Musashi's Book of Five Rings)
reigando_musashi.highlight_en: The rock cave where Miyamoto Musashi wrote his book of military tactics, ``The Book of Five Rings''. The place where Musashi achieved enlightenment in his later years
reigando_musashi.text_en: Reigan Cave is a rock cave located halfway up Mt. Kinpu in Nishi Ward, Kumamoto City, and is known as the place where the master swordsman Miyamoto Musashi spent his later years writing his timeless martial arts book, ``The Book of Five Rings.'' Musashi came to Kumamoto around 1640 at the invitation of Tadatoshi Hosokawa, and since then he has remained in this area, devoting himself to training and writing. Completed in 1645, the Book of Five Rings consists of five volumes: Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, and Sky, and is read worldwide today not only as a theory of martial arts but also as a theory of management and strategy. A statue of Musashi is enshrined inside the cave, and the ``500 Arhats'' lined with statues of Arhats at the entrance to Reigan Cave are also worth seeing. Musashi passed away two weeks after finishing this writing.

kumamoto_kokai_school.name: 熊本洋学校跡（旧済々黌）
kumamoto_kokai_school.kana: くまもとようがっこうあときゅうせいせいこう

transit.name: 市電「熊本城・市役所前」

kumamoto_kokai_school.highlight: ジェーンズ大尉が近代教育を伝えた熊本の文明開化の拠点
kumamoto_kokai_school.text: 熊本洋学校は、1871年（明治4年）に細川藩（熊本藩）の払い下げを受けた旧藩校の跡地に設立された近代教育施設です。お雇い外国人・ルロイ・ジャニン・ジェーンズ（Leroy Lansing Janes）大尉がアメリカから招かれ、英語・数学・自然科学などの近代学問を教えました。ジェーンズの感化を受けた生徒たちは1876年に「熊本バンド」と呼ばれるキリスト教信仰集会を結成し、その後の日本のキリスト教界・文化界に多大な影響を与えました。海老名弾正・金森通倫・小崎弘道らがここで学んでいます。
kumamoto_kokai_school.name_en: Kumamoto Western School Ruins (formerly Saisei School)
kumamoto_kokai_school.highlight_en: The base of civilization and enlightenment in Kumamoto, where Captain Janes introduced modern education.
kumamoto_kokai_school.text_en: Kumamoto Western School is a modern educational facility established in 1871 (Meiji 4) on the site of a former domain school sold by the Hosokawa clan (Kumamoto clan). A hired foreigner, Captain Leroy Lansing Janes, was invited from America to teach modern subjects such as English, mathematics, and natural science. In 1876, students inspired by Janes formed a Christian congregation called the Kumamoto Band, which had a great influence on the Christian and cultural worlds of Japan thereafter. Danjo Ebina, Michitori Kanamori, Hiromichi Ozaki and others studied here.

aso_caldera_ancient.name: 阿蘇カルデラと古代の祭祀
aso_caldera_ancient.kana: あそかるでらとこだいのさいし
aso_caldera_ancient.highlight: 世界最大級のカルデラに刻まれた人類の歴史。縄文時代から続く火山信仰
aso_caldera_ancient.text: 阿蘇カルデラは、南北25km・東西18kmの世界最大級のカルデラで、約9万年前の巨大噴火によって形成されました。カルデラ内には現在も約5万人が生活しており、世界でも類例のない「カルデラ内居住」の景観を呈しています。縄文時代からこの地に人々が暮らした証拠が発掘されており、阿蘇の火山を神として崇める信仰は古代から続いています。阿蘇神社の「火振り神事」は国の重要無形民俗文化財で、火山の神への感謝と鎮火祈願が今も続けられています。中岳火口の活発な噴煙は、人々が火山と共生してきた歴史を象徴しています。
aso_caldera_ancient.highlight_en: Human history carved in one of the world's largest calderas. Volcano belief that has continued since the Jomon period
aso_caldera_ancient.text_en: Aso Caldera is one of the world's largest calderas, measuring 25 km from north to south and 18 km from east to west, and was formed by a huge eruption about 90,000 years ago. Approximately 50,000 people still live within the caldera, creating a landscape that is unique in the world. Evidence has been unearthed that people have lived in this area since the Jomon period, and the faith that worships Aso's volcano as a god has continued since ancient times. Aso Shrine's ``Hifuri Shinto ritual'' is a nationally designated Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property, and continues to this day to give thanks to the volcano god and pray for the fire to be extinguished. The active plume of the Nakadake crater symbolizes the history of people coexisting with volcanoes.

minamata_modern_history.name: 水俣・近代産業と歴史
minamata_modern_history.kana: みなまたきんだいさんぎょうとれきし
minamata_modern_history.highlight: 近代化学工業の発展と水俣病。日本の産業史と環境史の原点
minamata_modern_history.text: 水俣は、1907年（明治40年）に日本窒素肥料（現チッソ）の工場が設立されて以来、近代化学工業の一大拠点として発展した城下町ならぬ「企業城下町」です。最盛期には工場が市の経済を支配し、水俣は九州有数の工業都市でした。しかし1950年代から有機水銀を含む廃水の海洋排出により、深刻な公害病「水俣病」が発生。1956年の公式確認後も長年にわたる被害が続き、多くの患者が苦しみました。水俣病は日本の四大公害病の一つとして世界に知られ、環境保護・人権問題の観点から国際的にも重要な教訓を残しています。
minamata_modern_history.highlight_en: The development of modern chemical industry and Minamata disease. The origins of Japan's industrial and environmental history
minamata_modern_history.text_en: Minamata is not just a castle town, but a ``corporate castle town'' that has developed as a major base for modern chemical industry since the Nippon Nitrogen Fertilizer (currently Chisso) factory was established in 1907 (Meiji 40). At its peak, factories dominated the city's economy, making Minamata one of the leading industrial cities in Kyushu. However, starting in the 1950s, the discharge of wastewater containing organic mercury into the ocean caused a serious pollution disease called Minamata disease. Even after its official confirmation in 1956, the damage continued for many years, and many patients suffered. Minamata disease is known around the world as one of Japan's four major pollution-related diseases, and has left important lessons internationally from the perspective of environmental protection and human rights issues.

aso_shrine_main.name: 阿蘇神社
aso_shrine_main.highlight: 全国約500社の阿蘇神社の総本社。日本三大楼門の一つを持つ古社
aso_shrine_main.text: 阿蘇神社は、全国に約450社ある阿蘇神社の総本社で、創建は約2300年前とされる肥後国一之宮です。阿蘇の神（健磐龍命・阿蘇都媛命など十二神）を祀り、阿蘇大宮司家（阿蘇家）が代々神職を務めてきました。阿蘇家は南北朝時代に南朝方として活躍し、戦国時代には島津氏・大友氏と抗争しました。楼門は「日本三大楼門」の一つとして国の重要文化財に指定されていましたが、2016年の熊本地震で倒壊し、現在修復工事が進んでいます。3月の「火振り神事」は田の神への感謝を表す国の重要無形民俗文化財です。
aso_shrine_main.highlight_en: Headquarters of approximately 500 Aso Shrines nationwide. An old shrine with one of Japan's three major tower gates
aso_shrine_main.text_en: Aso Shrine is the headquarters of approximately 450 Aso Shrines nationwide, and is said to have been founded approximately 2,300 years ago. It enshrines the gods of Aso (twelve gods such as Keniwa Ryu no Mikoto and Aso Tsuhime no Mikoto), and the Aso Daiguji family (Aso family) has served as the Shinto priest for generations. The Aso family was active as a member of the Southern Court during the period of the Northern and Southern Courts, and fought against the Shimazu and Otomo clans during the Sengoku period. The tower gate was designated as a national important cultural property as one of Japan's three major tower gates, but it collapsed in the 2016 Kumamoto earthquake, and restoration work is currently underway. The ``Hifuri Shinto ritual'' held in March is a national important intangible folk cultural property that expresses gratitude to the god of rice fields.

yamaga_ancient_culture.name: 山鹿温泉と菊池川流域の古代文化
yamaga_ancient_culture.kana: やまがおんせんときくちかわりゅういきのこだいぶんか

transit.name: バス「山鹿バスセンター」（産交バス）

yamaga_ancient_culture.highlight: 装飾古墳の宝庫・菊池川流域。山鹿灯籠まつりの伝統が息づく温泉地
yamaga_ancient_culture.text: 山鹿市は、熊本県北部の菊池川流域に位置し、古来から「山鹿の湯」として知られる温泉地です。神武天皇の東征伝説や景行天皇の巡行伝説とも結びついた由緒ある地で、周辺には多数の古墳が分布しています。特に装飾古墳（石室内壁に絵が描かれた古墳）の密集地として知られ、チブサン古墳・オブサン古墳などが保存されています。山鹿灯籠まつりは、頭上に和紙製の灯籠を乗せた女性が踊る「千人灯籠踊り」で有名で、国の重要無形民俗文化財に指定されています。江戸時代には豊前街道の宿場町として栄えました。
yamaga_ancient_culture.name_en: Yamaga Onsen and the ancient culture of the Kikuchi River basin
yamaga_ancient_culture.highlight_en: The Kikuchi River basin is a treasure trove of decorated tombs. A hot spring resort where the tradition of the Yamaga Lantern Festival lives on
yamaga_ancient_culture.text_en: Yamaga City is located in the Kikuchi River basin in northern Kumamoto Prefecture, and is a hot spring area known since ancient times as ``Yamaga no Yu.'' It is a historic place that is associated with the legend of Emperor Jimmu's expedition to the East and the legend of Emperor Keiko's pilgrimage, and there are many ancient tombs scattered around the area. It is especially known as a place with a large concentration of decorated tumuli (tumuli with paintings painted on the walls of their stone interiors), including the Chibusan tumulus and Obsan tumulus. The Yamaga Toro Festival is famous for its ``Sennin Toro Odori'' dance performed by women carrying Japanese paper lanterns on their heads, and has been designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property. During the Edo period, it flourished as a post town on the Buzen Kaido.

hitoyoshi_kumagawa.name: 人吉・球磨川の林業と焼酎文化
hitoyoshi_kumagawa.kana: ひとよしくまがわのりんぎょうとしょうちゅうぶんか
hitoyoshi_kumagawa.highlight: 球磨川の急流を利用した木材流送と球磨焼酎。人吉盆地の豊かな産業史
hitoyoshi_kumagawa.text: 人吉盆地は、球磨川が形成した盆地で、相良氏が700年にわたって治めた地域です。球磨川は日本三大急流の一つで、山間部から切り出された木材を川下りで運ぶ「木材流送」が江戸時代から行われ、林業が地域の主要産業でした。また、盆地の豊富な湧水と良質な米を利用した「球磨焼酎」の醸造も盛んで、全国唯一の「球磨焼酎」（地理的表示）として知られます。人吉温泉も古くから知られ、「温泉地」としての歴史も長い。2020年の球磨川大水害では甚大な被害を受けましたが、復興が進んでいます。
hitoyoshi_kumagawa.name_en: Forestry and shochu culture in Hitoyoshi/Kuma River
hitoyoshi_kumagawa.highlight_en: Wood transportation and Kuma shochu using the rapids of the Kuma River. Hitoyoshi Basin's rich industrial history
hitoyoshi_kumagawa.text_en: The Hitoyoshi Basin is a basin formed by the Kuma River, and is an area ruled by the Sagara clan for 700 years. The Kuma River is one of Japan's three major rapids, and the ``timber transport'' process of transporting wood cut from the mountains downriver has been practiced since the Edo period, and forestry was the main industry in the area. In addition, brewing of ``Kuma Shochu'' using the basin's abundant spring water and high quality rice is popular, and it is known as the only ``Kuma Shochu'' (Geographical Indication) in Japan. Hitoyoshi Onsen has also been known for a long time, and has a long history as a hot spring resort. Although the area suffered severe damage in the 2020 Kuma River flood, reconstruction is progressing.

upper_amakusa_history.name: 上天草・龍ヶ岳の製塩と島の歴史
upper_amakusa_history.kana: かみあまくさりゅうがたけのせいえんとしまのれきし

transit.name: バス「龍ヶ岳」（天草市バス）

upper_amakusa_history.highlight: 有明海に面した島々の製塩と漁業。天草四郎の足跡が残る隠れ里
upper_amakusa_history.text: 上天草市（旧龍ヶ岳町・松島町・大矢野町・姫戸町）は、天草上島の北部に位置し、有明海と八代海に囲まれた島々からなります。江戸時代には製塩業が盛んで、有明海の海水を利用した塩田が各地に設けられていました。1637〜1638年の島原・天草一揆では、天草四郎時貞が活躍した地域に近く、一揆参加者が立て篭もったとされる遺構も残っています。一揆後の急激な人口減少により他藩からの移住が進み、独特の人口構成と文化が形成されました。リアス式海岸と多島海の景観は「天草松島」として知られる名勝です。
upper_amakusa_history.name_en: Kamiamakusa/Mt. Ryugatake salt production and history of the island
upper_amakusa_history.highlight_en: Salt production and fishing on the islands facing the Ariake Sea. A hidden village where the footprints of Shiro Amakusa remain
upper_amakusa_history.text_en: Kamiamakusa City (formerly Ryugatake Town, Matsushima Town, Oyano Town, and Himedo Town) is located in the northern part of Amakusa Kamijima and consists of islands surrounded by the Ariake Sea and the Yatsushiro Sea. During the Edo period, the salt industry was flourishing, and salt fields were established in various locations that utilized seawater from the Ariake Sea. It is close to the area where Amakusa Shiro Tokisada was active during the Shimabara-Amakusa Uprising of 1637-1638, and remains of a structure where the uprising participants are said to have barricaded themselves. Due to the rapid population decline after the uprising, migration from other domains progressed, resulting in the formation of a unique population structure and culture. The scenery of the ria coast and the archipelago is a scenic spot known as ``Amakusa Matsushima.''

nishihara_seinan_sites.name: 西原村の西南戦争史跡
nishihara_seinan_sites.kana: にしはらむらのせいなんせんそうしせき
nishihara_seinan_sites.highlight: 西南戦争で政府軍と薩摩軍が激突した阿蘇外輪山の戦地
nishihara_seinan_sites.text: 西原村は、阿蘇外輪山の西側に位置する村で、1877年の西南戦争において激しい戦闘が繰り広げられた地域です。政府軍（官軍）は熊本城への薩摩軍の補給路を断つべく、阿蘇外輪山を越えるルートを重視しました。村内各所に当時の戦闘の痕跡が残り、弾痕の残る木・砲台跡・官軍墓地などが現存しています。2016年の熊本地震では村が甚大な被害を受けましたが、西南戦争の史跡は震災復興の過程でも大切に保存されています。西原村の「萌の里」からは阿蘇外輪山の全景を望むことができ、当時の激戦地の地形を実感できます。
nishihara_seinan_sites.name_en: Seinan War historical site in Nishihara Village
nishihara_seinan_sites.highlight_en: Aso Somma, the battlefield where the government army and the Satsuma army clashed during the Seinan Rebellion
nishihara_seinan_sites.text_en: Nishihara Village is located on the west side of Mt. Aso, and was the site of a fierce battle during the Satsuma Rebellion of 1877. In order to cut off the Satsuma army's supply route to Kumamoto Castle, the government army focused on the route that crossed the Aso outer rim. Traces of battles from that time remain in various parts of the village, including trees with bullet holes, remains of artillery batteries, and a government military cemetery. Although the village suffered severe damage in the 2016 Kumamoto Earthquake, the historic sites of the Seinan Rebellion have been carefully preserved during the earthquake reconstruction process. From ``Moe no Sato'' in Nishihara Village, you can see a panoramic view of Mt. Aso, and get a feel for the topography of the fierce battleground at the time.

kumamoto_seinan_overview.name: 熊本鎮台跡・古城跡（西南戦争の牙城）
kumamoto_seinan_overview.kana: くまもとちんだいあとこじょうあとせいなんせんそうのがじょう

transit.name: 市電「熊本城・市役所前」

kumamoto_seinan_overview.highlight: 西南戦争で薩摩軍5万が攻めあぐねた熊本鎮台。明治政府の守りの要
kumamoto_seinan_overview.text: 明治新政府は廃藩置県後の1871年、全国に四つの鎮台（軍管区）を設置しました。熊本鎮台は九州全体を管轄し、熊本城をそのまま軍事施設として活用しました。1877年の西南戦争では、西郷隆盛率いる薩摩軍が熊本城を包囲しましたが、谷干城司令長官率いる鎮台兵約3600名が50日以上にわたり籠城を続け、薩摩軍2万以上を足止めしました。この籠城の成功が政府軍の反転攻勢の基盤となり、最終的な西南戦争の帰趨を決定づけました。鎮台跡は現在も陸上自衛隊の施設として使用されており、城内の一部で当時の遺構を見ることができます。
kumamoto_seinan_overview.name_en: Kumamoto Chindai Ruins/Old Castle Ruins (stronghold of the Seinan War)
kumamoto_seinan_overview.highlight_en: During the Seinan War, 50,000 Satsuma troops unsuccessfully attacked the Kumamoto base. The key to the Meiji government's defense
kumamoto_seinan_overview.text_en: In 1871, after the abolition of feudal domains and establishment of prefectures, the new Meiji government established four military districts across the country. Kumamoto Chindai had jurisdiction over all of Kyushu, and used Kumamoto Castle as a military facility. During the Seinan War in 1877, the Satsuma army led by Takamori Saigo besieged Kumamoto Castle, but approximately 3,600 Chindai troops led by Commander-in-Chief Tani Kanjo remained in the castle for over 50 days, stranding over 20,000 Satsuma troops. The success of this siege became the basis for the government army's reversal offensive and determined the eventual outcome of the Seinan War. The Chindai ruins are still used as a Japan Ground Self-Defense Force facility, and you can see the remains of those days in some parts of the castle.

bungo_kokubunji.name: 豊後国分寺跡
bungo_kokubunji.kana: ぶんごこくぶんじあと
bungo_kokubunji.highlight: 聖武天皇の国分寺建立の詔により建てられた豊後の国立寺院跡
bungo_kokubunji.text: 豊後国分寺は、741年に聖武天皇が発した「国分寺建立の詔」により全国に建てられた国立寺院の一つで、豊後国（現大分県）の中心寺院です。七重塔の礎石が残っており、かつての壮大な伽藍の規模を今に伝えています。大分市内には現在も「国分」の地名が残り、古代の行政中心地であったことを示しています。奈良時代の豊後は大野川・大分川流域に多くの集落が発展し、国府・国分寺・国分尼寺がこの地域に整備されました。現在は史跡公園として整備されており、礎石を間近に見学できます。
bungo_kokubunji.highlight_en: The ruins of a national temple in Bungo, built in response to Emperor Shomu's edict to establish a Kokubunji temple.
bungo_kokubunji.text_en: Bungo Kokubunji is one of the national temples built across the country in accordance with the ``Edict to Establish Kokubunji'' issued by Emperor Shomu in 741, and is the central temple of Bungo Province (present-day Oita Prefecture). The foundation stones of the seven-storied pagoda remain, giving us a sense of the scale of the once magnificent temple. The place name "Kokubu" still remains in Oita City, indicating that it was an ancient administrative center. In Bungo during the Nara period, many villages developed in the Onogawa and Oita River basins, and the Kokufu, Kokubunji, and Kokubun nunnery were established in this area. It is currently maintained as a historical park, and you can see the foundation stones up close.

komozu_shrine.name: 薦神社（宇佐神宮の元宮）
komozu_shrine.kana: こもずじんじゃうさじんぐうのもとみや
komozu_shrine.highlight: 宇佐神宮の元宮とされる古社。「薦」の池から御神体の薦が宇佐へ奉られた
komozu_shrine.text: 薦神社（三角池薦神社）は、大分県中津市に鎮座する古社で、宇佐神宮の元宮とも呼ばれます。境内の「三角池」に自生する「薦（真菰）」を御神体として宇佐神宮に奉納する神事が古代から続けられており、これが薦神社の名の由来です。宇佐神宮は全国に約4万4千社ある八幡神社の総本社で、日本三大八幡宮の一つですが、薦神社はその淵源とも言われる重要な神社です。中津市内には福澤諭吉旧居もあり、古代から近代まで多彩な歴史を持つ地域です。
komozu_shrine.name_en: Kosho Shrine (former shrine of Usa Shrine)
komozu_shrine.highlight_en: An old shrine considered to be the former shrine of Usa Jingu. The sacred object of recommendation was offered to Usa from the Pond of “Ko”.
komozu_shrine.text_en: Kozo Shrine (Sankakuike Kozo Shrine) is an ancient shrine located in Nakatsu City, Oita Prefecture, and is also called the former shrine of Usa Jingu. Since ancient times, a ritual has been carried out to dedicate the ``Komo (Makomo)'' that grows wild in the ``Sankaku Pond'' in the precincts to Usa Jingu as the object of worship, and this is the origin of the name ``Komo Shrine.'' Usa Shrine is the headquarters of the approximately 44,000 Hachiman Shrines nationwide, and is one of the three major Hachiman Shrines in Japan, but Komo Shrine is an important shrine that is said to be the origin of all of them. Nakatsu City is also home to the former residence of Yukichi Fukuzawa, and is an area with a rich history from ancient times to modern times.

ontatayaki_village.name: 小鹿田焼の里
ontatayaki_village.highlight: ユネスコ無形文化遺産。300年変わらぬ技法で焼かれる民陶の里
ontatayaki_village.text: 小鹿田焼（おんたやき）は、大分県日田市の山里・皿山地区で18世紀初頭から続く伝統的な陶芸です。1705年頃に小石原焼（福岡県）の陶工が技術を伝えたのが起源で、以来300年以上にわたり10軒の窯元が同じ技法を守り続けています。「唐臼（からうす）」と呼ばれる水力で動く杵で土を砕く製法は、今も変わらず続けられています。飛び鉋・刷毛目・流し掛けなどの装飾技法が特徴で、民芸運動の父・柳宗悦も高く評価しました。2008年にユネスコの無形文化遺産に登録されています。
ontatayaki_village.highlight_en: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. A village of folk pottery made using techniques that have remained unchanged for 300 years
ontatayaki_village.text_en: Onta-yaki is a traditional pottery that has continued since the early 18th century in the Sarayama district of Hita City, Oita Prefecture. Its origins date back to around 1705, when potters from Koishiwara ware (Fukuoka Prefecture) passed down the technique, and since then 10 potteries have continued to use the same technique for over 300 years. The manufacturing method of crushing the soil with a water-powered pestle called a ``karausu'' continues to this day. It is characterized by decorative techniques such as flying planes, brush marks, and flowing patterns, and was highly praised by Yanagi Soetsu, the father of the folk art movement. It was registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2008.

nagayu_tansan_spa.name: 長湯温泉（炭酸泉の医療史）
nagayu_tansan_spa.kana: ながゆおんせんたんさんせんのいりょうし

transit.name: 竹田市コミュニティバス「長湯温泉」

nagayu_tansan_spa.highlight: 日本一の炭酸泉。ドイツ・バートクロイツナハに並ぶ世界最高濃度の炭酸水素泉
nagayu_tansan_spa.text: 長湯温泉（大分県竹田市）は、日本有数の炭酸泉として知られ、その泉質は世界最高水準の炭酸濃度を誇ります。「日本一の炭酸泉」とも称され、心臓・血管疾患への効果が古くから知られていました。江戸時代には豊後岡藩（中川氏）の湯治場として整備され、藩主も入湯に訪れました。明治以降は西洋医学的な観点からも炭酸泉の医療効果が注目され、ドイツ人医師エルウィン・フォン・ベルツも絶賛したと伝えられます。「ガニ湯」と呼ばれる川岸の露天風呂は、長湯温泉のシンボル的な存在です。
nagayu_tansan_spa.name_en: Nagayu Onsen (medical history of carbonated springs)
nagayu_tansan_spa.highlight_en: The best carbonated spring in Japan. The world's highest concentration hydrogen carbonate spring rivals Bad Kreuznach in Germany
nagayu_tansan_spa.text_en: Nagayu Onsen (Takeda City, Oita Prefecture) is known as one of Japan's leading carbonated springs, and its spring quality boasts one of the highest levels of carbonic acid concentration in the world. It is also known as ``Japan's best carbonated spring'' and has long been known for its effects on cardiovascular and vascular diseases. During the Edo period, it was developed as a hot spring spa for the Bungooka domain (Nakagawa clan), and the lord of the domain also visited to take a bath. After the Meiji period, the medical effects of carbonated springs attracted attention from a Western medical perspective, and it is said that German doctor Erwin von Belz praised them highly. 「ガニ湯」と呼ばれる川岸の露天風呂は、長湯温泉のシンボル的な存在です。

ishigahara_battle.name: 石垣原の戦い跡
ishigahara_battle.kana: いしがはらのたたかいあと
ishigahara_battle.highlight: 関ヶ原と同日に豊後で起きた「西の関ヶ原」。大友・黒田軍と西軍の激突
ishigahara_battle.text: 石垣原の戦いは、1600年（慶長5年）9月15日、関ヶ原の戦いと同じ日に豊後国（大分県）で起きた合戦です。関ヶ原で徳川家康（東軍）と石田三成（西軍）が激突するのと時を同じくして、豊後では大友義統（西軍）が黒田如水（東軍）と激突しました。大友義統はかつて秀吉に改易された家を再興しようと西軍に与しましたが、黒田如水の巧みな戦略に敗れ、大友氏は完全に滅亡しました。戦場跡の石垣原には現在も石碑が残り、「西の関ヶ原」とも呼ばれるこの戦いの歴史を伝えています。
ishigahara_battle.highlight_en: "Western Sekigahara" occurred in Bungo on the same day as Sekigahara. Clash between Otomo/Kuroda army and Western army
ishigahara_battle.text_en: The Battle of Ishigakihara was a battle that took place in Bungo Province (Oita Prefecture) on September 15, 1600, the same day as the Battle of Sekigahara. At the same time as Tokugawa Ieyasu (Eastern Army) and Ishida Mitsunari (Western Army) clashed at Sekigahara, Otomo Yoshimune (Western Army) clashed with Kuroda Josui (Eastern Army) at Bungo. Yoshimune Otomo joined the Western army in an attempt to rebuild the family that had been destroyed by Hideyoshi, but he was defeated by Josui Kuroda's clever strategy and the Otomo clan was completely destroyed. A stone monument still remains at Ishigakihara, the battlefield site, telling the history of this battle, also known as the "Sekigahara of the West."

buzen_kokubunji.name: 豊前国分寺跡
buzen_kokubunji.kana: ぶぜんこくぶんじあと
buzen_kokubunji.highlight: 北九州・豊前の国分寺跡。三重塔（江戸再建）が現存する貴重な史跡
buzen_kokubunji.text: 豊前国分寺は、741年の聖武天皇の詔により豊前国（現在の福岡県南東部〜大分県北部）に建立された国立寺院です。現在の行橋市に位置し、江戸時代に再建された三重塔が今も残っています。この三重塔は奈良時代の七重塔とは異なりますが、江戸時代の寺院建築として価値が高く、国の重要文化財に指定されています。境内には奈良時代の七重塔の礎石も保存されており、古代と近世の二つの時代の痕跡を同時に見ることができます。周辺には馬ヶ岳城跡など中世の史跡も多く残っています。
buzen_kokubunji.highlight_en: Ruins of Kokubunji Temple in Buzen, Kitakyushu. A valuable historical site where the three-storied pagoda (rebuilt in the Edo period) still exists
buzen_kokubunji.text_en: Buzen Kokubunji is a national temple built in Buzen Province (present-day southeastern Fukuoka Prefecture to northern Oita Prefecture) by Emperor Shomu's edict in 741. Located in present-day Yukuhashi City, the three-storied pagoda that was rebuilt during the Edo period still remains. Although this three-storied pagoda is different from the seven-storied pagoda of the Nara period, it is highly valuable as a temple building from the Edo period, and has been designated as an important cultural property of the country. The foundation stone of a seven-storied pagoda from the Nara period is also preserved within the precincts, allowing you to see traces of both ancient and modern eras at the same time. There are many medieval historical sites such as the Umagatake Castle Ruins in the surrounding area.

ajimu_basin_oita.name: 安心院盆地の農村景観
ajimu_basin_oita.kana: あじむぼんちののうそんけいかん

transit.name: 宇佐市コミュニティバス「安心院」

ajimu_basin_oita.highlight: 日本のアグリツーリズム発祥地。スッポン・ワイン・湧水で知られる里山
ajimu_basin_oita.text: 安心院（あじむ）盆地は、大分県宇佐市の山間に広がる農村地帯で、豊かな湧水と温暖な気候に恵まれた地域です。江戸時代から農業が盛んで、特にスッポン養殖（日本有数の産地）とブドウ栽培が知られています。安心院ワインは九州ワインのパイオニアとして知られ、地域の農業文化の多様性を示しています。また、日本のアグリツーリズム（農村観光）の発祥地としても知られ、農家民泊の先進的な取り組みが1992年から始まりました。周辺には縄文時代の遺跡や磨崖仏など歴史的遺産も豊富です。
ajimu_basin_oita.highlight_en: The birthplace of Japanese agritourism. Satoyama known for soft-shelled turtles, wine, and spring water
ajimu_basin_oita.text_en: The Ajimu Basin is a rural area in the mountains of Usa City, Oita Prefecture, blessed with abundant spring water and a warm climate. Agriculture has flourished since the Edo period, and the area is particularly known for its soft-shelled turtle farming (one of Japan's leading producers) and grape cultivation. Ajimu Wine is known as a pioneer of Kyushu wine, demonstrating the diversity of the region's agricultural culture. It is also known as the birthplace of Japan's agritourism (rural tourism), and advanced efforts to provide farm stays began in 1992. The surrounding area is also rich in historical heritage, such as ruins from the Jomon period and Buddhist statues on cliffs.

beppu_foreign_history.name: 別府・外国人避暑地の歴史
beppu_foreign_history.kana: べっぷがいこくじんひしょちのれきし
beppu_foreign_history.highlight: 明治期に外国人が愛した国際温泉リゾート。油屋熊八と別府近代観光の歴史
beppu_foreign_history.text: 別府温泉は、日本有数の湧出量を誇る温泉地で、明治時代に外国人居留地として整備されてから国際的な観光地として発展しました。近代別府観光の父とも言われる油屋熊八は、1911年（明治44年）に「亀の井旅館」を創業し、バスガールを採用した「亀の井バス」や「山は富士、海は瀬戸内、湯は別府」のキャッチコピーで別府を全国にPRしました。外国人向けの洋式設備を整えたこともあり、在日外国人の間で「東洋のナポリ」とも称されました。鉄輪地区の蒸し湯など独自の温泉文化も中世から続く伝統を持ちます。
beppu_foreign_history.name_en: History of Beppu, a summer resort for foreigners
beppu_foreign_history.highlight_en: An international hot spring resort loved by foreigners during the Meiji period. Aburaya Kumahachi and the history of modern tourism in Beppu
beppu_foreign_history.text_en: Beppu Onsen is a hot spring area that boasts one of the highest volumes of hot spring water in Japan, and has developed into an international tourist destination since it was developed as a foreign settlement during the Meiji period. Kumahachi Aburaya, who is said to be the father of modern Beppu tourism, founded the Kamenoi Ryokan in 1911 (Meiji 44) and promoted Beppu nationwide with the Kamenoi Bus, which employed bus girls, and the catchphrase "Mountains are Fuji, the sea is Seto Inland Sea, and the hot springs are Beppu." It was also known as the ``Naples of the East'' among foreigners living in Japan, as it was equipped with Western-style facilities for foreigners. The unique hot spring culture such as steam baths in the Kannawa area has a tradition dating back to the Middle Ages.

naoiri_stone_bridges.name: 豊後大野の石橋群
naoiri_stone_bridges.kana: ぶんごおおののいしばしぐん
naoiri_stone_bridges.highlight: 国内最大規模の石橋群。肥後石工が築いた江戸期の石造アーチ橋が20橋以上現存
naoiri_stone_bridges.text: 豊後大野市（旧直入郡・大野郡）には、江戸時代に肥後（熊本）の石工集団が架けた石造アーチ橋が20橋以上現存しており、国内最大規模の石橋群として知られています。「轟橋」「白山橋」「市場橋」など多くの橋が国の重要文化財・史跡に指定されています。これらの石橋は、九州山地から産出する阿蘇溶結凝灰岩（通称「阿蘇ピンク石」）を加工して造られており、美しいアーチと落ち着いた色合いが特徴です。現在も生活道路として使用されているものも多く、数百年の時を経た橋が現役であることは驚くべきことです。
naoiri_stone_bridges.highlight_en: The largest group of stone bridges in Japan. More than 20 stone arch bridges from the Edo period built by Higo stonemasons still exist.
