naoiri_stone_bridges.text_en: In Bungo-Ono City (formerly Naoiri District/Ono District), there are over 20 existing stone arch bridges built by a group of stonemasons from Higo (Kumamoto) during the Edo period, and it is known as the largest group of stone bridges in Japan. Many bridges, such as Todoroki Bridge, Hakusan Bridge, and Ichiba Bridge, have been designated as national important cultural properties and historic sites. These stone bridges are made from Aso welded tuff (commonly known as ``Aso pink stone'') produced in the Kyushu mountains, and are characterized by beautiful arches and subdued colors. Many of these bridges are still in use as community roads, and it is amazing that bridges that have been around for hundreds of years are still in use.

bungo_ono_valley.name: 緒方・原尻周辺の歴史と景観
bungo_ono_valley.kana: おがたはらじりしゅうへんのれきしとけいかん
bungo_ono_valley.highlight: 「東洋のナイアガラ」原尻の滝と緒方氏の歴史が交差する大野川流域
bungo_ono_valley.text: 大野川の支流・緒方川流域は、古代から人々が暮らした豊かな地域です。南北朝時代には後醍醐天皇方の武将として活躍した緒方氏の本拠地であり、多くの山城跡が周辺に残っています。幅120メートル・高さ20メートルの馬蹄形をした「原尻の滝」は「東洋のナイアガラ」とも呼ばれ、滝の上を渡る吊り橋からの景観が圧巻です。玄武岩の溶岩台地が侵食されてできた景観で、地質学的にも価値が高く、「おおいた豊後大野ジオパーク」として整備されています。縄文時代の遺跡や古墳も周辺に点在しています。
bungo_ono_valley.name_en: History and scenery around Ogata and Harajiri
bungo_ono_valley.highlight_en: The Ono River basin, where the history of the Ogata clan intersects with Harajiri Falls, the “Niagara of the East”
bungo_ono_valley.text_en: The Ogata River basin, a tributary of the Ono River, is a rich area where people have lived since ancient times. During the Nanbokucho period, it was the home base of the Ogata clan, who were active as military commanders for Emperor Go-Daigo, and many mountain castle ruins remain in the surrounding area. The horseshoe-shaped Harajiri Falls, which is 120 meters wide and 20 meters high, is also known as the ``Niagara of the East,'' and the view from the suspension bridge that crosses over the falls is spectacular. The landscape was created by the erosion of a basalt lava plateau, and is of great geological value, and has been maintained as the Oita Bungo-Ono Geopark. There are also ruins and ancient tombs from the Jomon period scattered around the area.

takanabe_castle.name: 高鍋城跡・藩校明倫堂
takanabe_castle.kana: たかなべじょうあとはんこうめいりんどう
takanabe_castle.highlight: 秋月藩から移封した高鍋藩・秋月氏の居城。名君・秋月種茂と藩校の地
takanabe_castle.text: 高鍋城は、江戸時代に高鍋藩（秋月氏・3万石）の居城として整備された城です。秋月氏はもともと福岡の秋月（現朝倉市）を本拠としていた武将で、関ヶ原の戦い後に日向高鍋に移封されました。8代藩主・秋月種茂（1748〜1816年）は藩政改革に取り組み、藩校「明倫堂」を設立して教育を充実させた名君として知られます。明倫堂の教育は多くの有能な人材を育て、高鍋藩出身者が明治維新後の各界で活躍しました。城跡は現在「高鍋城跡公園」として整備され、石垣や堀が残っています。
takanabe_castle.highlight_en: The residence of the Akizuki clan of the Takanabe clan, which was transferred from the Akizuki clan. The land of the famous prince Akizuki Taneshige and his domain school
takanabe_castle.text_en: Takanabe Castle is a castle built during the Edo period as the residence of the Takanabe clan (Akizuki clan, 30,000 koku). The Akizuki clan was originally a military commander based in Akizuki, Fukuoka (present-day Asakura City), and was transferred to Hyuga-Takanabe after the Battle of Sekigahara. The 8th lord of the domain, Taneshige Akizuki (1748-1816), is known as a great ruler who worked to reform the domain's administration and established the domain school Meirindo to improve education. Meirindo's education fostered many talented people, and those from the Takanabe domain went on to play active roles in various fields after the Meiji Restoration. The castle ruins are currently maintained as the Takanabe Castle Ruins Park, and the stone walls and moat remain.

ito_clan_miyazaki.name: 伊東氏館跡・都於郡城跡
ito_clan_miyazaki.kana: いとうしやかたあととのこおりじょうあと
ito_clan_miyazaki.highlight: 戦国期に日向国の大半を制した伊東義祐の本城。九州最大規模の山城群
ito_clan_miyazaki.text: 都於郡城は、戦国時代に日向国を支配した伊東氏の本城で、宮崎県西都市の丘陵地帯に築かれた大規模な城です。最盛期の伊東義祐は日向国内に48城を持つとも言われ、九州屈指の大名として君臨しました。しかし1578年の「耳川の戦い」で薩摩の島津義久に大敗し、伊東氏は日向から追放されました。義祐は豊後の大友宗麟を頼って落ち延び、後に豊臣秀吉の九州征伐で日向国への帰還を果たしましたが、全盛期の勢力は取り戻せませんでした。城跡は五つの曲輪が連なる遺構が良く残り、県内最大規模の山城とも言われます。
ito_clan_miyazaki.name_en: Ito clan mansion ruins/Miyakogun castle ruins
ito_clan_miyazaki.highlight_en: The main castle of Yoshisuke Ito, who controlled most of Hyuga Province during the Sengoku period. The largest mountain castle group in Kyushu
ito_clan_miyazaki.text_en: Miyakogun Castle is the main castle of the Ito clan, which ruled Hyuga Province during the Sengoku period, and is a large castle built on a hill in Saito, Miyazaki Prefecture. At his peak, Yoshisuke Ito was said to have 48 castles in Hyuga Province, and reigned as one of the most prominent daimyo in Kyushu. However, in the Battle of Mimikawa in 1578, the Ito clan was defeated by Yoshihisa Shimazu of Satsuma, and the Ito clan was expelled from Hyuga. Yoshisuke fled to Bungo, relying on Sorin Otomo, and later returned to Hyuga Province with Toyotomi Hideyoshi's conquest of Kyushu, but he was unable to regain the power he had during his heyday. The castle ruins have well-preserved remains of a series of five castles, and are said to be the largest mountain castle in the prefecture.

miyakonojo_kaminobori.name: 都城・神柱宮
miyakonojo_kaminobori.kana: みやこのじょうかみばしらぐう
miyakonojo_kaminobori.highlight: 都城盆地の総鎮守。島津氏発祥の地・都城の歴史を守り続ける古社
miyakonojo_kaminobori.text: 神柱宮は、宮崎県都城市の中心部に鎮座する古社で、都城盆地の総鎮守として崇められてきました。都城は島津氏の発祥地とも言われ（都城島津家）、中世には北原氏・相良氏・伊東氏・島津氏が激しく争った要衝でした。島津氏は都城に「都城」（旧称「懸かりの城」）を築き、都城島津家が代々この地を治めました。神柱宮の創建は9世紀頃とも伝えられ、歴代島津氏の崇敬を受けました。現在も地域の中心的な神社として多くの参拝者を集め、都城の「六月灯（夏越）」の中心となっています。
miyakonojo_kaminobori.highlight_en: General guardian of Miyakonojo Basin. An old shrine that continues to protect the history of Miyakonojo, the birthplace of the Shimazu clan
miyakonojo_kaminobori.text_en: Jinbashira Shrine is an ancient shrine located in the center of Miyakonojo City, Miyazaki Prefecture, and has been revered as the general guardian of the Miyakonojo Basin. Miyakonojo is also said to be the birthplace of the Shimazu clan (Miyakonojo Shimazu family), and was a strategic point where the Kitahara, Sagara, Ito, and Shimazu clans fought fiercely during the medieval period. The Shimazu clan built ``Miyakonojo'' (formerly known as ``Kakari no Castle'') in Miyakonojo, and the Miyakonojo Shimazu family ruled this area for generations. Jinbashira Shrine is said to have been built around the 9th century, and was revered by successive generations of the Shimazu clan. Today, it continues to be the central shrine of the region, attracting many worshipers, and is the center of Miyakonojo's ``Rokugatsuto (Natsugoe)'' festival.

nichinan_coast_history.name: 日南海岸・飫肥杉と海の道
nichinan_coast_history.kana: にちなんかいがんおびすぎとうみのみち
nichinan_coast_history.highlight: 飫肥藩が育てた飫肥杉が支えた近世の木材輸出。酒谷川・広渡川の木材流送史
nichinan_coast_history.text: 日南市周辺の山間地帯では、江戸時代に飫肥藩（伊東氏・5万1千石）が杉の植林を奨励し、「飫肥杉」と呼ばれる優良材木を大量に生産しました。飫肥杉は脂分が多く耐水性に優れているため、主に船材として大阪・江戸の木材市場に供給されました。木材は酒谷川・広渡川を利用した「木材流送（筏流し）」で沿岸まで運ばれ、日南海岸の港から船積みされました。この林業と海運の組み合わせが飫肥藩の財政を支えました。現在も飫肥杉の美しい林が日南山地を覆っており、サイクリングコースとして整備されています。
nichinan_coast_history.name_en: Nichinan Coast/Obi Cedar and Sea Road
nichinan_coast_history.highlight_en: Wood exports in the early modern period were supported by Obi cedars grown by the Obi clan. Log transport history of Sakatani River and Hiroto River
nichinan_coast_history.text_en: In the mountainous area around Nichinan City, during the Edo period, the Obi clan (Ito clan, 51,000 koku) encouraged the planting of cedar trees, producing a large amount of high-quality lumber called "Obi cedar." Because Obi cedar has a high oil content and excellent water resistance, it was mainly supplied to the Osaka and Edo lumber markets as ship material. The wood was transported to the coast by ``wood transport'' (rafting) using the Sakatani River and Hiroto River, and was loaded by ship from ports on the Nichinan coast. This combination of forestry and shipping supported the Obi clan's finances. Today, a beautiful forest of Obi cedar still covers the Nichinan Mountains, and has been maintained as a cycling course.

mimitsu_port.name: 美々津港（神武東征伝説の地）
mimitsu_port.kana: みみつこうじんむとうせいでんせつのち
mimitsu_port.highlight: 神武天皇が東征へ出発したとされる神話の港。江戸期の商家町並みが現存
mimitsu_port.text: 美々津は、宮崎県日向市の耳川河口に位置する港町で、神武天皇が東征（東の地に国を建てるための遠征）に出発したと伝わる「神話の港」です。『日本書紀』には、神武天皇が日向を出発して大和（奈良）へ向かったとの記述があり、美々津はその出発地の一つとされています。江戸時代には耳川流域の山間部から切り出した木材や物産の積出港として繁栄し、商家の町並みが形成されました。現在も「重要伝統的建造物群保存地区」に選定された江戸〜明治期の商家建築が残っており、散策が楽しめます。
mimitsu_port.name_en: Mimitsu Port (legendary place of Jimmu East Expedition)
mimitsu_port.highlight_en: A mythical port where Emperor Jinmu is said to have departed on his eastern expedition. Existing merchant townscape from the Edo period
mimitsu_port.text_en: Mimitsu is a port town located at the mouth of the Mimi River in Hyuga City, Miyazaki Prefecture, and is said to be the ``mythical port'' where Emperor Jinmu set out on his expedition to the east (an expedition to establish a country in the east). The Nihon Shoki records that Emperor Jinmu left Hyuga for Yamato (Nara), and Mimitsu is said to be one of his starting points. During the Edo period, it prospered as a shipping port for lumber and other products cut from the mountains of the Mimi River basin, and a townscape of merchant houses was formed. Today, merchant houses from the Edo to Meiji eras, which have been selected as an ``Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings,'' still remain, and you can enjoy a stroll around them.

tsuno_shrine_miyazaki.name: 都農神社
tsuno_shrine_miyazaki.highlight: 日向国一之宮。神武天皇が東征に際して祈願したと伝わる古社
tsuno_shrine_miyazaki.text: 都農神社は、大己貴命（おおなむちのみこと）を祀る日向国一之宮で、創建は神代とも言われる古社です。『日本書紀』によると、神武天皇が東征の際にこの地で祈願したと伝えられており、日向の国を代表する神社として崇められてきました。中世には伊東氏・島津氏などの有力武将の崇敬を受け、社殿の造営・修復が繰り返されました。現在の社殿は江戸時代に再建されたもので、境内の杜は「宮崎の巨樹・古木百選」に選ばれた大樹が立ち並ぶ鎮守の森を形成しています。県内屈指の初詣スポットでもあります。
tsuno_shrine_miyazaki.highlight_en: Hyuga Province Ichinomiya. An old shrine where Emperor Jimmu is said to have prayed before his expedition to the east.
tsuno_shrine_miyazaki.text_en: Tsuno Shrine is an ancient shrine in Hyuga Province that enshrines Onamuchi no Mikoto, and is said to have been founded in the age of the gods. According to the Nihon Shoki, Emperor Jimmu is said to have prayed here during his expedition to the east, and it has been revered as a shrine representing the Hyuga country. In the Middle Ages, the shrine was revered by powerful military commanders such as the Ito clan and the Shimazu clan, and the shrine was repeatedly constructed and restored. The current shrine building was rebuilt in the Edo period, and the precincts form a sacred forest lined with large trees that have been selected as one of Miyazaki's top 100 giant and ancient trees. It is also one of the prefecture's best New Year's visit spots.

hinokage_history.name: 日之影・奥日向の山岳文化
hinokage_history.kana: ひのかげおくひゅうがのさんがくぶんか

transit.name: 高千穂鉄道「日之影温泉」駅跡（現道の駅）

hinokage_history.highlight: 日之影川沿いに残る石垣の集落と渓谷美。奥日向の山岳武士文化の面影
hinokage_history.text: 日之影町は、宮崎県北部の山間に位置し、日之影川が刻む深い渓谷沿いに集落が点在する地域です。中世には延岡藩の支配下に置かれた山間の要地であり、急峻な地形を活かした山城が各所に築かれました。石垣を用いた棚田や屋敷の造りは、山岳地帯で暮らした人々の高い技術力を示しています。明治期には国鉄高千穂線が開通し、山間地の産物輸送に活躍しましたが、2005年の台風被害で廃線となりました。廃線跡を利用した「高千穂あまてらす鉄道」のグランド・スーパーカートが観光名所となっています。
hinokage_history.highlight_en: The stone walled village and beautiful valley that remain along the Hinokage River. Traces of mountain samurai culture in Okuhinata
hinokage_history.text_en: Hinokage Town is located in the mountains of northern Miyazaki Prefecture, and is an area dotted with villages along a deep valley carved by the Hinokage River. In the Middle Ages, it was an important mountainous area under the control of the Nobeoka clan, and mountain castles were built in various locations to take advantage of the steep terrain. The construction of terraced rice fields and mansions using stone walls shows the high level of technical ability of the people who lived in the mountainous region. During the Meiji period, the JNR Takachiho Line was opened and was used to transport products in mountainous areas, but it was discontinued due to typhoon damage in 2005. The Grand Super Cart of the Takachiho Amaterasu Railway, which used the ruins of an abandoned railway line, has become a tourist attraction.

takachiho_yayoi.name: 高千穂・弥生遺跡と神楽の里
takachiho_yayoi.kana: たかちほやよいいせきとかぐらのさと

transit.name: 宮崎交通バス「高千穂バスセンター」

takachiho_yayoi.highlight: 天孫降臨神話の聖地・高千穂に刻まれた弥生文化の痕跡
takachiho_yayoi.text: 高千穂町周辺は、天照大御神が天岩戸に隠れた神話や天孫・瓊瓊杵尊（ニニギノミコト）が降臨した「天孫降臨」の舞台として知られる神話の地ですが、同時に縄文〜弥生時代の遺跡も数多く残る地域です。日之影川・五ヶ瀬川流域の遺跡からは弥生土器・石器・鉄製品などが出土しており、古代から人々が豊かな自然の中で暮らしていたことがわかります。高千穂神楽は毎年11月〜2月にかけて各集落の神社で夜を徹して奉納され、国の重要無形民俗文化財に指定されています。神話と弥生文化が重なり合う特別な地域です。
takachiho_yayoi.highlight_en: Traces of Yayoi culture etched in Takachiho, the sacred place of the myth of the descent of the Tenson
takachiho_yayoi.text_en: The area around Takachiho Town is a mythical place known for the myth that Amaterasu Omikami hid in Amanoiwato, and for the ``Descent of the Tenson'' where the descendant of the Tenson, Ninigi no Mikoto, descended, but it is also an area where many ruins from the Jomon to Yayoi periods remain. Yayoi pottery, stone tools, iron products, and other items have been excavated from ruins in the Hinokage River and Gokase River basins, showing that people have lived in a rich natural environment since ancient times. Takachiho Kagura is dedicated throughout the night at shrines in each village from November to February every year, and has been designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property. It is a special region where mythology and Yayoi culture overlap.

nishimera_mountain_warriors.name: 西米良・米良氏の山岳文化
nishimera_mountain_warriors.kana: にしめらめらしのさんがくぶんか

transit.name: 西米良村コミュニティバス「村所」

nishimera_mountain_warriors.highlight: 球磨川最上流域の秘境。米良氏が統治した山岳武士文化の地
nishimera_mountain_warriors.text: 西米良村は、宮崎県の最西部・一ツ瀬川（球磨川上流域）の奥地に位置する秘境の村です。中世には「米良氏」という山岳武士が独自の支配を行い、江戸時代には熊本藩（人吉藩）と日向藩の境界地帯として特殊な行政が続きました。「米良の庄」と呼ばれたこの地域は、薩摩・肥後・日向の三国が接する山岳地帯で、各勢力の争いを巧みにかわして自立を保ちました。山深い地域ゆえに独自の文化が育まれ、「米良の舞」など特有の芸能が今も伝承されています。村所城跡など中世の遺構が残っています。
nishimera_mountain_warriors.name_en: Mountain culture of Nishimera and the Mera clan
nishimera_mountain_warriors.highlight_en: An unexplored region in the upper reaches of the Kuma River. Land of mountain samurai culture ruled by the Mera clan
nishimera_mountain_warriors.text_en: Nishimera Village is an unexplored village located deep in the westernmost part of Miyazaki Prefecture, along the Hitotsuse River (upstream of the Kuma River). In the Middle Ages, mountain samurai called the Mera clan ruled independently, and during the Edo period, a special administration continued as a border area between the Kumamoto clan (Hitoyoshi clan) and the Hyuga clan. This area, known as ``Mera no Sho,'' was a mountainous region where the three countries of Satsuma, Higo, and Hyuga came into contact, and it maintained its independence by deftly fending off the conflicts of each power. Because of the deep mountainousness of the region, a unique culture has been nurtured, and unique performing arts such as the "Mera no Mai" are still passed down to this day. Medieval remains remain, including the ruins of Muradokoro Castle.

miyakonojo_ancient_burial.name: 都城盆地の古墳群
miyakonojo_ancient_burial.kana: みやこのじょうぼんちのこふんぐん
miyakonojo_ancient_burial.highlight: 都城盆地に集中する古墳群。前方後円墳が示す大和王権との関係
miyakonojo_ancient_burial.text: 都城盆地（宮崎県都城市周辺）には、古墳時代（3〜7世紀）の古墳が数多く分布しています。前方後円墳・円墳・方墳など様々な形態の古墳が確認されており、ヤマト王権の影響がこの南九州の地にも及んでいたことを示しています。特に「六野原古墳群」は古墳時代中期の大型古墳を含む重要な古墳群です。出土品には埴輪・鉄製武器・装身具などがあり、当時の日向の豪族が大和の文化を受け入れながら独自の政治勢力を形成していた様子が伺えます。都城市立美術館・図書館に出土品が展示されています。
miyakonojo_ancient_burial.highlight_en: A group of ancient tombs concentrated in the Miyakonojo Basin. Relationship with the Yamato royal power shown by keyhole-shaped tumuli
miyakonojo_ancient_burial.text_en: The Miyakonojo Basin (around Miyakonojo City, Miyazaki Prefecture) is home to many ancient tombs from the Kofun period (3rd to 7th century). Various types of burial mounds have been confirmed, including keyhole-shaped tombs, round tombs, and rectangular tombs, indicating that the influence of the Yamato kingship extended to this area of ​​southern Kyushu. In particular, the Rokunohara Tumulus Group is an important tumulus group that includes large tumuli from the middle of the Kofun period. The excavated items include clay clay figures, iron weapons, and jewelry, showing how the Hyuga clans of the time were forming their own political power while accepting Yamato culture. The excavated items are on display at the Miyakonojo City Museum and Library.

sendai_castle_satsuma.name: 薩摩川内城跡（新田城）
sendai_castle_satsuma.kana: さつませんだいじょうあとにったじょう
sendai_castle_satsuma.highlight: 薩摩国守護・島津氏の重要拠点。中世薩摩の政治中心地
sendai_castle_satsuma.text: 薩摩川内（せんだい）は、川内川流域に開けた薩摩国の中心地で、中世には島津氏の重要拠点として栄えました。新田城（にったじょう）は島津氏が築いた山城で、薩摩国支配の軍事的要衝でした。川内川は薩摩の物産を輸送する幹線水路として機能し、江戸時代には薩摩藩の重要な米蔵・陣屋が置かれました。近世には薩摩焼（苗代川焼）の産地としても知られ、朝鮮から連れてきた陶工たちが優れた陶磁器を生み出しました。現在は薩摩川内市歴史民俗資料館で地域の歴史を学べます。
sendai_castle_satsuma.highlight_en: An important base for the Shimazu clan, the guardians of Satsuma Province. Political center of medieval Satsuma
sendai_castle_satsuma.text_en: Satsuma Sendai is the center of Satsuma Province, located in the Sendai River basin, and flourished as an important base of the Shimazu clan during the medieval period. Nitta Castle was a mountain castle built by the Shimazu clan and was a strategic military center for the control of Satsuma. The Kawauchi River served as the main waterway for transporting Satsuma's products, and during the Edo period it was home to important rice warehouses and jinya of the Satsuma domain. In the early modern period, it was also known as a production area for Satsuma ware (Naesirogawa ware), where potters brought from Korea created excellent ceramics. Currently, you can learn about the history of the area at the Satsumasendai City History and Folklore Museum.

koshikijima_history.name: 甑島（遣唐使の中継地）
koshikijima_history.kana: こしきじまけんとうしのちゅうけいち

transit.name: 川内港からフェリー約2時間

koshikijima_history.highlight: 遣唐使船が風待ちした孤島。中世には流刑の地としても知られる
koshikijima_history.text: 甑島（こしきじま）は、鹿児島県薩摩川内市の西方、東シナ海に浮かぶ島々です。古代の遣唐使が中国へ渡る際の風待ち・寄港地として重要な役割を担いました。また「肥前の甑」として流刑地としても使われ、平安時代には多くの貴族・武将が島送りにされました。島には縄文時代からの遺跡が残り、独自の海洋文化が育まれてきました。「甑島の里神楽」は国の重要無形民俗文化財に指定されており、島の人々が古来から受け継いできた神事芸能です。長目の浜・ナポレオン岩など雄大な自然景観も魅力です。
koshikijima_history.name_en: Koshikijima (stopping point for envoys sent to Tang Dynasty)
koshikijima_history.highlight_en: A solitary island where the envoys to Tang Dynasty waited for the wind. Also known as a place of exile in the Middle Ages
koshikijima_history.text_en: Koshikijima is an island floating in the East China Sea to the west of Satsumasendai City, Kagoshima Prefecture. It played an important role as a waiting port and a port of call for envoys to China in ancient times. It was also used as a penal colony called ``Hizen no Koshiki,'' and many nobles and military commanders were sent to the island during the Heian period. Ruins from the Jomon period remain on the island, and a unique maritime culture has been nurtured. ``Koshikijima no Sato Kagura'' has been designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property, and is a ritual performing art that has been passed down by the people of the island since ancient times. The magnificent natural scenery such as Nagame Beach and Napoleon Rock is also attractive.

okinoerabu_saigo.name: 沖永良部島（西郷隆盛流刑地）
okinoerabu_saigo.kana: おきのえらぶじまさいごうたかもりるけいち

transit.name: 沖永良部空港（鹿児島から約1時間）

okinoerabu_saigo.highlight: 西郷隆盛が2度目の流刑中に土牢に幽閉された島。ここで一念転機
okinoerabu_saigo.text: 沖永良部島は、鹿児島県の南端に近い奄美諸島の一島で、西郷隆盛が2度目の流刑（1862〜1864年）を過ごした地です。薩摩藩主・島津久光の怒りを買った西郷は、島に着くや否や土牢に幽閉され、極めて過酷な環境で生活しました。しかし代官・土持政照の尽力により待遇が改善され、西郷は島の人々に学問を教えながら思索の日々を送りました。この流刑中の苦難が西郷の精神を鍛え、維新の指導者としての人格形成に大きな影響を与えたと言われます。島内には西郷が幽閉された土牢跡と記念館があります。
okinoerabu_saigo.highlight_en: The island where Saigo Takamori was imprisoned in a dungeon during his second exile. This is a turning point
okinoerabu_saigo.text_en: Okinoerabu Island is an island in the Amami Islands near the southern tip of Kagoshima Prefecture, and is where Saigo Takamori spent his second exile (1862-1864). Saigo incurred the wrath of Hisamitsu Shimazu, the lord of Satsuma, and was imprisoned in a dungeon as soon as he arrived on the island, living in extremely harsh conditions. However, thanks to the efforts of the magistrate, Masateru Tsuchimochi, his treatment improved, and Saigo spent his days thinking and teaching the people of the island. It is said that the hardships during this exile strengthened Saigo's spirit and had a great influence on his character development as a leader of the Meiji Restoration. On the island, there are the ruins of the dungeon where Saigo was imprisoned and a memorial hall.

makurazaki_fishing.name: 枕崎漁港と鰹節産業の歴史
makurazaki_fishing.kana: まくらざきぎょこうとかつおぶしさんぎょうのれきし
makurazaki_fishing.highlight: 日本一の鰹節産地・枕崎。江戸時代から続く「薩摩節」の本場
makurazaki_fishing.text: 枕崎市は、鹿児島県薩摩半島の南端に位置し、日本有数の鰹節産地として知られます。「薩摩節」と呼ばれる枕崎の鰹節は江戸時代から全国に知られ、現在も国内生産量の約3分の1を占めます。枕崎港にはかつおを積んだ漁船が次々と入港し、水揚げから加工まで一貫した産業が町の経済を支えてきました。明治以降は遠洋漁業も盛んになり、南洋漁業の基地としても重要な役割を果たしました。「かつお公社」では鰹節の製造工程を見学でき、削りたての鰹節を試食することもできます。
makurazaki_fishing.name_en: History of Makurazaki Fishing Port and the Katsuobushi Industry
makurazaki_fishing.highlight_en: Makurazaki is Japan's number one bonito flakes production area. The home of "Satsuma-bushi" that has continued since the Edo period
makurazaki_fishing.text_en: Makurazaki City is located at the southern tip of the Satsuma Peninsula in Kagoshima Prefecture and is known as one of Japan's leading bonito flakes production areas. Makurazaki bonito flakes, also known as ``Satsuma-bushi,'' have been known throughout the country since the Edo period, and still account for about one-third of domestic production. Fishing boats loaded with bonito arrive at Makurazaki Port one after another, and an integrated industry from landing to processing has supported the town's economy. After the Meiji period, deep-sea fishing became popular, and the area also played an important role as a base for South Sea fishing. At Katsuo Kosha, you can see the bonito flakes manufacturing process and even sample freshly shaved bonito flakes.

shibushi_kofun.name: 志布志湾と大隅の古墳群
shibushi_kofun.kana: しぶしわんとおおすみのこふんぐん

transit.name: 鹿児島交通バス「志布志」

shibushi_kofun.highlight: 南九州最大規模の古墳群が集中する地域。大隅国の古代王権の中心
shibushi_kofun.text: 志布志湾沿岸地域（鹿児島県志布志市・大崎町周辺）は、大隅半島に古墳時代（3〜7世紀）の古墳が数多く分布する地域です。特に「唐仁古墳群」は九州最大規模の前方後円墳を含む古墳群で、国の史跡に指定されています。主墳の「唐仁大塚古墳」は全長140メートルに及ぶ大型前方後円墳で、大和王権との強い結びつきを示しています。この地域は古代の大隅国の政治・文化の中心地であり、中国や南方との交流を示す遺物も出土しています。曽於市・志布志市の博物館で出土品を見学できます。
shibushi_kofun.name_en: Shibushi Bay and Osumi Tumulus Group
shibushi_kofun.highlight_en: An area with the largest concentration of ancient tombs in southern Kyushu. The center of the ancient royal power of Osumi Province
shibushi_kofun.text_en: The Shibushi Bay coastal area (around Shibushi City and Osaki Town, Kagoshima Prefecture) is an area where many ancient tombs from the Kofun period (3rd to 7th century) are distributed on the Osumi Peninsula. In particular, the Tojin Tumulus Group includes the largest keyhole-shaped tumulus in Kyushu, and is designated as a national historic site. The main tomb, Tonin Otsuka Tumulus, is a large keyhole-shaped tumulus with a total length of 140 meters, demonstrating its strong ties to the Yamato dynasty. This area was the political and cultural center of Osumi Province in ancient times, and artifacts that indicate interaction with China and the south have been unearthed. You can view excavated items at museums in Soo City and Shibushi City.

hishikari_gold_mine.name: 菱刈金山（日本最大の金山）
hishikari_gold_mine.kana: ひしかりきんざんにほんさいだいのきんざん

transit.name: バス「菱刈役場前」（いさバス）

hishikari_gold_mine.highlight: 世界最高品位の金鉱山。1985年発見以来の累積産出量は日本最大
hishikari_gold_mine.text: 菱刈金山は、鹿児島県伊佐市（旧菱刈町）に所在する日本最大の金鉱山です。1985年に住友金属鉱山が発見し、その後の開発で世界的にも稀な高品位（1トン当たり金40グラム超）の金鉱床であることが判明しました。累積産出量は200トン以上（金換算）に達し、日本の金産出量の大部分を占めています。菱刈周辺は古代から温泉や鉱物資源に恵まれた地域で、鎌倉・室町時代にも金採掘の記録があります。現在も現役の鉱山として稼働しており、坑道見学ツアーも実施されています。
hishikari_gold_mine.name_en: Hishikari Gold Mine (Japan's largest gold mine)
hishikari_gold_mine.highlight_en: The world's highest grade gold mine. Cumulative production since discovery in 1985 is the largest in Japan
hishikari_gold_mine.text_en: Hishikari Gold Mine is the largest gold mine in Japan, located in Isa City (formerly Hishikari Town), Kagoshima Prefecture. It was discovered by Sumitomo Metal Mining in 1985, and subsequent development revealed that it is a high-grade gold deposit (more than 40 grams of gold per ton), which is rare in the world. Cumulative production has reached over 200 tons (gold equivalent), accounting for the majority of Japan's gold production. The area around Hishikari has been blessed with hot springs and mineral resources since ancient times, and there are records of gold mining during the Kamakura and Muromachi periods. It is still in operation as an active mine, and tours are also available.

osumi_kokufu.name: 大隅国府跡
osumi_kokufu.highlight: 律令時代の大隅国の行政中心地。隼人征討後に設置された国府
osumi_kokufu.text: 大隅国府は、奈良時代に設置された大隅国（現鹿児島県東部）の行政中心地です。720〜721年の「隼人の乱」平定後、ヤマト朝廷は南九州の支配を強化するため大隅国を設置し、国府・国分寺を整備しました。隼人はもともと南九州の先住民的な存在で、ヤマト王権とは独自の関係を持ちながら、隼人舞などの文化も宮廷に伝えました。国府跡周辺には条里制の地割りが残る地域もあり、奈良時代の計画的な土地利用の痕跡を見ることができます。霧島市国分地区には発掘調査の成果を展示する施設があります。
osumi_kokufu.highlight_en: The administrative center of Osumi Province during the Ritsuryo period. Kokufu established after Hayato's conquest
osumi_kokufu.text_en: Osumi Kokufu is the administrative center of Osumi Province (present-day eastern Kagoshima Prefecture) established during the Nara period. After the Hayato Rebellion was pacified in 720-721, the Yamato court established Osumi Province in order to strengthen its control over southern Kyushu, and established the Kokufu and Kokubunji temples there. Hayato was originally an indigenous people of southern Kyushu, and while having a unique relationship with the Yamato kingship, they also brought culture such as Hayato dance to the imperial court. There are areas around the Kokufu site where land divisions based on the Jori system remain, and you can see traces of planned land use during the Nara period. There is a facility in the Kokubu district of Kirishima City that displays the results of excavations.

yamakawa_port_history.name: 山川港（琉球・アジア貿易の窓口）
yamakawa_port_history.kana: やまかわこうりゅうきゅうあじあぼうえきのまどぐち
yamakawa_port_history.highlight: 薩摩藩が琉球・中国・東南アジアと秘密貿易を行った歴史的な港
yamakawa_port_history.text: 山川港は、鹿児島県指宿市の薩摩半島南端に位置する天然の良港で、古代から東シナ海・南シナ海への航海の出発点として機能してきました。中世には薩摩の倭寇・商人が琉球・中国・東南アジアと交易する際の重要拠点でした。1609年に薩摩藩が琉球王国を征服した後は、琉球を通じた中国（清）との秘密貿易（抜け荷）の窓口として機能し、薩摩藩の財政を潤しました。この密貿易で得た富が幕末の薩摩藩の富国強兵政策を支えた面もあります。港周辺には弥生時代の遺跡も残り、古代からの長い海の歴史を刻んでいます。
yamakawa_port_history.highlight_en: A historical port where the Satsuma clan conducted secret trade with Ryukyu, China, and Southeast Asia.
yamakawa_port_history.text_en: Yamakawa Port is a good natural port located at the southern tip of the Satsuma Peninsula in Ibusuki City, Kagoshima Prefecture, and has functioned as a departure point for voyages to the East China Sea and South China Sea since ancient times. In the Middle Ages, it was an important base for Satsuma's Wakō and merchants to trade with Ryukyu, China, and Southeast Asia. After the Satsuma Domain conquered the Ryukyu Kingdom in 1609, it functioned as a window for secret trade with China (Qing) through the Ryukyus, enriching the Satsuma Domain's finances. The wealth gained from this smuggling trade supported the Satsuma clan's policy of enriching the country and strengthening its military at the end of the Edo period. Ruins from the Yayoi period remain around the port, marking a long maritime history dating back to ancient times.

fukuyama_castle_aira.name: 福山城跡（姶良の武家文化）
fukuyama_castle_aira.kana: ふくやまじょうあとあいらのぶけぶんか
fukuyama_castle_aira.highlight: 島津氏の重臣・北郷氏らが治めた姶良の中世城郭。薩摩武士文化の結晶
fukuyama_castle_aira.text: 姶良（あいら）地方（現鹿児島県姶良市）は、大隅半島の付け根に位置し、中世から江戸時代にかけて薩摩・大隅両国の交通の要衝として重要な地域でした。福山城（姶良城ともいう）は島津氏の重臣・北郷氏らが守った山城で、大隅支配の拠点でした。加治木は江戸時代に島津氏の支藩「加治木島津家」が置かれた地で、薩摩武士の気風と文化を今に伝えます。幕末には精忠組（誠忠組）と呼ばれる改革派武士グループがここで活動し、維新の原動力となりました。「加治木まつり」は姶良地方最大の伝統行事です。
fukuyama_castle_aira.name_en: Fukuyama Castle ruins (Samurai culture of Aira)
fukuyama_castle_aira.highlight_en: A medieval castle in Aira ruled by the Kitago clan, a senior vassal of the Shimazu clan. Crystallization of Satsuma samurai culture
fukuyama_castle_aira.text_en: The Aira region (currently Aira City, Kagoshima Prefecture) is located at the base of the Osumi Peninsula, and was an important region from the Middle Ages to the Edo period as a transportation hub between Satsuma and Osumi. Fukuyama Castle (also known as Aira Castle) was a mountain castle protected by the Kitago clan, a senior vassal of the Shimazu clan, and was the base of Osumi's rule. Kajiki was the site of the Kajiki Shimazu family, a branch of the Shimazu clan, during the Edo period, and it conveys the ethos and culture of the Satsuma samurai to this day. At the end of the Edo period, a reformist samurai group called the Seichu-gumi operated here and became the driving force behind the Meiji Restoration. "Kajiki Festival" is the largest traditional event in the Aira region.

taniyama_ancient.name: 谷山・坊津道と薩摩の歴史街道
taniyama_ancient.kana: たにやまぼうのつみちとさつまのれきしかいどう
taniyama_ancient.highlight: 鹿児島市南部の古代街道。「南の天草」坊津へ続く薩摩の海防道
taniyama_ancient.text: 谷山地区（鹿児島市南部）から南薩の坊津へと続く「坊津道」は、古代から近世にかけて薩摩の重要な道でした。奈良時代に遣唐使船の寄港地として栄えた坊津（「日本三津」の一）へのルートとして機能し、中国・琉球との外交・交易を支えました。谷山には古代の条里制地割りの痕跡が残る地域があり、奈良時代の計画的な農地開発が行われたことを示しています。幕末には薩摩藩の海防強化により沿岸部に砲台が築かれ、その遺構も残っています。谷山は現在鹿児島市に合併されていますが、独自の地域文化を保っています。
taniyama_ancient.highlight_en: An ancient road in the southern part of Kagoshima City. Satsuma coast road leading to Bozu, “Amakusa of the South”
taniyama_ancient.text_en: The Bozu Road, which runs from the Taniyama area (southern part of Kagoshima City) to Bozu in Minamisatsu, was an important road in Satsuma from ancient times to early modern times. It functioned as a route to Botsu (one of Japan's Three Tsutsu), which prospered as a port of call for envoys envoys to China during the Nara period, and supported diplomacy and trade with China and the Ryukyus. There are areas in Taniyama where traces of the ancient Jori system of land division remain, indicating that systematic agricultural land development took place during the Nara period. At the end of the Edo period, as the Satsuma domain strengthened its coastal defenses, a battery was built along the coast, and its remains still remain. Although Taniyama has now been merged with Kagoshima City, it has maintained its unique regional culture.

kanzeonji_dazaifu.name: 観世音寺
kanzeonji_dazaifu.highlight: 天智天皇が母・斉明天皇の冥福を祈り建立を命じた官寺。日本最古の梵鐘を有し、奈良・東大寺や法隆寺と深く関わる九州仏教の中心地。
kanzeonji_dazaifu.text: 観世音寺は7世紀後半、天智天皇が母・斉明天皇の菩提を弔うために建立を命じた官寺です。完成まで約80年を要したとされ、奈良時代の大宰府を代表する寺院として国家的保護を受けました。境内に現存する梵鐘は日本最古のものと言われ、奈良の東大寺の鐘と同じ鋳型から作られたとの伝承があります。道鏡事件で有名な弓削道鏡がここで没したとも伝わり、平安時代には菅原道真も参拝したと記録されています。かつては七堂伽藍が立ち並ぶ大寺院でしたが、中世以降に衰退し、現在は宝蔵に多数の仏像を収蔵しています。
kanzeonji_dazaifu.highlight_en: An official temple ordered by Emperor Tenji to pray for the repose of his mother, Emperor Saimei. The center of Kyushu Buddhism, which has Japan's oldest temple bell and is deeply connected to Nara's Todaiji Temple and Horyuji Temple.
kanzeonji_dazaifu.text_en: Kanzeon-ji Temple is an official temple that was ordered to be built in the late 7th century by Emperor Tenji to mourn the death of his mother, Emperor Saimei. It is said that it took approximately 80 years to complete, and it received national protection as a representative temple of Dazaifu during the Nara period. The temple bell that still exists within the temple grounds is said to be the oldest in Japan, and legend has it that it was made from the same mold as the bell at Todaiji Temple in Nara. It is said that Dokyo Yuge, famous for the Dokyo Incident, died here, and it is recorded that Michizane Sugawara also visited the shrine during the Heian period. It was once a large temple with seven temples, but it has declined since the Middle Ages and now houses a large number of Buddhist statues in its treasury.

homazan_shrine.name: 宝満山竈門神社
homazan_shrine.kana: ほうまんざんかまどじんじゃ
homazan_shrine.highlight: 大宰府の鬼門を守る霊山・宝満山の麓に鎮座。古代より修験道の霊場として崇められ、大宰府赴任の官人たちが必ず参詣した神聖な山。
homazan_shrine.text: 宝満山（標高829m）は大宰府の北東、鬼門の方角に位置する霊山で、山頂には竈門神社の上宮が鎮座しています。麓の下宮は縁結びの神として現在も人気ですが、古代には大宰府を守護する軍事・宗教上の要地でした。山上には古代の磐座信仰の痕跡が残り、奈良時代から修験道の行場として栄えました。菅原道真が太宰府配流中に詣でたとも伝えられ、歌人たちにも愛された山です。山頂から望む博多湾と筑紫平野の景観は、古代の人々が「神の山」と崇めた理由を今も物語っています。
homazan_shrine.highlight_en: It is enshrined at the foot of Mt. Homan, a sacred mountain that protects Dazaifu's Demon Gate. A sacred mountain that has been revered as a sacred site for Shugendo since ancient times, and was always visited by government officials assigned to Dazaifu.
homazan_shrine.text_en: Mt. Homan (829m above sea level) is a sacred mountain located in the direction of Kimon, northeast of Dazaifu, and the upper shrine of Kamado Shrine is enshrined at the top of the mountain. Shimomiya at the foot of the mountain is still popular today as a god of matchmaking, but in ancient times it was a military and religious point that protected Dazaifu. Traces of the ancient Iwaza faith remain on the mountaintop, and it flourished as a training ground for Shugendo since the Nara period. It is said that Michizane Sugawara visited this mountain during his exile in Dazaifu, and it was also loved by poets. The view of Hakata Bay and the Chikushi Plain from the top of the mountain still shows why ancient people worshiped it as the ``Mountain of the Gods.''

najima_castle.name: 名島城跡
najima_castle.highlight: 小早川隆景が築いた豊前・筑前支配の拠点。豊臣秀吉も訪れた水城で、関ヶ原後に黒田長政が福岡城を築くまで筑前の中心であった。
najima_castle.text: 名島城は博多湾に突き出した小半島に築かれた海城で、もとは立花氏の居城でしたが、天正15年（1587年）に小早川隆景が入城し大規模に整備しました。豊臣秀吉が朝鮮出兵の際に立ち寄り、茶会を開いたことでも知られています。関ヶ原の戦い後、黒田長政が筑前を領有すると福岡城の築城資材として名島城の建物が移築され、廃城となりました。現在は石垣の一部と土塁が残り、名島神社の境内に往時の面影を伝えています。眼前に広がる博多湾の景色は、かつての「海の城」としての戦略的価値を今も示しています。
najima_castle.highlight_en: A base for controlling Buzen and Chikuzen built by Takakage Kobayakawa. Mizuki was also visited by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, and was the center of Chikuzen until Kuroda Nagamasa built Fukuoka Castle after Sekigahara.
najima_castle.text_en: 名島城は博多湾に突き出した小半島に築かれた海城で、もとは立花氏の居城でしたが、天正15年（1587年）に小早川隆景が入城し大規模に整備しました。 It is also known that Toyotomi Hideyoshi stopped by and held a tea party when he sent troops to Korea.関ヶ原の戦い後、黒田長政が筑前を領有すると福岡城の築城資材として名島城の建物が移築され、廃城となりました。 Today, part of the stone wall and earthworks remain, giving the grounds of Najima Shrine a vestige of the past. The view of Hakata Bay that stretches out in front of you still shows its strategic value as a former "sea castle."

umi_hachimangu.name: 宇美八幡宮
umi_hachimangu.highlight: 神功皇后が応神天皇を産んだと伝わる「産みの宮」。安産・子育ての神として全国に知られ、境内の湯蓋の森・鎮懐石は国の天然記念物・史跡。
umi_hachimangu.text: 宇美八幡宮は、神功皇后が三韓征伐から帰還後にこの地で応神天皇を出産したという伝説に基づく古社です。「宇美」の地名は「産み」に由来するとされ、安産の神として古くから皇室や武家の崇敬を集めました。境内には樹齢2000年ともいわれる大楠「湯蓋の森」が鬱蒼と茂り、神功皇后が産後に石を懐に入れて休んだとされる「鎮懐石」も保存されています。この鎮懐石は万葉集にも詠まれた歌枕で、奈良・平安時代から歌人に親しまれてきました。毎年秋には豪壮な放生会も行われ、地域の信仰の中心です。
umi_hachimangu.highlight_en: It is said that Empress Jingu gave birth to Emperor Ojin at the Birth Palace. Known throughout the country as the god of safe childbirth and child rearing, the Yubuta no Mori and Chinkaiseki shrines within the shrine grounds are national natural monuments and historic sites.
umi_hachimangu.text_en: Umi Hachimangu Shrine is an old shrine based on the legend that Empress Jingu gave birth to Emperor Ojin here after returning from the Sankan Conquest. The place name ``Umi'' is said to come from the word ``childbirth'', and has been revered by the imperial family and samurai families since ancient times as the god of safe childbirth. In the precincts, there is a dense forest of large camphor trees that are said to be 2,000 years old called "Yukata no Mori", and the "Chinkaiseki" where Empress Jingu is said to have rested with a stone in her bosom after giving birth is also preserved. This Chinkaiseki is a song pillow that was written in the Manyoshu, and has been popular with poets since the Nara and Heian periods. A spectacular Hojo-e is held every fall, and it is a center of local worship.

hirabaru_ruins.name: 平原遺跡
hirabaru_ruins.highlight: 日本最大の銅鏡「内行花文鏡」が出土した弥生時代の王墓。伊都国の女王墓とも言われ、邪馬台国論争に深く関わる九州最重要の弥生遺跡の一つ。
hirabaru_ruins.text: 平原遺跡は糸島市に所在する弥生時代後期（2世紀末〜3世紀初頭）の方形周溝墓で、1965年の発掘調査で日本最大の鏡である内行花文鏡（直径46.5cm）をはじめ多数の銅鏡・玉類が出土しました。副葬品の豪華さから、伊都国の首長、あるいは女王（卑弥呼と同時代？）の墓とする説があり、邪馬台国論争においても重要な位置を占めます。出土品は現在、糸島市立伊都国歴史博物館に収蔵されており、国宝級の内容とも評価されています。伊都国はかつて一大率が置かれ、中国・朝鮮半島との外交窓口となった地です。
hirabaru_ruins.highlight_en: A royal tomb from the Yayoi period where Japan's largest bronze mirror, the Uchigyo Hanabun Mirror, was unearthed. It is said to be the tomb of the queen of Ito Province, and is one of the most important Yayoi ruins in Kyushu, deeply involved in the Yamataikoku controversy.
hirabaru_ruins.text_en: The Hirabaru Ruins are square groove tombs from the late Yayoi period (late 2nd century to early 3rd century) located in Itoshima City, and excavations in 1965 unearthed a large number of bronze mirrors and beads, including the Uchigyo Flower Pattern Mirror (46.5 cm in diameter), the largest mirror in Japan. Because of the luxury of the burial goods, there is a theory that this is the tomb of the leader or queen of Ito Province (contemporary with Himiko?), and it also plays an important role in the Yamataikoku controversy. The excavated items are currently stored at the Itoshima City Ito-Kuni Museum of History, and are considered to be national treasures. Ito Province was once a place where a major military power was established and served as a diplomatic contact point with China and the Korean Peninsula.

kawara_copper.name: 香春岳（採銅所）
kawara_copper.kana: かわらだけ・さいどうしょ
kawara_copper.highlight: 奈良の大仏（東大寺盧舎那仏）の鋳造に使われた銅の産地。古代日本最大の銅山として「和銅」の地名の由来にも関わる歴史的採掘地。
kawara_copper.text: 香春岳は田川郡香春町にそびえる石灰岩の山で、その麓の採銅所は奈良時代に国家的な銅山として開発されました。749年に完成した東大寺の大仏（盧舎那仏）の鋳造には莫大な量の銅が必要とされ、この地の銅山が主要供給源の一つとなりました。「採銅所」という地名はそのまま当時の機能を伝えており、古代の官営採掘の歴史を今に残す貴重な地です。山頂付近には香春神社の奥宮が鎮座し、新羅系の渡来氏族・辛嶋氏が祀ったと伝わる神を合祀しています。セメント採掘で山容が大きく変わりましたが、地域の古代史を語る上で欠かせない場所です。
kawara_copper.highlight_en: This is the origin of the copper used to cast the Great Buddha of Nara (Roshanabutsu of Todaiji Temple). A historic mining site that is also the origin of the name "Wado" as Japan's largest copper mine in ancient times.
kawara_copper.text_en: Mt. Kaharudake is a limestone mountain that rises in Kaharu Town, Tagawa District, and the copper mine at its foot was developed as a national copper mine during the Nara period. The casting of the Great Buddha (Roshanabutsu) at Todaiji Temple, which was completed in 749, required a huge amount of copper, and the local copper mine was one of the main sources of this supply. The place's name ``Copper Mining Works'' conveys its function at the time, and it is a valuable place that still retains the history of ancient government-run mining. Near the top of the mountain is the inner shrine of Koharu Shrine, which enshrines the deity that is said to have been enshrined by the Karashima clan, an immigrant clan from Silla. Although the mountain's appearance has changed significantly due to cement mining, it is an essential place to talk about the ancient history of the area.

noko_island_history.name: 能古島の歴史遺跡
noko_island_history.kana: のこのしまのれきしいせき
noko_island_history.highlight: 博多湾に浮かぶ離島で、万葉集にも詠まれた「能古の島」。元寇の際の防塁遺構や古墳が点在し、博多の歴史を海から見守り続けた島。
noko_island_history.text: 能古島は博多湾のほぼ中央に浮かぶ周囲12kmの小島です。万葉集に「ぬこの島」として詠まれ、古代から人が暮らしていた証拠となる古墳や遺跡が島内に点在しています。鎌倉時代の元寇（文永・弘安の役）では、博多湾に侵攻したモンゴル・元軍の艦隊が能古島付近に停泊したとされ、島の防衛が重要な意味を持ちました。島内には元寇に関連する伝説地や、戦国時代の争乱を伝える史跡も残っています。江戸時代には黒田藩の管轄下に置かれ、薪炭の供給地として機能しました。現在も牧歌的な自然の中に歴史の層が重なる、博多湾の隠れた史跡スポットです。
noko_island_history.highlight_en: ``Noko Island'' is a remote island floating in Hakata Bay, and is written about in the Manyoshu. The island is dotted with the ruins of fortifications and ancient tombs from the Mongol invasion, and has continued to watch over Hakata's history from the sea.
noko_island_history.text_en: Nokojima is a small island with a circumference of 12km located almost in the center of Hakata Bay. It is referred to as ``Nuko Island'' in the Manyoshu, and there are ancient tombs and ruins dotted around the island that provide evidence that people have lived here since ancient times. During the Mongol Invasion (Bun'ei-Koan War) during the Kamakura period, the Mongolian Yuan army fleet that invaded Hakata Bay is said to have anchored near Noko Island, and the defense of the island was important. There are also legendary sites related to the Mongol invasion and historical sites that tell of the conflicts of the Sengoku period. During the Edo period, it came under the jurisdiction of the Kuroda clan and functioned as a source of firewood and charcoal. It is a hidden historical spot in Hakata Bay where layers of history overlap in the idyllic nature.

tachibana_castle.name: 立花山城跡
tachibana_castle.kana: たちばなやまじょうあと
tachibana_castle.highlight: 九州随一の知将・立花道雪・宗茂父子が守った難攻不落の山城。大友氏の北部九州支配を支えた戦略拠点で、天下無双の武将・立花宗茂の活躍の地。
tachibana_castle.text: 立花山城は標高367mの立花山山頂に築かれた山城で、大友氏の武将・戸次鑑連（後の立花道雪）が長年にわたって守った要塞です。落雷で半身不随になりながらも輿に乗って戦場を駆け巡った道雪の武勇は語り草となっています。その娘婿・立花宗茂は「西国無双の武将」と称えられ、関ヶ原で西軍に属して改易されながらも旧領に復帰した唯一の大名として有名です。城跡からは博多湾から筑紫平野まで一望でき、この地が北部九州支配の要であったことがよく分かります。現在は登山道が整備され、ハイキングコースとしても人気です。
tachibana_castle.highlight_en: An impregnable mountain castle protected by Kyushu's most intelligent generals, father and son Michisetsu Tachibana and Muneshige. A strategic base that supported the Otomo clan's control over northern Kyushu, and the place where Muneshige Tachibana, an unparalleled military commander, played an active role.
tachibana_castle.text_en: Tachibanayama Castle is a mountain castle built on the summit of Mt. Tachibana at an altitude of 367 meters, and is a fortress that was protected for many years by the Otomo clan's military commander Toji Kanren (later Tachibana Dosetsu). Although his body was partially paralyzed by a lightning strike, Michisetsu's bravery as he rode around the battlefield in a palanquin has become a legend. His son-in-law, Muneshige Tachibana, was hailed as ``the unparalleled military commander of the Western region,'' and is famous for being the only daimyo who belonged to the Western army at Sekigahara and was transferred, but returned to his former territory. The castle ruins offer a panoramic view from Hakata Bay to the Chikushi Plain, making it clear that this area was a key point in the domination of northern Kyushu. Currently, there are mountain trails in place and it is also a popular hiking course.

ongagawa_ancient.name: 遠賀川流域の弥生遺跡
ongagawa_ancient.kana: おんががわりゅういきのやよいいせき
ongagawa_ancient.highlight: 弥生文化の東方伝播ルートとなった遠賀川式土器の発祥地。稲作と金属器をもたらした渡来文化が列島へ広がる「弥生の幹線道路」の出発点。
ongagawa_ancient.text: 遠賀川は北部九州から瀬戸内海方面へ続く交通の要衝で、弥生時代に「遠賀川式土器」と呼ばれる土器型式の発祥地として日本考古学史上極めて重要な地域です。この土器型式は弥生前期に西日本全域へ急速に広まり、稲作文化の東方伝播を象徴するものとして知られています。流域の各地に弥生時代の集落遺跡が点在し、大陸から伝わった水田稲作・青銅器・鉄器が日本列島へ広がっていく過程を考古学的に追うことができます。遠賀川の水運は古代・中世も続き、炭鉱開発で知られる近代まで、この地域の歴史を一貫して支えてきた大動脈です。
ongagawa_ancient.name_en: Yayoi ruins in the Onga River basin
ongagawa_ancient.highlight_en: The birthplace of Ongagawa-style pottery, which became the route for the eastward spread of Yayoi culture. The starting point of the Yayoi Main Road, where the imported culture that brought rice cultivation and metal tools spread to the archipelago.
ongagawa_ancient.text_en: The Onga River is an important transportation hub from northern Kyushu to the Seto Inland Sea, and is an extremely important area in the history of Japanese archeology as the birthplace of a type of pottery called ``Onga River pottery'' during the Yayoi period. This pottery type spread rapidly throughout western Japan during the early Yayoi period, and is known to symbolize the eastward spread of rice cultivation culture. There are ruins of villages from the Yayoi period dotted throughout the basin, and it is possible to trace archaeologically the process by which rice paddy cultivation, bronze tools, and iron tools, which were introduced from the continent, spread to the Japanese archipelago. The Onga River has been a major artery that has consistently supported the region's history, from ancient and medieval times to modern times when it was known for the development of coal mines.

fukuoka_castle_reconstructed.name: 黒田官兵衛・長政ゆかりの地（福岡城下）
fukuoka_castle_reconstructed.kana: くろだかんべえ・ながまさゆかりのち
fukuoka_castle_reconstructed.highlight: 豊臣秀吉の軍師・黒田官兵衛と、その子・長政が整備した福岡城下。関ヶ原の功績で筑前52万石を得た黒田家が築いた近世城下町の原点。
fukuoka_castle_reconstructed.text: 「天下の軍師」として知られる黒田官兵衛（如水）は、関ヶ原の戦い後、息子・長政が筑前52万石を拝領したことで博多に黒田藩を樹立しました。長政は慶長6年（1601年）から福岡城の築城を開始し、名島城の資材を移して7年がかりで完成させます。城下町の区画整備では、博多の豪商たちを城下に移住させ、博多・福岡の二都が融合した独特の都市構造が生まれました。官兵衛自身は隠居して如水と名乗り、城下で薬草園を開いたとも伝えられています。現在の大濠公園はかつての外堀跡であり、城下の水利システムの名残を今に伝えています。
fukuoka_castle_reconstructed.name_en: Place related to Kuroda Kanbei and Nagamasa (Fukuoka Castle Town)
fukuoka_castle_reconstructed.highlight_en: Fukuoka Castle was developed by Toyotomi Hideyoshi's military commander Kuroda Kanbei and his son Nagamasa. The origin of the early modern castle town built by the Kuroda family, who earned 520,000 koku in Chikuzen thanks to their exploits at Sekigahara.
fukuoka_castle_reconstructed.text_en: After the Battle of Sekigahara, Kuroda Kanbei (Josui), known as the ``nation's tactician,'' established the Kuroda clan in Hakata after his son Nagamasa received 520,000 koku of Chikuzen. Nagamasa began construction of Fukuoka Castle in 1601 and completed it over seven years, transferring materials from Najima Castle. In the development of the castle town, wealthy merchants from Hakata moved to the castle town, creating a unique urban structure that merged the two capitals of Hakata and Fukuoka. It is said that Kanbei himself retired, took the name Josui, and opened a medicinal herb garden in the castle town. The current Ohori Park is the ruins of the former outer moat, and the remains of the castle's water supply system can still be seen today.

kurume_castle.name: 久留米城跡（篠山城）
kurume_castle.kana: くるめじょうあと・ささやまじょう
kurume_castle.highlight: 筑後21万石・久留米藩有馬氏の居城。筑後川を天然の堀とした平城で、明治維新まで約250年にわたり久留米藩政の中枢を担った。
kurume_castle.text: 久留米城は筑後川の北岸に築かれた平城で、江戸時代には久留米藩21万石を治めた有馬氏の居城として栄えました。もともとは戦国時代に毛利氏家臣の問田氏が築いた城で、関ヶ原後に有馬豊氏が入城して大改修を行いました。筑後川を南の外堀として利用した堅固な構造で、本丸・二の丸・三の丸が整備された大規模な城郭です。天守は建てられませんでしたが、本丸には御殿が置かれ、藩主の居所として機能しました。現在は本丸跡に篠山神社が鎮座し、石垣と堀の一部が往時の姿を伝えています。
kurume_castle.highlight_en: Chikugo 210,000 koku, the residence of the Arima clan of the Kurume domain. It was a flat castle with the Chikugo River as its natural moat, and served as the center of Kurume domain government for about 250 years until the Meiji Restoration.
kurume_castle.text_en: Kurume Castle is a flat castle built on the north bank of the Chikugo River, and during the Edo period it prospered as the residence of the Arima clan, who ruled the Kurume domain with an income of 210,000 koku. The castle was originally built by the Toda clan, a vassal of the Mori clan, during the Sengoku period, and after Sekigahara, the Yutaka Arima clan entered the castle and underwent major renovations. It is a large-scale castle with a strong structure that uses the Chikugo River as its southern outer moat, and has a main castle, a second castle, and a third castle. Although no castle tower was built, a palace was placed in the main keep and served as the residence of the lord of the domain. Currently, Sasayama Shrine is located on the site of the main enclosure, and the stone walls and part of the moat still remain as they were in the past.

suiten_gu_kurume.name: 水天宮（全国総本宮）
suiten_gu_kurume.highlight: 壇ノ浦で入水した安徳天皇と建礼門院を祀る全国総本宮。安産・子授けの神として有名で、久留米城内に鎮座した唯一無二の「城内の神社」。
suiten_gu_kurume.text: 水天宮の総本宮は久留米藩の城内に鎮座するという珍しい神社で、源平合戦の壇ノ浦（1185年）で入水した安徳天皇と、その母・建礼門院らを主祭神としています。平家の女官・按察使局伊勢が主君の霊を筑後国の鷺野ヶ原に祀ったのが起源とされます。江戸時代に久留米藩9代藩主・有馬頼徳が、江戸の有馬家下屋敷に分霊を勧請したことで「江戸の水天宮」が誕生し、安産・子育ての神として江戸庶民に爆発的に広まりました。現在も全国各地に約100社の水天宮があり、すべて久留米が総本宮です。
suiten_gu_kurume.highlight_en: This is the main shrine for the whole country, and it enshrines Emperor Antoku, who drowned in Dan-no-ura, and Kenreimon-in. Famous as the god of safe childbirth and child-bearing, Kurume Castle is a one-of-a-kind shrine located within Kurume Castle.
suiten_gu_kurume.text_en: The main shrine of Suitengu Shrine is a rare shrine located within the castle grounds of the Kurume clan, and the main deities enshrined are Emperor Antoku, who drowned in Dannoura during the Genpei War (1185), and his mother Kenreimonin. It is said to have its origin when the Heike clan's lady-in-waiting, Ansakushibu Ise, enshrined the spirit of her lord at Saginogagahara in Chikugo Province. During the Edo period, Yorinori Arima, the 9th lord of the Kurume domain, solicited a spirit to visit the Arima family's mansion in Edo, and ``Edo's Suitengu'' was born, and it spread explosively among the common people of Edo as a god of safe childbirth and child rearing. Currently, there are approximately 100 Suitengu shrines all over the country, all of which are headquartered in Kurume.

bairinji_kurume.name: 梅林寺
bairinji_kurume.highlight: 久留米藩主・有馬家の菩提寺。筑後川沿いに広がる名刹で、境内の梅林と国指定重要文化財の仏像群が名高く、近代剣道の祖・江口楽翁ゆかりの地。
bairinji_kurume.text: 梅林寺は寛永3年（1626年）、久留米藩初代藩主・有馬豊氏が父の菩提を弔うために建立した臨済宗妙心寺派の寺院です。以来、有馬家代々の菩提寺として手厚く保護され、広大な境内には歴代藩主の霊廟が並んでいます。境内に植えられた梅の木は早春に美しく咲き、「梅林寺の梅」として古くから親しまれています。寺に伝わる彫刻や工芸品には国の重要文化財指定品も含まれ、久留米藩の文化的豊かさを示しています。また、幕末から明治にかけて活躍した禅僧・大愚良寛の師匠にあたる人物もこの寺に縁があり、近代禅の歴史との接点も持ちます。
bairinji_kurume.highlight_en: The family temple of the Arima family, the lords of the Kurume domain. This famous temple spreads along the Chikugo River, and is famous for its plum grove and Buddhist statues that are designated as nationally important cultural properties, and is connected to Rakuo Eguchi, the founder of modern Kendo.
bairinji_kurume.text_en: Bairinji is a temple of the Myoshinji sect of the Rinzai sect, built in 1626 by Yutaka Arima, the first lord of the Kurume domain, to mourn his father's body. Since then, it has been carefully protected as the family temple of the Arima family for generations, and the mausoleums of successive feudal lords line the vast grounds. The plum trees planted within the precincts bloom beautifully in early spring and have been popularly known as the ``Bairin-ji Plums'' for a long time. The sculptures and crafts handed down at the temple include some that have been designated as nationally important cultural properties, demonstrating the cultural richness of the Kurume clan. In addition, the master of the Zen monk Daigurōkan, who was active from the end of the Edo period to the Meiji period, also has ties to this temple, and has connections with the history of modern Zen.

kurume_kasuri.name: 久留米絣発祥の地
kurume_kasuri.kana: くるめがすりはっしょうのち
kurume_kasuri.highlight: 日本三大絣の一つ・久留米絣の発祥地。江戸後期に少女・井上伝が偶然の発見から独自の技法を確立し、筑後一帯の農家の副業として全国に広まった。
kurume_kasuri.text: 久留米絣は文化2年（1805年）頃、久留米近郊の農家の少女・井上伝（12歳）が、古い着物の白い斑点模様を不思議に思って解いてみたところ、糸が括られて染まっていなかったことに気づき、同様の技法を独自に開発したことが始まりとされています。この手法は筑後平野の農家に急速に広まり、副業として定着しました。久留米絣は藍染めと手括りによる素朴な幾何学模様が特徴で、丈夫で美しいことから庶民の日常着として全国に普及しました。現在は国の重要無形文化財に指定されており、久留米市内に今も伝統的な製織工房が残っています。
kurume_kasuri.highlight_en: The birthplace of Kurume Kasuri, one of the three major Kasuri in Japan. In the late Edo period, a young girl, Den Inoue, established a unique technique through a chance discovery, and it spread throughout the country as a side job for farmers in the Chikugo area.
kurume_kasuri.text_en: Kurume Kasuri is said to have originated around 1805, when a 12-year-old farmer girl named Den Inoue from a village near Kurume wondered about the white speckled pattern on an old kimono, and when she tried to unravel it, she realized that the thread had been tied and was not dyed, and she developed a similar technique on her own. This method quickly spread to farmers in the Chikugo Plain and became established as a side job. Kurume Kasuri is characterized by its simple geometric patterns created by indigo dyeing and hand-tying, and because it is durable and beautiful, it has become popular throughout the country as everyday wear for the common people. It is currently designated as a national important intangible cultural property, and traditional weaving workshops still remain in Kurume City.

arima_rebellion.name: 久留米藩・有馬事件ゆかりの地
arima_rebellion.kana: くるめはん・ありまじけんゆかりのち
arima_rebellion.highlight: 幕末の久留米藩を揺るがした「久留米藩難事件」（1871年）の舞台。勤王派と佐幕派の藩内抗争が明治維新後も尾を引き、多数の藩士が処刑された悲劇の地。
arima_rebellion.text: 久留米藩は江戸時代を通じて21万石の外様大名・有馬氏が治めましたが、幕末には尊王攘夷運動が藩内で激化し、過激な勤王派が台頭しました。明治維新後の1871年、新政府はこれを「不穏」と判断し、藩内の勤王派指導者ら数十名を一斉に処分する「久留米藩難事件」が起きました。この事件で多くの志士が斬罪・流罪に処され、久留米の地に深い傷跡を残しました。有馬氏は外様ながら江戸期を通じて21万石を維持し、近代久留米の礎を築きましたが、その終幕は藩士たちの悲劇で彩られていました。城跡周辺には処刑地や関連史跡が点在しています。
arima_rebellion.name_en: Kurume Domain/Place related to the Arima Incident
arima_rebellion.highlight_en: The setting for the Kurume Clan Incident (1871), which shook the Kurume Clan at the end of the Edo period. It was a tragic place where the feud between the loyalists and the Sabaku factions continued even after the Meiji Restoration, and many feudal retainers were executed.
arima_rebellion.text_en: Throughout the Edo period, the Kurume domain was ruled by the Arima clan, a feudal lord with a wealth of 210,000 koku, but at the end of the Edo period, the son-no-joi movement intensified within the domain, and radical pro-king factions rose to prominence. In 1871, after the Meiji Restoration, the new government judged this to be ``disturbing,'' and the ``Kurume Clan Incident'' occurred, in which dozens of loyalist leaders within the domain were summarily punished. As a result of this incident, many patriots were executed and exiled, leaving a deep scar on the land of Kurume. Despite being an outsider, the Arima clan maintained a net worth of 210,000 koku throughout the Edo period and laid the foundation for modern Kurume, but its final days were marked by the tragedies of the feudal retainers. The area around the castle ruins is dotted with execution sites and related historical sites.

tataragahama_battle.name: 多々良浜古戦場
tataragahama_battle.kana: たたらはまこせんじょう
tataragahama_battle.highlight: 1336年、九州に逃れた足利尊氏が菊池武敏率いる南朝軍を破り、京都奪還への逆転劇が始まった決戦地。日本史の流れを変えた南北朝最重要の合戦の一つ。
tataragahama_battle.text: 多々良浜の戦いは建武3年（1336年）3月、博多湾東岸の多々良浜（現・福岡市東区）で行われた合戦です。後醍醐天皇方の武将・菊池武敏が率いる南朝軍（約60,000）に対し、九州へ落ち延びた足利尊氏軍（約30,000）が激突しました。数で劣る尊氏軍でしたが、作戦が功を奏して菊池軍を撃破。この勝利を機に尊氏は九州の武士団を糾合して東上し、同年の湊川の戦いで楠木正成を破って京都を奪還、室町幕府の樹立へとつながりました。「九州から天下が変わった」とも言える歴史的転換点です。
tataragahama_battle.highlight_en: In 1336, Takauji Ashikaga, who had fled to Kyushu, defeated the Southern Court army led by Taketoshi Kikuchi, and the decisive battle began in his bid to recapture Kyoto. One of the most important battles between the Northern and Southern Courts that changed the course of Japanese history.
tataragahama_battle.text_en: The Battle of Tatarahama was a battle that took place in March 1336 at Tatarahama (present-day Higashi Ward, Fukuoka City) on the east coast of Hakata Bay. Ashikaga Takauji's army (approximately 30,000 soldiers) who had escaped to Kyushu clashed with the Southern Court army (approximately 60,000 troops) led by Taketoshi Kikuchi, a military commander on Emperor Go-Daigo's side. Although Takauji's army was inferior in numbers, their strategy was successful and they defeated Kikuchi's army. Taking advantage of this victory, Takauji rallied the samurai groups in Kyushu and marched east, defeating Masashige Kusunoki at the Battle of Minatogawa in the same year and recapturing Kyoto, leading to the establishment of the Muromachi Shogunate. It is a historical turning point that can be said to be ``the world changed from Kyushu''.

seisai_shogunate_dazaifu.name: 征西将軍府跡（大宰府）
seisai_shogunate_dazaifu.kana: せいせいしょうぐんふあと
seisai_shogunate_dazaifu.highlight: 後醍醐天皇の皇子・懐良親王が九州の南朝政権「征西将軍府」を置いた地。20年以上にわたって北朝・室町幕府と対抗し、明との国交にも関与した九州南朝の中枢。
seisai_shogunate_dazaifu.text: 征西将軍府は、後醍醐天皇の皇子・懐良親王が九州の南朝勢力を統率するために置いた政権機関です。懐良親王は1336年に九州へ下向し、菊池氏の援助を受けながら長年にわたって北朝・室町幕府の九州探題と戦い続けました。1361年には大宰府を占拠することに成功し、ここに征西将軍府を開いて九州の多くの武士を従えました。明（中国）との外交でも「日本国王」として交渉するなど、独自の政権を運営。しかし1372年に今川了俊が九州探題として赴任すると徐々に圧迫され、大宰府を失って最終的に衰退しました。
seisai_shogunate_dazaifu.highlight_en: This is where Emperor Go-Daigo's son, Imperial Prince Kaneyoshi, established the Southern Court government in Kyushu, the Seisei Shogunate. The center of the Southern Court of Kyushu, which fought against the Northern Court and the Muromachi Shogunate for over 20 years, and was also involved in diplomatic relations with the Ming Dynasty.
seisai_shogunate_dazaifu.text_en: The Seisei Shogunate was a government institution established by Emperor Go-Daigo's son, Imperial Prince Kaneyoshi, to control the Southern Court forces in Kyushu. Imperial Prince Kaneyoshi went to Kyushu in 1336 and, with the support of the Kikuchi clan, continued to fight against the Kyushu tandai of the Northern Court and the Muromachi Shogunate for many years. In 1361, he succeeded in occupying Dazaifu, established the Seisei Shogunate here, and served many samurai from Kyushu. He operated his own government, negotiating diplomacy with Ming (China) as the "King of Japan." However, in 1372, when Ryoshun Imagawa was appointed as Kyushu Tandai, the area was gradually put under pressure, lost Dazaifu, and finally declined.

shoni_clan_ruins.name: 少弐氏館跡（太宰府周辺）
shoni_clan_ruins.kana: しょうにしやかたあと
shoni_clan_ruins.highlight: 鎌倉〜南北朝期、九州の政治を左右した少弐氏の拠点。元寇では北条氏と並んで九州防衛を主導し、南北朝期には北朝方として菊池氏（南朝）と筑後川をはさんで激闘を繰り広げた。
shoni_clan_ruins.text: 少弐氏は鎌倉時代から室町時代にかけて九州北部に強大な勢力を張った武家で、大宰少弐（大宰府の次官）を世襲したことから「少弐」を苗字としました。元寇（文永・弘安の役）では少弐景資・資能らが北条氏と並んで防衛の中核を担い、「弘安の役」での活躍は特に名高いものです。南北朝期には北朝・室町幕府方に属し、南朝方の菊池氏と筑後川をはさんで幾度も激突しました。1359年の大保原合戦（筑後川の戦い）では菊池武光・懐良親王連合軍に大敗を喫し、少弐頼尚が命からがら逃れるという危機も経験しました。
shoni_clan_ruins.highlight_en: From Kamakura to the Nanbokucho period, this was the base of the Shoni clan, who influenced the politics of Kyushu. During the Mongol invasion, he led the defense of Kyushu alongside the Hojo clan, and during the period of the Northern and Southern Courts, he fought a fierce battle with the Kikuchi clan (Southern Court) across the Chikugo River.
shoni_clan_ruins.text_en: The Shoni clan was a samurai family that had a powerful influence in northern Kyushu from the Kamakura period to the Muromachi period, and they adopted the surname ``Shoni'' because they inherited the position of Dazai Shoni (vice minister of Dazaifu). During the Mongol invasions (Bun'ei and Koan roles), Shoni Keisuke, Suenori, and others played the core of the defense alongside the Hojo clan, and their role in the ``Koan roles'' is particularly famous. During the period of the Northern and Southern Courts, it belonged to the Northern Court and the Muromachi Shogunate, and clashed many times with the Kikuchi clan of the Southern Court across the Chikugo River. At the Battle of Ohobara (Battle of the Chikugo River) in 1359, they suffered a crushing defeat against the combined forces of Takemitsu Kikuchi and Imperial Prince Kaneyoshi, and experienced a crisis in which Yorinao Shoni narrowly escaped with his life.

ouchi_clan_fukuoka.name: 大内氏の北部九州支配ゆかりの地
ouchi_clan_fukuoka.kana: おおうちしのほくぶきゅうしゅうしはいゆかりのち
ouchi_clan_fukuoka.highlight: 西日本最大の戦国大名・大内氏が豊前・筑前へ勢力を伸ばした拠点群。日明貿易を独占し、山口を「西の京」と呼ばれる文化都市に育てた大内文化の九州への波及地。
ouchi_clan_fukuoka.text: 大内氏は山口を本拠とした室町〜戦国時代の大大名で、全盛期には豊前・筑前・周防・長門・石見など6か国以上を支配しました。日明貿易（勘合貿易）を細川氏と競って独占し、莫大な富をもとに「西の京」山口に庭園・寺院・芸術を集積しました。大内氏の北部九州進出は南北朝時代にまでさかのぼり、豊前・筑前の武士団を傘下に収めて少弐氏や大友氏と抗争を繰り広げました。1551年の「大寧寺の変」で当主・義隆が家臣・陶晴賢に滅ぼされるまで、九州北部の歴史を左右する存在であり続けました。
ouchi_clan_fukuoka.name_en: Place associated with the Ouchi clan's control of northern Kyushu
ouchi_clan_fukuoka.highlight_en: A group of bases where the Ouchi clan, the largest Sengoku daimyo in Western Japan, expanded their influence to Buzen and Chikuzen. This is the area where the Ouchi culture spread to Kyushu, monopolizing the trade between Japan and the Ming Dynasty and developing Yamaguchi into a cultural city known as ``Western Capital''.
ouchi_clan_fukuoka.text_en: The Ouchi clan was a feudal lord from the Muromachi to Sengoku periods based in Yamaguchi, and at its peak ruled over six countries, including Buzen, Chikuzen, Suo, Nagato, and Iwami. He competed with the Hosokawa clan to monopolize the Japan-Ming trade (counter trade), and used his vast wealth to accumulate gardens, temples, and art in Yamaguchi, the "Kyoto of the West." The Ouchi clan's expansion into northern Kyushu dates back to the period of the Northern and Southern Courts, when it brought under its control the samurai corps of Buzen and Chikuzen and waged a conflict with the Shoni clan and the Otomo clan. It continued to be an influential figure in the history of northern Kyushu until the ``Daineiji Incident'' of 1551, when the head of the family, Yoshitaka, was overthrown by his vassal, Sue Haruken.

chikugogawa_nancho.name: 大保原古戦場跡碑（筑後川の戦い）
chikugogawa_nancho.kana: おおほうばるこせんじょうあとひちくごがわのたたかい

transit.name: 西鉄天神大牟田線小郡駅

chikugogawa_nancho.highlight: 1359年、懐良親王・菊池武光の南朝軍が北朝軍を撃破した「日本三大合戦」の一つ。小郡市役所隣の公園に建つ古戦場跡碑。
chikugogawa_nancho.text: 大保原の合戦（筑後川の戦い）は正平14年（1359年）8月、懐良親王と菊池武光率いる南朝軍が少弐頼尚の北朝軍を筑後川沿いで撃破した大合戦です。戦力差を覆す菊池軍の奮戦で南朝が勝利し、その後の大宰府占領へとつながりました。日本三大合戦の一つに数えられ、小郡市役所隣の公園に大保原古戦場跡碑が建てられています。
chikugogawa_nancho.name_en: Ohobaru Battlefield Monument (Battle of Chikugo River)
chikugogawa_nancho.highlight_en: In 1359, the Southern Court army of Imperial Prince Kaenaga, Takemitsu Kikuchi defeated the Northern Court army, one of the ``Three Great Battles of Japan.'' A historic battlefield monument stands in the park next to Ogori City Hall.
chikugogawa_nancho.text_en: The Battle of Ohobara (Battle of the Chikugo River) was a great battle that took place in August 1359, in which the Southern Court army led by Imperial Prince Kaneyoshi and Takemitsu Kikuchi defeated the Northern Court army led by Shoni Yorinao along the Chikugo River. The Southern Court won thanks to the brave fighting of Kikuchi's army, which overcame the difference in military strength, leading to the subsequent occupation of Dazaifu. It is counted as one of Japan's three major battles, and a monument to the Ohobaru battlefield has been erected in the park next to Ogori City Hall.

naniwa_palace.name: 難波宮跡

transit.name: 大阪メトロ谷町四丁目駅

naniwa_palace.highlight: 孝徳天皇が645年の大化改新後に定めた最初の「難波長柄豊碕宮」跡。大阪が日本の首都だった時代を伝える国の特別史跡。
naniwa_palace.text: 難波宮は7世紀中頃、大化改新後に孝徳天皇が造営した宮殿跡です。現在の大阪城公園南側に広がるこの地は、日本史上初めて「難波」が都として機能した場所であり、後に聖武天皇も難波宮を造営しています。発掘調査で大極殿・朝堂院の礎石が確認されており、古代国家形成期の政治の中心地であったことが明らかになっています。大阪が「天下の台所」として栄える遥か以前、ここが日本の首都だったという事実は、この地の歴史的深さを物語っています。
naniwa_palace.highlight_en: This is the site of the first Nambagara Hosakigu Shrine established by Emperor Kotoku after the Taika Reform in 645. A special national historic site that tells the story of the time when Osaka was the capital of Japan.
naniwa_palace.text_en: Naniwa Palace is the remains of a palace built by Emperor Kotoku in the mid-7th century after the Taika Reforms. This area, which extends to the south of present-day Osaka Castle Park, is the place where Namba functioned as the capital for the first time in Japanese history, and Emperor Shomu later built Namba Palace. Excavations have confirmed the foundation stones of Daigokuden and Chodoin, making it clear that it was the political center during the formation of the ancient nation. The fact that Osaka was the capital of Japan long before it prospered as the "nation's kitchen" speaks to the historical depth of this area.

shitenoji_osaka.name: 四天王寺

transit.name: 大阪メトロ四天王寺前夕陽ヶ丘駅

shitenoji_osaka.highlight: 聖徳太子が593年に創建した日本最古の官寺。物部守屋との戦いに勝利した際の誓願として建立され、日本仏教の礎を築いた。
shitenoji_osaka.text: 四天王寺は推古天皇元年（593年）、聖徳太子が物部守屋との戦いで勝利した際に四天王に誓った寺院として創建した、日本最古の官寺の一つです。伽藍配置は「四天王寺式」と呼ばれ、南から中門・五重塔・金堂・講堂が一直線に並ぶ独特の様式で、日本の寺院建築の原型となりました。幾度も火災に遭いながらも再建を繰り返し、現在の建物はコンクリート造ですが創建時の様式を忠実に再現しています。太子信仰の聖地として古来多くの参詣者を集め、毎月22日の「太子忌」には今も多くの参拝者が訪れます。
shitenoji_osaka.highlight_en: Japan's oldest government temple, founded in 593 by Prince Shotoku. It was built as a vow after winning the battle with Mononobe Moriya, and laid the foundation of Japanese Buddhism.
shitenoji_osaka.text_en: Shitennoji is one of Japan's oldest official temples, built in 593, the first year of Emperor Suiko's reign, as a temple that Prince Shotoku swore to the Shitennou after his victory in the battle against Mononobe Moriya. The layout of the temple was called the ``Shitennoji style,'' a unique style in which the central gate, five-storied pagoda, main hall, and lecture hall were lined up in a straight line from the south, and became the prototype of Japanese temple architecture. Although it suffered many fires, it was rebuilt repeatedly, and although the current building is made of concrete, it faithfully reproduces the original style. It has attracted many pilgrims since ancient times as a sacred place for the worship of the Prince, and even today, many worshipers visit on the 22nd of every month, the day of the death of the Prince.

osaka_castle.name: 大阪城

transit.name: 大阪メトロ谷町四丁目駅

osaka_castle.highlight: 豊臣秀吉が天下統一の象徴として築いた巨大城郭。大坂冬・夏の陣の舞台となり、徳川の世で再建された現天守は歴史博物館として年間数百万人が訪れる。
osaka_castle.text: 大阪城は天正11年（1583年）、豊臣秀吉が石山本願寺の跡地に天下統一の拠点として築城を開始した巨大城郭です。完成当時は三重の堀と総石垣を備えた日本最大の城で、黄金の茶室を持ち込んだ秀吉の権勢を誇示する建築でした。慶長20年（1615年）の大坂夏の陣で豊臣氏が滅亡すると、徳川幕府が再建。現在の天守は昭和6年に鉄筋コンクリートで再建されたものです。城跡は大阪城公園として整備され、春の桜の名所としても知られています。
osaka_castle.highlight_en: A huge castle built by Toyotomi Hideyoshi as a symbol of unifying the country. It served as the stage for the Osaka Winter and Summer Sieges, and the current castle tower, which was rebuilt during the Tokugawa era, is visited by millions of people a year as a historical museum.
osaka_castle.text_en: Osaka Castle is a huge castle built by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1583 on the site of Ishiyama Honganji Temple as a base for unifying the country. At the time of its completion, it was the largest castle in Japan, with a triple moat and a full stone wall, and was a building that flaunted the power of Hideyoshi, who brought in a golden tea room. After the Toyotomi clan was destroyed in the Summer Siege of Osaka in 1615, the Tokugawa shogunate was rebuilt. The current castle tower was rebuilt with reinforced concrete in 1930. The castle ruins have been maintained as Osaka Castle Park, and are also known as a famous spot for cherry blossom viewing in spring.

mozu_kofun.name: 百舌鳥古墳群（仁徳天皇陵）
mozu_kofun.highlight: 世界最大級の墳墓・仁徳天皇陵古墳を中心とする世界遺産。全長486mの前方後円墳はエジプトのピラミッドと並ぶ世界三大墳墓の一つ。
mozu_kofun.text: 百舌鳥古墳群は大阪府堺市に集中する古墳時代（4〜5世紀）の巨大古墳群で、2019年にユネスコ世界文化遺産に登録されました。中心をなす仁徳天皇陵古墳（大仙陵古墳）は全長486mと世界最大級の前方後円墳で、クフ王のピラミッドや始皇帝陵と並ぶ世界三大墳墓の一つとされています。古墳時代の日本が高度な土木技術と強大な王権を持っていたことを示す遺産であり、周囲の濠に映る古墳の姿は悠久の歴史を静かに伝えています。現在も宮内庁が管理する陵墓のため内部への立ち入りはできません。
mozu_kofun.highlight_en: A world heritage site centered around the Nintoku Emperor Mausoleum, one of the world's largest burial mounds. This keyhole-shaped tomb with a total length of 486 meters is one of the three largest tombs in the world, along with the Egyptian pyramids.
mozu_kofun.text_en: The Mozu Tumulus Group is a group of huge burial mounds from the Kofun period (4th to 5th century) concentrated in Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture, and was registered as a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site in 2019. The Nintoku Emperor's Mausoleum (Daisenryo Tumulus), which forms the center of the site, is one of the world's largest keyhole-shaped tombs with a total length of 486 meters, and is considered one of the three largest tombs in the world, along with the Pyramid of King Khufu and the Mausoleum of the First Emperor. It is a heritage site that shows that Japan had advanced civil engineering technology and powerful royal authority during the Kofun period, and the appearance of the kofun, reflected in the surrounding moat, quietly conveys its eternal history. Even now, it is not possible to enter the mausoleum as it is still managed by the Imperial Household Agency.

sumiyoshi_taisha.name: 住吉大社
sumiyoshi_taisha.highlight: 全国2300社の住吉神社の総本社。神功皇后の三韓征伐を守護した海の神を祀り、「住吉造」と呼ばれる独自の建築様式は日本最古の神社建築形式の一つ。
sumiyoshi_taisha.text: 住吉大社は全国に約2300社ある住吉神社の総本社で、航海・和歌の神として古代から崇められてきました。主祭神は底筒男命・中筒男命・表筒男命の住吉三神と神功皇后で、三韓征伐の際に海神として神功皇后を守護したとされています。本殿4棟は「住吉造」という古代の建築様式を現代に伝え、国宝に指定されています。平安時代には歌人・紀貫之らが参詣し、万葉集にも数多く詠まれた由緒ある古社です。初詣参拝者数は全国トップクラスで、毎年200万人以上が訪れます。
sumiyoshi_taisha.highlight_en: Headquarters of 2,300 Sumiyoshi Shrines nationwide. It enshrines the god of the sea who protected Empress Jingu during her conquest of the Three Koreas, and its unique architectural style called ``Sumiyoshi-zukuri'' is one of the oldest shrine architectural styles in Japan.
sumiyoshi_taisha.text_en: Sumiyoshi Taisha is the headquarters of approximately 2,300 Sumiyoshi shrines nationwide, and has been worshiped since ancient times as the god of navigation and Japanese poetry. The main deities enshrined here are the three Sumiyoshi deities: Sokozutsuo-no-Mikoto, Nakazutsuo-no-Mikoto, and Omotzutsuo-no-Mikoto, and Empress Jingu, who is said to have protected Empress Jingu as a sea god during the Sankan Conquest. The four buildings of the main hall have inherited the ancient architectural style of ``Sumiyoshi-zukuri'' into the present day, and have been designated as national treasures. It is an old shrine with a long history, where poet Ki Tsurayuki and others visited during the Heian period, and many poems are included in the Manyoshu. The number of New Year's pilgrims is among the highest in Japan, with over 2 million people visiting each year.

ishiyama_honganji.name: 石山本願寺跡（信長10年戦争の地）
ishiyama_honganji.kana: いしやまほんがんじあと
ishiyama_honganji.text: 石山本願寺は浄土真宗本願寺派の本山で、現在の大阪城の地に1496年に蓮如が築いた寺院兼要塞都市。1570-1580年の「石山合戦」では織田信長と10年間にわたる宗教戦争を繰り広げ、ついに顕如が信長と和睦し退去した。跡地には豊臣秀吉が大阪城を築き、本願寺は京都堀川に移転（西本願寺）した。
ishiyama_honganji.highlight: 信長と10年戦った浄土真宗の要塞都市。後に大阪城が築かれた地
ishiyama_honganji.name_en: Ishiyama Honganji Temple Ruins (Spot of Nobunaga's 10 Years' War)
ishiyama_honganji.highlight_en: A fortress city of the Jodo Shinshu sect that fought against Nobunaga for 10 years. The place where Osaka Castle was later built
ishiyama_honganji.text_en: Ishiyama Honganji is the head temple of the Jodo Shinshu Honganji sect, and is a temple and fortress city built by Rennyo in 1496 on the site of present-day Osaka Castle. In the ``Ishiyama Battle'' of 1570-1580, he fought a ten-year religious war with Nobunaga Oda, and finally Kennyo made peace with Nobunaga and left. Toyotomi Hideyoshi built Osaka Castle on the site, and Honganji Temple was moved to Horikawa, Kyoto (Nishi Honganji Temple).

domyoji_tenmangu.name: 道明寺天満宮
domyoji_tenmangu.kana: どうみょうじてんまんぐう
domyoji_tenmangu.highlight: 菅原道真が太宰府へ配流される際に立ち寄り、別れを惜しんだ縁の地。道真が愛した梅の名所として知られ、古くから「河内の天神さん」として親しまれる。
domyoji_tenmangu.text: 道明寺天満宮は菅原道真の叔母・覚寿尼が住んでいた寺院に隣接する神社で、延喜元年（901年）に道真が大宰府へ左遷される際にここへ立ち寄り、叔母との別れを惜しんだと伝えられています。道真は境内の梅を愛で「鴬よ 梅の林の 花咲かば 思い出でずや 謡わずや」と詠んだとされます。道明寺という地名は、道真が当地の菅原氏の氏寺に立ち寄ったことに由来するとも伝わります。春には梅が咲き誇り、道真の悲しみの旅を偲ぶ多くの参拝者が訪れます。隣接する道明寺には国宝の十一面観音像が安置されています。
domyoji_tenmangu.highlight_en: This is the place where Michizane Sugawara stopped by when he was exiled to Dazaifu and regretted saying goodbye. It is known as a famous spot for plum blossoms, which was loved by Michizane, and has been affectionately known as ``Tenjin-san of Kawachi'' since ancient times.
domyoji_tenmangu.text_en: Domyoji Tenmangu Shrine is a shrine adjacent to the temple where Michizane Sugawara's aunt, Kakujuni, lived.It is said that Michizane stopped here when he was demoted to Dazaifu in 901, regretting parting ways with his aunt. It is said that Michizane was so in love with the plum blossoms in the temple grounds that he composed a poem, ``O Umugi, the blooming flower of the plum grove, without memories, without singing.'' It is said that the name Domyoji comes from Michizane's visit to the Sugawara clan's temple here. In spring, the plum trees are in full bloom and many worshipers come to remember Michizane's sad journey. The adjacent Domyoji Temple houses the eleven-faced Kannon statue, a national treasure.

chausuyama_osaka.name: 茶臼山古戦場（天王寺）
chausuyama_osaka.kana: ちゃうすやまこせんじょう
chausuyama_osaka.highlight: 大坂夏の陣（1615年）最大の激戦地。真田信繁（幸村）が徳川家康の本陣に突撃し、家康をあと一歩まで追い詰めた「日本一の兵」最後の戦場。
chausuyama_osaka.text: 茶臼山は天王寺公園内に位置する小丘で、大坂冬の陣では真田信繁（幸村）が、夏の陣では徳川家康と豊臣方の双方が陣地として使用した激戦の地です。慶長20年（1615年）5月の大坂夏の陣では、真田信繁がわずかな手勢を率いて徳川家康の本陣に突撃し、家康が二度も自害を覚悟したと伝えられています。「日本一の兵（つわもの）」と称えられた信繁はここで壮絶な最期を遂げ、豊臣氏もこの戦いで滅亡しました。現在は天王寺公園の一角に史跡として保存されています。
chausuyama_osaka.highlight_en: The site of the fiercest battle during the Osaka Summer Campaign (1615). The final battlefield of Japan's No. 1 soldier, where Nobushige Sanada (Yukimura) charges at Tokugawa Ieyasu's main camp and corners Ieyasu to one step.
chausuyama_osaka.text_en: Chausuyama is a small hill located in Tennoji Park, and was the site of a fierce battle that was used as a base by Nobushige Sanada (Yukimura) during the Osaka Winter Siege and by both Tokugawa Ieyasu and Toyotomi during the Summer Siege. During the summer campaign in Osaka in May 1615, Sanada Nobushige led a small force to attack Tokugawa Ieyasu's main camp, and it is said that Ieyasu twice prepared for suicide. Nobushige, who was hailed as ``Japan's best soldier,'' met a tragic end here, and the Toyotomi clan was also destroyed in this battle. It is currently preserved as a historic site in a corner of Tennoji Park.

takatsuki_castle.name: 高槻城跡
takatsuki_castle.highlight: キリシタン大名・高山右近の居城。信仰ゆえに領地を捨てた「不屈の信仰者」右近の生涯と、摂津を治めた城の歴史を伝える近畿の重要史跡。
takatsuki_castle.text: 高槻城はキリシタン大名として知られる高山右近が城主を務めた城です。右近は領民にもキリスト教への改宗を勧め、高槻は「キリシタン王国」と呼ばれるほどでした。天正15年（1587年）、豊臣秀吉のバテレン追放令により棄教か追放かを迫られると、右近は富裕な領地を捨てて信仰を選びました。その後も各地を転々とし、最終的に家康のキリシタン禁教令でマニラに追放、1615年に現地で没しました。2017年に列福（カトリックの福者認定）され、「殉教者」として今も多くの信者に崇敬されています。
takatsuki_castle.highlight_en: The residence of the Christian daimyo Takayama Ukon. An important historical site in the Kinki region that tells the life of Ukon, an ``indomitable believer'' who abandoned his territory because of his faith, and the history of the castle that ruled Settsu.
takatsuki_castle.text_en: Takatsuki Castle is a castle where Takayama Ukon, known as a Christian daimyo, served as the castle's lord. Ukon encouraged the people of his territory to convert to Christianity, and Takatsuki was even called the ``Christian Kingdom.'' In 1587, when Toyotomi Hideyoshi ordered him to banish the Batteren, he was forced to either renounce Christianity or be exiled, so he abandoned his wealthy territory and chose the faith. After that, he moved from place to place, and was finally exiled to Manila under Ieyasu's edict banning Christianity, where he died in 1615. He was beatified (Catholic beatification) in 2017 and is still revered by many believers as a "martyr."

ikutama_shrine.name: 生國魂神社

transit.name: 大阪メトロ谷町九丁目駅

ikutama_shrine.highlight: 神武天皇が大阪上陸の際に創建したと伝わる大阪最古の神社。難波・石山本願寺の変遷を見守り、上方文化の中心地として落語や文楽とも深く関わる。
ikutama_shrine.text: 生國魂神社は神武天皇東征の際に創建されたと伝わる大阪最古の神社で、大阪の守護神として「いくたまさん」の愛称で親しまれています。もともと石山本願寺の地（現在の大阪城）にありましたが、豊臣秀吉の大坂城築城に際して現在地に移されました。江戸時代には境内に芸能の場が開かれ、上方落語の祖・米沢彦八がここで辻噺を行ったことから、今も落語家の石碑が立っています。また境内の浄瑠璃神社は文楽の祖・植村文楽軒を祀っており、大阪の芸能文化の発祥地としての性格も持つ神社です。
ikutama_shrine.highlight_en: The oldest shrine in Osaka, said to have been built by Emperor Jimmu when he landed in Osaka. He has watched over the evolution of Ishiyama Honganji Temple in Namba, and is deeply involved in Rakugo and Bunraku as the center of Kamigata culture.
ikutama_shrine.text_en: Ikkunitama Shrine is the oldest shrine in Osaka, said to have been built during Emperor Jimmu's eastern expedition, and is affectionately known as ``Ikutama-san'' as the guardian deity of Osaka. It was originally located at the site of Ishiyama Honganji Temple (currently Osaka Castle), but was moved to its current location when Toyotomi Hideyoshi built Osaka Castle. During the Edo period, a place for performing arts was opened within the precincts, and Hikohachi Yonezawa, the founder of Kamigata Rakugo, performed his Tsujibanashi here, and a stone monument to his Rakugo story still stands today. Joruri Shrine on the grounds is also dedicated to Uemura Bunrakuken, the founder of Bunraku, and is a shrine that also has the character of being the birthplace of Osaka's performing arts culture.

heian_palace_ruins.name: 平安宮大極殿跡
heian_palace_ruins.kana: へいあんきゅうだいごくでんあと
heian_palace_ruins.highlight: 794年から400年以上、日本の首都だった平安京の中枢。天皇が政務を執った大極殿の跡地は今も発掘が続き、古代都市の壮大なスケールを今に伝える。
heian_palace_ruins.text: 平安宮は延暦13年（794年）に桓武天皇が奈良から遷都して以来、鎌倉時代まで約400年間、日本の政治・文化の中心として機能した王城の地です。大極殿は天皇が正式な儀式を行う最重要の建物で、現在の千本丸太町交差点付近に位置していました。平安京は唐の長安をモデルに設計され、碁盤の目状の街路は現在の京都市街の基礎となっています。現在は「大極殿公園」として整備され、礎石などが保存されています。千年の都の出発点を感じることができる静かな史跡です。
heian_palace_ruins.highlight_en: The center of Heiankyo, which was the capital of Japan for over 400 years from 794. Excavation continues at the site of Daigokuden, where the Emperor conducted his political affairs, and the grand scale of the ancient city is still visible today.
heian_palace_ruins.text_en: Heian Shrine is a royal castle that functioned as the center of Japanese politics and culture for about 400 years, from the time Emperor Kanmu moved the capital from Nara in 794 until the Kamakura period. Daigokuden was the most important building where the emperor held formal ceremonies, and was located near the current Senbonmarutamachi intersection. Heian-kyo was designed after Chang'an in the Tang Dynasty, and its grid-shaped streets are the basis of today's Kyoto city. Currently, it is maintained as Daigokuden Park, and the foundation stones are preserved. It is a quiet historical site where you can feel the starting point of the Millennium City.

kinkakuji.name: 金閣寺（鹿苑寺）
kinkakuji.highlight: 足利義満が建立した北山文化の象徴。三層の楼閣を金箔で覆った絢爛な姿は室町幕府の栄華を体現し、世界遺産・世界中から年間500万人が訪れる京都の顔。
kinkakuji.text: 金閣寺（正式名：鹿苑寺）は室町幕府3代将軍・足利義満が応永4年（1397年）に建立した山荘・北山殿を起源とします。義満の死後に禅寺となりました。舎利殿（金閣）は三層構造で、第二・三層が金箔で覆われており、鏡湖池に映る姿は「北山文化」の豪華絢爛な美意識を象徴しています。昭和25年（1950年）に放火により焼失しましたが、昭和30年に再建。三島由紀夫の小説『金閣寺』のモデルにもなりました。1994年にユネスコ世界文化遺産に登録され、現在も年間数百万人が訪れる京都を代表する観光地です。
kinkakuji.highlight_en: A symbol of Kitayama culture built by Yoshimitsu Ashikaga. The gorgeous three-story tower covered in gold leaf embodies the glory of the Muromachi Shogunate, and is the face of Kyoto, a world heritage site and visited by 5 million people a year from all over the world.
kinkakuji.text_en: Kinkaku-ji (official name: Rokuon-ji) has its origins in Kitayama-dono, a mountain villa built in 1397 by Yoshimitsu Ashikaga, the third shogun of the Muromachi shogunate. After Yoshimitsu's death, it became a Zen temple. The Shariden (Kinkaku) has a three-tiered structure, with the second and third floors covered in gold leaf, and its reflection in the mirror lake symbolizes the gorgeous aesthetic sense of Kitayama culture. It was destroyed by arson in 1950, but was rebuilt in 1955. It was also the model for Yukio Mishima's novel ``Kinkakuji.'' Registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1994, it is still one of Kyoto's leading tourist destinations, visited by millions of people every year.

ginkakuji.name: 銀閣寺（慈照寺）
ginkakuji.highlight: 足利義政が創建した東山文化の粋。金閣に対して銀箔は張られなかったが、侘びた美意識と枯山水庭園は後の日本文化に決定的な影響を与えた。
ginkakuji.text: 銀閣寺（正式名：慈照寺）は室町幕府8代将軍・足利義政が文明14年（1482年）から造営した山荘・東山殿を起源とします。応仁の乱で荒廃した京都の中で、義政は政治から離れ、東山の山麓に美の世界を追求しました。銀閣（観音殿）は金閣と対照的に素木のままですが、その侘びた美しさが「東山文化」の精神を体現しています。枯山水の庭園「銀沙灘」と「向月台」は独特の砂の造形で有名です。能・茶道・華道・水墨画など、現代日本文化の多くがここで洗練された東山文化から発展しています。
ginkakuji.highlight_en: The essence of Higashiyama culture founded by Yoshimasa Ashikaga. Although no silver leaf was applied to Kinkaku, its rustic aesthetic sense and dry landscape garden had a decisive influence on later Japanese culture.
ginkakuji.text_en: Ginkaku-ji Temple (official name: Jisho-ji Temple) has its origins in Higashiyama-dono, a mountain villa built in 1482 by Yoshimasa Ashikaga, the 8th shogun of the Muromachi Shogunate. In Kyoto, which was devastated by the Onin War, Yoshimasa left politics and pursued the world of beauty at the foot of Higashiyama. In contrast to the Golden Pavilion, the Ginkaku (Kannonden) is made of raw wood, but its rustic beauty embodies the spirit of Higashiyama Culture. The Karesansui gardens ``Ginsha-nada'' and ``Kogetsudai'' are famous for their unique sand formations.
