Much of modern Japanese culture, such as Noh, tea ceremony, flower arranging, and ink painting, developed here from the sophisticated Higashiyama culture.

fushimi_inari.name: 伏見稲荷大社
fushimi_inari.kana: ふしみいなりたいしゃ
fushimi_inari.highlight: 全国3万社の稲荷神社の総本社。和銅4年（711年）創建の古社で、朱色の千本鳥居が連なる参道は外国人旅行者から最も人気の日本の観光地に選ばれ続ける。
fushimi_inari.text: 伏見稲荷大社は和銅4年（711年）に創建されたと伝わる、全国3万社以上の稲荷神社の総本社です。稲荷山全体が神域とされ、山上までの参道に奉納された無数の朱色の鳥居が「千本鳥居」として世界的に有名です。もともとは農業・食物の神でしたが、中世以降は商売繁盛・諸業繁栄の神として広く信仰され、江戸時代には庶民の参詣地として賑わいました。近年は外国人観光客から「最も行きたい日本の観光地」として毎年上位に選ばれており、年間数百万人が訪れます。
fushimi_inari.highlight_en: Headquarters of 30,000 Inari shrines nationwide. This ancient shrine was founded in 711, and its approach, lined with a thousand vermilion torii gates, continues to be chosen as one of Japan's most popular tourist destinations by foreign travelers.
fushimi_inari.text_en: Fushimi Inari Taisha is said to have been founded in 711 and is the headquarters of over 30,000 Inari shrines nationwide. The whole of Mt. Inari is considered a sacred area, and the countless vermilion torii gates dedicated to the approach to the top of the mountain are world-famous as the ``Senbon Torii''. Originally the god of agriculture and food, since the Middle Ages it has been widely worshiped as a god of prosperous business and various industries, and during the Edo period it became a popular place of worship for the common people. In recent years, it has been chosen as one of the top tourist destinations in Japan by foreign tourists every year, and millions of people visit each year.

toji_kyoto.name: 東寺（教王護国寺）
toji_kyoto.highlight: 平安遷都とともに創建された官寺。空海（弘法大師）が嵯峨天皇から賜り真言密教の根本道場とした。高さ55mの五重塔は木造建築として日本最高を誇る。
toji_kyoto.text: 東寺は延暦15年（796年）、平安遷都とともに王城鎮護のために創建された官寺です。弘仁14年（823年）に嵯峨天皇から空海（弘法大師）に下賜され、以来真言密教の根本道場として栄えました。高さ約55mの五重塔は江戸時代に再建されたもので、木造塔として日本一の高さを誇り、京都の象徴的な景観を形成しています。講堂内には密教の世界観を立体的に表現した21体の仏像群「立体曼荼羅」が安置されており、国宝・重要文化財の宝庫です。毎月21日の「弘法市」は弘法大師の命日に由来する縁日で、多くの露店が並びます。
toji_kyoto.highlight_en: A government temple built with the transfer of the capital to the Heian period. Kukai (Kobo Daishi) received it from Emperor Saga and made it the fundamental dojo of Shingon Esoteric Buddhism. The five-storied pagoda with a height of 55 meters is the tallest wooden structure in Japan.
toji_kyoto.text_en: To-ji Temple is a government temple that was built in 796, along with the transfer of the capital to the Heian period, to protect the royal castle. It was granted to Kukai (Kobo Daishi) by Emperor Saga in 823, and since then it has flourished as the fundamental dojo of Shingon Esoteric Buddhism. The five-storied pagoda, approximately 55 meters high, was rebuilt during the Edo period and is the tallest wooden pagoda in Japan, forming a symbolic landscape of Kyoto. Inside the auditorium is a ``3D mandala'', a group of 21 Buddhist statues that three-dimensionally express the worldview of Esoteric Buddhism, and is a treasure trove of national treasures and important cultural properties. Kobo Market, held on the 21st of every month, is a festival that commemorates the anniversary of Kobo Daishi's death, and is lined with many stalls.

nijo_castle.name: 二条城
nijo_castle.highlight: 徳川家康が築き、15代慶喜が大政奉還を宣言した場所。開府から幕末まで江戸時代の始まりと終わりを見届けた、徳川幕府267年の歴史を刻む世界遺産。
nijo_castle.text: 二条城は慶長8年（1603年）、将軍・徳川家康が天皇への参内や西国大名との会見のために築いた平城です。家康・秀忠・家光の三代にわたって整備され、絢爛な二の丸御殿（国宝）は「鶯張りの廊下」で知られ、障壁画の多くが狩野派の手によるものです。元治元年（1863年）には将軍・家茂が滞在し、慶応3年（1867年）には15代将軍・慶喜が大政奉還を宣言した歴史的な場所でもあります。江戸時代の始まりを告げた城が、江戸時代の終わりも見届けるという歴史の皮肉を体感できる、世界遺産の名城です。
nijo_castle.highlight_en: It was built by Tokugawa Ieyasu and the place where the 15th generation, Yoshinobu, declared the restoration of imperial rule. A world heritage site that marks the 267-year history of the Tokugawa Shogunate, which witnessed the beginning and end of the Edo period from the opening of the Edo period to the end of the Edo period.
nijo_castle.text_en: Nijo Castle is a flat castle built in 1603 by the shogun Tokugawa Ieyasu to visit the Emperor and have meetings with feudal lords from the western regions. The gorgeous Ninomaru Palace (National Treasure), which was maintained over three generations: Ieyasu, Hidetada, and Iemitsu, is known for its ``nightingale-covered corridor,'' and many of the wall paintings are by the Kano school. It is also a historical place where Shogun Iemochi stayed in the first year of Genji (1863), and where the 15th Shogun Yoshinobu declared the restoration of imperial rule in 1867. It is a world heritage site where you can experience the irony of history: the castle that heralded the beginning of the Edo period also witnessed the end of the Edo period.

byodoin.name: 平等院鳳凰堂
byodoin.kana: びょうどういんほうおうどう
byodoin.highlight: 10円硬貨のデザインで有名な平安貴族文化の最高傑作。藤原頼通が極楽浄土を地上に再現した建築で、創建から約1000年間ほぼ当初の姿を保つ国宝建築。
byodoin.text: 平等院鳳凰堂は永承7年（1052年）、関白・藤原頼通が父・道長の別荘を寺院に改め、翌年に建立した阿弥陀堂です。中央の中堂と左右の翼廊・尾廊が鳳凰が羽を広げたような形をしていることから「鳳凰堂」と呼ばれます。阿弥陀如来坐像（国宝）を祀り、極楽浄土の宮殿を地上に再現したとされる建物は、平安貴族文化「国風文化」の最高峰として評価されています。10円硬貨と1万円紙幣（鳳凰）のデザインに採用されており、日本人に最もなじみ深い文化財の一つです。1994年に世界文化遺産に登録されました。
byodoin.highlight_en: A masterpiece of Heian aristocratic culture, famous for its design on the 10 yen coin. Fujiwara Yorimichi's architecture recreated the Pure Land of Paradise on earth, and is a national treasure that has maintained almost its original appearance for about 1,000 years since its construction.
byodoin.text_en: Byodo-in Phoenix Hall is an Amida-do hall built in 1052 by Kanpaku Fujiwara Yorimichi, who converted his father Michinaga's villa into a temple, and built it the following year. It is called ``Phoenix Hall'' because the central hall and the transepts and transepts on the left and right sides are shaped like a phoenix spreading its wings. The building, which enshrines the seated statue of Amida Nyorai (a national treasure) and is said to be a reproduction of a paradise paradise palace on earth, is regarded as the pinnacle of Heian aristocratic culture, ``Kokufu culture''. It is used in the design of the 10 yen coin and the 10,000 yen banknote (Phoenix), and is one of the cultural assets most familiar to Japanese people. It was registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site in 1994.

daigoji.name: 醍醐寺
daigoji.highlight: 豊臣秀吉最後の宴「醍醐の花見」の舞台。真言宗の大寺院で国宝・重要文化財が1000点超。五重塔は京都府下最古の木造建築。
daigoji.text: 醍醐寺は貞観16年（874年）に聖宝理源大師が創建した真言宗の大寺院で、国宝・重要文化財の数は約1000点以上に上る文化財の宝庫です。五重塔は天暦5年（951年）建立で京都府下最古の木造建築として知られます。慶長3年（1598年）には豊臣秀吉が醍醐寺で大規模な花見の宴「醍醐の花見」を催し、千人を超える女房衆を集めた豪奢な宴は秀吉最晩年の大イベントでした。広大な寺域は下醍醐・上醍醐に分かれ、春の桜、秋の紅葉も美しく、1994年に世界文化遺産に登録されています。
daigoji.highlight_en: The setting for Toyotomi Hideyoshi's last banquet, ``Daigo no Hanami.'' A large temple of the Shingon sect with over 1,000 national treasures and important cultural properties. The five-storied pagoda is the oldest wooden structure in Kyoto Prefecture.
daigoji.text_en: Daigoji Temple is a large temple of the Shingon sect founded by Shoho Rigen Daishi in the 16th year of the Jogan era (874), and is a treasure trove of cultural properties with over 1,000 national treasures and important cultural properties. The five-storied pagoda was built in 951 and is known as the oldest wooden structure in Kyoto Prefecture. In 1598, Toyotomi Hideyoshi held a large-scale cherry blossom viewing party, ``Daigo no Hanami,'' at Daigoji Temple.The lavish banquet, which attracted over 1,000 wives, was a major event in Hideyoshi's final years. The vast temple grounds are divided into Shimo-Daigo and Kamidaigo, and the cherry blossoms in spring and the autumn leaves are beautiful, and it was registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site in 1994.

kurama_dera.name: 鞍馬寺
kurama_dera.highlight: 源義経（牛若丸）が幼少期に修行した山岳霊場。鞍馬天狗との修行伝説が息づく深山の寺で、平安末期の武将の英雄伝説と山岳信仰が交差する神秘の地。
kurama_dera.text: 鞍馬寺は宝亀元年（770年）に創建されたと伝わる山岳寺院で、都の北を守護する霊場として平安時代から崇められてきました。源義経（幼名・牛若丸）が11歳からこの地で修行したとされ、境内には義経ゆかりの「背比べ石」や「義経堂」が残っています。鞍馬天狗から兵法を学んだという伝説は後世の創作ですが、義経がこの地で剣術・学問を習得したことは確かなようです。山中には豊かな自然が広がり、「鞍馬山のパワースポット」として現代でも多くの参拝者を集めています。
kurama_dera.highlight_en: A sacred mountain site where Minamoto no Yoshitsune (Ushiwakamaru) trained as a child. A temple in the deep mountains where the legend of training with the Kurama Tengu lives on, and a mysterious place where the heroic legends of military commanders from the late Heian period intersect with mountain worship.
kurama_dera.text_en: Kurama-dera Temple is a mountain temple that is said to have been built in the first year of Houki (770), and has been revered since the Heian period as a sacred place that protects the north of the capital. It is said that Minamoto no Yoshitsune (childhood name: Ushiwakamaru) trained here from the age of 11, and within the precincts there are remains of the ``separate stone'' and ``Gikeido'' that are associated with Yoshitsune. The legend that Yoshitsune learned military techniques from Kurama Tengu is a creation of later generations, but it seems certain that Yoshitsune learned swordsmanship and scholarship here. Rich nature spreads out in the mountains, and even today it attracts many worshipers as the "power spot of Mt. Kurama."

hozugawa_kyoto.name: 保津川（亀岡）の歴史
hozugawa_kyoto.kana: ほづがわ・かめおかのれきし

transit.name: JR亀岡駅
transit.walk: 徒歩15分（保津川下り乗船場）

hozugawa_kyoto.highlight: 角倉了以が1606年に私財を投じて開削した水運の大動脈。江戸時代の京都・大阪の物流を支えた保津川と、丹波の中心・亀岡城下の歴史が交差する地。
hozugawa_kyoto.text: 保津川は丹波高地から嵐山へと流れる険しい渓谷で、慶長11年（1606年）に京都の豪商・角倉了以が幕府の許可を得て開削した水路です。了以はわずか数ヶ月で巨岩を砕き、丹波の物資を京都へ運ぶ水運ルートを開きました。これにより丹波の米・木材・炭などが保津川を下って京都・大坂へ供給され、近畿の物流を大きく変えました。亀岡は明智光秀が築いた亀山城の城下町で、本能寺の変出陣の地でもあります。現在も保津川下りとして観光客に親しまれている渓谷美は、江戸時代から変わらぬ自然の姿です。
hozugawa_kyoto.highlight_en: This is a major water transportation artery that Ryoi Kadokura constructed in 1606 with his own money. A place where the history of the Hozugawa River, which supported the logistics of Kyoto and Osaka during the Edo period, intersects with the history of Kameoka Castle, the center of Tanba.
hozugawa_kyoto.text_en: The Hozugawa River is a steep valley that flows from the Tanba Highlands to Arashiyama, and is a waterway that was excavated in 1606 by Ryoi Kadokura, a wealthy Kyoto merchant, with permission from the Shogunate. In just a few months, Ryoi crushed the huge rock and opened a water transport route to transport goods from Tamba to Kyoto. As a result, rice, wood, charcoal, etc. from Tamba were supplied to Kyoto and Osaka down the Hozugawa River, greatly changing logistics in the Kinki region. Kameoka is the castle town of Kameyama Castle, built by Akechi Mitsuhide, and is also the site of Honnoji Temple's outpost. The beauty of the valley, which is still popular among tourists today as a boat ride down the Hozugawa River, has a natural appearance that has not changed since the Edo period.

himeji_castle.name: 姫路城
himeji_castle.highlight: 「白鷺城」の愛称で親しまれる日本最大の木造城郭。世界遺産・国宝のダブル指定を受け、400年前の姿をほぼ完全に保つ奇跡の名城。
himeji_castle.text: 姫路城は慶長14年（1609年）に池田輝政が現在の天守を完成させた姫路藩の居城です。白漆喰で覆われた純白の外観から「白鷺城」と呼ばれ、大小83棟の建物が複雑に連なる巨大城郭は、攻め手を惑わす迷路のような縄張りで難攻不落を誇りました。江戸時代を通じて実戦にさらされず、明治の廃城令でも取り壊しを免れ、第二次世界大戦の空襲でも奇跡的に焼失しなかったため、築城当時の姿をほぼ完全に残しています。1993年に日本初の世界文化遺産の一つとして登録され、年間100万人以上が訪れる日本を代表する名城です。
himeji_castle.highlight_en: Japan's largest wooden castle, affectionately known as "White Heron Castle." This miraculous castle has been designated both as a World Heritage Site and a National Treasure, and has remained almost exactly as it was 400 years ago.
himeji_castle.text_en: Himeji Castle is the residence of the Himeji domain, where Terumasa Ikeda completed the current castle tower in 1609. It was nicknamed ``White Heron Castle'' because of its pure white exterior covered with white plaster, and was impregnable with its maze-like territory that confused attackers. It was not exposed to actual combat during the Edo period, was not demolished under the Meiji Castle Abandonment Ordinance, and miraculously did not burn down during the air raids of World War II, so it remains almost exactly as it was when it was built. Registered as one of Japan's first World Cultural Heritage Sites in 1993, it is a famous castle that represents Japan and is visited by more than 1 million people a year.

arima_onsen_history.name: 有馬温泉の歴史
arima_onsen_history.kana: ありまおんせんのれきし
arima_onsen_history.highlight: 日本書紀にも記される日本最古の温泉地の一つ。豊臣秀吉が最も愛した湯として知られ、太閤が9度も訪れた歴史と、金泉・銀泉の二種の名湯が今も湧き出る。
arima_onsen_history.text: 有馬温泉は大己貴命・少彦名命が発見したと伝わる日本三古湯の一つで、日本書紀にも舒明天皇・孝徳天皇が行幸したと記録されています。特に豊臣秀吉が有馬を愛したことで有名で、9度にわたって来湯し、北政所（ねね）と過ごした湯治の記録が残っています。金色に濁る「金泉」（塩化物泉）と無色透明の「銀泉」（炭酸泉・ラジウム泉）の二種類の源泉が特徴で、それぞれ異なる泉質を持ちます。江戸時代には「天下の三名泉」に数えられ、現代も年間200万人以上が訪れる関西屈指の温泉地です。
arima_onsen_history.highlight_en: One of Japan's oldest hot spring resorts, recorded in the Nihon Shoki. It is known as the most loved hot spring by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, and has a history of being visited by Taiko nine times, and two types of famous hot springs, Kinsen and Ginsen, still gush out to this day.
arima_onsen_history.text_en: Arima Onsen is one of the three oldest hot springs in Japan, and is said to have been discovered by Ōmi Takamikoto and Sukhikona-no-Mikoto, and it is also recorded in the Nihon Shoki that Emperor Jomei and Emperor Kotoku visited there. In particular, Toyotomi Hideyoshi is famous for his love for Arima, and there are records of him visiting the hot springs nine times and spending time with Nene Kitamandokoro. It is characterized by two types of hot springs, the golden-colored ``Kinsen'' (chloride spring) and the colorless and transparent ``Ginsen'' (carbonated spring/radium spring), each with different spring quality. During the Edo period, it was counted as one of the top three hot springs in the world, and even today it is one of the best hot springs in the Kansai region, visited by more than 2 million people a year.

akashi_castle.name: 明石城跡
akashi_castle.highlight: 元和5年（1619年）、徳川家康の孫・小笠原忠真が築いた西国支配の要衝。子午線が通る「時の街・明石」の歴史と、幕府の西国警備戦略が交差する城跡。
akashi_castle.text: 明石城は元和5年（1619年）、徳川家康の命を受けた小笠原忠真が築いた平山城です。西国大名への備えとして戦略的に配置され、東西に延びる丘陵上に本丸・二の丸・三の丸が配置されました。天守は建てられなかった代わりに四隅に二重・三重の隅櫓が設けられ、そのうち坤櫓と巽櫓が現存しています。明石は東経135度の子午線が通る「時の標準地」として知られ、明治以降は日本標準時の基準となりました。城跡は現在「明石公園」として整備され、桜の名所としても市民に親しまれています。
akashi_castle.highlight_en: In 1619, this was a strategic point for the control of the western region, built by Tokugawa Ieyasu's grandson, Ogasawara Tadazane. The castle ruins are where the history of Akashi, the City of Time, through which the meridian passes, intersects with the Shogunate's Saigoku security strategy.
akashi_castle.text_en: Akashi Castle is a Hirayama castle built in 1619 by Ogasawara Tadamasa under the orders of Tokugawa Ieyasu. It was strategically placed in preparation for the feudal lords of the Western region, and the Honmaru, Ninomaru, and Sannomaru were placed on top of a hill extending from east to west. A castle tower was not built, but double and triple corner turrets were built at the four corners, of which Kon-yagura and Tatsumi-yagura still exist. Akashi is known as the "standard place of time" as the meridian of 135 degrees east longitude passes through it, and from the Meiji era onwards, it became the standard for Japan Standard Time. The castle ruins are now maintained as Akashi Park, and are popular among citizens as a famous spot for cherry blossom viewing.

takeda_castle.name: 竹田城跡
takeda_castle.highlight: 「天空の城」「日本のマチュピチュ」と呼ばれる山城跡。秋の朝に雲海の上に浮かぶ石垣の光景は幻想的で、近年SNSで世界的に注目される。
takeda_castle.text: 竹田城は室町時代中期に山名宗全が築いたとされる山城で、標高353mの虎臥山の山頂に広がる石垣群が特徴です。戦国末期に羽柴秀長の攻撃を受けて落城し、関ヶ原の戦い後に廃城となりました。秋の朝に円山川の川霧が雲海となり、その上に石垣が浮かび上がる幻想的な光景が「天空の城」として話題となり、近年は年間40万人以上が訪れる兵庫の人気観光地になっています。山全体に整然と積まれた野面積みの石垣は保存状態が良く、戦国時代の山城の姿をよく伝えています。
takeda_castle.highlight_en: The ruins of a mountain castle are known as ``Castle in the Sky'' and ``Japan's Machu Picchu.'' The sight of a stone wall floating above a sea of ​​clouds on an autumn morning is a fantastic sight, and has recently gained worldwide attention on social media.
takeda_castle.text_en: Takeda Castle is a mountain castle that is said to have been built by Sozen Yamana in the middle of the Muromachi period, and is characterized by a group of stone walls that spread out on the top of Mt. Koga, which is 353 meters above sea level. At the end of the Sengoku period, the castle fell under attack by Hidenaga Hashiba, and was abandoned after the Battle of Sekigahara. On autumn mornings, the river mist of the Maruyama River turns into a sea of ​​clouds, and the fantastic sight of a stone wall rising above it has become a hot topic of conversation as the ``castle in the sky.'' In recent years, it has become a popular tourist destination in Hyogo, visited by more than 400,000 people a year. The field-style stone walls piled up neatly throughout the mountain are well-preserved and give a good impression of what the mountain castle looked like during the Sengoku period.

ikuta_shrine_kobe.name: 生田神社
ikuta_shrine_kobe.highlight: 神功皇后が創建したと伝わる神戸最古の神社。「神戸」という地名の起源となった「神の戸（かみのへ）」の神社で、源平合戦の生田の森の決戦地。
ikuta_shrine_kobe.text: 生田神社は神功皇后が三韓征伐からの帰途に創建したと伝わる古社で、稚日女尊を主祭神とします。「神戸」という地名は、この神社に奉仕した「神戸（かんべ）」と呼ばれる人々の集落に由来するとされており、神戸の起源ともいえる神社です。源平合戦の際には「生田の森」が平家の陣地となり、激しい戦いが繰り広げられました。現在の社殿は阪神大震災で甚大な被害を受け再建されたものですが、神戸の中心に位置する都市の鎮守として市民に深く親しまれています。縁結びの神としても人気が高い神社です。
ikuta_shrine_kobe.highlight_en: Kobe's oldest shrine is said to have been founded by Empress Jingu. This is the shrine of ``Kaminohe,'' which is the origin of the name ``Kobe,'' and the decisive battle site in Ikuta Forest during the Genpei War.
ikuta_shrine_kobe.text_en: Ikuta Shrine is an old shrine that is said to have been founded by Empress Jingu on her way back from the Sankan Conquest, and the main deity is Wakkachi Onnason. The place name ``Kobe'' is said to come from the village of people called ``Kanbe'' who served at this shrine, and this shrine can be said to be the origin of Kobe. During the Genpei War, Ikuta no Mori became a base for the Heike clan, and a fierce battle took place there. The current shrine building was rebuilt after being severely damaged in the Great Hanshin Earthquake, but it is deeply loved by citizens as the guardian of the city located in the center of Kobe. This shrine is also popular as the god of matchmaking.

hyogo_port_history.name: 兵庫津・兵庫の関跡
hyogo_port_history.kana: ひょうごのつ・ひょうごのせきあと
hyogo_port_history.highlight: 平清盛が日宋貿易の拠点として整備した古代港湾都市。南北朝時代には足利尊氏が「観応の擾乱」を経てここから新たな時代を開き、室町幕府誕生の地となった。
hyogo_port_history.text: 兵庫津（現在の神戸市兵庫区）は古代から「大輪田泊」として機能した港湾都市で、平清盛が日宋貿易の拠点として整備したことで飛躍的に発展しました。清盛はここに「経ヶ島」という人工島を造成し、大型船が入港できる港を整備しています。南北朝時代には観応の擾乱で劣勢となった足利尊氏がこの地で再起を図り、弟・直義との和解後に室町幕府を安定させた場所でもあります。江戸時代も西廻り航路の要港として栄え、幕末の開港で神戸港が開かれるまで、近畿の海上交通の中心であり続けました。
hyogo_port_history.highlight_en: An ancient port city developed by Taira no Kiyomori as a base for trade between Japan and Song. During the Nanbokucho period, Takauji Ashikaga ushered in a new era through the Kanno Disturbance, and it became the birthplace of the Muromachi Shogunate.
hyogo_port_history.text_en: Hyogotsu (present-day Hyogo Ward, Kobe City) is a port city that has functioned as ``Owata Tomari'' since ancient times, and it developed rapidly after Taira no Kiyomori established it as a base for trade between Japan and Song. Kiyomori built an artificial island called ``Kyogashima'' here and developed a port where large ships could enter. During the period of the Northern and Southern Courts, Takauji Ashikaga, who had fallen out of favor due to the Kanno Disturbance, tried to make a comeback in this area and stabilized the Muromachi Shogunate after making peace with his younger brother Tadayoshi. It flourished as a key port on the westbound route during the Edo period, and continued to be the center of maritime traffic in the Kinki region until the opening of Kobe Port at the end of the Edo period.

nishinomiya_shrine.name: 西宮神社
nishinomiya_shrine.highlight: 全国3500社のえびす神社の総本社。毎年1月10日の「十日えびす」開門神事・福男選びは全国中継される新春の風物詩で、商売繁盛の神「えべっさん」の総本宮。
nishinomiya_shrine.text: 西宮神社は恵比須神（えびす様）を主祭神とする全国約3500社のえびす神社の総本社です。創建の詳細は不明ですが、中世から「西宮のえびす」として広く信仰を集め、江戸時代には「えびす講」として商人たちの信仰を集めました。毎年1月10日に行われる「開門神事・福男選び」は、午前6時の開門と同時に参道を走り最初に本殿に到達した3人が「福男」に選ばれる行事で、全国的に有名なお正月の風物詩です。阪神大震災で甚大な被害を受け多くの建物が倒壊しましたが、現在は復興を遂げ、関西随一の初詣スポットとして年間100万人以上が参拝します。
nishinomiya_shrine.highlight_en: Headquarters of 3,500 Ebisu Shrines nationwide. The ``Toka Ebisu'' gate-opening ceremony and lucky man selection held on January 10th every year is a New Year's tradition that is broadcast nationwide, and is the main shrine of ``Ebessan,'' the god of business prosperity.
nishinomiya_shrine.text_en: Nishinomiya Shrine is the headquarters of approximately 3,500 Ebisu Shrines nationwide whose main deity is Ebisu-sama. Although the details of its founding are unknown, it has been widely worshiped since the Middle Ages as ``Ebisu of Nishinomiya,'' and during the Edo period, it attracted the faith of merchants as ``Ebisu-ko.'' The ``Open Gate Ceremony - Fuku Otoko Selection'' is held on January 10th every year, and is a nationally famous New Year's tradition in which the first three people who run along the approach to the shrine and reach the main shrine at the same time as the gate opens at 6 a.m. are selected as the ``Fuku Otoko.'' Although it was severely damaged in the Great Hanshin Earthquake and many buildings collapsed, it has now been rebuilt and is the best New Year's visit spot in Kansai, with more than 1 million people visiting the shrine each year.

izushi_castle.name: 出石城跡と出石の町並み
izushi_castle.kana: いずしじょうあととまちなみ

transit.name: 全但バス出石バスターミナル

izushi_castle.highlight: 但馬の小京都と呼ばれる城下町。江戸後期に信州・仙石家の国替えで蕎麦職人が移住したことで「出石そば」が誕生し、独特の食文化と城下町風情が共存する。
izushi_castle.text: 出石は但馬国の中心として栄えた城下町で、出石城は慶長9年（1604年）に小出吉英によって築かれた山城です。江戸中期、信州上田藩から仙石政明が国替えとなる際、信州の蕎麦職人を連れてきたことが「出石そば」の起源とされています。以来、出石は「蕎麦の町」として全国に知られるようになりました。城下町の町割りが今も残り、辰鼓楼（明治3年建立の時計台）を中心に白壁の武家屋敷・商家が連なる景観は「但馬の小京都」と称されます。現在も年間100万人以上が訪れる但馬最大の観光地です。
izushi_castle.name_en: Izushi Castle ruins and Izushi townscape
izushi_castle.highlight_en: A castle town called Tajima's Little Kyoto. Izushi soba was born in the late Edo period when soba craftsmen moved to Shinshu and the Sengoku clan, and the unique food culture and castle town atmosphere coexisted there.
izushi_castle.text_en: Izushi is a castle town that flourished as the center of Tajima Province, and Izushi Castle is a mountain castle built by Yoshihide Koide in 1604. Izushi soba is said to have its origins in the mid-Edo period, when Masaaki Sengoku moved from the Shinshu Ueda domain to another country and brought over soba craftsmen from Shinshu. Since then, Izushi has become known throughout the country as the ``soba town.'' The town layout of the castle town still remains, and the landscape of white-walled samurai residences and merchant houses centered around the Shinkoro (clock tower built in 1898) has earned it the nickname ``Tajima's Little Kyoto.'' Today, it is Tajima's largest tourist destination, visited by more than 1 million people a year.

miki_castle.name: 三木城跡（別所氏の城）
miki_castle.highlight: 羽柴秀吉の「三木の干殺し」で知られる籠城戦の舞台。播磨の雄・別所長治が2年近く籠城しながら最後に自刃して城兵を救った悲劇の城。
miki_castle.text: 三木城は播磨の有力武将・別所長治が籠城した城で、天正6年（1578年）から天正8年（1580年）にかけて、羽柴秀吉（豊臣秀吉）による「三木の干殺し」と呼ばれる兵糧攻めを受けました。秀吉は力攻めをせず周囲に付城を多数築いて城を封鎖し、兵糧を断つ戦略を取りました。約2年間の籠城の末、城内は飢餓に陥り、長治は城兵の助命を条件に妻子とともに自刃して開城しました。長治の辞世「今はただ恨みもあらじ諸人の命にかわる我が身とおもえば」は後世に語り継がれ、悲劇の武将として今も地元に慕われています。
miki_castle.highlight_en: This is the stage of Hideyoshi Hashiba's siege battle, famous for ``Miki's Hansatsu''. This is the tragic castle where the hero of Harima, Nagaharu Bessho, was imprisoned for nearly two years before finally committing suicide to save the castle's soldiers.
miki_castle.text_en: Miki Castle was the castle where Nagaharu Bessho, a powerful military commander in Harima, was holed up, and from 1578 to 1580, it was subjected to a military raid called ``Miki's Dry Kill'' by Hideyoshi Hashiba (Hideyoshi Toyotomi). Instead of attacking by force, Hideyoshi adopted a strategy of building numerous castles around the castle to blockade it and cut off its food supply. After about two years of siege, the castle fell into famine, and Nagaharu, along with his wife and children, committed suicide and surrendered the castle in exchange for the lives of the castle's soldiers. When Choji died, he said, ``Now I don't hold any grudges, but I thought of myself as my life at stake.'' This has been passed down to future generations, and he is still admired by the locals as a tragic military commander.

ikarugasho_hyogo.name: 鵤荘（斑鳩寺）
ikarugasho_hyogo.kana: いかるがしょう・はりまいかるがでら
ikarugasho_hyogo.highlight: 聖徳太子が奈良・法隆寺の荘園として設けた播磨の鵤荘に創建された古刹。太子直筆と伝わる聖徳太子像や太子ゆかりの文化財を多く伝える播磨の聖地。
ikarugasho_hyogo.text: 斑鳩寺（鵤寺）は推古天皇14年（606年）、聖徳太子が法隆寺（斑鳩寺）の荘園・鵤荘に創建したとされる播磨最古の寺院の一つです。「鵤（いかるが）」の地名は奈良の斑鳩（法隆寺がある地名）と同じで、太子がこの地を法隆寺荘園として開発したことに由来します。境内には太子直筆と伝わる「聖徳太子御影」や、三重塔（重要文化財）などが残り、播磨の聖徳太子信仰の中心地として古くから参拝者を集めています。現在は天台宗の寺院として護持され、多くの文化財を今に伝えています。
ikarugasho_hyogo.highlight_en: This ancient temple was built in Harima's Unso, which Prince Shotoku established as a manor for Horyuji Temple in Nara. A sacred place in Harima, home to a statue of Prince Shotoku that is said to have been handwritten by the prince, as well as many cultural assets related to the prince.
ikarugasho_hyogo.text_en: Ikaruga-ji Temple (Ken-ji Temple) is one of the oldest temples in Harima, and is said to have been built by Prince Shotoku in the 14th year of Emperor Suiko (606) in the manor of Horyu-ji Temple (Ikaruga-dera Temple). The place name ``Ikaruga'' is the same as Ikaruga in Nara (where Horyuji Temple is located), and comes from the fact that the Crown Prince developed this area as the Horyuji Manor. Within the precincts, there are remains such as the Prince Shotoku Mikage, which is said to have been handwritten by the Prince, and the three-storied pagoda (an important cultural property), and it has long been a center of worship for Prince Shotoku in Harima, attracting worshipers. Currently, it is protected as a temple of the Tendai sect, and many cultural assets have been passed down to this day.

todaiji.name: 東大寺

transit.name: 市内循環バス大仏殿春日大社前

todaiji.highlight: 聖武天皇が国家鎮護のために建立した奈良の大仏を安置する世界最大級の木造建築。高さ15mの盧舎那仏は鎮護国家の願いを込め、日本中から人・物・資金を集めて完成した。
todaiji.text: 東大寺は天平15年（743年）に聖武天皇が「大仏建立の詔」を出し、天平勝宝4年（752年）に大仏開眼供養が行われた奈良時代を代表する大寺院です。本尊の盧舎那仏（奈良の大仏）は高さ約15mの金銅仏で、完成には全国から技術者・資材・資金が集められ、当時の日本の国力を結集した事業でした。現在の大仏殿は江戸時代に再建されたもので、当初より小さくなったにもかかわらず幅57m・高さ49mと木造建築として世界最大規模です。「正倉院」を有し、世界遺産にも登録された奈良を代表する史跡です。
todaiji.highlight_en: One of the largest wooden structures in the world, housing the Great Buddha of Nara, built by Emperor Shomu to protect the nation. The 15m-tall Roshanabutsu was completed with people, materials, and funds gathered from all over Japan, with the hope of protecting the nation.
todaiji.text_en: Todaiji is a large temple representing the Nara period, where Emperor Shomu issued an edict to erect the Great Buddha in 743, and a memorial service to open the eyes of the Great Buddha was held in 752. The principal image of Buddha, Roshanabutsu (Nara's Great Buddha), is a gilt bronze Buddha approximately 15 meters in height, and its completion required engineers, materials, and funds from all over the country, making it a project that brought together the national strength of Japan at the time. The current Great Buddha Hall was rebuilt in the Edo period, and although it is smaller than it was originally, it is the largest wooden building in the world at 57m wide and 49m high. It is a historic site representative of Nara and is home to Shosoin, which is also registered as a World Heritage Site.

horyuji.name: 法隆寺
horyuji.highlight: 607年に聖徳太子が建立した世界最古の木造建築群。五重塔・金堂は1400年以上前の建物がそのまま現存し、日本初の世界文化遺産の一つ。
horyuji.text: 法隆寺は推古天皇15年（607年）に聖徳太子と推古天皇が用明天皇の病気平癒を願って建立したと伝わる寺院です。現存する五重塔・金堂は7世紀後半の再建とされますが、1400年以上前の木造建築が現存する奇跡の寺院であり、世界最古の木造建築群として世界的に知られています。広大な境内には西院伽藍・東院伽藍が広がり、収蔵する文化財は国宝・重要文化財が合わせて190件以上に上ります。1993年に姫路城とともに日本初の世界文化遺産に登録されました。聖徳太子の思想と飛鳥文化の精華が凝縮された日本仏教建築の原点です。
horyuji.highlight_en: The world's oldest wooden building complex, built by Prince Shotoku in 607. The five-storied pagoda and Kondo are buildings that are over 1,400 years old and still exist, and are one of Japan's first World Cultural Heritage Sites.
horyuji.text_en: Horyuji Temple is said to have been built by Prince Shotoku and Emperor Suiko in the 15th year of Emperor Suiko's reign (607) to pray for Emperor Yomei's recovery from illness. The existing five-storied pagoda and main hall are said to have been rebuilt in the latter half of the 7th century, but it is a miraculous temple that still has a wooden structure that is over 1,400 years old, and is known worldwide as the oldest wooden structure in the world. The vast precincts include the Saiin Garan and the Higashiin Garan, which house more than 190 national treasures and important cultural properties. In 1993, along with Himeji Castle, it was registered as Japan's first World Cultural Heritage Site. It is the origin of Japanese Buddhist architecture, condensing the ideas of Prince Shotoku and the essence of Asuka culture.

asuka_palace.name: 飛鳥宮跡（飛鳥）
asuka_palace.highlight: 推古天皇から持統天皇まで約100年間、日本の首都として機能した飛鳥の宮殿跡。大化改新・乙巳の変など日本国家形成の激動の舞台となった大和の地。
asuka_palace.text: 飛鳥地方（奈良県明日香村）は6〜7世紀に日本の政治・文化の中心として栄えた地域で、推古天皇の豊浦宮から持統天皇の藤原京まで、複数の宮殿が置かれました。大化元年（645年）には中大兄皇子（後の天智天皇）と中臣鎌足が蘇我入鹿を暗殺した「乙巳の変」が起き、「大化改新」へとつながる日本史最大の政変の舞台ともなりました。飛鳥板蓋宮跡・飛鳥浄御原宮跡などが発掘されており、古代国家形成期の日本の姿を伝える史跡が村内各所に点在しています。キトラ古墳・高松塚古墳など壁画古墳も集中する特別の地です。
asuka_palace.highlight_en: The Asuka palace ruins functioned as the capital of Japan for about 100 years from Emperor Suiko to Emperor Jito. The land of Yamato was the scene of turbulent events in the formation of the Japanese nation, including the Taika Reform and the Itsumi Incident.
asuka_palace.text_en: The Asuka region (Asuka Village, Nara Prefecture) flourished as the political and cultural center of Japan in the 6th and 7th centuries, and was home to several palaces, from Emperor Suiko's Toyoura Palace to Emperor Jito's Fujiwarakyo. In the first year of Taika (645), the ``Otsumi Incident'' occurred, in which Prince Naka no Oe (later Emperor Tenchi) and Nakatomi Kamatari assassinated Soga Iruka, and it became the stage for the largest political change in Japanese history, leading to the ``Taika Reform.'' The ruins of Asuka Itabashi Shrine and Asuka Kyoumihara Shrine have been excavated, and there are historical sites scattered throughout the village that tell us what Japan looked like during the formative period of the ancient nation. It is a special place with a large concentration of wall-painted tombs such as the Kitora tomb and the Takamatsuzuka tomb.

yoshino_kinpusenji.name: 吉野山・金峯山寺
yoshino_kinpusenji.kana: よしのやま・きんぷせんじ

transit.name: 近鉄吉野駅
transit.walk: 徒歩20分（ロープウェイも可）

yoshino_kinpusenji.highlight: 後醍醐天皇が南朝の皇居を置いた「南朝の都」。3万本の桜が咲き誇る霊峰・吉野山に、修験道の根本道場・金峯山寺が鎮座する信仰と歴史の地。
yoshino_kinpusenji.text: 吉野山は大和国の霊峰で、古くから修験道の聖地として山伏たちの修行の場でした。南北朝時代（1336年）には後醍醐天皇が吉野に逃れ、ここに南朝の皇居を置いて北朝・室町幕府と対立。吉野は約60年間、南朝の「都」として機能しました。山中に建つ金峯山寺蔵王堂は役行者が修験道の根本道場として開いた大堂で、高さ34mの巨大な本堂（国宝）には日本最大の秘仏・蔵王権現三体が安置されています。春には約3万本の桜が山を埋め尽くす「一目千本」の絶景で、世界遺産「紀伀山地の霊場と参詣道」の一部でもあります。
yoshino_kinpusenji.highlight_en: The "capital of the Southern Court" where Emperor Go-Daigo set up the Imperial Palace of the Southern Court. A place of faith and history where Kinpusen-ji Temple, the fundamental dojo of Shugendo, is located on Mt. Yoshino, a sacred mountain with 30,000 cherry blossoms in full bloom.
yoshino_kinpusenji.text_en: Mt. Yoshino is a sacred mountain in Yamato Province, and has long been a sacred place for Shugendo and a place for the training of Yamabushi. During the Nanbokucho period (1336), Emperor Go-Daigo fled to Yoshino and set up the Southern Court's imperial palace here, conflicting with the Northern Court and the Muromachi shogunate. Yoshino served as the "capital" of the Southern Court for about 60 years. The Zao Hall of Kinpusenji Temple, built in the mountains, is a large hall opened by En no Gyoja as the fundamental dojo of Shugendo.The huge main hall (national treasure) with a height of 34 meters enshrines three of Japan's largest hidden Buddhas, Zao Gongen. In spring, the mountain is covered with approximately 30,000 cherry blossom trees, creating a spectacular view of ``1,000 trees at a glance,'' and it is also part of the World Heritage Site ``Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kino Mountain Range.''

tanzan_shrine.name: 談山神社
tanzan_shrine.highlight: 大化改新の談合の地。中大兄皇子と中臣鎌足が蘇我入鹿打倒を密談した多武峰の山頂に立つ神社で、日本唯一の木造十三重塔が深山の紅葉の中に映える。
tanzan_shrine.text: 談山神社は藤原鎌足（中臣鎌足）を祀る神社で、境内の「御破裂山」山頂付近で645年に中大兄皇子と鎌足が蘇我入鹿打倒の密談を行ったと伝わり、「談い山（かたらいやま）」が社名の由来です。鎌足の没後、その子・定慧が父の墓所に十三重塔を建てたのが神社の起源とされます。境内の木造十三重塔は現存する唯一の木造十三重塔（重要文化財）として貴重です。秋の紅葉の名所としても名高く、朱塗りの社殿と紅葉のコントラストは大和路随一の絶景として知られています。
tanzan_shrine.highlight_en: The land of bid-rigging during the Taika Reforms. This shrine stands on the peak of Mt. Tommine, where Prince Naka no Oe and Kamatari Nakatomi had a secret meeting to overthrow Soga Iruka. Japan's only wooden 13-story pagoda stands out among the autumn leaves of the deep mountains.
tanzan_shrine.text_en: Tanzan Shrine is a shrine that enshrines Fujiwara no Kamatari (Nakatomi Kamatari), and it is said that in 645, Prince Naka no Oe and Kamatari had a secret meeting to overthrow Soga Iruka near the summit of Mt. Obatake in the precincts, and the name of the shrine comes from ``Katarayama'' (Talking Mountain). The origin of the shrine is said to be that after Kamatari's death, his son Sadae built a 13-story pagoda on his father's grave. The 13-story wooden pagoda in the precincts is valuable as the only existing 13-story wooden pagoda (Important Cultural Property). It is also famous as a famous spot for viewing the autumn leaves, and the contrast between the vermilion-painted shrine building and the autumn leaves is known as one of the most spectacular views on Yamatoji.

kasuga_taisha.name: 春日大社

transit.name: 市内循環バス春日大社本殿

kasuga_taisha.highlight: 藤原氏の氏神を祀る奈良の総社。768年の創建以来、千本以上の吊燈籠と石燈籠が参道を彩り、神鹿が自由に歩く古都の森に包まれた世界遺産。
kasuga_taisha.text: 春日大社は神護景雲2年（768年）に称徳天皇の命で藤原永手が創建した、藤原氏の氏神を祀る大社です。藤原氏が奈良時代から平安時代にかけて政治の中枢を握ったため、朝廷・貴族の篤い崇敬を受け、平安時代には「春日詣」が貴族の重要な行事となりました。境内には約3000基の燈籠（石燈籠約2000基・吊燈籠約1000基）が立ち並び、節分と中元に行われる「万燈籠」は幻想的な光景として知られています。神の使いとされる鹿が境内を自由に歩き、奈良公園全体で約1200頭が保護されています。1998年に世界文化遺産登録。
kasuga_taisha.highlight_en: A shrine in Nara that enshrines the guardian deity of the Fujiwara clan. Since its founding in 768, more than 1,000 hanging lanterns and stone lanterns have decorated the approach to the shrine, and this world heritage site is surrounded by an ancient forest where sacred deer roam freely.
kasuga_taisha.text_en: Kasuga Taisha Shrine was founded by Fujiwara Nagate in the second year of Jingo Keiun (768) on the orders of Emperor Shotoku, and is a shrine that enshrines the guardian deity of the Fujiwara clan. Because the Fujiwara clan held the center of politics from the Nara period to the Heian period, they were deeply revered by the imperial court and aristocrats, and during the Heian period, Kasuga pilgrimage became an important event for the aristocrats. Approximately 3,000 lanterns (approximately 2,000 stone lanterns and 1,000 hanging lanterns) line the grounds, and the ``Mantoro'' held during Setsubun and Chugen are known as a fantastic sight. Deer, considered to be messengers of the gods, roam freely within the grounds, and approximately 1,200 deer are protected throughout Nara Park. Registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site in 1998.

muroji.name: 室生寺
muroji.highlight: 女性の参詣を許した「女人高野」として知られる山岳寺院。室生川沿いの苔むした石段と五重塔が織りなす景観は日本の原風景そのもの。
muroji.text: 室生寺は宝亀年間（8世紀後半）に創建された真言宗の山岳寺院で、高野山が女性の参詣を禁じていたのに対し、古くから女性の参詣を受け入れてきたため「女人高野」として親しまれてきました。室生川沿いに杉木立が続き、苔むした石段の先に朱色の社殿群が点在する境内は、日本の山岳寺院の美しさを凝縮したような景観です。屋外に建つ五重塔（国宝）は高さ約16mと屋外の五重塔として日本最小で、繊細な美しさから「室生の宝塔」とも呼ばれます。1998年の台風で被害を受けましたが復元され、現在も訪れる人々を魅了しています。
muroji.highlight_en: A mountain temple known as ``Women's Koya'' that allows women to visit. The moss-covered stone steps and five-storied pagoda along the Murou River are a perfect example of the original Japanese landscape.
muroji.text_en: Muroji Temple is a mountain temple of the Shingon sect that was founded in the Hoki era (late 8th century).While Mount Koya prohibited women to visit, it has long been accepted by women, so it has been affectionately known as ``Women's Koya.'' The precincts, with a grove of cedar trees along the Murou River and a group of vermilion shrine buildings dotted with moss-covered stone steps, are a landscape that encapsulates the beauty of a Japanese mountain temple. The outdoor five-storied pagoda (national treasure) is approximately 16 meters high, making it the smallest outdoor five-storied pagoda in Japan, and is also called the ``Treasure Pagoda of Muro'' due to its delicate beauty. Although it was damaged by a typhoon in 1998, it has been restored and continues to attract visitors.

taimadera.name: 當麻寺
taimadera.highlight: 飛鳥時代創建の古刹で、東西に国宝の三重塔2基が対で現存する唯一の寺院。蓮糸で織られたとされる「當麻曼荼羅」と中将姫伝説で知られる大和の名刹。
taimadera.text: 當麻寺は飛鳥時代の推古天皇20年（612年）頃に創建されたと伝わる古刹です。東西に三重塔がそれぞれ1基ずつ現存する寺院は日本でここだけで、どちらも奈良時代建立の国宝として貴重な存在です。本尊の「當麻曼荼羅」は奈良時代の中将姫が一夜にして蓮糸で織り上げたという伝説で知られる巨大な綴織で、浄土曼荼羅の傑作として国宝に指定されています。中将姫の伝説は能・浄瑠璃・歌舞伎の題材となり、広く親しまれてきました。境内の牡丹は「当麻の牡丹」として有名で、春には多くの参拝者が訪れます。
taimadera.highlight_en: This is an ancient temple that was founded in the Asuka period, and is the only remaining temple with two national treasure three-storied pagodas in pairs on the east and west sides. A famous temple in Yamato known for the Taima Mandala, which is said to be woven from lotus thread, and the legend of Chujo Hime.
taimadera.text_en: Taima-dera Temple is an ancient temple that is said to have been built around the 20th year of Emperor Suiko (612) during the Asuka period. This is the only temple in Japan that still has three three-storied pagodas, one in the east and one in the west, and both are valuable national treasures built in the Nara period. The main object of worship, the Taima Mandala, is a gigantic tapestry that is said to have been woven in one night by a princess named Chusho from the Nara period using lotus thread, and is designated as a national treasure as a masterpiece of the Jodo mandala. The legend of Princess Chujo has become the subject of Noh, Joruri, and Kabuki, and has become widely popular. The peonies in the precincts are famous as ``Toma Peonies,'' and many worshipers visit in spring.

kashihara_jingu.name: 橿原神宮・畝傍山
kashihara_jingu.kana: かしはらじんぐう・うねびやま
kashihara_jingu.highlight: 初代・神武天皇が即位したと伝わる地に建つ神社。明治23年創建ながら大和三山の一つ・畝傍山を背に広大な神域が広がり、日本建国の原点を体感できる大社。
kashihara_jingu.text: 橿原神宮は神武天皇が橿原宮で即位したとされる地（紀元前660年とされる神話上の出来事）に、明治23年（1890年）に創建された神社です。主祭神は神武天皇と媛蹈鞴五十鈴媛命で、日本の初代天皇を祀る神社として全国から崇敬を集めています。境内は約50万坪の広大な神域で、背後に大和三山の一つ・畝傍山がそびえます。神武天皇陵（畝傍山東北陵）も隣接しており、日本建国の地としての荘厳な雰囲気を持ちます。紀元節（建国記念の日・2月11日）には全国から多くの参拝者が訪れます。
kashihara_jingu.highlight_en: A shrine built on the site where the first Emperor Jimmu is said to have ascended the throne. Founded in 1898, this grand shrine has a vast sacred area set against the backdrop of Mt. Unebi, one of the three mountains of Yamato, and allows you to experience the origins of Japan's founding.
kashihara_jingu.text_en: Kashihara Shrine is a shrine that was built in 1890 on the site where Emperor Jimmu is said to have ascended the throne at Kashihara Shrine (a mythical event that dates back to 660 BC). The main deities enshrined are Emperor Jinmu and Hime-keka Isuzu Hime-no-Mikoto, and it is revered from all over the country as a shrine that enshrines Japan's first emperor. The precincts are a vast sacred area of ​​approximately 500,000 tsubo, and Mt. Unebi, one of the three mountains of Yamato, rises in the background. The Mausoleum of Emperor Jimmu (Unebiyama Tohoku Mausoleum) is also adjacent, giving it a majestic atmosphere as the birthplace of Japan. Many worshipers come from all over the country on Kigen-bushi (February 11th, National Foundation Day).

azuchi_castle.name: 安土城跡
azuchi_castle.highlight: 織田信長が天下布武の象徴として築いた日本初の本格的天守を持つ城。完成からわずか3年で本能寺の変により灰燼に帰した「幻の城」の石垣が今も琵琶湖畔に残る。
azuchi_castle.text: 安土城は天正7年（1579年）に織田信長が琵琶湖東岸の安土山に完成させた画期的な城郭です。地上6階・地下1階の天主（天守）は日本初の本格的な高層建築で、黄金と朱を基調とした絢爛豪華な内装が宣教師ルイス・フロイスの記録に詳しく伝わっています。しかし天正10年（1582年）の本能寺の変で信長が斃れると、原因不明の火災で天主は焼失。わずか3年の栄華の後、「幻の城」となりました。現在は石垣と礎石のみが残り、信長の壮大な夢を静かに伝えています。
azuchi_castle.highlight_en: Built by Oda Nobunaga as a symbol of Tenkafubu, this is Japan's first castle with a full-fledged castle tower. The stone walls of the ``Phantom Castle'', which was reduced to ashes due to the Honnoji Incident just three years after its completion, still remain on the shores of Lake Biwa.
azuchi_castle.text_en: Azuchi Castle is an epoch-making castle built by Oda Nobunaga in 1579 on Azuchiyama on the eastern shore of Lake Biwa. The castle tower, which has 6 floors above ground and 1 floor below ground, was Japan's first full-fledged high-rise building, and the gorgeous interior, which was based on gold and vermilion, was detailed in the records of missionary Luis Frois. However, after Nobunaga died in the Honnoji Incident in 1582, the temple was destroyed by a fire of unknown cause. After only three years of prosperity, it became a "fantasy castle". Today, only the stone walls and foundation stones remain, quietly conveying Nobunaga's grand dream.

hikone_castle.name: 彦根城
hikone_castle.highlight: 徳川四天王の筆頭・井伊直政の後を継ぎ完成した国宝天守。幕末の大老・井伊直弼を生んだ井伊家35万石の居城で、桜の名所「玄宮園」と共に往時の姿を今に伝える。
hikone_castle.text: 彦根城は徳川四天王の一人・井伊直政の遺志を継ぎ、慶長12年（1607年）に嫡男・直継が完成させた城です。天守は国宝に指定されており、現存する12天守の一つとして往時の姿を伝えます。井伊家は江戸時代を通じて彦根藩35万石を領有し、幕府の重臣として活躍しました。特に幕末の大老・井伊直弼は日米修好通商条約に調印し、安政の大獄で吉田松陰らを処刑したことで知られ、桜田門外の変（1860年）で暗殺されました。天守前の「玄宮園」は近江八景を取り入れた大名庭園で、城と庭園の調和が美しい国の名勝です。
hikone_castle.highlight_en: This national treasure castle tower was completed by the successor of Ii Naomasa, the leader of the Tokugawa Four Heavenly Kings. The Ii family's 350,000 koku castle, which gave birth to Ii Naosuke, an elder at the end of the Tokugawa shogunate, is here, and along with Genkyuen, a famous cherry blossom viewing spot, it still conveys the image of the past.
hikone_castle.text_en: Hikone Castle was completed by his eldest son, Naotsugu, in 1607, following the wishes of Ii Naomasa, one of the Four Heavenly Kings of Tokugawa. The castle tower has been designated as a national treasure, and is one of the 12 existing castle towers that conveys what it looked like in the past. Throughout the Edo period, the Ii family owned 350,000 koku of Hikone domain and served as senior vassals of the shogunate. In particular, Naosuke Ii, an elder statesman at the end of the Edo period, is known for signing the Japan-US Treaty of Amity and Commerce and for executing Shoin Yoshida and others at Ansei's Great Prison, and was assassinated during the Sakuradamongai Incident (1860). Genkyuen in front of the castle tower is a daimyo garden that incorporates the Eight Views of Omi, and is a national scenic spot with a beautiful harmony between castle and garden.

enryakuji.name: 比叡山延暦寺
enryakuji.kana: ひえいざんえんりゃくじ

transit.name: 叡山電鉄八瀬比叡山口駅
transit.walk: ロープウェイ・ケーブル

enryakuji.highlight: 最澄が806年に開いた天台宗の総本山。法然・道元・日蓮・親鸞ら鎌倉仏教の開祖がすべてここで学んだ「日本仏教の母山」。信長の焼き討ちで全山灰燼に帰した歴史も持つ。
enryakuji.text: 延暦寺は延暦7年（788年）に最澄が比叡山に薬師如来を祀る堂を建てたことに始まる天台宗の総本山です。最澄の死後に「延暦寺」の寺号を賜り、平安時代には朝廷の厚い保護のもとで日本仏教の中心として発展しました。法然・道元・日蓮・親鸞・一遍ら鎌倉新仏教の開祖がすべて比叡山で修行した経歴を持ち、「日本仏教の母山」と称されます。元亀2年（1571年）、織田信長による「比叡山焼き討ち」で全山が焼却される大惨事を受けましたが、豊臣・徳川の時代に復興しました。1994年に世界文化遺産に登録されています。
enryakuji.highlight_en: The head temple of the Tendai sect, founded by Saicho in 806. This is the ``mother mountain of Japanese Buddhism,'' where the founders of Kamakura Buddhism, including Honen, Dogen, Nichiren, and Shinran, all studied. It also has a history of being reduced to ashes by Nobunaga's burning attack.
enryakuji.text_en: Enryakuji Temple is the head temple of the Tendai sect, which began in 788 when Saicho built a hall to enshrine Yakushi Nyorai on Mt. Hiei. After Saicho's death, the temple was given the name Enryakuji, and during the Heian period it developed as the center of Japanese Buddhism under the strong patronage of the Imperial Court. The founders of Kamakura New Buddhism, including Honen, Dogen, Nichiren, Shinran, and Ippen, all trained on Mt. Hiei, and it is known as the ``mother mountain of Japanese Buddhism.'' In 1571, Oda Nobunaga suffered a catastrophe in which the entire mountain was burned down, but it was rebuilt during the Toyotomi and Tokugawa eras. It was registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site in 1994.

ishiyamadera.name: 石山寺
ishiyamadera.highlight: 紫式部が『源氏物語』の構想を得たとされる琵琶湖畔の古刹。東大寺建立に使われた硅灰石の奇岩の上に伽藍が広がり、国宝の本堂と多宝塔が平安の雅を今に伝える。
ishiyamadera.text: 石山寺は天平19年（747年）に良弁僧正が開いたと伝わる真言宗の古刹で、境内に露出する「硅灰石」の巨岩が特徴です。東大寺の大仏建立の際にはこの石が使われたとも伝えられます。平安時代には参詣が貴族の間で流行し、紫式部が参籠中に観月楼から琵琶湖に映る月を見て『源氏物語』の構想を得たとの伝説が残ります。境内の「源氏の間」には紫式部の像が安置されています。国宝の本堂は平安時代建立の東寺様と和様を折衷した珍しい建築で、多宝塔は日本最古のものの一つです。
ishiyamadera.highlight_en: An ancient temple on the shores of Lake Biwa where Murasaki Shikibu is said to have gotten the idea for The Tale of Genji. The temple is built on top of a strangely shaped wollastonite rock that was used to build Todaiji Temple, and the main hall and pagoda, both national treasures, convey the elegance of the Heian period.
ishiyamadera.text_en: Ishiyama-dera Temple is an old temple of the Shingon sect that is said to have been opened by the priest Ryoben in 747, and is characterized by the huge wollastonite rock that is exposed within the temple grounds. It is said that this stone was used when constructing the Great Buddha at Todaiji Temple. Pilgrimage was popular among the aristocrats during the Heian period, and there is a legend that Murasaki Shikibu got the idea for ``The Tale of Genji'' when he saw the moon reflected in Lake Biwa from the moon viewing tower during his pilgrimage. A statue of Murasaki Shikibu is enshrined in the ``Genji no Ma'' in the precincts. The main hall, which is a national treasure, is an unusual architecture that combines Japanese styles with Toji Temple, which was built in the Heian period, and the Tahoto pagoda is one of the oldest in Japan.

nagahama_castle.name: 長浜城歴史博物館
nagahama_castle.kana: ながはまじょうれきしはくぶつかん
nagahama_castle.highlight: 羽柴秀吉が初めて城主となった城。琵琶湖畔の城下町として栄え、秀吉と石田三成の出会いの地「三献の茶」伝説が生まれた北近江の中心都市。
nagahama_castle.text: 長浜城は天正元年（1573年）に羽柴秀吉（豊臣秀吉）が浅井長政を滅ぼした後、浅井氏の旧領・北近江を与えられ、初めて城主として築いた城です。秀吉はここで城下町を整備し、楽市楽座を敷いて商業を振興、長浜は北近江の中心都市として発展しました。この地で家臣・石田三成が仕えることになった「三献の茶」の逸話（秀吉に3段階の温度の茶を出して才覚を認められたとされる話）は有名です。現在の城は昭和に再建された模擬天守で、歴史博物館として機能しています。黒壁スクエアを中心とした城下町の風情も人気です。
nagahama_castle.highlight_en: This is the castle where Hideyoshi Hashiba became the first lord. The central city of Kita-Omi, which flourished as a castle town on the shores of Lake Biwa and where Hideyoshi and Mitsunari Ishida met and where the legend of ``Sanken no tea'' was born.
nagahama_castle.text_en: Nagahama Castle was the first castle that Hashiba Hideyoshi (Toyotomi Hideyoshi) built in 1573 as the castle owner after he was granted the Azai clan's former territory of Kita-Omi after defeating Azai Nagamasa. Hideyoshi established a castle town here and established Rakuichi Rakuza to promote commerce, and Nagahama developed as the central city of Kita-Omi. There is a well-known anecdote about the ``Sanken-no-cha'' (the story of Hideyoshi's ability to serve tea at three different temperatures) that led his vassal Mitsunari Ishida to serve in this area. The current castle is a mock castle tower rebuilt in the Showa era and functions as a history museum. The castle town atmosphere centered around Kurokabe Square is also popular.

koka_shinobi.name: 甲賀の里・忍術村
koka_shinobi.kana: こうかのさと・にんじゅつむら
koka_shinobi.highlight: 伊賀と並ぶ二大忍者の里・甲賀の発祥地。戦国時代に甲賀五十三家の地侍が独自の諜報・戦闘技術を発展させ、徳川幕府にも仕えた忍者の里として現代も語り継がれる。
koka_shinobi.text: 甲賀（こうか）は三重県の伊賀と並んで「忍者の二大発祥地」とされる地で、室町時代から戦国時代にかけて甲賀五十三家の地侍が自衛のために独自の武術・諜報技術を発展させました。甲賀忍者は特定の主君を持たず、各地の大名から傭兵として雇われていましたが、徳川家康が大坂城攻めの際に甲賀忍者を幕府に召し抱えたことで「甲賀組」として組織化されました。現在も旧甲賀郡には忍者屋敷の遺構が残り、「甲賀の里 忍術村」などで忍者文化の体験ができます。甲賀は多羅尾氏をはじめ多くの忍者の里として知られています。
koka_shinobi.highlight_en: The birthplace of Koga, one of the two great ninja villages along with Iga. During the Sengoku period, the local samurai of the Koga 53 clan developed unique intelligence and combat techniques, and it is still passed down today as the home of ninjas who served the Tokugawa shogunate.
koka_shinobi.text_en: Along with Iga in Mie Prefecture, Koka is considered to be one of the two birthplaces of ninja, and from the Muromachi period to the Sengoku period, the local samurai of the 53 families of Koka developed their own martial arts and espionage techniques for self-defense. The Koga ninja did not have a specific master and were hired as mercenaries by feudal lords from around the country, but when Tokugawa Ieyasu recruited the Koga ninja to the shogunate during the siege of Osaka Castle, they were organized as the ``Koka-gumi''. Today, the remains of ninja mansions still remain in the former Koka District, and you can experience ninja culture at places such as Koka no Sato Ninjutsu Village. Koga is known as the home of many ninjas, including the Tarao clan.

omi_jingu.name: 近江神宮
omi_jingu.highlight: 667年に大津宮を定めた天智天皇を祀る神社。天智天皇が日本初の水時計「漏刻」を設置し時を告げた地として「時の記念日」に縁深く、かるたの聖地でもある。
omi_jingu.text: 近江神宮は昭和15年（1940年）に創建された比較的新しい神社ですが、祭神の天智天皇は7世紀に大津宮（現・大津市錦織）を都と定めた天皇です。天智天皇は天智10年（671年）に漏刻（水時計）を設置し、鐘や鼓で時刻を人々に知らせたことから、「時の記念日（6月10日）」ゆかりの神社として時計店や時間に関わる業種の崇敬を集めています。また百人一首を編んだ藤原定家の子孫が天智天皇の和歌から着想した経緯から、かるたの聖地として「競技かるた」の大会が毎年この神社で行われています。
omi_jingu.highlight_en: A shrine dedicated to Emperor Tenji, who established Otsunomiya in 667. It is also a sacred place for karuta, and is closely associated with the ``Time Anniversary'' as the place where Emperor Tenji installed Japan's first water clock, ``Rochoku,'' to tell the time.
omi_jingu.text_en: Omi Jingu is a relatively new shrine, having been built in 1940, but its enshrined deity, Emperor Tenchi, was an emperor who established Otsunomiya (now Nishikori, Otsu City) as his capital in the 7th century. Emperor Tenji installed a water clock in the 10th year of Tenchi (671) and used bells and drums to tell people the time, so it has become a shrine associated with the ``Time Anniversary'' (June 10th), and is revered by watch shops and businesses related to time. In addition, the descendants of Fujiwara Teika, who created Hyakunin Isshu, came up with the idea from Emperor Tenji's waka poems, and as a result, competitive karuta competitions are held at this shrine every year as a holy place for karuta.

kannoji_castle.name: 観音寺城跡
kannoji_castle.kana: かんのんじじょうあと
kannoji_castle.highlight: 南近江を支配した佐々木六角氏の巨大山城。標高432mの繖山全体に石垣や曲輪が広がり、戦国期の山城として信長に攻められ落城した。日本五大山城の一つ。
kannoji_castle.text: 観音寺城は近江守護・佐々木六角氏の居城で、繖山（きぬがさやま、標高432m）の山頂部に築かれた巨大な山城です。応仁の乱の頃から整備が進み、最盛期には山全体に数百の曲輪・石垣が広がる日本有数の山城として機能しました。永禄11年（1568年）、上洛する織田信長の軍勢が迫ると六角氏は抵抗することなく落城・逃亡し、以後衰退しました。現在は山中に石垣・礎石が残り、往時の巨大城郭の面影を伝えています。日本城郭協会が選ぶ「日本100名城」にも選定されており、城好きに人気の史跡です。
kannoji_castle.highlight_en: A huge mountain castle built by the Sasaki Rokkaku clan that ruled Minami Omi. Stone walls and curved walls spread across the entire length of Mt. Mt., which is 432 meters above sea level, and it was used as a mountain castle during the Sengoku period and was attacked and fell by Nobunaga. One of Japan's five great mountain castles.
kannoji_castle.text_en: Kanonji Castle is the residence of the Rokkaku Sasaki clan, the shugo of Omi, and is a huge mountain castle built on the top of Mt. Kinugasayama (432m above sea level). Construction began around the time of the Onin War, and at its peak it functioned as one of Japan's leading mountain castles, with hundreds of curved walls and stone walls spread throughout the mountain. In 1568, when Oda Nobunaga's army approaching Kyoto approached, the Rokkaku clan fell to the castle and fled without resisting, and the clan declined thereafter. Today, the stone walls and foundation stones remain in the mountains, giving us a glimpse of what was once a gigantic castle. It has been selected as one of Japan's 100 Famous Castles by the Japan Castle Association, and is a popular historical site for castle lovers.

gichuji_yoshinaka.name: 義仲寺
gichuji_yoshinaka.highlight: 源義仲（木曾義仲）と松尾芭蕉が並んで眠る異色の寺。「倶に野外に朽ちん」と遺言した芭蕉が木曾義仲を慕い、自らも義仲の傍らに葬られることを望んだ俳諧の聖地。
gichuji_yoshinaka.text: 義仲寺は源平合戦で活躍した源義仲（木曾義仲）の墓所に建てられた小さな寺院です。義仲は粗野な武将として知られ、京都を占領した際に略奪を行い民衆の恨みを買い、最終的には従弟の頼朝が派遣した義経・範頼軍によって粟津の戦いで討たれました。没後、義仲を慕う人々が大津に墓を建てました。江戸時代の俳人・松尾芭蕉は義仲の悲劇的な生涯に深く共感し、「木曾殿と背中合はせの寒さかな」と詠み、「倶に野外に朽ちん」と遺言して自らもこの地に葬られることを望みました。芭蕉の墓も義仲墓の隣に置かれており、俳諧の聖地として多くの俳人が参詣します。
gichuji_yoshinaka.highlight_en: A unique temple where Minamoto no Yoshinaka (Kiso Yoshinaka) and Matsuo Basho sleep side by side. This is a sacred place for haiku poets, where Basho, who wrote in his last will, ``I will rot in the open air,'' admired Yoshinaka Kiso and wished to be buried beside him.
gichuji_yoshinaka.text_en: Yoshinakaji is a small temple built on the grave site of Minamoto no Yoshinaka (Kiso Yoshinaka), who was active in the Genpei War. Yoshinaka was known as a rough-and-tumble military commander, and when he occupied Kyoto, he aroused the resentment of the people by plundering it, and was ultimately defeated at the Battle of Awazu by the forces of Yoshitsune and Noriyori sent by his cousin Yoritomo. After his death, people who admired Yoshinaka built a grave in Otsu. The Edo period haiku poet Matsuo Basho deeply sympathized with Yoshinaka's tragic life, and wished to be buried here as well, writing in a poem, ``It's cold, back to back with Kiso-dono,'' and he also wrote in his will, ``Let me rot in the open air.'' Basho's grave is also located next to Yoshinaka's grave, and many haiku poets visit this place as a sacred place for haiku.

koyasan.name: 高野山
koyasan.highlight: 空海（弘法大師）が816年に開いた真言密教の聖地。壇上伽藍・奥之院を中心に117の寺院が山上に集まり、今も弘法大師が入定（瞑想）し続けるという信仰を集める世界遺産。
koyasan.text: 高野山は弘仁7年（816年）に空海（弘法大師）が嵯峨天皇から賜り開いた真言密教の根本道場です。標高約900mの山上盆地に117の寺院が密集し、真言宗の総本山・金剛峯寺を中心とした宗教都市を形成しています。空海は承和2年（835年）に高野山奥之院で「入定」（瞑想に入ること）し、今なお生き続けているという信仰が続いています。奥之院の参道には織田信長・豊臣秀吉・伊達政宗ら戦国武将を含む20万基以上の墓碑・供養塔が並ぶ日本最大の霊場です。2004年に「紀伀山地の霊場と参詣道」として世界文化遺産に登録されました。
koyasan.highlight_en: A sacred place for Shingon Esoteric Buddhism, founded by Kukai (Kobo Daishi) in 816. A world heritage site where 117 temples, centered around Danjo Garan and Okunoin, gather on the mountain, and where people believe that Kobo Daishi continues to meditate.
koyasan.text_en: Koyasan is the fundamental dojo of Shingon Esoteric Buddhism, which was opened in 816 by Kukai (Kobo Daishi) as a gift from Emperor Saga. 117 temples are concentrated in the mountain basin at an altitude of about 900 meters, forming a religious city centered on Kongobu-ji, the head temple of the Shingon sect. There is a belief that Kukai entered into meditation (entered into meditation) at Okunoin on Mt. Koya in 835, and is still alive today. The approach to Okunoin is Japan's largest sacred site, with more than 200,000 tombstones and memorial towers, including those of Sengoku warlords such as Oda Nobunaga, Toyotomi Hideyoshi, and Date Masamune. In 2004, it was registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site as a ``Sacred Site and Pilgrimage Route in the Kili Mountains''.

kumano_hongu.name: 熊野本宮大社
kumano_hongu.kana: くまのほんぐうたいしゃ
kumano_hongu.highlight: 熊野三山の中心・全国3000社の熊野神社の総本社。平安時代に天皇・上皇が繰り返し参詣した「蟻の熊野詣」の目的地。八咫烏が導くサッカー日本代表のシンボルの地。
kumano_hongu.text: 熊野本宮大社は熊野三山（本宮・速玉・那智）の中核をなす、全国約3000社の熊野神社の総本社です。創建は崇神天皇の時代とされる古社で、平安時代から江戸時代にかけて天皇・上皇・法皇が繰り返し参詣した「熊野御幸」は百数十回に及び、庶民も「蟻の熊野詣」と呼ばれるほど大勢が参詣しました。熊野の神の使い・八咫烏（三本足のカラス）はサッカー日本代表のシンボルとして採用されています。もとは熊野川中洲の大斎原（おおゆのはら）に建っていましたが、明治22年の大洪水で現在地に移転。大斎原には今も大鳥居がそびえています。
kumano_hongu.highlight_en: The center of the Kumano Sanzan and the headquarters of 3,000 Kumano shrines nationwide. This is the destination of the ``Ari no Kumano Pilgrimage,'' which Emperors and Retired Emperors repeatedly visited during the Heian period. The symbol of Japan's national soccer team, led by the Yatagarasu.
kumano_hongu.text_en: Kumano Hongu Taisha is the central headquarters of the approximately 3,000 Kumano shrines nationwide, which form the core of the Kumano Sanzan (Hongu, Hayatama, and Nachi). It is an old shrine that is said to have been founded during the reign of Emperor Sujin, and from the Heian period to the Edo period, Emperors, Retired Emperors, and Cloistered Emperors repeatedly visited the shrine over 100 times, and so many ordinary people visited it that it was called the ``Ants' Kumano Pilgrimage.'' The Yatagarasu (three-legged crow), the messenger of the gods of Kumano, has been adopted as the symbol of the Japanese national soccer team. It was originally built in Oyunohara, Nakasu of the Kumano River, but was moved to its current location due to the great flood in 1891. The large torii gate still stands in Osaibara.

nachi_taisha.name: 熊野那智大社・那智の滝
nachi_taisha.kana: くまのなちたいしゃ・なちのたき
nachi_taisha.highlight: 落差133mの那智の滝を御神体とする熊野の古社。日本三名瀑の一つで、滝を仰ぐ青岸渡寺三重塔との組み合わせは和歌山を代表する絶景として世界遺産に刻まれる。
nachi_taisha.text: 熊野那智大社は那智の滝（落差133m）を御神体とする熊野三山の一社で、全国約4000社の那智神社の総本社です。那智の滝は日本三名瀑の一つで、古代の人々はこの巨大な滝を神の姿として崇めてきました。隣接する青岸渡寺は仁徳天皇の時代に印度の僧・裸形上人が那智の滝に修行して建立したと伝わる天台宗の寺院で、神仏習合の地として長く信仰されてきました。三重塔と那智の滝を同時に望む風景は日本の原風景として写真や絵画に多く描かれています。2004年に世界文化遺産「紀伀山地の霊場と参詣道」として登録されました。
nachi_taisha.highlight_en: An ancient shrine in Kumano whose deity is the 133m-high Nachi Falls. It is one of Japan's three famous waterfalls, and the combination of the three-story pagoda of Seigantoji Temple looking up at the waterfall has been inscribed on the World Heritage List as a spectacular view that represents Wakayama.
nachi_taisha.text_en: Kumano Nachi Taisha is one of the three Kumano shrines whose deity is Nachi Falls (133m high), and is the headquarters of approximately 4,000 Nachi shrines nationwide. Nachi Falls is one of Japan's top three waterfalls, and ancient people worshiped this gigantic waterfall as a divine figure. The adjacent Seigantoji Temple is a Tendai sect temple that is said to have been built during the era of Emperor Nintoku by the Indian monk Nugata Shonin who trained at Nachi Falls, and has long been worshiped as a place of syncretism between Shinto and Buddhism. The view of the three-storied pagoda and Nachi Falls at the same time is often depicted in photographs and paintings as an original Japanese landscape. In 2004, it was registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site, ``Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kibi Mountains''.

wakayama_castle.name: 和歌山城
wakayama_castle.highlight: 徳川御三家・紀州藩55万石の居城。徳川吉宗を輩出した紀州徳川家の城で、「紀州のみかん」で有名な城下町の中心。8代将軍吉宗の改革を生んだ紀州の智慧の地。
wakayama_castle.text: 和歌山城は天正13年（1585年）に豊臣秀吉の命で弟・秀長が築き、関ヶ原後に浅野幸長が改修した城です。元和5年（1619年）に徳川御三家の一つ・紀州藩が成立し、頼宣が55万石の大藩として整備しました。紀州徳川家からは享保の改革で知られる8代将軍・徳川吉宗が出ており、吉宗は紀州の農業技術や行政手腕を幕政に活かしました。また紀州は江戸時代から「みかんの産地」として有名で、現在も和歌山県は全国有数の柑橘産地です。昭和20年の空襲で焼失しましたが、昭和33年に再建されました。
wakayama_castle.highlight_en: The residence of the Kishu domain, one of the three major Tokugawa families, with a capital of 550,000 koku. It is the castle of the Kishu Tokugawa family, which produced Tokugawa Yoshimune, and is the center of the castle town famous for Kishu mandarin oranges. The land of wisdom in Kishu, which gave birth to the reforms of the 8th Shogun Yoshimune.
wakayama_castle.text_en: Wakayama Castle was built in 1585 by Toyotomi Hideyoshi's younger brother, Hidenaga, and renovated by Yukinaga Asano after Sekigahara. The Kishu domain, one of the three Tokugawa families, was established in 1619, and Yorinobu established it as a large domain with 550,000 koku. From the Kishu Tokugawa family came Tokugawa Yoshimune, the 8th shogun known for the Kyoho reforms, and Yoshimune utilized Kishu's agricultural technology and administrative skills in the shogunate. Kishu has also been famous as a ``mandarin orange producing area'' since the Edo period, and Wakayama Prefecture is still one of the leading citrus producing areas in Japan. It was burnt down in an air raid in 1945, but was rebuilt in 1955.

negoroji.name: 根来寺
negoroji.highlight: 鉄砲を持つ僧兵「根来衆」で知られる新義真言宗の根本道場。最盛期は4000坊・2万人の僧兵を擁したが豊臣秀吉に焼き討ちされた。大塔は戦火を免れた国宝の木造建築。
negoroji.text: 根来寺は平安末期に覚鑁上人（興教大師）が高野山から独立して創建した新義真言宗の根本道場です。室町時代に大きく発展し、最盛期には寺域に4000もの坊舎が並び、「根来衆」と呼ばれる鉄砲を持つ僧兵集団2万人を擁する一大勢力となりました。根来衆は早くから火縄銃を取り入れ、天正12年（1584年）の小牧・長久手の戦いでは徳川方に加わって参戦しました。天正13年（1585年）、紀州征伐に来た豊臣秀吉により大部分が焼き討ちされましたが、大塔（高さ40m）は奇跡的に焼け残り、現在は国宝に指定されています。
negoroji.highlight_en: This is the Nemoto dojo of the Shingi Shingon sect, known for its ``Negoroshu'' warrior monks with guns. At its peak, it had 4,000 monks and 20,000 monk soldiers, but it was burned down by Toyotomi Hideyoshi. The Great Pagoda is a national treasure wooden structure that survived the war.
negoroji.text_en: Negoroji Temple is the root dojo of the Shingi Shingon sect, which was founded by Kakuban Shonin (Kokyo Daishi) at the end of the Heian period, independent from Mt. Koya. It developed greatly during the Muromachi period, and at its peak there were 4,000 Buddhist temples lined up in the temple grounds, and it became a powerful force with 20,000 monk soldiers armed with guns called the Negoroshu. The Negoroshu adopted matchlock guns early on, and participated in the Battle of Komaki and Nagakute in 1584, joining the Tokugawa side. In 1585, most of the temple was burnt down by Toyotomi Hideyoshi who came to conquer Kishu, but the Great Pagoda (40m high) miraculously remained intact and is now designated as a national treasure.

kumano_hayatama.name: 熊野速玉大社
kumano_hayatama.kana: くまのはやたまたいしゃ
kumano_hayatama.highlight: 熊野三山の一社・新宮の鎮守。樹齢1000年以上の梛（なぎ）の巨木が御神木とし、古代の神々・速玉男命を祀る。熊野古道「大辺路」の終着点として巡礼者を迎えてきた。
kumano_hayatama.text: 熊野速玉大社は熊野三山の一社で、新宮市の熊野川河口近くに鎮座します。主祭神の熊野速玉大神・熊野夫須美大神は日本書紀にも登場する古い神々で、境内には樹齢1000年を超えるとされる御神木の梛の巨木が茂っています。熊野古道の各ルートが集まる熊野三山の一翼を担い、平安時代から多くの参詣者を迎えてきました。境内には国宝を多数収蔵し、熊野速玉大社の神宝は日本の古代祭祀の様子を今に伝える貴重な遺産です。隣接する神倉神社のゴトビキ岩は原始的な磐座信仰を伝え、毎年2月に行われる「お燈まつり」は国の重要無形民俗文化財です。
kumano_hayatama.highlight_en: Guardian of Shingu, one of the three Kumano shrines. A gigantic Nagi tree that is over 1,000 years old is considered a sacred tree, and the ancient gods Hayatamao-no-Mikoto are enshrined here. It has welcomed pilgrims as the final stop on the Kumano Kodo ``Ohechi.''
kumano_hayatama.text_en: Kumano Hayatama Taisha is one of the three Kumano shrines and is located near the mouth of the Kumano River in Shingu City. The main enshrined deities, Kumano Hayatama Okami and Kumano Fusumi Okami, are old gods that appear in the Nihon Shoki, and the shrine grounds are home to a huge sacred tree, said to be over 1000 years old. It plays a part in the Kumano Sanzan, where each route of the Kumano Kodo converges, and has welcomed many pilgrims since the Heian period. There are many national treasures stored within the shrine grounds, and the sacred treasures of Kumano Hayatama Taisha are a valuable heritage that tells us about Japan's ancient rituals. The Gotobiki Rock of the adjacent Kamikura Shrine conveys the primitive Iwaza faith, and the ``Oto Matsuri'' held every February is a national important intangible folk cultural property.

tomogashima.name: 友ヶ島（旧陸軍要塞跡）
tomogashima.highlight: 大阪湾防衛のため明治期に築かれた砲台・要塞跡が無人島にそのまま残る。アニメ「ラピュタ」の世界観を連想させる廃墟の蔦に覆われたレンガ建築が近年人気急上昇。
tomogashima.text: 友ヶ島は和歌山県沖合に浮かぶ無人島群（地の島・虎島・沖ノ島・神島）の総称です。明治時代、大阪湾への敵艦侵入を防ぐため旧日本陸軍が砲台・要塞を建設し、第二次世界大戦終了まで軍事施設として機能しました。終戦後は無人島となり、明治期のレンガ造りの建物・砲台・弾薬庫が自然の中に残されています。蔦に覆われた廃墟の光景が宮崎駿監督のアニメ「天空の城ラピュタ」の世界を連想させるとSNSで話題となり、近年は年間10万人以上の観光客が訪れる和歌山の人気スポットとなっています。
tomogashima.highlight_en: The ruins of artillery batteries and fortresses built during the Meiji period to defend Osaka Bay remain intact on the uninhabited island. Ruined brick buildings covered in ivy, reminiscent of the world of the anime ``Laputa,'' have skyrocketed in popularity in recent years.
tomogashima.text_en: Tomogashima is the collective name for a group of uninhabited islands (Jinoshima, Torashima, Okinoshima, and Kamishima) floating off the coast of Wakayama Prefecture. During the Meiji period, the former Japanese Army built a battery and fortress to prevent enemy ships from entering Osaka Bay, and it functioned as a military facility until the end of World War II. After the end of the war, the island became uninhabited, and the Meiji era brick buildings, artillery batteries, and ammunition depots remain in the natural surroundings. The sight of the ivy-covered ruins has become a hot topic on social media as it is reminiscent of the world of Hayao Miyazaki's anime ``Castle in the Sky,'' and in recent years it has become a popular spot in Wakayama that attracts more than 100,000 tourists a year.

kinokuni_ancient.name: 紀伊国分寺跡
kinokuni_ancient.highlight: 聖武天皇の詔により全国に建立された国分寺の紀伊国版。奈良時代の国家仏教政策の拠点として機能し、発掘調査で七重塔の礎石など当時の伽藍の様子が明らかになっている。
kinokuni_ancient.text: 紀伊国分寺は天平13年（741年）の聖武天皇の詔により全国60か国に建立を命じられた国分寺の一つで、現在の和歌山市府中に置かれました。国分寺は国ごとに国家の鎮護を祈る官寺として建立され、僧20名が常住して写経・法会を行う国家仏教の拠点でした。発掘調査では七重塔の礎石や金堂跡などが確認されており、奈良時代の壮大な伽藍の姿を示す遺構として保存されています。「府中」という地名は国府（国の政庁）があった地であることを示しており、この地が紀伊国の政治・宗教の中心地だったことがわかります。
kinokuni_ancient.highlight_en: Kii Province's version of Kokubunji temples built across the country by Emperor Shomu's edict. It functioned as a base for national Buddhist policy during the Nara period, and excavations have revealed the state of the temple at the time, including the foundation stones of the seven-storied pagoda.
kinokuni_ancient.text_en: Kii Kokubunji is one of the Kokubunji temples that were ordered to be built in 60 countries across Japan by Emperor Shomu's edict in 741, and was located in what is now Fuchu, Wakayama City. Kokubunji was built as an official temple for each country to pray for the protection of the nation, and was the center of national Buddhism, with 20 monks living there and conducting sutra copying and pujas. Excavations have revealed the foundation stones of a seven-storied pagoda and the ruins of the main hall, which have been preserved as remains of a magnificent temple from the Nara period. The place name ``Fuchu'' indicates that the Kokufu (national government office) was located there, indicating that this place was the political and religious center of Kii Province.

kokawa_dera.name: 粉河寺
kokawa_dera.highlight: 宝亀元年（770年）創建の西国三十三所第三番札所。3万坪の広大な境内に本堂（重要文化財）が建ち、近世に整備された枯山水の庭園は国の名勝に指定される紀の川沿いの名刹。
kokawa_dera.text: 粉河寺は宝亀元年（770年）、大伴孔子古が創建したと伝わる天台宗の寺院で、西国三十三所観音霊場の第三番札所として古来多くの巡礼者を集めてきました。主祭神は千手千眼観世音菩薩で、観音霊場として紀州最大の寺院に発展しました。江戸時代には紀州藩主・徳川家の帰依を受け、広大な境内が整備されました。本堂（重要文化財）前に広がる枯山水の庭園は桃山様式の石組みが特徴で、国の名勝に指定されています。参道には多くの商店が並び、門前町の風情を残す紀の川流域を代表する古刹です。
kokawa_dera.highlight_en: The third temple of Saigoku's 33 temples, built in 770. The main hall (an important cultural property) is built on the vast grounds of 30,000 tsubo, and the dry landscape garden developed in the early modern period is a famous temple along the Kinokawa River that has been designated as a national scenic spot.
kokawa_dera.text_en: Kokawa-dera Temple is a Tendai sect temple that is said to have been founded by Confucius Otomo in the first year of Houki (770), and has attracted many pilgrims since ancient times as the third shrine of the Saigoku Sanjusansho Kannon Sacred Sites. The main deity enshrined is the Thousand-Armed, Thousand-Eyed Kanzeon Bodhisattva, and it has developed into the largest temple in Kishu as a Kannon sacred place. During the Edo period, the Tokugawa family, the lords of the Kishu domain, devoted themselves to the temple, and the vast grounds were developed. The dry landscape garden in front of the main hall (an important cultural property) is characterized by Momoyama-style stonework and has been designated as a national scenic spot. The approach to the temple is lined with many shops, and it is an old temple that represents the Kinokawa River basin, retaining the atmosphere of a temple town.

onigajo_mie.name: 鬼ヶ城（熊野の奇岩海岸）
onigajo_mie.highlight: 長年の波浪と風雨が削り出した熊野灘の奇岩海岸。平安末期には水軍・多娥丸の根城だったとされ、坂上田村麻呂が征伐したとの伝説が残る世界遺産の海岸。
onigajo_mie.text: 鬼ヶ城は三重県熊野市の熊野灘沿岸に広がる奇岩・洞窟群で、荒波と風雨が長い年月をかけて凝灰岩を削り出した自然の造形物です。古来「鬼の棲む城」として畏れられ、平安時代末期には海賊・多娥丸（たがまる）の根城であったとされています。坂上田村麻呂が東征の際に多娥丸を征伐したという伝説が残り、地名の由来となっています。国の天然記念物および名勝に指定されており、2004年には「紀伀山地の霊場と参詣道」の一部としてユネスコ世界遺産にも登録されました。熊野灘の荒波が作り出した洞窟群を遊歩道で見学できます。
onigajo_mie.highlight_en: Kumanonada's strangely shaped rocky coast has been carved out by years of waves, wind and rain. The coast is said to have been the stronghold of the navy Tayamaru in the late Heian period, and is a world heritage site, where legend has it that Sakanoue Tamuramaro conquered it.
onigajo_mie.text_en: Onigajo is a group of strangely shaped rocks and caves that spreads out along the coast of the Kumanonada Sea in Kumano City, Mie Prefecture, and is a natural formation carved out of tuff over many years by rough waves and wind and rain. Since ancient times, it has been feared as a castle inhabited by demons, and is said to have been the stronghold of the pirate Tagamaru at the end of the Heian period. There is a legend that Sakanoue Tamuramaro conquered Tayamaru during his expedition to the east, which is the origin of the place's name. It has been designated as a national natural monument and a place of scenic beauty, and in 2004 it was also registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the "Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes of the Kiya Mountains." You can take a walk through the cave system created by the rough waves of the Kumano Sea.

ise_jingu_naiku.name: 伊勢神宮（内宮）
ise_jingu_naiku.kana: いせじんぐう・ないくう
ise_jingu_naiku.highlight: 天照大御神を祀る日本の総氏神・神社の最高峰。20年ごとに社殿を建て替える「式年遷宮」を1300年以上続け、「お伊勢参り」は江戸時代に生涯一度の夢だった。
ise_jingu_naiku.text: 伊勢神宮の内宮（皇大神宮）は天照大御神を主祭神とする、全国約8万社の神社の頂点に立つ最高の神社です。創建は垂仁天皇の時代（紀元前後）とされますが、歴史的証拠からは5〜6世紀頃とされています。20年ごとに社殿・神宝・装束のすべてを新調する「式年遷宮」は持統天皇の時代（690年）に始まり、2013年に第62回が行われました。江戸時代には「お伊勢参り」が庶民の間で大ブームとなり、全国から年間数百万人が参詣に訪れました。五十鈴川の清流で手を清め、深い杉木立の中を歩く参拝体験は今も変わりません。
ise_jingu_naiku.highlight_en: The highest peak of Japan's guardian deities and shrines that enshrine Amaterasu Omikami. The ``Shikinen Sengu'' process of rebuilding the shrine every 20 years has continued for over 1,300 years, and ``visiting Ise Shrine'' was a once-in-a-lifetime dream during the Edo period.
ise_jingu_naiku.text_en: The Naiku (Kotaijingu) of Ise Grand Shrine is the highest shrine of the approximately 80,000 shrines in Japan, whose main deity is Amaterasu Omikami. It is said to have been founded during the reign of Emperor Suinin (after BC), but historical evidence suggests that it was built around the 5th or 6th century. The Shikinen Sengu ceremony, in which the shrine, sacred treasures, and costumes are all renewed every 20 years, began during the reign of Emperor Jito (690), and was held for the 62nd time in 2013. During the Edo period, ``Oise Shrine'' became a big boom among the common people, with millions of people visiting from all over the country every year. The experience of visiting the shrine, which includes washing your hands in the clear waters of the Isuzu River and walking through deep cedar trees, remains the same.

ise_jingu_geku.name: 伊勢神宮（外宮）
ise_jingu_geku.kana: いせじんぐう・げくう
ise_jingu_geku.highlight: 食物・産業を司る豊受大御神を祀る伊勢神宮の外宮。内宮より先に外宮を参拝する「外宮先祭」の慣習があり、天照大御神の食事を司る神として朝夕の御饌の儀が1500年間絶えず続く。
ise_jingu_geku.text: 伊勢神宮の外宮（豊受大神宮）は食物・農業・産業を司る豊受大御神を祀ります。雄略天皇の時代（5世紀）に天照大御神の「食事係」として丹波から迎えられたとされ、内宮の食事を支える神として位置づけられています。毎朝夕、天照大御神に食事を奉る「日別朝夕大御饌祭」が1500年以上途切れることなく続けられており、日本の神祭りの古い形を伝えています。「伊勢参りは外宮から」という慣習があり、内宮より先に外宮を参拝する「外宮先祭」が正式な参拝順序とされています。外宮の北御門から入ると、静謐な森の空気が参拝者を包みます。
ise_jingu_geku.highlight_en: The outer shrine of Ise Grand Shrine is dedicated to Toyouke Omikami, the god of food and industry. There is a custom of ``Gekusakisai,'' which is to visit the Geku before visiting the Inner Shrine, and the morning and evening offerings have continued for 1,500 years as Amaterasu Omikami is the deity responsible for meals.
ise_jingu_geku.text_en: The outer shrine (Toyouke Daijingu) of Ise Grand Shrine enshrines Toyouke Daijingu, the god who governs food, agriculture, and industry. It is said that during the reign of Emperor Yuryaku (5th century), she was brought from Tanba as the ``meal attendant'' of Amaterasu Omikami, and is positioned as the deity that supports the meals at the Naiku. The Hibetsu Asayu Oomisensai, in which food is offered to Amaterasu Omikami every morning and evening, has continued uninterrupted for over 1,500 years, and is an old form of Japanese divine festival. There is a custom that ``Visiting Ise Shrine begins with the Geku,'' and the official order of worship is to visit the Geku before the Inner Shrine. As you enter through the north gate of the outer shrine, a tranquil forest atmosphere envelops worshipers.

matsusaka_castle.name: 松阪城跡
matsusaka_castle.highlight: 蒲生氏郷が築き「松阪商人」を育んだ城下町の中心。江戸時代に三井財閥の祖・三井高利を生んだ松阪は「商都」として栄え、本居宣長ゆかりの地でもある。
matsusaka_castle.text: 松阪城は天正16年（1588年）に蒲生氏郷が松ヶ島城から移って築いた城で、城下町の建設とともに商業を振興しました。江戸時代の松阪は「松阪商人」と呼ばれる豪商を多数輩出し、伊勢商人の中心地として栄えました。特に三井財閥の祖・三井高利は松阪出身で、江戸・京都・大阪に呉服店を展開して日本最大の商業資本を築きました。また松阪は国学者・本居宣長の出身地でもあり、宣長が35年にわたって講義を行った「鈴屋」が現存し、記念館として公開されています。「松阪牛」のブランド地としても全国に知られています。
matsusaka_castle.highlight_en: The center of the castle town that Ujisato Gamo built and nurtured the Matsusaka merchants. Matsusaka, where Takatoshi Mitsui, the founder of the Mitsui Zaibatsu, was born during the Edo period, flourished as a commercial capital and is also a place connected to Norinaga Motoori.
matsusaka_castle.text_en: Matsusaka Castle was built in 1588 by Ujisato Gamo, who moved from Matsugashima Castle to build a castle town and promote commerce. During the Edo period, Matsusaka produced many wealthy merchants called ``Matsuzaka merchants,'' and prospered as the center of Ise merchants. In particular, Takatoshi Mitsui, the founder of the Mitsui Zaibatsu, was born in Matsusaka and built Japan's largest commercial capital by opening kimono stores in Edo, Kyoto, and Osaka. Matsusaka is also the birthplace of Japanese scholar Norinaga Motoori, and Suzuya, where Norinaga gave lectures for 35 years, still exists and is open to the public as a memorial museum. It is also known throughout the country as the brand area for Matsusaka Beef.

iga_ueno_castle.name: 伊賀上野城
iga_ueno_castle.highlight: 忍者の里・伊賀の城。高石垣の高さは日本一（30m）を誇り、松尾芭蕉の生誕地でもある。伊賀流忍者博物館と合わせて「忍者・俳句の聖地」として多くの観光客が訪れる。
iga_ueno_castle.text: 伊賀上野城は慶長16年（1611年）に藤堂高虎が大坂に備えて高石垣を築いた城で、石垣の高さは約30mと日本最高を誇ります。天守は完成直前に暴風雨で倒壊し、現在の天守は昭和10年に復興されたものです。伊賀は甲賀と並ぶ忍者の二大発祥地で、城下には「伊賀流忍者博物館」があり、忍者屋敷・忍具・忍術の実演を見ることができます。また城の北側には俳聖・松尾芭蕉の生誕地があり、芭蕉翁記念館が整備されています。「古池や蛙飛び込む水の音」など俳句革命を起こした芭蕉の出発点として、俳句愛好者の聖地でもあります。
iga_ueno_castle.highlight_en: Iga Castle, the village of ninjas. It boasts the tallest stone wall in Japan (30m) and is also the birthplace of Matsuo Basho. Along with the Iga-ryu Ninja Museum, many tourists visit this place as a ``sacred place for ninjas and haiku.''
iga_ueno_castle.text_en: Iga Ueno Castle is a castle where Todo Takatora built a high stone wall in 1611 in preparation for Osaka, and the stone wall is about 30 meters high, the highest in Japan. The castle tower collapsed in a storm just before it was completed, and the current castle tower was rebuilt in 1933. Iga is one of the two birthplaces of ninja, along with Koga, and there is the Iga-ryu Ninja Museum in the castle town, where you can see ninja houses, ninja tools, and demonstrations of ninjutsu. Additionally, on the north side of the castle is the birthplace of haiku master Matsuo Basho, and the Basho Old Man Memorial Hall is maintained there. It is also a sacred place for haiku lovers, as it was the starting point for Basho, who started the haiku revolution with poems such as ``Old Ponds and the Sound of Water in which a Frog Jumps''.

saiku_ruins.name: 斎宮跡
saiku_ruins.highlight: 伊勢神宮に仕えた未婚の皇女「斎王」が暮らした宮殿跡。660年以上にわたり50人以上の斎王が伊勢に下り、源氏物語・枕草子にも登場する王朝ロマンの地。
saiku_ruins.text: 斎宮は伊勢神宮に仕えた「斎王（いつきのみこ）」と呼ばれる未婚の皇女が居住した宮殿で、現在の三重県多気郡明和町に位置していました。天皇の代替わりごとに新たな斎王が選ばれ、伊勢神宮への奉仕を終えるまでこの地で生活しました。制度は飛鳥時代（7世紀後半）から南北朝時代（14世紀）まで約660年間続き、50人以上の斎王が記録されています。万葉集・源氏物語・枕草子など古典文学にも斎王・斎宮が登場し、平安文化との深い関わりを持ちます。現在は発掘調査が続く史跡公園として整備され、「いつきのみや歴史体験館」で当時の生活が学べます。
saiku_ruins.highlight_en: This is the ruins of the palace where the unmarried princess Saio, who served the Ise Grand Shrine, lived. Over 660 years, more than 50 Saio descended to Ise, and it is a romantic land of the dynasty that appears in The Tale of Genji and The Pillow Book.
saiku_ruins.text_en: Saiku was a palace where an unmarried princess called ``Saio (Itsuki no Miko)'' who served the Ise Grand Shrine lived, and was located in present-day Meiwa Town, Taki District, Mie Prefecture. Each time a new emperor was replaced, a new Saio was chosen and lived here until he completed his service to Ise Grand Shrine. The system continued for approximately 660 years from the Asuka period (late 7th century) to the Nanbokucho period (14th century), and more than 50 Saio have been recorded. Saio and Saigu also appear in classical literature such as Manyoshu, The Tale of Genji, and The Pillow Book, and have a deep connection with Heian culture. Currently, it has been developed as a historical park where excavations continue, and you can learn about life at the time at the Itsukinomiya Historical Experience Center.

tado_taisha.name: 多度大社
tado_taisha.highlight: 「北伊勢大神宮」とも称される伊勢神宮に次ぐ格式を持つ古社。白馬が神前の坂を駆け上がる「上げ馬神事」は千年以上の伝統を誇り、国の重要無形民俗文化財に指定。
tado_taisha.text: 多度大社は天津彦根命を主祭神とする古社で、「北伊勢大神宮」とも称されるほど格式が高く、伊勢神宮に次ぐ崇敬を集めてきました。奈良時代の文献にも登場する古社で、平安時代には神宮寺が置かれ神仏習合の霊地として栄えました。毎年5月に行われる「上げ馬神事」は、若者が馬を駆って急勾配の坂を駆け上がらせ、その成否で農作物の豊凶を占う1000年以上の歴史を持つ神事で、国の重要無形民俗文化財に指定されています。多度の山から湧き出る清水は「多度の霊泉」として知られ、境内全体が霊気に満ちた聖域です。
tado_taisha.highlight_en: This is an ancient shrine that is second in status to Ise Grand Shrine, also known as ``Kita Ise Grand Shrine''. The Ageuma Shinto ritual, in which white horses run up the slope in front of the shrine, boasts a tradition of over 1,000 years and has been designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property.
tado_taisha.text_en: Tado Taisha Shrine is an ancient shrine whose main deity is Amatsu Hikone-no-Mikoto.It is so prestigious that it is also called the ``Kita Ise Grand Shrine'', and has been revered second only to Ise Grand Shrine. This is an old shrine that appears in literature from the Nara period, and during the Heian period, a Jingu-ji temple was built there and flourished as a sacred place for the syncretism of Shinto and Buddhism. The Ageuma Shinto ritual, which is held every May, is a ritual with a history of over 1,000 years, in which young people drive horses up a steep hill, and their success or failure predicts the abundance of crops.It has been designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property. The clear water gushing out from Mt. Tado is known as ``Tado no Sacred Spring,'' and the entire precinct is a sacred place filled with spiritual energy.

asamayama_kongoshouji.name: 朝熊山・金剛証寺
asamayama_kongoshouji.kana: あさまやま・こんごうしょうじ

transit.name: 伊勢・鳥羽スカイライン

asamayama_kongoshouji.highlight: 伊勢神宮の「鬼門」を守る真言宗の霊場。「お伊勢参らば朝熊をかけよ、朝熊かけねば片参り」と言われた伊勢参りの必参地で、山上からは伊勢湾と志摩半島が一望できる。
asamayama_kongoshouji.text: 金剛証寺は朝熊山（あさまやま、標高555m）の山頂近くに建つ真言宗の寺院で、空海の弟子・恵運が中興したと伝わります。伊勢神宮の「鬼門」（北東方向）を守護する寺として位置づけられ、「お伊勢参らば朝熊をかけよ、朝熊かけねば片参り」という俚諺の通り、伊勢参りの際には必ず朝熊山にも登ることが習わしとなっていました。江戸時代には多くの参詣者が訪れ、山頂の「岳」と呼ばれる一帯には死者の霊を祀る卒塔婆が林立する独特の風習が今も続いています。山頂からは伊勢湾・志摩半島・鳥羽を望む360度のパノラマが広がります。
asamayama_kongoshouji.highlight_en: A sacred site of the Shingon sect that protects the Demon Gate of Ise Grand Shrine. It is said to be a must-visit place for pilgrims to Ise, as it is said, ``If you go to Ise, go to Asaguma.
asamayama_kongoshouji.text_en: Kongoshoji Temple is a Shingon sect temple built near the summit of Mt. Asama (555m above sea level), and it is said to have been founded by Keiun, a disciple of Kukai. It was positioned as the temple that protected the "Kimon" (northeast direction) of Ise Grand Shrine, and as the proverb goes, "If you visit Ise, go to Asakuma, but if you don't go to Asakuma, it's a one-way visit." When visiting Ise, it was customary to climb Mt. Asakuma. During the Edo period, many pilgrims visited the mountain, and the unique custom of lining the area called ``Dake'' at the top of the mountain with sotoba, which enshrines the spirits of the dead, continues to this day. From the top of the mountain, you can enjoy a 360-degree panoramic view of Ise Bay, Shima Peninsula, and Toba.

toba_castle.name: 鳥羽城跡
toba_castle.highlight: 九鬼嘉隆が築いた海に浮かぶ「海城」。天下の将軍・豊臣秀吉も訪れた志摩の要港・鳥羽を治め、九鬼水軍の根拠地として伊勢・志摩の海を制した戦国大名の城。
