toba_castle.text: 鳥羽城は文禄3年（1594年）に九鬼嘉隆が築いた海城で、三方を海に囲まれた天然の要塞でした。九鬼氏は「海賊大名」として知られ、九鬼水軍は織田信長・豊臣秀吉に仕えて日本最初の鉄甲船を建造し、毛利水軍と戦った第二次木津川口の戦いで活躍しました。鳥羽は伊勢神宮への海路の玄関口でもあり、江戸時代も志摩国の要港として機能しました。現在は城山公園として整備されており、本丸跡からは鳥羽湾と点在する島々の絶景を望むことができます。城下には江戸時代の鳥羽藩の歴史を伝える史跡が残っています。
toba_castle.highlight_en: A floating castle built by Yoshitaka Kuki. It was the castle of a feudal lord from the Sengoku period who ruled Toba, an important port in Shima, which was visited by the nation's general, Toyotomi Hideyoshi, and who controlled the seas of Ise and Shima as the base of the Kuki navy.
toba_castle.text_en: Toba Castle was a sea castle built by Yoshitaka Kuki in 1594, and was a natural fortress surrounded by the sea on three sides. The Kuki clan was known as the "Pirate Daimyo," and the Kuki navy built Japan's first iron-clad ships in the service of Oda Nobunaga and Toyotomi Hideyoshi, and was active in the Second Battle of Kizukawaguchi against the Mouri navy. Toba is also the gateway to the sea route to Ise Grand Shrine, and also functioned as a key port for Shima Province during the Edo period. Currently, it is maintained as Shiroyama Park, and from the ruins of the main enclosure, you can enjoy a spectacular view of Toba Bay and the scattered islands. There are historic sites in the castle town that tell the history of the Toba clan during the Edo period.

akame_falls.name: 赤目四十八滝（修験道の地）
akame_falls.kana: あかめしじゅうはちたき
akame_falls.highlight: 伊賀の山中を流れる渓谷に連なる48の滝群。平安時代から修験道の行場として知られ、役行者・弘法大師ゆかりの霊地で、忍者修行の地としても伝えられる深山の聖域。
akame_falls.text: 赤目四十八滝は三重県名張市を流れる滝川に沿って約4kmにわたって連なる滝群の総称で、「四十八」は数が多いことを表す表現です。平安時代から修験道の行場として知られ、役行者や弘法大師も修行したとされる霊地です。「赤目」の名は、役行者がこの地で不動明王を感得した際に赤い目をした牛に乗って現れたという伝説に由来します。また伊賀忍者がこの険しい渓谷を修行の場として利用したとも伝えられており、忍者の聖地としても知られています。現在は国の天然記念物「赤目渓谷」として保護され、オオサンショウウオの生息地としても有名です。
akame_falls.highlight_en: A group of 48 waterfalls connected to a valley flowing through the mountains of Iga. A sacred area in the deep mountains that has been known as a training ground for Shugendo since the Heian period, a sacred place associated with En no Gyoja and Kobo Daishi, and also a place for ninja training.
akame_falls.text_en: Akame Shijuhachi Falls is a collective name for a group of waterfalls that stretches for approximately 4km along the Takigawa River that flows through Nabari City, Mie Prefecture, and "48" is an expression that refers to the large number of waterfalls. It has been known as a training ground for Shugendo since the Heian period, and is a sacred place where En no Gyoja and Kobo Daishi are said to have trained. The name ``Akame'' comes from the legend that En no Gyoja appeared riding a bull with red eyes when he perceived Fudo Myoo in this area. It is also said that the Iga ninja used this steep valley as a training ground, and it is also known as a sacred place for ninjas. It is currently protected as the national natural monument ``Akame Valley'' and is also famous as a habitat for giant salamanders.

kamishima_island.name: 神島
kamishima_island.highlight: 三島由紀夫の小説『潮騒』の舞台となった伊勢湾口の小島。伊勢湾・太平洋の分岐点に位置し古代から航海の要衝として知られ、灯台・神社・集落が凝縮した島。
kamishima_island.text: 神島は鳥羽市の沖合約11kmに浮かぶ周囲約3kmの小島で、伊勢湾と太平洋の境界に位置する航海の要衝です。古代から「神の島」として崇められ、島に鎮座する八代神社はこの地を通る船人たちの信仰を集めてきました。昭和29年（1954年）に三島由紀夫がこの島を訪れて若い漁師の純愛を描いた小説『潮騒』を執筆し、映画化も繰り返された名作の舞台として広く知られるようになりました。島内には「潮騒」ゆかりの場所が点在し、文学ファンが多く訪れます。また太平洋戦争中には旧海軍の監視哨が置かれた戦略的要地でもありました。
kamishima_island.highlight_en: A small island at the mouth of Ise Bay that was the setting for Yukio Mishima's novel "Sound of the Sea." Located at the junction of Ise Bay and the Pacific Ocean, this island has been known as a strategic point for navigation since ancient times, and is home to lighthouses, shrines, and villages.
kamishima_island.text_en: Kamishima is a small island with a circumference of approximately 3 km floating approximately 11 km off the coast of Toba City, and is a strategic point for navigation located on the border between Ise Bay and the Pacific Ocean. It has been worshiped as the "Island of the Gods" since ancient times, and Yashiro Shrine, which is enshrined on the island, has attracted the faith of boaters who pass through this area. In 1954, Yukio Mishima visited this island and wrote the novel "Shiosai", which depicts the pure love of a young fisherman, and it became widely known as the setting for a masterpiece that has been made into a movie many times. The island is dotted with places related to Shiosai, which are visited by many literature fans. It was also a strategic location where a former naval observation post was placed during the Pacific War.

tottori_castle.name: 鳥取城跡
tottori_castle.highlight: 羽柴秀吉の「干し殺し」兵糧攻めで落城した難攻不落の山城。久松山の頂に天守台が残る。
tottori_castle.text: 鳥取城は因幡国守護・山名氏が築いた山城で、戦国時代に毛利氏の支城となった。1581年、羽柴秀吉は兵糧攻めを採用し、城内の兵糧を断つため周囲に土塁を築いて完全に包囲した。飢えに苦しんだ守将・吉川経家は城兵の命と引き換えに自刃し開城。この戦いは「鳥取城の渇え殺し」として歴史に刻まれた。江戸時代には池田氏が入城し山麓に二ノ丸・三ノ丸を拡張。現在は久松公園として整備され、石垣と天守台が当時の姿を伝えている。
tottori_castle.highlight_en: An impregnable mountain castle that fell during Hideyoshi Hashiba's ``dry killing'' raid on supplies. The castle tower remains at the top of Mt. Hisamatsuyama.
tottori_castle.text_en: Tottori Castle is a mountain castle built by the Yamana clan, the shugo of Inaba Province, and became a branch castle of the Mori clan during the Sengoku period. In 1581, Hashiba Hideyoshi adopted a food offensive and completely surrounded the castle by building earthworks around it to cut off the food supply within the castle. Suffering from starvation, the general, Tsuneie Yoshikawa, committed suicide and surrendered the castle in exchange for the lives of his soldiers. This battle was etched into history as the ``Thirst Slayer of Tottori Castle''. During the Edo period, the Ikeda clan entered the castle and expanded Ninomaru and Sannomaru at the foot of the mountain. Currently, it is maintained as Hisamatsu Park, and the stone walls and castle tower still show what it looked like back then.

hakuto_coast.name: 白兎海岸
hakuto_coast.highlight: 『古事記』に記された「因幡の白兎」神話の舞台。大国主命が傷ついた白兎を救った伝説の浜辺。
hakuto_coast.text: 白兎海岸は日本最古の神話のひとつ「因幡の白兎」の舞台として知られる。『古事記』によれば、隠岐の島から渡ろうとした白兎がワニ（サメ）に毛皮を剥がされ苦しんでいたところ、大国主命が蒲の穂で傷を癒したという。浜には白兎神社が鎮座し、縁結びの神として信仰を集める。砂浜には蒲の群生が残り、神話の情景を今に伝えている。毎年春には白兎神話にちなんだ祭事も行われ、古代日本の口承文学が息づく場所だ。
hakuto_coast.highlight_en: The setting for the myth of ``The White Rabbit of Inaba,'' written in ``Kojiki.'' The legendary beach where Okuninushi no Mikoto saved an injured white rabbit.
hakuto_coast.text_en: Hakuto Beach is known as the setting for one of Japan's oldest myths, ``The White Rabbit of Inaba.'' According to the Kojiki, when a white rabbit was trying to cross from the Oki Islands and was suffering from having its fur ripped off by a crocodile (shark), Okuninushi healed the wound with an ear of cloves. Hakuto Shrine is located on the beach and is worshiped as the god of matchmaking. Clusters of grasshoppers remain on the sandy beach, conveying scenes from myths to this day. Festivals related to the White Rabbit myth are held every spring, and it is a place where ancient Japanese oral literature lives on.

mitokusan_nageiredo.name: 三徳山三佛寺投入堂
mitokusan_nageiredo.kana: みとくさんさんぶつじなげいれどう
mitokusan_nageiredo.highlight: 絶壁の岩窟に嵌め込まれた建築の謎。役行者が法力で投げ入れたと伝わる平安時代の懸造りの堂。
mitokusan_nageiredo.text: 三徳山三佛寺の奥院・投入堂は、垂直に切り立った断崖の岩窟に建てられた極めて特異な建造物で、国宝に指定されている。平安時代後期の建立とされ、役行者が法力で投げ入れたとの伝説から「投入堂」と呼ばれる。建設方法は現在も完全には解明されておらず、足場が組めない絶壁への建設は当時の建築技術の粋を集めたものと考えられる。参拝には急峻な山道を登る必要があり、輪袈裟を着けた修験道の聖地として今も多くの参拝者が訪れる。日本遺産にも認定されている。
mitokusan_nageiredo.highlight_en: The mystery of an architecture built into a rock cave on a cliff. It is said that En no Gyōja threw the temple into the Heian period hanging structure.
mitokusan_nageiredo.text_en: The inner temple and nageire-do hall of Mt. Mitoku Sanbutsu-ji Temple is an extremely unique structure built in a rock cave on a vertical cliff, and has been designated as a national treasure. It is said to have been built in the late Heian period, and is called ``Nageire-do'' because of the legend that En no Gyōja threw it in with his legal power. The method of construction is still not fully understood, and the construction on a cliff where scaffolding was not possible is considered to be the best of the architectural techniques of the time. It is necessary to climb a steep mountain path to visit the shrine, and many worshipers still visit it today as a sacred place for Shugendo people who wear robes. It is also recognized as a Japanese heritage site.

yonago_castle.name: 米子城跡
yonago_castle.highlight: 伯耆富士を望む湊山に築かれた城。四重五階の天守を持ち、山陰最大級の城郭だった。
yonago_castle.text: 米子城は天正年間に吉川広家が築城し、のちに中村一忠が四重五階の天守と四つの三重櫓を持つ大城郭に整備した。湊山の頂に立つ石垣は今も堅固に残り、眼下に中海と弓ヶ浜、晴れた日には大山（伯耆富士）を一望できる。江戸時代は鳥取藩の支城として池田家の家臣が城代を務めた。明治維新後に廃城令で建物は取り壊されたが、石垣と堀の遺構が往時の規模を伝えている。
yonago_castle.highlight_en: A castle built on Mt. Minato overlooking Hoki Fuji. It was one of the largest castles in the San'in region, with a four-story, five-story castle tower.
yonago_castle.text_en: Yonago Castle was built during the Tensho era by Hiroie Yoshikawa, and later Kazutada Nakamura developed it into a large castle with a four-layered, five-story castle tower and four triple-layered turrets. The stone wall at the top of Mt. Minato still stands strong, and you can see Nakaumi and Yumigahama beach below, as well as Mt. Daisen (Hoki Fuji) on clear days. During the Edo period, vassals of the Ikeda family served as castle owners as a branch castle of the Tottori clan. After the Meiji Restoration, the building was demolished under the Castle Abolition Order, but the remains of the stone walls and moat still give us an idea of ​​its former size.

jinfukaku.name: 仁風閣
jinfukaku.highlight: 明治40年築の白亜の洋館。皇太子（後の大正天皇）の山陰行啓のために建てられた迎賓館。
jinfukaku.text: 仁風閣は1907年（明治40年）、当時の皇太子嘉仁親王（後の大正天皇）の山陰行啓に備えて建設された洋風建築で、国の重要文化財に指定されている。設計は宮廷建築家・片山東熊によるフレンチルネサンス様式で、白い外壁と青い屋根が鳥取城跡の緑に映える。内部には螺旋階段や暖炉、豪華な調度品が残り、明治期の近代化と皇室への礼遇を物語る。鳥取藩主・池田家の庭園「仁風閣庭園」とともに市民の憩いの場として親しまれている。
jinfukaku.highlight_en: A chalk Western-style building built in 1900. A state guesthouse built for the Crown Prince (later Emperor Taisho)'s visit to San'in.
jinfukaku.text_en: Jinpukaku is a Western-style building built in 1907 (Meiji 40) in preparation for the visit of the then Crown Prince, Imperial Prince Yoshihito (later Emperor Taisho) to the San'in region, and is designated as a national important cultural property. It was designed in the French Renaissance style by court architect Higashikuma Katayama, and its white exterior walls and blue roof stand out against the greenery of the Tottori Castle ruins. Inside, the spiral staircase, fireplace, and luxurious furniture remain, testifying to the modernization of the Meiji era and the courteous treatment given to the imperial family. Along with Jinpukaku Garden, the garden of the Ikeda family, the lords of the Tottori domain, it is a popular place for citizens to relax.

wakasa_onigajo.name: 若桜鬼ヶ城
wakasa_onigajo.highlight: 標高734mの山頂に築かれた山名氏の要塞。秀吉の因幡侵攻時に最後まで抵抗した難攻不落の山城。
wakasa_onigajo.text: 若桜鬼ヶ城は因幡国の要衝・若桜に山名氏が築いた山城で、標高734メートルの鬼ヶ城山頂に位置する。1580年代、羽柴秀吉の因幡侵攻に際し、山名氏の家臣たちがこの城で抵抗を続けた。急峻な地形を利用した曲輪群と石垣が現在も良好な状態で残り、山陰地方でも有数の中世山城遺構として知られる。城下には江戸時代の商家が残る若桜の古い街並みが保存されており、城下町と山城が一体となった歴史景観を楽しめる。
wakasa_onigajo.highlight_en: A fortress built by the Yamana clan on the summit of a mountain at an altitude of 734m. An impregnable mountain castle that resisted Hideyoshi's invasion of Inaba until the end.
wakasa_onigajo.text_en: Wakasa Onigajo is a mountain castle built by the Yamana clan in Wakasa, a strategic location in Inaba Province, and is located at the top of Mt. Onigajo at an altitude of 734 meters. In the 1580s, vassals of the Yamana clan continued to resist Hideyoshi Hashiba's invasion of Inaba at this castle. The rock formations and stone walls that took advantage of the steep terrain still remain in good condition, and are known as some of the best medieval mountain castle remains in the San'in region. The old townscape of Wakasa, where merchant houses from the Edo period remain, has been preserved in the castle town, and you can enjoy the historic landscape of the castle town and mountain castle integrated into one.

uchihuse_castle.name: 打吹城跡（倉吉）
uchihuse_castle.highlight: 打吹山に築かれた伯耆守護・山名氏の拠点。白壁土蔵群が残る倉吉の城下町を見下ろす。
uchihuse_castle.text: 打吹城は室町時代に伯耆国守護・山名氏が打吹山（標高200m）に築いた山城で、戦国時代には南条氏と毛利氏の争奪戦が繰り広げられた。1580年代に毛利氏が秀吉に屈したことで廃城となったが、山頂には石垣の遺構が残る。城下には江戸時代から続く白壁土蔵群と玉川沿いの街並みが保存されており、重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に指定されている。打吹公園として整備された城山からは倉吉市街地と大山を望む絶景が広がる。
uchihuse_castle.highlight_en: The base of the Yamana clan, the guardian of Hoki, built on Mt. Utsubuki. It overlooks the castle town of Kurayoshi, where a group of white-walled storehouses remains.
uchihuse_castle.text_en: Utsubuki Castle is a mountain castle built on Mt. Utsubuki (200m above sea level) by the Yamana clan, the shugo of Hoki Province, during the Muromachi period, and was the site of a battle between the Nanjo clan and the Mori clan during the Sengoku period. The castle was abandoned in the 1580s when the Mori clan surrendered to Hideyoshi, but the remains of the stone wall remain on the mountaintop. In the castle town, a group of white-walled storehouses and a townscape along the Tamagawa River have been preserved since the Edo period, and it has been designated as an Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings. Shiroyama, which has been developed as Utsubuki Park, offers a spectacular view of Kurayoshi city and Mt. Daisen.

inaba_kokucho.name: 因幡国庁跡
inaba_kokucho.kana: いなばこくちょうあと
inaba_kokucho.highlight: 奈良時代に設置された因幡国の行政の中心地。政庁跡の礎石が発掘され、律令国家の地方支配を伝える。
inaba_kokucho.text: 因幡国庁は奈良時代に因幡国の行政を司るために設けられた国衙（こくが）で、現在の鳥取市国府町付近に位置する。発掘調査により正殿・脇殿・前殿の礎石が確認され、律令制度による地方統治の様子が明らかになっている。周辺には国分寺・国分尼寺の跡もあり、古代因幡国の中心地としての景観が復元されている。国府地区は平安時代の歌人・在原行平が任国として赴いた地ともされ、歌枕「立砂山」などの古代文学との関連も深い。
inaba_kokucho.highlight_en: The administrative center of Inaba Province, established during the Nara period. The foundation stone of the former government office was excavated, and it shows the local control of the Ritsuryo state.
inaba_kokucho.text_en: Inaba Kokucho was a state office established during the Nara period to manage the administration of Inaba Province, and is located near present-day Kokufu-cho, Tottori City. Excavations have confirmed the foundation stones of the main hall, side hall, and front hall, revealing the state of local governance under the Ritsuryo system. There are also ruins of Kokubunji and Kokubun nunnery in the surrounding area, and the landscape as the center of ancient Inaba province has been restored. The Kokufu area is said to be the place where the Heian period poet Yukihira Ariwara went to serve as a state official, and it is also closely related to ancient literature such as the poem ``Tatesanzan.''

oshiro_castle.name: 尾高城跡
oshiro_castle.highlight: 伯耆国の名族・南条氏の居城。毛利氏と尼子氏の争奪戦が繰り広げられた山陰の要衝。
oshiro_castle.text: 尾高城は室町時代に伯耆国の国人領主・南条氏が築いた山城で、山陰地方の政治的要衝に位置する。戦国時代には毛利氏と尼子氏の激しい争奪戦が展開され、南条氏は両勢力の間で巧みに生き残りを図った。城跡には曲輪・堀切・土塁などの遺構が良好に保存されており、中世山城の構造を学べる遺跡として知られる。眼下に広がる弓ヶ浜半島と日本海の眺望も素晴らしく、地元では「尾高の城山」として親しまれている。
oshiro_castle.highlight_en: The residence of the Nanjo clan, a prominent family in Hoki Province. A strategic point in the San'in region where the battle between the Mori clan and the Amago clan took place.
oshiro_castle.text_en: Odaka Castle is a mountain castle built by the Nanjo clan, a local feudal lord of Hoki Province, during the Muromachi period, and is located at a political strategic point in the San'in region. During the Sengoku period, there was a fierce battle between the Mori clan and the Amago clan, and the Nanjo clan skillfully tried to survive between the two powers. The castle ruins have well-preserved remains such as curve rings, horikiri, and earthworks, and are known as ruins where you can learn about the structure of medieval mountain castles. The view of the Yumigahama Peninsula and the Sea of ​​Japan spreading out below is spectacular, and it is affectionately known by locals as ``Odaka's Shiroyama.''

hoki_kodai_hill.name: 伯耆古代の丘公園
hoki_kodai_hill.kana: ほうきこだいのおかこうえん
hoki_kodai_hill.highlight: 弥生〜古墳時代の妻木晩田遺跡を中心とした公園。西日本最大級の弥生集落跡が大山を背景に広がる。
hoki_kodai_hill.text: 伯耆古代の丘公園は、西日本最大級の弥生〜古墳時代の集落遺跡「妻木晩田（むきばんだ）遺跡」を保存・活用した史跡公園だ。海抜90〜170メートルの丘陵地に170棟以上の竪穴住居・掘立柱建物が確認されており、弥生時代後期から古墳時代前期にかけて繁栄した大集落の全貌が明らかになっている。復元住居や展示施設で古代の暮らしを体験でき、晴れた日には大山（伯耆富士）と弓ヶ浜を一望できる絶景の中で古代の息吹を感じられる。
hoki_kodai_hill.highlight_en: A park centered around the Tsumaki Banta ruins from the Yayoi to Kofun periods. The ruins of one of the largest Yayoi villages in western Japan are spread out with Mt. Daisen in the background.
hoki_kodai_hill.text_en: Hoki Ancient Hill Park is a historic park that preserves and utilizes the Tsumaki Mukibanda Ruins, one of the largest settlement ruins from the Yayoi period to the Kofun period in western Japan. More than 170 pit dwellings and dug-out pillared buildings have been confirmed on the hillside between 90 and 170 meters above sea level, revealing the full picture of a large settlement that flourished from the late Yayoi period to the early Kofun period. You can experience ancient life in restored houses and exhibition facilities, and on clear days, you can feel the breath of ancient times in the spectacular view of Mt. Daisen (Hoki Fuji) and Yumigahama Beach.

izumo_taisha.name: 出雲大社
izumo_taisha.highlight: 縁結びの神・大国主大神を祀る日本最古の神社のひとつ。高さ48mの巨大神殿が古代に存在したと伝わる。
izumo_taisha.text: 出雲大社（正式名称：出雲大社）は島根県出雲市に鎮座し、大国主大神（おおくにぬしのかみ）を祀る日本最古の神社のひとつだ。本殿は大社造りと呼ばれる日本最古の神社建築様式で高さ24メートルを誇り、古代には48メートルもの高層神殿があったと伝わる。毎年旧暦10月（神在月）には全国の神々が出雲に集まると信じられ、縁結びの神事が執り行われる。2000年には境内で巨大な柱根が発見され、古代巨大神殿説が実証的に証明されて注目を浴びた。
izumo_taisha.highlight_en: One of the oldest shrines in Japan that enshrines Okuninushi Okami, the god of matchmaking. It is said that a huge temple with a height of 48 meters existed in ancient times.
izumo_taisha.text_en: Izumo Taisha (official name: Izumo Taisha) is located in Izumo City, Shimane Prefecture, and is one of the oldest shrines in Japan that enshrines Okuninushi no Kami. The main shrine is 24 meters high in Japan's oldest shrine architectural style called Taisha-zukuri, and it is said that in ancient times there were temples as high as 48 meters. It is believed that gods from all over the country gather in Izumo in October of the lunar calendar every year, and a matchmaking ritual is held there. In 2000, a huge pillar root was discovered within the temple grounds, and the theory of an ancient giant temple was empirically proven, attracting attention.

iwami_ginzan.name: 石見銀山遺跡
iwami_ginzan.kana: いわみぎんざんいせき
iwami_ginzan.highlight: 世界遺産。16〜17世紀に世界の銀産出量の3分の1を占めた「銀の島」の心臓部。
iwami_ginzan.text: 石見銀山は島根県大田市に位置し、2007年に「石見銀山遺跡とその文化的景観」としてユネスコ世界遺産に登録された。16世紀前半から採掘が始まり、最盛期の17世紀初頭には年間38トン以上の銀を産出し、世界の銀産出量の約3分の1を占めたとされる。この豊富な銀は戦国大名の財政を支え、豊臣秀吉・徳川家康ら天下人が直轄地として争い求めた。坑道（間歩）が600以上残り、代官所跡や商家群とともに江戸時代の鉱山都市の姿を今に伝えている。
iwami_ginzan.highlight_en: world heritage. The heart of the "Silver Island", which accounted for one-third of the world's silver production in the 16th and 17th centuries.
iwami_ginzan.text_en: Iwami Ginzan Ginzan is located in Ota City, Shimane Prefecture, and was registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007 as ``Iwami Ginzan Ruins and Its Cultural Landscape.'' Mining began in the first half of the 16th century, and at its peak in the early 17th century, it was said to have produced more than 38 tons of silver annually, accounting for about one-third of the world's silver production. This rich silver supported the finances of the feudal lords of the Sengoku period, and feudal figures such as Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu sought to claim it as a territory under their direct control. More than 600 mine shafts (passages) remain, and together with the remains of the magistrate's office and a group of merchant houses, it still represents the state of the mining town of the Edo period.

matsue_castle.name: 松江城
matsue_castle.highlight: 現存する12天守のひとつで唯一の国宝山陰の城。宍道湖に映える黒い天守は「千鳥城」の別名を持つ。
matsue_castle.text: 松江城は1611年（慶長16年）に堀尾吉晴が完成させた五層六階の天守を持つ城で、現存する12の天守の中で唯一の国宝として2015年に指定された。「千鳥城」の別名は天守屋根の千鳥破風に由来し、宍道湖（しんじこ）を望む丘の上に黒く聳える姿は山陰随一の景観を誇る。江戸時代には松平氏が10代にわたり藩主を務め、小泉八雲（ラフカディオ・ハーン）が逗留した城下町として近代にも文化的繁栄が続いた。城周辺の堀川では堀川遊覧船が運行される。
matsue_castle.highlight_en: San'in Castle is one of the 12 existing castle towers and is the only national treasure. The black castle tower that stands out against Lake Shinji is also known as ``Chidori Castle''.
matsue_castle.text_en: Matsue Castle is a castle with a five-story, six-story castle tower that was completed by Yoshiharu Horio in 1611 (Keicho 16), and was designated as a national treasure in 2015 as the only one of the 12 existing castle towers. The nickname ``Chidori Castle'' comes from the plover gables on the roof of the castle tower, and its black appearance towering over a hill overlooking Lake Shinji boasts one of the best views in the San'in area. During the Edo period, the Matsudaira clan served as the feudal lord for ten generations, and as a castle town where Yakumo Koizumi (Lafcadio Hearn) stayed, cultural prosperity continued into modern times. Horikawa sightseeing boats operate on the Horikawa River around the castle.

gassantonda_castle.name: 月山富田城跡
gassantonda_castle.kana: がっさんとだじょうあと
gassantonda_castle.highlight: 尼子経久が誇った山陰最大の城塞。毛利元就との死闘の末に落城した「難攻不落の城」。
gassantonda_castle.text: 月山富田城は出雲国守護・尼子氏の居城として戦国時代に山陰随一の大城郭に発展した。尼子経久は1508年に守護大名・京極氏から実権を奪い、出雲・因幡・伯耆など11カ国に及ぶ大勢力を築き上げた。1566年、毛利元就が大軍を率いて3年にわたる包囲を行い、尼子義久はついに降伏開城。この落城により尼子氏は滅亡し、中国地方は毛利氏に統一された。標高183メートルの険峻な山上に曲輪群と石垣が残り、戦国の息吹を今に伝える山城遺跡だ。
gassantonda_castle.highlight_en: The largest fortress in the San'in region, which Tsunehisa Amago was proud of. An ``impregnable castle'' that fell after a deadly battle with Motonari Mori.
gassantonda_castle.text_en: Gassan-Tomida Castle was the residence of the Amago clan, the guardian of Izumo Province, and developed into one of the largest castles in the San'in region during the Sengoku period. In 1508, Tsunehisa Amago usurped real power from the shugo daimyō, the Kyogoku clan, and built up a large power over 11 countries, including Izumo, Inaba, and Hoki. In 1566, Motonari Mori led a large army and carried out a three-year siege, and Yoshihisa Amago finally surrendered and surrendered. As a result of this castle fall, the Amago clan was destroyed, and the Chugoku region was unified by the Mori clan. On a steep mountain at an altitude of 183 meters, Kuruwa groups and stone walls remain, making it a mountain castle ruin that still conveys the spirit of the Sengoku period.

kojindani_site.name: 荒神谷遺跡
kojindani_site.highlight: 1984年に358本の銅剣が一括出土した衝撃の遺跡。日本最多の青銅器埋納遺跡として古代出雲の謎を深める。
kojindani_site.text: 荒神谷遺跡は1984年の発掘調査で358本の銅剣が一括出土し、考古学界に衝撃を与えた。それまで日本全国で見つかっていた弥生時代の銅剣の総数を上回る量が一箇所から発見されたのである。翌年の調査では銅鐸6個・銅矛16本も出土し、古代出雲における青銅器の大量保有と埋納の謎が深まった。これほど大量の青銅器を埋めた理由や目的は現在も解明されておらず、古代出雲王国の存在を示唆するものとして注目を集め続けている。博物館では出土品の複製を展示している。
kojindani_site.highlight_en: A shocking ruin where 358 bronze swords were unearthed in 1984. Deepening the mysteries of ancient Izumo as the site with the largest number of buried bronze wares in Japan.
kojindani_site.text_en: During the 1984 excavation of the Kojindani ruins, a total of 358 bronze swords were unearthed, shocking the archaeological world. The amount of swords found in one place exceeded the total number of Yayoi period bronze swords found all over Japan. In the following year, 6 bronze bells and 16 bronze pikes were also unearthed, deepening the mystery of the large amount of bronze wares possessed and buried in ancient Izumo. The reason and purpose for burying such a large amount of bronze tools is still unknown, and the site continues to attract attention as it suggests the existence of the ancient Izumo Kingdom. The museum displays reproductions of the excavated items.

kamoimakura_site.name: 加茂岩倉遺跡
kamoimakura_site.highlight: 銅鐸39個が一括出土した日本最多の銅鐸出土遺跡。荒神谷と合わせ古代出雲文明の中心地を示す。
kamoimakura_site.text: 加茂岩倉遺跡は1996年の工事中に偶然発見され、銅鐸39個が一括で出土した日本最多の銅鐸出土遺跡だ。出土した銅鐸の中には他の地域の銅鐸と同じ鋳型から作られたものが含まれており、古代の広域交流ネットワークの存在を示唆している。荒神谷遺跡からわずか3.4キロしか離れていないことも注目され、この周辺が古代出雲文明の中核地帯であったことがうかがえる。出雲弥生の森博物館では実物の銅鐸を展示しており、古代人の精神世界に触れることができる。
kamoimakura_site.highlight_en: This is Japan's largest site where 39 bronze bells have been unearthed. Together with Kojin Valley, it marks the center of the ancient Izumo civilization.
kamoimakura_site.text_en: The Kamo Iwakura ruins were discovered by chance during construction in 1996, and 39 bronze bells were unearthed in one go, making it the site with the largest number of bronze bells unearthed in Japan. Some of the excavated dotaku were made from the same molds as dotaku from other regions, suggesting the existence of an ancient wide-area exchange network. It is also noteworthy that it is only 3.4 kilometers away from the Kojindani ruins, indicating that this area was the core area of ​​the ancient Izumo civilization. The Izumo Yayoi Forest Museum exhibits actual bronze bells, allowing you to experience the spiritual world of ancient people.

oki_gotoba_haihonchi.name: 隠岐・後鳥羽上皇御配流地
oki_gotoba_haihonchi.kana: おきごとばじょうこうおはいりゅうち
oki_gotoba_haihonchi.highlight: 承久の乱に敗れた後鳥羽上皇が19年間を過ごした流刑地。島に今も残る御火葬塚が上皇の波乱の生涯を伝える。
oki_gotoba_haihonchi.text: 1221年（承久3年）の承久の乱で鎌倉幕府に敗れた後鳥羽上皇は、隠岐国（現在の島根県隠岐郡）に配流された。上皇は隠岐に渡ったのち19年間この島で過ごし、1239年に60歳で崩御した。「ももしきや古き軒端のしのぶにも　なほあまりある昔なりけり」と詠んだ百人一首の一首は隠岐での失意を映すとされる。後鳥羽院の御火葬塚は現在の西ノ島に残り、島の人々に大切に守られてきた。隠岐は後醍醐天皇も一時流された島で、鎌倉〜南北朝時代の政争と切り離せない地だ。
oki_gotoba_haihonchi.highlight_en: This is the penal colony where Retired Emperor Gotoba spent 19 years after being defeated in the Jokyu War. The cremation mound that still remains on the island tells the story of the retired emperor's turbulent life.
oki_gotoba_haihonchi.text_en: Retired Emperor Gotoba, who was defeated by the Kamakura shogunate in the Jokyu War in 1221, was exiled to Oki Province (present-day Oki District, Shimane Prefecture). After the retired emperor went to Oki, he lived on this island for 19 years and passed away in 1239 at the age of 60. The Hyakunin Isshu poem, which reads, ``Even in Momoshiki and the Shinobu of the Old Eaves, there are so many old stories'' is said to reflect the disappointment at Oki. The Gotoba-in cremation mound remains on present-day Nishinoshima and has been carefully protected by the people of the island. Oki is the island where Emperor Go-Daigo was exiled for a time, and is an area inseparable from the political strife between Kamakura and the Nanbokucho period.

wanibuchi_temple.name: 鰐淵寺
wanibuchi_temple.highlight: 594年創建と伝わる天台宗の古刹。武蔵坊弁慶が修行したとされる出雲の秘境に佇む古代霊場。
wanibuchi_temple.text: 鰐淵寺は594年（推古天皇2年）に智春上人が開基したと伝わる出雲の古刹で、天台宗に属する。平安時代末期には武蔵坊弁慶がこの寺で修行したという伝承があり、弁慶伝説ゆかりの地として知られる。境内には国の重要文化財に指定された蔵王堂（室町時代）をはじめ、摩尼輪塔・文殊堂などの古建築が残る。険しい渓谷の奥に位置し、苔むした石段と鬱蒼たる杉木立が醸す雰囲気は霊場にふさわしい神秘的な空間だ。
wanibuchi_temple.highlight_en: An ancient temple of the Tendai sect, said to have been founded in 594. An ancient sacred site located in an unexplored area of ​​Izumo where Musashibo Benkei is said to have trained.
wanibuchi_temple.text_en: Wanibuchi-ji Temple is an ancient temple in Izumo that is said to have been founded in 594 (the second year of Emperor Suiko's reign) by the priest Tomoharu, and belongs to the Tendai sect. There is a legend that Musashibo Benkei trained at this temple at the end of the Heian period, and it is known as the place associated with the legend of Benkei. Within the precincts, there are old buildings such as Zao-do (Muromachi period), which has been designated as a national important cultural property, as well as Mani Ring Pagoda and Monju-do. Located deep in a steep valley, the moss-covered stone steps and dense cedar trees create a mystical atmosphere befitting a sacred place.

izumo_kokucho.name: 出雲国庁跡
izumo_kokucho.kana: いずもこくちょうあと
izumo_kokucho.highlight: 律令時代に出雲国を統治した国庁（国衙）の跡地。正殿・脇殿の礎石が発掘され古代地方行政の中枢が判明した。
izumo_kokucho.text: 出雲国庁跡は現在の松江市大草町付近に位置し、奈良時代から平安時代にかけて出雲国の行政を担った国衙（こくが）の跡地だ。発掘調査により正殿・脇殿・後殿の礎石配置が明らかになり、律令制国家の地方統治機構の実態が解明された。出雲国は古代から大和朝廷との深いつながりを持ち、出雲大社の神官（国造）と国司が並立する独特の政治体制が続いた。周辺には意宇郡の中心地として栄えた古代寺院・神社の遺構が集中しており、古代出雲文化の核心地帯を形成している。
izumo_kokucho.highlight_en: This is the site of the National Government Office (Kokuga) that ruled Izumo Province during the Ritsuryo period. The foundation stones of the main hall and side hall were excavated, revealing the center of ancient local administration.
izumo_kokucho.text_en: The Izumo National Government Office Ruins is located near present-day Okusa-cho, Matsue City, and is the site of the Kokuga, which was responsible for the administration of Izumo Province from the Nara period to the Heian period. The excavation revealed the layout of the foundation stones of the main hall, side hall, and back hall, and the actual situation of the local governance structure of the Ritsuryo system was clarified. Izumo Province has had deep ties with the Yamato court since ancient times, and has had a unique political system in which the priests of Izumo Taisha Shrine (Kunizo) and the Kokushi coexisted. In the surrounding area, the remains of ancient temples and shrines that flourished as the center of Iu County are concentrated, forming the core area of ​​ancient Izumo culture.

masuda_nanajo_castle.name: 益田氏の七尾城跡
masuda_nanajo_castle.kana: ますだしのななおじょうあと
masuda_nanajo_castle.highlight: 石見の豪族・益田氏の本拠。七尾山に築かれた堅城で毛利氏の西国制覇に貢献した武将たちを輩出した。
masuda_nanajo_castle.text: 七尾城は石見国（現島根県益田市）の豪族・益田氏が七尾山に築いた山城で、戦国時代の山陰・山陽を結ぶ要衝に位置した。益田氏は毛利元就に臣従し、西国での毛利氏の勢力拡大を支えた。城跡には曲輪・堀切・石垣が良好に残り、山頂からは日本海と益田平野を一望できる。益田市内には益田氏の菩提寺・医光寺（雪舟が庭を作ったと伝わる）や万福寺など、室町文化の薫りを残す名刹が点在し、文化人としての側面を持った武将文化が花開いた地でもある。
masuda_nanajo_castle.highlight_en: The headquarters of the powerful Masuda clan of Iwami. The castle was built on Mt. Nanao and produced military commanders who contributed to the Mori clan's conquest of the western regions.
masuda_nanajo_castle.text_en: Nanao Castle was a mountain castle built on Mt. Nanao by the Masuda clan, a powerful clan from Iwami Province (present-day Masuda City, Shimane Prefecture), and was located at a strategic point connecting San'in and Sanyo during the Sengoku period. The Masuda clan served Motonari Mori as a vassal and supported the expansion of the Mori clan's influence in the western regions. The castle ruins have well-remained walls, horikiri, and stone walls, and from the top of the mountain, you can see the Sea of ​​Japan and the Masuda Plain. Masuda City is dotted with famous temples that retain the flavor of Muromachi culture, such as the Masuda clan's family temple, Ikoji Temple (where Sesshu is said to have built a garden), and Manpukuji Temple, and it is also a place where the culture of military commanders with cultural aspects flourished.

bitchu_matsuyama.name: 備中松山城
bitchu_matsuyama.kana: びっちゅうまつやまじょう
bitchu_matsuyama.highlight: 現存天守の中で唯一の山城。標高430mの天守から雲海に浮かぶ光景は「天空の城」と呼ばれる絶景だ。
bitchu_matsuyama.text: 備中松山城は岡山県高梁市の臥牛山（標高430メートル）山頂に建つ、現存する唯一の山城天守を持つ城だ。鎌倉時代の築城から数百年の歴史を持ち、現存する天守は17世紀後半に水谷勝宗が再建したもの。秋から冬の早朝には雲海が城を覆い、「天空の城」とも呼ばれる幻想的な光景が広がる。明治維新後に廃城となり荒廃したが、1929年に旧藩士・川上俊彦が私財を投じて修復。板野友仁ら有識者の尽力で国の重要文化財に指定され現在に至る。
bitchu_matsuyama.highlight_en: The only mountain castle among the existing castle towers. The sight of floating in a sea of ​​clouds from the castle tower at an altitude of 430m is a spectacular view that is called ``Castle in the Sky.''
bitchu_matsuyama.text_en: Bitchu Matsuyama Castle is the only castle in existence with a mountain castle tower, built on the summit of Mt. Gagyu (430 meters above sea level) in Takahashi City, Okayama Prefecture. It has a history of several hundred years since it was built in the Kamakura period, and the current castle tower was rebuilt by Katsumune Mizutani in the late 17th century. In the early mornings from autumn to winter, a sea of ​​clouds covers the castle, creating a fantastic sight that is also known as the ``castle in the sky.'' After the Meiji Restoration, the castle was abandoned and fell into disrepair, but in 1929, Toshihiko Kawakami, a former samurai, invested his personal funds to restore it. Thanks to the efforts of Tomohito Itano and other experts, it has been designated as a national important cultural property.

okayama_castle.name: 岡山城
okayama_castle.highlight: 宇喜多秀家が築いた黒い天守「烏城」。岡山後楽園と並び城下町岡山のシンボル。
okayama_castle.text: 岡山城は1597年（慶長2年）に宇喜多秀家が完成させた城で、黒塗りの下見板張りの外壁から「烏城（うじょう）」の別名を持つ。豊臣秀吉の寵愛を受けた宇喜多秀家は岡山城を豪華な城に整備したが、関ヶ原の戦いで西軍に属して敗れ八丈島に流罪となった。その後は小早川秀秋・池田氏が城主となり、池田光政の代に隣接する後楽園が造営された。戦時中の空襲で天守は焼失したが1966年に復元。2022年にリニューアルされた城内展示は充実した内容を誇る。
okayama_castle.highlight_en: Karasu Castle, a black castle tower built by Hideie Ukita. Along with Okayama Korakuen, it is a symbol of the castle town of Okayama.
okayama_castle.text_en: Okayama Castle was completed in 1597 by Hideie Ukita, and is also known as ``Crow Castle'' due to its black clapboard exterior walls. Hideie Ukita, who was favored by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, built Okayama Castle into a luxurious castle, but was defeated by the Western army at the Battle of Sekigahara and exiled to Hachijojima. After that, Hideaki Kobayakawa and the Ikeda clan became the lords of the castle, and the adjacent Korakuen was built during the reign of Mitsumasa Ikeda. The castle tower was destroyed by air raids during the war, but was restored in 1966. The castle exhibits, which were renewed in 2022, boast a rich content.

tsuyama_castle.name: 津山城跡（鶴山公園）
tsuyama_castle.highlight: 森忠政が築いた全国屈指の巨大石垣群を持つ平山城。日本三大平山城のひとつで桜の名所としても名高い。
tsuyama_castle.text: 津山城は1616年（元和2年）に森忠政が完成させた城で、鶴山（かくざん）の山上に数段に積み上げられた石垣群が壮観だ。江戸時代初期の築城技術の粋を集めた石垣の総延長は約1.5キロメートルにも及び、日本三大平山城のひとつに数えられる。明治の廃城令で天守は取り壊されたが、石垣と堀は良好に保存されており、春には約1000本の桜が城跡を彩る「日本さくら名所100選」の名所でもある。津山は江戸時代に蘭学が盛んな地としても知られ、宇田川玄随・箕作阮甫ら著名な蘭学者を輩出した。
tsuyama_castle.highlight_en: Hirayama Castle was built by Tadamasa Mori and has one of the largest stone walls in Japan. It is one of Japan's three major Hirayama castles and is also famous for its cherry blossom viewing.
tsuyama_castle.text_en: Tsuyama Castle was completed by Tadamasa Mori in 1616 (Genna 2), and the stone walls built in several tiers on top of Mt. Tsuru are spectacular. The total length of the stone wall, which is a collection of the best castle construction techniques from the early Edo period, is about 1.5 kilometers, and it is counted as one of the three great flat mountain castles in Japan. Although the castle tower was demolished under the Meiji era castle abolition ordinance, the stone walls and moat have been well preserved, and in spring, about 1,000 cherry blossom trees decorate the castle ruins, making it one of Japan's top 100 cherry blossom viewing spots. Tsuyama was also known as a place where Dutch studies flourished during the Edo period, producing famous Dutch scholars such as Genzui Udagawa and Natsuho Mitsukuri.

kibitsu_shrine.name: 吉備津神社
kibitsu_shrine.highlight: 日本唯一の比翼入母屋造り本殿（吉備津造り）を持つ古社。桃太郎伝説・温羅退治の舞台となった備前の大社。
kibitsu_shrine.text: 吉備津神社は岡山県岡山市北区に鎮座し、大吉備津彦命（おおきびつひこのみこと）を主祭神とする古社だ。室町時代初期に建立された本殿は「吉備津造り（比翼入母屋造り）」と呼ばれる日本唯一の建築様式で国宝に指定されている。大吉備津彦命は温羅（うら）という鬼を退治したとされ、この伝説が桃太郎伝説の原型とも言われる。全長360メートルの廻廊（重要文化財）は圧巻で、鳴釜神事（鑑定の神事）も有名だ。吉備路一帯には古代吉備王国の遺跡が集中している。
kibitsu_shrine.highlight_en: An old shrine with Japan's only Hiyo-irimoya-style main hall (Kibitsu-zukuri style). Bizen Taisha is the setting for the legend of Momotaro and the defeat of Ura.
kibitsu_shrine.text_en: Kibitsu Shrine is located in Kita Ward, Okayama City, Okayama Prefecture, and is an old shrine whose main deity is Okibitsuhiko no Mikoto. The main shrine, built in the early Muromachi period, is a unique architectural style in Japan called Kibitsu-zukuri (hiyoku-irimoya-zukuri), and has been designated as a national treasure. Daikibitsuhiko-no-Mikoto is said to have exterminated a demon called Ura, and this legend is said to be the origin of the Momotaro legend. The 360-meter-long corridor (an important cultural property) is a sight to behold, and the Narukama Shinto ritual (appraisal ritual) is also famous. The ruins of the ancient Kibi Kingdom are concentrated in the Kibiji area.

oni_no_shiro.name: 鬼ノ城

transit.name: 鬼城山ビジターセンター

oni_no_shiro.highlight: 白村江の戦い後に築かれた古代の朝鮮式山城。西門が復元された標高400mの謎の巨大城塞。
oni_no_shiro.text: 鬼ノ城は岡山県総社市の鬼城山（標高397メートル）に築かれた古代の山城で、663年の白村江の戦いで唐・新羅に敗れた後、朝廷が防衛のために築いた「朝鮮式山城」のひとつと考えられている。文献に記録がなく、いつ誰が築いたか明確ではない「幻の城」として知られる。総延長2.8キロメートルの城壁が山の稜線を巡り、4カ所の城門跡・水門跡・建物礎石などが発掘されている。復元された西門の雄姿は壮観で、遠く瀬戸内海まで見渡せる眺望も素晴らしい。温羅（鬼）の居城という伝説もある。
oni_no_shiro.highlight_en: An ancient Korean-style mountain fortress built after the Battle of Hakuchogang. A mysterious giant fortress at an altitude of 400m with a restored west gate.
oni_no_shiro.text_en: Kinojo Castle is an ancient mountain castle built on Mt. Onishiro (397 meters above sea level) in Soja City, Okayama Prefecture, and is considered to be one of the ``Korean-style mountain castles'' built by the Imperial Court for defense after it was defeated by Tang and Silla at the Battle of Hakusonko in 663. It is known as a ``phantom castle,'' as there is no written record of it, and it is unclear when and by whom it was built. A castle wall with a total length of 2.8 kilometers wraps around the ridgeline of the mountain, and the remains of four castle gates, water gates, and building foundation stones have been excavated. The restored west gate is spectacular, and the view that extends all the way to the Seto Inland Sea is also wonderful. There is also a legend that it is the residence of Ura (a demon).

takamatsu_castle_siege.name: 高松城跡（水攻め）
takamatsu_castle_siege.highlight: 羽柴秀吉が仕掛けた「水攻め」の舞台。一夜にして平城を海に沈めた奇策は本能寺の変の急報と重なった。
takamatsu_castle_siege.text: 備中高松城は毛利氏の支城として重要な役割を果たした平城で、沼地に囲まれた難攻不落の要塞だった。1582年、羽柴秀吉は正攻法では攻め落とせないと判断し、周囲に全長3キロを超える堤防を築いて近隣の川の水を引き込む「水攻め」を敢行。城はまたたく間に水没し、守将・清水宗治は孤立した。まさにこの時、主君・織田信長が本能寺の変で横死する報が届いた。秀吉は毛利方と即座に講和交渉を進め、清水宗治の切腹で和議が成立。その後秀吉は「中国大返し」で光秀討伐に向かった。
takamatsu_castle_siege.highlight_en: The stage for the ``water attack'' set up by Hideyoshi Hashiba. The ingenious plan to sink Heijo into the sea overnight coincided with the breaking news of the Honnoji Incident.
takamatsu_castle_siege.text_en: Bitchu Takamatsu Castle was a flat castle that played an important role as a branch castle of the Mori clan, and was an impregnable fortress surrounded by marshes. In 1582, Hideyoshi Hashiba decided that he could not conquer the area by direct attack, so he carried out a ``water attack'' by building an embankment over 3 km long around the area and drawing in water from nearby rivers. The castle was submerged in water in an instant, and the garrison, Muneharu Shimizu, was left alone. Just at this time, news arrived that his lord, Oda Nobunaga, had died in the Honnoji Incident. Hideyoshi immediately proceeded with peace negotiations with the Mori side, and a peace agreement was reached through Muneharu Shimizu's seppuku. After that, Hideyoshi set out to subjugate Mitsuhide with a ``Great Return to China.''

tsukuriyama_kofun.name: 造山古墳
tsukuriyama_kofun.highlight: 全長350mで日本第4位の前方後円墳。宮内庁管轄外のため自由に登ることができる古墳時代最大級の陵墓。
tsukuriyama_kofun.text: 造山古墳は全長350メートルを誇る5世紀前半の前方後円墳で、日本第4位の規模を持つ巨大古墳だ。大仙陵古墳（仁徳天皇陵）などの天皇陵とは異なり宮内庁の管轄外であるため、実際に古墳に登って内部の石室や墳丘の雰囲気を体感できる全国でも珍しい古墳として知られる。周辺にも複数の陪塚（ばいちょう）が残り、古代吉備王国の王がここに眠ったと考えられている。吉備王国は大和王権に匹敵する勢力を持ったとされ、その最高権力者の墓がこの造山古墳だったと推定される。
tsukuriyama_kofun.highlight_en: The 4th largest keyhole-shaped tumulus in Japan with a total length of 350m. One of the largest mausoleums of the Kofun period, which is outside the jurisdiction of the Imperial Household Agency and can be climbed freely.
tsukuriyama_kofun.text_en: Zoriyama Kofun is a keyhole-shaped tumulus dating back to the first half of the 5th century with a total length of 350 meters, making it the fourth largest tumulus in Japan. Unlike imperial tombs such as the Daisenryo Tumulus (Emperor Nintoku's Mausoleum), it is outside the jurisdiction of the Imperial Household Agency, so it is known as a rare tumulus in Japan where you can actually climb into the tumulus and experience the atmosphere of the stone chambers and mound inside. Several mounds remain in the surrounding area, and it is believed that the king of the ancient Kibi Kingdom was buried here. The Kibi Kingdom is said to have had a power comparable to the Yamato Dynasty, and it is presumed that the tomb of its most powerful person was this Zoriyama Tumulus.

bizen_kokubunji.name: 備前国分寺跡
bizen_kokubunji.kana: びぜんこくぶんじあと
bizen_kokubunji.highlight: 聖武天皇の詔により全国に建立された国分寺の備前国版。七重塔心礎が残り古代国家の仏教行政の規模を伝える。
bizen_kokubunji.text: 備前国分寺は741年（天平13年）の聖武天皇の詔によって全国に建立された官寺のひとつで、現在の岡山市北区一宮に位置する。発掘調査で七重塔の心礎（礎石）が確認されており、奈良の東大寺に次ぐ規模の伽藍配置が復元されている。吉備路サイクリングコースの途中に位置し、吉備津神社・造山古墳・鬼ノ城とともに古代吉備王国の遺跡群を構成する。現在も「備前国分寺」として法灯が継承されており、境内には奈良時代の礎石が残る。
bizen_kokubunji.highlight_en: Bizen Province's version of Kokubunji temples built across the country by Emperor Shomu's edict. The core foundation of the seven-storied pagoda remains, showing the scale of Buddhist administration in the ancient state.
bizen_kokubunji.text_en: Bizen Kokubunji is one of the official temples built across the country by Emperor Shomu's edict in 741, and is located in present-day Ichinomiya, Kita Ward, Okayama City. The foundation stone of the seven-storied pagoda has been confirmed during excavations, and the layout of the temple has been restored, making it the second largest temple after Todaiji Temple in Nara. Located in the middle of the Kibiji cycling course, it forms part of the ruins of the ancient Kibi Kingdom, along with Kibitsu Shrine, Zozan Kofun, and Kinojo Castle. The lantern has been passed down to this day as ``Bizen Kokubunji,'' and the foundation stones from the Nara period remain within the temple grounds.

ashimori_jinya.name: 足守藩陣屋跡
ashimori_jinya.kana: あしもりはんじんやあと
ashimori_jinya.highlight: 豊臣秀吉の正妻・北政所の兄・木下家定を祖とする小藩。白壁の商家と武家屋敷が残る岡山の小京都。
ashimori_jinya.text: 足守藩は豊臣秀吉の正妻・北政所（ねね）の兄・木下家定を藩祖とする2万5千石の小藩で、現在の岡山市北区足守に陣屋が置かれた。江戸時代を通じて木下氏が藩主を務め、陣屋周辺には今も白壁の商家・武家屋敷・用水路が当時の面影を残す。旧足守藩侍屋敷（重要文化財）や近水園（日本庭園）も残り、古い街並みとともに「岡山の小京都」として親しまれている。江戸時代の蘭学者・緒方洪庵（適塾を開いた医師）はこの足守の出身だ。
ashimori_jinya.highlight_en: A small domain whose founder was Kinoshita Iesada, the older brother of Kita no Mandokoro, the legal wife of Toyotomi Hideyoshi. Little Kyoto in Okayama where white-walled merchant houses and samurai residences remain.
ashimori_jinya.text_en: The Ashimori clan was a small domain of 25,000 koku whose founder was Kinoshita Iesada, the older brother of Toyotomi Hideyoshi's legal wife Nene Kita no Mandokoro.The clan was located in what is now Ashimori, Kita Ward, Okayama City. Throughout the Edo period, the Kinoshita clan served as the lord of the domain, and the area around the Jinya still retains traces of those days, including white-walled merchant houses, samurai residences, and irrigation canals. The former Ashimori clan samurai residence (an important cultural property) and Kinsuien (Japanese garden) remain, and along with the old townscape, it is affectionately known as ``Okayama's Little Kyoto.'' Koan Ogata, a Dutch scholar from the Edo period (a doctor who opened Tekijuku), was from this area.

itsukushima_shrine.name: 厳島神社
itsukushima_shrine.highlight: 世界遺産・海上に浮かぶ大鳥居。平清盛が造営した平家ゆかりの神社は潮が満ちると社殿が海に浮かぶ。
itsukushima_shrine.text: 厳島神社は広島県廿日市市宮島（厳島）に鎮座し、593年に佐伯鞍職が創建したと伝わる古社だ。現在の壮麗な社殿群は1168年に平清盛が造営したもので、平安貴族文化の美意識を体現した寝殿造りの建築が海上に展開する独特の景観を誇る。満潮時には社殿が海に浮かぶように見え、高さ16メートルの大鳥居が海中に立つ光景は日本三景のひとつに数えられる絶景だ。1996年にユネスコ世界遺産に登録され、国内外から年間400万人以上が訪れる。嚴島合戦（1555年）では毛利元就が陶晴賢を奇襲で破った戦場でもある。
itsukushima_shrine.highlight_en: A world heritage site, the large torii gate floating on the sea. The shrine built by Taira no Kiyomori and associated with the Heike clan floats on the sea when the tide is high.
itsukushima_shrine.text_en: Itsukushima Shrine is an ancient shrine located on Miyajima (Itsukushima) in Hatsukaichi City, Hiroshima Prefecture, and is said to have been founded by Saeki Kurashiki in 593. The current magnificent group of shrine buildings was built by Taira no Kiyomori in 1168, and boasts a unique landscape of Shinden-zukuri architecture, which embodies the aesthetic sense of Heian aristocratic culture, stretching out over the sea. At high tide, the shrine building appears to be floating on the sea, and the sight of the 16-meter-tall torii gate standing in the water is a spectacular sight that ranks as one of Japan's three most scenic views. It was registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996, and more than 4 million people visit from Japan and abroad every year. It was also the battlefield where Mori Motonari defeated Sue Harukata in a surprise attack during the Battle of Itsukushima (1555).

hiroshima_peace_dome.name: 原爆ドーム（広島平和記念碑）
hiroshima_peace_dome.highlight: 世界遺産。1945年8月6日の原爆投下で奇跡的に外壁が残った建物。核廃絶と平和を訴え続ける人類の記憶遺産。
hiroshima_peace_dome.text: 原爆ドームはもともと1915年にチェコ人建築家ヤン・レツルが設計した広島県産業奨励館として建設された。1945年8月6日午前8時15分、人類史上初めて戦争で使用された原子爆弾が爆心地から約160メートル上空で炸裂し、建物の鉄骨と外壁の一部が奇跡的に残存した。戦後、この廃墟を核廃絶・恒久平和の象徴として保存する運動が高まり、1996年にユネスコ世界遺産に登録された。毎年8月6日には平和記念式典が近隣の広島平和記念公園で行われ、世界に向けて不戦の誓いが発せられる。
hiroshima_peace_dome.highlight_en: world heritage. Miraculously, the outer walls of this building remained intact after the atomic bomb was dropped on August 6, 1945. A memory of humanity that continues to advocate for nuclear abolition and peace.
hiroshima_peace_dome.text_en: The Atomic Bomb Dome was originally built in 1915 as the Hiroshima Prefectural Industrial Promotion Hall, designed by Czech architect Jan Letzl. At 8:15 a.m. on August 6, 1945, the first atomic bomb used in war in human history exploded approximately 160 meters above ground zero, and miraculously the steel frame and part of the building's exterior walls survived. After the war, a movement to preserve the ruins as a symbol of nuclear abolition and permanent peace grew, and in 1996 it was registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Every year on August 6th, a peace commemorative ceremony is held at nearby Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park, where a pledge of no war is issued to the world.

hiroshima_castle.name: 広島城
hiroshima_castle.highlight: 毛利輝元が築いた三角州の城「鯉城」。原爆で倒壊するも復元された五層天守からは広島市街を一望できる。
hiroshima_castle.text: 広島城は1589年（天正17年）に毛利輝元が太田川デルタ（三角州）上に築いた平城で、「鯉城（りじょう）」の愛称を持つ。関ヶ原後に福島正則・浅野氏が城主となり、広島藩の政治的中心として繁栄した。1945年8月6日の原子爆弾投下により天守を含む建物の大部分が倒壊・焼失したが、1958年に外観復元された天守が建てられ、現在は歴史博物館として公開されている。原爆投下の記憶と江戸時代の城郭文化が重なり合う場所として、平和学習の拠点にもなっている。
hiroshima_castle.highlight_en: Koi Castle is a delta castle built by Terumoto Mori. The five-story castle tower, which was destroyed by the atomic bomb but has been restored, offers a panoramic view of Hiroshima city.
hiroshima_castle.text_en: Hiroshima Castle is a flat castle built by Mori Terumoto on the Otagawa delta in 1589 (Tensho 17), and is nicknamed ``Carp Castle.'' After Sekigahara, Masanori Fukushima and the Asano clan became the lords of the castle, and it prospered as the political center of the Hiroshima domain. Most of the buildings, including the castle tower, collapsed and burned down when the atomic bomb was dropped on August 6, 1945, but a restored castle tower was built in 1958, and is now open to the public as a historical museum. As a place where memories of the atomic bombing and castle culture of the Edo period overlap, it is also a base for peace studies.

yoshida_koriyama_castle.name: 吉田郡山城跡
yoshida_koriyama_castle.kana: よしだこおりやまじょうあと
yoshida_koriyama_castle.highlight: 毛利元就が本拠とした中国地方制覇の出発点。270超の曲輪を持つ巨大山城から元就が天下を狙った。
yoshida_koriyama_castle.text: 吉田郡山城は広島県安芸高田市に位置し、毛利氏の居城として中国地方の歴史の中核を担った山城だ。毛利元就はこの城を本拠として「三本の矢」の教えで知られる堅固な一族団結の政治を行い、尼子氏・大内氏という二大勢力の間で巧みに生き延びた。やがて大内氏の内紛（陶晴賢の謀反）を利用して勢力を拡大し、1566年に尼子氏を滅ぼして中国地方8カ国を制覇した。山頂から中腹にかけて270を超える曲輪が連なる大規模な山城遺構は圧巻で、毛利博物館と合わせて元就の生涯を詳しく学べる。
yoshida_koriyama_castle.highlight_en: Motonari Mori's base was the starting point for conquering the Chugoku region. Motonari aimed at the world from a gigantic mountain castle with over 270 curved wheels.
yoshida_koriyama_castle.text_en: Yoshida Koriyama Castle is located in Akitakada City, Hiroshima Prefecture, and is a mountain castle that played a central role in the history of the Chugoku region as the residence of the Mori clan. Motonari Mori used this castle as his base and practiced politics of solid clan unity, known as the teaching of the ``Three Arrows,'' and skillfully survived between the two major factions, the Amago clan and the Ouchi clan. Eventually, they expanded their power by taking advantage of the internal conflict within the Ouchi clan (Sue Harukata's rebellion), and in 1566, they destroyed the Amago clan and conquered eight countries in the Chugoku region. The large-scale ruins of the mountain castle, with more than 270 rock formations stretching from the summit to the middle of the mountain, are impressive, and together with the Mori Museum, you can learn more about Motonari's life.

tomonoura.name: 鞆の浦
tomonoura.highlight: 「潮待ちの港」として栄えた万葉の時代からの港町。坂本龍馬が藩船を砲撃されたいろは丸事件の舞台。
tomonoura.text: 鞆の浦は広島県福山市に位置し、瀬戸内海の潮流の要衝として万葉の時代から「潮待ちの港」として栄えた港町だ。室町幕府の15代将軍・足利義昭が信長に追われて毛利氏を頼り、この地に仮の幕府を開いたことでも知られる。江戸時代には朝鮮通信使が立ち寄る国際的な港として繁栄し、雁木・常夜灯・波止・焚場など江戸時代の港湾施設が今も完全な形で残る全国唯一の場所だ。1867年には坂本龍馬の海援隊の船・いろは丸が紀州藩船と衝突した「いろは丸事件」の舞台となり、龍馬が談判を行った場所としても有名だ。
tomonoura.highlight_en: A port town that has flourished since the Manyo era as a "port waiting for the tide." The scene of the Iroha Maru incident in which Ryoma Sakamoto's clan ship was shelled.
tomonoura.text_en: Tomonoura, located in Fukuyama City, Hiroshima Prefecture, is a port town that flourished as a ``port waiting for the tide'' since the Manyo era as a key point for the tidal currents of the Seto Inland Sea. It is also known that Yoshiaki Ashikaga, the 15th shogun of the Muromachi shogunate, relied on the Mori clan and opened a temporary shogunate in this area after being chased by Nobunaga. During the Edo period, it flourished as an international port where Korean envoys stopped by, and it is the only place in Japan where Edo period port facilities such as gangi, night lights, wharves, and fire pits still remain intact. In 1867, it was the scene of the Irohamaru Incident, in which Ryoma Sakamoto's Kaientai ship Irohamaru collided with a Kishu clan ship, and it is also famous as the place where Ryoma held negotiations.

fukuyama_castle.name: 福山城
fukuyama_castle.highlight: 日本で最後に建てられた幕府公認の大規模城郭。北面に鉄板を張った防御建築は現存最古の実例。
fukuyama_castle.text: 福山城は1622年（元和8年）に初代福山藩主・水野勝成が築いた城で、幕府直轄の大規模城郭として西日本支配の拠点となった。天守北側の壁面に鉄板を張り付けた防御構造は現存最古の例として知られ、国の重要文化財に指定されている。江戸幕府が最後に建設を許可した大城郭でもあり、石垣・堀・複数の現存建物が良好に残る。2022年に天守が大規模修理され、鉄板張りが復元されて往時の黒光りする北面の姿が蘇った。福山駅から徒歩3分という抜群のアクセスも魅力だ。
fukuyama_castle.highlight_en: The last large-scale castle officially recognized by the Shogunate built in Japan. The defensive building with iron plates on the north side is the oldest example still in existence.
fukuyama_castle.text_en: Fukuyama Castle was built in 1622 by Katsunari Mizuno, the first lord of the Fukuyama domain, and was a large-scale castle under the direct control of the Shogunate that served as a base for domination of western Japan. The defensive structure with iron plates attached to the north wall of the castle tower is known as the oldest existing example and has been designated as a national important cultural property. It was also the last large castle that the Edo Shogunate allowed construction of, and the stone walls, moat, and several existing buildings remain in good condition. In 2022, the castle tower underwent a large-scale repair, and the iron plating was restored, bringing back the black, shiny north face of the past. Another appeal is the excellent access, just a 3-minute walk from Fukuyama Station.

onomichi_jodoji.name: 尾道・浄土寺
onomichi_jodoji.highlight: 高僧・空海（弘法大師）ゆかりの寺。国宝の本堂・多宝塔が残り坂と寺の町・尾道を代表する古刹。
onomichi_jodoji.text: 浄土寺は616年に聖徳太子が創建したと伝わり、弘法大師空海も訪れた由緒ある古刹だ。鎌倉時代後期に再建された本堂と室町時代の多宝塔はいずれも国宝に指定されており、中世建築の粋を今に伝える。寺は尾道の斜面に建ち、眼下に尾道水道と向島を望む絶景が広がる。坂の多い尾道は多くの文人・映画監督に愛され、林芙美子・志賀直哉・小津安二郎らが愛した文化の薫る港町として知られる。浄土寺は尾道の景観を語る上で欠かせない存在だ。
onomichi_jodoji.highlight_en: A temple associated with the high priest Kukai (Kobo Daishi). An ancient temple whose main hall and Tahoto pagoda, which is a national treasure, is representative of Onomichi, a town of remaining slopes and temples.
onomichi_jodoji.text_en: Jodo-ji Temple is said to have been founded by Prince Shotoku in 616, and is an ancient temple that was even visited by Kobo Daishi Kukai. The main hall, which was rebuilt in the late Kamakura period, and the Tahoto pagoda, which dates back to the Muromachi period, have both been designated as national treasures, and still represent the essence of medieval architecture. The temple is built on the slope of Onomichi, with a spectacular view of the Onomichi Channel and Mukojima Island below. Onomichi, with its many hills, is known as a culturally rich port town that has been loved by many literary figures and film directors, including Fumiko Hayashi, Naoya Shiga, and Yasujiro Ozu. Jodoji Temple is an essential part of Onomichi's landscape.

mihara_castle.name: 三原城跡
mihara_castle.highlight: 毛利氏の水軍城。海に浮かんでいたことから「浮き城」と呼ばれた城で、三原駅のホームが本丸跡に重なる。
mihara_castle.text: 三原城は1567年（永禄10年）に毛利元就の三男・小早川隆景が瀬戸内海に突き出た小島を利用して築いた「浮き城」だ。海に囲まれた立地を活かした水軍城として毛利水軍の根拠地となり、豊臣秀吉の朝鮮出兵（文禄・慶長の役）でも重要な役割を担った。現在は三原駅の改良工事で本丸跡の大部分が駅のホームや線路となっており、駅構内に石垣が残るという全国でも珍しい「駅の中の城跡」となっている。天守台の石垣は良好に残り、往時の規模の大きさを今に伝える。
mihara_castle.highlight_en: The Mouri clan's naval castle. The castle was called the ``floating castle'' because it was floating on the sea, and the platform of Mihara Station overlaps with the ruins of the main castle.
mihara_castle.text_en: Mihara Castle is a floating castle built in 1567 by Takakage Kobayakawa, the third son of Mori Motonari, on a small island jutting out into the Seto Inland Sea. It was a naval castle that took advantage of its location surrounded by the sea, and served as a base for the Mouri navy, and also played an important role in Toyotomi Hideyoshi's invasion of Korea (Bunroku and Keicho War). Currently, most of the remains of the main enclosure are used as the station platform and railroad tracks due to renovation work at Mihara Station, making it a rare ``castle ruins inside a station'' in Japan, with stone walls remaining within the station premises. The stone wall of the castle tower remains in good condition and still conveys the scale of the castle in the past.

miyajima_misen.name: 宮島・弥山

transit.name: 宮島口フェリー＋ロープウェイ

miyajima_misen.highlight: 空海が開いた霊場・弥山は宮島の最高峰。消えずの霊火と原始林が古来の聖地の姿を今も守る。
miyajima_misen.text: 弥山（標高535メートル）は宮島（厳島）の最高峰で、806年に空海（弘法大師）が修行して開いた霊場だ。山頂付近の本堂には「消えずの火」と呼ばれる1200年以上燃え続ける霊火があり、広島市の平和記念公園「平和の灯」はこの火を移したものとされる。弥山の原始林は世界遺産の構成要素として厳島神社と一体的に保護されており、シカが闊歩する森の中に千年の信仰の痕跡が残る。世界遺産「厳島神社」を眼下に、瀬戸内海の多島美を望む山頂からの眺望は格別だ。
miyajima_misen.highlight_en: Mt. Misen, a sacred site founded by Kukai, is the highest peak on Miyajima. The unextinguished sacred fire and primeval forest still preserve the appearance of this ancient sacred place.
miyajima_misen.text_en: Mt. Misen (535 meters above sea level) is the highest peak on Miyajima (Itsukushima), and is a sacred site opened in 806 by Kukai (Kobo Daishi) as a training ground. In the main hall near the mountaintop, there is a sacred fire called the ``unquenchable fire'' that has been burning for over 1,200 years, and it is said that the ``Light of Peace'' in Hiroshima City's Peace Memorial Park was moved from this flame. The primeval forest of Mt. Misen is protected together with Itsukushima Shrine as a component of the World Heritage Site, and traces of a thousand years of faith remain in the forest where deer roam. The view from the mountaintop overlooking the world heritage site, Itsukushima Shrine, and the beautiful islands of the Seto Inland Sea is exceptional.

dannoura_battlefield.name: 壇ノ浦古戦場
dannoura_battlefield.kana: だんのうらこせんじょう
dannoura_battlefield.highlight: 1185年に源平合戦が終結した海峡の戦場。安徳天皇と平家一門が入水し武家政権の夜明けが訪れた。
dannoura_battlefield.text: 壇ノ浦は関門海峡の東端、現在の山口県下関市に位置し、1185年（元暦2年）3月24日に源平最後の決戦が行われた場所だ。強い潮流が流れるこの海峡で源義経率いる源氏軍が平家軍を追い詰め、午後には潮の流れが逆転して形勢が一転。敗北を悟った平家の人々は次々と海に飛び込み、7歳の安徳天皇も祖母・二位尼（平時子）に抱かれて入水された。「浪の下にも都の候ぞ」という二位尼の言葉は今も語り継がれる。この戦いで400年続いた貴族政治の時代が終わり、武家政権の時代が始まった。
dannoura_battlefield.highlight_en: The battlefield in the strait where the Genpei War ended in 1185. Emperor Antoku and the Heike clan drowned, and the dawn of the samurai government came.
dannoura_battlefield.text_en: Dan-no-ura is located at the eastern end of the Kanmon Straits, in present-day Shimonoseki City, Yamaguchi Prefecture, and is where the last decisive battle of the Genpei dynasty took place on March 24, 1185. The Minamoto clan forces led by Minamoto no Yoshitsune cornered the Heike army in this strait where strong currents flowed, and in the afternoon the tide reversed and the situation changed. Realizing their defeat, the Heike people jumped into the sea one after another, including the 7-year-old Emperor Antoku, who was carried into the water by his grandmother, Nii-ni (Taira Tokiko). Nii-ni's words, ``Even under the waves, there is a capital'' are still passed down to this day. This battle ended the era of aristocracy that had lasted for 400 years, and began the era of samurai government.

akama_jingu.name: 赤間神宮
akama_jingu.highlight: 壇ノ浦で入水した安徳天皇を祀る水天門の神社。耳なし芳一の怪談の舞台としても名高い。
akama_jingu.text: 赤間神宮は壇ノ浦で入水崩御した安徳天皇を祭神として祀る神社で、平家一門の塚（七盛塚）が境内に存在する。水天門（すいてんもん）と呼ばれる朱塗りの竜宮城を模した楼門が海際に建ち、壇ノ浦の海を見渡す印象的な景観を創出している。怪談の代表作「耳なし芳一」は、この神社で平家の亡霊に琵琶を弾かされた盲目の琵琶法師・芳一の物語で、小泉八雲（ラフカディオ・ハーン）の『怪談』に収録されて世界的に知られる。毎年春には先帝祭が盛大に催される。
akama_jingu.highlight_en: The Suitenmon shrine is dedicated to Emperor Antoku, who drowned in Dan-no-ura. It is also famous as the setting for the ghost story of Hoichi the Earless.
akama_jingu.text_en: Akama Jingu is a shrine that enshrines Emperor Antoku, who died in the water at Dan-no-ura, and there is a mound of the Heike clan (Nanamori-zuka) within the precincts. A vermilion-painted tower gate modeled after Ryugu Castle, called Suitenmon, is built on the seafront, creating an impressive view overlooking the Dannoura sea. ``Earless Hoichi'', a masterpiece of ghost stories, tells the story of Hoichi, a blind biwa master who is forced to play the biwa by the ghost of the Heike clan at this shrine, and is known worldwide after being included in Yakumo Koizumi's (Lafcadio Hearn's) ``Ghost Stories.'' The Sentei Festival is held grandly every spring.

hagi_castle.name: 萩城跡（指月公園）
hagi_castle.highlight: 毛利氏が築いた萩藩の居城。指月山と日本海に囲まれた立地に石垣が残り、明治維新の志士を育んだ城下町の象徴。
hagi_castle.text: 萩城は関ヶ原の戦いで西軍に敗れた毛利輝元が1604年（慶長9年）に指月山麓に築いた城で、江戸時代を通じて長州藩（萩藩）の政治の中心地となった。明治維新後に廃城となり建物は取り壊されたが、三ノ丸・二ノ丸・本丸の石垣と堀が良好に残り指月公園として公開されている。城下町には吉田松陰・高杉晋作・木戸孝允ら幕末志士の生家や旧宅が点在しており、幕末維新の舞台として「明治日本の産業革命遺産」の構成資産にも含まれる。萩焼の産地としても知られ伝統工芸が息づく。
hagi_castle.highlight_en: The residence of the Hagi clan built by the Mori clan. Surrounded by Mt. Shigetsu and the Sea of ​​Japan, the stone walls remain and are a symbol of the castle town that nurtured the patriots of the Meiji Restoration.
hagi_castle.text_en: Hagi Castle was built at the foot of Mt. Shizuki in 1604 by Mori Terumoto, who was defeated by the Western army at the Battle of Sekigahara, and served as the political center of the Choshu clan (Hagi clan) throughout the Edo period. After the Meiji Restoration, the castle became abandoned and the buildings were demolished, but the stone walls and moat of Sannomaru, Ninomaru, and Honmaru remain in good condition and are open to the public as Shizuki Park. The castle town is dotted with the birthplaces and former residences of Shoin Yoshida, Shinsaku Takasugi, Takayoshi Kido, and other patriots from the end of the Edo period, and is included in the ``Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution'' as the stage of the end of the Edo period. It is also known as a production area for Hagiyaki, where traditional crafts are still alive.

ruriko_pagoda.name: 瑠璃光寺五重塔
ruriko_pagoda.kana: るりこうじごじゅうのとう
ruriko_pagoda.highlight: 日本三名塔のひとつ。大内文化の粋を集めた優美な五重塔が香山公園に佇み「西の京」山口を象徴する。
ruriko_pagoda.text: 瑠璃光寺の五重塔は1442年（嘉吉2年）に大内盛見の菩提を弔うために建立された高さ31.2メートルの塔で、奈良の法隆寺・京都の醍醐寺とともに「日本三名塔」のひとつに数えられる国宝だ。大内氏は15世紀に西国に一大文化圏を形成し、都（京都）に劣らぬ「西の京」と呼ばれる山口の繁栄を誇った。周囲の香山公園には梅・桜・紅葉が四季を彩り、池に映る五重塔の倒影が絶美の景観をつくり出す。雪舟・宗祇ら著名な文化人も大内氏のもとに集まった。
ruriko_pagoda.highlight_en: One of the three famous pagodas in Japan. An elegant five-storied pagoda that brings together the essence of Ouchi culture stands in Koyama Park and symbolizes Yamaguchi, the "Kyoto of the West."
ruriko_pagoda.text_en: The five-storied pagoda of Ruriko-ji Temple is a 31.2-meter-tall pagoda that was built in 1442 (Kakichi 2nd year) to mourn the memory of Morimi Ouchi, and is a national treasure that is considered one of Japan's three great pagodas, along with Horyu-ji Temple in Nara and Daigo-ji Temple in Kyoto. In the 15th century, the Ouchi clan formed a major cultural area in the western part of Japan, boasting a prosperous Yamaguchi area that was called the ``Kyoto of the West'' and rivaled the capital (Kyoto). The surrounding Koyama Park is decorated with plum blossoms, cherry blossoms, and autumn leaves in all seasons, and the reflection of the five-storied pagoda in the pond creates an exquisite scenery. Famous cultural figures such as Sesshu and Sogi also gathered under the Ouchi clan.

kozanji_chofu.name: 長府・功山寺
kozanji_chofu.highlight: 鎌倉時代創建の禅寺。幕末に高杉晋作が80人の奇兵隊を率いて倒幕の旗揚げをした「功山寺挙兵」の地。
kozanji_chofu.text: 功山寺は1327年（嘉暦2年）に創建された曹洞宗の古刹で、国宝の仏殿は鎌倉時代の禅宗様建築の代表例として知られる。幕末の1864年12月、高杉晋作はわずか80名の奇兵隊を率いてこの寺の山門前で倒幕の旗揚げを行い、当時主流だった保守派（俗論党）への反撃を開始した。「動けば雷電の如く、発すれば風雨の如し」と言われた高杉の気迫が長州藩の命運を変えるきっかけとなり、維新への道が本格的に開かれた。境内には高杉晋作像が立ち、長府の古い武家屋敷街と合わせて幕末の空気を今に伝える。
kozanji_chofu.highlight_en: A Zen temple founded in the Kamakura period. At the end of the Edo period, Shinsaku Takasugi led a group of 80 military soldiers to raise the flag to overthrow the Shogunate.
kozanji_chofu.text_en: Kozan-ji Temple is an old temple of the Soto sect, founded in 1327 (Kareki 2), and its Buddhist hall, a national treasure, is known as a representative example of Zen sect-style architecture from the Kamakura period. In December 1864, at the end of the Edo period, Shinsaku Takasugi led a group of only 80 Kiheitai soldiers and raised the banner of overthrowing the Shogunate in front of the main gate of this temple, launching a counterattack against the then-mainstream conservative faction (Zokuron-to). Takasugi's spirit, which was said to ``move like thunderbolts, and emit it like wind and rain,'' became the trigger that changed the fate of the Choshu domain, and the road to the Meiji Restoration was opened in earnest. A statue of Shin Takasugi stands in the precincts, and together with the old samurai residence district of Chofu, it still conveys the atmosphere of the end of the Edo period.

iwakuni_castle.name: 岩国城・錦帯橋
iwakuni_castle.kana: いわくにじょうきんたいきょう
iwakuni_castle.highlight: 5連木造アーチ橋「錦帯橋」と山頂の岩国城が織りなす絶景。350年以上洪水に耐えた橋は木造橋梁の最高傑作。
iwakuni_castle.text: 錦帯橋は1673年（延宝元年）に岩国藩3代藩主・吉川広嘉が設計・建設した全長193メートルの5連木造アーチ橋で、日本三名橋のひとつだ。錦川の増水に対応するため橋桁を設けず木組みだけでアーチを構成する独創的な工法が採用され、洪水でも橋脚が流されないよう石積みの橋脚に木造の桁を渡す方式をとる。対岸の横山山頂には1962年に復元された岩国城天守がそびえ、橋と城の競演が絵画のような景観を作り出す。毎年春には橋の下から見上げる桜が名物で、夜桜のライトアップも美しい。
iwakuni_castle.highlight_en: Spectacular views of Kintai Bridge, a five-row wooden arch bridge, and Iwakuni Castle at the top of the mountain. The bridge, which withstood floods for over 350 years, is a masterpiece of wooden bridges.
iwakuni_castle.text_en: Kintaikyo Bridge is a five-row wooden arch bridge with a total length of 193 meters that was designed and built by Hiroyoshi Yoshikawa, the third lord of the Iwakuni domain, in 1673, and is one of the three most famous bridges in Japan. In order to cope with the rising waters of the Nishiki River, an original construction method was adopted in which the arch was constructed entirely of wood without installing bridge girders, and wooden girders were placed over the masonry piers to prevent the piers from being washed away in the event of flooding. Iwakuni Castle tower, restored in 1962, rises from the summit of Yokoyama on the opposite bank, and the combination of bridge and castle creates a picturesque landscape. The cherry blossoms seen from under the bridge are a specialty every spring, and the cherry blossoms illuminated at night are also beautiful.

shokasonjuku.name: 松下村塾
shokasonjuku.highlight: 吉田松陰が開いた私塾。伊藤博文・山縣有朋ら明治維新を担った多くの俊才を育てた2年8ヶ月の奇跡の学塾。
shokasonjuku.text: 松下村塾は吉田松陰が1857年（安政4年）から幽囚されながらも開いた小さな私塾で、わずか8畳と10畳の部屋しかない建物から明治維新を動かした俊才たちが巣立った。伊藤博文・山縣有朋・高杉晋作・久坂玄瑞・吉田稔麿ら「松下村塾の87名」が学び、その多くが維新の中心的役割を担った。松陰は「学問とは実行である」という信念のもと、身分や年齢を問わず塾生と共に学び議論した。1859年の安政の大獄で松陰は江戸で処刑されたが、その志は弟子たちによって実現された。世界遺産の構成資産。
shokasonjuku.highlight_en: A private school opened by Shoin Yoshida. A miraculous 2 year and 8 month cram school that trained many brilliant minds who were responsible for the Meiji Restoration, such as Hirobumi Ito and Aritomo Yamagata.
shokasonjuku.text_en: Matsushitasonjuku was a small private school opened by Shoin Yoshida while imprisoned in 1857 (Ansei 4), and from this building with only 8 and 10 tatami rooms, the brilliant minds who led the Meiji Restoration started. Hirobumi Ito, Aritomo Yamagata, Shinsaku Takasugi, Genzui Kusaka, Minoru Yoshida, and other ``87 members of the Matsushita Village School'' studied there, and many of them played a central role in the Meiji Restoration. Based on his belief that ``academics are actions,'' Shoin studied and discussed with students regardless of social status or age. Shoin was executed in Edo during the Great Prison of Ansei in 1859, but his aspirations were realized by his disciples. A component of a World Heritage Site.

hofu_tenmangu.name: 防府天満宮
hofu_tenmangu.highlight: 日本最初の天満宮。菅原道真の霊を最初に祀った社で、道真の太宰府への左遷の途上に創建された。
hofu_tenmangu.text: 防府天満宮は901年（延喜元年）、大宰府に向かう菅原道真が防府（当時の防石津）に立ち寄った際に地元の人々が祀り始めたとされる、日本で最初に創建された天満宮だ。道真の死後、その御霊を祀る神社として整備され、京都の北野天満宮・福岡の太宰府天満宮と並んで「日本三天神」のひとつに数えられる。学問の神様として受験生の信仰を集め、梅の名所としても名高い。境内には道真ゆかりの梅の木や社宝が多く、千年以上の歴史を誇る古社の格調が漂う。
hofu_tenmangu.highlight_en: Japan's first Tenmangu Shrine. It was the first shrine to enshrine the spirit of Sugawara Michizane, and was built during Michizane's demotion to Dazaifu.
hofu_tenmangu.text_en: Hofu Tenmangu Shrine is the first Tenmangu Shrine built in Japan, and is said to have been worshiped by local people in 901 when Sugawara no Michizane stopped by Hofu (then Hoishizu) on his way to Dazaifu. After Michizane's death, it was established as a shrine to enshrine his spirit, and is considered one of Japan's three Tenjin shrines, along with Kitano Tenmangu in Kyoto and Dazaifu Tenmangu in Fukuoka. It is worshiped by test takers as the god of learning, and is also famous for its plum blossoms. The precincts are filled with plum trees and shrine treasures related to Michizane, giving off the dignity of an ancient shrine with a history of over 1,000 years.

ouchi_yakata.name: 大内氏館跡・龍福寺
ouchi_yakata.kana: おおうちしやかたあとりゅうふくじ
ouchi_yakata.highlight: 「西の京」と称された山口を支配した大内氏の館跡。京文化を西国に伝えた文化大名の栄華の痕跡が残る。
ouchi_yakata.text: 大内氏館は中国地方から北部九州まで支配した室町時代の大名・大内氏の居館跡で、現在は龍福寺の境内となっている。大内氏は15世紀に最盛期を迎え、日明貿易・朝鮮貿易で巨富を蓄え、京都の貴族・文化人を山口に招いて「西の京」と呼ばれる文化都市を形成した。雪舟・宗祇・連歌師ら多くの文化人が大内氏のもとに集まり、山口は上方文化の西日本における発信地となった。1551年に陶晴賢のクーデターで大内義隆が自刃し大内氏は滅亡。館は灰燼に帰したが龍福寺本堂として一部が復元されている。
ouchi_yakata.highlight_en: This is the ruins of the residence of the Ouchi clan, who ruled Yamaguchi, which was known as the ``Western Capital.'' Traces of the prosperity of the cultural lords who brought Kyoto culture to the West remain.
ouchi_yakata.text_en: The Ouchi clan is the former residence of the Ouchi clan, a feudal lord from the Muromachi period who ruled from the Chugoku region to northern Kyushu, and is currently within the precincts of Ryufuku-ji Temple. The Ouchi clan reached its peak in the 15th century, amassing great wealth through trade between Japan and Ming Dynasty and Korea, and inviting Kyoto's aristocrats and intellectuals to Yamaguchi, creating a cultural city known as ``Western Capital.'' Many cultural figures such as Sesshu, Sogi, and renga masters gathered under the Ouchi clan, and Yamaguchi became the epicenter of Kamigata culture in western Japan. In 1551, Yoshitaka Ouchi committed suicide in a coup d'état led by Sue Harukata, and the Ouchi clan fell into ruin. The building was reduced to ashes, but part of it has been restored as the main hall of Ryufuku-ji Temple.

nagato_kokubunji.name: 長門国分寺跡
nagato_kokubunji.kana: ながとこくぶんじあと
nagato_kokubunji.highlight: 741年の聖武天皇の詔で建立された長門国の官寺。七重塔心礎と礎石群が奈良時代の地方仏教行政を今に伝える。
nagato_kokubunji.text: 長門国分寺は741年（天平13年）の聖武天皇の詔によって長門国に建立された官寺で、現在の山口県防府市国分寺町に位置する。発掘調査で七重塔の心礎・金堂・講堂の礎石が確認されており、奈良時代の大規模な伽藍配置が明らかになっている。国分寺は全国60余カ国に建てられた律令国家の仏教政策の産物で、長門国分寺もその重要な一翼を担った。境内には現在も「国分寺」として法灯が継承されており、奈良時代の礎石と現代の境内が共存する独特の景観が広がる。周辺には長門国府の遺跡も点在する。
nagato_kokubunji.highlight_en: An official temple of Nagato Province, built by Emperor Shomu's edict in 741. The seven-storied pagoda's central cornerstone and group of foundation stones tell us about the local Buddhist administration of the Nara period.
nagato_kokubunji.text_en: Nagato Kokubunji is a government temple built in Nagato Province in 741 by Emperor Shomu's edict, and is located in present-day Kokubunji-cho, Hofu City, Yamaguchi Prefecture. Excavations have confirmed the core foundation of the seven-storied pagoda, the main hall, and the foundation stones of the auditorium, revealing the large-scale layout of the temple during the Nara period. Kokubunji temples were a product of the Buddhist policy of the Ritsuryo state, which was established in more than 60 countries across the country, and Nagato Kokubunji also played an important role. The lanterns still remain in the temple grounds today as a ``Kokubunji'' temple, creating a unique landscape where the foundation stones of the Nara period coexist with the modern grounds. There are also ruins of Nagato Kokufu in the surrounding area.

tatetsuki_site.name: 楯築遺跡
tatetsuki_site.highlight: 弥生時代後期の大型墳丘墓。吉備王国の首長が眠るとされ、後の前方後円墳の原型となった墓制の宝庫。
tatetsuki_site.text: 楯築遺跡は岡山県倉敷市矢部に位置する弥生時代後期（2〜3世紀）の大型墳丘墓で、国の史跡に指定されている。直径43メートルの円丘から東西に突出部を持つ独特の形状は、後の前方後円墳につながる墓制の発展段階を示すとして注目される。墳丘の周囲には立石（弧帯石）が配置されており、吉備地方独自の祭祀遺物が多く出土した。古代吉備王国の有力首長の墓と考えられ、造山古墳と並んで吉備の古代権力の系譜を語る上で不可欠な遺跡だ。
tatetsuki_site.highlight_en: A large burial mound from the late Yayoi period. It is said that the chief of the Kibi Kingdom is buried here, and is a treasure trove of burial mounds that served as the prototype for later keyhole-shaped tumuli.
tatetsuki_site.text_en: The Tatetsuki Ruins are a large burial mound from the late Yayoi period (2nd to 3rd century) located in Yabe, Kurashiki City, Okayama Prefecture, and are designated as a national historic site. The unique shape of the mound, which is 43 meters in diameter and has protrusions extending east and west, is attracting attention as indicating the stage of development of the tomb system that led to later keyhole-shaped tombs. Standing stones (arc-shaped stones) are placed around the burial mound, and many ritual artifacts unique to the Kibi region have been unearthed. It is thought to be the tomb of a powerful chieftain of the ancient Kibi Kingdom, and along with the Zoriyama Tumulus, it is an essential ruin for telling the lineage of Kibi's ancient power.

takehara_townscape.name: 竹原の伝統的建造物群
takehara_townscape.kana: たけはらのでんとうてきけんぞうぶつぐん
takehara_townscape.highlight: 製塩と酒造で栄えた「安芸の小京都」。江戸中期から明治の商家・町家が奇跡的に残る重要伝統的建造物群保存地区。
takehara_townscape.text: 竹原は広島県竹原市に位置し、江戸時代に製塩業と酒造業で繁栄した港町だ。重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に指定された本町通り周辺には、江戸時代中期から明治時代にかけての商家・町家・寺院が軒を連ね「安芸の小京都」と呼ばれる景観を形成している。塩廻船で財を成した商人たちの邸宅には精巧な格子窓や白壁が今も残る。アニメ「たまゆら」の舞台としても知られ、ノスタルジックな街並みが全国から多くの観光客を引き付ける。日本酒「竹鶴」発祥の地でもある。
takehara_townscape.highlight_en: "Little Kyoto of Aki" flourished with salt manufacturing and sake brewing. An important preservation district for traditional buildings where merchant houses and townhouses from the mid-Edo period to the Meiji period miraculously remain.
takehara_townscape.text_en: Takehara, located in Takehara City, Hiroshima Prefecture, is a port town that flourished during the Edo period with its salt manufacturing and sake brewing industries. The area around Honmachi-dori Street, which has been designated as an Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings, is lined with merchant houses, townhouses, and temples dating from the mid-Edo period to the Meiji period, forming a landscape known as ``Aki's Little Kyoto.'' Elaborate lattice windows and white walls still remain in the residences of merchants who made their fortunes on saltwater ships. It is also known as the setting for the anime "Tamayura," and its nostalgic townscape attracts many tourists from all over the country. It is also the birthplace of the Japanese sake ``Taketsuru.''

sendai_castle.name: 仙台城跡（青葉城）
sendai_castle.highlight: 伊達政宗が築いた仙台70万石の居城。青葉山の本丸跡に立つ政宗騎馬像が東北の覇者を今に伝える。
sendai_castle.text: 仙台城（青葉城）は1601年（慶長6年）に伊達政宗が仙台湾を望む青葉山に築いた山城で、江戸時代を通じて仙台藩62万石（実高70万石超）の政治の中心地となった。明治以降の解体と太平洋戦争の空襲で建物は失われたが、石垣と本丸跡が残り、1935年に建立された政宗の騎馬像が来訪者を迎える。眼下には広瀬川と仙台市街が広がり、眼帯の独眼竜・伊達政宗の覇気が感じられる。仙台城跡全体が国の史跡に指定されており、博物館では政宗の生涯を詳しく解説している。
sendai_castle.highlight_en: The Sendai castle built by Date Masamune was worth 700,000 koku. The equestrian statue of Masamune that stands at the site of the main enclosure of Aobayama tells the story of the ruler of Tohoku.
sendai_castle.text_en: Sendai Castle (Aoba Castle) is a mountain castle built by Date Masamune in 1601 on Mt. Aoba overlooking Sendaidai.Throughout the Edo period, it became the political center of the Sendai domain with a capital of 620,000 koku (actual value of over 700,000 koku). Although the building was destroyed during the Meiji era and later during the air raids of the Pacific War, the stone walls and remains of the main enclosure remain, and visitors are greeted by the equestrian statue of Masamune erected in 1935. The Hirose River and the city of Sendai spread out below, and you can feel the ambition of Date Masamune, the one-eyed dragon with an eyepatch. The entire Sendai Castle ruins are designated as a national historic site, and the museum provides detailed explanations of Masamune's life.

hiraizumi_chusonji.name: 中尊寺（平泉）
hiraizumi_chusonji.highlight: 世界遺産・奥州藤原氏が築いた黄金の浄土。金色堂は源義経が自刃した後に兄・頼朝の侵攻から守られた聖地。
hiraizumi_chusonji.text: 中尊寺は850年に慈覚大師円仁が開山したと伝わり、12世紀に奥州藤原氏が「浄土思想」に基づいて壮大な伽藍を整備した。金色堂（国宝）は1124年建立で、内外を金箔で覆い藤原四代の遺体を安置する唯一無二の阿弥陀堂だ。源義経は兄・頼朝に追われ藤原秀衡を頼ってこの平泉に逃れたが、秀衡の死後に子・泰衡に攻められ1189年に自刃した（衣川館の戦い）。松尾芭蕉が「夏草や兵どもが夢の跡」と詠んだ土地として文学的にも名高い。2011年に世界遺産登録。
hiraizumi_chusonji.highlight_en: A world heritage site, the Golden Pure Land built by the Oshu Fujiwara clan. Konjikido is a sacred place where Minamoto no Yoshitsune committed suicide and was protected from the invasion of his older brother Yoritomo.
hiraizumi_chusonji.text_en: Chuson-ji Temple is said to have been founded by Jikaku Daishi Ennin in 850, and in the 12th century, the Oshu Fujiwara clan built a magnificent temple based on ``Pure Land Thought.'' Konjiki-do (National Treasure) was built in 1124 and is a one-of-a-kind Amida-do hall, covered inside and out with gold leaf and where the bodies of the four generations of Fujiwara are enshrined. Minamoto no Yoshitsune was chased by his older brother Yoritomo and fled to Hiraizumi with the help of Fujiwara Hidehira, but after Hidehira's death, he was attacked by his son Yasuhira and committed suicide in 1189 (Battle of Korokawa no Tate). It is also famous in literature as the place where Matsuo Basho wrote a poem, ``Summer grass and soldiers are the traces of dreams.'' Registered as a World Heritage Site in 2011.

yamagata_castle.name: 山形城跡（霞城）
yamagata_castle.highlight: 最上義光が拡大整備した最上藩の居城。関ヶ原後57万石の版図を誇り「霞城」の別名で親しまれる。
yamagata_castle.text: 山形城（霞城）は南北朝時代に斯波兼頼が築いたとされ、戦国時代に最上義光が大規模に拡張整備した。義光は関ヶ原の戦いで東軍に属し、上杉景勝の侵攻（慶長出羽合戦）を撃退して57万石の版図を確立した。江戸時代の山形は豊かな城下町として発展したが、その後幾度も藩主が替わった。現在は霞城公園として整備され、二の丸東大手門や本丸一文字門が復元されている。春の桜の名所としても知られ、最上義光の騎馬像が城跡に立つ。
yamagata_castle.highlight_en: The residence of the Mogami clan, which was expanded and maintained by Yoshimitsu Mogami. Boasting 570,000 koku of land after Sekigahara, it is also known as ``Kajo''.
yamagata_castle.text_en: Yamagata Castle (Kajo) is said to have been built by Kaneyori Shiba during the Nanbokucho period, and was expanded and maintained on a large scale by Yoshimitsu Mogami during the Sengoku period. Yoshimitsu belonged to the Eastern Army at the Battle of Sekigahara, repelled Kagekatsu Uesugi's invasion (Keicho Dewa Battle), and established a land base of 570,000 koku. During the Edo period, Yamagata developed as a prosperous castle town, but the feudal lords changed many times after that. Currently, it is maintained as Kajo Park, and the Ninomaru Higashi Ote Gate and Honmaru Ichimonji Gate have been restored. It is also known as a famous spot for viewing cherry blossoms in spring, and an equestrian statue of Mogami Yoshimitsu stands on the castle ruins.

wakamatsu_tsurugajo.name: 鶴ヶ城（会津若松城）
wakamatsu_tsurugajo.highlight: 保科正之が整備した会津松平家の居城。戊辰戦争で新政府軍の猛攻に1ヶ月耐えた「難攻不落の城」。
wakamatsu_tsurugajo.text: 会津若松城（鶴ヶ城）は14世紀に葦名氏が築いた城を、江戸時代初期に保科正之が近代的に整備した。保科正之は徳川秀忠の庶子でありながら徳川家への忠義を貫き、会津松平家23万石の藩祖として「名君」と謳われた。幕末の戊辰戦争（1868年）では新政府軍に包囲され、白虎隊の悲劇で知られる1ヶ月にわたる籠城戦を繰り広げた後に開城。天守は1965年に復元され、赤瓦の美しい姿が会津の象徴となっている。新島八重はこの城で戦った女性としても有名だ。
wakamatsu_tsurugajo.highlight_en: The residence of the Aizu Matsudaira family built by Masayuki Hoshina. This "impregnable castle" withstood the onslaught of the new government's army for a month during the Boshin War.
wakamatsu_tsurugajo.text_en: Aizuwakamatsu Castle (Tsuruga Castle) was built by the Ashina clan in the 14th century and modernized by Masayuki Hoshina in the early Edo period. Although Masayuki Hoshina was an illegitimate son of Hidetada Tokugawa, he remained loyal to the Tokugawa family, and as the founder of the Aizu-Matsudaira clan, which earned 230,000 koku, he was hailed as a ``great prince.'' During the Boshin War (1868) at the end of the Edo period, the castle was surrounded by new government forces, and the castle was surrendered after a month-long siege battle known for the tragedy of the Byakkotai. The castle tower was restored in 1965, and its beautiful red tiles have become a symbol of Aizu. Yae Niijima is also famous as the woman who fought in this castle.

mizusawa_goto.name: 後藤新平記念館（水沢）
mizusawa_goto.kana: ごとうしんぺいきねんかん
mizusawa_goto.highlight: 台湾・満州・東京市長として都市インフラを整備した「大風呂敷」後藤新平の出身地。今の東京の骨格を設計した人物。
mizusawa_goto.text: 後藤新平は1857年に岩手県水沢（現・奥州市）に生まれた医師・政治家だ。台湾総督府民政長官として台湾の衛生・鉄道・教育インフラを整備し、満鉄（南満洲鉄道）総裁として大陸経営の基盤を作り、東京市長として関東大震災後の帝都復興計画を立案した。「大風呂敷」と揶揄されながらも実行力で社会を変えた稀代の行政家で、現代の東京の都市計画の設計思想に彼の影響が色濃く残る。水沢の生家跡には記念館が建てられ、後藤の多岐にわたる業績を展示している。
mizusawa_goto.highlight_en: The birthplace of Shinpei Goto, the ``big furoshiki'' who developed urban infrastructure as the mayor of Taiwan, Manchuria, and Tokyo. The person who designed the framework of today's Tokyo.
mizusawa_goto.text_en: Shinpei Goto was a doctor and politician born in 1857 in Mizusawa, Iwate Prefecture (present-day Oshu City). As Secretary of Civil Affairs in the Taiwan Governor-General's Office, he developed Taiwan's sanitary, railway, and educational infrastructure; as president of the Manchuria Railway (South Manchuria Railway), he laid the foundations for continental management; and as mayor of Tokyo, he devised a plan for the restoration of the imperial capital after the Great Kanto Earthquake. Although he was ridiculed as a ``big furoshiki,'' he was a rare administrator who changed society with his executive power.His influence remains strongly in the design philosophy of modern Tokyo urban planning. A memorial hall has been built at the site of Mizusawa's birthplace, displaying Goto's wide-ranging achievements.

yonezawa_uesugi_shrine.name: 上杉神社・米沢城跡
yonezawa_uesugi_shrine.kana: うえすぎじんじゃよねざわじょうあと
yonezawa_uesugi_shrine.highlight: 上杉謙信・景勝・直江兼続を祀る上杉の聖地。直江兼続の「愛」の前立が象徴する義と知の米沢藩の中心。
yonezawa_uesugi_shrine.text: 米沢城跡（松岬公園）には上杉謙信・景勝・直江兼続を祀る上杉神社が鎮座する。米沢藩は関ヶ原後に上杉景勝が会津120万石から30万石に減封され、参謀・直江兼続とともにこの地を治めた。兼続は財政難の藩を立て直すため新田開発・産業振興を精力的に進め、米沢の「かね」（笹野一刀彫・米沢織）の礎を築いた。「愛」の前立の兜で知られる兼続は武将でありながら文化人でもあり、米沢藩の文教政策を担った。境内には上杉謙信の遺骸を祀る御堂もあり、越後から移された「義」の精神が息づく。
yonezawa_uesugi_shrine.highlight_en: A sacred place in Uesugi that enshrines Kenshin Uesugi, Kagekatsu, and Kanetsugu Naoe. The center of the Yonezawa clan of righteousness and wisdom, symbolized by Kanetsugu Naoe's "Love" front.
yonezawa_uesugi_shrine.text_en: Uesugi Shrine, which enshrines Uesugi Kenshin, Kagekatsu, and Naoe Kanetsugu, is located at the ruins of Yonezawa Castle (Matsumisaki Park).
