After Sekigahara, the Yonezawa domain was reduced to 300,000 koku from 1.2 million koku in Aizu, and Kagekatsu Uesugi ruled the area with his staff officer Kanetsugu Naoe. In order to rebuild the domain, which was in financial trouble, Kanetsugu energetically promoted the development of new fields and industrial development, and laid the foundation for Yonezawa's ``Kane'' (Sasano Ittobori and Yonezawa Ori). Kanetsugu, known for his helmet with the word ``love'' on the front, was a military commander but also a cultural figure, and was responsible for the Yonezawa clan's educational policy. There is also a hall on the grounds that enshrines the remains of Uesugi Kenshin, and the spirit of ``righteousness'' that was brought from Echigo lives on here.

goryokaku_hakodate.name: 五稜郭（函館・戊辰戦争最後の戦場）
goryokaku_hakodate.text: 五稜郭は江戸幕府が日米和親条約後の蝦夷地防衛のため、武田斐三郎の設計で1864年に完成させた星形の洋式城郭です。フランスの城塞都市を参考にした五角形の堀と土塁が特徴で、稜堡から十字砲火を浴びせられる近代的構造でした。1868年の戊辰戦争では榎本武揚率いる旧幕府軍が立てこもり、土方歳三も箱館戦争で奮戦したのち戦死しました。1869年5月に新政府軍に降伏し、これをもって戊辰戦争は終結しました。明治後は陸軍の練兵場、現在は国の特別史跡として公園化され、五稜郭タワーから星形の全景を見下ろせます。
goryokaku_hakodate.highlight: 戊辰戦争最後の戦場・日本初の洋式星形城郭。土方歳三終焉の地
goryokaku_hakodate.name_en: Goryokaku (the last battlefield of the Hakodate-Boshin War)
goryokaku_hakodate.highlight_en: The last battlefield of the Boshin War, Japan's first Western-style star-shaped castle. The place where Toshizo Hijikata died
goryokaku_hakodate.text_en: Goryokaku is a star-shaped Western-style castle designed by Takeda Hizaburo and completed in 1864 by the Edo Shogunate to protect Ezo after the Japan-US Treaty of Peace and Amity. It was a modern structure with a pentagonal moat and earthworks modeled after French fortified cities, and was able to be bombarded with cross fire from a bastion. During the Boshin War of 1868, the former shogunate army led by Takeaki Enomoto holed up there, and Toshizo Hijikata also died after fighting bravely in the Hakodate War. It surrendered to the new government forces in May 1869, ending the Boshin War. After the Meiji era, it was used as an army training ground, and now it is a park as a special national historic site, and you can enjoy a star-shaped panoramic view from Goryokaku Tower.

takeda_tsutsujigasaki.name: 武田氏館跡（躑躅ヶ崎館）
takeda_tsutsujigasaki.kana: たけだしやかたあとつつじがさきやかた
takeda_tsutsujigasaki.highlight: 武田信玄の本拠・甲府の館跡。「風林火山」の旗のもとで天下を狙った信玄の軍略の出発点。
takeda_tsutsujigasaki.text: 躑躅ヶ崎館（武田氏館）は甲斐国の守護大名・武田信玄が本拠とした平地の館で、現在の山梨県甲府市に位置する。戦国大名の多くが山城を本拠にした時代に、武田氏は機動性の高い騎馬軍団を活かすため平地の館を選んだ。信玄は「風林火山」（疾きこと風の如し、徐かなること林の如し、侵掠すること火の如し、動かざること山の如し）を旗印に、甲斐・信濃を中心に16カ国に勢力を広げた。現在は武田神社として整備され、信玄の幼名を冠した「信玄公まつり」が毎年開催される。発掘調査も進行中。
takeda_tsutsujigasaki.highlight_en: Ruins of Takeda Shingen's headquarters in Kofu. The starting point of Shingen's military strategy, which aimed at conquering the world under the banner of ``Furinkazan.''
takeda_tsutsujigasaki.text_en: Tsutsujigasakikan (Takeda clan mansion) is a mansion on a flat land that was the headquarters of Takeda Shingen, the shugo daimyo of Kai Province, and is located in present-day Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture. At a time when many feudal lords of the Sengoku period had mountain castles as their base, the Takeda clan chose a mansion on a flat land to take advantage of its highly mobile cavalry corps. Shingen spread his influence to 16 countries centered on Kai and Shinano under the banner of ``Furinkazan'' (speeding like the wind, slowing like a forest, encroaching like fire, and staying still like a mountain). Currently, it is maintained as Takeda Shrine, and the ``Shingen Festival'', named after Shingen's childhood name, is held every year. Excavation work is also underway.

kasugayama_castle.name: 春日山城跡
kasugayama_castle.kana: かすがやまじょうあと
kasugayama_castle.highlight: 越後の龍・上杉謙信の本拠。「敵に塩を送る」美談や川中島の激闘を指揮した難攻不落の山城。
kasugayama_castle.text: 春日山城は越後国（現新潟県）の山城で、戦国時代に上杉謙信が本拠とした難攻不落の要塞だ。謙信は「義」を重んじる武将として知られ、甲斐・武田信玄と川中島で5度にわたり激突した「義戦」が有名だ。また敵対する武田信玄に米と塩を送った「敵に塩を送る」の逸話が義の精神を象徴する。1578年に謙信が急逝すると御館の乱が起き後継争いが勃発。城は廃城となったが山頂に築かれた曲輪群・空堀・堀切の遺構が今も残り、謙信の銅像が城跡に立つ。眼下に直江津の日本海が広がる。
kasugayama_castle.highlight_en: The home base of Uesugi Kenshin, the Dragon of Echigo. An impregnable mountain castle that commanded Bidan and the fierce battle of Kawanakajima, which ``sends salt to the enemy.''
kasugayama_castle.text_en: Kasugayama Castle is a mountain castle in Echigo Province (now Niigata Prefecture), and is an impregnable fortress that was home to Uesugi Kenshin during the Sengoku period. Kenshin is known as a military commander who values ​​``righteousness,'' and is famous for the ``righteous battles'' in which he clashed five times with Takeda Shingen of Kai on Kawanakajima. Also, the anecdote of ``sending salt to the enemy,'' in which he sent rice and salt to his enemy Takeda Shingen, symbolizes the spirit of righteousness. When Kenshin suddenly passed away in 1578, the Otate Rebellion broke out and a battle for succession broke out. The castle has been abandoned, but the remains of the Kuruwa group, Karahori, and Horikiri built on the mountaintop still remain, and a bronze statue of Kenshin stands at the castle ruins. The Sea of ​​Japan in Naoetsu stretches out below.

ueda_castle.name: 上田城跡
ueda_castle.highlight: 真田昌幸・幸村が2度にわたり徳川軍を撃退した「真田の城」。第二次上田合戦では38000の軍を2000で退けた。
ueda_castle.text: 上田城は1583年（天正11年）に真田昌幸が築いた城で、真田家の本拠として難攻不落の名声を誇る。1585年の第一次上田合戦では徳川家康の軍7000を真田昌幸が2000の兵で撃退した。1600年の関ヶ原前夜・第二次上田合戦では徳川秀忠の軍38000を足止めし、秀忠を関ヶ原本戦に間に合わせなかった。真田幸村（信繁）は父・昌幸のもとでこの城を守った後、大坂の陣で家康を苦しめ「日本一の兵」と讃えられた。現在も三重の堀と石垣・城門が残り、春には堀に映る桜が名物だ。
ueda_castle.highlight_en: Sanada Castle is where Masayuki Sanada and Yukimura defeated the Tokugawa army twice. In the Second Battle of Ueda, an army of 38,000 was defeated by 2,000.
ueda_castle.text_en: Ueda Castle was built by Masayuki Sanada in 1583 (Tensho 11), and boasts an impregnable reputation as the headquarters of the Sanada family. In the First Battle of Ueda in 1585, Masayuki Sanada repulsed Tokugawa Ieyasu's army of 7,000 troops with 2,000 soldiers. At the Second Battle of Ueda on the eve of Sekigahara in 1600, he held back Hidetada Tokugawa's army of 38,000 men, preventing Hidetada from arriving in time for the main battle at Sekigahara. After Yukimura Sanada (Nobushige) defended this castle under his father Masayuki, he tormented Ieyasu at the Battle of Osaka and was praised as ``Japan's best soldier.'' Today, the Mie moat, stone walls, and castle gates still remain, and the cherry blossoms reflected in the moat in spring are famous.

kamakura_okura_bakufu.name: 大倉幕府跡・鶴岡八幡宮
kamakura_okura_bakufu.kana: おおくらばくふあとつるがおかはちまんぐう
kamakura_okura_bakufu.highlight: 源頼朝が開いた日本最初の武家政権の本拠地。北条義時はここで承久の乱を制し武士の世を盤石にした。
kamakura_okura_bakufu.text: 鎌倉は1185年に源頼朝が武家政権を樹立した日本最初の幕府所在地だ。大倉幕府跡（現・鶴岡八幡宮の東）には頼朝が建てた政所の跡が残る。北条義時は頼朝の妻・北条政子の弟で、初代執権・北条時政の後継として2代執権に就任。1221年の承久の乱では後鳥羽上皇の討幕命令に対して坂東武者を率いて圧倒的勝利を収め、上皇を隠岐に流した。これにより武家政権が朝廷より上位に立つことが確立され、鎌倉幕府は安定した統治体制を築いた。
kamakura_okura_bakufu.highlight_en: The headquarters of Japan's first samurai government, founded by Minamoto no Yoritomo. Yoshitoki Hojo won the Jokyu War here and solidified the samurai world.
kamakura_okura_bakufu.text_en: Kamakura was the seat of Japan's first shogunate, where Minamoto no Yoritomo established a samurai government in 1185. The remains of the government office built by Yoritomo remain at the Okura Shogunate site (to the east of present-day Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine). Yoshitoki Hojo was the younger brother of Yoritomo's wife, Masako Hojo, and was appointed as the second regent, succeeding the first regent, Tokimasa Hojo. In the Jokyu War in 1221, he led the Bando warriors and won an overwhelming victory against the Retired Emperor Gotoba's order to attack the shogunate, and exiled the Retired Emperor to Oki. This established the samurai government as being superior to the imperial court, and the Kamakura shogunate established a stable governance system.

odawara_castle.name: 小田原城
odawara_castle.highlight: 北条早雲が奪い後北条氏100年の本拠となった難攻不落の城。秀吉の23万大軍にも耐えた関東最強の城塞。
odawara_castle.text: 小田原城は1495年（明応4年）に北条早雲（伊勢宗瑞）が大森氏から奪取し、後北条氏の本拠として5代にわたり関東支配の中枢となった城だ。早雲は下剋上の先駆者として伊豆・相模を制し、後北条氏は関東全域に勢力を広げた。1590年に豊臣秀吉が23万の大軍で包囲（小田原征伐）した際も城は容易には落ちなかったが、孤立した北条氏政は最終的に降伏し戦国時代が終焉を迎えた。江戸時代には大久保氏が城主となり、現在の天守は1960年に復元されたもので、春の桜の名所として多くの観光客が訪れる。
odawara_castle.highlight_en: An impregnable castle that served as the base of the Hojo clan for 100 years after being captured by Hojo Soun. The strongest fortress in the Kanto region, which withstood Hideyoshi's 230,000-strong army.
odawara_castle.text_en: Odawara Castle was captured by Hojo Soun (Ise Sozui) from the Omori clan in 1495, and served as the headquarters of the Gohojo clan and became the center of Kanto control for five generations. Soun, as a pioneer in the invasion, took control of Izu and Sagami, and the Gohojo clan expanded its influence throughout the Kanto region. In 1590, when Toyotomi Hideyoshi surrounded the castle with a large army of 230,000 men (Odawara Conquest), the castle did not fall easily, but the isolated Hojo Ujimasa eventually surrendered, and the Sengoku period came to an end. During the Edo period, the Okubo clan became the castle's lord, and the current castle tower was restored in 1960, and is visited by many tourists as a famous spring cherry blossom viewing spot.

shibusawa_asukayama.name: 渋沢栄一記念館・飛鳥山
shibusawa_asukayama.kana: しぶさわえいいちきねんかんあすかやま
shibusawa_asukayama.highlight: 渋沢栄一が晩年を過ごした飛鳥山邸跡。約500の企業を設立した「日本資本主義の父」の思想と生涯を学べる。
shibusawa_asukayama.text: 渋沢栄一は1840年（天保11年）に武蔵国血洗島村（現・埼玉県深谷市）に生まれ、幕臣から明治政府官僚を経て実業家に転じた。第一国立銀行・東京ガス・東京海上保険など約500の企業と約600の社会公共事業の設立・育成に関わり「日本資本主義の父」と呼ばれる。晩年を過ごした東京・飛鳥山の邸宅跡に渋沢史料館が設けられており、旧渋沢庭園の「晩香廬」「青淵文庫」（ともに国の重要文化財）が残る。2024年から新一万円札の肖像に採用され、再び脚光を浴びている。
shibusawa_asukayama.highlight_en: The ruins of the Asukayama residence where Eiichi Shibusawa spent his later years. You can learn about the thoughts and life of the ``father of Japanese capitalism,'' who founded approximately 500 companies.
shibusawa_asukayama.text_en: Eiichi Shibusawa was born in Chiaraijima Village, Musashi Province (present-day Fukaya City, Saitama Prefecture) in 1840 (Tenpo 11), and worked as a retainer of the shogunate, then a Meiji government bureaucrat, and then a businessman. He is known as the ``father of Japanese capitalism'' as he was involved in the establishment and development of approximately 500 companies, including the Daiichi National Bank, Tokyo Gas, and Tokio Marine Insurance, as well as approximately 600 social and public enterprises. The Shibusawa Historical Museum has been established on the site of the mansion where he spent his later years in Asukayama, Tokyo, and the former Shibusawa Gardens, ``Bankoro'' and ``Seibuchi Bunko'' (both nationally important cultural properties) remain. From 2024, his portrait will be featured on the new 10,000 yen bill, and he is once again in the spotlight.

sahara_ino_tadataka.name: 伊能忠敬記念館（佐原）
sahara_ino_tadataka.kana: いのうただたかきねんかん
sahara_ino_tadataka.highlight: 50歳から全国測量を始め日本初の精密地図を完成させた伊能忠敬の旧宅と記念館。小江戸・佐原の商家街に残る。
sahara_ino_tadataka.text: 伊能忠敬は1745年（延享2年）に現在の千葉県山武市に生まれ、17歳で下総国佐原（現・香取市）の商家・伊能家に婿入りして家業を再建した。50歳で引退後に江戸で測量・天文学を学び、1800年から1816年まで17年かけて全国を歩いて測量し「大日本沿海輿地全図」を完成させた。その精度は現代の地図と誤差わずか1/1000という驚異的なもので、江戸時代の技術水準を遥かに超えた業績だ。佐原には旧宅・伊能忠敬記念館があり、江戸情緒漂う小野川沿いの商家街とともに訪問できる。
sahara_ino_tadataka.highlight_en: This is the former home and memorial hall of Tadataka Ino, who began surveying the country at the age of 50 and completed Japan's first precise map. It remains in the merchant district of Sawara, Little Edo.
sahara_ino_tadataka.text_en: Tadataka Ino was born in 1745 in present-day Sammu City, Chiba Prefecture, and at the age of 17 he married into the Ino family, a merchant family in Sawara, Shimousa Province (present-day Katori City), and rebuilt the family business. After retiring at the age of 50, he studied surveying and astronomy in Edo, and spent 17 years from 1800 to 1816 surveying the entire country on foot, completing the ``Great Japan Coastal Land Map.'' Its accuracy was astounding, with an error of just 1/1000 compared to modern maps, an achievement that far exceeded the technological level of the Edo period. In Sawara, there is the Ino Tadataka Memorial Museum, which is a former residence, and can be visited along with the merchant district along the Onogawa River, which has an Edo-style atmosphere.

edo_castle_ruins.name: 江戸城跡（皇居東御苑）
edo_castle_ruins.highlight: 徳川将軍265年の本拠・江戸城。天下普請で築かれた日本最大の城郭は今も皇居の石垣にその威容を伝える。
edo_castle_ruins.text: 江戸城は1457年に太田道灌が築き、1590年に徳川家康が入城してから大改修が行われた。3代将軍・家光の代に全国の大名が参加する「天下普請」で完成した巨大城郭で、天守の高さは約58メートルと推定され日本最大だった。2代将軍・徳川秀忠は参勤交代制度の整備など幕藩体制の骨格を作り、3代家光のもとで鎖国政策が完成した。1657年の明暦の大火で天守は焼失し再建されなかったが、本丸・二の丸・三の丸の石垣と堀が現在も皇居として保存されている。
edo_castle_ruins.name_en: Edo Castle Ruins (Imperial Palace East Garden)
edo_castle_ruins.highlight_en: Edo Castle, the headquarters of the Tokugawa Shogunate for 265 years. Japan's largest castle was built under the Tenka Civil War, and its majesty can still be seen in the stone walls of the Imperial Palace.
edo_castle_ruins.text_en: Edo Castle was built by Ota Dokan in 1457, and underwent major renovations after Tokugawa Ieyasu entered the castle in 1590. It was a gigantic castle completed during the ``Tenka Fusho'' project during the reign of the third shogun, Iemitsu, in which daimyo from all over the country participated, and the castle tower was estimated to be approximately 58 meters high, making it the largest in Japan. The second shogun, Hidetada Tokugawa, created the framework of the shogunate system, including the establishment of the sankin-tatai system, and the policy of national isolation was completed under the third shogun, Iemitsu. The castle tower was destroyed in the Great Meireki Fire of 1657 and was not rebuilt, but the stone walls and moat of Honmaru, Ninomaru, and Sannomaru are still preserved as the Imperial Palace.

miburo_kyoto.name: 壬生寺・新選組屯所跡
miburo_kyoto.kana: みぶでらしんせんぐみとんしょあと
miburo_kyoto.highlight: 新選組が結成当初に屯所を置いた壬生村の旧八木邸・壬生寺。沖田総司も稽古に励んだ幕末剣士たちの聖地。
miburo_kyoto.text: 1863年（文久3年）に京都守護職を補佐するため組織された新選組は、初代局長・芹沢鴨・近藤勇のもと壬生村（現在の京都市中京区）に屯所を置いた。旧前川邸・旧八木邸が現存しており、当時の面影が今も残る。壬生寺には新選組隊士の霊を弔う塔があり、局長・近藤勇の胸像が立つ。沖田総司は一番隊組長として天才剣士の名を轟かせたが、結核に侵されながら幕末の動乱を戦い抜いた。新選組最後の局長・近藤勇が処刑されたのちも、副長・土方歳三は函館まで戦い続けた。
miburo_kyoto.highlight_en: Mibu-dera, the former Yagi residence in Mibu Village, where the Shinsengumi set up its base when it was first formed. A sacred place for swordsmen at the end of the Edo period, where Okita Souji practiced hard.
miburo_kyoto.text_en: The Shinsengumi, which was organized in 1863 (Bunkyu 3) to assist the Kyoto Shugo, established a base in Mibu Village (present-day Nakagyo Ward, Kyoto City) under the first director, Kamo Serizawa and Isamu Kondo. The former Maekawa residence and former Yagi residence still exist, and traces of those days still remain. At Mibu-dera Temple, there is a pagoda dedicated to the souls of Shinsengumi members, and a bust of Isamu Kondo, the chief of the Shinsengumi, stands there. Souji Okita gained fame as a genius swordsman as the leader of the first division, but fought through the turmoil at the end of the Edo period while suffering from tuberculosis. Even after the last Shinsengumi chief, Isamu Kondo, was executed, the vice-commander, Toshizo Hijikata, continued to fight until Hakodate.

ganryujima_shimonoseki.name: 巌流島（宮本武蔵・佐々木小次郎決闘地）
ganryujima_shimonoseki.highlight: 1612年に宮本武蔵と佐々木小次郎が決闘した無人島。「燕返し」対「時間差」の剣豪対決の伝説が今も息づく。
ganryujima_shimonoseki.text: 巌流島（舟島）は下関と北九州の間の関門海峡に浮かぶ小島で、1612年（慶長17年）に宮本武蔵と佐々木小次郎の決闘が行われた場所として知られる。小次郎の流派名「巌流」から「巌流島」と呼ばれるようになった。武蔵は約束の時刻に大幅に遅れて現れ心理的圧迫を与え、一撃で小次郎を倒したという伝説が残る。武蔵はその後も諸国を旅して剣の修行を続け、晩年に熊本で熊本藩主・細川忠利に仕えながら『五輪書』を執筆した。決闘の地として両者の銅像が立ち、関門海峡の潮風が吹き抜ける。
ganryujima_shimonoseki.name_en: Ganryu Island (Miyamoto Musashi and Sasaki Kojiro duel site)
ganryujima_shimonoseki.highlight_en: A deserted island where Miyamoto Musashi and Sasaki Kojiro fought a duel in 1612. The legend of the swordsman showdown between ``Tsubamegaeshi'' and ``Time Difference'' still lives on.
ganryujima_shimonoseki.text_en: Ganryujima (Funajima) is a small island floating in the Kanmon Strait between Shimonoseki and Kitakyushu, and is known as the site of the duel between Miyamoto Musashi and Sasaki Kojiro in 1612. It came to be called ``Ganryujima'' from Kojiro's school name ``Ganryu.'' Legend has it that Musashi appeared much later than the agreed time, put psychological pressure on Kojiro, and defeated Kojiro with a single blow. Musashi continued his sword training by traveling around the country, and in his later years wrote the Book of Five Rings while serving Tadatoshi Hosokawa, the lord of the Kumamoto domain, in Kumamoto. As the site of the duel, bronze statues of both men stand, and the sea breeze from the Kanmon Straits blows through.

okazaki_castle.name: 岡崎城
okazaki_castle.highlight: 徳川家康の生誕地。三河武士を束ねて天下を取る道は、この岡崎城から始まった。
okazaki_castle.text: 岡崎城は1542年（天文11年）に徳川家康が誕生した城で、松平氏代々の居城だ。家康は幼少期に人質として今川氏・織田氏のもとに送られ、桶狭間の戦い後に独立して三河を統一。岡崎を本拠に「三河武士」の忠義の精神を核とした強固な軍団を形成した。1570年に浜松城に移るまで岡崎が本拠地で、家康の天下取りの出発点として「神君出生の地」と尊ばれた。現在の天守は1959年に復元されたもの。城内には家康館が設けられ、大河ドラマとのコラボ展示も充実。桜の名所としても名高い。
okazaki_castle.highlight_en: Birthplace of Tokugawa Ieyasu. The path to uniting the Mikawa samurai and conquering the country began from Okazaki Castle.
okazaki_castle.text_en: Okazaki Castle is the castle where Tokugawa Ieyasu was born in 1542 (Tenbun 11), and is the residence of the Matsudaira clan for generations. Ieyasu was sent as a hostage to the Imagawa and Oda clans when he was a child, and after the Battle of Okehazama he became independent and unified Mikawa. Based in Okazaki, they formed a strong army with the spirit of loyalty of the ``Mikawa samurai'' at its core. Okazaki was the home base until moving to Hamamatsu Castle in 1570, and was revered as the ``birthplace of the gods,'' as it was the starting point for Ieyasu's takeover of the country. The current castle tower was restored in 1959. The Ieyasu Pavilion is set up within the castle, and there are many exhibits in collaboration with historical dramas. It is also famous as a cherry blossom viewing spot.

okehazama_battlefield.name: 桶狭間古戦場
okehazama_battlefield.kana: おけはざまこせんじょう
okehazama_battlefield.highlight: 1560年、織田信長が2000の兵で今川義元の25000大軍を奇襲した天下分け目の合戦地。信長の名を天下に知らしめた一戦。
okehazama_battlefield.text: 1560年（永禄3年）5月、今川義元は25000（諸説あり）の大軍を率いて上洛（京都入り）を目指した。尾張の小大名・織田信長は清洲城でわずか2000の兵を率いて出陣し、桶狭間の狭隘な谷筋で豪雨を突いて奇襲を仕掛けた。義元は本陣で首を取られ今川軍は崩壊、今川氏の覇権は終焉を迎えた。この戦いで信長の名が全国に轟き、徳川家康が今川氏から独立するきっかけにもなった。現在は桶狭間古戦場公園が整備され、義元の墓と信長の像が向き合うように立っている。
okehazama_battlefield.highlight_en: In 1560, Oda Nobunaga attacked Imagawa Yoshimoto's 25,000-strong army by surprise with 2,000 soldiers. The battle that made Nobunaga's name known throughout the world.
okehazama_battlefield.text_en: In May 1560, Yoshimoto Imagawa led a large army of 25,000 soldiers (there are various theories) and headed for Kyoto (entering Kyoto). Oda Nobunaga, a minor feudal lord from Owari, led a mere 2,000 soldiers to Kiyosu Castle and launched a surprise attack in the narrow valley of Okehazama against the heavy rain. Yoshimoto was beheaded at his headquarters, the Imagawa army collapsed, and the Imagawa clan's hegemony came to an end. This battle made Nobunaga's name known throughout the country and served as an opportunity for Tokugawa Ieyasu to become independent from the Imagawa clan. Currently, Okehazama Battlefield Park has been developed, and Yoshimoto's grave and Nobunaga's statue stand facing each other.

gifu_castle.name: 岐阜城（稲葉山城）
gifu_castle.highlight: 斎藤道三が本拠とし織田信長が「天下布武」を掲げた城。標高329mから濃尾平野を見渡した天下人たちの眺望。
gifu_castle.text: 岐阜城（稲葉山城）は難攻不落の山城として戦国時代に重要な役割を担った。斎藤道三は美濃国主としてこの城を本拠に「下克上」の典型を体現した。1567年に織田信長が斎藤氏を滅ぼして入城し、城の名を「岐阜城」に改めて「天下布武」の印を使い始めた。信長はここから全国統一への歩みを加速させた。1600年の関ヶ原の戦いで西軍の拠点となった後に廃城となり、現在の天守は1956年に復元されたもの。標高329メートルの金華山頂からは濃尾平野と長良川が一望できる。
gifu_castle.highlight_en: This castle was the base of Saito Dōsan and Oda Nobunaga's motto of ``Tenka Fubu.'' A view of the people of Japan looking out over the Nobi Plain from an altitude of 329m.
gifu_castle.text_en: Gifu Castle (Inabayama Castle) played an important role during the Sengoku period as an impregnable mountain castle. Dosan Saito, as the lord of Mino Province, used this castle as his base, embodying the epitome of ``Gokujo.'' In 1567, Oda Nobunaga overthrew the Saito clan and entered the castle, changing the name of the castle to ``Gifu Castle'' and beginning to use the seal ``Tenkafubu.'' From this point on, Nobunaga accelerated his progress toward national unification. After serving as a base for the Western Army during the Battle of Sekigahara in 1600, the castle was abandoned, and the current castle tower was restored in 1956. From the summit of Mt. Kinka, which is 329 meters above sea level, you can see the Nobi Plain and the Nagara River.

bodaisan_castle_gifu.name: 菩提山城跡（竹中氏陣屋）
bodaisan_castle_gifu.kana: ぼだいさんじょうあとたけなかしじんや
bodaisan_castle_gifu.highlight: 竹中半兵衛の本拠・菩提山城。わずか16人で稲葉山城を奪取した天才軍師の知略の拠点が関ヶ原近くに残る。
bodaisan_castle_gifu.text: 竹中半兵衛（重治）は岐阜県垂井町の菩提山城を本拠とした戦国時代の武将で、「二兵衛」のひとりとして豊臣秀吉の軍師を務めた天才軍略家だ。1564年にわずか16人で岐阜城（稲葉山城）を一時占拠した奇策で名を馳せた。秀吉の播磨攻めに従軍中、1579年に現地で36歳の若さで病没した。「もし半兵衛が生きていれば天下の趨勢も変わっていた」と言われるほどの才能を惜しまれた。山頂の城跡には曲輪・石垣が残り、竹中陣屋の跡には竹中氏を祀る陣屋跡と半兵衛の墓がある。
bodaisan_castle_gifu.highlight_en: Bodaiyama Castle, the base of Takenaka Hanbei. The base of the ingenuity of the genius tactician who captured Inabayama Castle with only 16 men remains near Sekigahara.
bodaisan_castle_gifu.text_en: Takenaka Hanbei (Shigeharu) was a military commander during the Sengoku period who was based at Bodaiyama Castle in Tarui Town, Gifu Prefecture, and was a genius strategist who served as one of the ``Nibei'' and a tactician to Toyotomi Hideyoshi. He became famous for his ingenious plan to temporarily occupy Gifu Castle (Inabayama Castle) in 1564 with just 16 people. While participating in Hideyoshi's attack on Harima, he died of illness at the young age of 36 in 1579. His talent was so greatly missed that it was said, ``If Hanbei had lived, the trends of the world would have changed.'' Kuruwa and stone walls remain at the castle ruins at the top of the mountain, and at the site of Takenaka Jinya there are the remains of the Jinya where the Takenaka clan is enshrined and the grave of Hanbei.

honnoji_ruins.name: 本能寺跡（本能寺の変）
honnoji_ruins.highlight: 1582年6月2日、明智光秀が主君・織田信長を討った「本能寺の変」の舞台。歴史最大の謎が今も議論され続ける地。
honnoji_ruins.text: 1582年（天正10年）6月2日、織田信長が宿泊していた京都の本能寺を明智光秀軍1万3千が包囲した。信長は「是非に及ばず」と言い放ち少数の近習と戦ったが、火が回ると本能寺内で自刃したとされる（享年49歳）。光秀の謀反の動機は「怨恨説」「野望説」「黒幕説」などが今も議論される歴史最大の謎だ。変の報を聞いた羽柴秀吉は直ちに中国大返しを決行し、13日後の山崎の戦いで光秀を討った。現在の本能寺は後に移転再建されたもので、元の本能寺跡は石碑のみが残る。
honnoji_ruins.highlight_en: The scene of the ``Honnoji Incident'' on June 2, 1582, when Akechi Mitsuhide defeated his lord Oda Nobunaga. A place where history's greatest mysteries are still being debated.
honnoji_ruins.text_en: On June 2, 1582, 13,000 Akechi Mitsuhide's troops surrounded Honnoji Temple in Kyoto, where Oda Nobunaga was staying. Nobunaga fought against a small number of his followers, saying, ``I have no choice,'' but when the fire started, it is said that he committed suicide inside Honno-ji Temple (passed away at the age of 49). The motive behind Mitsuhide's rebellion is one of history's greatest mysteries, with theories such as ``grudge theory,'' ``ambition theory,'' and ``mastermind theory'' still being debated. When Hideyoshi Hashiba heard the news of the incident, he immediately carried out a major offensive against China and defeated Mitsuhide at the Battle of Yamazaki 13 days later. The current Honnoji Temple was later relocated and rebuilt, and only the stone monument remains of the original Honnoji Temple site.

toji_in_kyoto.name: 等持院（足利将軍家菩提寺）
toji_in_kyoto.highlight: 足利歴代将軍の菩提寺。夢窓疎石が作庭した枯山水に足利尊氏ら15代将軍の木像が安置される室町の聖地。
toji_in_kyoto.text: 等持院は1341年（暦応4年）に足利尊氏が夢窓疎石を開山として創建した臨済宗天龍寺派の寺院で、室町幕府歴代将軍の菩提寺だ。境内には3代・義満の天竜寺境内に対応する「芙蓉池」「清漣亭」などの庭園が残り、方丈内には初代・尊氏から15代・義昭まで全15代の足利将軍の木像が安置されている。足利尊氏は後醍醐天皇の建武新政から離反して室町幕府を開き、南北朝の内乱を経て武家政権の二元的支配を確立した。京都観光では見落とされがちだが、室町文化を理解する上で重要な寺院だ。
toji_in_kyoto.highlight_en: The family temple of successive Ashikaga shoguns. A sacred place in Muromachi where wooden statues of the 15th shoguns, including Takauji Ashikaga, are enshrined in a dry landscape created by Soseki Muso.
toji_in_kyoto.text_en: Toji-in is a temple of the Tenryu-ji sect of the Rinzai sect, founded in 1341 by Takauji Ashikaga, who founded Muso Soseki, and is the family temple of successive shoguns of the Muromachi shogunate. Within the precincts, gardens such as ``Fuyo Pond'' and ``Seiren-tei'' remain, which correspond to the Tenryu-ji Temple grounds of the 3rd generation, Yoshimitsu, and in the hojo, wooden statues of all 15 Ashikaga shoguns, from the first generation, Takauji, to the 15th generation, Yoshiaki, are enshrined. Takauji Ashikaga broke away from Emperor Go-Daigo's Kenmu Restoration and established the Muromachi Shogunate, and after the civil war between the Northern and Southern Courts, he established dual control of the samurai government. Although it is often overlooked when sightseeing in Kyoto, it is an important temple in understanding Muromachi culture.

hojoji_ruins_kyoto.name: 法成寺跡（藤原道長の御堂）
hojoji_ruins_kyoto.highlight: 「この世をば我が世とぞ思ふ」と詠んだ藤原道長が建立した御堂。摂関政治の絶頂を象徴する寺院の遺跡。
hojoji_ruins_kyoto.text: 法成寺は1020年（寛仁4年）に藤原道長が自らの発願で建立した壮大な寺院で、「御堂関白」の異名の由来となった。道長は4人の娘を3人の天皇に嫁がせ（三后同時）、1018年に「この世をば我が世とぞ思ふ望月の虧けたることもなしと思へば」と詠んだ。この歌は藤原家の絶頂と道長の自信を端的に表す。法成寺は御堂・九体阿弥陀堂・五大堂などを備えた平安最大級の寺院だったが、火災と戦乱で失われた。現在は石碑と案内板が残るのみだが、京都御苑周辺に平安王朝の中心地としての歴史が重なる。
hojoji_ruins_kyoto.highlight_en: This temple was built by Fujiwara no Michinaga, who wrote the poem, ``If I consider this world to be my own,'' The ruins of a temple that symbolizes the zenith of regent politics.
hojoji_ruins_kyoto.text_en: Hojo-ji Temple is a magnificent temple built in 1020 by Fujiwara no Michinaga at his own request, and is where the nickname ``Mido Kanpaku'' comes from. Michinaga married four of his daughters to three emperors (three empresses at the same time), and in 1018 he wrote a poem that said, ``If you think of this world as your own, Mochizuki won't let you down.'' This song clearly expresses the peak of the Fujiwara family and Michinaga's confidence. Hojo-ji Temple was one of the largest temples in the Heian period, with a mido hall, nine Amida halls, and a Godaido hall, but it was lost in a fire and war. Currently, only stone monuments and information boards remain, but the area around Kyoto Gyoen National Garden has a history of being the center of the Heian Dynasty.

kusunoki_minatogawa.name: 湊川神社（楠木正成公墓所）
kusunoki_minatogawa.highlight: 後醍醐天皇への忠義を貫いて湊川で散った「大楠公」楠木正成を祀る神社。明治天皇が「贈正一位」を授けた忠臣の聖地。
kusunoki_minatogawa.text: 楠木正成は1336年（建武3年）の湊川の戦いで足利尊氏の大軍に敗れ、弟・正季と刺し違えて壮烈な最期を遂げた。「七生報国」（七度生まれ変わっても国に報いる）の遺言は武士の忠義の象徴とされ、江戸時代以降「大楠公」として称えられた。明治時代には天皇への忠義の象徴として最高位の正一位が贈られ、湊川神社が創建された。正成の本拠・千早赤阪城（大阪府）での籠城戦では少数で幕府軍を翻弄した軍略の天才でもある。神社境内には正成の墓碑があり、今も多くの崇敬者が訪れる。
kusunoki_minatogawa.highlight_en: This shrine is dedicated to Masashige Kusunoki, the Great Kusunoki Duke, who died in the Minatogawa River due to his loyalty to Emperor Go-Daigo. It is a sacred place for the loyal subjects of Emperor Meiji, who bestowed the title of ``Gift First Rank.''
kusunoki_minatogawa.text_en: Masashige Kusunoki was defeated by Takauji Ashikaga's large army at the Battle of Minatogawa in 1336 (Kenmu 3), and met a tragic end in a stabbing with his younger brother Masaki. The will of ``Nanasho Hokoku'' (repay the country even if you are reborn seven times) was considered a symbol of the samurai's loyalty, and from the Edo period onwards, he was praised as ``Great Kusunoki.'' During the Meiji period, the highest rank of Shoichii was awarded as a symbol of loyalty to the Emperor, and Minatogawa Shrine was built. He was also a military genius who toyed with the shogunate army in a small group during the siege battle at Masashige's stronghold, Chihaya-Akasaka Castle (Osaka Prefecture). Masashige's tombstone is located within the shrine grounds, and many worshipers still visit it.

fukuzawa_nakatsu.name: 福沢諭吉旧居（中津）
fukuzawa_nakatsu.kana: ふくざわゆきちきゅうきょ
fukuzawa_nakatsu.highlight: 「天は人の上に人を造らず」。慶應義塾の創設者・福沢諭吉が幼少期を過ごした大分県中津の旧居が公開されている。
fukuzawa_nakatsu.text: 福沢諭吉は1835年（天保6年）に大坂で生まれたが、幼少期を父の赴任先・中津藩（大分県中津市）で過ごした。封建的身分制度への強い反発を持ちながら成長した諭吉は、緒方洪庵の適塾で蘭学を学んだ後、欧米に3度渡航して西洋文明を日本に紹介した。著書『学問のすゝめ』は「天は人の上に人を造らず、人の下に人を造らず」の一節で始まり、340万部を売り上げた明治最大のベストセラーとなった。慶應義塾を創設し独立自尊の精神を広めた諭吉の旧居は中津市の史跡として公開されている。
fukuzawa_nakatsu.highlight_en: "Heaven does not create man above man." The former residence of Keio University founder Yukichi Fukuzawa in Nakatsu, Oita Prefecture, where he spent his childhood, has been opened to the public.
fukuzawa_nakatsu.text_en: Yukichi Fukuzawa was born in Osaka in 1835 (Tenpo 6), but spent his childhood in the Nakatsu domain (Nakatsu City, Oita Prefecture), where his father was posted. Yukichi grew up with a strong opposition to the feudal class system, and after studying Dutch studies at Koan Ogata's Tekijuku, he traveled to Europe and America three times to introduce Western civilization to Japan. His book ``Advance of Learning'' begins with the line, ``Heaven does not create a person above a person, nor a person below a person,'' and became the biggest bestseller of the Meiji period, selling 3.4 million copies. The former residence of Yukichi, who founded Keio University and spread the spirit of independence and self-respect, is open to the public as a historic site in Nakatsu City.

okao_castle_kochi.name: 岡豊城跡（長宗我部氏の本拠）
okao_castle_kochi.highlight: 四国を統一した長宗我部元親の本拠。土佐の小領主から「姫若子」が四国の覇者となった戦国の奇跡の出発点。
okao_castle_kochi.text: 岡豊城は土佐国（現高知県）の長宗我部氏の居城で、標高97メートルの山頂に築かれた山城だ。長宗我部元親は幼少期「姫若子」と呼ばれ文弱に見えたが、初陣で獅子奮迅の戦いぶりを見せ「鬼若子」に変身した。1575年に長浜の戦いで一条氏を破り土佐を統一し、その後20年で四国4カ国をほぼ平定した。しかし1585年に豊臣秀吉の四国征伐に敗れ土佐一国のみに封じられた。城跡からは高知平野と土佐湾を一望でき、高知県立歴史民俗資料館が隣接する。元親の銅像が駐車場に立つ。
okao_castle_kochi.name_en: Okatoyo Castle Ruins (base of the Chosokabe clan)
okao_castle_kochi.highlight_en: The headquarters of Motochika Chosokabe, who unified Shikoku. The starting point of the miracle of the Sengoku period, when ``Himewakako'' became the ruler of Shikoku from a small feudal lord in Tosa.
okao_castle_kochi.text_en: Okatoyo Castle is the residence of the Chosokabe clan of Tosa Province (present-day Kochi Prefecture), and is a mountain castle built on the summit of a mountain 97 meters above sea level. Motochika Chosokabe was called ``Himewakako'' when he was young and appeared to be a weak writer, but in his first battle he showed a lion's courage and swiftness in battle and transformed into ``Oniwakako.'' In 1575, he defeated the Ichijo clan at the Battle of Nagahama and unified Tosa, and in the next 20 years he largely subdued the four countries of Shikoku. However, in 1585, it was defeated in Toyotomi Hideyoshi's conquest of Shikoku and was confined to Tosa Province. The castle ruins offer a panoramic view of Kochi Plain and Tosa Bay, and the Kochi Prefectural Museum of History and Folklore is adjacent to it. A bronze statue of Motochika stands in the parking lot.

kitasato_memorial_kumamoto.name: 北里柴三郎記念館（小国町）
kitasato_memorial_kumamoto.kana: きたさとしばさぶろうきねんかん
kitasato_memorial_kumamoto.highlight: 破傷風・ペスト研究で近代医学を切り開いた北里柴三郎の生誕地。熊本県小国町に記念館と生家が残る。
kitasato_memorial_kumamoto.text: 北里柴三郎は1853年（嘉永5年）に熊本県阿蘇郡小国村（現・小国町）に生まれた近代医学の先駆者だ。ドイツ・コッホ研究所で破傷風菌の純粋培養と血清療法を世界で初めて確立し（1890年）、続いてペスト菌を香港で発見（1894年）した。帰国後に伝染病研究所・北里研究所を設立し、日本の近代医学の礎を築いた。弟子・志賀潔による赤痢菌発見にも貢献し、ノーベル賞候補にも挙がった。2024年から千円札の肖像に採用されており、記念館では業績と生涯を詳しく紹介している。
kitasato_memorial_kumamoto.highlight_en: The birthplace of Shibasaburo Kitasato, who pioneered modern medicine through research on tetanus and plague. A memorial hall and his birthplace remain in Oguni Town, Kumamoto Prefecture.
kitasato_memorial_kumamoto.text_en: Shibasaburo Kitasato was a pioneer of modern medicine who was born in 1853 in Oguni Village, Aso District, Kumamoto Prefecture (now Oguni Town). He established the world's first pure culture of Clostridium tetani and serum therapy at the Koch Institute in Germany (1890), and subsequently discovered the plague bacterium in Hong Kong (1894). After returning to Japan, he established the Kitasato Institute of Infectious Disease Research and laid the foundation for modern medicine in Japan. He also contributed to the discovery of Shigella by his disciple Kiyoshi Shiga, and was nominated for the Nobel Prize. His portrait will be featured on the 1,000 yen bill starting in 2024, and the memorial museum introduces his achievements and life in detail.

yanagawa_tachibana.name: 柳川藩・立花氏の旧居
yanagawa_tachibana.kana: やながわはんたちばなしきゅうきょ
yanagawa_tachibana.highlight: 関ヶ原で改易されながら旧領を回復した戦国唯一の武将・立花宗茂の本拠。水郷・柳川の堀割は今も宗茂の時代の面影を残す。
yanagawa_tachibana.text: 立花宗茂は九州の名将・高橋紹運の子で、立花道雪の娘婿となり柳川城主となった。関ヶ原の戦いで西軍に属して改易されたが、その武名と人柄から旧臣たちの嘆願が続き、1620年に旧領・柳川藩を回復した。「関ヶ原で改易されながら旧領をそのまま回復した武将は宗茂ただひとり」と言われ、戦国最高の評価を受ける。徳川家からの信頼も厚く、大阪冬の陣・夏の陣でも活躍した。水郷・柳川の堀割を船で巡る「川下り」は江戸時代の城下町の面影を今に伝える名物観光になっている。
yanagawa_tachibana.name_en: Former residence of the Tachibana clan of the Yanagawa domain
yanagawa_tachibana.highlight_en: The home base of Muneshige Tachibana, the only warlord of the Sengoku period who regained his former territory after being abducted at Sekigahara. The water village of Yanagawa's moat still retains traces of the days of Muneshige.
yanagawa_tachibana.text_en: Muneshige Tachibana was the son of Joun Takahashi, a famous general in Kyushu, and became the son-in-law of Michisetsu Tachibana and the lord of Yanagawa Castle. At the Battle of Sekigahara, he belonged to the Western army and was given up, but due to his military name and personality, his former vassals continued to petition him, and in 1620 he regained his former territory, the Yanagawa domain. It is said that Muneshige was the only military commander who was able to restore his former territory intact even though it was abducted at Sekigahara, and he received the highest praise from the Sengoku period. He was highly trusted by the Tokugawa family, and was active in the Osaka Winter Siege and Summer Siege. ``River rafting'' by boat along the moat of Yanagawa, a water town, has become a famous tourist attraction that still retains the vestiges of the castle town of the Edo period.

sugita_genpaku_obama.name: 杉田玄白記念公共図書館・小浜
sugita_genpaku_obama.kana: すぎたげんぱくきねんこうきょとしょかん
sugita_genpaku_obama.highlight: 『解体新書』翻訳で日本の西洋医学の扉を開いた杉田玄白が仕えた若狭藩の城下町・小浜。近代医学の夜明けの地。
sugita_genpaku_obama.text: 杉田玄白は1733年（享保18年）に若狭国（現福井県）小浜藩の医師の家に生まれ、藩医として活躍した。1771年（明和8年）に江戸で刑死した罪人の解剖（腑分け）を見学した玄白は、手にしていたオランダの解剖書「ターヘル・アナトミア」の精密さに驚き、前野良沢・中川淳庵らとともに翻訳を開始。3年半の苦闘の末に1774年に『解体新書』を刊行した。これが日本初の本格的な西洋医学書となり、蘭学の発展と近代医学の基礎を築いた。晩年の著書『蘭学事始』には苦労の翻訳作業の様子が生き生きと描かれている。
sugita_genpaku_obama.name_en: Genpaku Sugita Memorial Public Library, Obama
sugita_genpaku_obama.highlight_en: Obama is a castle town in the Wakasa domain where Genpaku Sugita, who opened the door to Western medicine in Japan with his translation of Kaitai Shinsho, served. The dawn of modern medicine.
sugita_genpaku_obama.text_en: Genpaku Sugita was born in 1733 (Kyoho 18) into a family of doctors in the Obama domain of Wakasa Province (present-day Fukui Prefecture), and was active as a doctor for the domain. In 1771 (Meiwa 8), Genpaku observed the dissection (dissection) of criminals executed in Edo, and was amazed at the precision of the Dutch anatomical book ``Taher Anatomia'' that he had in hand, and began translating it with Ryotaku Maeno, Jun'an Nakagawa, and others. After three and a half years of struggle, he published ``Kaitai Shinsho'' in 1774. This became Japan's first full-fledged Western medical book, and laid the foundation for the development of Dutch studies and modern medicine. In his late book, ``Dangaku Jijisho'', he vividly describes the laborious translation process.

ono_imoko_memorial.name: 法隆寺周辺・小野妹子ゆかりの地
ono_imoko_memorial.kana: ほうりゅうじしゅうへんおののいもこゆかりのち
ono_imoko_memorial.highlight: 「日出づる処の天子」の親書を隋に届けた小野妹子が活躍した飛鳥時代の政治的中心地。聖徳太子の外交政策の実行者。
ono_imoko_memorial.text: 小野妹子は飛鳥時代の外交官で、607年（推古天皇15年）に聖徳太子の命を受けて遣隋使として隋の煬帝のもとへ派遣された。「日出づる処の天子、書を日没する処の天子に致す」という対等外交を主張する国書を届けた妹子の行動は、当時の国際常識から大きく外れた挑戦的なものだったが、隋からの返礼使を伴って帰国することに成功した。翌608年には再び隋へ渡り、高向玄理・南淵請安らを留学生として同行させた。法隆寺周辺は聖徳太子・小野妹子らが活動した飛鳥文化の中心地だ。
ono_imoko_memorial.name_en: Around Horyuji Temple/Places related to Imoko Ono
ono_imoko_memorial.highlight_en: 「日出づる処の天子」の親書を隋に届けた小野妹子が活躍した飛鳥時代の政治的中心地。 Executor of Prince Shotoku's foreign policy.
ono_imoko_memorial.text_en: 小野妹子は飛鳥時代の外交官で、607年（推古天皇15年）に聖徳太子の命を受けて遣隋使として隋の煬帝のもとへ派遣された。 「日出づる処の天子、書を日没する処の天子に致す」という対等外交を主張する国書を届けた妹子の行動は、当時の国際常識から大きく外れた挑戦的なものだったが、隋からの返礼使を伴って帰国することに成功した。 The following year, in 608, he traveled to Sui again and brought along Genri Takamukai and Ukeyasu Nanbuchi as exchange students. The area around Horyuji Temple is the center of Asuka culture, where Prince Shotoku and Imoko Ono were active.

fujiwara_kyo_ruins.name: 藤原宮跡
fujiwara_kyo_ruins.highlight: 694年から710年まで3代の天皇が居住した最初の本格的宮都。藤原不比等が大宝律令を完成させた「律令国家の心臓部」。
fujiwara_kyo_ruins.text: 藤原京は694年（持統8年）に持統天皇が遷都した日本最初の本格的な宮都で、現在の奈良県橿原市に位置する。中国の長安をモデルに碁盤の目状の街路を持ち、東西約5.3キロ・南北約4.8キロの規模を誇った。藤原不比等は持統・文武・元明天皇の三代に仕え、大宝律令（701年）と養老律令の制定を主導して律令制度を確立した。不比等は藤原氏の権勢を固め、娘・宮子を文武天皇に嫁がせて天皇家と藤原氏の縁を結んだ。藤原京は平城京への遷都（710年）まで16年間使用された。菜の花と大和三山の景色が美しい。
fujiwara_kyo_ruins.highlight_en: The first full-fledged imperial capital where three emperors lived from 694 to 710. The "heart of the Ritsuryo state" where Fujiwara Fuhito completed the Taiho Ritsuryo code.
fujiwara_kyo_ruins.text_en: Fujiwarakyo was Japan's first full-fledged imperial capital, where Emperor Jito moved it in 694 (8th year of Jito), and it is located in present-day Kashihara City, Nara Prefecture. Modeled after Chang'an in China, it had a grid-like grid of streets, and boasted a size of approximately 5.3 kilometers from east to west and approximately 4.8 kilometers from north to south. FUJIWARA no Fuhito served three generations, Emperor Jito, Emperor Bunmu, and Emperor Genmei, and established the Ritsuryo system by leading the enactment of the Taiho Ritsuryo Code (701) and the Yoro Ritsuryo Code. Fuhito consolidated the power of the Fujiwara clan and married his daughter, Miyako, to Emperor Monmu, thereby creating a bond between the imperial family and the Fujiwara clan. Fujiwara-kyo was used for 16 years until the capital was transferred to Heijo-kyo in 710. The scenery of rape blossoms and Yamato Sanzan is beautiful.

kamimachi_wakayama_castle.name: 和歌山城（紀州徳川家）
kamimachi_wakayama_castle.highlight: 紀州藩55万石の居城。8代将軍・徳川吉宗が紀州藩主として藩政改革を行い天下を取る力を蓄えた城。
kamimachi_wakayama_castle.text: 和歌山城は1585年（天正13年）に豊臣秀吉の弟・秀長が築城し、江戸時代には御三家のひとつ・紀州徳川家55万石の居城となった。徳川吉宗は1705年に紀州藩主となり、倹約・新田開発・財政再建に取り組んだ。その手腕が認められ1716年に8代将軍に就任し、享保の改革を断行して幕府財政を再建した。「暴れん坊将軍」として時代劇でも人気の吉宗は、サツマイモ・朝鮮人参の普及など庶民政策でも知られる。城は太平洋戦争の空襲で焼失したが1958年に復元され、虎伏山に立つ三連立天守が美しい。
kamimachi_wakayama_castle.highlight_en: The residence of the Kishu domain with a capital of 550,000 koku. A castle where the 8th shogun, Yoshimune Tokugawa, as the lord of the Kishu domain reformed the domain's administration and amassed the power to take over the country.
kamimachi_wakayama_castle.text_en: Wakayama Castle was built in 1585 by Toyotomi Hideyoshi's younger brother Hidenaga, and during the Edo period it became the residence of the Kishu Tokugawa family, one of the three imperial families, with a capital of 550,000 koku. Tokugawa Yoshimune became the lord of the Kishu domain in 1705 and worked on frugality, new rice field development, and financial restructuring. His skills were recognized and he was appointed as the 8th shogun in 1716, carrying out the Kyoho reforms and rebuilding the shogunate's finances. Yoshimune, who is popular in historical dramas as the ``rambunctious general,'' is also known for his policies for the common people, such as the promotion of sweet potatoes and Korean ginseng. The castle was destroyed by air raids during the Pacific War, but was restored in 1958, and the three tower towers on Mt. Torafuse are beautiful.

tanuma_sagara_castle.name: 相良城跡（田沼意次の城下町）
tanuma_sagara_castle.highlight: 老中・田沼意次が幕府の重商主義政策を推進した相良藩5万7千石の城下町。「賄賂政治」の陰に隠れた経済センスの地。
tanuma_sagara_castle.text: 田沼意次は1719年に生まれ、10代将軍・徳川家治の信任を得て老中として幕政を主導した。株仲間の公認・長崎貿易の振興・蝦夷地（北海道）開発・印旛沼干拓など重商主義的な政策を積極的に推進した革新的政治家だ。しかし天明の大飢饉・浅間山噴火などの天災と賄賂が横行する政治風土から評価が低下し、家治の死後に失脚した。後世「田沼時代」として重商主義の先駆け的評価を受けており、実は近代経済政策の先見性を持つ人物として再評価が進んでいる。静岡県牧之原市（旧相良町）に相良城跡が残る。
tanuma_sagara_castle.name_en: Sagara Castle Ruins (Tanuma Otsuji Castle Town)
tanuma_sagara_castle.highlight_en: A castle town of 57,000 koku in the Sagara domain, where Roju Tanuma Okitsugu promoted the shogunate's mercantilist policies. A land of economic sense hidden behind "bribery politics".
tanuma_sagara_castle.text_en: Tanuma Otsuji was born in 1719 and gained the trust of the 10th shogun, Ieharu Tokugawa, and led the shogunate as Roju. He was an innovative politician who actively promoted mercantilist policies such as the recognition of Kabu Nakama, the promotion of trade in Nagasaki, the development of Ezo (Hokkaido), and the reclamation of Inbanuma Swamp. However, due to natural disasters such as the Great Tenmei Famine and the eruption of Mt. Asama, and a political climate where bribery was rampant, his reputation declined, and he fell from power after Ieharu's death. He was later praised as a pioneer of mercantilism during the ``Tanuma period,'' and is in fact being reevaluated as a man with the foresight to modern economic policy. The ruins of Sagara Castle remain in Makinohara City, Shizuoka Prefecture (formerly Sagara Town).

iwakura_residence_kyoto.name: 岩倉具視幽棲旧宅
iwakura_residence_kyoto.kana: いわくらともみゆうせいきゅうたく
iwakura_residence_kyoto.highlight: 倒幕の陰謀を練った岩倉具視の隠棲地。公武合体派から倒幕の参謀へ転換した明治維新の仕掛け人の旧宅。
iwakura_residence_kyoto.text: 岩倉具視は公家出身でありながら幕末の政局を動かした維新の参謀だ。当初は和宮降嫁（公武合体）を推進したが、攘夷派公家によって京都を追放され、この洛北岩倉の地に約5年間幽棲した。この蟄居期間に倒幕派との連絡を密にし、大政奉還後に「王政復古の大号令」のシナリオを描いた。明治維新後は右大臣として岩倉使節団（1871〜73年）を率いて欧米を視察し、帰国後は内治優先・漸進的近代化路線を主導した。旧宅は国の重要文化財に指定されており、往時の幕末政局を物語る。
iwakura_residence_kyoto.highlight_en: The hiding place of Tomomi Iwakura, who hatched a plot to overthrow the Shogunate. This is the former home of one of the architects of the Meiji Restoration who transitioned from being a member of the kobu union to a staff member who overthrew the shogunate.
iwakura_residence_kyoto.text_en: Tomomi Iwakura was a member of the Meiji Restoration staff who controlled the political situation at the end of the Edo period, although he was a nobleman. At first, he promoted the marriage of Kazunomiya (kobu union), but he was expelled from Kyoto by the Joi faction court nobles and lived in exile in Iwakura, Rakuhoku for about five years. During this period of seclusion, he maintained close contact with those who overthrew the shogunate, and drew up a scenario for a ``grand edict for the restoration of imperial rule'' after the restoration of imperial rule. After the Meiji Restoration, he led the Iwakura Mission (1871-1873) as Minister of the Right and toured Europe and America, and after returning to Japan, he led a policy of prioritizing domestic rule and gradual modernization. The former residence has been designated as a national important cultural property and is a testament to the political situation at the end of the Edo period.

yamagata_aritomo_murinan.name: 無鄰菴（山縣有朋の別荘）
yamagata_aritomo_murinan.highlight: 明治を陰で動かした山縣有朋が晩年に過ごした南禅寺そばの名庭。1903年の日露戦争前夜の国策会議もここで行われた。
yamagata_aritomo_murinan.text: 無鄰菴は山縣有朋が1896年（明治29年）に南禅寺近くに作った別荘で、七代目・小川治兵衛が作庭した近代日本庭園の傑作として国の名勝に指定されている。有朋は松下村塾出身の長州人で、奇兵隊から明治陸軍を創設し二度の内閣総理大臣を務めた。「山縣系軍閥」として昭和軍国主義の遠因を作った一方で、明治国家の制度設計において最も強大な政治権力を握り続けた人物だ。1903年にはここで伊藤博文・桂太郎・小村寿太郎との「無鄰菴会議」が開かれ日露戦争前夜の外交方針が決定された。
yamagata_aritomo_murinan.highlight_en: A famous garden near Nanzenji Temple where Aritomo Yamagata, who was behind the Meiji era, spent his later years. The national policy meeting on the eve of the Russo-Japanese War in 1903 was also held here.
yamagata_aritomo_murinan.text_en: Murin-an is a villa built by Aritomo Yamagata near Nanzen-ji Temple in 1896 (Meiji 29), and is designated as a national scenic spot as a masterpiece of modern Japanese gardens created by the seventh generation, Jihei Ogawa. Aritomo was a Choshu native who graduated from the Matsushita Village School, founded the Meiji Army from the Kiheiheitai, and served as Prime Minister twice. While he was the cause of Showa militarism as a ``Yamagata-type warlord,'' he continued to hold the greatest political power in designing the system of the Meiji state. In 1903, the ``Murinan Conference'' was held here with Hirobumi Ito, Taro Katsura, and Jutaro Komura, and diplomatic policy was decided on the eve of the Russo-Japanese War.

tanabe_castle_hosokawa.name: 田辺城跡（細川幽斎の籠城地）
tanabe_castle_hosokawa.highlight: 細川幽斎が関ヶ原前夜に籠城し「古今伝授」の断絶を恐れた朝廷が和睦を仲介した伝説の城。文武両道の極致。
tanabe_castle_hosokawa.text: 細川幽斎（藤孝）は武将でありながら「古今伝授」（古今和歌集の秘伝の解釈を口伝する文化の継承者）でもあった。関ヶ原前夜の1600年、西軍・石田三成方の1万5千の大軍が田辺城に500の兵で籠城する幽斎を包囲した。籠城が長引く中、朝廷は幽斎が持つ「古今伝授」が断絶することを恐れて勅使を遣わし和睦を仲介。幽斎は秘伝を天皇に伝授して開城した。文化と武力を兼ね備えた幽斎の生き様は戦国きっての文化人武将として知られ、田辺城跡は現在も舞鶴公園として残っている。
tanabe_castle_hosokawa.highlight_en: This is a legendary castle where Hosokawa Yusai imprisoned himself on the eve of Sekigahara, and where the Imperial Court, fearing the end of ``Kokin transmission'', mediated peace. The pinnacle of both literary and martial arts.
tanabe_castle_hosokawa.text_en: Hosokawa Yusai (Fujitaka) was a military commander, but also a ``Kokindenju'' (inheritor of the culture of orally transmitting secret interpretations of Kokin Wakashu). In 1600, on the eve of Sekigahara, a large army of 15,000 soldiers led by Mitsunari Ishida of the Western Army besieged Yusai, who was holed up in Tanabe Castle with 500 soldiers. As the siege dragged on, the imperial court, fearing that Yusai's ``kokin transmission'' would be cut off, sent an imperial envoy to mediate peace. Yusai taught the secret to the Emperor and opened the castle. Yusai's lifestyle, which combined culture and military power, made him known as the most cultural military commander of the Sengoku period, and the ruins of Tanabe Castle still remain today as Maizuru Park.

kamo_mabuchi_hamamatsu.name: 賀茂真淵記念館（浜松）
kamo_mabuchi_hamamatsu.kana: かものまぶちきねんかん
kamo_mabuchi_hamamatsu.highlight: 万葉集研究で国学の礎を築き本居宣長に影響を与えた賀茂真淵の生地・浜松。「ますらをぶり」を提唱した国学の巨人。
kamo_mabuchi_hamamatsu.text: 賀茂真淵は1697年（元禄10年）に遠江国（現・静岡県浜松市）に生まれた国学者で、荷田春満に師事した後に江戸で国学を大成させた。万葉集を精力的に研究し「ますらをぶり」（男性的・力強い歌風）を提唱、古代日本の精神に回帰することを説いた。1763年に本居宣長と松坂で一夜語り合い（「松坂の一夜」）、宣長が古事記研究に進む方向を定めた師弟関係で知られる。江戸の屋敷には多くの門人が集まり、国学四大人（真淵・宣長・春満・篤胤）のひとりとして近代国学の礎を築いた。
kamo_mabuchi_hamamatsu.highlight_en: Hamamatsu is the birthplace of Mabuchi Kamo, whose research on Manyoshu laid the foundation for Japanese studies and influenced Norinaga Motoori. A giant of Japanese studies who advocated ``Marasura Buri.''
kamo_mabuchi_hamamatsu.text_en: Mabuchi Kamo was a Japanese scholar who was born in Totomi Province (present-day Hamamatsu City, Shizuoka Prefecture) in 1697 (Genroku 10), and after studying under Harumitsu Kada, he completed his studies in Japanese in Edo. He vigorously studied the Manyoshu and advocated ``Masura-oburi'' (masculine, powerful style of poetry), calling for a return to the spirit of ancient Japan. He is known for his one-night talk with Norinaga Motoori in Matsuzaka in 1763 ('One Night at Matsuzaka'), and the relationship between teacher and student that set Norinaga's direction in researching the Kojiki. Many disciples gathered at his mansion in Edo, and as one of the four great masters of Japanese studies (Mabuchi, Norinaga, Harumitsu, and Atsutane), he laid the foundation for modern Japanese studies.

matsuura_monument.name: 松浦武四郎記念館
matsuura_monument.kana: まつうらたけしろうきねんかん
matsuura_monument.highlight: 北海道の名付け親・松浦武四郎の出身地・三重県松阪の記念館。6度の北海道探検の記録と資料を公開。
matsuura_monument.text: 松浦武四郎は1818年（文政元年）に伊勢国（現三重県）に生まれた幕末の探検家だ。10代後半から全国を放浪し、30代以降は6度にわたり蝦夷地（北海道）を探検して詳細な地図と報告書を作成した。1869年に新政府から蝦夷地の名称案を求められた際、「北加伊道」など6案を提出し「北海道」に決定した。アイヌの人々の文化と言語を記録した先駆的民族学者でもある。生家の近くに記念館が設けられ、探検日誌や地図などの資料が展示されている。
matsuura_monument.highlight_en: A memorial museum in Matsusaka, Mie Prefecture, the birthplace of Takeshiro Matsuura, the godfather of Hokkaido. Records and materials from six Hokkaido expeditions are released.
matsuura_monument.text_en: Takeshiro Matsuura was an explorer born in Ise Province (present-day Mie Prefecture) in 1818 (first year of the Bunsei era) at the end of the Edo period. Since his late teens, he has been wandering around the country, and since his 30s, he has explored Ezochi (Hokkaido) six times and created detailed maps and reports. In 1869, when the new government asked for a proposed name for Ezochi, six proposals were submitted, including ``Kitakanido,'' and ``Hokkaido'' was chosen. He was also a pioneering ethnographer who recorded the culture and language of the Ainu people. A memorial hall has been set up near his birthplace, and materials such as expedition logs and maps are on display.

yoda_obihiro.name: 依田勉三入植地（帯広）
yoda_obihiro.kana: よだべんぞうにゅうしょくち
yoda_obihiro.highlight: 依田勉三が率いた「晩成社」が十勝平野の開拓を始めた地。荒野を農地に変えた北海道農業の原点。
yoda_obihiro.text: 依田勉三は1853年に静岡県松崎町に生まれ、1882年（明治15年）に同志27人と「晩成社」を組織して十勝の原野に入植した。当時の十勝平野は原始林と湿地が広がる未開の地で、開拓の連続的失敗にも諦めずに農業・牧畜を続けた。勉三の不屈の精神は後続の移民を呼び十勝農業の礎となった。「農は国の大本なり」を信条に生涯を北海道開拓に捧げ、1925年に帯広で没した。帯広には入植地の記念碑が立ち、依田の意志を継いだ十勝農業が今日の農業王国を形成している。
yoda_obihiro.highlight_en: This is where Banseisha, led by Benzo Yoda, began developing the Tokachi plains. The origin of Hokkaido agriculture, which turned wilderness into farmland.
yoda_obihiro.text_en: Benzo Yoda was born in Matsuzaki-cho, Shizuoka Prefecture in 1853, and in 1882 (Meiji 15), he and 27 comrades formed Bansei-sha and settled in the wilderness of Tokachi. At that time, the Tokachi Plain was an unexplored area with vast expanses of primeval forests and wetlands, and despite successive failures in cultivation, they continued farming and livestock farming. Benzo's indomitable spirit attracted subsequent immigrants and became the foundation of Tokachi agriculture. He devoted his life to developing Hokkaido with the belief that ``Agriculture is the foundation of the country,'' and died in Obihiro in 1925. A monument to the settlement stands in Obihiro, and Tokachi agriculture, which inherited Yoda's will, has formed today's agricultural kingdom.

osamu_dazai_kanagi.name: 太宰治記念館「斜陽館」
osamu_dazai_kanagi.kana: だざいおさむきねんかんしゃようかん
osamu_dazai_kanagi.highlight: 津軽の大地主の邸宅に生まれた作家・太宰治の生家「斜陽館」。『人間失格』の著者の出生の地。
osamu_dazai_kanagi.text: 太宰治（本名・津島修治）は1909年（明治42年）に青森県北津軽郡金木町（現・五所川原市）の大地主の家に生まれた。生家は明治40年に建てられた大規模な和洋折衷の邸宅で、現在は太宰治記念館「斜陽館」として公開されている。太宰は東大仏文科在学中から同人誌「海豹」「青い花」などで活躍し、『走れメロス』『富嶽百景』『人間失格』など不朽の名作を残した。1948年6月に玉川上水に入水し39歳で没した。金木町には太宰の「ふるさと」が息づき、津軽の風土と文学の関係を深く感じられる。
osamu_dazai_kanagi.highlight_en: Shayokan is the birthplace of the writer Osamu Dazai, who was born in the mansion of a large landowner in Tsugaru. Birthplace of the author of No Longer Human.
osamu_dazai_kanagi.text_en: Osamu Dazai (real name Shuji Tsushima) was born in 1909 (Meiji 42) into a family of a large landowner in Kanagi-cho, Kitatsugaru-gun, Aomori Prefecture (present-day Goshogawara City). His birthplace was a large-scale Japanese-Western style mansion built in 1900, and is now open to the public as the Osamu Dazai Memorial Hall, Shayokan. Dazai was active in doujinshi such as ``Umihyo'' and ``Aoihana'' while he was a student at the Department of French Literature at the University of Tokyo, and left timeless masterpieces such as ``Run, Melos,'' ``One Hundred Views of Mt. Fuji,'' and ``No Longer Human.'' In June 1948, he entered Tamagawa Josui and died at the age of 39. Kanagi-cho is home to Dazai's hometown, and you can deeply feel the relationship between Tsugaru's culture and literature.

hara_takashi_birthplace.name: 原敬記念館（盛岡）
hara_takashi_birthplace.kana: はらたかしきねんかん
hara_takashi_birthplace.highlight: 日本最初の本格政党内閣を組織した「平民宰相」原敬の生誕地・盛岡。爵位を持たず「平民」として首相となった。
hara_takashi_birthplace.text: 原敬は1856年（安政3年）に岩手県盛岡（当時は南部藩）に生まれた。外交官・新聞記者を経て政治家となり、立憲政友会総裁として1918年に日本初の本格的な政党内閣（原内閣）を組織した。華族でない「平民」として首相に就任したため「平民宰相」と呼ばれた。積極的な普通選挙への関心、税制改革など内政に尽力したが1921年に東京駅で刺客に刺され65歳で没した。盛岡には原敬記念館があり、政治活動の記録と共に彼の思想が展示されている。
hara_takashi_birthplace.highlight_en: Morioka is the birthplace of Takashi Hara, the ``commoner prime minister'' who organized Japan's first full-fledged political party cabinet. He became prime minister as a ``commoner'' without having a peerage.
hara_takashi_birthplace.text_en: Takashi Hara was born in Morioka, Iwate Prefecture (then part of the Nanbu domain) in 1856 (Ansei 3). After working as a diplomat and newspaper reporter, he became a politician, and in 1918 formed Japan's first full-fledged political party cabinet (Hara Cabinet) as president of the Rikken Seiyukai. He was called the ``Commoner Prime Minister'' because he assumed the position of Prime Minister as a ``commoner'' who was not a member of the peerage. Although he was actively interested in universal suffrage and devoted himself to domestic affairs, including tax reform, he was stabbed by an assassin at Tokyo Station in 1921 and died at the age of 65. There is a Takashi Hara Memorial Museum in Morioka, where his ideas are exhibited along with records of his political activities.

miyazawa_kenji_hanamaki.name: 宮沢賢治記念館（花巻）
miyazawa_kenji_hanamaki.kana: みやざわけんじきねんかん
miyazawa_kenji_hanamaki.highlight: 「雨ニモマケズ」「銀河鉄道の夜」の詩人・宮沢賢治の故郷・花巻。理想と現実の狭間で生きた天才の足跡を辿る。
miyazawa_kenji_hanamaki.text: 宮沢賢治は1896年（明治29年）に岩手県花巻町（現花巻市）に生まれた詩人・童話作家・農業指導者だ。「雨ニモマケズ」「銀河鉄道の夜」「注文の多い料理店」など、宇宙的・宗教的世界観と東北の自然が融合した独自の作品群を生み出した。花巻農学校の教師として農業技術の普及にも尽力し、「イーハトーブ」（岩手をモデルにした理想郷）の実現を夢見た。37歳で結核により没したが、死後に評価が急騰し今では日本を代表する文学者として世界的に知られる。
miyazawa_kenji_hanamaki.highlight_en: Hanamaki is the hometown of Kenji Miyazawa, the poet of ``Ame Nimo Makezu'' and ``Night on the Galactic Railway.'' Follow in the footsteps of a genius who lived between ideals and reality.
miyazawa_kenji_hanamaki.text_en: Kenji Miyazawa was born in 1896 (Meiji 29) in Hanamaki Town (now Hanamaki City), Iwate Prefecture, and is a poet, fairy tale writer, and agricultural instructor. He has created a unique body of work that combines a cosmic and religious worldview with Tohoku's nature, such as ``Ame Nimo Makezu'', ``Night on the Galaxy Express'', and ``Restaurant with Many Orders''. As a teacher at Hanamaki Agricultural School, he worked hard to spread agricultural technology and dreamed of realizing ``Ihatov'' (a utopia modeled on Iwate). Although he died of tuberculosis at the age of 37, his reputation skyrocketed after his death, and he is now known worldwide as one of Japan's leading literary figures.

noguchi_hideyo_inawashiro.name: 野口英世記念館（猪苗代）
noguchi_hideyo_inawashiro.kana: のぐちひでよきねんかん
noguchi_hideyo_inawashiro.highlight: 黄熱病研究で世界に名を馳せた細菌学者・野口英世の生家跡と記念館。猪苗代湖畔の貧農出身から世界へ飛躍した。
noguchi_hideyo_inawashiro.text: 野口英世は1876年（明治9年）に福島県猪苗代町の貧しい農家に生まれた。幼少期に左手に火傷を負い、医師・渡部鼎の援助で治療を受けたことが医師を志すきっかけとなった。渡米後にロックフェラー医学研究所でオシュコ・トレポネーマの研究（梅毒螺旋菌純粋培養）で世界的名声を得た。1927年に黄熱病研究のためガーナに赴いたが自ら黄熱病に感染し51歳で没した。千円札の肖像として知られる英世の生家跡に記念館が建ち、猪苗代湖を望む景観とともに不屈の生涯を伝えている。
noguchi_hideyo_inawashiro.highlight_en: The birthplace and memorial hall of Hideyo Noguchi, a bacteriologist who became world-famous for his yellow fever research. From a humble farming background on the shores of Lake Inawashiro, he made the leap to the world.
noguchi_hideyo_inawashiro.text_en: Hideyo Noguchi was born in 1876 (Meiji 9) to a poor farmer in Inawashiro Town, Fukushima Prefecture. When he was a child, he suffered a burn on his left hand, and received treatment with the help of doctor Kanae Watanabe, which led him to aspire to become a doctor. After moving to the United States, he gained worldwide fame for his research on Oshco treponema (pure culture of Syphilis spiralis) at the Rockefeller Institute for Medical Research. In 1927, he went to Ghana to research yellow fever, but contracted it himself and died at the age of 51. A memorial hall has been built on the site of Hideyo's birthplace, known for his portrait on the 1,000 yen bill, and tells the story of his indomitable life with a view overlooking Lake Inawashiro.

kanazawa_castle.name: 金沢城・兼六園
kanazawa_castle.kana: かなざわじょうけんろくえん
kanazawa_castle.highlight: 前田利家が築いた加賀百万石の本拠。日本三名園のひとつ兼六園と金沢城が一体となった北陸の文化都市の象徴。
kanazawa_castle.text: 金沢城は前田利家が1583年（天正11年）に入城して以来、加賀藩の本拠として整備された。加賀藩百万石は徳川将軍家に次ぐ大藩として江戸時代を通じて存続し、工芸・学問・文化を積極的に振興した。隣接する兼六園は江戸時代初期から歴代藩主が整備した回遊式庭園で、日本三名園のひとつに数えられる。金沢は戦災を受けなかったため武家屋敷・茶屋街・寺町が往時の姿を残し、北陸最大の文化都市として多くの観光客を集める。
kanazawa_castle.highlight_en: The headquarters of Kaga Hyakumangoku, built by Toshiie Maeda. Kenrokuen, one of Japan's top three gardens, and Kanazawa Castle are a symbol of Hokuriku's cultural city.
kanazawa_castle.text_en: Kanazawa Castle has been maintained as the headquarters of the Kaga clan since Toshiie Maeda entered the castle in 1583 (Tensho 11). The Kaga Domain Hyakumangoku continued throughout the Edo period as the second largest domain after the Tokugawa Shogunate, and actively promoted crafts, scholarship, and culture. The adjacent Kenrokuen Garden is a strolling garden maintained by successive feudal lords since the early Edo period, and is considered one of Japan's top three gardens. Kanazawa was not damaged by the war, so its samurai residences, teahouse district, and temple towns remain intact, and it attracts many tourists as Hokuriku's largest cultural city.

motoori_norinaga_matsusaka.name: 本居宣長記念館（松坂）
motoori_norinaga_matsusaka.kana: もとおりのりながきねんかん
motoori_norinaga_matsusaka.highlight: 国学の大成者・本居宣長が生涯を過ごした松坂の町。35年かけた『古事記伝』の執筆に明け暮れた「知の巨人」の聖地。
motoori_norinaga_matsusaka.text: 本居宣長は1730年（享保15年）に伊勢国松坂（現三重県松阪市）に生まれ、医師として生計を立てながら国学研究を続けた。1763年に賀茂真淵と一夜語り合った「松坂の一夜」を機に『古事記』の研究に専念し、35年をかけて全44巻の『古事記伝』を完成させた。「もののあわれ」を日本文学の本質として提唱し、日本の古典文学・古代語研究の基礎を確立した。その思想は幕末の尊王思想・国粋主義にも影響を与えた。記念館には宣長の自筆稿本・愛用品が展示されている。
motoori_norinaga_matsusaka.highlight_en: Matsuzaka is the town where Norinaga Motoori, a master of Japanese studies, spent his entire life. This is the sacred place of the ``giant of knowledge'' who spent 35 years writing ``Kojikiden.''
motoori_norinaga_matsusaka.text_en: Norinaga Motoori was born in Matsusaka, Ise Province (present-day Matsusaka City, Mie Prefecture) in 1730, and continued to study Japanese studies while earning a living as a doctor. In 1763, he had a one-night conversation with Kamo Mabuchi called ``One Night at Matsuzaka,'' and as a result, he devoted himself to researching the ``Kojiki,'' and it took him 35 years to complete the 44-volume ``Kojikiden.'' He advocated ``mono no aware'' as the essence of Japanese literature, and established the foundation for the study of Japanese classical literature and ancient languages. This ideology also influenced the idea of ​​reverence for the king and nationalism at the end of the Edo period. Norinaga's handwritten manuscripts and favorite items are on display at the memorial hall.

basho_iga_ueno.name: 芭蕉翁記念館（伊賀上野）
basho_iga_ueno.kana: ばしょうおうきねんかん
basho_iga_ueno.highlight: 「古池や蛙飛び込む水の音」。俳聖・松尾芭蕉の生地・伊賀上野。三重の山里から世界を揺るがす詩人が生まれた。
basho_iga_ueno.text: 松尾芭蕉は1644年（正保元年）に伊賀国上野（現三重県伊賀市）に生まれた。藤堂藩に仕えながら俳諧を学び、29歳で江戸へ下って俳諧師として活動した。「古池や蛙飛び込む水の音」（1686年）で侘び・寂びの俳諧を確立し、各地を旅して「おくのほそ道」「野ざらし紀行」など多くの紀行文を著した。俳諧を単なる言葉遊びから芸術の高みへ引き上げた功績は計り知れない。伊賀上野には芭蕉翁記念館と生家跡があり、城下町の情緒と合わせて俳聖の故郷を感じられる。
basho_iga_ueno.highlight_en: "The sound of old ponds and water with frogs jumping in." Iga Ueno is the birthplace of haiku master Matsuo Basho. A poet who shook the world was born from the mountain village of Mie.
basho_iga_ueno.text_en: Matsuo Basho was born in 1644 in Ueno, Iga Province (present-day Iga City, Mie Prefecture). He learned haiku while serving the Todo clan, and at the age of 29 moved to Edo to work as a haiku master. He established the style of wabi/sabi haiku with ``Old Ponds and the Sound of Water in which a Frog Jumps'' (1686), and traveled extensively and wrote many travelogues such as ``Oku no Hosomichi'' and ``Wild Travels.'' His accomplishments in raising haikai from mere word play to the height of art are immeasurable. Iga Ueno is home to the Basho Memorial Museum and the ruins of his birthplace, where you can feel the haiku master's hometown as well as the atmosphere of a castle town.

sawayama_castle_ishida.name: 佐和山城跡（石田三成の居城）
sawayama_castle_ishida.highlight: 「義に生きた」石田三成の居城跡。関ヶ原前夜まで豊臣政権を支えた三成の本拠・彦根に隣接する城山。
sawayama_castle_ishida.text: 佐和山城は滋賀県彦根市にある山城で、石田三成が拠点とした城として知られる。三成は豊臣秀吉の家臣として検地・朝鮮出兵の兵站管理など行政・実務で卓越した才能を発揮した。秀吉没後、徳川家康との対立が深まり関ヶ原の戦いでは西軍の大将として戦ったが敗退し処刑された。かつては「悪役」とされた三成だが近年は「義のために戦った」忠義の人として再評価が著しく、人気が急上昇している。城跡からは琵琶湖を一望でき、近隣の石田三成像と合わせて三成の生き様を偲べる。
sawayama_castle_ishida.highlight_en: The castle ruins of Mitsunari Ishida, who ``lived righteously.'' Shiroyama, adjacent to Hikone, was the base of Mitsunari, who supported the Toyotomi government until the eve of Sekigahara.
sawayama_castle_ishida.text_en: Sawayama Castle is a mountain castle located in Hikone City, Shiga Prefecture, and is known as the castle where Ishida Mitsunari was based. As a vassal of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, Mitsunari displayed outstanding talent in administrative and practical matters, including land surveying and managing the logistics of dispatching troops to Korea. After Hideyoshi's death, the conflict with Tokugawa Ieyasu deepened, and he fought as a general of the Western army at the Battle of Sekigahara, but was defeated and executed. Mitsunari was once seen as a ``villain,'' but in recent years his popularity has skyrocketed as he has been reevaluated as a loyal man who ``fought for justice.'' The castle ruins offer a panoramic view of Lake Biwa, and together with the nearby Ishida Mitsunari statue, you can remember Mitsunari's way of life.

hikone_castle_ii.name: 彦根城（井伊家の居城）
hikone_castle_ii.highlight: 現存12天守のひとつ・国宝彦根城。大老・井伊直弼が生きた城で桜田門外の変の背景となった幕末の政治劇の舞台。
hikone_castle_ii.text: 彦根城は1622年（元和8年）に完成した井伊氏の居城で、現存する12天守のひとつとして国宝に指定されている。井伊直弼は1815年に彦根城内で生まれ、1850年に藩主に就任。1858年に大老として日米修好通商条約に調印し開国を推進したが、安政の大獄で反対派を大量処罰した。翌1860年の「桜田門外の変」で水戸浪士に暗殺された（46歳）。「開国の英断か、反動政治か」と今も評価が分かれる波乱の生涯を刻んだ城だ。キャラクター「ひこにゃん」でも知られる。
hikone_castle_ii.name_en: Hikone Castle (residence of the Ii family)
hikone_castle_ii.highlight_en: One of the 12 existing castle towers, Hikone Castle is a national treasure. This is the castle where the Great Elder, Naosuke Ii, lived, and is the setting for a political drama at the end of the Edo period that served as the background for the Sakuradamongai Incident.
hikone_castle_ii.text_en: Hikone Castle is the residence of the Ii clan, completed in 1622, and is designated as a national treasure as one of the 12 remaining castle towers. Naosuke Ii was born in Hikone Castle in 1815 and became the lord of the domain in 1850. In 1858, as Tairo, he signed the Japan-US Treaty of Amity and Commerce and promoted the opening of the country, but he punished many opponents in the Ansei Great Prison. The following year, in 1860, he was assassinated by Mito Roshi during the Sakuradamongai Incident (age 46). It is a castle that marked a turbulent life, with opinions still divided as to whether it was a wise decision to open the country or reactionary politics. Also known for the character "Hikonyan".

odani_castle_azai.name: 小谷城跡（浅井長政の居城）
odani_castle_azai.highlight: お市の方と悲劇の愛を生きた浅井長政の本拠。義のために信長との同盟を破り小谷城で散った戦国の薄命。
odani_castle_azai.text: 小谷城は滋賀県長浜市の山上に築かれた浅井氏の居城だ。浅井長政は1564年に織田信長の妹・お市の方と婚姻して同盟を結んだが、1570年に旧来の同盟国・越前朝倉氏を信長が攻めたため義のために信長と決別した。以後2年間にわたる攻防の末、1573年に信長に攻め落とされ長政は自刃した。妻・お市と三人の娘（後の茶々・初・江）は城を脱出したが、この悲劇は後の豊臣・徳川時代に深く影を落とした。城跡は国の史跡で、湖北の山並みと琵琶湖を一望できる絶景だ。
odani_castle_azai.name_en: Odari Castle Ruins (Castle of Nagamasa Asai)
odani_castle_azai.highlight_en: The home base of Nagamasa Asai, who lived a tragic love affair with Oichi no Kata. For the sake of righteousness, Sengoku broke away from his alliance with Nobunaga and died at Odari Castle.
odani_castle_azai.text_en: Odari Castle is the residence of the Asai clan, built on a mountain in Nagahama City, Shiga Prefecture. Nagamasa Azai married Oda Nobunaga's sister Oichi in 1564 and formed an alliance with him, but in 1570 he broke up with Nobunaga for the sake of righteousness as Nobunaga attacked his old ally, the Echizen Asakura clan. After a two-year battle, it was defeated by Nobunaga in 1573, and Nagamasa committed suicide. His wife Oichi and three daughters (later Chacha, Hatsu, and Go) escaped from the castle, but this tragedy cast a deep shadow on the later Toyotomi and Tokugawa eras. The castle ruins are a national historic site and offer a spectacular view of the mountains of Hubei and Lake Biwa.

urasenke_kyoto.name: 表千家・裏千家（茶道の聖地）
urasenke_kyoto.kana: おもてせんけうらせんけ
urasenke_kyoto.highlight: 千利休の孫・宗旦が分けた表千家・裏千家。「わびさび」「一期一会」の精神が今も受け継がれる日本茶道の総本山。
urasenke_kyoto.text: 千利休は1522年（大永2年）に堺の商家に生まれ、武野紹鴎に茶の湯を学んで「侘び茶」を大成させた。信長・秀吉に厚遇されて茶頭を務めたが、1591年に秀吉の怒りを買い切腹を命じられた（享年70歳）。利休の死後、その精神は弟子・孫の世代に受け継がれ利休の孫・宗旦が三家（表千家・裏千家・武者小路千家）に分けて伝承した。京都上京区に現存する表千家・裏千家の家元は今も利休の「一期一会」「和敬清寂」の精神を継承し、茶道の総本山として世界中の茶人が訪れる。
urasenke_kyoto.highlight_en: Omotesenke and Urasenke were divided by Sen no Rikyu's grandson Sotan. The headquarters of the Japanese tea ceremony, where the spirit of "wabi-sabi" and "once in a lifetime encounter" is still passed down to this day.
urasenke_kyoto.text_en: Sen no Rikyu was born into a merchant family in Sakai in 1522, and after learning the tea ceremony from Joo Takeno, he perfected the style of ``Wabi-cha.'' He was well received by Nobunaga and Hideyoshi and served as tea master, but in 1591 he angered Hideyoshi and was ordered to commit seppuku (passed away at the age of 70). After Rikyu's death, this spirit was passed on to his disciples and grandchildren, and Rikyu's grandson, Sotan, divided it into three schools (Omotesenke, Urasenke, and Mushanokojisenke) and inherited it. The Omotesenke and Urasenke schools that still exist in Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto, continue to inherit Rikyu's spirit of ``once in a lifetime'' and ``wakei seijaku,'' and are visited by tea masters from all over the world as the head temple of the tea ceremony.

tekijuku_osaka.name: 適塾（緒方洪庵の蘭学塾）
tekijuku_osaka.highlight: 福沢諭吉・大村益次郎ら明治を担う人材を育てた緒方洪庵の蘭学塾。近代日本の「知の揺りかご」となった大阪の旧跡。
tekijuku_osaka.text: 適塾は1838年（天保9年）に緒方洪庵が大阪に開いた蘭学塾で、現在の大阪市中央区北浜に当時の建物が現存している（国の史跡・重要文化財）。オランダ語の医学書を解読しながら西洋医学・蘭学を学ぶシステムは当時の最先端で、福沢諭吉・大村益次郎・橋本左内・長与専斎など幕末・明治に活躍する多くの人材を輩出した。洪庵は天然痘予防のため種痘を普及させ数十万人の命を救ったとも言われる。慶應義塾（福沢諭吉）の精神的源流もここに始まる。
tekijuku_osaka.highlight_en: Koan Ogata's Dutch studies school trained people who were responsible for the Meiji era, such as Yukichi Fukuzawa and Masujiro Omura. A historic site in Osaka that became the ``cradle of knowledge'' of modern Japan.
tekijuku_osaka.text_en: Tekijuku is a Western studies school opened in Osaka by Koan Ogata in 1838, and the original building still exists in what is now Kitahama, Chuo Ward, Osaka (a national historic site and important cultural property). The system of learning Western medicine and Dutch studies while deciphering Dutch medical books was the most advanced at the time, producing many people who were active in the late Edo period and Meiji period, such as Yukichi Fukuzawa, Masujiro Omura, Sanai Hashimoto, and Sensai Nagayo. It is said that Koan spread vaccination to prevent smallpox and saved hundreds of thousands of lives. The spiritual origins of Keio University (Yukichi Fukuzawa) also began here.

godai_osaka_exchange.name: 大阪取引所（旧・大阪株式取引所）
godai_osaka_exchange.kana: おおさかとりひきじょ
godai_osaka_exchange.highlight: 五代友厚が設立した大阪商工会議所のそばに立つ取引所。近代大阪経済の礎を築いた「大阪の恩人」の銅像が立つ。
godai_osaka_exchange.text: 五代友厚は1836年（天保7年）に薩摩藩（鹿児島）に生まれた武士・実業家で、明治維新後に大阪経済の発展に身を捧げた。大阪商工会議所の設立（1878年）・大阪株式取引所の創設・大阪紡績会社の設立など大阪の近代経済インフラを次々と整備した。「大阪の恩人」と称され大阪取引所前に銅像が立つ。2015年のNHK朝の連続ドラマ「あさが来た」で広岡浅子を支える実業家として描かれ再評価が進んだ。現在の大阪取引所（デリバティブ市場の中心）の前身を作った人物だ。
godai_osaka_exchange.highlight_en: This exchange stands next to the Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry, which was founded by Tomoatsu Godai. A bronze statue of the ``Benefactor of Osaka'' who built the foundation of modern Osaka's economy stands here.
godai_osaka_exchange.text_en: Tomoatsu Godai was a samurai and businessman born in 1836 in the Satsuma domain (Kagoshima), and devoted himself to the development of the Osaka economy after the Meiji Restoration. He developed Osaka's modern economic infrastructure one after another, including the establishment of the Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry (1878), the establishment of the Osaka Stock Exchange, and the establishment of the Osaka Spinning Company. He is known as the ``Benefactor of Osaka'' and has a bronze statue erected in front of the Osaka Exchange. In 2015, he was portrayed as a businessman who supports Asako Hirooka in the NHK morning drama series ``Asa ga Kita'', which led to his being reevaluated. He is the person who created the predecessor of the current Osaka Exchange (the center of the derivatives market).

todaiji_gyoki.name: 東大寺大仏殿
todaiji_gyoki.kana: とうだいじだいぶつでん

transit.name: 東大寺大仏殿前バス停

todaiji_gyoki.highlight: 世界最大の木造建築に安置される奈良の大仏。行基が勧進し聖武天皇の国家鎮護の願いを込めて752年に開眼された。
todaiji_gyoki.text: 東大寺の毘盧遮那仏（奈良の大仏）は743年（天平15年）の聖武天皇の詔で造営が始まり、752年に開眼供養が行われた。高僧・行基は全国を巡り大仏造営のための資金・物資・人手を集める「勧進」を行い、庶民の間に広く支持を得た。高さ14.7メートルの大仏の鋳造には当時の国家財政の大部分が投入され、延べ260万人が動員されたとされる。インドの僧・菩提僊那が開眼の導師を務め国際色豊かな奈良時代の文化を象徴している。現在の大仏殿（江戸時代再建）は世界最大の木造建築だ。
todaiji_gyoki.highlight_en: The Great Buddha of Nara is enshrined in the world's largest wooden structure. It was recommended by Gyoki and opened in 752 with Emperor Shomu's wishes for the protection of the nation.
todaiji_gyoki.text_en: Construction of Biroshanabutsu (Great Buddha of Nara) at Todaiji Temple began in 743 (Tenpyo 15) by an edict from Emperor Shomu, and a memorial service for opening the eyes was held in 752. The high priest Gyoki traveled around the country campaigning to collect funds, supplies, and manpower for the construction of the Great Buddha, and gained wide support among the common people. Most of the national finances at the time were invested in casting the 14.7-meter-tall Great Buddha, and a total of 2.6 million people are said to have been mobilized. Bodhisena, an Indian monk, served as an eye-opening guru and symbolizes the cosmopolitan culture of the Nara period. The current Great Buddha Hall (rebuilt in the Edo period) is the largest wooden structure in the world.

toshoda_ji_ganjin.name: 唐招提寺
toshoda_ji_ganjin.highlight: 6度の渡航挑戦で失明しながら来日した鑑真が建立した戒律の本山。国宝の金堂と鑑真和上像が天平の祈りを今に伝える。
toshoda_ji_ganjin.text: 唐招提寺は759年（天平宝字3年）に唐の高僧・鑑真が創建した律宗の総本山だ。鑑真は743年に初めての日本渡航を試みてから754年の成功まで6度の挑戦を行い、嵐・海賊・出国妨害・眼病により失明しながらも志を曲げなかった。来日後は東大寺で授戒を行い、晩年にこの寺を建立した。国宝の金堂は奈良時代を代表する最高の建築で、鑑真の肖像を模した国宝「鑑真和上像」は日本最古の肖像彫刻として知られる。毎年6月には鑑真忌として蓮の花が開く中で法要が行われる。
toshoda_ji_ganjin.highlight_en: The head temple of the precepts was built by Ganjin, who came to Japan after six attempts to travel and lost his eyesight. The Kondo hall, a national treasure, and the statue of Ganjin Wajo convey the Tenpyo prayers to this day.
toshoda_ji_ganjin.text_en: Toshodai-ji Temple is the head temple of the Ritsu sect, founded in 759 by the high priest Ganjin of the Tang Dynasty. Ganjin made six attempts from his first attempt to travel to Japan in 743 until his success in 754, and despite losing his eyesight due to storms, pirates, obstacles to his departure, and eye disease, he never wavered in his will. After coming to Japan, he gave precepts at Todaiji Temple, and built this temple in his later years. The Kondo Hall, a national treasure, is the finest architecture representing the Nara period, and the national treasure ``Ganjin Wajo-zo'', which is a portrait of Ganjin, is known as the oldest portrait sculpture in Japan. Every year in June, a memorial service is held amidst the blooming lotus flowers to commemorate Ganjin's death.

matsuyama_castle_shiki.name: 松山城・正岡子規記念博物館
matsuyama_castle_shiki.kana: まつやまじょうまさおかしききねんはくぶつかん
matsuyama_castle_shiki.highlight: 「柿食へば鐘が鳴るなり法隆寺」。松山出身の正岡子規と秋山真之の故郷。道後温泉・松山城が坂の上の雲の世界を今に伝える。
matsuyama_castle_shiki.text: 松山は愛媛県の県庁所在地で、明治の文化・軍事を担った多くの偉人を輩出した。正岡子規は1867年（慶応3年）に松山に生まれ、「写生」の理念で俳句・短歌を革新し近代文学の扉を開いた。親友・夏目漱石が松山中学に赴任してきたときの交流は文学史に残る。同時代の松山出身・秋山真之は日本海海戦の作戦立案者として日本をロシアに勝利させた。松山城（現存天守）・道後温泉・子規記念博物館が一帯にあり、司馬遼太郎の『坂の上の雲』の舞台として観光地として整備されている。
matsuyama_castle_shiki.highlight_en: ``When you eat persimmons, the bell rings and you go to Horyuji Temple.'' The hometown of Shiki Masaoka and Masayuki Akiyama from Matsuyama. Dogo Onsen and Matsuyama Castle convey the world of clouds on the slopes.
matsuyama_castle_shiki.text_en: Matsuyama is the prefectural capital of Ehime Prefecture and produced many great figures who were responsible for the culture and military of the Meiji period. Masaoka Shiki was born in Matsuyama in 1867 (Keio 3), and with the idea of ​​``sketching'' he revolutionized haiku and tanka, opening the door to modern literature. The exchange that took place when his best friend, Natsume Soseki, was assigned to Matsuyama Junior High School will remain in literary history. Masayuki Akiyama, a contemporary from Matsuyama, led Japan to victory over Russia as a strategy planner for the Battle of the Sea of ​​Japan. The area includes Matsuyama Castle (the existing castle tower), Dogo Onsen, and Shiki Memorial Museum, and is being developed as a tourist destination as it was the setting for Ryotaro Shiba's ``Clouds on the Slope.''

kochi_castle_tosa.name: 高知城・板垣退助像
kochi_castle_tosa.kana: こうちじょういたがきたいすけぞう
kochi_castle_tosa.highlight: 「板垣死すとも自由は死せず」。高知城前には自由民権運動の旗手・板垣退助の銅像が立ち土佐の進取の気風を伝える。
kochi_castle_tosa.text: 高知城は1603年（慶長8年）に山内一豊が築いた土佐藩の居城で、現存する天守・本丸御殿は国宝に指定されている。江戸時代を通じて山内家が治めた土佐は「いごっそう」（頑固者）と呼ばれる気風を持ち、多くの幕末志士を輩出した。板垣退助は1837年に高知に生まれ、明治以後は民撰議院設立建白書を提出して自由民権運動を起こした。1882年に岐阜で刺されながら「板垣死すとも自由は死せず」と叫んだとされる逸話で有名。現在も高知城前の板垣像は土佐の自由の精神を象徴している。
kochi_castle_tosa.highlight_en: “Even if Itagaki dies, freedom will never die.” In front of Kochi Castle, there is a bronze statue of Taisuke Itagaki, the standard-bearer of the Freedom and People's Rights Movement, which conveys Tosa's enterprising spirit.
kochi_castle_tosa.text_en: Kochi Castle was the residence of the Tosa clan, built by Kazutoyo Yamauchi in 1603, and the existing castle tower and Honmaru Palace are designated as national treasures. Tosa, ruled by the Yamauchi family throughout the Edo period, had an ethos known as ``Igosso'' (stubborn people) and produced many patriots at the end of the Edo period. Taisuke Itagaki was born in Kochi in 1837, and after the Meiji period he started the Freedom and People's Rights Movement by submitting a petition to establish the House of Representatives. He is famous for an anecdote in which he is said to have shouted, ``Itagaki may die, but freedom will never die'' while being stabbed in Gifu in 1882. Even today, the Itagaki statue in front of Kochi Castle symbolizes Tosa's spirit of freedom.

ryoma_nakaoka_kochi.name: 坂本龍馬・中岡慎太郎像（桂浜）
ryoma_nakaoka_kochi.kana: さかもとりょうまなかおかしんたろうぞう
ryoma_nakaoka_kochi.highlight: 太平洋を見つめる坂本龍馬の銅像が立つ桂浜。龍馬と中岡慎太郎は薩長同盟成立後ともに近江屋で暗殺された土佐の英雄。
ryoma_nakaoka_kochi.text: 桂浜は高知市の南端、太平洋に面した美しい弧状の砂浜で、坂本龍馬の銅像（高さ13.5メートル）が太平洋を見つめている。龍馬とともに薩長同盟の成立に奔走した中岡慎太郎は高知県北川村の出身で、1867年に龍馬とともに京都・近江屋で暗殺された。二人は大政奉還の実現直後に30歳前後の若さで散った。高知では「龍馬と慎太郎」はセットで語られる土佐の英雄で、中岡の故郷・北川村にも銅像が立つ。桂浜からは太平洋が一望でき、龍馬が「太平洋に出たい」と夢見た気持ちが伝わる絶景だ。
ryoma_nakaoka_kochi.name_en: Statues of Ryoma Sakamoto and Shintaro Nakaoka (Katsurahama)
ryoma_nakaoka_kochi.highlight_en: Katsurahama is home to a bronze statue of Ryoma Sakamoto staring out at the Pacific Ocean. Ryoma and Shintaro Nakaoka were Tosa heroes who were both assassinated at Omiya after the Satsuma-cho alliance was established.
ryoma_nakaoka_kochi.text_en: Katsurahama Beach is a beautiful arc-shaped sandy beach facing the Pacific Ocean at the southern tip of Kochi City, with a bronze statue of Ryoma Sakamoto (13.5 meters tall) staring out into the Pacific Ocean. Shintaro Nakaoka, who worked hard with Ryoma to establish the Satsuma-Choshu Alliance, was a native of Kitagawa Village, Kochi Prefecture, and was assassinated along with Ryoma in Omiya, Kyoto in 1867. The two passed away at the young age of around 30, just after the restoration of imperial rule was realized. In Kochi, ``Ryoma and Shintaro'' are heroes of Tosa that are talked about in sets, and a bronze statue of them is also erected in Nakaoka's hometown of Kitagawa Village. Katsurahama offers a panoramic view of the Pacific Ocean, a spectacular view that conveys Ryoma's dream of ``going out to the Pacific Ocean.''

saga_castle_nabeshima.name: 佐賀城跡・鍋島直正ゆかりの地
saga_castle_nabeshima.kana: さがじょうあとなべしまなおまさ
saga_castle_nabeshima.highlight: 日本最初の蒸気船・反射炉を作った先覚大名・鍋島直正の佐賀藩。幕末日本のテクノロジー革命の中心地。
saga_castle_nabeshima.text: 佐賀藩は幕末に最も進んだ科学技術を持つ藩のひとつとして知られる。10代藩主・鍋島直正（閑叟）は1844年に日本初の西洋式反射炉を建設し鋳鉄大砲の製造を開始、1855年には日本初の蒸気船「凌風丸」を完成させた。この軍事技術力が明治政府への人材輩出（大隈重信・江藤新平・副島種臣ら）と直結した。現在の佐賀城跡（本丸歴史館）は当時の本丸御殿が一部復元されており、鍋島家の文書・遺品とともに幕末佐賀の先進性を伝える。大隈重信の旧宅も徒歩圏内にある。
saga_castle_nabeshima.name_en: Saga Castle ruins/place related to Nabeshima Naomasa
saga_castle_nabeshima.highlight_en: The Saga domain of Nabeshima Naomasa, a pioneering feudal lord who built Japan's first steamship and reverberatory furnace. The center of Japan's technological revolution at the end of the Edo period.
saga_castle_nabeshima.text_en: The Saga domain was known as one of the domains with the most advanced science and technology at the end of the Edo period. Nabeshima Naomasa (Kanso), the 10th feudal lord, built Japan's first Western-style reverberatory furnace in 1844 and began manufacturing cast iron cannons, and in 1855 completed Japan's first steamship, the Ryofu Maru. This military technical ability was directly linked to the production of human resources for the Meiji government (Shigenobu Okuma, Shinpei Eto, Taneomi Soejima, etc.). The current Saga Castle Ruins (Honmaru History Museum) is a partially restored Honmaru Palace from that time, and along with the documents and belongings of the Nabeshima family, it conveys the advanced nature of Saga at the end of the Edo period. Shigenobu Okuma's former home is also within walking distance.

siebold_narutaki.name: シーボルト記念館（鳴滝塾跡）
siebold_narutaki.kana: しーぼるときねんかん
siebold_narutaki.highlight: 出島から鳴滝に塾を開いたドイツ人医師シーボルト。日本の近代医学・博物学の礎を作り日本と西洋の架け橋となった。
siebold_narutaki.text: フィリップ・フランツ・フォン・シーボルトは1796年にドイツで生まれ、1823年にオランダ東インド会社の医師として長崎・出島に赴任した。鳴滝に私塾「鳴滝塾」を開き高野長英・伊東玄朴ら多くの日本人医師を育てた。九州各地・江戸への旅行で動植物・地理・民俗を調査し膨大な資料をヨーロッパに送った。しかし1828年に国外持ち出し禁止の日本地図を所持していたことが発覚し「シーボルト事件」で国外追放となった。帰国後に著した『日本』は19世紀ヨーロッパの日本研究の基本文献となった。
siebold_narutaki.highlight_en: Siebold, a German doctor, opened a cram school in Narutaki from Dejima. He laid the foundation for modern medicine and natural history in Japan and became a bridge between Japan and the West.
siebold_narutaki.text_en: Philipp Franz von Siebold was born in Germany in 1796, and in 1823 was assigned to Dejima, Nagasaki as a doctor for the Dutch East India Company. He opened a private school, Narutaki Juku, in Narutaki and trained many Japanese doctors, including Choei Takano and Genboku Ito. He researched flora and fauna, geography, and folklore during his trips to various parts of Kyushu and Edo, and sent a huge amount of material to Europe. However, in 1828, he was found to be in possession of a map of Japan that was prohibited to be taken out of the country, and he was deported from the country as part of the ``Siebold Incident''. After returning to Japan, he wrote ``Japan,'' which became the basic text for Japanese studies in 19th century Europe.

funai_castle_otomo.name: 府内城跡・大友宗麟ゆかりの地
funai_castle_otomo.kana: ふないじょうあとおおともそうりん
funai_castle_otomo.highlight: キリシタン大名・大友宗麟が豊後の都市・府内（現大分）を本拠に南蛮文化を花開かせた。ザビエルを招いた宗教と交易の拠点。
funai_castle_otomo.text: 大友宗麟（義鎮）は1530年に豊後国（現大分県）の大名家に生まれ、九州6カ国を制する大勢力を築いた。南蛮貿易を積極的に推進し、フランシスコ・ザビエルを府内に招いてキリスト教の布教を認めた。自らも晩年にドン・フランシスコとして洗礼を受けた。府内（現大分市）は南蛮文化が花開いた「九州のローマ」となり、鉄砲・医薬品・西洋文明が流入した。しかし1578年の耳川の戦いで島津義久に大敗し勢力が急速に衰え、1587年の豊臣秀吉の九州征伐の直前に没した。
funai_castle_otomo.name_en: Funai castle ruins/place related to Otomo Sorin
funai_castle_otomo.highlight_en: The Christian feudal lord Otomo Sourin flourished Nanban culture based in the Bungo city of Funai (present-day Oita). A center of religion and trade that invited Xavier.
funai_castle_otomo.text_en: Otomo Sorin (Yoshishige) was born in 1530 into a feudal lord family in Bungo Province (present-day Oita Prefecture), and built up a powerful force that controlled six countries in Kyushu.
