He actively promoted trade between the two countries, invited Francisco Xavier to the prefecture, and approved the missionary work of Christianity. He himself was baptized as Don Francisco in his later years. Funai (present-day Oita City) became the ``Rome of Kyushu,'' where Nanban culture flourished, and guns, medicine, and Western civilization poured in. However, he was defeated by Yoshihisa Shimazu at the Battle of Mimikawa in 1578, and his power rapidly declined, and he died just before Toyotomi Hideyoshi's conquest of Kyushu in 1587.

shuri_castle_okinawa.name: 首里城
shuri_castle_okinawa.highlight: 世界遺産・琉球王国の王城。尚泰が廃位されるまで450年間続いた琉球王国の中心。2019年の火災から復元中。
shuri_castle_okinawa.text: 首里城は15世紀初頭に尚巴志が琉球を統一した際に整備され、尚氏王統450年にわたる琉球王国の政治・文化の中心地となった。中国・日本・東南アジアの影響を融合した独自の建築様式は世界遺産（2000年登録）の構成要素となっている。1879年（明治12年）の琉球処分で最後の国王・尚泰が廃位されて沖縄県が設置され、450年の王国の歴史が終わった。太平洋戦争の沖縄戦で壊滅したが1992年に復元。2019年の火災で正殿が焼失したが、現在再建工事が進んでいる。
shuri_castle_okinawa.highlight_en: A world heritage site, the royal castle of the Ryukyu Kingdom. The center of the Ryukyu Kingdom, which lasted for 450 years until Shōyasu was dethroned. Currently being restored from the 2019 fire.
shuri_castle_okinawa.text_en: Shuri Castle was built when Sho Hashi unified the Ryukyus in the early 15th century, and became the political and cultural center of the Ryukyu Kingdom during the 450-year reign of the Sho Dynasty. Its unique architectural style, which combines influences from China, Japan, and Southeast Asia, is a component of the World Heritage Site (registered in 2000). In 1879 (Meiji 12), the last king, Shōyasu, was dethroned and Okinawa Prefecture was established, ending the 450-year history of the kingdom. It was destroyed during the Battle of Okinawa during the Pacific War, but was restored in 1992. The main hall was destroyed in a fire in 2019, but reconstruction work is currently underway.

togo_kagoshima.name: 東郷平八郎生誕地・加治屋町
togo_kagoshima.kana: とうごうへいはちろうせいたんち
togo_kagoshima.highlight: 「東洋のネルソン」東郷平八郎の生誕地。日本海海戦でロシアのバルチック艦隊を全滅させ日露戦争の勝利に決定的に貢献。
togo_kagoshima.text: 東郷平八郎は1848年（嘉永元年）に薩摩藩加治屋町（現鹿児島市）に生まれた。西南戦争・日清戦争を経て連合艦隊司令長官となり、1905年の日本海海戦でロシアのバルチック艦隊を対馬沖でほぼ全滅させた。「敵艦見ゆ」の報告から丁字戦法で圧勝したこの海戦は世界海戦史上最大の完全勝利とされ「東洋のネルソン」として全世界に名を轟かせた。「神様・仏様・東郷様」と崇拝された東郷は1934年に87歳で没。鹿児島・加治屋町は西郷隆盛・大久保利通も生まれた「明治維新の産地」だ。
togo_kagoshima.name_en: Kajiyamachi, the birthplace of Heihachiro Togo
togo_kagoshima.highlight_en: The birthplace of Heihachiro Togo, the ``Nelson of the East.'' He annihilated Russia's Baltic Fleet in the Battle of the Sea of ​​Japan, making a decisive contribution to victory in the Russo-Japanese War.
togo_kagoshima.text_en: 東郷平八郎は1848年（嘉永元年）に薩摩藩加治屋町（現鹿児島市）に生まれた。 After the Seinan War and the Sino-Japanese War, he became commander-in-chief of the Combined Fleet, and in 1905, in the Battle of the Sea of ​​Japan, he almost annihilated Russia's Baltic Fleet off the coast of Tsushima. This naval battle, in which he achieved an overwhelming victory based on the report of ``enemy ships in sight'' using T-shaped tactics, was said to be the largest complete victory in the history of world naval warfare, and became known around the world as ``Nelson of the Orient.'' 「神様・仏様・東郷様」と崇拝された東郷は1934年に87歳で没。鹿児島・加治屋町は西郷隆盛・大久保利通も生まれた「明治維新の産地」だ。

saito_city_miyazaki.name: 西都原古墳群・若山牧水記念館
saito_city_miyazaki.kana: さいとばるこふんぐん
saito_city_miyazaki.highlight: 古代の古墳群と近代の歌人・若山牧水の故郷が共存する宮崎の歴史地区。「白鳥は哀しからずや」の詩情が流れる。
saito_city_miyazaki.text: 西都市周辺は宮崎県最大の古墳群（西都原古墳群）と幕末の思想家・安井息軒の塾跡、そして「旅の詩人」若山牧水の故郷が集まる歴史地区だ。若山牧水は1885年に宮崎県東臼杵郡東郷村（現日向市）に生まれた歌人で、早稲田大学在学中から歌集を発表し旅と酒を愛した独自の詩風で知られる。「白鳥は哀しからずや空の青海のあをにも染まずただよふ」は国語教科書の定番だ。牧水の生誕地・日向市には記念館があり、宮崎の美しい山河と詩人の世界が重なる。
saito_city_miyazaki.name_en: Saitobaru Tumulus Group/Wakayama Bokusui Memorial Museum
saito_city_miyazaki.highlight_en: Miyazaki's historic district is home to ancient burial mounds and the hometown of modern poet Bokusui Wakayama. The poetic sentiment of ``Swans are not sad'' flows.
saito_city_miyazaki.text_en: The area surrounding Saito City is a historical area where Miyazaki Prefecture's largest group of burial mounds (Saitobaru Burial Mounds), the ruins of the cram school of late Edo period thinker Yasui Soken, and the hometown of ``traveling poet'' Bokusui Wakayama are located. Wakayama Bokusui was a poet who was born in 1885 in Togo Village, Higashiusuki District, Miyazaki Prefecture (present-day Hyuga City).He published a collection of poems while attending Waseda University, and is known for his unique poetic style, which reflected his love of travel and alcohol. ``The swan is not sad, nor does the blue sea of ​​the sky stain the darkness,'' is a standard in Japanese language textbooks. There is a memorial museum in Hyuga City, Bakisui's birthplace, where the beautiful mountains and rivers of Miyazaki overlap with the world of the poet.

kagiya_no_tsuji_iga.name: 鍵屋の辻決闘場跡
kagiya_no_tsuji_iga.kana: かぎやのつじけっとうじょうあと
kagiya_no_tsuji_iga.highlight: 荒木又右衛門が主君の仇を討った日本三大仇討ちの地
kagiya_no_tsuji_iga.text: 鍵屋の辻は、寛永11年（1634年）に荒木又右衛門が渡辺数馬と共に仇の河合又五郎を討ち取った場所です。日本三大仇討ちの一つに数えられ、又右衛門の壮絶な剣技は今も語り継がれています。現在は石碑と説明板が建ち、当時の決闘の様子を伝えています。
kagiya_no_tsuji_iga.highlight_en: Japan's three major revenge sites where Mataemon Araki avenged his master's death
kagiya_no_tsuji_iga.text_en: Locksmith's Tsuji is the place where Mataemon Araki and Kazuma Watanabe killed his enemy Matagoro Kawai in 1634. It is counted as one of Japan's three greatest revenges, and Mataemon's fierce sword skills are still talked about today. Today, a stone monument and an information board have been erected, telling the story of the duel at the time.

soma_nakamura_castle.name: 相馬中村城跡
soma_nakamura_castle.kana: そうまなかむらじょうあと
soma_nakamura_castle.highlight: 相馬氏代々の居城、相馬義胤が大改修した平山城
soma_nakamura_castle.text: 相馬中村城は、戦国大名・相馬氏の居城として知られています。相馬義胤はこの城を整備し、後北条氏や伊達氏と渡り合いながら相馬領を守り続けました。現在は相馬中村神社の境内となっており、本丸跡の高台から太平洋を望むことができます。
soma_nakamura_castle.highlight_en: Hirayama Castle, the residence of the Soma clan for generations, was extensively renovated by Yoshitane Soma
soma_nakamura_castle.text_en: Soma Nakamura Castle is known as the residence of the Sengoku feudal lord, the Soma clan. Soma Yoshitane maintained this castle and continued to protect Soma territory while competing with the Gohojo clan and the Date clan. Currently, it is part of the grounds of Soma Nakamura Shrine, and you can see the Pacific Ocean from the hill of the main enclosure ruins.

tokushima_castle_hachisuka.name: 徳島城跡・鷲の門
tokushima_castle_hachisuka.kana: とくしまじょうあとわしのもん
tokushima_castle_hachisuka.highlight: 蜂須賀家政が築いた阿波藩25万石の中心城郭
tokushima_castle_hachisuka.text: 徳島城は、豊臣秀吉の家臣・蜂須賀家政が天正13年（1585年）に阿波国に入封し築城した城です。城下町とともに整備され、阿波踊りの発祥とも言われる賑わいを見せました。現在は石垣と復元された鷲の門が残り、城山は眉山から続く緑豊かな丘陵に囲まれています。
tokushima_castle_hachisuka.highlight_en: The central castle of the Awa domain, built by Iemasa Hachisuka and costing 250,000 koku.
tokushima_castle_hachisuka.text_en: Tokushima Castle is a castle built by Iemasa Hachisuka, a vassal of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who entered Awa Province in 1585. It was developed along with the castle town, and was a bustling place that is said to be the birthplace of Awa Odori. Today, the stone walls and the restored Eagle Gate remain, and Shiroyama is surrounded by lush green hills that extend from Mt. Bizan.

kaminoyama_castle_shingen.name: 上山城（霞城）
kaminoyama_castle_shingen.kana: かみのやまじょうかすみがじょう

transit.name: JR奥羽本線かみのやま温泉駅

kaminoyama_castle_shingen.highlight: 最上氏と武田氏系将士が争った出羽の要衝
kaminoyama_castle_shingen.text: 上山城は出羽国の要衝として戦国時代に争奪が続いた城です。武田信玄の重臣・山県昌景ら武田系の武将とゆかりが深く、江戸時代には土岐氏の城として整備されました。現在は模擬天守が建ち、置賜地方の雄大な山並みと温泉街を一望できます。
kaminoyama_castle_shingen.highlight_en: A strategic point in Dewa where the Mogami clan and Takeda clan warriors fought.
kaminoyama_castle_shingen.text_en: Kaminoyama Castle was a strategically important castle in Dewa Province and was frequently contested during the Sengoku period. It has deep connections with Takeda lineage military commanders such as Yamagata Masakage, a senior vassal of Takeda Shingen, and was built as a castle by the Toki clan during the Edo period. Currently, a mock castle tower has been erected, offering a panoramic view of the majestic mountains and hot spring town of the Okitama region.

tsu_castle_todo.name: 津城跡（藤堂高虎の城）
tsu_castle_todo.kana: つじょうあととうどうたかとらのしろ

transit.name: JR紀勢本線・近鉄名古屋線津駅

tsu_castle_todo.highlight: 藤堂高虎が大改修した伊勢32万石の居城
tsu_castle_todo.text: 津城は、築城の名人として知られる藤堂高虎が慶長13年（1608年）から大改修を行った城です。高虎は今治・大洲・宇和島・伊予大洲など各地の城を手掛けた名築城家で、津城もその卓越した縄張り技術が発揮されています。現在は石垣と隅櫓が残り、高虎の銅像が城跡公園に建っています。
tsu_castle_todo.highlight_en: Ise's 320,000 koku castle that was extensively renovated by Takatora Todo
tsu_castle_todo.text_en: Tsu Castle is a castle that was extensively renovated in 1608 by Todo Takatora, known as a master castle builder. Takatora was a famous castle builder who built castles in various places such as Imabari, Ozu, Uwajima, and Iyo Ozu, and Tsu Castle also demonstrates his outstanding territorial skills. Today, the stone wall and corner turret remain, and a bronze statue of Takatora stands in the castle ruins park.

zuishinin_ono_komachi.name: 随心院（小野小町ゆかり）
zuishinin_ono_komachi.kana: ずいしんいんおのこまちゆかり

transit.name: 京都市営地下鉄東西線小野駅

zuishinin_ono_komachi.highlight: 絶世の美女・小野小町が晩年を過ごしたと伝わる門跡寺院
zuishinin_ono_komachi.text: 随心院は、真言宗善通寺派の門跡寺院で、小野小町が晩年を過ごしたと伝わる地です。境内には小野小町の化粧井戸や供養塔があり、春にはしだれ梅の美しさで知られます。百人一首にも選ばれた和歌の名手・小野小町の面影を今に伝える古刹です。
zuishinin_ono_komachi.highlight_en: Monzeki Temple, where the unparalleled beauty Ono Komachi is said to have spent her later years.
zuishinin_ono_komachi.text_en: Zuishin-in is a monzeki temple of the Zentsuji sect of the Shingon sect, and is said to be the place where Ono Komachi spent his later years. The shrine grounds include Ono Komachi's makeup well and memorial tower, and are known for the beauty of the weeping plum blossoms in spring. This is an ancient temple that still retains the image of Ono Komachi, a master of waka poetry who was selected as one of the 100 people who sang the best poems.

yoshinaka_birthplace_musashino.name: 木曾義仲産湯の井戸（嵐山町）
yoshinaka_birthplace_musashino.kana: きそよしなかうぶゆのいどあらしまちょう

transit.name: 東武東上線武蔵嵐山駅

yoshinaka_birthplace_musashino.highlight: 源義仲（木曾義仲）の産地・比企氏ゆかりの地
yoshinaka_birthplace_musashino.text: 埼玉県嵐山町は、源義仲（木曾義仲）が幼少期を過ごしたとされる地です。父・源義賢の死後、幼い義仲は信濃国木曾に逃れましたが、生誕地の比企地方には産湯の井戸が残っています。義仲は後に「朝日将軍」と呼ばれ、倶利伽羅峠の戦いで平家を打ち破りましたが、最後は宇治川で源義経に討たれました。
yoshinaka_birthplace_musashino.name_en: Kiso Yoshinaka Hot Spring Well (Arashiyama Town)
yoshinaka_birthplace_musashino.highlight_en: Production area of ​​Minamoto no Yoshinaka (Kiso Yoshinaka) and a place related to the Hiki clan
yoshinaka_birthplace_musashino.text_en: Arashiyama-cho, Saitama Prefecture is said to be the place where Minamoto no Yoshinaka (Kiso Yoshinaka) spent his childhood. After the death of his father, Minamoto no Yoshitaka, the young Yoshinaka fled to Kiso, Shinano Province, but the birthing well still remains in his birthplace, the Hiki region. Yoshinaka was later called the ``Asahi Shogun'' and defeated the Taira clan at the Battle of Kurikara Pass, but was ultimately defeated by Minamoto no Yoshitsune at the Ujigawa River.

nichiren_tanjoji.name: 誕生寺（日蓮聖人の生誕地）
nichiren_tanjoji.kana: たんじょうじにちれんしょうにんのせいたんち
nichiren_tanjoji.highlight: 日蓮が「日本第一の法華経行者」を目指した生誕地の霊場
nichiren_tanjoji.text: 誕生寺は、鎌倉時代の僧・日蓮が建長5年（1253年）に開宗した日蓮宗の総本山の一つで、日蓮の生誕地に建てられた寺院です。日蓮は「南無妙法蓮華経」の題目を唱え、幕府への諫暁書を提出するなど激しい布教活動を行いました。境内の旧鐘楼堂や仁王門など重要文化財が多数残っています。
nichiren_tanjoji.highlight_en: Sacred place of birth where Nichiren aimed to become ``Japan's number one Lotus Sutra practitioner''
nichiren_tanjoji.text_en: Tanjoji Temple is one of the head temples of the Nichiren sect, which was founded by the Kamakura period monk Nichiren in 1253, and is a temple built on Nichiren's birthplace. Nichiren chanted the title ``Namu-myoho-renge-kyo,'' and submitted a letter of admonition to the shogunate, and engaged in intense missionary activities. Many important cultural properties remain within the temple grounds, including the old bell tower and the Niomon gate.

koishikawa_mito_yashiki.name: 小石川後楽園（水戸藩上屋敷跡）
koishikawa_mito_yashiki.kana: こいしかわこうらくえんみとはんかみやしきあと

transit.name: 都営地下鉄大江戸線・三田線後楽園駅

koishikawa_mito_yashiki.highlight: 水戸光圀・徳川斉昭が愛した大名庭園、弘道館と並ぶ水戸藩の精神的拠点
koishikawa_mito_yashiki.text: 小石川後楽園は、水戸藩の江戸上屋敷として整備された大名庭園です。二代藩主・水戸光圀が完成させ、幕末には尊王攘夷運動の拠点として注目された水戸藩の中心でした。徳川斉昭は「弘道館」を作り天狗党など多くの志士を育てました。庭園内の大泉水や円月橋など美しい景観が今も保たれています。
koishikawa_mito_yashiki.name_en: Koishikawa Korakuen (Ruins of the Mito clan's mansion)
koishikawa_mito_yashiki.highlight_en: A daimyo garden loved by Mitsukuni Mito and Nariaki Tokugawa, a spiritual base of the Mito domain along with Kodokan.
koishikawa_mito_yashiki.text_en: Koishikawa Korakuen is a feudal lord garden that was maintained as the Edo residence of the Mito domain. It was completed by Mito Mitsukuni, the second lord of the domain, and was the center of the Mito domain, which attracted attention as a base for the son-no-joi movement at the end of the Edo period. Tokugawa Nariaki built the Kodokan and trained many patriots, including the Tenguto. Beautiful landscapes such as the large spring water and Engetsu Bridge within the garden are still preserved.

mamiya_rinzo_memorial.name: 間宮林蔵記念館（つくばみらい市）
mamiya_rinzo_memorial.kana: まみやりんぞうきねんかんつくばみらいし

transit.name: 関東鉄道常総線守谷駅

mamiya_rinzo_memorial.highlight: 樺太が島であると証明した探検家・間宮林蔵の生誕地
mamiya_rinzo_memorial.text: 間宮林蔵は文化5年（1808年）に樺太探検を行い、樺太が島であることを確認しました。この海峡は後に「間宮海峡」と命名されています。江戸幕府の命により蝦夷地・樺太・大陸沿岸の探検を行い、世界地図に名を残した日本の探検家です。つくばみらい市の生誕地には記念館が建てられています。
mamiya_rinzo_memorial.highlight_en: The birthplace of Rinzo Mamiya, the explorer who proved that Sakhalin was an island.
mamiya_rinzo_memorial.text_en: Rinzo Mamiya conducted an expedition to Sakhalin in 1808 and confirmed that Sakhalin was an island. This strait was later named ``Mamiya Strait''. He was a Japanese explorer who left his name on the world map by exploring Ezo, Sakhalin, and the coast of the continent under the orders of the Edo Shogunate. A memorial hall has been built at his birthplace in Tsukubamirai City.

tanaka_shozo_museum.name: 田中正造記念館（佐野市）
tanaka_shozo_museum.kana: たなかしょうぞうきねんかんさのし
tanaka_shozo_museum.highlight: 日本初の公害問題・足尾銅山鉱毒事件に立ち向かった政治家の故郷
tanaka_shozo_museum.text: 田中正造は明治時代の政治家で、栃木県の足尾銅山による渡良瀬川の鉱毒汚染に立ち向かった「日本の公害運動の父」です。明治34年（1901年）には明治天皇への直訴を試みたことでも知られ、晩年は村を捨てずに鉱毒被害地に残り続けました。佐野市出身で、生家跡に記念館が整備されています。
tanaka_shozo_museum.highlight_en: The hometown of the politician who fought against Japan's first pollution problem, the Ashio Copper Mine Poisoning Incident.
tanaka_shozo_museum.text_en: Shozo Tanaka was a politician during the Meiji era and was the ``father of Japan's pollution movement'' who fought against the pollution of the Watarase River by the Ashio Copper Mine in Tochigi Prefecture. He is also known for attempting to appeal directly to Emperor Meiji in 1901, and in his later years he remained in the area affected by mining poisoning without abandoning his village. He was born in Sano City, and a memorial hall has been established at the site of his birthplace.

doshisha_niijima.name: 同志社大学・新島会館（新島襄の地）
doshisha_niijima.kana: どうししゃだいがくにいじまかいかんにいじまじょうのち

transit.name: 京都市営地下鉄今出川駅すぐ

doshisha_niijima.highlight: 新島襄が設立したキリスト教主義の学校・同志社英学校の創設の地
doshisha_niijima.text: 新島襄は安政元年（1843年）生まれの教育者・キリスト教指導者です。明治期に密出国してアメリカで学び帰国後、明治8年（1875年）に京都・今出川に同志社英学校（現・同志社大学）を設立しました。「一国の良心とも言うべき人物を養成する」という理念を掲げ、日本の近代教育に大きな影響を与えました。
doshisha_niijima.name_en: Doshisha University/Niijima Kaikan (Nijima Jyo no land)
doshisha_niijima.highlight_en: The birthplace of Doshisha English School, a Christian school founded by Niijima Jo
doshisha_niijima.text_en: Jo Niijima was an educator and Christian leader born in 1843. During the Meiji period, he secretly left Japan to study in the United States, and after returning to Japan, he established Doshisha English School (currently Doshisha University) in Imadegawa, Kyoto in 1875. The school's philosophy of ``nurturing people who can be called the conscience of a nation'' had a great influence on modern education in Japan.

hanawa_hokiichi_honjo.name: 塙保己一記念館（本庄市）
hanawa_hokiichi_honjo.kana: はなわほきいちきねんかんほんじょうし
hanawa_hokiichi_honjo.highlight: 全盲ながら日本最大の古典叢書『群書類従』を編纂した国学者の故郷
hanawa_hokiichi_honjo.text: 塙保己一は幼いころに失明しながらも国学・和学の研究を続け、日本最大の古典叢書『群書類従』（665冊）を編纂した江戸時代の学者です。その偉業はヘレン・ケラーにも「私の理想の人」と称えられました。埼玉県本庄市の出身で、温故知新館（記念館）では業績を紹介しています。
hanawa_hokiichi_honjo.highlight_en: The hometown of a Japanese scholar who compiled Japan's largest classical collection, Gunshoju, despite being completely blind.
hanawa_hokiichi_honjo.text_en: Koichi Hanawa was a scholar of the Edo period who continued researching Japanese and Japanese studies despite losing his eyesight at a young age, and compiled Japan's largest classical series, Gunshoju (665 volumes). His accomplishments were praised by Helen Keller, who called him ``my ideal person.'' He was born in Honjo City, Saitama Prefecture, and his achievements are introduced at the Onko Chishinkan (memorial hall).

ogino_ginko_kumagaya.name: 荻野吟子顕彰碑（熊谷市）
ogino_ginko_kumagaya.kana: おぎのぎんこけんしょうひくまがやし
ogino_ginko_kumagaya.highlight: 日本初の女性公認医師・荻野吟子の生誕地
ogino_ginko_kumagaya.text: 荻野吟子は明治14年（1885年）に日本で初めて医師免許を取得した女性医師です。当時の法律で女性の受験が認められない中、粘り強い働きかけで試験受験を勝ち取り、現在の熊谷市俵瀬に生まれた彼女の功績を讃える碑が建てられています。NHK大河ドラマ「花神」でも描かれた女性開拓者の生涯が偲ばれます。
ogino_ginko_kumagaya.highlight_en: Birthplace of Japan's first female certified doctor, Ginko Ogino
ogino_ginko_kumagaya.text_en: Ginko Ogino was the first female doctor in Japan to receive a medical license in 1885. Although women were not allowed to take the exam under the law at the time, she was born in what is now Tawarase, Kumagaya City, and a monument has been erected to honor her achievements. The life of a female pioneer depicted in the NHK Taiga drama "Kashin" is remembered.

ishikawajima_yoseba.name: 石川島人足寄場跡（長谷川平蔵ゆかり）
ishikawajima_yoseba.kana: いしかわじまにんそくよせばあとはせがわへいぞうゆかり

transit.name: 東京メトロ有楽町線月島駅

ishikawajima_yoseba.highlight: 鬼平こと長谷川平蔵が設立した日本初の授産施設・人足寄場の跡地
ishikawajima_yoseba.text: 石川島は隅田川河口の小島で、寛政2年（1790年）に火付盗賊改方長官・長谷川平蔵の発案で日本初の授産施設「人足寄場」が設置されました。無宿者や軽犯罪者に職業訓練を施す先進的な社会施設で、平蔵の人道的な治安改革の象徴です。池波正太郎の時代小説『鬼平犯科帳』で知られる平蔵の業績が偲ばれる地です。
ishikawajima_yoseba.name_en: Ishikawa Islander footfall site (related to Hasegawa Hirazo)
ishikawajima_yoseba.highlight_en: The site of Japan's first vocational training facility and footfall hall established by Heizo Hasegawa, also known as Onihei.
ishikawajima_yoseba.text_en: Ishikawajima is a small island at the mouth of the Sumida River, and in 1790, Japan's first vocational facility, ``Hitosokuyoroba,'' was established at the idea of ​​Heizo Hasegawa, the Chief of Fire and Thief Reform. It is an advanced social facility that provides vocational training to homeless people and petty criminals, and is a symbol of Heizo's humane security reform. This is a place where the achievements of Heizo, known for Shotaro Ikenami's historical novel "Onihei Hankacho", are remembered.

hiraga_gennai_sanuki.name: 平賀源内旧宅・記念館（東かがわ市）
hiraga_gennai_sanuki.kana: ひらがげんないきゅうたくきねんかんひがしかがわし
hiraga_gennai_sanuki.highlight: エレキテル・土用の丑の日など奇才の発明家・平賀源内の生誕地
hiraga_gennai_sanuki.text: 平賀源内は江戸時代中期の発明家・戯作者・蘭学者です。讃岐国（香川県）志度浦に生まれ、静電気発生装置「エレキテル」の復元・改良や、土用の丑の日にうなぎを食べる習慣を作ったことでも知られます。本草学・陶芸・油絵・戯曲など多彩な才能を持ち、「奇才」として江戸の人々を驚かせ続けました。
hiraga_gennai_sanuki.name_en: Hiraga Gennai Former Residence/Memorial Hall (Higashikagawa City)
hiraga_gennai_sanuki.highlight_en: The birthplace of Gennai Hiraga, the genius inventor of Electric Teru and Doyo no Ushi no Hi.
hiraga_gennai_sanuki.text_en: Gennai Hiraga was an inventor, playwright, and Dutch scholar during the mid-Edo period. Born in Shidoura, Sanuki Province (Kagawa Prefecture), he is also known for restoring and improving the static electricity generator ``Erekiteru'' and for creating the custom of eating eel on the ox day. Possessing diverse talents such as herbal studies, pottery, oil painting, and drama, he continued to amaze the people of Edo as a ``genius.''

ryokan_goan.name: 五合庵・良寛記念館（出雲崎町）
ryokan_goan.kana: ごごうあんりょうかんきねんかんいずもざきまち
ryokan_goan.highlight: 漂泊の僧・良寛が20年間暮らした粗末な庵と生誕地
ryokan_goan.text: 良寛は江戸時代後期の禅僧・歌人・書家で、越後出雲崎の出身です。国上山の五合庵という小さな庵に20年以上住み、子どもたちと手鞠をついたり書を認めたりして過ごしました。その清廉で無欲な生き方は多くの人に愛され、「良寛さん」として親しまれています。書は独特の柔らかさで知られ、書道史上の名品として今も高く評価されています。
ryokan_goan.highlight_en: The humble hermitage where wandering monk Ryokan lived for 20 years and his birthplace
ryokan_goan.text_en: Ryokan was a Zen monk, poet, and calligrapher from the late Edo period, and was born in Izumozaki, Echigo. I lived in a small hermitage called Gogo-an on Mt. Kunikami for more than 20 years, spending my time playing temari and appreciating calligraphy with the children. His pure and selfless way of life is loved by many people, and he is affectionately known as "Ryokan-san." The calligraphy is known for its unique softness and is still highly regarded as a masterpiece in the history of calligraphy.

kawai_tsugunosuke_nagaoka.name: 河井継之助記念館（長岡市）
kawai_tsugunosuke_nagaoka.kana: かわいつぎのすけきねんかんながおかし
kawai_tsugunosuke_nagaoka.highlight: ガトリング砲を率いて官軍と戦った越後長岡藩の最後の家老
kawai_tsugunosuke_nagaoka.text: 河井継之助は幕末の越後長岡藩の家老で、西洋式軍備の近代化に努めました。戊辰戦争では武装中立を試みましたが交渉が決裂し、日本で初めてガトリング砲を実戦投入して官軍と激闘を繰り広げました。長岡城陥落後も転戦し、会津若松への退却途中で傷が悪化し29歳で没しました。司馬遼太郎の小説『峠』で知られます。
kawai_tsugunosuke_nagaoka.highlight_en: The last retainer of the Echigo-Nagaoka clan who led a Gatling gun and fought against the government army.
kawai_tsugunosuke_nagaoka.text_en: Tsuginosuke Kawai was a chief retainer of the Echigo-Nagaoka domain at the end of the Edo period, and worked to modernize Western-style military equipment. During the Boshin War, they attempted armed neutrality, but negotiations broke down, and they were the first in Japan to use the Gatling gun in combat, leading to a fierce battle with the government army. After the fall of Nagaoka Castle, he continued to fight, and while retreating to Aizuwakamatsu, his wounds worsened and he died at the age of 29. It is best known for Ryotaro Shiba's novel ``Toge''.

yasuda_garden_sumida.name: 旧安田庭園（墨田区）
yasuda_garden_sumida.kana: きゅうやすだていえんすみだく
yasuda_garden_sumida.highlight: 明治の大財閥・安田財閥を築いた安田善次郎が所有した大名庭園
yasuda_garden_sumida.text: 旧安田庭園は、江戸時代に常陸府中藩の大名庭園として作られ、明治時代に安田財閥の創始者・安田善次郎が所有した潮入回遊式庭園です。安田善次郎は越中（富山）出身の両替商から身を起こし、安田銀行（現・みずほ銀行）など安田財閥を築き上げました。大正11年（1922年）に東京市に寄贈され、現在は一般公開されています。
yasuda_garden_sumida.highlight_en: A feudal lord garden owned by Zenjiro Yasuda, who built the Yasuda Zaibatsu, a major conglomerate in the Meiji era.
yasuda_garden_sumida.text_en: The former Yasuda Garden was created as a daimyo garden for the Hitachi-Fuchu domain during the Edo period, and is a tidal stroll garden owned by Zenjiro Yasuda, the founder of the Yasuda Zaibatsu, during the Meiji period. Zenjiro Yasuda started his career as a money exchanger from Etchu (Toyama) and built the Yasuda Zaibatsu, which included Yasuda Bank (currently Mizuho Bank). It was donated to the City of Tokyo in 1922 and is now open to the public.

hashimoto_sanai_fukui.name: 橋本左内旧宅跡・顕彰碑（福井市）
hashimoto_sanai_fukui.kana: はしもとさないきゅうたくあとけんしょうひふくいし
hashimoto_sanai_fukui.highlight: 26歳で安政の大獄に散った天才的開明派志士の故郷
hashimoto_sanai_fukui.text: 橋本左内は越前福井藩（現・福井市）出身の幕末の志士で、適塾で緒方洪庵に学んだ蘭学者・政治家です。松平春嶽に仕え、将軍継嗣問題では一橋慶喜を支持しましたが、安政の大獄で安政6年（1859年）に26歳の若さで処刑されました。「啓発録」は彼が15歳のときに書いた自己鍛錬の書で、今も読み継がれています。
hashimoto_sanai_fukui.name_en: Hashimoto Sanai former house ruins/monument monument (Fukui City)
hashimoto_sanai_fukui.highlight_en: The hometown of a genius Kaimei-ha patriot who was exiled to the Great Prison of Ansei at the age of 26.
hashimoto_sanai_fukui.text_en: Hashimoto Sanai was a samurai from the Echizen Fukui domain (present-day Fukui City) at the end of the Edo period, and a Dutch scholar and politician who studied under Koan Ogata at Tekijuku. He served Shungaku Matsudaira and supported Yoshinobu Hitotsubashi in the issue of succession to the shogun, but he was executed at the age of 26 in 1859 at the Great Prison of Ansei. ``Enlightenment Records'' is a book on self-discipline that he wrote when he was 15 years old, and it is still being read today.

yuri_kimasa_fukui.name: 由利公正誕生地碑（福井市）
yuri_kimasa_fukui.kana: ゆりきまさたんじょうちひふくいし
yuri_kimasa_fukui.highlight: 五箇条の御誓文の草案を書き、新政府の財政を担った由利公正の生誕地
yuri_kimasa_fukui.text: 由利公正は越前福井藩士出身で、明治維新の財政政策を担った政治家です。慶応4年（1868年）の五箇条の御誓文の草案「議事之体大意」を起草した一人として知られています。東京府知事も務め、明治政府の近代国家建設に貢献しました。福井市内には橋本左内と並んで誕生地碑が残っています。
yuri_kimasa_fukui.highlight_en: Birthplace of Yuri Masayoshi, who drafted the Five Articles Oath and was responsible for the finances of the new government.
yuri_kimasa_fukui.text_en: Yuri Masayoshi was a samurai of the Echizen Fukui clan and a politician who was responsible for fiscal policy during the Meiji Restoration. He is known as one of the people who drafted the Five-Article Oath Draft ``Giji no Taidai'' in 1868. He also served as governor of Tokyo Prefecture and contributed to the construction of a modern nation by the Meiji government. There is a birthplace monument in Fukui City, along with Hashimoto Sanai.

senkoji_enkubutsu.name: 千光寺・円空仏（高山市）
senkoji_enkubutsu.kana: せんこうじえんくうぶつたかやまし
senkoji_enkubutsu.highlight: 独自の粗彫りで全国を巡り円空仏を彫り続けた修行僧・円空ゆかりの寺
senkoji_enkubutsu.text: 千光寺は飛騨高山の山中にある真言宗の古刹で、江戸時代の仏師・円空が多くの仏像を残した寺として知られます。円空は一生をかけて12万体の仏を彫ることを誓い、全国各地を旅しながら独特の荒削りな木彫仏を残しました。千光寺には国内最多の円空仏が保存され、その素朴で力強い造形美が多くの参拝者を引きつけています。
senkoji_enkubutsu.highlight_en: A temple connected to Enku, a monk who continued to carve Enku Buddha throughout the country with his unique rough carvings.
senkoji_enkubutsu.text_en: Senkoji Temple is an old temple of the Shingon sect located in the mountains of Hida Takayama, and is known as the temple where the Edo period Buddhist sculptor Enku left many Buddhist statues. Enku vowed to carve 120,000 Buddhas over the course of his life, and traveled all over the country leaving behind unique, rough-hewn wooden Buddhas. Senkoji Temple has the largest number of Enku Buddhas preserved in Japan, and its simple yet powerful beauty attracts many visitors.

zenshoan_tesshu.name: 全生庵（山岡鉄舟の菩提寺）
zenshoan_tesshu.kana: ぜんしょうあんやまおかてっしゅうのぼだいじ

transit.name: 東京メトロ千代田線根津駅

zenshoan_tesshu.highlight: 剣・禅・書の三道を極めた「幕末三舟」山岡鉄舟が晩年に整備した寺
zenshoan_tesshu.text: 全生庵は台東区谷中にある禅寺で、幕末から明治にかけて活躍した山岡鉄舟が明治16年（1883年）に開いた寺です。鉄舟は勝海舟・高橋泥舟とともに「幕末三舟」と称され、西郷隆盛との会談で江戸城無血開城に貢献しました。剣（一刀正伝無刀流）・禅・書の三道を極めた鉄舟の位牌が安置され、落語家ゆかりの幽霊画でも知られます。
zenshoan_tesshu.highlight_en: A temple built in the later years of Tesshu Yamaoka, one of the three masters of the three arts of swordsmanship, Zen, and calligraphy at the end of the Edo period.
zenshoan_tesshu.text_en: Zenshoan is a Zen temple located in Yanaka, Taito Ward, and was opened in 1883 by Tesshu Yamaoka, who was active from the end of the Edo period to the Meiji period. Tesshu, along with Kaishu Katsu and Deishu Takahashi, was known as the ``Three Ships of the End of the Edo Period'' and contributed to the bloodless surrender of Edo Castle through a meeting with Takamori Saigo. The memorial tablet of Tesshu, who mastered the three arts of swordsmanship (Itto Shoden Muto-ryu), Zen, and calligraphy, is enshrined here, and it is also known for its ghost paintings related to rakugo performers.

toyoda_sakichi_museum.name: 豊田佐吉記念館（湖西市）
toyoda_sakichi_museum.kana: とよださきちきねんかんこさいし
toyoda_sakichi_museum.highlight: 自動織機を発明しトヨタ自動車の礎を築いた「発明王」の生家
toyoda_sakichi_museum.text: 豊田佐吉は遠江国山口村（現・湖西市）出身で、自動織機の発明に生涯を捧げた「発明王」です。明治24年（1891年）に木製動力織機を発明し、その後も改良を重ねて自動織機を完成させました。この特許をイギリスの企業に売却して得た資金が、息子・豊田喜一郎によるトヨタ自動車の創業につながりました。生家が保存・公開されています。
toyoda_sakichi_museum.highlight_en: Birthplace of the "King of Inventions" who invented the automatic loom and laid the foundation for Toyota Motor Corporation
toyoda_sakichi_museum.text_en: Sakichi Toyoda was a native of Yamaguchi Village, Totomi Province (present-day Kosai City), and was the ``King of Inventions'' who devoted his life to inventing the automatic loom. In 1891, he invented a wooden power loom, and after that he continued to make improvements and perfect the automatic loom. The funds obtained from selling this patent to a British company led to the founding of Toyota Motor Corporation by his son, Kiichiro Toyoda. His birthplace has been preserved and opened to the public.

zojoji_kazunomiya.name: 増上寺（和宮の御霊廟）
zojoji_kazunomiya.kana: ぞうじょうじかずのみやのごりょうびょう

transit.name: 都営地下鉄三田線芝公園駅

zojoji_kazunomiya.highlight: 孝明天皇の妹・和宮が将軍家茂の正室として嫁いだ徳川家の菩提寺
zojoji_kazunomiya.text: 増上寺は港区芝に建つ浄土宗の大本山で、徳川将軍家の菩提寺として知られています。和宮親子内親王は孝明天皇の妹として生まれ、公武合体政策のために第14代将軍徳川家茂に降嫁しました。家茂の死後も江戸城に留まり、官軍の江戸攻撃を和らげるため尽力したとも言われています。増上寺の徳川家霊廟には和宮も葬られています。
zojoji_kazunomiya.highlight_en: The family temple of the Tokugawa family, where Emperor Komei's younger sister, Kazunomiya, married Shogun Iemochi as his legal wife.
zojoji_kazunomiya.text_en: Zojoji is the head temple of the Jodo sect of Buddhism, located in Shiba, Minato Ward, and is known as the family temple of the Tokugawa Shogunate. The Imperial Princess Kazunomiya was born as the younger sister of Emperor Komei, and was married off to the 14th Shogun, Iemochi Tokugawa, in order to implement the policy of combining the civil and military forces. It is said that he remained in Edo Castle even after Iemochi's death and worked hard to soften the attack on Edo by the government army. Kazunomiya is also buried in the Tokugawa family mausoleum at Zojoji Temple.

takataya_kahei_awaji.name: 高田屋嘉兵衛資料館（洲本市）
takataya_kahei_awaji.kana: たかたやかへいしりょうかんすもとし

transit.name: 本四海峡バス・高速艇で洲本港下船後タクシー

takataya_kahei_awaji.highlight: 北方領土開発と日露外交に貢献した廻船業者・高田屋嘉兵衛の生誕地
takataya_kahei_awaji.text: 高田屋嘉兵衛は淡路島出身の江戸時代の廻船商人で、択捉島の航路を開き蝦夷地交易で財を成しました。文化10年（1813年）にロシア軍艦に拿捕され抑留されましたが、逆に日露関係の仲介役として活躍し日本人捕虜の釈放に貢献しました。「北方の英雄」として今も高く評価されています。
takataya_kahei_awaji.highlight_en: The birthplace of Kahei Takadaya, a shipping contractor who contributed to the development of the Northern Territories and Japan-Russia diplomacy.
takataya_kahei_awaji.text_en: Kahei Takadaya was a shipping merchant from Awaji Island during the Edo period who opened the sea route to Etorofu Island and made a fortune through trade with Ezo. In 1813, he was captured by a Russian warship and interned, but instead he played an active role as a mediator in Japan-Russia relations and contributed to the release of Japanese prisoners of war. He is still highly regarded as the ``Hero of the North.''

minakata_kumagusu_tanabe.name: 南方熊楠顕彰館（田辺市）
minakata_kumagusu_tanabe.kana: みなかたくまぐすけんしょうかんたなべし
minakata_kumagusu_tanabe.highlight: 粘菌研究・民俗学・神社合祀反対運動で知られる天才博物学者の邸宅跡
minakata_kumagusu_tanabe.text: 南方熊楠は和歌山県田辺市出身の博物学者・民俗学者で、「南方マンダラ」と呼ばれる独自の思想体系と粘菌（変形菌）研究で世界的に知られています。イギリスで研究生活を送りながら『ネイチャー』に多数の論文を発表しました。晩年は神社合祀に反対する運動を展開し、環境保護の先駆者とも評価されています。
minakata_kumagusu_tanabe.highlight_en: The residence of a genius naturalist known for his slime mold research, folklore, and anti-shrine enshrinement movement.
minakata_kumagusu_tanabe.text_en: Minakata Kumagusu is a naturalist and folklorist from Tanabe City, Wakayama Prefecture, and is known worldwide for his unique system of thought called ``Minakata Mandala'' and for his research on slime molds (transforming fungi). While working as a researcher in the UK, he published numerous papers in Nature. In his later years, he campaigned against the combined enshrinement of shrines, and has been praised as a pioneer in environmental protection.

katsu_kaishu_zenpukuji.name: 善福寺（勝海舟の墓）
katsu_kaishu_zenpukuji.kana: ぜんぷくじかつかいしゅうのはか

transit.name: 東京メトロ銀座線外苑前駅（/ JR中央線信濃町駅から徒歩15分）

katsu_kaishu_zenpukuji.highlight: 江戸城無血開城を実現した幕末の大政治家・勝海舟の墓所
katsu_kaishu_zenpukuji.text: 勝海舟（勝義邦・勝麟太郎）は江戸幕府の旗本として生まれ、咸臨丸で太平洋を横断したことで知られます。幕末には陸軍総裁として西郷隆盛と会談し、江戸城の無血開城を実現して多くの命を救いました。明治政府でも枢密院顧問官などを務め、「海舟」の号で知られる書を多く残しています。世田谷区の洗足池公園にも墓があります。
katsu_kaishu_zenpukuji.highlight_en: The grave of Kaishu Katsu, a great politician at the end of the Edo period who achieved the bloodless surrender of Edo Castle.
katsu_kaishu_zenpukuji.text_en: Kaishu Katsu (Yoshikuni Katsu, Rintaro Katsu) was born as a hatamoto of the Edo shogunate, and is known for crossing the Pacific Ocean on the Kanrin Maru. At the end of the Edo period, as head of the army, he met with Takamori Saigo and achieved the bloodless surrender of Edo Castle, saving many lives. He also served as a Privy Council advisor in the Meiji government, and left behind many books known under the name ``Kaishu.'' There is also a grave in Senzokuike Park in Setagaya Ward.

soseki_museum_shinjuku.name: 漱石山房記念館（新宿区）
soseki_museum_shinjuku.kana: そうせきさんぼうきねんかんしんじゅくく

transit.name: 東京メトロ東西線早稲田駅

soseki_museum_shinjuku.highlight: 『坊っちゃん』『吾輩は猫である』の夏目漱石が晩年を過ごした旧宅跡の記念館
soseki_museum_shinjuku.text: 漱石山房記念館は、文豪・夏目漱石が晩年の9年間を過ごした旧宅「漱石山房」の跡地に建てられた記念館です。漱石はここで「木曜会」という文学サロンを開き、多くの弟子たちに囲まれながら『三四郎』『こころ』などの代表作を執筆しました。館内では漱石の書斎を再現した展示や直筆原稿が公開されています。
soseki_museum_shinjuku.highlight_en: A memorial hall on the site of the former residence where Natsume Soseki, the author of “Botchan” and “I am a Cat,” spent his later years.
soseki_museum_shinjuku.text_en: The Soseki Sanbo Memorial Hall is a memorial hall built on the site of the former residence of the literary great Natsume Soseki, where he spent the last nine years of his life. Soseki held a literary salon called ``Thursday Party'' here, and wrote his masterpieces such as ``Sanshiro'' and ``Kokoro'' while surrounded by many of his disciples. Inside the museum, there are exhibits that recreate Soseki's study and handwritten manuscripts.

john_manjiro_tosa_nakahama.name: 中濱万次郎生誕地（土佐清水市）
john_manjiro_tosa_nakahama.kana: なかはままんじろうせいたんち（とさしみずし）

transit.name: 土佐くろしお鉄道中村駅

john_manjiro_tosa_nakahama.highlight: 漁師から米国で教育を受け日米の架け橋となったジョン万次郎の生誕地
john_manjiro_tosa_nakahama.text: 中濱万次郎（ジョン万次郎）は天保2年（1831年）に土佐国中浜村（現・土佐清水市）に生まれた漁師です。14歳のとき漁の遭難でアメリカの捕鯨船に救助され、アメリカで教育を受けた最初の日本人の一人となりました。帰国後は幕府の通訳として活躍し、日米和親条約締結にも関わるなど日米関係の架け橋となりました。
john_manjiro_tosa_nakahama.highlight_en: The birthplace of John Manjiro, a fisherman who was educated in the United States and became a bridge between Japan and the United States.
john_manjiro_tosa_nakahama.text_en: Manjiro Nakahama (John Manjiro) was a fisherman born in 1831 in Nakahama Village, Tosa Province (present-day Tosashimizu City). At the age of 14, he was rescued by an American whaling ship in a fishing accident and became one of the first Japanese to receive an education in the United States. After returning to Japan, he served as an interpreter for the shogunate and was involved in the conclusion of the Treaty of Peace and Amity between Japan and the United States, becoming a bridge between Japan and the United States.

rai_sanyo_hiroshima.name: 頼山陽史跡資料館（広島市）
rai_sanyo_hiroshima.kana: らいさんようしせきしりょうかんひろしまし
rai_sanyo_hiroshima.highlight: 『日本外史』で幕末の尊王攘夷思想に影響を与えた漢詩人・頼山陽の旧居
rai_sanyo_hiroshima.text: 頼山陽は江戸時代後期の漢詩人・歴史家で、広島藩士の家に生まれました。代表作『日本外史』は源平から徳川時代までの武家政権の歴史を漢文体で描いた歴史書で、幕末の志士たちの尊王思想に大きな影響を与えました。広島市の旧居「頼山陽史跡資料館」では直筆の詩や書が展示されています。
rai_sanyo_hiroshima.name_en: Rai Sanyo Historical Site Museum (Hiroshima City)
rai_sanyo_hiroshima.highlight_en: Former residence of Rai Sanyo, a Chinese poet who influenced the son-no-joi ideology at the end of the Edo period in his book ``Japanese Foreign History.''
rai_sanyo_hiroshima.text_en: Rai Sanyo was a Chinese poet and historian of the late Edo period, and was born into a family of samurai of the Hiroshima clan. His masterpiece, ``Nihon Gaishi,'' is a historical book that depicts the history of the samurai government from the Genpei period to the Tokugawa period in a Chinese style, and had a great influence on the patriotism of the patriots at the end of the Edo period. His handwritten poems and calligraphy are on display at Rai Sanyo Historical Museum, his former residence in Hiroshima City.

nogi_shrine_aoyama.name: 乃木神社（乃木希典を祀る）
nogi_shrine_aoyama.kana: のぎじんじゃのぎまれすけをまつる

transit.name: 東京メトロ千代田線乃木坂駅

nogi_shrine_aoyama.highlight: 明治天皇崩御に殉死した陸軍大将・乃木希典と妻静子を祀る神社
nogi_shrine_aoyama.text: 乃木神社は港区赤坂に鎮座し、明治の陸軍大将・乃木希典とその妻静子を祀っています。乃木希典は日露戦争での旅順攻略戦（203高地）の司令官として知られ、明治45年（1912年）に明治天皇の崩御を聞き殉死しました。境内には乃木将軍の旧邸宅（乃木邸）も保存され、明治の軍人の気概と悲劇が偲ばれます。
nogi_shrine_aoyama.highlight_en: A shrine dedicated to Maresuke Nogi, an army general who died on the death of Emperor Meiji, and his wife Shizuko.
nogi_shrine_aoyama.text_en: Nogi Shrine is located in Akasaka, Minato Ward, and is dedicated to the Meiji era army general Maresuke Nogi and his wife Shizuko. Maresuke Nogi was known as the commander of the Battle of Port Arthur (203 Highlands) during the Russo-Japanese War, and died in 1912 upon hearing of the death of Emperor Meiji. The former residence of General Nogi (Nogi Residence) is also preserved within the precincts, and is a reminder of the spirit and tragedy of the Meiji military.

kodama_gentaro_memorial.name: 児玉源太郎記念館（周南市）
kodama_gentaro_memorial.kana: こだまげんたろうきねんかんしゅうなんし
kodama_gentaro_memorial.highlight: 日露戦争の勝利を導いた陸軍の知将・児玉源太郎の故郷
kodama_gentaro_memorial.text: 児玉源太郎は山口県都濃郡富田村（現・周南市）出身の陸軍大将で、日露戦争（1904〜05年）では満州軍総参謀長として活躍し、奉天会戦での勝利に貢献しました。第4代台湾総督としても後藤新平を登用して台湾の近代化を推進した優れた行政家でもありました。
kodama_gentaro_memorial.highlight_en: Hometown of Gentaro Kodama, the intelligent army general who led to victory in the Russo-Japanese War
kodama_gentaro_memorial.text_en: Gentaro Kodama was an army general from Tomita Village, Tsuno District, Yamaguchi Prefecture (currently Shunan City), and served as the chief of general staff of the Manchurian Army during the Russo-Japanese War (1904-05), contributing to victory at the Battle of Mukden. He was also an excellent administrator who promoted the modernization of Taiwan by appointing Shinpei Goto as the fourth Governor-General of Taiwan.

inukai_tsuyoshi_museum.name: 犬養木堂記念館（岡山市）
inukai_tsuyoshi_museum.kana: いぬかいぼくどうきねんかんおかやまし
inukai_tsuyoshi_museum.highlight: 「話せばわかる」と言い五・一五事件で暗殺された大正デモクラシーの政治家
inukai_tsuyoshi_museum.text: 犬養毅（木堂）は岡山県川上村（現・岡山市北区足守）出身の政治家で、明治から昭和にかけて政党政治を牽引しました。第29代内閣総理大臣として1931年に就任しましたが、翌1932年の五・一五事件で海軍青年将校に暗殺されました。「話せばわかる」という言葉は今も語り継がれており、大正デモクラシーを象徴する政治家として知られています。
inukai_tsuyoshi_museum.highlight_en: A politician from the Taisho democracy who was assassinated during the May 15th Incident, who said, ``You'll understand if you talk to me.''
inukai_tsuyoshi_museum.text_en: Takeshi Inukai (Kido) was a politician from Kawakami Village, Okayama Prefecture (currently Ashimori, Kita Ward, Okayama City), and was a leading figure in party politics from the Meiji period to the Showa period. He was appointed as the 29th Prime Minister in 1931, but was assassinated by a young naval officer in the May 15 Incident the following year. The phrase ``If you talk about it, you will understand'' is still passed down to this day, and he is known as a politician who symbolizes Taisho democracy.

takashima_shuhan_nagasaki.name: 高島秋帆旧宅跡（長崎市）
takashima_shuhan_nagasaki.kana: たかしましゅうはんきゅうたくあとながさきし
takashima_shuhan_nagasaki.highlight: 洋式砲術を日本に広め近代軍事の基礎を築いた長崎の豪商・高島秋帆の旧宅跡
takashima_shuhan_nagasaki.text: 高島秋帆は長崎の豪商出身の蘭学者・砲術家で、天保12年（1841年）に徳丸原（東京都板橋区）で日本初の西洋式砲術演習を行いました。その実力を恐れた幕府によって投獄されますが、ペリー来航後に釈放され、江川英龍らとともに日本の近代軍備の確立に貢献しました。長崎には旧宅跡と関連史跡が残っています。
takashima_shuhan_nagasaki.name_en: Takashima Akiho former residence site (Nagasaki City)
takashima_shuhan_nagasaki.highlight_en: The former residence of Akiho Takashima, a wealthy Nagasaki merchant who spread Western-style gunnery to Japan and laid the foundations for the modern military.
takashima_shuhan_nagasaki.text_en: Akiho Takashima was a Dutch scholar and gunner who was originally from a wealthy merchant in Nagasaki, and in 1841 conducted Japan's first Western-style gunnery exercises at Tokumaruhara (Itabashi Ward, Tokyo). The shogunate feared his strength and imprisoned him, but he was released after Perry arrived, and together with Hidetatsu Egawa and others, he contributed to the establishment of Japan's modern armament. In Nagasaki, the ruins of old houses and related historical sites remain.

yokoi_shonan_shijiken.name: 四時軒跡（横井小楠の旧宅）
yokoi_shonan_shijiken.kana: しじけんあとよこいしょうなんのきゅうたく

transit.name: 熊本市電水前寺公園電停

yokoi_shonan_shijiken.highlight: 松平春嶽に招かれ日本の近代化を構想した幕末の思想家・横井小楠の旧宅
yokoi_shonan_shijiken.text: 四時軒は熊本市沼山津にある横井小楠の旧宅です。横井小楠は肥後熊本藩士出身の儒学者・政治家で、「公議政体論」を唱え明治維新の思想的礎を築きました。越前福井藩主・松平春嶽に仕え、勝海舟・坂本龍馬にも影響を与えた開明的思想家です。明治2年（1869年）に暗殺されましたが、その志は明治維新に受け継がれました。
yokoi_shonan_shijiken.highlight_en: The former home of Yokoi Kokusu, a thinker at the end of the Edo period who was invited by Matsudaira Shungaku to envision the modernization of Japan.
yokoi_shonan_shijiken.text_en: Shijiken is the former home of Kokusu Yokoi in Numayamazu, Kumamoto City. Yokoi Kogusu was a Confucian scholar and politician who was a samurai of the Higo-Kumamoto clan, and advocated the ``Public Government Theory,'' which laid the ideological foundation for the Meiji Restoration. He was an enlightened thinker who served Matsudaira Shungaku, the lord of Echizen Fukui domain, and influenced Kaishu Katsu and Ryoma Sakamoto. Although he was assassinated in 1869, his aspirations were carried on into the Meiji Restoration.

tokuutomi_soho_arao.name: 徳富蘇峰・蘆花記念文学館（荒尾市）
tokuutomi_soho_arao.kana: とくとみそほうろかきねんぶんがくかんあらおし
tokuutomi_soho_arao.highlight: ジャーナリスト・徳富蘇峰と小説家・蘆花兄弟を顕彰する文学館
tokuutomi_soho_arao.text: 徳富蘇峰（猪一郎）は熊本県水俣出身のジャーナリスト・評論家で、『国民新聞』を創刊し明治から昭和にかけて膨大な著作を残しました。弟の徳富蘆花（健次郎）は小説『不如帰』で名声を得た作家です。荒尾市大牟田近くの旧宅「蘆花文庫」を中心に整備された記念文学館で、兄弟の足跡を辿ることができます。
tokuutomi_soho_arao.name_en: Tokutomi Soho and Roka Memorial Museum of Literature (Arao City)
tokuutomi_soho_arao.highlight_en: A literary museum honoring journalist Soho Tokutomi and the novelists Roka Brothers.
tokuutomi_soho_arao.text_en: Soho Tokutomi (Iichiro) was a journalist and critic from Minamata, Kumamoto Prefecture, who founded the Kokumin Shimbun and wrote a large number of works from the Meiji period to the Showa period. His younger brother Roka Tokutomi (Kenjiro) is a writer who gained fame for his novel ``Funyoki.'' You can follow in the footsteps of the brothers at this memorial literature museum built around their former home, Roka Bunko, near Omuta, Arao City.

nikko_rinnoji_shodo.name: 日光山輪王寺（勝道上人開山）
nikko_rinnoji_shodo.kana: にっこうさんりんのうじしょうどうしょうにんかいさん

transit.name: JR日光線日光駅・東武日光線東武日光駅（またはバス）

nikko_rinnoji_shodo.highlight: 奈良時代に勝道上人が開山した日光信仰の根本霊場
nikko_rinnoji_shodo.text: 日光山輪王寺は、天平神護2年（766年）に勝道上人が日光山（男体山）に登拝して開山した古刹です。勝道上人は日光を「二荒山」（ふたらさん）と名付け、その信仰は後に日光東照宮など日光全山の霊場へと発展しました。三仏堂は日光山随一の大堂で、千手観音・阿弥陀如来・馬頭観音の三体の仏を安置しています。
nikko_rinnoji_shodo.name_en: Nikkosan Rinnoji Temple (founded by Shodo Shonin)
nikko_rinnoji_shodo.highlight_en: A sacred place of Nikko worship founded by Shodo Shonin in the Nara period
nikko_rinnoji_shodo.text_en: Nikkosan Rinnoji Temple is an old temple founded by Shodo Shonin who climbed Mt. Nikko (Mt. Nantai) to worship in the second year of the Tenpyo Jingo era (766). Shodo Shonin named Nikko ``Mt. Futara'' (Futarasan), and his faith later developed into Nikko Toshogu Shrine and other sacred sites throughout the mountains of Nikko. Sanbutsu-do Hall is the largest hall on Mt. Nikko, and enshrines three Buddhas: Senju Kannon, Amida Nyorai, and Bato Kannon.

munakata_shiko_museum.name: 棟方志功記念館（青森市）
munakata_shiko_museum.kana: むなかたしこうきねんかんあおもりし
munakata_shiko_museum.highlight: 世界的版画家・棟方志功の生誕地にある作品を多数収蔵する記念館
munakata_shiko_museum.text: 棟方志功は青森市出身の版画家で、独自の木版画技法を確立し国際的に高い評価を得ました。「板画」と自ら呼んだその力強い作品はヴェネチア国際版画大賞など世界的な賞を受賞し、棟方自身も「わだばゴッホになる」と志を立てた情熱的な芸術家でした。青森市の記念館には多くの板画作品が収蔵・展示されています。
munakata_shiko_museum.highlight_en: A memorial museum containing many works located in the birthplace of world-renowned printmaker Shiko Munakata
munakata_shiko_museum.text_en: Shiko Munakata was a printmaker from Aomori City who established his own unique woodblock printing techniques and received high praise internationally. His powerful works, which he called ``board paintings,'' won international awards such as the Venice International Print Award, and Munakata himself was a passionate artist who aspired to ``become Van Gogh in Wadaba.'' Many board paintings are stored and exhibited at the Aomori City Memorial Museum.

doi_bansui_residence.name: 土井晩翠旧居（仙台市）
doi_bansui_residence.kana: どいばんすいきゅうきょせんだいし

transit.name: 仙台市営地下鉄南北線勾当台公園駅

doi_bansui_residence.highlight: 「荒城の月」の作詞者・土井晩翠が長年暮らした旧居
doi_bansui_residence.text: 土井晩翠は仙台出身の詩人・英文学者で、滝廉太郎が作曲した「荒城の月」の作詞者として知られています。東北大学の前身・第二高等学校教授を務めながら漢詩文調の詩を多く作り、明治詩壇を代表する詩人の一人となりました。仙台市内の旧居は現在公開されており、晩翠ゆかりの品々が展示されています。
doi_bansui_residence.highlight_en: The former residence of Doi Bansui, the lyricist of “Kojo no Tsuki”, who lived for many years.
doi_bansui_residence.text_en: Bansui Doi is a poet and scholar of English literature from Sendai, and is known as the lyricist for ``Kojo no Tsuki'' composed by Rentaro Taki. While serving as a professor at the Second High School, the predecessor of Tohoku University, he wrote many poems in the style of Chinese poetry, and became one of the leading poets of the Meiji poetic world. The former residence in Sendai City is now open to the public, and items related to Bansui are on display.

yoshino_sakuzo_furukawa.name: 吉野作造記念館（大崎市古川）
yoshino_sakuzo_furukawa.kana: よしのさくぞうきねんかんおおさきしふるかわ
yoshino_sakuzo_furukawa.highlight: 「民本主義」を唱え大正デモクラシーを牽引した政治学者の故郷
yoshino_sakuzo_furukawa.text: 吉野作造は宮城県古川（現・大崎市）出身の政治学者で、大正時代に「民本主義」を提唱し普通選挙と議会政治の確立を訴えました。東京帝国大学教授として活躍し、「大正デモクラシー」の理論的支柱となりました。故郷の大崎市には生誕100年を記念して設立された記念館があり、大正期の民主主義運動の資料を多数展示しています。
yoshino_sakuzo_furukawa.name_en: Yoshino Sakuzo Memorial Museum (Furukawa, Osaki City)
yoshino_sakuzo_furukawa.highlight_en: Hometown of a political scientist who advocated ``people's principles'' and led Taisho democracy.
yoshino_sakuzo_furukawa.text_en: Sakuzo Yoshino was a political scientist from Furukawa, Miyagi Prefecture (present-day Osaki City) who advocated ``people's principles'' during the Taisho era, calling for universal suffrage and the establishment of parliamentary politics. He served as a professor at Tokyo Imperial University and became a theoretical pillar of Taisho democracy. In his hometown of Osaki City, there is a memorial museum established to commemorate the 100th anniversary of his birth, which displays many materials related to the democratic movement of the Taisho period.

saito_mokichi_museum.name: 斎藤茂吉記念館（上山市）
saito_mokichi_museum.kana: さいとうもきちきねんかんかみのやまし

transit.name: JR奥羽本線かみのやま温泉駅

saito_mokichi_museum.highlight: 歌集『赤光』で近代短歌を革新した歌人・斎藤茂吉の出身地の記念館
saito_mokichi_museum.text: 斎藤茂吉は山形県上山市出身の歌人・精神科医で、正岡子規・伊藤左千夫の流れを汲むアララギ派の中心として近代短歌を代表する一人です。代表歌集『赤光』は「死にたまふ母」など母の死を悼んだ作品で知られ、激しい生命感と写実性で高く評価されています。上山市の記念館では直筆原稿や遺品が展示されています。
saito_mokichi_museum.highlight_en: A memorial hall in the birthplace of Mokichi Saito, the poet who revolutionized modern tanka with his collection of poems, ``Akako.''
saito_mokichi_museum.text_en: Mokichi Saito is a poet and psychiatrist from Kaminoyama City, Yamagata Prefecture, and one of the representatives of modern tanka as the center of the Araragi school, which descends from Shiki Masaoka and Sachio Ito. His representative collection of poems, ``Akako,'' is known for works mourning the death of his mother, such as ``Shittamafu Haha,'' and is highly praised for its intense sense of life and realism. His handwritten manuscripts and belongings are on display at the Kaminoyama Memorial Hall.

shimazaki_toson_magome.name: 島崎藤村記念館（南木曽町馬籠）
shimazaki_toson_magome.kana: しまざきとうそんきねんかんなぎそまちまごめ
shimazaki_toson_magome.highlight: 『夜明け前』『破戒』を書いた明治の文豪・島崎藤村の生誕地・馬籠宿
shimazaki_toson_magome.text: 馬籠宿は中山道の宿場町で、明治の文豪・島崎藤村の生誕地です。藤村は旧家の長子として生まれ、代表作『夜明け前』では明治維新で崩壊していく木曾の旧家の姿を描きました。また『破戒』は部落差別をテーマにした近代文学の先駆的作品です。馬籠宿の旧本陣跡に記念館が建ち、石畳の街道沿いに江戸時代の雰囲気が残っています。
shimazaki_toson_magome.name_en: Shimazaki Toson Memorial Museum (Magome, Nagiso Town)
shimazaki_toson_magome.highlight_en: Magome-juku, the birthplace of Toson Shimazaki, a literary giant of the Meiji period who wrote “Before Dawn” and “Hakai”
shimazaki_toson_magome.text_en: Magome-juku is a post town on the Nakasendo Road and the birthplace of Toson Shimazaki, a great writer of the Meiji period. Fujimura was born as the eldest child of an old family, and his masterpiece ``Before Dawn'' depicts the collapse of the old Kiso family during the Meiji Restoration. In addition, ``Hakkai'' is a pioneering work of modern literature that focuses on Buraku discrimination. A memorial hall was built on the site of Magome-juku's former headquarters, and the atmosphere of the Edo period remains along the stone-paved road.

yosano_akiko_sakai.name: 与謝野晶子文学館（堺市）
yosano_akiko_sakai.kana: よさのあきこぶんがくかんさかいし
yosano_akiko_sakai.highlight: 「君死にたまふことなかれ」を詠んだ歌人・与謝野晶子の生誕地
yosano_akiko_sakai.text: 与謝野晶子は明治11年（1878年）に大阪府堺市に生まれた歌人・著作家です。鳳（晶子の旧姓）家は和菓子商の家柄で、晶子は和歌に親しみながら育ちました。代表作『みだれ髪』で情熱的な愛の詩を発表し、日露戦争では弟への詩「君死にたまふことなかれ」で反戦の声を上げました。堺市には生誕地と文学館が設けられています。
yosano_akiko_sakai.highlight_en: Birthplace of Akiko Yosano, the poet who wrote “Kimi Shitamafu Kotokinare”
yosano_akiko_sakai.text_en: Akiko Yosano is a poet and writer born in 1878 in Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture. The Otori (Akiko's maiden name) family was a Japanese confectionery business, and Akiko grew up being familiar with waka. He published a passionate love poem in his masterpiece ``Midarekami,'' and during the Russo-Japanese War, he raised his voice against the war with a poem he wrote to his younger brother, ``Don't let me die.'' Sakai City has his birthplace and a literary museum.

yanagita_kunio_fukusaki.name: 柳田國男生家（福崎町）
yanagita_kunio_fukusaki.kana: やなぎたくにおせいかふくさきちょう
yanagita_kunio_fukusaki.highlight: 日本民俗学の父・柳田國男が生まれた農村の旧家
yanagita_kunio_fukusaki.text: 柳田國男は兵庫県神崎郡福崎町出身の民俗学者で、日本民俗学の創始者として知られています。農山村を歩いて民間伝承を調査した代表作『遠野物語』は日本民俗学の古典であり、「座敷童子」「河童」「ざしきわらし」などの民話収集でも知られます。福崎町の生家は国の史跡に指定され、隣接する辻川山公園にはカッパの像が設置されています。
yanagita_kunio_fukusaki.highlight_en: The old farmhouse where Kunio Yanagita, the father of Japanese folklore, was born.
yanagita_kunio_fukusaki.text_en: Kunio Yanagida is a folklorist from Fukusaki-cho, Kanzaki-gun, Hyogo Prefecture, and is known as the founder of Japanese folklore. His masterpiece ``Tono Monogatari'', in which he researched folklore by walking through rural villages, is a classic of Japanese folklore, and he is also known for his collection of folk tales such as ``Zashikiwarashi'', ``Kappa'', and ``Zashikiwarashi''. His birthplace in Fukusaki Town has been designated as a national historic site, and a statue of a kappa has been installed in the adjacent Tsujikawayama Park.

ozaki_hosai_shodoshima.name: 一夜庵（尾崎放哉終焉の地）
ozaki_hosai_shodoshima.kana: いちやあんおざきほうさいしゅうえんのち
ozaki_hosai_shodoshima.highlight: 「咳をしても一人」の俳人・尾崎放哉が命尽きるまで住んだ庵
ozaki_hosai_shodoshima.text: 一夜庵は小豆島の西光寺境内にある小さな庵で、自由律俳句の俳人・尾崎放哉（本名・秀雄）が大正15年（1926年）に亡くなるまで暮らした地です。「咳をしても一人」「入れ物がない両手で受ける」など孤独と自由を詠んだ句で知られ、種田山頭火とともに自由律俳句の双璧として評価されています。
ozaki_hosai_shodoshima.name_en: Ichiyaan (the place where Houya Ozaki ended his life)
ozaki_hosai_shodoshima.highlight_en: The hermitage where Houya Ozaki, the haiku poet who said, “Even if you cough, you’re alone,” lived until the end of his life.
ozaki_hosai_shodoshima.text_en: Ichiyaan is a small hermitage located within the precincts of Saikoji Temple on Shodoshima Island, where Houya Ozaki (real name Hideo), a free haiku haiku poet, lived until his death in 1926. He is known for his poems about solitude and freedom, such as ``Even if I cough, I'm alone'' and ``I have no container to catch it with both hands,'' and along with Taneda Santouka, he is regarded as one of the two greats of free-tempered haiku.

kagawa_toyohiko_kobe.name: 賀川豊彦記念・松沢資料館（神戸市）
kagawa_toyohiko_kobe.kana: かがわとよひこきねんまつざわしりょうかんこうべし

transit.name: 神戸市営地下鉄新長田駅

kagawa_toyohiko_kobe.highlight: 神戸のスラムで社会活動を続けたキリスト教社会運動家・賀川豊彦ゆかりの地
kagawa_toyohiko_kobe.text: 賀川豊彦は兵庫県神戸市生まれのキリスト教社会運動家・作家で、神戸の貧民街（新川地区）でスラム支援活動を行いました。労働運動・農民運動にも関わり、ノーベル平和賞候補にも名が挙がりました。自伝的小説『死線を越えて』はベストセラーとなり、社会変革への情熱と信仰の力を伝えています。
kagawa_toyohiko_kobe.name_en: Toyohiko Kagawa Memorial Matsuzawa Museum (Kobe City)
kagawa_toyohiko_kobe.highlight_en: A place connected to Toyohiko Kagawa, a Christian social activist who continued his social activities in the slums of Kobe.
kagawa_toyohiko_kobe.text_en: Toyohiko Kagawa is a Christian social activist and writer born in Kobe City, Hyogo Prefecture, who conducted slum support activities in Kobe's slums (Shinkawa district). He was involved in the labor and peasant movements, and was even nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize. His autobiographical novel Beyond the Line of Death became a bestseller, conveying his passion for social change and the power of faith.

kikuchi_kan_takamatsu.name: 菊池寛記念館（高松市）
kikuchi_kan_takamatsu.kana: きくちかんきねんかんたかまつし

transit.name: 高松琴平電気鉄道片原町駅

kikuchi_kan_takamatsu.highlight: 直木賞・芥川賞を創設した文豪・菊池寛の生誕地
kikuchi_kan_takamatsu.text: 菊池寛は高松市出身の小説家・劇作家で、『父帰る』『恩讐の彼方に』などの名作を残しました。大正11年（1922年）に文藝春秋社を創立し、芥川賞・直木賞を創設して日本文学の発展に大きく貢献しました。その功績を称え、高松市には菊池寛記念館が設けられ、直木賞・芥川賞の受賞作品も展示されています。
kikuchi_kan_takamatsu.highlight_en: The birthplace of Hiroshi Kikuchi, the literary giant who founded the Naoki Prize and the Akutagawa Prize.
kikuchi_kan_takamatsu.text_en: Hiroshi Kikuchi was a novelist and playwright from Takamatsu City, who left behind masterpieces such as ``My Father Returns'' and ``Beyond the Benevolence.'' He founded Bungeishunjusha in 1922, established the Akutagawa Prize and the Naoki Prize, and greatly contributed to the development of Japanese literature. In honor of his achievements, the Hiroshi Kikuchi Memorial Museum has been established in Takamatsu City, where winning works from the Naoki Prize and the Akutagawa Prize are on display.

nagai_takashi_nyokodo.name: 如己堂（永井隆の旧宅）
nagai_takashi_nyokodo.kana: にょこどうながいたかしのきゅうたく

transit.name: JR長崎駅（路面電車・浦上駅前）

nagai_takashi_nyokodo.highlight: 原爆で被爆しながら「長崎の鐘」を書き続けた医師・永井隆の旧宅
nagai_takashi_nyokodo.text: 如己堂は長崎市浦上の2畳一間の小さな家で、長崎医科大学教授・永井隆が原爆による白血病で闘病しながら過ごした終の棲家です。永井隆は昭和20年（1945年）の長崎原爆投下を自ら体験しながら、被爆者の救護に当たり、著書『長崎の鐘』で核廃絶と平和の大切さを世界に訴えました。如己堂の隣には永井隆記念館が建っています。
nagai_takashi_nyokodo.highlight_en: The former home of Takashi Nagai, a doctor who continued to write "The Bell of Nagasaki" while being exposed to the atomic bomb.
nagai_takashi_nyokodo.text_en: Nyokodo is a small house of 2 tatami mats in size in Urakami, Nagasaki City, and is the final home of Takashi Nagai, a professor at Nagasaki Medical University, who was battling leukemia caused by the atomic bombing. Takashi Nagai personally experienced the dropping of the atomic bomb on Nagasaki in 1945, worked to rescue survivors, and appealed to the world the importance of nuclear abolition and peace in his book ``The Bell of Nagasaki.'' The Takashi Nagai Memorial Museum is located next to Nyokodo.

nitobe_inazo_morioka.name: 新渡戸稲造生誕地（盛岡市）
nitobe_inazo_morioka.kana: にとべいなぞうせいたんちもりおかし
nitobe_inazo_morioka.highlight: 5000円札に描かれた農学者・教育者で『武士道』を英語で著した新渡戸稲造の生誕地
nitobe_inazo_morioka.text: 新渡戸稲造は岩手県盛岡（旧・南部藩）出身の農学者・教育者・国際人で、英語で著した『BUSHIDO（武士道）』で日本精神を世界に広めました。国際連盟の事務次長を務め、また東京女子大学の初代学長として女子教育にも尽くしました。旧5000円札に肖像が使われ、盛岡市の生誕地公園に顕彰碑が建っています。
nitobe_inazo_morioka.highlight_en: The birthplace of Inazo Nitobe, an agronomist and educator who wrote "Bushido" in English, depicted on the 5,000 yen bill.
nitobe_inazo_morioka.text_en: Inazo Nitobe was an agronomist, educator, and cosmopolitan from Morioka, Iwate Prefecture (former Nanbu Domain), who spread the Japanese spirit around the world with his English book ``BUSHIDO.'' She served as deputy secretary-general of the League of Nations and also devoted herself to women's education as the first president of Tokyo Women's University. His portrait is featured on the old 5,000 yen bill, and a monument is erected in his birthplace park in Morioka City.

hirata_atsutane_akita.name: 平田篤胤旧宅跡・顕彰碑（秋田市）
hirata_atsutane_akita.kana: ひらたあつたねきゅうたくあとけんしょうひあきたし
hirata_atsutane_akita.highlight: 復古神道を大成し幕末の尊王攘夷運動に影響を与えた国学者の故郷
hirata_atsutane_akita.text: 平田篤胤は出羽秋田藩出身の国学者で、本居宣長の国学をさらに発展させ「復古神道」を大成しました。神代文字の研究や異界・霊魂の世界への関心から独自の宇宙観・神道論を展開し、その思想は幕末の尊王攘夷運動の精神的支柱の一つとなりました。秋田市内には旧宅跡と顕彰碑が残っています。
hirata_atsutane_akita.name_en: Atsutane Hirata's former residence site and monument (Akita City)
hirata_atsutane_akita.highlight_en: The hometown of a Japanese scholar who established Restoration Shinto and influenced the son-no-joi movement at the end of the Edo period.
hirata_atsutane_akita.text_en: Hirata Atsutane was a Japanese scholar from the Dewa Akita domain, who further developed Norinaga Motoori's Japanese studies and established ``Retro Shinto.'' He developed his own cosmology and Shinto theory based on his research on ancient scripts and his interest in other worlds and the world of spirits, and his ideas became one of the spiritual pillars of the Sonno-joi movement at the end of the Edo period. The ruins of his old house and a monument commemorating him still remain in Akita City.

ishikawa_rikino_daisen.name: 石川理紀之助翁の碑（大仙市）
ishikawa_rikino_daisen.kana: いしかわりきのすけおうのひだいせんし
ishikawa_rikino_daisen.highlight: 秋田の農業近代化に捧げた「老農」石川理紀之助の活動の地
ishikawa_rikino_daisen.text: 石川理紀之助は秋田県大曲（現・大仙市）の農家出身で、農業技術の普及と農村改良に生涯を捧げた農業指導家です。「老農」と呼ばれ、秋田県内各地を歩いて農業改良を指導し、稲作技術の向上と農村の自立を訴えました。明治農業の改革者として秋田の農業史に大きな足跡を残しています。
ishikawa_rikino_daisen.highlight_en: The place of activity of Rikinosuke Ishikawa, an "old farmer" who dedicated himself to the modernization of Akita's agriculture.
ishikawa_rikino_daisen.text_en: Rikinosuke Ishikawa was a farmer in Omagari, Akita Prefecture (now Daisen City), and is an agricultural instructor who devoted his life to spreading agricultural technology and improving rural villages. Known as the "Old Farmer," he traveled throughout Akita Prefecture to teach agricultural improvement and appeal for improvements in rice cultivation techniques and rural independence. As a Meiji agricultural reformer, he left a huge mark on Akita's agricultural history.

mogami_tokunai_murayama.name: 最上徳内顕彰碑（村山市）
mogami_tokunai_murayama.kana: もがみとくないけんしょうひむらやまし
mogami_tokunai_murayama.highlight: 蝦夷地・千島を探検し北方領土の地理情報を確立した探検家の故郷
mogami_tokunai_murayama.text: 最上徳内は出羽村山郡（現・村山市）出身の江戸時代の探検家で、寛政年間に蝦夷地・千島列島・カラフトの調査を行いました。当時最も詳細な北方地理情報を幕府に報告し、後の間宮林蔵らの探検にも影響を与えました。北海道・サハリン方面の地図作成に貢献した先駆者として評価されています。
mogami_tokunai_murayama.highlight_en: The hometown of the explorer who explored Ezochi and the Kuril Islands and established geographic information on the Northern Territories.
mogami_tokunai_murayama.text_en: Mogami Tokunai was an Edo period explorer from Dewa Murayama District (present-day Murayama City) who conducted research on Ezo, the Kuril Islands, and Karaft during the Kansei era. He reported the most detailed northern geographic information to the shogunate at the time, and influenced later explorations by Rinzo Mamiya and others. He is recognized as a pioneer who contributed to the creation of maps for Hokkaido and Sakhalin.

sekigahara_battlefield.name: 関ヶ原古戦場
sekigahara_battlefield.kana: せきがはらこせんじょう
sekigahara_battlefield.text: 関ヶ原は1600年10月21日、徳川家康率いる東軍と石田三成率いる西軍が激突した「天下分け目の戦い」の舞台です。約8万vs約10万という日本史上最大級の合戦は、わずか半日で決着しました。西軍方の小早川秀秋の裏切りが勝敗を分けたとも言われ、この一戦で徳川270年の天下が決まりました。現在は各武将の陣跡や石碑が残る史跡公園として整備され、家康の最終陣地・決戦地の碑、島津義弘の退き口など、激戦の記憶が随所に刻まれています。岐阜関ヶ原古戦場記念館では最新の研究成果と映像で合戦を追体験できます。
sekigahara_battlefield.highlight: 天下分け目の一戦。半日で江戸時代の幕が開いた地
sekigahara_battlefield.highlight_en: The battle that will decide the world. The place where the curtain of the Edo period opened in half a day
sekigahara_battlefield.text_en: Sekigahara is the location of the Battle of Tenka, which took place on October 21, 1600, when the eastern army led by Tokugawa Ieyasu and the western army led by Ishida Mitsunari clashed. One of the largest battles in Japanese history, with a battle of approximately 80,000 vs. 100,000, was concluded in just half a day. It is said that the betrayal of Hideaki Kobayakawa of the western army made the difference between victory and defeat, and this battle decided the Tokugawa empire for 270 years. Currently, it is maintained as a historical park where the campsites and stone monuments of various military commanders remain, and memories of the fierce battle are engraved everywhere, such as the monument of Ieyasu's final camp and decisive battle site, and Yoshihiro Shimazu's retreat. At the Gifu Sekigahara Battlefield Memorial Museum, you can relive the battle with the latest research results and videos.

kawanakajima_battlefield.name: 川中島古戦場（八幡原史跡公園）
kawanakajima_battlefield.kana: かわなかじまこせんじょうはちまんはらしせきこうえん
kawanakajima_battlefield.highlight: 武田信玄と上杉謙信が5度にわたって激突した戦国最大のライバル対決の地
kawanakajima_battlefield.text: 川中島は長野市南部の犀川と千曲川が合流する平野で、武田信玄と上杉謙信が永禄4年（1561年）に最大規模の第四次合戦を含む5回にわたって激突した地です。両雄が馬上で直接対決したとされる伝説も残り、信玄・謙信一騎打ちの銅像が史跡公園に建てられています。「敵に塩を送る」という故事も川中島の緊張関係から生まれた逸話です。
kawanakajima_battlefield.highlight_en: The site of the Sengoku period's greatest rivalry, where Takeda Shingen and Uesugi Kenshin clashed five times.
kawanakajima_battlefield.text_en: Kawanakajima is a plain in the southern part of Nagano City where the Sai and Chikuma rivers meet, and is the place where Takeda Shingen and Uesugi Kenshin clashed five times, including the largest battle, the Fourth Battle, in 1561. There is also a legend that the two men fought directly on horseback, and a bronze statue of Shingen and Kenshin dueling has been erected in a historical park. The story of ``sending salt to the enemy'' is also an anecdote that was born out of the tense relations on Kawanakajima.

nagashino_battlefield.name: 長篠古戦場・設楽原決戦場（新城市）
nagashino_battlefield.kana: ながしのこせんじょうしたらがはらけっせんじょうしんしろし
nagashino_battlefield.highlight: 鉄砲三段撃ちで武田騎馬軍団を破った戦国史上最も革新的な合戦の地
nagashino_battlefield.text: 長篠・設楽原の戦いは天正3年（1575年）に行われた戦国時代の決戦で、織田信長・徳川家康連合軍が武田勝頼率いる騎馬軍団と激突しました。信長は馬防柵を築いて鉄砲隊を配置し、「三段撃ち」で武田の精鋭騎馬軍団を次々と撃破。戦国最強と謳われた武田軍が壊滅し、鉄砲が戦国の戦術を根本から変えた歴史的転換点となりました。
nagashino_battlefield.highlight_en: The site of the most innovative battle in Sengoku history, where the Takeda cavalry corps was defeated by three-stage gunfire.
nagashino_battlefield.text_en: The Battle of Nagashino and Shitarahara was a decisive battle during the Sengoku period that took place in 1575, when the combined forces of Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu clashed with the cavalry corps led by Takeda Katsuyori. Nobunaga built a horse stockade and deployed a gun corps, and used a ``three-stage attack'' to defeat Takeda's elite cavalry corps one after another. The Takeda army, hailed as the strongest in the Sengoku period, was destroyed, and it became a historical turning point when guns fundamentally changed the tactics of the Sengoku period.

shizugatake_battlefield.name: 賤ヶ岳古戦場（長浜市）
shizugatake_battlefield.kana: しずがたけこせんじょうながはまし

transit.name: JR北陸本線木ノ本駅（またはリフト）

shizugatake_battlefield.highlight: 信長没後の覇権をめぐり羽柴秀吉が柴田勝家を破った天下統一への決定的一戦
shizugatake_battlefield.text: 賤ヶ岳の戦いは天正11年（1583年）に琵琶湖北岸の賤ヶ岳周辺で行われた合戦で、本能寺の変後に織田家の跡継ぎをめぐり羽柴秀吉と柴田勝家が激突しました。秀吉の電撃的な行軍「大返し」が勝敗を決し、勝家は北ノ庄城に敗走して妻・お市の方とともに自害しました。この勝利で秀吉は信長後継者としての地位を確立しました。「賤ヶ岳の七本槍」として知られる猛将たちも活躍しました。
shizugatake_battlefield.highlight_en: A decisive battle for the unification of Japan in which Hideyoshi Hashiba defeated Katsuie Shibata for supremacy after Nobunaga's death.
shizugatake_battlefield.text_en: The Battle of Shizugatake was a battle that took place around Mt. Shizugatake on the north shore of Lake Biwa in 1583, when Hideyoshi Hashiba and Katsuie Shibata clashed over who would become the successor to the Oda family after the Honnoji Incident. Hideyoshi's electric march ``Ogaeshi'' decided the outcome, and Katsuie fled to Kitanosho Castle and committed suicide along with his wife Oichi. With this victory, Hideyoshi established himself as Nobunaga's successor. The fierce generals known as the ``Seven Spears of Shizugatake'' also played an active role.

yamazaki_battlefield.name: 山崎古戦場・天王山（大山崎町）
yamazaki_battlefield.kana: やまざきこせんじょうてんのうざんおおやまざきちょう

transit.name: 阪急京都線大山崎駅（/ JR山崎駅から徒歩15分）

yamazaki_battlefield.highlight: 本能寺の変後わずか11日で明智光秀を討ち取り「三日天下」を終わらせた激戦地
yamazaki_battlefield.text: 山崎の戦いは天正10年（1582年）6月13日、本能寺の変から11日後に行われた合戦です。中国大返しで電撃的に引き返した羽柴秀吉が明智光秀と激突し、わずか数時間で光秀軍を壊滅させました。「天下分け目の天王山」という言葉はこの戦いから生まれ、今も勝負の分岐点を意味する言葉として使われています。山頂からは大阪湾まで望む絶景が広がります。
yamazaki_battlefield.highlight_en: The fierce battleground where Akechi Mitsuhide was defeated and the ``Three Days of Tenka'' ended just 11 days after the Honnoji Incident.
yamazaki_battlefield.text_en: The Battle of Yamazaki was fought on June 13, 1582, 11 days after the Honnoji Incident. Hashiba Hideyoshi, who made a shocking comeback to China, collided with Mitsuhide Akechi, annihilating Mitsuhide's army in just a few hours. The phrase ``Tenka-wakeme Tennozan'' was born from this battle, and is still used today to signify the turning point in battle. From the top of the mountain, you can enjoy a spectacular view all the way to Osaka Bay.

kurikara_battlefield.name: 倶利伽羅峠古戦場（津幡町・小矢部市）
kurikara_battlefield.kana: くりからとうげこせんじょうつばたまちおやべし

transit.name: IRいしかわ鉄道津幡駅（またはタクシー）

kurikara_battlefield.highlight: 木曾義仲が平家の大軍に牛の角に火をつけて突撃させ大勝した奇策の古戦場
kurikara_battlefield.text: 倶利伽羅峠の戦いは寿永2年（1183年）5月、木曾義仲（源義仲）率いる源氏軍が平家の大軍を撃破した合戦です。義仲は暗夜に牛の角に松明を縛り付けて平家軍に突撃させる奇策を用い、平家軍は峠の谷底に転落して壊滅しました。この勝利で義仲は上洛への道を開き「朝日将軍」と称えられましたが、後に義経に討たれ若くして命を落とします。
kurikara_battlefield.name_en: Kurikara Pass Ancient Battlefield (Tsubata Town/Oyabe City)
kurikara_battlefield.highlight_en: The ancient battlefield where Kiso Yoshinaka won a landslide victory by charging the large Heike army by setting fire to the horns of bulls.
kurikara_battlefield.text_en: The Battle of Kurikara Pass was fought in May 1183, in which the Minamoto clan army led by Kiso Yoshinaka (Minamoto no Yoshinaka) defeated a large Heike army. Yoshinaka used a strange trick in the dark of night, tying torches to the horns of cows and making them charge at the Heike army, and the Heike army fell to the bottom of the mountain pass and was destroyed. This victory paved the way for Yoshinaka to ascend to Kyoto, and he was hailed as the ``Asahi General,'' but he was later defeated by Yoshitsune and died at a young age.

dannoura_heike_ruins.name: 壇ノ浦合戦跡・みもすそ川公園
dannoura_heike_ruins.kana: だんのうらかっせんあとみもすそがわこうえん

transit.name: みもすそ川バス停すぐ

dannoura_heike_ruins.highlight: 源平合戦の最終決戦・壇ノ浦で平家が滅亡し安徳天皇が入水した歴史の場所
dannoura_heike_ruins.text: 壇ノ浦は関門海峡に位置し、文治元年（1185年）3月24日に源義経率いる源氏軍と平家軍が激突した源平合戦最後の決戦地です。海流と潮目を読んだ義経の戦術が功を奏し平家軍は壊滅。平清盛の孫・安徳天皇（8歳）は祖母・二位尼に抱かれて入水し、平家一門は滅亡しました。みもすそ川公園には源義経と平知盛の大砲像が向かい合って建っています。
dannoura_heike_ruins.highlight_en: The final decisive battle of the Genpei War, the historical place where the Heike family was destroyed at Dan-no-ura and where Emperor Antoku drowned.
dannoura_heike_ruins.text_en: Dan-no-ura is located in the Kanmon Straits and was the final battle site of the Genpei War, where the Minamoto clan forces led by Minamoto no Yoshitsune and the Heike forces clashed on March 24, 1185. Yoshitsune's tactics, which read the ocean currents and tides, were successful and the Heike army was annihilated. Taira no Kiyomori's grandson, Emperor Antoku (age 8), drowned in the arms of his grandmother, Nii-ni, and the Heike clan fell into ruin. In Mimosuso River Park, cannon statues of Minamoto no Yoshitsune and Taira Tomomori stand facing each other.

henmanji_chikugo_monument.name: 遍萬寺・筑後川合戦の碑
henmanji_chikugo_monument.kana: へんまんじちくごがわかっせんのひ

transit.name: 西鉄天神大牟田線宮の陣駅（宮ノ陣5-12-66）

henmanji_chikugo_monument.highlight: 宮ノ陣神社に隣接する遍萬寺境内に建つ「懐良親王・菊池武光公 筑後川合戦の碑」
henmanji_chikugo_monument.text: 遍萬寺は久留米市宮ノ陣に建つ浄土真宗の寺院で、境内に「懐良親王・菊池武光公 筑後川合戦の碑」が建てられています。宮ノ陣は筑後川の戦い（大保原合戦）の激戦地の一つで、南朝軍が北朝方の少弐軍を撃退した場所のほど近くにあります。隣接する宮ノ陣神社には「将軍梅」と呼ばれる樹齢数百年の梅の木も残っています。
henmanji_chikugo_monument.highlight_en: ``Monument of Imperial Prince Kaneyoshi and Prince Takemitsu Kikuchi of the Battle of Chikugo River'' is built in the precincts of Henmanji Temple adjacent to Miyanojin Shrine.
henmanji_chikugo_monument.text_en: Henman-ji Temple is a Jodo Shinshu temple located in Miyanojin, Kurume City, and the ``Monument to Imperial Prince Kaneyoshi, Takemitsu Kikuchi, and the Battle of Chikugo River'' is erected on the grounds. Miyanojin was one of the fierce battlegrounds of the Battle of Chikugo River (Battle of Ohobara), and is located close to the place where the Southern Court's army repulsed the Shoni army of the Northern Court. At the adjacent Miyanojin Shrine, there is also a plum tree that is several hundred years old, called ``Shogun Ume.''

katsuzui_castle_awa.name: 勝瑞城館跡（三好氏の阿波支配拠点）
katsuzui_castle_awa.kana: かつずいじょうかんあとみよしうじのあわしはいきょてん
katsuzui_castle_awa.highlight: 細川氏・三好氏が阿波国を支配した戦国時代の大規模城館跡、国の史跡
katsuzui_castle_awa.text: 勝瑞城館跡は、室町時代から戦国時代にかけて阿波国を支配した細川氏・三好氏の居館跡です。三好長慶の父・三好元長がここを拠点に勢力を拡大し、三好氏全盛期の政治・文化の中心地となりました。発掘調査で堀や礎石が確認され、国の史跡に指定されています。
katsuzui_castle_awa.name_en: Shozui Castle Ruins (Miyoshi clan's base of control in Awa)
katsuzui_castle_awa.highlight_en: A national historic site, the ruins of a large castle from the Sengoku period when the Hosokawa and Miyoshi clans ruled Awa Province
katsuzui_castle_awa.text_en: Shozui Castle ruins are the remains of the residences of the Hosokawa and Miyoshi clans, who ruled Awa Province from the Muromachi period to the Sengoku period. Motonaga Miyoshi, the father of Nagayoshi Miyoshi, expanded his influence from this base, and it became the center of politics and culture during the heyday of the Miyoshi clan. Excavations revealed the moat and foundation stones, and it has been designated as a national historic site.

ichinomiya_castle_awa.name: 一宮城跡（阿波一宮）
ichinomiya_castle_awa.kana: いちのみやじょうあとあわいちのみや
ichinomiya_castle_awa.highlight: 南北朝時代に築かれた阿波国最大の山城跡、細川氏・長宗我部氏が争奪した要衝
ichinomiya_castle_awa.text: 一宮城は南北朝時代に阿波守護・細川氏が築いた山城で、阿波国の政治的中枢として機能しました。後に長宗我部氏が入城するなど争奪が続き、豊臣軍の四国征伐で落城しました。現在は石垣や郭跡が残る山城で、山頂からは吉野川平野を一望できます。
ichinomiya_castle_awa.highlight_en: The ruins of Awa Province's largest mountain castle, built during the Nanbokucho period, and a strategic point fought over by the Hosokawa and Chosokabe clans.
ichinomiya_castle_awa.text_en: Ichinomiya Castle was a mountain castle built by the Hosokawa clan, the shugo of Awa during the period of the Northern and Southern Courts, and functioned as the political center of Awa Province. Later, the Chosokabe clan entered the castle, and the battle for the castle continued, and the castle fell during the Toyotomi army's conquest of Shikoku. Today, it is a mountain castle with stone walls and ruins remaining, and you can see the Yoshinogawa plain from the mountaintop.

bando_furyo_camp.name: 板東俘虜収容所跡・ドイツ館（鳴門市）
bando_furyo_camp.kana: ばんどうふりょしゅうようじょあとどいつかんなるとし
bando_furyo_camp.highlight: 第一次世界大戦中のドイツ兵捕虜が日本初のベートーベン「第九」を演奏した地
bando_furyo_camp.text: 板東俘虜収容所は大正6年（1917年）に開設され、第一次世界大戦で捕虜となったドイツ兵約1000人が収容されました。所長・松江豊寿の人道的な処遇のもと、捕虜たちは音楽や演劇を楽しみ、大正7年（1918年）6月1日に日本で初めてベートーベンの交響曲第九番を全曲演奏しました。現在はドイツ館として整備され、日独友好の象徴となっています。
bando_furyo_camp.name_en: Bando POW Camp Ruins/German Pavilion (Naruto City)
bando_furyo_camp.highlight_en: The place where German prisoners of war during World War I played Beethoven's "Ninth" for the first time in Japan.
bando_furyo_camp.text_en: Bando Prisoner of War Camp was opened in 1917 and housed approximately 1,000 German soldiers captured during World War I. Under the humane treatment of the warden, Toyohisa Matsue, the POWs enjoyed music and drama, and on June 1, 1918, they performed Beethoven's Ninth Symphony in its entirety for the first time in Japan. Currently, it is being maintained as the German Pavilion and has become a symbol of Japan-Germany friendship.

naruto_uzushio.name: 鳴門の渦潮・うずしお観潮船
naruto_uzushio.kana: なるとのうずしおうずしおかんちょうせん
naruto_uzushio.highlight: 世界三大潮流の一つ、万葉集にも詠まれた鳴門海峡の大渦潮
naruto_uzushio.text: 鳴門海峡の渦潮は、紀伊水道と播磨灘の潮流差によって生まれる世界三大潮流の一つです。万葉集には「鳴門の浪は大渦に」と詠まれ、古来より人々を魅了してきました。大潮時には直径30メートルにも達する巨大な渦が発生し、渦の道や観潮船から間近に観察できます。
naruto_uzushio.highlight_en: The great whirlpools of the Naruto Strait, one of the world's three major currents and written about in the Manyoshu.
naruto_uzushio.text_en: The whirlpools of the Naruto Strait are one of the three major tidal currents in the world, created by the difference in tidal currents between the Kii Channel and the Harima Sea. The Manyoshu poem says, ``Naruto's waves become a maelstrom,'' and it has fascinated people since ancient times. During spring tides, gigantic whirlpools up to 30 meters in diameter occur, and can be observed up close from the whirlpool path or from a sightseeing boat.

oboke_gorge_history.name: 大歩危・祖谷渓（平家落人の里）
oboke_gorge_history.kana: おおぼけいやだにへいけおちゅうどのさと

transit.name: JR土讃線大歩危駅（・バス）

oboke_gorge_history.highlight: 壇ノ浦の戦いで敗れた平家の落人が隠れ住んだと伝わる秘境の渓谷
oboke_gorge_history.text: 祖谷渓は徳島県三好市の深山幽谷で、平家の落人が壇ノ浦の合戦後に逃れ住んだという伝説が残る地です。かずら橋や平家屋敷など落人文化の遺構が点在し、急峻な地形が外部との隔絶を保ちました。大歩危峡とともに吉野川の雄大な渓谷美を誇り、国の天然記念物に指定されています。
oboke_gorge_history.highlight_en: An unexplored valley where it is said that the Heike fugitives who were defeated in the Battle of Dan-no-ura lived in hiding.
oboke_gorge_history.text_en: Iya Gorge is a deep mountain valley in Miyoshi City, Tokushima Prefecture, where legend has it that the Heike stragglers fled to live there after the Battle of Dannoura. Remains of the fugitive culture such as Kazurabashi Bridge and Heike residences are scattered here and there, and the steep topography kept the area isolated from the outside world. Along with Oboke Gorge, it boasts the beauty of the majestic Yoshino River valley and has been designated as a national natural monument.

ryuoji_temple_awa.name: 霊山寺（四国八十八ヶ所第一番）
ryuoji_temple_awa.kana: りょうぜんじしこくはちじゅうはちかしょだいいちばん
ryuoji_temple_awa.highlight: 弘法大師・空海が開創した四国八十八ヶ所霊場の第一番札所
ryuoji_temple_awa.text: 霊山寺は奈良時代に行基が開基し、弘法大師空海が四国霊場の第一番札所として定めたと伝わる真言宗の寺院です。お遍路の出発地として全国から参拝者が訪れ、白衣・菅笠・金剛杖を身につけた巡礼者の姿が絶えません。境内には弘法大師像と多宝塔が建ち、四国遍路の精神的な旅立ちの地となっています。
ryuoji_temple_awa.name_en: Ryozenji Temple (No. 1 of the 88 temples in Shikoku)
ryuoji_temple_awa.highlight_en: The first of the 88 sacred sites in Shikoku founded by Kobo Daishi, Kukai
ryuoji_temple_awa.text_en: Ryozen-ji Temple is a Shingon sect temple founded by Gyoki in the Nara period and said to have been designated by Kobo Daishi Kukai as the number one sacred site in Shikoku. Worshipers come from all over the country as the starting point for the pilgrimage, and pilgrims wearing white robes, sedge hats, and diamond-shaped canes are always seen there. A statue of Kobo Daishi and a Tahoto pagoda are built in the precincts, making it a spiritual starting point for pilgrims on the Shikoku Pilgrimage.

awa_jurobe_yashiki.name: 阿波十郎兵衛屋敷（人形浄瑠璃の地）
awa_jurobe_yashiki.kana: あわじゅうろうべえやしきにんぎょうじょうるりのち
awa_jurobe_yashiki.highlight: 阿波踊りと並ぶ徳島の伝統芸能・阿波人形浄瑠璃の実演が見られる史跡
awa_jurobe_yashiki.text: 阿波十郎兵衛屋敷は、江戸時代に実在した白子屋お半・十郎兵衛の物語を題材にした人形浄瑠璃「傾城阿波の鳴門」ゆかりの地です。徳島藩が育んだ阿波人形浄瑠璃は、人形遣い・太夫・三味線の三業が一体となった芸能で、国の重要無形民俗文化財に指定されています。屋敷内では毎日定期公演が行われています。
awa_jurobe_yashiki.highlight_en: A historical site where you can see demonstrations of Awa Ningyo Joruri, a traditional performing art of Tokushima that rivals Awa Odori.
awa_jurobe_yashiki.text_en: Awa Jurobei House is the place where the puppet theater ``Kanjo Awa no Naruto'' is based on the story of Shirakoya Ohan Jurobei, who existed in the Edo period. Awa Ningyo Joruri, developed by the Tokushima clan, is a performing art that combines the three arts of puppetry, tayu, and shamisen, and has been designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property. Regular performances are held in the mansion every day.

wakimachi_udatsu.name: 脇町うだつの町並み（美馬市）
wakimachi_udatsu.kana: わきまちうだつのまちなみみまし
wakimachi_udatsu.highlight: 藍商人が栄えた江戸〜明治期の商家建築が残る「うだつの上がる」町並み
wakimachi_udatsu.text: 脇町は吉野川中流に位置し、江戸時代から明治にかけて阿波藍の集散地として栄えた商業都市です。「うだつの上がる」という言葉の語源ともなった防火壁（うだつ）を持つ白漆喰の商家が約400メートルにわたって続き、国の重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に指定されています。
wakimachi_udatsu.highlight_en: The ``Udatsu no Nagar'' townscape retains merchant house architecture from the Edo to Meiji periods, when indigo merchants flourished.
wakimachi_udatsu.text_en: Wakimachi is located in the middle reaches of the Yoshinogawa River and is a commercial city that flourished as a distribution center for Awa indigo from the Edo period to the Meiji period. The white stucco merchant houses with fire walls (udatsu), which are the origin of the word ``udatsu rising'', extend for approximately 400 meters and have been designated as a nationally important preservation district for groups of traditional buildings.

awa_kokubunji.name: 阿波国分寺跡（徳島市）
awa_kokubunji.kana: あわこくぶんじあととくしまし
awa_kokubunji.highlight: 聖武天皇の詔で建立された阿波の国分寺、現在も四国遍路第15番札所として続く古刹
awa_kokubunji.text: 阿波国分寺は天平13年（741年）、聖武天皇が諸国に建立を命じた国分寺の一つです。現在は四国八十八ヶ所霊場第15番札所として知られ、境内には奈良時代の礎石が残っています。藤原氏ゆかりの七重塔跡も発見されており、阿波国の古代仏教文化を今に伝えています。
awa_kokubunji.highlight_en: Kokubunji Temple in Awa was built by Emperor Shomu's edict, and is an ancient temple that continues today as the 15th temple on the Shikoku Pilgrimage Route.
awa_kokubunji.text_en: Awa Kokubunji is one of the Kokubunji temples that Emperor Shomu ordered to be built in various countries in 741. It is currently known as the 15th temple of the 88 Sacred Sites of Shikoku, and the foundation stones from the Nara period remain within the grounds. The ruins of a seven-storied pagoda associated with the Fujiwara clan have also been discovered, conveying the ancient Buddhist culture of Awa Province.

bizan_tokushima.name: 眉山公園（徳島市）
bizan_tokushima.kana: びざんこうえんとくしまし
bizan_tokushima.highlight: 徳島城下を見守る「眉の山」、阿波踊りや徳島藩の歴史を一望する展望地
bizan_tokushima.text: 眉山は徳島市のシンボルとも言える標高290メートルの山で、その稜線が眉のように見えることから名付けられました。山頂からは吉野川河口・徳島平野・紀伊水道を一望でき、かつては徳島城の詰城として機能しました。さだまさしの小説・映画「眉山」の舞台としても知られ、夜景スポットとしても人気です。
bizan_tokushima.highlight_en: ``Byanoyama'' watches over Tokushima Castle, an observation point that overlooks Awa Odori and the history of the Tokushima clan.
bizan_tokushima.text_en: Bizan is a 290 meter high mountain that can be said to be the symbol of Tokushima City, and was named because its ridgeline looks like an eyebrow. From the mountaintop, you can see the Yoshinogawa estuary, the Tokushima Plain, and the Kii Channel, and it once functioned as the fortress of Tokushima Castle. It is also known as the setting for Masashi Sada's novel and movie ``Bizan'' and is also a popular night view spot.

marugame_castle.name: 丸亀城（石垣の名城）
marugame_castle.kana: まるがめじょういしがきのめいじょう
marugame_castle.highlight: 現存12天守の一つ、日本一高い石垣（60m）を誇る丸亀藩京極氏の居城
marugame_castle.text: 丸亀城は讃岐国丸亀平野に築かれた平山城で、現存する12天守の一つです。特に4段重ねの石垣は高さ約60メートルに達し、日本一高い城の石垣として知られています。江戸時代は京極氏の城下町として栄え、現存天守は寛永年間に建てられた木造3層の小ぶりながら美しい天守で、国の重要文化財に指定されています。
marugame_castle.highlight_en: The castle of the Kyogoku clan of the Marugame clan, which boasts one of the 12 existing castle towers and the highest stone wall (60m) in Japan.
marugame_castle.text_en: Marugame Castle is a flat mountain castle built on the Marugame Plain in Sanuki Province, and is one of the 12 remaining castle towers. In particular, the four-tiered stone wall reaches a height of approximately 60 meters and is known as the tallest castle stone wall in Japan. During the Edo period, it flourished as a castle town of the Kyogoku clan, and the existing castle tower is a small but beautiful three-story wooden castle tower built during the Kanei era, and has been designated as a national important cultural property.

yashima_battlefield.name: 屋島古戦場（源平合戦の地）
yashima_battlefield.kana: やしまこせんじょうげんぺいかっせんのち

transit.name: 高松琴平電気鉄道琴電屋島駅

yashima_battlefield.highlight: 那須与一が扇の的を射た源平屋島の戦い（1185年）の古戦場
yashima_battlefield.text: 屋島は高松市北東部の台地状の半島で、寿永4年（1185年）2月に源義経率いる源氏軍と平家軍が激突した屋島の戦いの舞台です。「扇の的」で那須与一が平家の船上の扇を射抜いた故事はここで起き、源平合戦最後の陸上決戦となりました。屋島寺や源平合戦ミュージアムがあり、讃岐富士とも呼ばれる景観の中に古戦場の史跡が残っています。
yashima_battlefield.name_en: Yashima Battlefield (ground of the Genpei War)
yashima_battlefield.highlight_en: The old battlefield of the Battle of Genpei Yashima (1185), where Nasu Yoichi hit the target with his fan.
yashima_battlefield.text_en: Yashima is a plateau-like peninsula in the northeastern part of Takamatsu City, and was the site of the Battle of Yashima, where the Minamoto clan forces led by Minamoto no Yoshitsune and the Heike forces clashed in February 1185. The story of Nasu Yoichi shooting through a fan on a Heike ship at ``Ogi no Target'' occurred here, and it was the final land battle of the Genpei War. There is Yashima-dera Temple and the Genpei War Museum, and historic sites of the old battlefield remain in the landscape that is also known as Sanuki Fuji.

zentsuji_kukai.name: 善通寺（弘法大師の生誕地）
zentsuji_kukai.kana: ぜんつうじこうぼうだいしのせいたんち
zentsuji_kukai.highlight: 四国八十八ヶ所第75番札所・真言宗の総本山、空海（弘法大師）の生誕地
zentsuji_kukai.text: 善通寺は弘法大師・空海が延暦23年（807年）に父の佐伯直田公（さえきのあたいたぎみ）の邸宅跡に建立した寺で、空海の生誕地とされています。東寺・高野山と並ぶ真言宗三大霊跡の一つで、誕生院と西院の二院からなる広大な境内に金堂・五重塔など重要文化財が多数残ります。境内には空海が生まれたとされる産湯の井戸もあります。
