zentsuji_kukai.highlight_en: The 75th temple of the 88 temples in Shikoku, the head temple of the Shingon sect, and the birthplace of Kukai (Kobo Daishi)
zentsuji_kukai.text_en: Zentsuji is a temple built by Kobo Daishi Kukai in 807 on the site of the residence of his father, Saeki Naota, and is said to be Kukai's birthplace. It is one of the three major sacred sites of the Shingon sect, along with To-ji Temple and Mt. Koya, and there are many important cultural properties such as the Kondo Hall and the five-storied pagoda within the vast precincts, which consist of two temples, Tanjo-in Temple and Sai-in Temple. There is also a well on the grounds where Kukai is said to have been born.

kotohira_shrine.name: 金刀比羅宮（こんぴらさん）
kotohira_shrine.kana: ことひらぐうこんぴらさん

transit.name: JR土讃線琴平駅（（本宮まで785段））

kotohira_shrine.highlight: 全国のこんぴらさんの総本宮、江戸時代に「一生に一度はこんぴら参り」と言われた海の守護神
kotohira_shrine.text: 金刀比羅宮は象頭山の中腹に鎮座する古社で、海上交通の守護神として全国の船乗りや庶民から篤く信仰されてきました。江戸時代には「一生に一度はこんぴら参り」と言われ、東海道・中山道と並ぶ金比羅街道が整備されるほどの賑わいでした。本宮まで785段の石段が続き、奥社まで登ると讃岐平野と瀬戸内海を一望できます。
kotohira_shrine.highlight_en: The main shrine of Konpira-san all over the country, the guardian deity of the sea that was said to be visited at least once in a lifetime during the Edo period.
kotohira_shrine.text_en: Kotohira Shrine is an ancient shrine located halfway up Mt. Zouzu, and has been devoutly worshiped by sailors and ordinary people from all over the country as the guardian deity of maritime transportation. During the Edo period, it was said that you should visit Konpira at least once in your life, and it was so popular that the Konpira Kaido road was built to rival the Tokaido and Nakasendo roads. There are 785 stone steps leading up to the main shrine, and if you climb up to the Okusha Shrine, you can see the Sanuki Plain and the Seto Inland Sea.

mannogike_kukai.name: 満濃池（空海が修築した日本最大の農業池）
mannogike_kukai.kana: まんのういけくうかいがしゅうちくしたにほんさいだいののうぎょういけ
mannogike_kukai.highlight: 奈良時代に造られ弘法大師・空海が修築した日本最大の農業用ため池
mannogike_kukai.text: 満濃池は周囲約20キロメートルを誇る日本最大の農業用ため池で、奈良時代初期（701年頃）に讃岐国司・道守朝臣らが築造しました。たびたび決壊し修復が困難を極めていましたが、弘法大師・空海が弘仁12年（821年）に3ヶ月で修築を完成させたと伝わります。農業水利の確保に生涯を捧げた空海の功績を示す史跡です。
mannogike_kukai.name_en: Manno Pond (Japan's largest agricultural pond built by Kukai)
mannogike_kukai.highlight_en: Japan's largest agricultural reservoir built during the Nara period and renovated by Kobo Daishi and Kukai
mannogike_kukai.text_en: Manno Pond is the largest agricultural pond in Japan, with a circumference of approximately 20 kilometers, and was built by Sanuki Kokushi Michimori Asaomi and others in the early Nara period (around 701). Although it was often destroyed and repaired was extremely difficult, it is said that Kobo Daishi Kukai completed the renovation in 3 months in 821. This is a historical site that shows the achievements of Kukai, who dedicated his life to securing agricultural irrigation.

shirogamineji_sutoku.name: 白峯寺・崇徳天皇陵（坂出市）
shirogamineji_sutoku.kana: しろみねじすとくてんのうりょうさかいでし

transit.name: JR予讃線坂出駅（・タクシー）

shirogamineji_sutoku.highlight: 保元の乱で讃岐に流され没した崇徳上皇が葬られた霊場
shirogamineji_sutoku.text: 白峯寺は四国八十八ヶ所第81番札所で、境内に崇徳天皇（崇徳上皇）の陵墓があります。崇徳上皇は保元元年（1156年）の保元の乱に敗れて讃岐国に流され、長寛2年（1164年）にこの地で崩御しました。怨霊として恐れられた崇徳院は後に京都・白峯神宮に祀られましたが、讃岐での薨去の地として白峯寺は今も多くの参拝者が訪れます。
shirogamineji_sutoku.name_en: Shiramineji Temple and Mausoleum of Emperor Sutoku (Sakaide City)
shirogamineji_sutoku.highlight_en: A sacred place where Retired Emperor Sutoku, who was exiled to Sanuki during the Hogen Rebellion, was buried.
shirogamineji_sutoku.text_en: Shiramineji Temple is the 81st of the 88 temples in Shikoku, and the tomb of Emperor Sutoku (Retired Emperor Sutoku) is located within the temple grounds. Retired Emperor Sutoku was defeated in the Hogen War in 1156 and exiled to Sanuki Province, where he passed away in 1164. Sutoku-in, who was feared as a vengeful spirit, was later enshrined at Shiramine Shrine in Kyoto, but Shiramine-ji Temple, where he died in Sanuki, is still visited by many worshipers.

hiketa_castle.name: 引田城跡（東かがわ市）
hiketa_castle.kana: ひけたじょうあとひがしかがわし
hiketa_castle.highlight: 讃岐東部の海城・引田城、仙石秀久や生駒氏など歴代の城主が争った要衝
hiketa_castle.text: 引田城は瀬戸内海に突き出した半島の山頂に築かれた典型的な海城で、讃岐東部の海上交通の要衝として機能しました。豊臣秀吉の家臣・仙石秀久が入城し、その後生駒氏が讃岐を支配した際の重要拠点となりました。急峻な岩山に残る石垣が美しく、眼下には播磨灘が広がります。
hiketa_castle.highlight_en: Kaijo and Hikita Castle in eastern Sanuki, strategic points where successive castle lords such as Hidehisa Sengoku and the Ikoma clan fought over each other.
hiketa_castle.text_en: Hikita Castle is a typical maritime castle built on the top of a peninsula that juts out into the Seto Inland Sea, and served as a strategic point for maritime transportation in eastern Sanuki. Hidehisa Sengoku, a vassal of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, entered the castle and later became an important base when the Ikoma clan ruled Sanuki. The stone wall that remains on the steep rocky mountain is beautiful, and the Harima Sea spreads out below.

takamatsu_castle.name: 高松城跡（玉藻公園）
takamatsu_castle.kana: たかまつじょうあとたまもこうえん
takamatsu_castle.highlight: 海に浮かぶ「海城」、松平氏12万石の居城で国の特別史跡
takamatsu_castle.text: 高松城は天正16年（1588年）に生駒親正が築き、後に徳川家康の孫・松平頼重が讃岐に封じられた際の居城となりました。三方を海に囲まれた「海城」として知られ、城内に海水を引き込んだ堀には鯛が泳いでいたと伝わります。現在は玉藻公園として整備され、月見櫓・水手御門・渡櫓が現存し国の重要文化財に指定されています。
takamatsu_castle.highlight_en: ``Kaijō'' floating on the sea, the residence of the Matsudaira clan with 120,000 koku of land and a special national historic site
takamatsu_castle.text_en: Takamatsu Castle was built by Chikamasa Ikoma in 1588, and later became the residence of Yorishige Matsudaira, the grandson of Tokugawa Ieyasu, when he was confined to Sanuki. It is known as a ``sea castle'' because it is surrounded by the sea on three sides, and it is said that sea bream were swimming in the moat that drew seawater into the castle. Currently, it is maintained as Tamamo Park, and the Tsukimi Yagura, Mizute Gomon, and Watari Yagura remain and are designated as important cultural properties of the country.

shido_temple_fujiwara.name: 志度寺（藤原不比等ゆかりの地）
shido_temple_fujiwara.kana: しどじふじわらのふひとゆかりのち

transit.name: 高松琴平電気鉄道志度駅

shido_temple_fujiwara.highlight: 藤原不比等の母・海女が命を落とした「海女の珠取り」伝説の地、四国霊場第86番札所
shido_temple_fujiwara.text: 志度寺は飛鳥時代に創建された真言宗の古刹で、四国八十八ヶ所第86番札所です。藤原鎌足の遺品・面向不背玉（めんこうふはいのたま）が海底に沈み、藤原不比等の命で海女がその珠を取り戻す際に命を落としたという「海女の珠取り」の伝説で知られます。境内の「曲水の庭」は江戸時代の大名庭園として名高く、不比等の墓とされる石塔も残っています。
shido_temple_fujiwara.name_en: Shidoji Temple (place related to Fujiwara Fuhito)
shido_temple_fujiwara.highlight_en: Shikoku Sacred Site No. 86, the legendary place of "Ama's Pearl Catch" where Fujiwara Fuhito's mother, Ama, lost her life.
shido_temple_fujiwara.text_en: Shido-ji Temple is an ancient temple of the Shingon sect founded in the Asuka period, and is the 86th temple among the 88 temples of Shikoku. It is famous for the legend of the ``Ama's Pearl Retrieval'', in which Fujiwara Kamatari's belongings, Menkofu Hai no Tama, sank to the bottom of the ocean, and an ama diver lost her life trying to retrieve the pearl at the behest of Fujiwara Fuhito. The ``Kyokusui Garden'' in the precincts is famous as a feudal lord garden from the Edo period, and the stone tower that is said to be Fuhito's tomb still remains.

kagawa_salt_history.name: 入浜式塩田跡・塩の資料館（坂出市）
kagawa_salt_history.kana: いりはましきえんでんあとしおのしりょうかんさかいでし
kagawa_salt_history.highlight: 江戸時代から昭和中期まで「讃岐の塩」として全国に知られた入浜式製塩業の史跡
kagawa_salt_history.text: 讃岐（香川）は温暖少雨の気候を活かし、江戸時代から全国有数の製塩地として知られていました。入浜式塩田と呼ばれる潮汐を利用した製塩技術は江戸時代に発達し、「讃岐の白い黄金」として流通しました。坂出市の塩の資料館では往時の塩田道具や製塩工程が展示され、讃岐塩業の歴史を今に伝えています。
kagawa_salt_history.name_en: Irihama-style salt fields and salt museum (Sakaide City)
kagawa_salt_history.highlight_en: A historical site of the Irihama-style salt manufacturing industry, known nationwide as "Sanuki Salt" from the Edo period to the mid-Showa period.
kagawa_salt_history.text_en: Sanuki (Kagawa) has been known as one of the nation's leading salt producing regions since the Edo period, taking advantage of its warm and dry climate. A salt manufacturing technique that uses the tides, called Irihama-style salt fields, was developed during the Edo period and was distributed as ``Sanuki's white gold.'' The Salt Museum in Sakaide City exhibits salt field tools and salt production processes from the past, telling the history of the Sanuki salt industry.

imabari_castle_todo.name: 今治城（藤堂高虎が築いた海城）
imabari_castle_todo.kana: いまばりじょうとうどうたかとらがきずいたうみしろ
imabari_castle_todo.highlight: 海水を引き込んだ堀を持つ日本三大海城の一つ、藤堂高虎が慶長7年に築城
imabari_castle_todo.text: 今治城は慶長7年（1602年）に藤堂高虎が伊予に入封して築いた平城で、海水を直接引き込んだ三重の堀を持つ日本三大海城の一つです。高虎は海城の縄張り技術に卓越した築城の名手として知られ、今治城はその代表作の一つです。現在は復元天守と石垣が残り、堀には鯛などの海魚が泳いでいます。
imabari_castle_todo.name_en: Imabari Castle (Sea castle built by Todo Takatora)
imabari_castle_todo.highlight_en: One of the three major sea castles in Japan, with a moat filled with seawater, it was built by Todo Takatora in 1986.
imabari_castle_todo.text_en: Imabari Castle is a flat castle built by Todo Takatora in 1602 when he entered Iyo, and is one of Japan's three major sea castles with a triple moat that draws in seawater directly. Takatora is known as a master castle builder who excels in sea castle territorial techniques, and Imabari Castle is one of his masterpieces. Today, the restored castle tower and stone walls remain, and sea fish such as sea bream swim in the moat.

ozu_castle.name: 大洲城（肱川の城下町）
ozu_castle.kana: おおずじょうひじかわのじょうかまち
ozu_castle.highlight: 肱川沿いの「伊予の小京都」、木造復元天守が美しい大洲藩加藤氏の居城
ozu_castle.text: 大洲城は肱川が蛇行する丘に建つ城で、「伊予の小京都」と呼ばれる大洲の中心です。江戸時代は加藤氏の大洲藩の居城として栄えました。天守は明治に解体されましたが、2004年に古写真と古材料をもとに木造で完全復元され、全国でも珍しい本格木造復元天守として注目されています。
ozu_castle.highlight_en: ``Iyo's Little Kyoto'' along the Hijigawa River, the residence of the Kato clan of Ozu Domain with a beautiful restored wooden castle tower
ozu_castle.text_en: Ozu Castle is a castle built on a hill where the Hijikawa River meanders, and is the center of Ozu, which is known as ``Iyo's Little Kyoto.'' During the Edo period, it flourished as the residence of the Kato clan's Ozu domain. The castle tower was dismantled in the Meiji era, but in 2004 it was completely restored as a wooden structure based on old photographs and old materials, and is attracting attention as one of the rare authentic wooden restored castle towers in Japan.

uwajima_castle.name: 宇和島城（現存12天守）
uwajima_castle.kana: うわじまじょうげんそんじゅうにてんしゅ
uwajima_castle.highlight: 伊達氏が治めた南予の要城、現存12天守のうち唯一の独立式層塔型天守
uwajima_castle.text: 宇和島城は慶長6年（1601年）に藤堂高虎が築き、その後伊達秀宗（伊達政宗の長男）が宇和島藩初代藩主として入城しました。現存する天守は寛文年間に建て替えられたもので、現存12天守の一つです。独立式層塔型という独特の構造を持ち、三ノ丸から続く急峻な石段が城の威容を高めています。
uwajima_castle.highlight_en: An important castle in Nanyo ruled by the Date clan, the only independent tower tower out of 12 existing castle towers.
uwajima_castle.text_en: Uwajima Castle was built by Todo Takatora in 1601, and later, Date Hidemune (Date Masamune's eldest son) entered the castle as the first lord of the Uwajima domain. The current castle tower was rebuilt during the Kanbun era and is one of the 12 castle towers in existence. It has a unique structure in the form of an independent layered tower, and the steep stone steps leading from Sannomaru add to the castle's majesty.

dogo_onsen_history.name: 道後温泉本館（日本最古の温泉）
dogo_onsen_history.kana: どうごおんせんほんかんにほんさいこのおんせん

transit.name: 松山市電道後温泉電停すぐ

dogo_onsen_history.highlight: 3000年の歴史を誇る日本最古の温泉、夏目漱石『坊っちゃん』の舞台
dogo_onsen_history.text: 道後温泉は愛媛県松山市に位置し、日本書紀にも記された日本最古の温泉の一つです。神話では少彦名命（すくなひこなのみこと）が傷を癒したとされ、聖徳太子や大国主命ゆかりの伝説も多く残っています。明治27年（1894年）に建てられた道後温泉本館は国の重要文化財で、夏目漱石の小説『坊っちゃん』の「湯」のモデルとしても有名です。
dogo_onsen_history.name_en: Dogo Onsen Main Building (Japan's oldest hot spring)
dogo_onsen_history.highlight_en: Japan's oldest hot spring with a history of 3000 years, the setting for Natsume Soseki's ``Botchan''
dogo_onsen_history.text_en: Dogo Onsen is located in Matsuyama City, Ehime Prefecture, and is one of the oldest hot springs in Japan, recorded in the Nihon Shoki. In mythology, Sukunahikona no Mikoto is said to have healed wounds, and there are many legends related to Prince Shotoku and Okuninushi no Mikoto. The Dogo Onsen Main Building, built in 1894, is a nationally important cultural property and is famous as the model for the hot spring in Natsume Soseki's novel Botchan.

noshima_murakami_navy.name: 能島城跡（能島村上水軍の本拠）
noshima_murakami_navy.kana: のしまじょうあとのしまむらかみすいぐんのほんきょ
noshima_murakami_navy.highlight: 瀬戸内最強の海賊衆・村上水軍の本城、今も潮流で守られた孤島の城跡
noshima_murakami_navy.text: 能島城は今治市沖の瀬戸内海に浮かぶ無人島・能島に築かれた海城で、戦国時代に瀬戸内海を支配した村上水軍（能島村上氏）の本拠地です。周囲を激しい潮流が取り囲み、天然の要害として機能しました。織田信長も海上交通権を握る村上水軍を重視し同盟を結ぼうとしたほど、その海洋軍事力は絶大でした。
noshima_murakami_navy.name_en: Noshima Castle Ruins (base of Noshima Murakami Navy)
noshima_murakami_navy.highlight_en: The main castle of the Murakami Navy, the strongest pirates in Setouchi, the ruins of a castle on an isolated island still protected by the currents.
noshima_murakami_navy.text_en: Noshima Castle is a sea castle built on Noshima, an uninhabited island in the Seto Inland Sea off the coast of Imabari City, and was the headquarters of the Murakami Navy (Noshima Murakami clan), which ruled the Seto Inland Sea during the Sengoku period. Surrounded by strong currents, it functioned as a natural fortress. Murakami's maritime military power was so great that even Oda Nobunaga valued the Murakami Navy's control of maritime traffic and tried to form an alliance with it.

kawano_clan_yuzuki.name: 湯築城跡（河野氏の居城）
kawano_clan_yuzuki.kana: ゆづきじょうあとかわのうじのきょじょう

transit.name: 松山市電道後温泉電停

kawano_clan_yuzuki.highlight: 鎌倉から戦国時代まで伊予を支配した河野氏の本城、道後温泉隣接の国史跡
kawano_clan_yuzuki.text: 湯築城は道後温泉のすぐそばに築かれた平山城で、鎌倉時代から戦国時代にかけて伊予国の守護大名・河野氏の居城でした。二重の堀と土塁が良好に残り、国の史跡に指定されています。発掘調査では当時の武家屋敷・武具・陶磁器などが多数出土し、中世伊予の生活文化を伝えています。
kawano_clan_yuzuki.highlight_en: The main castle of the Kono clan, which ruled Iyo from Kamakura to the Sengoku period, is a national historic site adjacent to Dogo Onsen.
kawano_clan_yuzuki.text_en: Yuzuki Castle is a Hirayama castle built right next to Dogo Onsen, and was the residence of the Kono clan, the shugo daimyo of Iyo Province from the Kamakura period to the Sengoku period. The double moat and earthworks remain in good condition and are designated as a national historic site. During the excavation, many samurai residences, weapons, and ceramics from that time were unearthed, conveying the lifestyle culture of medieval Iyo.

akehama_history.name: 宇和島伊達家菩提寺・善応寺（宇和島市）
akehama_history.kana: うわじまだてけぼだいじぜんのうじうわじまし
akehama_history.highlight: 仙台伊達家の分家・宇和島伊達家の菩提寺、伊達秀宗の霊廟が残る
akehama_history.text: 善応寺は宇和島藩主・伊達家の菩提寺で、初代藩主・伊達秀宗以来歴代藩主の霊廟が設けられています。伊達秀宗は伊達政宗の長男として生まれ、大坂の陣後に宇和島10万石に封じられました。仙台伊達氏の文化を南予の地に持ち込み、武家文化と伊達家の伝統が今もこの地に息づいています。
akehama_history.name_en: Uwajima Date Family Temple / Zennoji Temple (Uwajima City)
akehama_history.highlight_en: The family temple of the Uwajima Date family, a branch of the Sendai Date family, and the mausoleum of Hidemune Date remain.
akehama_history.text_en: Zenno-ji Temple is the family temple of the Date family, the lords of Uwajima, and contains the mausoleums of successive lords since the first lord, Hidemune Date. Date Hidemune was born as the eldest son of Date Masamune, and after the Battle of Osaka, he was confined to Uwajima with 100,000 koku. The culture of the Sendai Date clan was brought to the land of Nanyo, and samurai culture and the traditions of the Date clan are still alive in this area.

saijo_daimyo_history.name: 西条陣屋跡（松平氏の西条藩）
saijo_daimyo_history.kana: さいじょうじんやあとまつだいらうじのさいじょうはん
saijo_daimyo_history.highlight: 御三家・紀州徳川家の支藩として栄えた西条藩の陣屋跡
saijo_daimyo_history.text: 西条陣屋は江戸時代の西条藩（現・愛媛県西条市）の藩庁跡です。西条藩は寛永13年（1636年）に紀州徳川家の支藩として立藩し、松平（紀州）頼純が初代藩主となりました。御三家の支藩として格式高く、現在も石垣と堀の一部が残っています。西条市は「うちぬき」と呼ばれる自噴地下水でも有名です。
saijo_daimyo_history.name_en: Saijo Jinya ruins (Saijo domain of the Matsudaira clan)
saijo_daimyo_history.highlight_en: The remains of the Saijo clan's camp, which flourished as a branch of the Kishu Tokugawa family, one of the three major families.
saijo_daimyo_history.text_en: Saijo Jinya is the site of the Edo period domain office of the Saijo domain (currently Saijo City, Ehime Prefecture). The Saijo domain was established in 1636 as a branch domain of the Kishu Tokugawa family, with Matsudaira (Kishu) Yorisumi becoming the first lord. It has a high status as a branch domain of the three Gosanke clans, and some of the stone walls and moat still remain today. Saijo City is also famous for its artesian groundwater called ``Uchinuki.''

matsuyama_city_history.name: 松山城天守（現存12天守）
matsuyama_city_history.kana: まつやまじょうてんしゅげんそんじゅうにてんしゅ
matsuyama_city_history.highlight: 加藤嘉明が築いた現存12天守の一つ、連立式天守が完存する全国唯一の城
matsuyama_city_history.text: 松山城は慶長7年（1602年）に加藤嘉明が築城を開始した平山城で、現存する12天守の一つです。天守・小天守・南隅櫓・北隅櫓・多聞櫓が連なる「連立式天守」が完全に残る全国唯一の城として知られています。幕末には長州征伐に反対した松山藩が戊辰戦争で官軍に包囲されるなど激動の歴史を刻んでいます。
matsuyama_city_history.highlight_en: One of the 12 existing castle towers built by Yoshiaki Kato, it is the only castle in Japan with a complete combination of tower towers.
matsuyama_city_history.text_en: Matsuyama Castle is a Hirayama castle whose construction was started by Yoshiaki Kato in 1602, and is one of the 12 castle towers still in existence. It is known as the only castle in Japan where the ``contiguous castle tower'' consisting of the castle tower, small castle tower, south corner turret, north corner turret, and Tamon turret remains intact. At the end of the Edo period, the Matsuyama clan, which opposed the Choshu conquest, was surrounded by government forces during the Boshin War, and the area has a turbulent history.

mishima_yukashima_village.name: 佐田岬半島・三崎の集落（伊方町）
mishima_yukashima_village.kana: さだみさきはんとうみさきのしゅうらくいかたちょう
mishima_yukashima_village.highlight: 四国最西端の細長い半島に点在する漁村集落、瀬戸内と宇和海を一望する絶景
mishima_yukashima_village.text: 佐田岬半島は四国最西端に延びる細長い半島で、日本最長の岬の一つです。江戸時代は宇和島藩の支配下にあり、半島に点在する集落は漁業と農業で独自の文化を育みました。半島先端からは豊後水道を挟んで大分県を望むことができ、沖合の海峡は豊後水道の海流が激しい難所として知られています。
mishima_yukashima_village.highlight_en: Spectacular views overlooking the Seto Inland Sea and the Uwa Sea, a fishing village dotted on a long and narrow peninsula at the westernmost tip of Shikoku
mishima_yukashima_village.text_en: Cape Sadamisaki Peninsula is a long and narrow peninsula that extends to the westernmost tip of Shikoku, and is one of the longest capes in Japan. During the Edo period, it was under the control of the Uwajima clan, and the villages scattered on the peninsula developed a unique culture based on fishing and agriculture. From the tip of the peninsula, you can see Oita Prefecture across the Bungo Channel, and the offshore strait is known as a difficult spot due to the strong ocean currents of the Bungo Channel.

uradu_castle_chosokabe.name: 浦戸城跡（長宗我部氏の本城）
uradu_castle_chosokabe.kana: うらどじょうあとちょうそかべうじのほんじょう

transit.name: 高知市桂浜方面バスで桂浜下車、徒歩15分

uradu_castle_chosokabe.highlight: 長宗我部元親が晩年を過ごし土佐を統治した四国統一の象徴的な城
uradu_castle_chosokabe.text: 浦戸城は桂浜の高台に築かれた城で、長宗我部元親が天正16年（1588年）に本拠を岡豊城からここに移しました。元親は四国をほぼ統一し土佐・阿波・伊予・讃岐の四国四国主として名乗りましたが、豊臣秀吉の四国征伐で敗れ土佐一国に封じられました。関ヶ原の戦い後に山内一豊が入城し高知城を築くまで土佐の中心地でした。
uradu_castle_chosokabe.name_en: Urato Castle ruins (main castle of the Chosokabe clan)
uradu_castle_chosokabe.highlight_en: A symbolic castle for the unification of Shikoku where Motochika Chosokabe spent his later years ruling Tosa.
uradu_castle_chosokabe.text_en: Urato Castle is a castle built on a hill in Katsurahama, and Motochika Chosokabe moved his headquarters here from Oka Toyo Castle in 1588. Motochika almost unified Shikoku and called himself the lord of the Shikoku region of Tosa, Awa, Iyo, and Sanuki, but he was defeated in Toyotomi Hideyoshi's conquest of Shikoku and was confined to Tosa Province. It was the center of Tosa until Kazutoyo Yamauchi entered the castle after the Battle of Sekigahara and built Kochi Castle.

ryoma_birthplace_kochi.name: 坂本龍馬誕生地碑（高知市）
ryoma_birthplace_kochi.kana: さかもとりょうまたんじょうちひこうちし

transit.name: 土佐電鉄上町一丁目電停

ryoma_birthplace_kochi.highlight: 日本の夜明けを夢見た幕末の志士・坂本龍馬の生誕地
ryoma_birthplace_kochi.text: 坂本龍馬は天保6年（1835年）、土佐藩の郷士・坂本八平の次男として高知市上町に生まれました。脱藩後に勝海舟の門下となり海援隊を組織、薩長同盟の成立に奔走して日本の近代化に向けた道筋を開きました。生誕地には石碑が建てられ、龍馬が幼少期を過ごした土地として多くの龍馬ファンが訪れます。
ryoma_birthplace_kochi.highlight_en: The birthplace of Ryoma Sakamoto, a patriot at the end of the Edo period who dreamed of the dawn of Japan.
ryoma_birthplace_kochi.text_en: Ryoma Sakamoto was born in Kamimachi, Kochi City in 1835 as the second son of Happei Sakamoto, a samurai of the Tosa domain. After breaking away from the domain, he became a disciple of Kaishu Katsu, organized the Kaientai, and worked hard to establish the Satsuma-Choshu alliance, paving the way for Japan's modernization. A stone monument has been erected at his birthplace, and many Ryoma fans visit the place where he spent his childhood.

takechi_zuizan_dojo.name: 武市瑞山旧宅跡・道場跡（高知市）
takechi_zuizan_dojo.kana: たけちずいざんきゅうたくあとどうじょうあとこうちし
takechi_zuizan_dojo.highlight: 土佐勤王党を組織し尊王攘夷運動を牽引した武市半平太の旧宅と道場跡
takechi_zuizan_dojo.text: 武市半平太（瑞山）は土佐藩の郷士出身で、文久元年（1861年）に土佐勤王党を組織して尊王攘夷運動の中心となりました。坂本龍馬・中岡慎太郎ら多くの志士が同党に集まりましたが、藩内の権力闘争で投獄され、元治元年（1864年）に切腹を命じられました。旧宅跡と剣道道場跡には顕彰碑が建てられています。
takechi_zuizan_dojo.name_en: Former Takeichi Zuizan residence and dojo ruins (Kochi City)
takechi_zuizan_dojo.highlight_en: The former home and dojo ruins of Hanpeita Takeichi, who organized the Tosa Kinno-to and led the son-no-joi movement.
takechi_zuizan_dojo.text_en: Hanpeita Takeichi (Zuizan) was a former samurai of the Tosa domain, and in 1861 he organized the Tosa Kinnoto party and became the center of the sonno-joi movement. Many patriots, including Ryoma Sakamoto and Shintaro Nakaoka, joined the party, but due to a power struggle within the domain, they were imprisoned and ordered to commit seppuku in 1864. A memorial monument has been erected at the site of his former residence and Kendo dojo.

nakaoka_shintaro_birthplace.name: 中岡慎太郎館（北川村）
nakaoka_shintaro_birthplace.kana: なかおかしんたろうかんきたがわむら

transit.name: 土佐くろしお鉄道奈半利駅

nakaoka_shintaro_birthplace.highlight: 陸援隊を率い龍馬とともに暗殺された幕末志士・中岡慎太郎の生誕地
nakaoka_shintaro_birthplace.text: 中岡慎太郎は天保14年（1843年）、土佐国安芸郡北川村に生まれました。武市瑞山の土佐勤王党に参加後、薩摩藩と連携して倒幕運動を展開し、陸援隊を組織して倒幕の志士たちを束ねました。慶応3年（1867年）11月15日、坂本龍馬とともに京都・近江屋で暗殺されました。北川村の記念館では慎太郎の生涯と業績を展示しています。
nakaoka_shintaro_birthplace.highlight_en: Birthplace of Shintaro Nakaoka, a patriot at the end of the Edo period who led the Rikuentai and was assassinated along with Ryoma.
nakaoka_shintaro_birthplace.text_en: Shintaro Nakaoka was born in 1843 in Kitagawa Village, Aki District, Tosa Province. After joining Takeichi Mizuzan's Tosa Kinnoto party, he collaborated with the Satsuma domain to develop a movement to overthrow the shogunate, and organized the Rikuentai to unite the patriots who wanted to overthrow the shogunate. On November 15, 1867, he was assassinated along with Ryoma Sakamoto at Omiya, Kyoto. The Kitagawa Village Memorial Hall exhibits Shintaro's life and achievements.

yamauchi_kochi_domain.name: 山内家宝物資料館（高知市）
yamauchi_kochi_domain.kana: やまうちけほうもつしりょうかんこうちし

transit.name: 土佐電鉄高知城前電停

yamauchi_kochi_domain.highlight: 関ヶ原後に土佐20万石に封じられた山内家の甲冑・刀剣・古文書などを収蔵
yamauchi_kochi_domain.text: 山内家宝物資料館は高知城の二の丸跡に建てられた展示施設で、土佐藩主・山内家に伝わる甲冑・刀剣・能装束・古文書などの文化財を収蔵・展示しています。山内一豊は関ヶ原の戦いでの功績により徳川家康から土佐20万石を与えられ、妻・千代との「内助の功」の逸話でも知られています。
yamauchi_kochi_domain.highlight_en: Stores the Yamauchi family's armor, swords, ancient documents, etc., which were sealed in Tosa 200,000 koku after Sekigahara.
yamauchi_kochi_domain.text_en: The Yamauchi Family Treasures Museum is an exhibition facility built on the Ninomaru ruins of Kochi Castle, and stores and exhibits cultural assets such as armor, swords, Noh costumes, and ancient documents handed down by the Yamauchi family, the lords of the Tosa domain. Kazutoyo Yamauchi was given 200,000 koku of Tosa by Tokugawa Ieyasu for his achievements in the Battle of Sekigahara, and is also known for his anecdote about ``Uchisuke's exploits'' with his wife Chiyo.

tosa_han_gakko_chidokan.name: 旧土佐藩校「致道館」跡（高知市）
tosa_han_gakko_chidokan.kana: きゅうとさはんこうちどうかんあとこうちし

transit.name: 土佐電鉄高知城前電停

tosa_han_gakko_chidokan.highlight: 幕末の土佐藩の藩校で坂本龍馬・武市半平太ら多くの志士を育てた教育機関
tosa_han_gakko_chidokan.text: 致道館は土佐藩が文政7年（1824年）に設置した藩校で、藩士の子弟に儒学・武術・兵学などを教えました。坂本龍馬・武市半平太・中岡慎太郎など幕末の土佐志士たちもここで学んだとされています。明治以降は廃止されましたが、跡地には碑が建てられ、土佐の人材育成の歴史を伝えています。
tosa_han_gakko_chidokan.name_en: Former Tosa domain school "Chidokan" ruins (Kochi City)
tosa_han_gakko_chidokan.highlight_en: An educational institution that trained many patriots such as Ryoma Sakamoto and Hanpeita Takeichi at the domain school of the Tosa domain at the end of the Edo period.
tosa_han_gakko_chidokan.text_en: Chidokan was a domain school established by the Tosa domain in 1824 to teach Confucianism, martial arts, military tactics, etc. to the children of domain warriors. It is said that Tosa patriots at the end of the Edo period, such as Ryoma Sakamoto, Hanpeita Takeichi, and Shintaro Nakaoka, studied here. Although it was abolished after the Meiji era, a monument was erected at the site, telling the history of human resource development in Tosa.

shimanto_river_history.name: 四万十川・中村御所跡（四万十市）
shimanto_river_history.kana: しまんとがわなかむらごしょあとしまんとし

transit.name: 土佐くろしお鉄道中村駅

shimanto_river_history.highlight: 応仁の乱を逃れた一条氏が「土佐の小京都」を築いた幡多の地
shimanto_river_history.text: 四万十市（旧中村市）は、応仁の乱（1467年）を逃れた公卿・一条教房が幡多荘に下向し「土佐の小京都」と呼ばれる文化都市を築いた地です。一条氏は京都の公家文化を土佐の地に伝え、約100年間この地を支配しました。中村御所跡をはじめ、鎌倉末期からの歴史と四万十川の清流が交わる歴史ある地域です。
shimanto_river_history.highlight_en: The land of Hata where the Ichijo clan, who fled the Onin War, built "Tosa's Little Kyoto"
shimanto_river_history.text_en: Shimanto City (formerly Nakamura City) is the place where Norifusa Ichijo, a court noble who fled the Onin War (1467), moved to Hatataso and built a cultural city called ``Little Kyoto of Tosa''. The Ichijo clan brought Kyoto's court noble culture to Tosa and ruled the area for about 100 years. It is a historic area where history from the late Kamakura period, including the ruins of the Nakamura Imperial Palace, intersects with the clear waters of the Shimanto River.

aki_chosokabe_birthplace.name: 長宗我部元親生誕地（安芸市）
aki_chosokabe_birthplace.kana: ちょうそかべもとちかせいたんちあきし

transit.name: 土佐くろしお鉄道安芸駅

aki_chosokabe_birthplace.highlight: 土佐の出雲に生まれ四国をほぼ統一した戦国大名・長宗我部元親の出生地
aki_chosokabe_birthplace.text: 長宗我部元親は天文8年（1539年）、土佐安芸郡に生まれたとも伝わる戦国大名です。幼少期は色白で「姫若子」と呼ばれていましたが、初陣の長浜の戦いで勇猛ぶりを発揮し「鬼若子」と称えられました。その後土佐から阿波・伊予・讃岐へと版図を広げ、四国統一寸前まで達しましたが豊臣秀吉の四国征伐で土佐一国に封じられました。
aki_chosokabe_birthplace.highlight_en: Birthplace of Motochika Chosokabe, a feudal lord from the Sengoku period who was born in Izumo, Tosa Prefecture, and almost unified Shikoku.
aki_chosokabe_birthplace.text_en: Chosokabe Motochika is a Sengoku daimyo who is said to have been born in Tosa Aki District in 1539. As a child, she was called ``Himewakako'' due to her fair skin, but she was praised as ``Oniwakako'' for her bravery during her first battle at the Battle of Nagahama. Afterwards, they expanded from Tosa to Awa, Iyo, and Sanuki, and almost reached the point of unifying Shikoku, but Toyotomi Hideyoshi's conquest of Shikoku confined them to Tosa.

itagaki_memorial_kochi.name: 板垣退助記念館・生誕地碑（高知市）
itagaki_memorial_kochi.kana: いたがきたいすけきねんかんせいたんちひこうちし
itagaki_memorial_kochi.highlight: 「板垣死すとも自由は死せず」の言葉と自由民権運動で知られる政治家の故郷
itagaki_memorial_kochi.text: 板垣退助は天保8年（1837年）に土佐藩士の家に生まれた政治家で、明治10年（1877年）に立志社を設立し自由民権運動の先導者となりました。明治15年（1882年）に岐阜で遊説中に暴漢に刺された際に「板垣死すとも自由は死せず」と叫んだとされる逸話は有名です。土佐の自由民権精神を体現した政治家として、高知の象徴的人物です。
itagaki_memorial_kochi.name_en: Taisuke Itagaki Memorial Hall/Birthplace Monument (Kochi City)
itagaki_memorial_kochi.highlight_en: Hometown of a politician known for his words, ``Itagaki may die, but freedom never dies'' and the freedom and civil rights movement.
itagaki_memorial_kochi.text_en: Taisuke Itagaki was a politician born in 1837 to a family of samurai of the Tosa clan.He established Risshisha in 1877 and became a leader of the Freedom and People's Rights Movement. There is a famous anecdote in which he is said to have shouted, ``Itagaki may die, but freedom will never die'' when he was stabbed by a thug while campaigning in Gifu in 1882. He is a symbol of Kochi as a politician who embodies the Tosa spirit of freedom and civil rights.

tosa_reoma_world_history.name: 土佐山田・繁藤の石器時代遺跡（香美市）
tosa_reoma_world_history.kana: とさやまだしげとうのせっきじだいいせきかみし
tosa_reoma_world_history.highlight: 縄文・弥生時代の遺物が出土した高知の古代文化を伝える遺跡地帯
tosa_reoma_world_history.text: 香美市には縄文・弥生時代から古代にかけての遺跡が多数分布しており、土佐の先史文化を今に伝えています。物部川流域には古代豪族・物部氏ゆかりの伝承も残り、高知平野の開拓の歴史を物語る遺跡群となっています。香美市立やなせたかし記念館（アンパンマンミュージアム）もあり、現代文化とも結びついた地域です。
tosa_reoma_world_history.name_en: Stone Age ruins of Tosa Yamada and Shigefuji (Kami City)
tosa_reoma_world_history.highlight_en: A ruins area that conveys the ancient culture of Kochi, where relics from the Jomon and Yayoi periods were excavated.
tosa_reoma_world_history.text_en: Kami City is home to many ruins dating from the Jomon and Yayoi periods to ancient times, which preserve Tosa's prehistoric culture. In the Monobe River basin, there are still traditions related to the Mononobe clan, an ancient powerful clan, and it is a group of ruins that tell the history of the development of the Kochi Plain. There is also the Kami City Takashi Yanase Memorial Museum (Anpanman Museum), and the area is connected to modern culture.

mito_kodokan.name: 水戸城跡・弘道館
mito_kodokan.kana: みとじょうあとこうどうかん
mito_kodokan.highlight: 徳川斉昭が創設した水戸藩の藩校、尊王攘夷運動の精神的拠点
mito_kodokan.text: 弘道館は水戸藩第9代藩主・徳川斉昭が天保12年（1841年）に創設した藩校で、日本最大規模の藩校の一つです。「文武不岐」を理念とし、儒学・医学・天文学から武道まで幅広く教え、水戸学の拠点として尊王攘夷運動に多大な影響を与えました。国の特別史跡に指定され、幕末の志士たちが学んだ建物が今も残っています。
mito_kodokan.highlight_en: A domain school of the Mito domain founded by Tokugawa Nariaki, a spiritual base of the Sonno-joi movement
mito_kodokan.text_en: Kodokan was founded in 1841 by Nariaki Tokugawa, the 9th lord of the Mito domain, and is one of the largest domain schools in Japan. Adhering to the philosophy of ``Bun-bu-Fu-Ki'', he taught a wide range of subjects from Confucianism, medicine, astronomy to martial arts, and had a great influence on the Son-no-Joi movement as a base for Mito studies. It has been designated as a national special historic site, and the building where the patriots studied at the end of the Edo period still remains.

mito_kairakuen.name: 偕楽園（水戸）

transit.name: JR常磐線偕楽園駅（臨時）または水戸駅

mito_kairakuen.highlight: 徳川斉昭が造営した日本三名園の一つ、約3000本の梅で名高い水戸藩の庭園
mito_kairakuen.text: 偕楽園は水戸藩第9代藩主・徳川斉昭が弘化4年（1847年）に造営した庭園で、金沢の兼六園・岡山の後楽園とともに「日本三名園」の一つに数えられます。「衆と偕（とも）に楽しむ」という斉昭の理念のもと、藩士だけでなく領民にも開放された公園として整備されました。約100種3000本の梅が春に咲き誇る梅の名所として全国的に知られています。
mito_kairakuen.highlight_en: One of Japan's top three gardens built by Tokugawa Nariaki, the Mito domain garden is famous for its approximately 3,000 plum trees.
mito_kairakuen.text_en: Kairakuen is a garden built by Nariaki Tokugawa, the 9th lord of the Mito domain, in 1847, and is considered one of the ``Three Great Gardens of Japan'' along with Kenrokuen in Kanazawa and Korakuen in Okayama. Based on Nariaki's philosophy of ``having fun together with the people,'' the park was developed as a park open not only to feudal retainers but also to the people of the domain. It is known nationwide as a famous plum blossom viewing spot where approximately 3,000 plum trees of 100 different varieties bloom in spring.

kashima_jingu.name: 鹿島神宮
kashima_jingu.highlight: 武神・タケミカヅチを祀る東国最古の神宮、鹿島神道流発祥の地
kashima_jingu.text: 鹿島神宮は茨城県鹿嶋市に鎮座する武神・タケミカヅチノミコトを主祭神とする古社で、全国約600社の鹿島神社の総本社です。神武天皇即位の際に武器を奉じたとされる神で、武道・武家から篤く崇敬されてきました。「鹿島神道流」剣術の発祥地でもあり、宮本武蔵も挑んだとされる聖地です。奥参道の杉並木は神秘的な雰囲気を醸し出しています。
kashima_jingu.highlight_en: The oldest shrine in eastern Japan, which enshrines the god of war, Takemikazuchi, and the birthplace of the Kashima Shinto style.
kashima_jingu.text_en: Kashima Shrine is an ancient shrine located in Kashima City, Ibaraki Prefecture whose main deity is Takemikazuchinomikoto, the god of war, and is the headquarters of approximately 600 Kashima Shrines nationwide. This deity is said to have been enshrined with weapons at the time of Emperor Jinmu's accession to the throne, and has been deeply revered by martial arts and samurai families. It is also the birthplace of Kashima Shinto-ryu swordsmanship, and is said to be a sacred place where Miyamoto Musashi even tried his hand at it. The cedar trees along the Oku-sando path create a mystical atmosphere.

tsukuba_shrine.name: 筑波山・筑波神社
tsukuba_shrine.kana: つくばさんつくばじんじゃ

transit.name: つくばエクスプレスつくば駅（・ロープウェイ）

tsukuba_shrine.highlight: 万葉集に詠まれた関東平野の霊峰、イザナギ・イザナミを祀る古社
tsukuba_shrine.text: 筑波山は関東平野に孤立してそびえる標高877メートルの霊峰で、男体山と女体山の二峰からなります。万葉集には「筑波嶺の峰より落つる男女川」と詠まれ、古来より人々に親しまれてきました。山頂の筑波神社はイザナギ・イザナミの二神を祀り、縁結びの神として信仰を集めています。江戸時代には「西の富士、東の筑波」と称えられた名山です。
tsukuba_shrine.highlight_en: An ancient shrine that enshrines Izanagi and Izanami, the sacred peaks of the Kanto Plain that are mentioned in the Manyoshu.
tsukuba_shrine.text_en: Mt. Tsukuba is a sacred mountain with an altitude of 877 meters that stands isolated on the Kanto Plain, and consists of two peaks: Mt. Nantai and Mt. Nyotai. The Manyoshu poem says, ``Men and women's river falls from the peak of Tsukuba-mine,'' and it has been loved by people since ancient times. Tsukuba Shrine at the top of the mountain enshrines two gods, Izanagi and Izanami, and is worshiped as a god of matchmaking. It is a famous mountain that was praised as ``Fuji of the west and Tsukuba of the east'' during the Edo period.

satake_ota_castle.name: 太田城跡・佐竹氏館跡（常陸太田市）
satake_ota_castle.kana: おおたじょうあとさたけうじやかたあとひたちおおたし
satake_ota_castle.highlight: 常陸を200年以上支配した佐竹氏の本拠地、関ヶ原後に秋田へ転封
satake_ota_castle.text: 太田城は常陸国を長きにわたって支配した佐竹氏の本拠地です。佐竹氏は源義光を祖とする名門武家で、南北朝から戦国時代にかけて常陸国の大部分を支配しました。関ヶ原の戦いで中立を守ったため、徳川家康に疑われて秋田に転封を命じられました。現在は西山城跡とともに佐竹氏の栄華を偲ぶ史跡となっています。
satake_ota_castle.name_en: Ota Castle Ruins/Satake Clan Remains (Hitachiota City)
satake_ota_castle.highlight_en: After Sekigahara, the stronghold of the Satake clan who ruled Hitachi for over 200 years, they moved to Akita.
satake_ota_castle.text_en: Ota Castle is the home of the Satake clan, which ruled Hitachi Province for a long time. The Satake clan was a prestigious samurai family whose ancestor was Minamoto no Yoshimitsu, and ruled most of Hitachi Province from the Nanbokucho period to the Sengoku period. Because he remained neutral during the Battle of Sekigahara, he was suspected by Tokugawa Ieyasu and ordered to transfer to Akita. Today, along with the ruins of Nishiyama Castle, it is a historical site commemorating the prosperity of the Satake clan.

nishiyamasou_mitsukuni.name: 西山荘（水戸光圀の隠居所）
nishiyamasou_mitsukuni.kana: せいざんそうみとみつくにのいんきょじょ
nishiyamasou_mitsukuni.highlight: 「水戸黄門」水戸光圀が大日本史編纂に晩年を捧げた隠居所
nishiyamasou_mitsukuni.text: 西山荘は水戸藩第2代藩主・徳川光圀（水戸黄門）が元禄4年（1691年）から没するまでの10年間を過ごした隠居所です。光圀はここで「大日本史」の編纂事業を続け、全397巻に及ぶ歴史書の完成に向けて晩年を捧げました。質素な藁葺きの建物が当時のまま保存され、国の史跡に指定されています。テレビドラマ「水戸黄門」の光圀像の原点となった場所です。
nishiyamasou_mitsukuni.highlight_en: ``Mito Komon'' A retirement place where Mitsukuni Mito devoted his later years to compiling the history of Great Japan.
nishiyamasou_mitsukuni.text_en: Nishizanso is a retirement place where Tokugawa Mitsukuni (Mito Komon), the second lord of the Mito domain, spent 10 years from Genroku 4 (1691) until his death. Mitsukuni continued his work on compiling the Great History of Japan here, devoting his later years to completing the 397-volume history book. The simple thatched building has been preserved as it was back then and is designated as a national historic site. This is the origin of the statue of Mitsukuni in the TV drama ``Mito Komon.''

ibaraki_tsuchiura_castle.name: 土浦城跡（亀城公園）
ibaraki_tsuchiura_castle.kana: つちうらじょうあときじょうこうえん
ibaraki_tsuchiura_castle.highlight: 水濠に囲まれた「水城」、江戸時代に土屋氏・朽木氏が治めた霞ヶ浦近くの城
ibaraki_tsuchiura_castle.text: 土浦城は霞ヶ浦の西岸に築かれた平城で、水濠を巧みに利用した典型的な「水城」です。「亀城」とも呼ばれ、東日本で唯一現存する2棟の城郭建築（東櫓・西櫓）を持ちます。江戸時代には譜代大名が次々と入れ替わって統治し、明治以降は亀城公園として市民に親しまれています。
ibaraki_tsuchiura_castle.highlight_en: Mizuki, a castle surrounded by a water moat, is a castle near Lake Kasumigaura that was ruled by the Tsuchiya and Kuchiki clans during the Edo period.
ibaraki_tsuchiura_castle.text_en: Tsuchiura Castle is a flat castle built on the west bank of Lake Kasumigaura, and is a typical ``water castle'' that skillfully utilizes a water moat. Also known as ``Turtle Castle'', it is the only castle in eastern Japan with two surviving castle buildings (east turret and west turret). During the Edo period, the area was ruled by successive feudal lords, and since the Meiji period, it has been popular among citizens as Kamishiro Park.

hitachi_kokubunji.name: 常陸国分寺跡・国府跡（石岡市）
hitachi_kokubunji.kana: ひたちこくぶんじあとこくふあとせきおかし
hitachi_kokubunji.highlight: 聖武天皇の詔で建立された常陸国の国分寺、古代東国支配の中心地
hitachi_kokubunji.text: 常陸国分寺は天平13年（741年）に聖武天皇が建立を命じた国分寺で、常陸国の仏教文化の中心でした。付近には常陸国府（国衙）跡もあり、奈良時代の東国支配の要として機能した地域です。現在も七重塔の礎石などが残り、常陸国の古代史を伝える重要な史跡となっています。
hitachi_kokubunji.highlight_en: Kokubunji Temple in Hitachi Province, built by Emperor Shomu's edict, was the center of ancient Eastern rule.
hitachi_kokubunji.text_en: Hitachi Kokubunji was ordered to be built by Emperor Shomu in 741, and was the center of Buddhist culture in Hitachi Province. There are also the ruins of the Hitachi Kokufu (Kokuga) nearby, and the area functioned as a key point for the control of the eastern provinces during the Nara period. The foundation stones of the seven-storied pagoda still remain today, making it an important historical site that tells of the ancient history of Hitachi Province.

yuki_castle.name: 結城城跡（結城市）
yuki_castle.kana: ゆうきじょうあとゆうきし
yuki_castle.highlight: 結城氏が200年以上守った城、応永の乱・結城合戦など激動の舞台
yuki_castle.text: 結城城は結城氏が14世紀に築いた城で、南北朝・室町時代を通じて関東の要衝として機能しました。永享12年（1440年）の結城合戦では、関東公方・足利持氏の遺児を匿った結城氏持が幕府軍に攻められ落城しました。この合戦は室町時代の東国支配の転換点となった歴史的事件で、城跡には石碑が残っています。
yuki_castle.highlight_en: Castle protected by the Yuki clan for over 200 years, stage of turbulent events such as the Oei War and the Battle of Yuki
yuki_castle.text_en: Yuki Castle was built by the Yuki clan in the 14th century, and served as a strategic point in the Kanto region throughout the Nanbokucho and Muromachi periods. During the Battle of Yuki in 1440, Yuki Ujimochi, who hid the orphaned son of Kanto Kubo Mochiuji Ashikaga, was attacked by the shogunate army and fell to the castle. This battle was a historical event that marked a turning point in the control of eastern Japan during the Muromachi period, and a stone monument remains at the castle ruins.

kasama_castle.name: 笠間城跡・笠間稲荷神社
kasama_castle.kana: かさまじょうあとかさまいなりじんじゃ
kasama_castle.highlight: 日本三大稲荷の一つ・笠間稲荷と、佐竹氏・浅野氏ゆかりの山城跡
kasama_castle.text: 笠間城は常陸国の山城で、鎌倉時代から江戸時代まで笠間氏・宍戸氏・浅野氏などが相次いで城主となった要衝です。城下の笠間稲荷神社は日本三大稲荷の一つに数えられ、年間300万人以上の参拝者が訪れます。江戸時代には浅野内匠頭（赤穂藩主）の祖が笠間藩主を務めたことでも知られています。
kasama_castle.highlight_en: Kasama Inari, one of the three major Inari shrines in Japan, and the ruins of a mountain castle connected to the Satake and Asano clans
kasama_castle.text_en: Kasama Castle is a mountain castle in Hitachi Province, and was a strategic location where the Kasama clan, Shishido clan, and Asano clan were successive lords from the Kamakura period to the Edo period. Kasama Inari Shrine in the castle town is counted as one of the three major Inari shrines in Japan, and more than 3 million people visit each year. It is also known that the ancestor of Asano Takukami (lord of Ako domain) served as lord of Kasama domain during the Edo period.

nikko_toshogu.name: 日光東照宮
nikko_toshogu.kana: にっこうとうしょうぐう

transit.name: JR日光線・東武日光線日光駅

nikko_toshogu.highlight: 徳川家康を神として祀った絢爛豪華な江戸初期の建築群、世界遺産
nikko_toshogu.text: 日光東照宮は元和3年（1617年）に徳川家康の霊廟として創建され、3代将軍家光が寛永13年（1636年）に大規模な改築を行いました。「見ざる・聞かざる・言わざる」の三猿、眠り猫など精緻な彫刻が施された社殿群は世界遺産に登録されています。「日光を見ずして結構と言うなかれ」と称えられる絢爛豪華な建築は、江戸幕府の権威と繁栄を象徴しています。
nikko_toshogu.highlight_en: A world heritage site, a group of gorgeous buildings from the early Edo period that enshrined Tokugawa Ieyasu as a god.
nikko_toshogu.text_en: Nikko Toshogu Shrine was built in 1617 as a mausoleum for Tokugawa Ieyasu, and the third shogun, Iemitsu, made extensive renovations in 1636. The shrine buildings, which have elaborate carvings such as the Three Monkeys and the Sleeping Cat, are registered as a World Heritage Site. The gorgeous architecture, which is said to be ``don't say no without seeing Nikko,'' symbolizes the authority and prosperity of the Edo shogunate.

ashikaga_school.name: 足利学校
ashikaga_school.highlight: フランシスコ・ザビエルが「日本最大の学校」と称えた日本最古の学校
ashikaga_school.text: 足利学校は平安時代の創建とも室町時代の再興ともいわれる日本最古の学校で、15〜16世紀に最盛期を迎えました。禅僧・関東管領上杉憲実が再興し、易学・兵法・医学などを教えた当時の最高学府です。フランシスコ・ザビエルは1549年に「日本最大の坂東の大学」と称え、その名声は世界に知られていました。現在は当時の建物が復元・整備されています。
ashikaga_school.highlight_en: Japan's oldest school, hailed by Francisco Xavier as "Japan's greatest school"
ashikaga_school.text_en: Ashikaga School is Japan's oldest school, said to have been founded in the Heian period and revived in the Muromachi period, and reached its peak in the 15th and 16th centuries. It was the highest academic school at the time when the Zen monk and Kanto Kanrei Norizane Uesugi rebuilt it and taught subjects such as science, military tactics, and medicine. In 1549, Francisco Xavier called it ``Japan's largest Bando university,'' and its reputation was known around the world. The original building has now been restored and maintained.

nasu_yoichi_shrine.name: 那須神社・那須与一ゆかりの地（那須町）
nasu_yoichi_shrine.kana: なすじんじゃなすのよいちゆかりのちなすまち
nasu_yoichi_shrine.highlight: 屋島の戦いで扇の的を射た弓の名手・那須与一の出身地
nasu_yoichi_shrine.text: 那須町は源平合戦の屋島の戦いで「扇の的」を射た名射手・那須与一の出身地です。那須与一は寿永4年（1185年）2月の屋島の戦いで、波に揺れる平家の船上の扇を一矢で射落とし、源平両軍から喝采を浴びました。那須神社には与一ゆかりの品が伝わり、地元では那須与一を称える伝説が今も語り継がれています。
nasu_yoichi_shrine.name_en: Nasu Shrine, place related to Yoichi Nasu (Nasu Town)
nasu_yoichi_shrine.highlight_en: Birthplace of Yoichi Nasu, the master archer who hit the target with a fan during the Battle of Yashima.
nasu_yoichi_shrine.text_en: Nasu Town is the birthplace of Yoichi Nasu, a famous archer who shot a fan target at the Battle of Yashima during the Genpei War. At the Battle of Yashima in February 1185, Nasu Yoichi shot down a fan on a Heike ship that was swaying in the waves with a single arrow, and received applause from both Genpei and Heike armies. Items related to Yoichi have been handed down at Nasu Shrine, and local legends praising him are still passed down to this day.

oyama_meeting_site.name: 小山評定跡（小山市）
oyama_meeting_site.kana: おやまひょうじょうあとおやまし
oyama_meeting_site.highlight: 関ヶ原の戦い直前、徳川家康が諸将の忠誠を確認した歴史的な軍議の地
oyama_meeting_site.text: 小山評定は慶長5年（1600年）7月25日、徳川家康が小山（現・小山市）で行った軍議です。上杉景勝討伐に向かっていた家康が石田三成挙兵の報を受け、この地で諸将に去就を問いました。福島正則ら諸大名が家康への忠誠を誓い、これが関ヶ原の戦いでの東軍結束の出発点となりました。現在は祇園城跡公園内に評定跡の碑が建っています。
oyama_meeting_site.highlight_en: The historic military council site where Tokugawa Ieyasu confirmed the loyalty of his generals just before the Battle of Sekigahara
oyama_meeting_site.text_en: The Oyama Hōjō was a military council held by Tokugawa Ieyasu in Oyama (present-day Oyama City) on July 25, 1600. Ieyasu, who was on his way to subjugate Kagekatsu Uesugi, received news of Mitsunari Ishida's raising of an army, and here he asked the various generals about their resignation. Masanori Fukushima and other feudal lords swore loyalty to Ieyasu, and this became the starting point for the unity of the Eastern Army at the Battle of Sekigahara. Currently, a monument commemorating the ruins stands in Gion Castle Ruins Park.

utsunomiya_castle.name: 宇都宮城跡（清明台）
utsunomiya_castle.kana: うつのみやじょうあとせいめいだい
utsunomiya_castle.highlight: 江戸時代に本多氏・奥平氏が治めた下野の要衝、戊辰戦争の激戦地
utsunomiya_castle.text: 宇都宮城は鎌倉時代から宇都宮氏が支配した要衝で、江戸時代には本多正純・奥平氏などが城主となりました。戊辰戦争では旧幕府軍と新政府軍が激しく争い「宇都宮戦争」が起き、城下の大半が焼失しました。現在は清明台と富士見やぐらが復元され、城址公園として整備されています。
utsunomiya_castle.highlight_en: A strategic point in Shimotsuke, ruled by the Honda and Okudaira clans during the Edo period, and the site of a fierce battle during the Boshin War.
utsunomiya_castle.text_en: Utsunomiya Castle has been a strategic point ruled by the Utsunomiya clan since the Kamakura period, and Masazumi Honda and the Okudaira clan became the castle lords in the Edo period. During the Boshin War, the former shogunate army and the new government army fought fiercely, leading to the Utsunomiya War, in which most of the castle town was burnt down. Currently, Seimeidai and Fujimi Yagura have been restored and maintained as a castle ruins park.

karasawayama_castle.name: 唐沢山城跡（佐野市）
karasawayama_castle.kana: からさわやまじょうあとさのし

transit.name: 東武佐野線田沼駅（またはタクシー）

karasawayama_castle.highlight: 関東七名城の一つ、上杉謙信が11度攻めて落とせなかった難攻不落の山城
karasawayama_castle.text: 唐沢山城は佐野氏が築いた関東屈指の山城で、上杉謙信が11度にわたり攻撃したものの一度も落城しなかった「難攻不落の城」として知られています。天然の地形を巧みに利用した縄張りは、難攻不落の理由を今も物語っています。現在は唐沢山神社の境内となっており、春の桜の名所としても知られています。
karasawayama_castle.highlight_en: An impregnable mountain castle that Uesugi Kenshin attacked 11 times and was unable to capture, one of the seven famous castles in the Kanto region.
karasawayama_castle.text_en: Karasawayama Castle is one of the best mountain castles in the Kanto region built by the Sano clan, and is known as an ``impregnable castle'' that Uesugi Kenshin attacked 11 times but never fell. The territory, which skillfully exploits the natural terrain, still shows why it is so impregnable. It is currently part of the precincts of Karasawayama Shrine, and is also known as a famous spot for cherry blossom viewing in spring.

nikko_futarasan.name: 日光二荒山神社
nikko_futarasan.kana: にっこうふたらさんじんじゃ
nikko_futarasan.highlight: 日光山信仰の源・二荒山（男体山）の神を祀る世界遺産の古社
nikko_futarasan.text: 日光二荒山神社は、勝道上人が延暦3年（784年）に男体山に登頂し創建したと伝わる古社です。日光の氏神として「二荒（ふたら）」の山に宿る神々を祀り、日光東照宮・輪王寺とともに「二社一寺」として世界遺産に登録されています。本社・中宮祠・奥宮の三社からなり、男体山の山頂に奥宮が鎮座しています。
nikko_futarasan.highlight_en: An old shrine that is a World Heritage Site and enshrines the god of Mt. Futara (Mt. Nantai), the source of Mt. Nikko worship.
nikko_futarasan.text_en: Nikko Futarasan Shrine is an old shrine that is said to have been founded by Shonin Shonin after he climbed Mt. Nantai in the 3rd year of Enryaku (784). As Nikko's guardian deity, it enshrines the gods that dwell in the mountains of Futara, and has been registered as a World Heritage site as "Two Shrines and One Temple" along with Nikko Toshogu Shrine and Rinnoji Temple. It consists of three shrines: the main shrine, the Chugu Shrine, and the Okumiya, and the Okumiya is located at the top of Mt. Nantai.

mashiko_pottery.name: 益子・濱田庄司記念益子参考館
mashiko_pottery.kana: ましこはまだしょうじきねんましこさんこうかん
mashiko_pottery.highlight: 民藝運動の巨匠・濱田庄司が育てた益子焼の里、生活美術の聖地
mashiko_pottery.text: 益子は栃木県芳賀郡の焼き物の里で、民藝運動の指導者・濱田庄司が昭和5年（1930年）に移住して以来、日本を代表する陶芸の産地として発展しました。濱田は柳宗悦・バーナード・リーチとともに「用の美」を追求する民藝運動を推進し、益子焼に独自の美を吹き込みました。益子参考館では濱田の作品と世界各地の民芸品を展示しています。
mashiko_pottery.name_en: Mashiko/Shoji Hamada Memorial Mashiko Reference Museum
mashiko_pottery.highlight_en: A Mashiko ware village cultivated by Shoji Hamada, a master of the Mingei movement, a sacred place for lifestyle art.
mashiko_pottery.text_en: Mashiko is a pottery village in Haga District, Tochigi Prefecture, and since Shoji Hamada, the leader of the Mingei movement, moved here in 1930, it has developed into one of Japan's leading pottery production areas. Together with Soetsu Yanagi and Bernard Leach, Hamada promoted the Mingei movement in pursuit of ``useful beauty'' and imbued Mashiko ware with a unique beauty. The Mashiko Reference Museum exhibits Hamada's works and folk crafts from around the world.

nikko_taiyuin.name: 大猷院（徳川家光の霊廟）
nikko_taiyuin.kana: たいゆういんとくがわいえみつのれいびょう
nikko_taiyuin.highlight: 日光東照宮を造営した3代将軍家光の霊廟、祖父・家康を超えない設計
nikko_taiyuin.text: 大猷院は3代将軍・徳川家光の霊廟で、慶安4年（1651年）に建てられました。家光は「祖父・家康公を超えてはならない」との遺言を残したとされ、東照宮より規模を抑えつつも絢爛豪華な建築となっています。日光東照宮・二荒山神社とともに世界遺産に登録され、夜叉門・皇嘉門など独特の意匠を持つ門が数多く残っています。
nikko_taiyuin.highlight_en: The mausoleum of the third shogun Iemitsu, who built Nikko Toshogu Shrine, has a design that surpasses that of his grandfather Ieyasu.
nikko_taiyuin.text_en: Taiyu-in is the mausoleum of the third shogun, Tokugawa Iemitsu, and was built in 1651. It is said that Iemitsu left behind a will stating that he should not surpass his grandfather, Prince Ieyasu, and although it is smaller in scale than Toshogu Shrine, it is still a gorgeous building. It has been registered as a World Heritage Site along with Nikko Toshogu Shrine and Futarasan Shrine, and many gates with unique designs remain, such as Yashamon and Kokamon.

shimotsuke_kokubunji.name: 下野国分寺跡・下野薬師寺跡（下野市）
shimotsuke_kokubunji.kana: しもつけこくぶんじあとしもつけやくしじあとしもつけし
shimotsuke_kokubunji.highlight: 奈良時代、東国の僧侶が戒律を受けた下野薬師寺と国分寺の古代遺跡群
shimotsuke_kokubunji.text: 下野国分寺は聖武天皇の詔で建立された国分寺で、隣接する下野薬師寺は奈良時代に東国唯一の戒壇が置かれた寺院です。鑑真が唐招提寺建立前に逗留したとも伝わり、多くの僧侶がここで正式な戒律を授かりました。現在は七重塔跡の礎石などが残り、奈良時代の東国仏教文化の重要性を伝えています。
shimotsuke_kokubunji.name_en: Shimotsuke Kokubunji Temple Ruins / Shimotsuke Yakushiji Temple Ruins (Shimotsu City)
shimotsuke_kokubunji.highlight_en: The ancient ruins of Shimono Yakushiji and Kokubunji, where monks from eastern Japan received precepts during the Nara period.
shimotsuke_kokubunji.text_en: Shimotsuke Kokubunji is a Kokubunji temple built by Emperor Shomu's edict, and the adjacent Shimotsuke Yakushiji is the only temple in the eastern part of Japan that had a Buddhist altar during the Nara period. It is said that Ganjin stayed here before Toshodaiji was built, and many monks received formal precepts here. Today, the foundation stones of the seven-storied pagoda remain, conveying the importance of Togoku Buddhist culture during the Nara period.

tomioka_seishi.name: 富岡製糸場（世界遺産）
tomioka_seishi.kana: とみおかせいしじょうせかいいさん

transit.name: 上信電鉄上信線上州富岡駅

tomioka_seishi.highlight: 明治5年創業、日本の近代化と製糸業発展の象徴・世界遺産の工場遺跡
tomioka_seishi.text: 富岡製糸場は明治5年（1872年）に明治政府が設立した官営模範工場で、フランスの技術を導入した日本初の本格的な器械製糸工場です。日本の近代産業の礎となり、良質な生糸を世界に輸出して外貨獲得に貢献しました。2014年に「富岡製糸場と絹産業遺産群」として世界文化遺産に登録され、明治の殖産興業政策を象徴する施設として保存されています。
tomioka_seishi.highlight_en: Established in 1895, the ruins of a factory that is a symbol of Japan's modernization and the development of the silk industry and a World Heritage Site
tomioka_seishi.text_en: Tomioka Silk Mill is a government-run model factory established by the Meiji government in 1872, and is Japan's first full-scale mechanical silk mill that introduced French technology. It became the cornerstone of Japan's modern industry and contributed to earning foreign currency by exporting high-quality raw silk to the world. In 2014, it was registered as a World Cultural Heritage Site as the "Tomioka Silk Mill and Silk Industry Heritage Group," and has been preserved as a symbol of the Meiji era's industrial promotion policy.

numata_castle_sanada.name: 沼田城跡（真田氏の沼田領）
numata_castle_sanada.kana: ぬまたじょうあとさなだうじのぬまたりょう
numata_castle_sanada.highlight: 真田昌幸・信幸が領した上野の要衝、徳川・北条・上杉が争った城
numata_castle_sanada.text: 沼田城は真田昌幸が天正7年（1579年）に占領して以来、真田氏の重要拠点となった城です。徳川・北条・上杉の三者が激しく争う中、昌幸は巧みな外交で沼田城を守り抜きました。関ヶ原の戦い後は昌幸の長男・信幸（信之）が沼田藩を立藩。現在は沼田城跡公園として整備され、利根川と片品川に挟まれた河岸段丘の地形が天然の要害であったことを示しています。
numata_castle_sanada.name_en: Numata Castle ruins (Numata territory of the Sanada clan)
numata_castle_sanada.highlight_en: A strategic point in Ueno that was ruled by Masayuki Sanada and Nobuyuki, and a castle fought over by Tokugawa, Hojo, and Uesugi.
numata_castle_sanada.text_en: Numata Castle has been an important base for the Sanada clan since Masayuki Sanada occupied it in 1579. While the Tokugawa, Hojo, and Uesugi clans fought fiercely, Masayuki successfully defended Numata Castle through skillful diplomacy. After the Battle of Sekigahara, Masayuki's eldest son, Nobuyuki (Nobuyuki) established the Numata domain. Currently, it is maintained as Numata Castle Ruins Park, and the topography of the river terrace between the Tone River and Katashin River indicates that it was a natural fortress.

kanayama_castle.name: 金山城跡（太田市）
kanayama_castle.kana: かなやまじょうあとおおたし

transit.name: 東武伊勢崎線太田駅（・徒歩）

kanayama_castle.highlight: 関東七名城の一つ、新田氏の流れを汲む岩松氏・由良氏が守った難攻不落の山城
kanayama_castle.text: 金山城は南北朝時代に新田氏の一族・岩松家純が築いた山城で、標高239メートルの金山頂上に位置する難攻不落の城です。関東七名城の一つに数えられ、石敷き通路・石積みの堀・貯水池など当時としては珍しい石造建築が多く残っています。上杉謙信・武田信玄も攻略できなかった堅城で、国の史跡に指定されています。
kanayama_castle.highlight_en: One of the seven famous castles in Kanto, an impregnable mountain castle protected by the Iwamatsu and Yura clans, descendants of the Nitta clan.
kanayama_castle.text_en: Kanayama Castle is a mountain castle built by Iazumi Iwamatsu, a member of the Nitta clan, during the Nanbokucho period, and is an impregnable castle located on the top of Kanayama at an altitude of 239 meters. It is counted as one of the seven famous castles in the Kanto region, and many stone structures that were rare at the time remain, such as stone-paved walkways, stone moats, and reservoirs. It is a fortress that even Uesugi Kenshin and Takeda Shingen were unable to capture, and it is designated as a national historic site.

minowajyo_nagano.name: 箕輪城跡（高崎市）
minowajyo_nagano.kana: みのわじょうあとたかさきし
minowajyo_nagano.highlight: 武田信玄が落とし、のちに徳川四天王・井伊直政が入城した西上野の要衝
minowajyo_nagano.text: 箕輪城は永正9年（1512年）に長野業尚が築いた平山城で、西上野の中心として機能しました。武田信玄が永禄9年（1566年）に攻略し、豊臣秀吉による天下統一後は徳川四天王の一人・井伊直政が入城しました。直政はのちに彦根藩を立藩しますが、箕輪城時代に育んだ「井伊の赤備え」が有名な部隊を形成しました。
minowajyo_nagano.highlight_en: A strategic point in Nishi-Ueno that was captured by Takeda Shingen and later entered by Ii Naomasa, one of the Four Heavenly Kings of Tokugawa.
minowajyo_nagano.text_en: Minowa Castle is a Hirayama castle built by Nagano Narihisa in 1512 and served as the center of Nishi-Ueno. Takeda Shingen captured the castle in 1566, and after Toyotomi Hideyoshi unified the country, one of the Four Tokugawa Kings, Ii Naomasa, entered the castle. Naomasa later founded the Hikone domain, and the ``Ii Red Arms'' that he had cultivated during his time at Minowa Castle formed a famous military unit.

serada_toshogu.name: 世良田東照宮（太田市）
serada_toshogu.kana: せらだとうしょうぐうおおたし

transit.name: 東武伊勢崎線世良田駅

serada_toshogu.highlight: 徳川氏の発祥の地・新田荘に建つ東照宮、日光から移築された社殿
serada_toshogu.text: 世良田東照宮は寛永20年（1643年）、3代将軍・徳川家光が徳川氏の祖先・得川（世良田）義季の地に建立した東照宮です。日光東照宮の旧拝殿を移築したもので、国の重要文化財に指定されています。新田荘は徳川家康の先祖とされる新田氏・得川氏の発祥地で、徳川氏のルーツを伝える聖地です。
serada_toshogu.highlight_en: Toshogu shrine built in Nittasho, the birthplace of the Tokugawa clan, the main shrine relocated from Nikko
serada_toshogu.text_en: Serada Toshogu Shrine was built in 1643 by the third shogun, Tokugawa Iemitsu, on the land of Tokugawa (Serada) Yoshisue, the ancestor of the Tokugawa clan. The former shrine of Nikko Toshogu Shrine was relocated and is designated as a national important cultural property. Nitta-so is the birthplace of the Nitta and Tokugawa clans, who are said to be the ancestors of Tokugawa Ieyasu, and is a sacred place that conveys the roots of the Tokugawa clan.

kusatsu_onsen_history.name: 草津温泉・片岡鶴太郎美術館（草津町）
kusatsu_onsen_history.kana: くさつおんせんかたおかつるたろうびじゅつかんくさつまち

transit.name: JR吾妻線長野原草津口駅

kusatsu_onsen_history.highlight: 日本三名泉の一つ・草津温泉、湯畑と時間湯の文化が残る江戸時代の湯治場
kusatsu_onsen_history.text: 草津温泉は「草津よいとこ一度はおいで」の民謡で知られる日本を代表する温泉地で、毎分3万2千リットルを超える自然湧出量は日本一とも言われます。江戸時代には「天下の名湯」として多くの湯治客が訪れ、徳川将軍家も御汲上の湯として用いました。温泉街の中心に位置する「湯畑」は温泉が吹き出す壮大な光景を作り出しています。
kusatsu_onsen_history.highlight_en: Kusatsu Onsen, one of Japan's top three hot springs, is an Edo-era hot springs spa where the culture of hot springs and hot springs still remains.
kusatsu_onsen_history.text_en: Kusatsu Onsen is one of Japan's most representative hot springs, known for the folk song "Kusatsu is a good place to visit once," and is said to have the highest amount of natural hot spring water in Japan, exceeding 32,000 liters per minute. During the Edo period, many people came to enjoy the hot springs as it was known as ``the world's famous hot springs'', and the Tokugawa shogunate also used it as a water bath. Yubatake, located in the center of the hot spring town, creates a spectacular sight of hot springs gushing out.

agatsuma_nakasendo.name: 碓氷峠・坂本宿跡（安中市）
agatsuma_nakasendo.kana: うすいとうげさかもとじゅくあとあんなかし
agatsuma_nakasendo.highlight: 中山道の難所・碓氷峠の東麓に発展した坂本宿、峠を越える旅人で賑わった宿場
agatsuma_nakasendo.text: 碓氷峠は上野国と信濃国の境界をなす難所で、中山道の最大の難所として多くの旅人を苦しめました。東麓の坂本宿は峠越えの準備をする旅人で賑わい、江戸時代の宿場の雰囲気が今も残っています。明治時代にはアプト式鉄道が敷かれ、近代交通の歴史も刻んでいます。
agatsuma_nakasendo.highlight_en: Sakamoto-juku developed at the eastern foot of Usui Pass, a difficult part of Nakasendo, and was a post station crowded with travelers crossing the pass.
agatsuma_nakasendo.text_en: Usui Pass is a difficult point that forms the border between Ueno and Shinano provinces, and was the most difficult point on the Nakasendo route, causing many travelers to suffer. Sakamoto-juku at the eastern foot of the mountain is crowded with travelers preparing to cross the mountain pass, and still retains the atmosphere of an Edo-period post station. In the Meiji era, the Abt-style railway was laid, marking the history of modern transportation.

ogo_castle_uesugi.name: 厩橋城跡・前橋城跡（前橋市）
ogo_castle_uesugi.kana: まやばしじょうあとまえばしじょうあとまえばしし
ogo_castle_uesugi.highlight: 上杉謙信も支配した上野国の要衝、江戸時代には酒井氏・松平氏の城下町
ogo_castle_uesugi.text: 厩橋城（後の前橋城）は利根川に臨む平城で、上杉謙信が関東進出の際に重視した上野国の要衝です。謙信はここを関東支配の拠点とし、北条氏康と激しく争いました。江戸時代には酒井忠世・松平家が城主となり、前橋藩の中心として発展しました。現在は前橋公園として整備されています。
ogo_castle_uesugi.name_en: Umayabashi Castle Ruins/Maebashi Castle Ruins (Maebashi City)
ogo_castle_uesugi.highlight_en: A strategic point in Ueno Province, which was also ruled by Kenshin Uesugi, and a castle town of the Sakai and Matsudaira clans during the Edo period.
ogo_castle_uesugi.text_en: Umayabashi Castle (later Maebashi Castle) is a flat castle overlooking the Tone River, and is a strategic point in Ueno Province that Uesugi Kenshin focused on when expanding into the Kanto region. Kenshin used this as his base for domination of the Kanto region, and fought fiercely with Ujiyasu Hojo. During the Edo period, Tadayo Sakai and the Matsudaira family became the lords of the castle, and it developed as the center of the Maebashi domain. Currently, it is maintained as Maebashi Park.

kannonyama_kofun.name: 観音山古墳（高崎市）
kannonyama_kofun.kana: かんのんやまこふんたかさきし
kannonyama_kofun.highlight: 6世紀の東日本最大規模の前方後円墳、国宝の金銅製馬具が出土
kannonyama_kofun.text: 観音山古墳は6世紀後半（古墳時代後期）に造られた前方後円墳で、墳丘長97メートルを誇る東日本最大規模の古墳の一つです。国宝に指定された金銅製馬具・鏡・装身具など豪華な副葬品が出土しており、当時の上野国（群馬）に強大な豪族が存在したことを示しています。
kannonyama_kofun.highlight_en: East Japan's largest keyhole-shaped tumulus dating from the 6th century, with national treasure gilt-bronze horse harness unearthed
kannonyama_kofun.text_en: Kannonyama Tumulus is a keyhole-shaped tumulus built in the late 6th century (late Kofun period), and is one of the largest tumuli in eastern Japan, measuring 97 meters long. Luxury grave goods such as gilt bronze horse harnesses, mirrors, and jewelry designated as national treasures have been unearthed, indicating that a powerful ruling family existed in Ueno Province (Gunma) at the time.

akagi_shrine_gunma.name: 赤城神社（前橋市）
akagi_shrine_gunma.kana: あかぎじんじゃまえばしし
akagi_shrine_gunma.highlight: 上野国一之宮・赤城山頂に鎮座する古社、上杉謙信も戦勝祈願した武神の社
akagi_shrine_gunma.text: 赤城神社は上野国一之宮として古くから信仰された古社で、赤城山山頂の大沼湖畔に鎮座しています。主祭神は赤城大明神（大己貴命・豊城入彦命）で、関東の武将から篤く信仰されました。上杉謙信も出陣前に戦勝を祈願したと伝わり、関東管領として関東を支配した謙信の信仰の地です。
akagi_shrine_gunma.highlight_en: An old shrine located at the top of Mt. Akagi in Ichinomiya, Ueno Province, a shrine of the god of war where Uesugi Kenshin also prayed for victory in battle.
akagi_shrine_gunma.text_en: Akagi Shrine is an old shrine that has been worshiped since ancient times as the Ichinomiya of Ueno Province, and is located on the shores of Lake Onuma at the summit of Mt. Akagi. The main deity enshrined is Akagi Daimyojin (Otomi no Mikoto and Toyogi Irihiko no Mikoto), which was deeply worshiped by military commanders in the Kanto region. It is said that Kenshin Uesugi also prayed for victory before going into battle, and it is a place of worship for Kenshin, who ruled the Kanto region as Kanto Kanrei.

kawagoe_castle.name: 川越城本丸御殿（川越市）
kawagoe_castle.kana: かわごえじょうほんまるごてんかわごえし
kawagoe_castle.highlight: 「小江戸」川越の中心城郭、全国に数少ない現存する本丸御殿
kawagoe_castle.text: 川越城は長禄元年（1457年）に太田道真・道灌父子が築いた城で、江戸時代には川越藩の中心として栄えました。現存する本丸御殿は嘉永2年（1849年）に建てられたもので、全国に16棟しかない現存本丸御殿の一つです。川越は「小江戸」と呼ばれ、江戸の経済・文化の影響を強く受けた城下町として今も多くの観光客が訪れます。
kawagoe_castle.highlight_en: The central castle of Kawagoe, known as “Little Edo,” is one of the few surviving Honmaru Palaces in Japan.
kawagoe_castle.text_en: Kawagoe Castle was built by father and son Ota Michizane and Dokan in the first year of Choroku (1457), and flourished as the center of the Kawagoe clan during the Edo period. The existing Honmaru Palace was built in 1849 and is one of only 16 Honmaru Palaces in existence nationwide. Kawagoe is known as ``Little Edo'' and is still visited by many tourists as a castle town that was strongly influenced by the economy and culture of Edo.

oshi_castle_mizuseme.name: 忍城跡（行田市）
oshi_castle_mizuseme.kana: おしじょうあとぎょうだし
oshi_castle_mizuseme.highlight: 石田三成の水攻めにも落ちなかった「浮き城」、映画・のぼうの城の舞台
oshi_castle_mizuseme.text: 忍城は成田氏の居城で、天正18年（1590年）の豊臣秀吉の小田原攻めの際に石田三成が水攻めを試みたことで有名です。広大な沼地の中に建つ「浮き城」は3万石の石堤を築いた水攻めにも屈せず、小田原城の開城まで持ちこたえました。この逸話は小説・映画「のぼうの城」の題材となり、全国的に知られています。
oshi_castle_mizuseme.highlight_en: Ishida Mitsunari's ``Floating Castle'' that survived a water attack, the setting for the movie Nobou no Castle
oshi_castle_mizuseme.text_en: Oshi Castle was the residence of the Narita clan, and is famous for Ishida Mitsunari's attempt to attack Odawara during Toyotomi Hideyoshi's attack on Odawara in 1590. The ``floating castle'' built in a vast swamp did not succumb to the water attack caused by the construction of a stone embankment of 30,000 koku, and withstood the opening of Odawara Castle. This anecdote became the subject of the novel and movie ``Nobo no Shiro'' and is known nationwide.

hachigata_castle.name: 鉢形城跡（寄居町）
hachigata_castle.kana: はちがたじょうあとよりいまち
hachigata_castle.highlight: 後北条氏四男・氏邦が守った荒川沿いの堅城、豊臣秀吉の小田原攻めで落城
hachigata_castle.text: 鉢形城は荒川と深沢川が合流する断崖上に築かれた天然の要害で、後北条氏の重臣・北条氏邦の居城でした。天正18年（1590年）の豊臣秀吉の小田原攻めでは前田利家・上杉景勝らの大軍に包囲され、1ヶ月以上籠城した後に開城しました。現在は国の史跡として発掘・整備が進んでいます。
hachigata_castle.highlight_en: A strong fort along the Arakawa River that was defended by Ujikuni, the fourth son of the Gohojo clan, and fell during Toyotomi Hideyoshi's attack on Odawara.
hachigata_castle.text_en: Hachigata Castle is a natural fortress built on a cliff where the Arakawa and Fukasawa rivers meet, and was the residence of Ujikuni Hojo, a senior vassal of the Gohojo clan. During Toyotomi Hideyoshi's attack on Odawara in 1590, the castle was surrounded by a large army led by Toshiie Maeda and Kagekatsu Uesugi, and was confined for over a month before surrendering. It is currently being excavated and maintained as a national historic site.

sugaya_yakata_hatakeyama.name: 菅谷館跡（嵐山町）
sugaya_yakata_hatakeyama.kana: すがやたちあとらんざんまち

transit.name: 東武東上線武蔵嵐山駅

sugaya_yakata_hatakeyama.highlight: 源頼朝に仕えた鎌倉武士の鑑・畠山重忠の館跡、武蔵武士の里
sugaya_yakata_hatakeyama.text: 菅谷館は鎌倉時代の武将・畠山重忠の居館跡です。重忠は源頼朝に仕えた武士の鑑とも称えられ、一ノ谷の戦いでは馬を担いで崖を下ったという勇猛なエピソードで知られます。元久2年（1205年）に北条氏の謀略で謀反の疑いをかけられ、武蔵二俣川で討ち取られました。国の史跡に指定され、中世武蔵の武士文化を今に伝えています。
sugaya_yakata_hatakeyama.highlight_en: Musashi samurai village, ruins of Shigetada Hatakeyama's residence, a model of the Kamakura samurai who served Minamoto no Yoritomo
sugaya_yakata_hatakeyama.text_en: Sugayakan is the former residence of Shigetada Hatakeyama, a military commander from the Kamakura period. Shigetada is hailed as a model samurai who served Minamoto no Yoritomo, and is known for his brave story of descending a cliff carrying a horse during the Battle of Ichinotani. In 1205, he was suspected of rebellion due to a plot by the Hojo clan and was killed at Musashi Futamata River. It has been designated as a national historic site and preserves the samurai culture of medieval Musashi.

mitsumine_shrine.name: 三峯神社（秩父市）
mitsumine_shrine.kana: みつみねじんじゃちちぶし

transit.name: 西武秩父線西武秩父駅

mitsumine_shrine.highlight: 日本武尊が創建したと伝わる関東屈指のパワースポット、奥秩父の霊山
mitsumine_shrine.text: 三峯神社は奥秩父の山中に鎮座する古社で、日本武尊（ヤマトタケルノミコト）が東征の際に創建したと伝えられています。狼（お犬さま）を神使とする珍しい神社で、「気力充実」のご利益があるとして全国から参拝者が集まります。標高1100メートルに位置し、霧に包まれた境内は幽玄な雰囲気を醸し出しています。
mitsumine_shrine.highlight_en: A sacred mountain in Oku-Chichibu, one of the best power spots in the Kanto region, said to have been founded by Takeru Nihon.
mitsumine_shrine.text_en: Mitsumine Shrine is an old shrine located in the mountains of Oku-Chichibu, and is said to have been founded by Yamato Takeru no Mikoto during his eastern expedition. This is a rare shrine with a wolf (dog) as its divine messenger, and worshipers from all over the country gather here to pray for its blessings of "enhancing energy." Located at an altitude of 1,100 meters, the shrine grounds are shrouded in mist, creating a mysterious atmosphere.

chichibu_shrine.name: 秩父神社（秩父市）
chichibu_shrine.kana: ちちぶじんじゃちちぶし
chichibu_shrine.highlight: 武蔵国四宮・知知夫国の一宮、徳川家光が造営した彫刻豊かな本殿
chichibu_shrine.text: 秩父神社は知知夫国（武蔵国北西部）の一宮として2000年以上の歴史を誇る古社です。現在の本殿は天正20年（1592年）に徳川家康が再建し、3代将軍家光が寛文4年（1664年）に造営したもので、「子育ての虎」「北辰の梟」など精緻な彫刻で飾られています。毎年12月3日の「秩父夜祭」は日本三大曳山祭の一つとして国の重要無形民俗文化財に指定されています。
chichibu_shrine.highlight_en: The main shrine of Musashi Province's Shinomiya and Chichibu Province's richly carved main shrines built by Tokugawa Iemitsu.
chichibu_shrine.text_en: Chichibu Shrine is an old shrine with a history of over 2000 years as the shrine of Chichibu Province (northwest Musashi Province). The current main shrine was rebuilt by Tokugawa Ieyasu in 1592 and constructed by the third shogun Iemitsu in 1664, and is decorated with elaborate carvings such as the ``Tiger Raising Children'' and the ``Owl of the Hokushin.'' The Chichibu Night Festival, held on December 3rd every year, is one of Japan's three major Hikiyama festivals and has been designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property.

yoshimi_hyakuana.name: 吉見百穴（吉見町）
yoshimi_hyakuana.kana: よしみひゃくあなよしみまち
yoshimi_hyakuana.highlight: 古墳時代後期の横穴式墳墓群、219穴が岩山に穿たれた関東最大の横穴墓
yoshimi_hyakuana.text: 吉見百穴は岩山の斜面に219個の横穴が掘られた古墳時代後期（6〜7世紀）の横穴式墳墓群で、国の史跡に指定されています。明治19年（1886年）に人類学者・坪井正五郎らが調査を行い、副葬品として勾玉・管玉・鉄刀などが出土しています。太平洋戦争中には地下軍需工場として使用された歴史も持ちます。
yoshimi_hyakuana.highlight_en: A group of horizontal cave tombs from the late Kofun period, the largest horizontal cave tomb in the Kanto region with 219 holes dug into the rocky mountain.
yoshimi_hyakuana.text_en: Yoshimi Hyakana is a group of horizontal hole-style tombs dating from the late Kofun period (6th to 7th century), where 219 horizontal holes were dug into the slope of a rocky mountain, and are designated as a national historic site. In 1886, anthropologist Shogoro Tsuboi and others conducted a survey, and excavated grave goods such as magatama beads, pipe beads, and iron swords. It also has a history of being used as an underground munitions factory during the Pacific War.

komagome_koma_shrine.name: 高麗神社（日高市）
komagome_koma_shrine.kana: こまじんじゃひだかし

transit.name: 西武池袋線武蔵高萩駅

komagome_koma_shrine.highlight: 高句麗からの渡来人・高麗王若光を祀る神社、「出世明神」として政界人が参拝
komagome_koma_shrine.text: 高麗神社は霊亀2年（716年）に武蔵国に設置された高麗郡の郡司・高麗王若光を祀る神社です。若光は高句麗滅亡後に日本に渡来した高句麗王族とされ、関東各地に定住した高麗人（高句麗からの渡来人）1799人を率いてこの地を開拓しました。歴代の総理大臣や大臣が参拝後に大臣・首相に就任したという「出世明神」として知られています。
komagome_koma_shrine.highlight_en: A shrine dedicated to Goguryeo King Wakamitsu, an immigrant from Goguryeo, visited by political figures as a ``Shusse Myojin''
komagome_koma_shrine.text_en: Koma Shrine is a shrine established in Musashi Province in 716 to enshrine Koma King Wakamitsu, the county governor of Koma County. Wakamitsu is said to be a member of the Goguryeo royal family who came to Japan after the fall of Goguryeo, and he led 1,799 Goryeo people (immigrants from Goguryeo) who settled in various parts of the Kanto region to develop this area. It is known as the ``Shusse Myojin'' shrine, where successive prime ministers and ministers became ministers or prime ministers after visiting the shrine.

kitain_kawagoe.name: 喜多院・川越大師（川越市）
kitain_kawagoe.kana: きたいんかわごえだいしかわごえし
kitain_kawagoe.highlight: 天海僧正ゆかりの寺、江戸城から移築された建物と五百羅漢で有名
kitain_kawagoe.text: 喜多院は天長7年（830年）創建の天台宗の寺院で、江戸時代には天海大僧正が住職を務め徳川家との深い繋がりを持ちました。江戸城から移築されたとされる「家光誕生の間」「春日局化粧の間」を有し、539体の個性豊かな石像が並ぶ五百羅漢でも知られます。境内は国の重要文化財に指定される建物が集中する関東屈指の文化財の宝庫です。
kitain_kawagoe.highlight_en: A temple associated with Sosho Tenkai, famous for the building relocated from Edo Castle and the 500 Arhats
kitain_kawagoe.text_en: Kita-in is a temple of the Tendai sect, founded in 830. During the Edo period, Tenkai Daiso served as the chief priest and had deep ties with the Tokugawa family. It has the ``Iemitsu Birth Room'' and ``Kasuga Tsuburo Kosho Room,'' which are said to have been relocated from Edo Castle, and is also known for the 500 Arhats, which are lined with 539 unique stone statues. The precincts are one of the greatest treasure troves of cultural properties in the Kanto region, with a large concentration of buildings designated as nationally important cultural properties.

musashi_kokubunji.name: 武蔵国分寺跡（国分寺市）
musashi_kokubunji.kana: むさしこくぶんじあとこくぶんじし
musashi_kokubunji.highlight: 聖武天皇の詔で建立された武蔵国分寺、七重塔跡と金堂跡が残る
musashi_kokubunji.text: 武蔵国分寺は天平13年（741年）に聖武天皇の詔で建立された武蔵国の国分寺で、七重塔・金堂・講堂などを備えた大規模寺院でした。鎌倉時代に新田義貞の兵火で焼失しましたが、遺跡からは多量の軒丸瓦・軒平瓦が出土し、往時の繁栄を偲ばせます。現在は史跡として整備された公園となっています。
musashi_kokubunji.highlight_en: Musashi Kokubunji was built by Emperor Shomu's edict, and the ruins of the seven-storied pagoda and Kondo remain.
musashi_kokubunji.text_en: Musashi Kokubunji is a Kokubunji in Musashi Province that was built in 741 by Emperor Shomu's edict, and was a large temple with a seven-storied pagoda, a main hall, and an auditorium. During the Kamakura period, it was burnt down by Nitta Yoshisada's military fire, but a large number of eave-maru and eave-hira tiles have been excavated from the ruins, reminding us of the prosperity of the past. It is now a park maintained as a historical site.

chiba_castle_chiba_clan.name: 千葉城跡・千葉神社（千葉市）
chiba_castle_chiba_clan.kana: ちばじょうあとちばじんじゃちばし

transit.name: 千葉都市モノレール千葉公園駅

chiba_castle_chiba_clan.highlight: 源頼朝挙兵を支援した千葉氏の本拠、房総の名族が築いた猪鼻城
chiba_castle_chiba_clan.text: 千葉城（猪鼻城）は鎌倉時代以来房総を支配した千葉氏の本拠地です。千葉常胤は源頼朝が伊豆で挙兵した際にいち早く馳せ参じ、頼朝の関東制覇を支えた重要な功臣です。千葉氏は南北朝時代まで房総の大豪族として君臨しました。現在は郷土博物館が建てられ、隣接する千葉神社には妙見菩薩が祀られています。
chiba_castle_chiba_clan.highlight_en: Inohana Castle was built by a prominent family from Boso and was the headquarters of the Chiba clan, which supported Minamoto no Yoritomo's raising an army.
chiba_castle_chiba_clan.text_en: Chiba Castle (Inohana Castle) is the stronghold of the Chiba clan, which ruled Boso since the Kamakura period. Chiba Tsunetane was an important vassal who was the first to join Minamoto no Yoritomo when he raised an army in Izu, and supported Yoritomo's conquest of the Kanto region. The Chiba clan ruled as a powerful clan in Boso until the Nanbokucho period. Currently, a local museum has been built, and Myoken Bosatsu is enshrined at the adjacent Chiba Shrine.

tateyama_satomi_castle.name: 館山城跡・里見氏（館山市）
tateyama_satomi_castle.kana: たてやまじょうあとさとみうじたてやまし

transit.name: JR内房線館山駅（またはタクシー）

tateyama_satomi_castle.highlight: 後北条氏と争った安房国の戦国大名・里見氏の居城、「南総里見八犬伝」の舞台
tateyama_satomi_castle.text: 館山城は天正6年（1578年）頃に里見義頼が築いたとされる安房国の城で、里見氏の最後の本拠地となりました。里見氏は小田原の北条氏と房総をめぐって激しく争い「犬懸・稲村の争い」などの合戦を繰り広げました。滝沢馬琴の読本「南総里見八犬伝」の舞台として知られ、現在は模擬天守に里見氏に関する博物館が設けられています。
tateyama_satomi_castle.highlight_en: The residence of the Satomi clan, a feudal lord from the Sengoku period in Awa Province who fought with the Gohojo clan, and the setting for Nanso Satomi Hakkenden.
tateyama_satomi_castle.text_en: 館山城は天正6年（1578年）頃に里見義頼が築いたとされる安房国の城で、里見氏の最後の本拠地となりました。 The Satomi clan engaged in fierce battles with the Hojo clan of Odawara over Boso, such as the ``Inukake-Inamura battle.'' It is known as the setting for Takizawa Bakin's book ``Nanso Satomi Hakkenden,'' and a museum related to the Satomi clan is currently set up in the mock castle tower.

narita_naritasan.name: 成田山新勝寺（成田市）
narita_naritasan.kana: なりたさんしんしょうじなりたし
narita_naritasan.highlight: 平将門の乱鎮圧のために開山、年間1000万人以上が参拝する不動明王の大寺院
narita_naritasan.text: 成田山新勝寺は天慶3年（940年）、寛朝大僧正が平将門の乱を鎮めるために開山したと伝わる真言宗智山派の大本山です。本尊・不動明王は「成田の不動さん」として江戸時代から篤く信仰され、市川団十郎ら歌舞伎役者との縁も深く「成田屋」という屋号の由来となりました。年間約1000万人が参拝する日本屈指の寺院です。
narita_naritasan.highlight_en: A large temple of Fudo Myoo that was founded to suppress Taira no Masakado's rebellion and is visited by more than 10 million people a year.
narita_naritasan.text_en: Naritasan Shinshoji Temple is the head temple of the Chizan school of the Shingon sect, and is said to have been founded in 940 by Kancho Daisoji in order to quell the Taira no Masakado Rebellion. The principal image, Fudo Myoo, has been devoutly worshiped since the Edo period as ``Narita's Fudo-san,'' and his close ties to Kabuki actors such as Danjuro Ichikawa are the origin of the name ``Naritaya.'' It is one of Japan's leading temples, visited by approximately 10 million people a year.

katori_shrine.name: 香取神宮（香取市）
katori_shrine.kana: かとりじんぐうかとりし
katori_shrine.highlight: 経津主神を祀る東国最古の神宮、鹿島神宮とともに「東国の二大神宮」
katori_shrine.text: 香取神宮は千葉県香取市に鎮座する経津主大神（ふつぬしのおおかみ）を主祭神とする古社で、全国約400社の香取神社の総本社です。対岸の茨城・鹿島神宮とともに「東国の二大神宮」として古代から東国の守護神として崇められてきました。神宮の杜には樹齢数百年の杉が立ち並び、荘厳な雰囲気を醸し出しています。
katori_shrine.highlight_en: Kashima Shrine is the oldest shrine in Eastern Japan, enshrining the main deity Tsunetsu, and is one of the two major shrines in Eastern Japan.
katori_shrine.text_en: Katori Shrine is an ancient shrine enshrined in Katori City, Chiba Prefecture, whose main deity is Futsunushi no Okami, and is the headquarters of approximately 400 Katori Shrines nationwide. Along with Kashima Jingu in Ibaraki on the opposite shore, it has been worshiped as the guardian deity of the eastern region since ancient times as one of the two major shrines of the eastern region. The shrine's forest is lined with cedar trees that are hundreds of years old, creating a majestic atmosphere.

sakura_castle_hotta.name: 佐倉城跡・国立歴史民俗博物館（佐倉市）
sakura_castle_hotta.kana: さくらじょうあとこくりつれきしみんぞくはくぶつかんさくらし
sakura_castle_hotta.highlight: 堀田氏が治めた「北の佐倉、南の薩摩」と呼ばれた名城、日本最大の歴史博物館を併設
sakura_castle_hotta.text: 佐倉城は慶長15年（1610年）に土井利勝が築いた城で、江戸時代を通じて幕府の重臣・堀田氏の居城として重要視されました。「北の佐倉、南の薩摩」と並び称された戦略上の要衝で、多くの名臣を輩出した名藩として知られます。城跡には国立歴史民俗博物館が建ち、日本の歴史・民俗・考古に関する総合博物館として多くの来場者を迎えています。
sakura_castle_hotta.name_en: Sakura Castle Ruins/National Museum of Japanese History (Sakura City)
sakura_castle_hotta.highlight_en: A famous castle called ``Sakura of the North, Satsuma of the South'' ruled by the Hotta clan, with Japan's largest history museum attached.
sakura_castle_hotta.text_en: Sakura Castle was built by Toshikatsu Doi in 1610, and throughout the Edo period it was considered important as the residence of the Hotta clan, a senior vassal of the shogunate. It is known as a strategically important domain that has been referred to as ``Sakura in the north and Satsuma in the south,'' and is known as a famous domain that has produced many famous vassals. The National Museum of Japanese History is built on the castle ruins, and it welcomes many visitors as a comprehensive museum about Japanese history, folklore, and archeology.

odaira_masako_chiba.name: 大多喜城跡（本多忠勝の城）
odaira_masako_chiba.kana: おおたきじょうあとほんだただかつのしろ
odaira_masako_chiba.highlight: 徳川四天王・本多忠勝が関ヶ原後に入城した房総の城、里山に建つ復元天守
odaira_masako_chiba.text: 大多喜城は永禄10年（1567年）に里見氏の家臣が築き、慶長6年（1601年）に徳川四天王の一人・本多忠勝が入城しました。忠勝は戦国時代に57回出陣して一度も傷を負わなかった猛将で、「世に過ぎたるものが二つあり、唐の頭（唐傘）に本多平八」と称えられた名将です。現在は模擬天守が建ち、城内は千葉県立中央博物館大多喜城分館となっています。
odaira_masako_chiba.highlight_en: A reconstructed castle tower in a village in Satoyama, a castle in Boso where Honda Tadakatsu, one of the Four Heavenly Kings of Tokugawa, entered the castle after Sekigahara.
odaira_masako_chiba.text_en: Otaki Castle was built by vassals of the Satomi clan in 1567, and Honda Tadakatsu, one of the Four Tokugawa Kings, entered the castle in 1601. Tadakatsu was a fierce general who went to war 57 times during the Sengoku period without ever getting injured.He was praised as ``There are two things that are too good to be true, and Heihachi Honda is the head of the Tang Dynasty.'' Currently, a mock castle tower has been erected, and the castle grounds are now the Chiba Prefectural Central Museum Otaki Castle Branch.

sekiyado_castle_chiba.name: 関宿城跡・関宿藩（野田市）
sekiyado_castle_chiba.kana: せきやどじょうあとせきやどはんのだし
sekiyado_castle_chiba.highlight: 利根川と江戸川の分岐点に位置する「要の城」、古河公方と北条氏が争奪した戦略拠点
sekiyado_castle_chiba.text: 関宿城は利根川と江戸川の分岐点という水運の要衝に位置し、古河公方・北条氏・里見氏など戦国の雄が争奪を繰り返した戦略的要衝です。江戸時代には松平氏・久世氏など譜代大名の居城となり、水運の要として繁栄しました。現在は千葉県立関宿城博物館が建ち、江戸時代の水運と城下町の歴史を展示しています。
sekiyado_castle_chiba.highlight_en: "Kaname Castle" located at the junction of the Tone River and the Edogawa River, a strategic base fought over by the Koga Kubo and the Hojo clan
sekiyado_castle_chiba.text_en: Sekijuku Castle is located at the junction of the Tone River and the Edogawa River, a key point for water transport, and is a strategic point that was repeatedly fought over by the Koga Kubo, the Hojo clan, the Satomi clan, and other Sengoku clans. During the Edo period, it became the residence of Fudai feudal lords such as the Matsudaira clan and the Kuze clan, and prospered as a key point for water transport. Currently, the Chiba Prefectural Sekijuku Castle Museum stands here, exhibiting the history of water transportation and the castle town during the Edo period.

boso_peninsula_ancient.name: 上総国分寺跡・国府跡（市原市）
boso_peninsula_ancient.kana: かずさこくぶんじあとこくふあといちはらし
boso_peninsula_ancient.highlight: 奈良時代の上総国の政治・宗教の中心、七重塔跡が残る古代遺跡群
boso_peninsula_ancient.text: 上総国分寺は聖武天皇の詔により建立された上総国の国分寺で、七重塔・金堂・講堂を備えた奈良時代の大伽藍でした。近くには上総国府跡もあり、奈良時代の房総の政治・文化の中心地として機能していました。現在は七重塔の礎石が残り、国の史跡として保護されています。
boso_peninsula_ancient.highlight_en: A group of ancient ruins with the remains of a seven-storied pagoda, the political and religious center of Kazusa Province during the Nara period.
boso_peninsula_ancient.text_en: Kazusa Kokubunji is a Kokubunji temple in Kazusa Province that was built by Emperor Shomu's edict, and was a large temple in the Nara period that included a seven-storied pagoda, a main hall, and a lecture hall. Nearby is the ruins of Kazusa Kokufu, which functioned as the political and cultural center of Boso during the Nara period. Today, the foundation stone of the seven-storied pagoda remains and is protected as a national historic site.

sawara_town_chiba.name: 佐原の町並み・伊能忠敬旧宅（香取市）
sawara_town_chiba.kana: さわらのまちなみいのうただたかきゅうたくかとりし
sawara_town_chiba.highlight: 「北総の小江戸」佐原と日本初の実測全国地図を作った伊能忠敬の旧宅
sawara_town_chiba.text: 佐原は小野川沿いに江戸時代の商家建築が残る「北総の小江戸」と呼ばれる古い町並みで、国の重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に選定されています。伊能忠敬はここで測量・地図作成事業を開始し、56歳から17年かけて日本全国を歩き測量して日本初の実測全国地図「大日本沿海輿地全図」を完成させました。旧宅は今も保存されています。
sawara_town_chiba.name_en: Sawara townscape/Ino Tadataka's former residence (Katori City)
sawara_town_chiba.highlight_en: Sawara, “Little Edo of Hokuso” and the former home of Tadataka Ino, who created Japan’s first surveyed national map
sawara_town_chiba.text_en: Sawara is an old town known as ``Hokuso's Little Edo,'' where merchant houses from the Edo period remain along the Onogawa River, and it has been designated as a nationally important preservation district for groups of traditional buildings. Tadataka Ino started his surveying and mapping business here, and from the age of 56 he spent 17 years walking and surveying all over Japan, completing Japan's first actually surveyed national map, ``Dainippon Coastal Land Complete Map.'' The old house is still preserved.

inohana_castle_edo.name: 市川・国府台城跡（市川市）
inohana_castle_edo.kana: いちかわこうのだいじょうあといちかわし
inohana_castle_edo.highlight: 里見氏と北条氏が二度にわたって激突した「国府台合戦」の古戦場
inohana_castle_edo.text: 国府台は江戸川沿いの台地で、天文7年（1538年）と永禄7年（1564年）の二度にわたって里見氏と後北条氏が激突した「国府台合戦」の舞台です。天文の合戦では北条氏綱が里見義堯を破り下総への支配を固め、永禄の合戦でも北条氏康が里見氏を撃退しました。江戸川を挟んだ要衝として中世関東史の重要な舞台となった地です。
inohana_castle_edo.highlight_en: The old battlefield of the Battle of Kokufudai, where the Satomi clan and Hojo clan clashed twice.
inohana_castle_edo.text_en: Kokufudai is a plateau along the Edogawa River, and was the scene of the ``Kokufudai Battle,'' where the Satomi clan and the Gohojo clan clashed twice in 1538 and 1564. In the Battle of Tenbun, Hojo Ujitsuna defeated Yoshiya Satomi and consolidated his control over Shimousa, and in the Battle of Eiroku, Hojo Ujiyasu defeated the Satomi clan. As a strategic point across the Edogawa River, it was an important stage in medieval Kanto history.

edo_castle_honmaru.name: 江戸城跡・皇居東御苑
edo_castle_honmaru.kana: えどじょうあとこうきょひがしぎょえん
edo_castle_honmaru.highlight: 太田道灌が築き徳川将軍家260年の居城となった日本最大の城郭跡
