edo_castle_honmaru.text: 江戸城は長禄元年（1457年）に太田道灌が築いた城を、徳川家康が慶長8年（1603年）以降に大拡張した日本最大の城郭です。本丸・二の丸・三の丸など複雑な郭が広がり、総面積は約230万平方メートルに及びます。明治維新後は皇居となり、東御苑は一般に公開されています。本丸跡の天守台石垣はかつての絢爛たる天守を想像させます。
edo_castle_honmaru.name_en: Edo Castle Ruins/Imperial Palace East Garden
edo_castle_honmaru.highlight_en: Japan's largest castle ruins built by Dokan Ota and served as the residence of the Tokugawa shogunate for 260 years.
edo_castle_honmaru.text_en: Edo Castle is the largest castle in Japan, built by Dokan Ota in 1457 and greatly expanded by Ieyasu Tokugawa after 1603. It has a complex area including Honmaru, Ninomaru, and Sannomaru, and has a total area of ​​approximately 2.3 million square meters. After the Meiji Restoration, it became the Imperial Palace, and East Garden is open to the public. The castle tower stone wall at the site of the main keep reminds us of the gorgeous castle tower of the past.

sensoji_asakusa.name: 浅草寺・浅草（台東区）
sensoji_asakusa.kana: せんそうじあさくさたいとうく

transit.name: 東京メトロ銀座線浅草駅

sensoji_asakusa.highlight: 推古天皇36年（628年）創建と伝わる東京最古の寺院、雷門と五重塔が象徴
sensoji_asakusa.text: 浅草寺は推古天皇36年（628年）に漁師の兄弟が隅田川で観音像を引き上げたことを縁起とする東京最古の寺院です。江戸時代には「浅草の観音さま」として庶民の信仰を集め、門前町は江戸随一の繁華街として賑わいました。「雷門」と大提灯は浅草の象徴として世界的に知られ、参道・仲見世は現在も多くの参拝者・観光客で賑わっています。
sensoji_asakusa.highlight_en: The oldest temple in Tokyo, said to have been built in the 36th year of Emperor Suiko (628), symbolized by the Kaminarimon gate and five-storied pagoda.
sensoji_asakusa.text_en: Sensoji Temple is Tokyo's oldest temple, dating back to 628, when a pair of fishermen's brothers pulled up a statue of Kannon from the Sumida River. During the Edo period, it attracted the faith of the common people as the ``Kannon of Asakusa'', and Monzen-cho became the busiest downtown area of ​​the Edo period. Kaminarimon and the large lantern are known worldwide as symbols of Asakusa, and the approach to the shrine, Nakamise, is still crowded with worshipers and tourists.

kanda_myojin_masakado.name: 神田明神（千代田区）
kanda_myojin_masakado.kana: かんだみょうじんちよだく
kanda_myojin_masakado.highlight: 平将門を祀る江戸総鎮守、関東の英雄・将門の首塚が江戸の守護神となった
kanda_myojin_masakado.text: 神田明神は天平2年（730年）創建の古社で、江戸時代に徳川家康が江戸城の鬼門除けとして整備し「江戸総鎮守」となりました。主祭神の一柱・平将門命は関東の英雄として、北条政子・足利尊氏・徳川家康らも平将門の祟りを恐れ手厚く祀りました。将門の首塚は大手町にあり、現代でも都市伝説のスポットとして知られています。
kanda_myojin_masakado.highlight_en: The Edo Soshinju enshrines Taira no Masakado, and the head mound of Masakado, a hero of the Kanto region, became the guardian deity of Edo.
kanda_myojin_masakado.text_en: Kanda Myojin is an old shrine that was founded in 730. During the Edo period, Tokugawa Ieyasu maintained it as a protection against evil spirits at Edo Castle, and it became the ``Edo general guardian''. One of the main deities, Taira no Masakado, was considered a hero of the Kanto region, and Hojo Masako, Ashikaga Takauji, Tokugawa Ieyasu, and others also feared Taira no Masakado's curse and carefully enshrined him. Masakado's Kubizuka is located in Otemachi and is known as a spot of urban legend even today.

yanaka_cemetery_history.name: 谷中墓地・経王寺（台東区）
yanaka_cemetery_history.kana: やなかぼちえいこうじたいとうく
yanaka_cemetery_history.highlight: 最後の将軍・徳川慶喜や幕末の志士が眠る、明治以降の東京の歴史を刻む墓地
yanaka_cemetery_history.text: 谷中墓地は江戸時代の天王寺墓地を前身とし、明治以降に整備された都内最大の墓地の一つです。最後の将軍・徳川慶喜、横山大観、長谷川一夫など多くの著名人が眠っています。隣接する経王寺は戊辰戦争の際に彰義隊の残党が立てこもり官軍に砲撃された寺として知られ、当時の弾痕が山門に今も残っています。
yanaka_cemetery_history.highlight_en: A cemetery marking the history of Tokyo since the Meiji era, where the last shogun Yoshinobu Tokugawa and other patriots at the end of the Edo period are buried.
yanaka_cemetery_history.text_en: Yanaka Cemetery, whose predecessor was Tennoji Cemetery in the Edo period, is one of the largest cemeteries in Tokyo that was developed after the Meiji period. Many famous people are buried here, including the last shogun Yoshinobu Tokugawa, Yokoyama Taikan, and Kazuo Hasegawa. The adjacent Keioji Temple is known as the temple where the remnants of the Shogitai barricaded themselves in during the Boshin War and were bombarded by the government army, and bullet holes from that time can still be seen on the Sanmon gate.

ueno_hill_shogitai.name: 上野公園・彰義隊の墓（台東区）
ueno_hill_shogitai.kana: うえのこうえんしょうぎたいのはかたいとうく
ueno_hill_shogitai.highlight: 慶応4年（1868年）の上野戦争で旧幕府軍・彰義隊が壊滅した戦場跡
ueno_hill_shogitai.text: 上野の山（忍岡）は慶応4年（1868年）5月15日、江戸城の明け渡しに反発した旧幕府軍・彰義隊約3000人が陣を張り、新政府軍と激突した「上野戦争」の舞台です。大村益次郎が率いる政府軍の砲撃で彰義隊は半日で壊滅しました。現在は西郷隆盛像や博物館が集まる公園として親しまれ、彰義隊の墓が上野公園内にひっそりと残っています。
ueno_hill_shogitai.highlight_en: The battlefield site where the former Shogunate army and Shogitai were destroyed in the Ueno War in 1868.
ueno_hill_shogitai.text_en: Ueno Mountain (Oshioka) is the site of the ``Ueno War'' on May 15, 1868, when approximately 3,000 members of the Shogitai, the former shogunate army, rebelled against the surrender of Edo Castle and set up camp, clashing with the new government army. Shogitai was annihilated in half a day by artillery bombardment by government forces led by Masujiro Omura. Today, it is a popular park with a statue of Saigo Takamori and a museum, and the graves of the Shogitai still remain quietly within Ueno Park.

shiba_zojoji_temple.name: 芝大神宮・芝東照宮（港区）
shiba_zojoji_temple.kana: しばだいじんぐうしばとうしょうぐうみなとく

transit.name: 都営地下鉄三田線芝公園駅

shiba_zojoji_temple.highlight: 家康を祀る芝東照宮と関東の伊勢神宮・芝大神宮、増上寺に隣接する神社群
shiba_zojoji_temple.text: 芝東照宮は元和3年（1617年）に徳川家康を祀って創建された東照宮で、徳川将軍家の菩提寺・増上寺に隣接しています。境内には家康が手植えしたと伝わるイチョウの巨木が残っています。隣接する芝大神宮は「関東のお伊勢さん」として親しまれる古社で、天照大御神・豊受大神を祀り、江戸時代から庶民の信仰を集めてきました。
shiba_zojoji_temple.name_en: Shiba Daijingu Shrine/Shiba Toshogu Shrine (Minato Ward)
shiba_zojoji_temple.highlight_en: A group of shrines adjacent to Shiba Toshogu Shrine, which enshrines Ieyasu, Ise Jingu Shrine, Shiba Daijingu Shrine, and Zojoji Temple in Kanto
shiba_zojoji_temple.text_en: Shiba Toshogu Shrine was built in 1617 to enshrine Tokugawa Ieyasu, and is adjacent to Zojoji, the family temple of the Tokugawa shogunate. A huge ginkgo tree that is said to have been hand-planted by Ieyasu remains on the grounds. The adjacent Shiba Daijingu Shrine is an old shrine that is affectionately known as the ``Ise-san of Kanto.'' It enshrines Amaterasu Omikami and Toyouke Omikami, and has been worshiped by the common people since the Edo period.

rikugien_garden.name: 六義園（文京区）
rikugien_garden.kana: りくぎえんぶんきょうく
rikugien_garden.highlight: 元禄時代に柳沢吉保が造営した江戸随一の大名庭園、しだれ桜の名所
rikugien_garden.text: 六義園は元禄8年（1695年）から7年かけて、5代将軍徳川綱吉の側用人・柳沢吉保が造営した大名庭園です。古今集の和歌の世界を庭園で表現した「回遊式築山泉水庭園」で、明治時代には岩崎弥太郎（三菱創業者）が所有し東京市に寄贈されました。国の特別名勝に指定され、春のしだれ桜・秋の紅葉が特に美しい都内屈指の庭園です。
rikugien_garden.highlight_en: One of Edo's most famous feudal lord gardens, built by Yoshiyasu Yanagisawa during the Genroku period, and a famous spot for weeping cherry blossoms.
rikugien_garden.text_en: Rikugien is a feudal lord garden that was constructed by Yoshiyasu Yanagisawa, a servant of the fifth shogun, Tsunayoshi Tokugawa, over a period of seven years starting in 1695. This is a ``circular rock garden with spring water garden'' that expresses the world of waka poems from the Kokinshu in a garden.It was owned by Yataro Iwasaki (founder of Mitsubishi) during the Meiji period and donated to the city of Tokyo. Designated as a national special scenic spot, it is one of the best gardens in Tokyo with particularly beautiful weeping cherry blossoms in the spring and autumn leaves in the fall.

hachioji_castle.name: 八王子城跡（八王子市）
hachioji_castle.kana: はちおうじじょうあとはちおうじし
hachioji_castle.highlight: 北条氏の後継城として豊臣軍に落とされた関東最大の山城の一つ
hachioji_castle.text: 八王子城は天正15年（1587年）頃に後北条氏の重臣・北条氏照が築いた山城で、関東屈指の規模を誇ります。天正18年（1590年）の豊臣秀吉の小田原攻めでは前田利家・上杉景勝率いる3万以上の軍勢に攻撃され、守備隊が全滅するほどの激戦となりました。現在は国の史跡として整備され、城の石垣や曲輪跡を散策できます。
hachioji_castle.highlight_en: One of the largest mountain castles in the Kanto region, which was lost to the Toyotomi army as a successor castle to the Hojo clan.
hachioji_castle.text_en: Hachioji Castle is a mountain castle built around 1587 by Ujiteru Hojo, a senior vassal of the Gohojo clan, and is one of the largest castles in the Kanto region. During Toyotomi Hideyoshi's attack on Odawara in 1590, the city was attacked by over 30,000 troops led by Maeda Toshiie and Uesugi Kagekatsu, and the battle was so fierce that the garrison was wiped out. It is now maintained as a national historic site, and you can take a walk around the castle's stone walls and curved ruins.

sengakuji_ako_ronin.name: 泉岳寺・赤穂義士の墓（港区）
sengakuji_ako_ronin.kana: せんがくじあこうぎしのはかみなとく

transit.name: 都営地下鉄浅草線泉岳寺駅

sengakuji_ako_ronin.highlight: 忠臣蔵・赤穂浪士47人が主君の仇を討ち命を捧げた大石内蔵助ら義士の墓所
sengakuji_ako_ronin.text: 泉岳寺は港区高輪にある曹洞宗の寺院で、元禄15年（1702年）12月に吉良邸討ち入りを果たした赤穂浪士47人が主君・浅野内匠頭の墓前に吉良上野介の首を供えた後、全員が切腹した地として知られています。大石内蔵助ら47義士の墓は現在も境内に並び、毎年12月14日の義士祭には多くの参拝者が訪れます。
sengakuji_ako_ronin.name_en: Sengakuji Temple, Tomb of Ako Gishi (Minato Ward)
sengakuji_ako_ronin.highlight_en: Chushingura: The graveyard of 47 Ako Ronins, including Kuranosuke Oishi, who sacrificed their lives to avenge their lords.
sengakuji_ako_ronin.text_en: Sengakuji is a Soto sect temple located in Takanawa, Minato Ward, and is known as the place where 47 Ako samurai samurai who raided the Kira residence in December 1702 committed seppuku after offering the head of Kira Kaminosuke in front of the grave of their master Asano Takumi no Kami. The graves of 47 Gishi samurai, including Kuranosuke Oishi, still line the grounds today, and many worshipers visit the Gishi Festival on December 14th every year.

koishikawa_korakuen.name: 小石川植物園・伝通院（文京区）
koishikawa_korakuen.kana: こいしかわしょくぶつえんでんずういんぶんきょうく

transit.name: 都営地下鉄三田線白山駅

koishikawa_korakuen.highlight: 江戸幕府の薬草園が起源の植物園と徳川将軍家の女性が眠る伝通院
koishikawa_korakuen.text: 小石川植物園は元禄8年（1695年）に幕府が設けた「小石川御薬園」を起源とし、貧民救済のための小石川養生所も設置されました。現在は東京大学大学院の附属植物園として4000種以上の植物を保存しています。近隣の伝通院は徳川家康の生母・於大の方が葬られた寺で、歴代将軍の縁者・女性が多く埋葬された浄土宗の大寺院です。
koishikawa_korakuen.highlight_en: A botanical garden that originated from the medicinal herb garden of the Edo shogunate, and Dentsuin, where the women of the Tokugawa shogunate are buried.
koishikawa_korakuen.text_en: The Koishikawa Botanical Garden has its origins in the Koishikawa Medicinal Garden established by the Shogunate in 1695, and the Koishikawa Health Center was also established to help the poor. Currently, it is the affiliated botanical garden of the University of Tokyo Graduate School, preserving more than 4,000 species of plants. Nearby Dentsuin is the temple where Tokugawa Ieyasu's mother, Odai, was buried, and is a large Jodo sect temple where many female relatives of successive shoguns were buried.

kamakura_daibutsu.name: 鎌倉大仏・高徳院（鎌倉市）
kamakura_daibutsu.kana: かまくらだいぶつこうとくいんかまくらし
kamakura_daibutsu.highlight: 建長4年（1252年）造立、露座の阿弥陀如来像は国宝・日本三大仏の一つ
kamakura_daibutsu.text: 鎌倉の大仏は建長4年（1252年）に造立が始まった阿弥陀如来の銅造坐像で、高さ約13.4メートルを誇ります。かつては大仏殿に安置されていましたが、明応年間の大地震・大津波で殿舎が流失し露座となりました。「露坐の大仏」として親しまれ、与謝野晶子が「かまくらや みほとけなれど 釈迦牟尼は 美男におはす」と詠んだ国宝の仏像です。
kamakura_daibutsu.highlight_en: Built in 1252, the open-air Amida Nyorai statue is a national treasure and one of Japan's three great Buddha statues.
kamakura_daibutsu.text_en: The Great Buddha of Kamakura is a bronze seated statue of Amida Nyorai whose construction began in 1252, and it boasts a height of approximately 13.4 meters. It was once enshrined in the Great Buddha Hall, but the hall was washed away by the great earthquake and tsunami of the Meiō era, and it was left out in the open. It is a national treasure statue that is affectionately known as the ``Great Buddha Seated in the Open Air,'' and which Akiko Yosano wrote in a poem, ``Even though Shakyamuni is a beautiful man, he is beautiful.''

tsurugaoka_hachimangu.name: 鶴岡八幡宮（鎌倉市）
tsurugaoka_hachimangu.kana: つるがおかはちまんぐうかまくらし
tsurugaoka_hachimangu.highlight: 源頼朝が鎌倉幕府の精神的支柱として整備した武家の都・鎌倉の中心社
tsurugaoka_hachimangu.text: 鶴岡八幡宮は源頼義が天喜4年（1063年）に由比郷に祀ったことを起源とし、源頼朝が文治3年（1187年）に現在地に移して整備した武家の都・鎌倉の中心社です。若宮大路の段葛（ケヤキ並木）は頼朝が政子の安産を祈願して造営したと伝わります。源実朝暗殺事件（1219年）の舞台でもあり、鎌倉幕府の栄枯盛衰を見守ってきた歴史ある神社です。
tsurugaoka_hachimangu.highlight_en: The central shrine of Kamakura, the samurai capital, established by Minamoto no Yoritomo as the spiritual pillar of the Kamakura shogunate.
tsurugaoka_hachimangu.text_en: Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine has its origins in Minamoto no Yoriyoshi's enshrinement in Yuigo in 1063, and is the central shrine of the samurai capital of Kamakura, where Minamoto no Yoritomo moved it to its current location in 1187. It is said that the rows of zelkova trees along Wakamiya Oji Road were built by Yoritomo to pray for Masako's safe delivery. It is also the setting for the Minamoto no Sanetomo assassination incident (1219), and is a historic shrine that has watched over the rise and fall of the Kamakura Shogunate.

yoritomo_tomb_kamakura.name: 源頼朝の墓・白旗神社（鎌倉市）
yoritomo_tomb_kamakura.kana: みなもとのよりとものはかしらはたじんじゃかまくらし
yoritomo_tomb_kamakura.highlight: 武家政権・鎌倉幕府を開いた源頼朝が眠る法華堂跡と白旗神社
yoritomo_tomb_kamakura.text: 源頼朝は建久10年（1199年）に53歳で没し、鎌倉の法華堂（大倉幕府近く）に葬られました。現在は頼朝の墓（五輪塔）が小高い丘の上に立ち、白旗神社が隣接して頼朝を祀っています。頼朝は平治の乱で敗れて伊豆に流されてから20年近くの雌伏を経て、治承4年（1180年）に挙兵し鎌倉幕府を開いた日本初の武家政権の創始者です。
yoritomo_tomb_kamakura.name_en: Minamoto no Yoritomo's grave, Shirahata Shrine (Kamakura City)
yoritomo_tomb_kamakura.highlight_en: Hokke-do Hall ruins and Shirahata Shrine where Minamoto no Yoritomo, founder of the samurai government and Kamakura shogunate, is buried
yoritomo_tomb_kamakura.text_en: Minamoto no Yoritomo died in 1199 at the age of 53 and was buried at Hokke-do Hall in Kamakura (near the Okura Shogunate). Currently, Yoritomo's grave (Gorinto) stands on a small hill, and Shirahata Shrine is adjacent to it, where Yoritomo is enshrined. Yoritomo was defeated in the Heiji Rebellion and exiled to Izu, where he spent nearly 20 years in exile, before raising an army in 1180 and establishing the Kamakura Shogunate, the founder of Japan's first samurai government.

hakone_sekisho.name: 箱根関所跡（箱根町）
hakone_sekisho.kana: はこねせきしょあとはこねまち

transit.name: 箱根登山鉄道箱根湯本駅
transit.walk: 箱根海賊船で箱根町港

hakone_sekisho.highlight: 「入り鉄砲に出女」で知られる江戸幕府の東海道最重要関所の復元
hakone_sekisho.text: 箱根関所は元和5年（1619年）に江戸幕府が東海道に設けた重要な関所で、「入り鉄砲に出女」（江戸への武器の持ち込みと、人質として江戸に住む大名の妻の脱出を監視）を厳しく取り締まりました。芦ノ湖の西岸に位置し、現在は当時の建物が復元され、関所の役割や仕組みを伝える博物館として整備されています。
hakone_sekisho.highlight_en: Restoration of the Edo Shogunate's most important checkpoint on the Tokaido Road, known for ``entering the gun and leaving the woman.''
hakone_sekisho.text_en: The Hakone Checkpoint was an important checkpoint established by the Edo Shogunate in 1619 on the Tokaido Road, and strictly controlled ``entering guns and leaving women'' (bringing weapons into Edo and monitoring the escape of the wives of feudal lords living in Edo as hostages). Located on the west bank of Lake Ashi, the original building has now been restored and is now used as a museum to explain the role and structure of the checkpoint.

kamakura_hokoji.name: 北条氏政墓・小田原評定の地（小田原市）
kamakura_hokoji.kana: ほうじょううじまさのはかおだわらひょうじょうのちおだわらし
kamakura_hokoji.highlight: 「小田原評定」の語源となった豊臣秀吉の小田原攻めで滅亡した後北条氏の終焉
kamakura_hokoji.text: 後北条氏の居城・小田原城では天正18年（1590年）、豊臣秀吉の大軍に包囲された際に長期にわたる家臣会議（小田原評定）が行われ、決断できないまま開城・滅亡しました。「小田原評定」は今も「結論の出ない会議」を指す言葉として使われています。城内には北条氏政・氏照の墓があり、後北条氏5代の歴史を伝えています。
kamakura_hokoji.name_en: Hojo Ujimasa Tomb/Odawara Evaluation Site (Odawara City)
kamakura_hokoji.highlight_en: The end of the Gohojo clan, which was destroyed by Toyotomi Hideyoshi's attack on Odawara, which became the origin of the word "Odawara Hyojo"
kamakura_hokoji.text_en: When Odawara Castle, the residence of the Gohojo clan, was surrounded by Toyotomi Hideyoshi's large army in 1590, a long meeting of vassals (Odawara Hōsei) was held, and the castle was surrendered and destroyed without a decision being made. The term ``Odawara evaluation'' is still used today to refer to a ``conference without a conclusion.'' Inside the castle are the graves of Ujimasa Hojo and Ujiteru, telling the history of the five generations of the Gohojo clan.

nitta_yoshisada_inamuragasaki.name: 稲村ヶ崎（新田義貞が海に剣を投げた地）
nitta_yoshisada_inamuragasaki.kana: いなむらがさきにったよしさだがうみにつるぎをなげたち

transit.name: 江ノ島電鉄稲村ヶ崎駅

nitta_yoshisada_inamuragasaki.highlight: 新田義貞が黄金の太刀を海に投げ干潮を呼び鎌倉幕府を倒した伝説の岬
nitta_yoshisada_inamuragasaki.text: 稲村ヶ崎は鎌倉西端の岬で、元弘3年（1333年）に新田義貞が鎌倉幕府を倒すため黄金の太刀を海に投じて龍神に祈ると海が干上がり、岬を迂回して鎌倉に突入したという伝説で知られています。義貞はここから鎌倉に侵入し、北条高時が切腹して約140年続いた鎌倉幕府を滅ぼしました。岬には義貞の石碑が建ち、眼下には相模湾が広がります。
nitta_yoshisada_inamuragasaki.name_en: Inamuragasaki (the place where Yoshisada Nitta threw his sword into the sea)
nitta_yoshisada_inamuragasaki.highlight_en: The legendary cape where Nitta Yoshisada threw his golden sword into the sea and summoned low tide to defeat the Kamakura Shogunate.
nitta_yoshisada_inamuragasaki.text_en: Inamuragasaki is a cape on the western edge of Kamakura, and it is known from the legend that in 1333, Yoshisada Nitta threw a golden sword into the sea and prayed to the dragon god in order to defeat the Kamakura shogunate, but the sea dried up and he bypassed the cape and entered Kamakura. From here, Yoshisada invaded Kamakura, where Hojo Takatoki committed seppuku and destroyed the Kamakura shogunate, which had lasted about 140 years. A stone monument to Yoshisada is erected on the cape, and Sagami Bay stretches out below.

yokohama_kaiko_kinenkan.name: 横浜開港記念館・象の鼻（横浜市）
yokohama_kaiko_kinenkan.kana: よこはまかいこうきねんかんぞうのはなよこはまし

transit.name: みなとみらい線日本大通り駅

yokohama_kaiko_kinenkan.highlight: 安政6年（1859年）の横浜開港から始まる近代日本の玄関口の歴史
yokohama_kaiko_kinenkan.text: 横浜は安政6年（1859年）に日米修好通商条約に基づき開港した近代日本の玄関口です。象の鼻地区には幕末の波止場が復元され、開港以来の外国との交流の歴史を伝えています。横浜開港記念館（ジャックの塔）は大正6年（1917年）に開港50周年を記念して建てられた歴史的建造物で、国の重要文化財に指定されています。
yokohama_kaiko_kinenkan.name_en: Yokohama Port Opening Memorial Museum/Zou-no-hana (Yokohama City)
yokohama_kaiko_kinenkan.highlight_en: The history of the gateway to modern Japan, starting with the opening of Yokohama Port in 1859
yokohama_kaiko_kinenkan.text_en: Yokohama is the gateway to modern Japan, opened in 1859 based on the Japan-US Treaty of Amity and Commerce. In the Zou-no-hana district, the quay from the end of the Edo period has been restored, telling the history of exchanges with foreign countries since the opening of the port. Yokohama Port Opening Memorial Hall (Jack's Tower) is a historical building built in 1917 to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the opening of the port, and is designated as a national important cultural property.

perry_kurihama_monument.name: ペリー来航の碑・久里浜（横須賀市）
perry_kurihama_monument.kana: ぺりーらいこうのひくりはまよこすかし

transit.name: 京急久里浜線京急久里浜駅

perry_kurihama_monument.highlight: 嘉永6年（1853年）にペリー提督が黒船で上陸し日本の開国を迫った史跡
perry_kurihama_monument.text: 久里浜は嘉永6年（1853年）7月8日、アメリカの東インド艦隊司令長官マシュー・ペリーが4隻の黒船（蒸気船）を率いて来航し、幕府に開国を迫った上陸地点です。翌年の日米和親条約締結へとつながるこの「黒船来航」は、日本が鎖国から開国へと転換した歴史的瞬間でした。ペリー公園には上陸記念碑とペリーの胸像が建てられています。
perry_kurihama_monument.highlight_en: Historical site where Commodore Perry landed on his black ship in 1853 and pressed for the opening of Japan.
perry_kurihama_monument.text_en: Kurihama was the landing site on July 8, 1853, when Matthew Perry, commander of the American East India Fleet, came to sea with four black ships (steamboats) and pressed the Shogunate to open the country. The arrival of the Black Ships, which led to the conclusion of the Treaty of Peace and Amity between the United States and Japan the following year, was a historic moment when Japan transitioned from isolation to openness. Perry Park has a landing monument and a bust of Perry.

miura_clan_kinugasa.name: 衣笠城跡（横須賀市）
miura_clan_kinugasa.kana: きぬがさじょうあとよこすかし
miura_clan_kinugasa.highlight: 相模三浦半島を支配した三浦氏の本拠城、源頼朝挙兵を支えた名族の城
miura_clan_kinugasa.text: 衣笠城は三浦半島の山中に築かれた山城で、鎌倉時代以前から相模国三浦郡を支配した三浦氏の本拠地です。三浦義明は源頼朝が伊豆で挙兵した際に積極的に支援し、89歳で衣笠城に立て籠もり頼朝の逃亡を助けながら討ち死にしました。三浦氏はその後も鎌倉幕府の重要な御家人として活躍しましたが、宝治元年（1247年）の宝治合戦で北条氏に滅ぼされました。
miura_clan_kinugasa.highlight_en: The base castle of the Miura clan, which ruled the Sagami-Miura Peninsula, and the castle of a prominent family that supported Minamoto no Yoritomo's army.
miura_clan_kinugasa.text_en: Kinugasa Castle is a mountain castle built in the mountains of the Miura Peninsula, and is the home base of the Miura clan, which ruled Miura District, Sagami Province from before the Kamakura period. Yoshiaki Miura actively supported Minamoto no Yoritomo when he raised an army in Izu, and at the age of 89, he barricaded himself in Kinugasa Castle and was killed in battle while helping Yoritomo escape. The Miura clan continued to play an active role as an important retainer of the Kamakura shogunate, but was defeated by the Hojo clan in the Hoji War in 1247.

ishiobashi_yoritomo.name: 石橋山古戦場（小田原市）
ishiobashi_yoritomo.kana: いしばしやまこせんじょうおだわらし
ishiobashi_yoritomo.highlight: 源頼朝が旗揚げして緒戦に敗れ、洞窟に身を隠した再起への出発点
ishiobashi_yoritomo.text: 石橋山は治承4年（1180年）8月23日、源頼朝が三百余騎で挙兵して平家方の大庭景親率いる三千の軍勢と戦い大敗した地です。頼朝は僅かな従者とともに山中を逃れ、洞窟（しとどの窟）に身を隠してから房総半島へ脱出しました。この一戦を経て千葉・上総・武蔵の大豪族の支援を得た頼朝は関東を制圧し、鎌倉幕府開設への道を歩み始めます。
ishiobashi_yoritomo.highlight_en: The starting point for Minamoto no Yoritomo's comeback after raising his flag and losing in the first battle, he hid in a cave.
ishiobashi_yoritomo.text_en: Ishibashiyama is the place where Minamoto no Yoritomo raised an army with over 300 cavalry on August 23, 1180, and was defeated in a battle against 3,000 troops led by Kagechika Oba of the Taira clan. Yoritomo fled the mountains with a small number of his followers, hid in a cave, and then escaped to the Boso Peninsula. After this battle, Yoritomo gained support from the powerful clans of Chiba, Kazusa, and Musashi, conquered the Kanto region, and began the path to establishing the Kamakura Shogunate.

nagoya_castle.name: 名古屋城
nagoya_castle.text: 名古屋城は、徳川家康が1610年に九男・義直のために築城を命じた城です。天下普請として福島正則・加藤清正など外様大名も動員され、わずか5年で完成しました。金の鯱鉾は城の富と権力の象徴として知られ、天守閣の最上部に雄雄しく鎮座しています。江戸時代を通じて尾張徳川家の居城として栄え、御三家筆頭として幕府を支え続けました。明治維新後は陸軍の施設となり、第二次世界大戦の空襲で天守閣は焼失しましたが、1959年に再建。現在は国の特別史跡に指定され、年間200万人以上が訪れる名古屋を代表する観光地となっています。
nagoya_castle.highlight: 金の鯱で有名な尾張徳川家の居城。天下普請の傑作
nagoya_castle.highlight_en: The castle of the Owari Tokugawa family, famous for its Golden Shachi. A masterpiece of world construction
nagoya_castle.text_en: Nagoya Castle is a castle ordered by Tokugawa Ieyasu to be built in 1610 for his ninth son, Yoshinao. Foreign feudal lords such as Masanori Fukushima and Kiyomasa Kato were mobilized to undertake the work, and the project was completed in just five years. The golden chachiboko is known as a symbol of the castle's wealth and power, and sits majestically at the top of the castle tower. Throughout the Edo period, it flourished as the residence of the Owari Tokugawa family, and continued to support the shogunate as the leader of the three major families. After the Meiji Restoration, it became an army facility, and although the castle tower was destroyed by air raids during World War II, it was rebuilt in 1959. It is currently designated as a national special historic site and is a major tourist destination in Nagoya, visited by more than 2 million people a year.

inuyama_castle.name: 犬山城
inuyama_castle.text: 犬山城は、1537年に織田信長の叔父・織田信康が現在の天守の前身を築いたとされる城です。木曽川沿いの断崖絶壁に建つ天守は国宝に指定されており、現存12天守のひとつです。信長の桶狭間出陣の際の拠点となり、その後も小牧・長久手の戦いなど数々の合戦の舞台となりました。江戸時代には成瀬家が城主となり、明治まで存続。廃城令でも取り壊しを免れ、2004年まで個人所有という珍しい歴史を持ちます。天守からは木曽川の清流と濃尾平野を一望でき、季節ごとに変わる景色が訪れる人々を魅了しています。
inuyama_castle.highlight: 国宝天守を持つ現存城。木曽川断崖に建つ戦国の名城
inuyama_castle.highlight_en: An existing castle with a national treasure tower. A famous castle from the Sengoku period built on the Kiso River cliff
inuyama_castle.text_en: Inuyama Castle is a castle that is said to have been built in 1537 by Nobuyasu Oda, the uncle of Oda Nobunaga, who built the forerunner of the current castle tower. The castle tower, which stands on a cliff along the Kiso River, is designated as a national treasure and is one of the 12 existing castle towers. It served as Nobunaga's base when he marched to Okehazama, and was the scene of numerous battles thereafter, including the battles of Komaki and Nagakute. The Naruse family became the lords of the castle during the Edo period and continued to exist until the Meiji period. It has an unusual history of being privately owned until 2004, having escaped demolition under the Castle Abandonment Ordinance. From the castle tower, you can see the clear stream of the Kiso River and the Nobi Plain, and the scenery that changes with the seasons attracts visitors.

sunpu_castle.name: 駿府城跡
sunpu_castle.text: 駿府城は、徳川家康が幼少期に人質として過ごし、晩年に大御所として君臨した城です。今川氏の城下町・駿府に1585年、家康が初めて入城。関ヶ原の戦いで天下を取った後、将軍職を息子秀忠に譲りながらも実権を握り続けた「大御所政治」の舞台となりました。家康は1616年、駿府城で75歳の生涯を閉じています。江戸時代には天守が二度焼失し再建されましたが、現在は石垣と堀が往時の面影を伝えています。発掘調査では家康時代の石垣が次々と発見され、大型天守台の復元工事も進んでいます。
sunpu_castle.highlight: 家康が人質として過ごし大御所として没した城。晩年の舞台
sunpu_castle.highlight_en: A castle where Ieyasu spent time as a hostage and died as a great lord. stage in later years
sunpu_castle.text_en: Sunpu Castle is the castle where Tokugawa Ieyasu spent his childhood as a hostage, and where he ruled as a great lord in his later years. In 1585, Ieyasu entered Sunpu, the castle town of the Imagawa clan, for the first time. After conquering the country at the Battle of Sekigahara, it became the stage for the ``Ogosho politics'' in which he continued to hold real power even though he handed over the post of shogun to his son Hidetada. Ieyasu passed away at Sunpu Castle in 1616 at the age of 75. During the Edo period, the castle tower was burnt down twice and rebuilt, but today the stone walls and moat still retain the vestiges of the past. During excavations, stone walls from the Ieyasu era were discovered one after another, and restoration work on the large castle tower is also progressing.

hamamatsu_castle.name: 浜松城
hamamatsu_castle.text: 浜松城は、徳川家康が29歳から45歳まで約17年間を過ごした「出世城」です。家康はここを拠点に遠江・三河を治め、信長との同盟を深め、武田信玄と激突した三方ヶ原の戦いで大敗を喫したのも、この城の目と鼻の先でした。その後もここから多くの城主が出世し、老中・大老などの要職に就いたことから「出世城」の別名がついています。野面積みの石垣は当時の技術を伝える貴重な遺構で、国の史跡に指定。天守は1958年に復興され、家康の甲冑や武器などの展示で往時の威容を偲ぶことができます。
hamamatsu_castle.highlight: 家康が17年間の青春を過ごした「出世城」
hamamatsu_castle.highlight_en: Shusse Castle, where Ieyasu spent 17 years of his youth
hamamatsu_castle.text_en: Hamamatsu Castle is the ``castle of success'' where Tokugawa Ieyasu spent approximately 17 years from the age of 29 to 45. Ieyasu ruled Totomi and Mikawa from this castle, deepening his alliance with Nobunaga, and it was just a stone's throw from this castle that he clashed with Takeda Shingen and suffered a crushing defeat at the Battle of Mikatagahara. After that, many castle lords rose through the ranks and held important positions such as roju and tairo, which is why it was given the nickname ``Success Castle.'' The field stone wall is a valuable structure that conveys the technology of the time, and has been designated as a national historic site. The castle tower was rebuilt in 1958, and you can remember the grandeur of the past with displays of Ieyasu's armor and weapons.

matsumoto_castle.name: 松本城
matsumoto_castle.text: 松本城は、1504年頃に築城された深志城が起源で、武田信玄の支配を経て、1590年に石川数正・康長父子が近世城郭として整備しました。現存する五重六階の天守は最古の国宝天守のひとつで、烏城とも呼ばれる黒塗りの外壁が印象的です。安土桃山時代に建てられた大天守は戦のための「月見櫓」も備え、実戦と雅の両立を示しています。明治時代に廃城・競売にかかりそうになりましたが、市民の熱意ある保存運動で守られました。北アルプスを背景にした天守の姿は日本を代表する絶景のひとつで、毎年多くの観光客が訪れます。
matsumoto_castle.highlight: 現存最古級の国宝天守。黒の烏城と北アルプスの絶景
matsumoto_castle.highlight_en: The oldest existing national treasure castle tower. Spectacular views of Kuro Karasu Castle and the Northern Alps
matsumoto_castle.text_en: Matsumoto Castle originated from Fukashi Castle, which was built around 1504, and after being ruled by Takeda Shingen, it was developed as an early modern castle in 1590 by father and son Kazumasa Ishikawa and Yasunaga. The existing five-story, six-story castle tower is one of the oldest national treasures, and its black-painted outer walls, also known as Crow Castle, are impressive. The large castle tower, built during the Azuchi-Momoyama period, also has a ``Tsukimi turret'' for use in battles, demonstrating the balance between actual warfare and elegance. During the Meiji period, the castle was about to be abandoned and auctioned off, but it was saved thanks to the passionate preservation efforts of the citizens. The appearance of the castle tower with the Northern Alps in the background is one of the most spectacular views in Japan, and is visited by many tourists every year.

ichijodani_ruins.name: 一乗谷朝倉氏遺跡
ichijodani_ruins.kana: いちじょうだにあさくらしいせき
ichijodani_ruins.text: 一乗谷は、越前の戦国大名・朝倉氏が5代にわたって約103年間栄えた城下町の遺跡です。最盛期の人口は約1万人を誇り、京文化を取り入れた「小京都」として栄華を誇りました。織田信長に義兄弟の仲を破られた11代・朝倉義景は1573年に一乗谷を焼かれ、自害して朝倉氏は滅亡。町は戦火と土砂に埋もれ、400年以上の眠りの後に発掘調査が始まりました。現在は特別史跡・特別名勝に指定され、戦国の城下町がほぼ完全な形で地下に保存されており、武家屋敷や町並みが復原展示されています。
ichijodani_ruins.highlight: 戦国の城下町が地下に丸ごと眠る。発掘された幻の都
ichijodani_ruins.highlight_en: The entire castle town of the Sengoku era lies underground. The phantom city discovered
ichijodani_ruins.text_en: Ichijodani is the ruins of a castle town where Echizen's Sengoku feudal lord, the Asakura clan, flourished for about 103 years over five generations. At its peak, the city boasted a population of approximately 10,000 people and flourished as a ``Little Kyoto'' that incorporated Kyoto culture. The 11th generation, Yoshikage Asakura, whose brother-in-law relationship was broken by Oda Nobunaga, burned down Ichijodani in 1573, committed suicide, and the Asakura clan came to an end. The town was buried under war fires and mud, and after lying dormant for over 400 years, excavations began. Currently designated as a Special Historic Site and Special Place of Scenic Beauty, the castle town of the Sengoku period has been preserved in its almost complete form underground, and restored samurai residences and townscapes are on display.

komaki_castle.name: 小牧山城跡
komaki_castle.kana: こまきやまじょうあと
komaki_castle.text: 小牧山城は、1563年に織田信長が美濃攻略の拠点として築いた城です。山全体を削り石垣を積んだ画期的な構造は、安土城の原型ともいわれています。信長は稲葉山城（岐阜城）を攻略した後に廃城とし、その後は徳川家康と豊臣秀吉が争った小牧・長久手の戦い（1584年）での家康の本陣となりました。現在の天守は1967年に建てられた歴史資料館で、発掘調査では信長時代の石垣や礎石が次々と発見されています。山頂からは濃尾平野が一望でき、信長が眼下に見据えた天下への野望が感じられます。
komaki_castle.highlight: 信長が美濃攻略に築き、後に家康の本陣となった丘城
komaki_castle.highlight_en: A hill castle built by Nobunaga during the capture of Mino, which later became Ieyasu's headquarters.
komaki_castle.text_en: Komakiyama Castle was built in 1563 by Oda Nobunaga as a base for conquering Mino. The groundbreaking structure, carved out of the entire mountain and piled up with stone walls, is said to be the prototype of Azuchi Castle. Nobunaga abandoned Inabayama Castle (Gifu Castle) after capturing it, and it later became Ieyasu's headquarters during the Battle of Komaki-Nagakute (1584), fought between Tokugawa Ieyasu and Toyotomi Hideyoshi. The current castle tower is a historical museum built in 1967, and during excavations, stone walls and foundation stones from the Nobunaga era have been discovered one after another. From the top of the mountain, you can see the Nobi Plain, and you can feel Nobunaga's ambitions for the world below.

mikatagahara_battlefield.name: 三方ヶ原古戦場跡
mikatagahara_battlefield.kana: みかたがはらこせんじょうあと
mikatagahara_battlefield.text: 三方ヶ原の戦いは1572年12月、武田信玄が上洛作戦の途中で徳川家康・織田信長連合軍と激突した合戦です。「風林火山」の旗印のもと2万7千の武田軍に対し、家康は8千の兵で迎え撃ちましたが、兵力差は歴然。家康は大敗を喫し、命からがら浜松城に逃げ帰ったとされます。その際に脱糞した家康が、忘れないよう自らの醜態を絵にさせたという「しかみ像」は有名です。この敗戦が家康の最大の教訓となり、以降の戦略に大きな影響を与えました。古戦場碑や犀ヶ崖資料館が当時の激戦を今に伝えます。
mikatagahara_battlefield.highlight: 家康生涯最大の敗戦。信玄に完敗し命からがら逃げた地
mikatagahara_battlefield.highlight_en: The biggest defeat of Ieyasu's life. The place where he was completely defeated by Shingen and barely escaped with his life.
mikatagahara_battlefield.text_en: The Battle of Mikatagahara was fought in December 1572, when Takeda Shingen clashed with the combined forces of Tokugawa Ieyasu and Oda Nobunaga during the invasion of Kyoto. Ieyasu attacked Takeda's 27,000-strong army under the banner of ``Furinkazan'' with 8,000 soldiers, but the difference in strength was clear. It is said that Ieyasu suffered a crushing defeat and fled back to Hamamatsu Castle with his life. The famous Shikami statue is said to have been created by Ieyasu, who defecated at the time, and had his abomination painted as a reminder. This defeat was Ieyasu's biggest lesson and had a major impact on his subsequent strategies. The old battlefield monument and the Saiga Cliff Museum tell us about the fierce battles of those days.

toyama_castle.name: 富山城跡・富山市郷土博物館
toyama_castle.text: 富山城は、1543年頃に神保長職が築いたとされる城です。戦国時代には佐々成政が入城し、信長・秀吉に仕えながら独自の支配を確立しました。成政は秀吉に反旗を翻した後、真冬の北アルプスを越えて家康に援軍を求めた「さらさら越え」の逸話で知られています。江戸時代には加賀前田家の支城となり、富山藩前田家が城下町を整備。「薬の富山」として全国に行商人を送り出す産業の拠点ともなりました。現在は天守風の市郷土博物館が建ち、富山藩の歴史と薬売りの文化を伝えています。
toyama_castle.highlight: 佐々成政の「さらさら越え」で有名。薬の富山の歴史の城
toyama_castle.name_en: Toyama Castle Ruins/Toyama City Folk Museum
toyama_castle.highlight_en: Famous for Sassa Narimasa's ``Sarasaragoe''. Toyama’s historical castle of medicine
toyama_castle.text_en: Toyama Castle is said to have been built by Jinbo Nagatoki around 1543. During the Sengoku period, Sassa Narimasa entered the castle and established his own rule while serving Nobunaga and Hideyoshi. After Narimasa rebelled against Hideyoshi, he is known for the anecdote of ``Sarasaragoe,'' in which he crossed the Northern Alps in the middle of winter to request reinforcements from Ieyasu. During the Edo period, it became a branch castle of the Kaga Maeda family, and the Maeda family of the Toyama domain developed a castle town. Known as ``Toyama of medicine,'' it also became an industrial base that sent out peddlers all over the country. Currently, the Tenshu Kaze City Folk Museum stands here, telling the history of the Toyama clan and the culture of medicine sellers.

hirosaki_castle.name: 弘前城
hirosaki_castle.text: 弘前城は、1611年に津軽藩初代藩主・津軽信枚が築いた城です。東北地方で唯一の現存天守を持ち、国の重要文化財に指定されています。三層の天守は質素ながら品格があり、白壁と朱塗りの欄干が美しく調和しています。桜の名所としても名高く、ソメイヨシノをはじめ約2,600本の桜が咲き誇る春には「弘前さくらまつり」が開かれ、城と桜の競演は日本随一と称えられます。津軽藩は江戸時代を通じて10万石の藩として存続し、津軽三味線や弘前ねぷたなど独自の文化を育みました。
hirosaki_castle.highlight: 東北唯一の現存天守。桜2600本が咲き誇る日本屈指の花見城
hirosaki_castle.highlight_en: The only existing castle tower in Tohoku. One of Japan's best cherry blossom viewing castles with 2,600 cherry blossom trees in full bloom
hirosaki_castle.text_en: Hirosaki Castle was built in 1611 by Tsugaru Nobuhira, the first lord of the Tsugaru domain. It has the only existing castle tower in the Tohoku region and is designated as a national important cultural property. The three-story castle tower is simple but dignified, and the white walls and vermilion-painted railings harmonize beautifully. It is also famous as a cherry blossom viewing spot, and the ``Hirosaki Cherry Blossom Festival'' is held in the spring when approximately 2,600 cherry blossom trees, including Somei Yoshino cherry trees, are in full bloom, and the castle and cherry blossoms are said to be the best in Japan. The Tsugaru domain continued as a domain of 100,000 koku throughout the Edo period, and cultivated its own unique culture such as Tsugaru shamisen and Hirosaki Neputa.

sannai_maruyama_ruins.name: 三内丸山遺跡
sannai_maruyama_ruins.kana: さんないまるやまいせき
sannai_maruyama_ruins.text: 三内丸山遺跡は、約5900年前から4200年前にかけて栄えた縄文時代最大級の集落遺跡です。2021年にユネスコ世界文化遺産「北海道・北東北の縄文遺跡群」の構成資産として登録されました。六本柱建物は直径約1mの栗の柱を等間隔に並べた大型建造物で、縄文人の高度な建築技術を示しています。遺跡からは大量の土偶・土器のほか、翡翠・黒曜石など遠方との交易品も出土し、広域なネットワークの存在が明らかになっています。縄文時代のイメージを覆す、定住・交易・文化の拠点として世界的な注目を集めています。
sannai_maruyama_ruins.highlight: ユネスコ世界遺産。縄文最大の集落が示す高度な文明
sannai_maruyama_ruins.highlight_en: UNESCO World Heritage Site. Advanced civilization demonstrated by the largest Jomon settlement
sannai_maruyama_ruins.text_en: The Sannai Maruyama ruins are one of the largest settlement ruins from the Jomon period, which flourished from about 5,900 to 4,200 years ago. In 2021, it was registered as a component of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Jomon Ruins in Hokkaido and Northern Tohoku." The six-pillar building is a large building made of chestnut pillars approximately 1 meter in diameter arranged at even intervals, demonstrating the advanced architectural techniques of the Jomon people. In addition to large quantities of clay figurines and pottery, the ruins also unearthed items such as jade and obsidian, which were traded with distant places, revealing the existence of a wide-area network. It is attracting worldwide attention as a center of settlement, trade, and culture, overturning the image of the Jomon period.

matsushima_zuiganji.name: 松島・瑞巌寺
matsushima_zuiganji.kana: まつしま・ずいがんじ
matsushima_zuiganji.text: 松島は日本三景のひとつで、260余りの松が茂る小島が湾内に点在する絶景の地です。瑞巌寺は平安時代に創建され、伊達政宗が1609年に5年の歳月をかけて大改修した東北随一の禅寺です。本堂は国宝に指定され、豪華な彫刻と狩野派の障壁画が政宗の権威を今に伝えます。松尾芭蕉は「おくのほそ道」の旅でこの地を訪れ、その美しさに言葉を失ったと伝えられています。東日本大震災では大きな被害を受けましたが、復興を遂げ、多くの観光客が訪れる宮城を代表する景勝地として輝きを取り戻しています。
matsushima_zuiganji.highlight: 日本三景のひとつ。政宗が再建した国宝の禅寺と260の島々
matsushima_zuiganji.highlight_en: One of the three most scenic views of Japan. National treasure Zen temple and 260 islands rebuilt by Masamune
matsushima_zuiganji.text_en: Matsushima is one of Japan's three most scenic spots, with over 260 small islands covered with pine trees scattered throughout the bay. Zuigan-ji Temple was founded in the Heian period and is the largest Zen temple in the Tohoku region, which was extensively renovated by Date Masamune in 1609 over a period of five years. The main hall has been designated as a national treasure, and the gorgeous carvings and wall paintings of the Kano school convey Masamune's authority to this day. It is said that Matsuo Basho visited this place on his ``Oku no Hosomichi'' trip and was speechless by its beauty. Although it suffered severe damage in the Great East Japan Earthquake, it has been restored and has regained its brilliance as a representative scenic spot in Miyagi that is visited by many tourists.

tagajo_ruins.name: 多賀城跡
tagajo_ruins.text: 多賀城は724年に創建された陸奥国府・鎮守府で、奈良・平安時代の東北経営の中枢でした。大和朝廷が蝦夷との境界を定め、東北を支配するための最前線基地として機能しました。9世紀には坂上田村麻呂の活躍もあり、陸奥の支配が進みました。平安時代後期に前九年・後三年の役が起こり、陸奥の覇権をめぐって源氏と奥州藤原氏の前身勢力が争いました。特別史跡に指定された城跡からは多数の木簡・土器が出土し、奈良時代の行政文書なども発見されています。東北歴史博物館が隣接し、発掘成果を展示しています。
tagajo_ruins.highlight: 奈良時代の東北支配の拠点。大和朝廷と蝦夷の境界線
tagajo_ruins.highlight_en: A base for domination of Tohoku during the Nara period. Boundary line between Yamato court and Ezo
tagajo_ruins.text_en: Taga Castle was the provincial capital and military base of Mutsu, founded in 724, and was the center of Tohoku management during the Nara and Heian periods. It served as a front-line base for the Yamato court to establish a border with Ezo and control the Tohoku region. In the 9th century, due to the success of Sakanoue Tamuramaro, the control of Mutsu advanced. In the latter half of the Heian period, the War of Nine Years of War and War of Three Years of Later occurred, during which the predecessor powers of the Minamoto clan and the Oshu Fujiwara clan fought for supremacy in Mutsu. Numerous wooden tablets and pottery have been unearthed from the castle ruins, which have been designated as a special historical site, as well as administrative documents from the Nara period. The Tohoku Museum of History is located next door and exhibits the results of the excavation.

hiraizumi_motsuji.name: 毛越寺（平泉）
hiraizumi_motsuji.kana: もうつうじ（ひらいずみ）
hiraizumi_motsuji.text: 毛越寺は、嘉祥3年（850年）に慈覚大師円仁が開山し、奥州藤原氏2代・基衡と3代・秀衡が大規模に造営した平安時代の大寺院です。往時は堂塔40、僧坊500を数え、中尊寺をしのぐ規模を誇ったと伝えられますが、兵火により建物はすべて焼失しました。現在は浄土庭園と伽藍遺構が特別史跡・特別名勝に指定されており、大泉が池を中心とした池泉回遊式庭園は平安時代の作庭様式を今に伝える貴重な遺構です。世界遺産「平泉の文化遺産」の構成資産のひとつで、毎年5月に行われる「曲水の宴」は平安絵巻さながらの優雅さです。
hiraizumi_motsuji.highlight: 平安の浄土庭園が奇跡的に残る世界遺産。藤原氏の栄華の跡
hiraizumi_motsuji.highlight_en: A world heritage site where the Heian Pure Land garden miraculously remains. Traces of the Fujiwara clan's prosperity
hiraizumi_motsuji.text_en: Motsuji Temple is a large Heian period temple founded by Jikaku Daishi Ennin in 850 and constructed on a large scale by Motohira, the second generation of the Oshu Fujiwara clan, and Hidehira, the third generation. It is said that in the past, it had 40 halls and pagodas and 500 monks' quarters, boasting a scale larger than Chusonji, but all of the buildings were destroyed by military fire. Currently, the Jodo garden and the remains of the temple are designated as special historical sites and special scenic spots, and the pond strolling garden, centered around Oizumigaike Pond, is a valuable remains that still conveys the garden style of the Heian period. It is one of the constituent assets of the World Heritage Site "Hiraizumi Cultural Heritage," and the "Kyokusui Banquet" held every May is as elegant as a Heian picture scroll.

aizu_tsurugajo_higashiyama.name: 会津東山温泉・会津藩校日新館
aizu_tsurugajo_higashiyama.kana: あいづひがしやまおんせん・にっしんかん
aizu_tsurugajo_higashiyama.text: 会津藩校日新館は、1803年に会津藩が設立した全国屈指の藩校です。「什の掟」に象徴される厳格な武士道教育で知られ、「ならぬことはならぬ」の精神が会津武士の魂を育てました。幕末の戊辰戦争では、日新館で学んだ若者たちが白虎隊として組織され、16〜17歳の少年たちが鶴ヶ城の炎を見て自刃するという悲劇が生まれました。東山温泉は松尾芭蕉も訪れた歴史ある温泉地で、会津の奥座敷として知られています。幕末の激動を生きた会津人の誇りと悲哀が、この地域の随所に刻まれています。
aizu_tsurugajo_higashiyama.highlight: 「ならぬことはならぬ」の会津藩校。白虎隊を育てた精神の地
aizu_tsurugajo_higashiyama.highlight_en: The Aizu clan school of ``What should happen is not allowed to happen.'' The land of the spirit that nurtured the Byakkotai
aizu_tsurugajo_higashiyama.text_en: Aizu Clan School Nisshinkan was established by the Aizu Clan in 1803 and is one of the best schools in Japan. It is known for its strict Bushido education, symbolized by the ``laws of law,'' and the spirit of ``what must be done must not be done'' nurtured the soul of the Aizu samurai. During the Boshin War at the end of the Edo period, young people who had studied at Nisshinkan were organized into the Byakkotai, and a tragedy occurred when 16 to 17-year-old boys committed suicide after seeing the flames at Tsuruga Castle. Higashiyama Onsen is a historic hot spring area that Matsuo Basho also visited, and is known as the back-room of Aizu. The pride and sorrow of the Aizu people who lived through the turbulent times at the end of the Edo period are etched throughout this region.

nihonmatsu_castle.name: 二本松城跡（霞ヶ城）
nihonmatsu_castle.kana: にほんまつじょうあと
nihonmatsu_castle.text: 二本松城は、室町時代に二本松氏が築いた山城で、伊達政宗との激戦の舞台として知られます。1586年の戦いでは伊達政宗が二本松城を攻略、城主・畠山義継を謀殺するという事件も起きました。江戸時代には丹羽光重が城を大改修し、近世城郭として整備しました。幕末の戊辰戦争では会津と並んで旧幕府方として奮戦し、14〜17歳の少年兵「二本松少年隊」が組織されました。菊人形まつりで有名な霞ヶ城公園として整備され、秋には約200体の菊人形が展示され多くの観光客を集めます。
nihonmatsu_castle.highlight: 戊辰戦争で少年兵が戦った城。菊人形で有名な霞ヶ城
nihonmatsu_castle.highlight_en: A castle where child soldiers fought during the Boshin War. Kasumigajo, famous for its chrysanthemum dolls
nihonmatsu_castle.text_en: Nihonmatsu Castle is a mountain castle built by the Nihonmatsu clan during the Muromachi period, and is known as the site of a fierce battle with Date Masamune. In the battle of 1586, Date Masamune captured Nihonmatsu Castle and assassinated the castle's lord, Yoshitsugu Hatakeyama. During the Edo period, Mitsushige Niwa extensively renovated the castle and developed it into a modern castle. During the Boshin War at the end of the Edo period, the area fought bravely alongside Aizu on the side of the former shogunate, and the ``Nihonmatsu Shonen Tai'' (child soldiers between the ages of 14 and 17) was formed. It has been developed as Kasumigajo Park, famous for its chrysanthemum doll festival, and in the fall, about 200 chrysanthemum dolls are displayed, attracting many tourists.

akita_senshu_castle.name: 秋田城跡・千秋公園
akita_senshu_castle.kana: あきたじょうあと・せんしゅうこうえん
akita_senshu_castle.text: 秋田城は、733年に設置された出羽国の国府・鎮守府として機能した古代の城柵です。蝦夷支配の拠点として奈良時代から平安時代にかけて整備され、水洗トイレの遺構が発見されたことで注目を集めました。後に佐竹義宣が関ヶ原後に常陸から移封され久保田城を築き、久保田藩（秋田藩）の拠点となりました。現在の千秋公園は久保田城の跡地で、秋田藩佐竹家の歴史を伝える博物館が整備されています。ヒメマスや比内地鶏など秋田の食文化と、なまはげなどの民俗文化の中心地として今も賑わっています。
akita_senshu_castle.highlight: 奈良時代の城柵から江戸の藩城へ。東北支配の長い歴史
akita_senshu_castle.highlight_en: From the castle fences of the Nara period to the domain castles of Edo. Long history of domination in Tohoku
akita_senshu_castle.text_en: Akita Castle is an ancient castle fence that was established in 733 and functioned as the capital and military base of Dewa Province. It was developed from the Nara period to the Heian period as a base for Ezo domination, and attracted attention when the remains of flush toilets were discovered. Later, after Sekigahara, Yoshinobu Satake was transferred from Hitachi and built Kubota Castle, which became the base of the Kubota domain (Akita domain). Today's Senshu Park is the site of Kubota Castle, and houses a museum that tells the history of the Satake family of the Akita domain. It is still a thriving center of Akita's food culture such as Himemasu and Hinai chicken, as well as folk culture such as Namahage.

yamagata_risshakuji.name: 山寺（立石寺）
yamagata_risshakuji.kana: やまでら（りっしゃくじ）
yamagata_risshakuji.text: 立石寺（山寺）は、860年に慈覚大師円仁が開山した天台宗の山岳寺院です。奇岩・奇石がそびえる山肌に堂塔が点在し、1015段の石段を登る参道は修行の道として古来多くの参拝者が訪れました。松尾芭蕉が1689年の「おくのほそ道」の旅でこの地を訪れ、「閑さや岩にしみ入る蝉の声」と詠んだ句はあまりにも有名です。山頂の五大堂からは最上川と山形盆地を一望でき、芭蕉が感じた静寂と自然の偉大さが今も変わりません。四季折々の景観が美しく、紅葉の季節には特に多くの人々が訪れます。
yamagata_risshakuji.highlight: 「閑さや岩にしみ入る蝉の声」芭蕉が詠んだ山岳霊場
yamagata_risshakuji.highlight_en: ``The silence and the voice of cicadas that penetrate the rocks'' is a sacred mountain site that Basho wrote about.
yamagata_risshakuji.text_en: Risshokuji (Mountain Temple) is a mountain temple of the Tendai sect, founded by Jikaku Daishi Ennin in 860. Temples and pagodas are dotted on the mountain surface where strangely shaped rocks and stones rise, and the approach that climbs 1015 stone steps has been visited by many worshipers since ancient times as a path for ascetic practices. Matsuo Basho visited this area on his ``Oku no Hosomichi'' trip in 1689, and is famous for his poem, ``The silence and the voice of the cicadas penetrating the rocks.'' Godaido Hall at the top of the mountain offers a panoramic view of the Mogami River and the Yamagata Basin, and the tranquility and grandeur of nature that Basho felt has not changed to this day. The scenery is beautiful in all seasons, and many people visit especially during the autumn foliage season.

morioka_castle.name: 盛岡城跡（岩手公園）
morioka_castle.text: 盛岡城は、南部藩の居城として1633年に完成した総石垣の城です。南部氏は鎌倉時代から続く名門で、戦国から江戸にかけて南部家が岩手を治め続けました。花崗岩を積み上げた石垣は「烏城」と呼ばれるほど堅固で美しく、明治以降は公園として整備されました。明治時代にはこの盛岡から原敬（日本初の本格的政党内閣総理大臣）、新渡戸稲造（「武士道」の著者）など多くの人材が輩出されました。石川啄木もこの城跡を愛し「不来方のお城の草に寝ころびて空に吸はれし十五の心」と詠みました。
morioka_castle.highlight: 石川啄木が愛した花崗岩の名城。明治の偉人を輩出した盛岡
morioka_castle.highlight_en: A famous granite castle loved by Takuboku Ishikawa. Morioka, which produced great figures of the Meiji era
morioka_castle.text_en: Morioka Castle is a castle built entirely of stone walls and was completed in 1633 as the residence of the Nanbu domain. The Nanbu clan has been a prestigious family since the Kamakura period, and continued to rule Iwate from the Sengoku period to the Edo period. The stone wall made of stacked granite is so strong and beautiful that it was nicknamed ``Crow Castle,'' and it was developed as a park after the Meiji period. During the Meiji period, Morioka produced many talented people, including Takashi Hara (Japan's first full-fledged political party prime minister) and Inazo Nitobe (author of ``Bushido''). Takuboku Ishikawa also loved this castle ruins and wrote a poem about it, saying, ``Fifteen hearts lie down in the grass of the castle of the undiscovered and are sucked into the sky.''

goryokaku.name: 五稜郭跡
goryokaku.text: 五稜郭は1866年に完成した西洋式星形要塞で、江戸幕府が北方防衛と貿易管理のために築きました。星形の形状は西洋の築城術を取り入れたもので、砲撃に強い設計です。幕末の戊辰戦争では、旧幕府軍の榎本武揚・土方歳三らがここを拠点に新政府軍と最後の戦いを繰り広げました（箱館戦争・1868〜69年）。土方歳三はこの地で討ち死にし、幕府軍最後の抵抗が終わりを告げました。現在は五稜郭公園として整備され、約1600本の桜の名所として親しまれています。五稜郭タワーから見る星形の全景は圧巻です。
goryokaku.highlight: 土方歳三最後の地。幕末最後の戦いが繰り広げられた星形要塞

transit.name: 函館市電「五稜郭公園前」

goryokaku.highlight_en: Toshizo Hijikata's last place. A star-shaped fortress where the final battle at the end of the Edo period took place.
goryokaku.text_en: Goryokaku is a Western-style star-shaped fort that was completed in 1866 and was built by the Edo shogunate for northern defense and trade control. The star-shaped shape incorporates Western castle-building techniques, and is designed to be resistant to bombardment. During the Boshin War at the end of the Edo period, former Shogunate forces such as Takeaki Enomoto and Toshizo Hijikata used this place as a base for the final battle against the new government forces (Hakodate War, 1868-69). Hijikata Toshizo was killed here, marking the end of the Shogunate's last resistance. Currently, it is maintained as Goryokaku Park and is a popular spot for viewing the approximately 1,600 cherry blossom trees. The star-shaped panorama seen from Goryokaku Tower is breathtaking.

matsumae_castle.name: 松前城・松前藩屋敷
matsumae_castle.text: 松前城は、北海道唯一の日本式城郭で、1854年に完成した天守が現存（復元）しています。松前藩は江戸時代を通じて蝦夷地（北海道）を支配した唯一の藩で、アイヌとの交易「場所請負制」によって繁栄しました。和人とアイヌの文化が交わる独特の歴史を持ち、北前船との交易で栄えた港町でもありました。幕末には函館奉行所の設置とともに北方警備の役割も担いました。城下町の松前には多くの寺院が残り、北海道の中でも独自の城下町文化を今に伝えています。
matsumae_castle.highlight: 北海道唯一の日本式城郭。アイヌとの交易で栄えた松前藩の拠点
matsumae_castle.highlight_en: The only Japanese-style castle in Hokkaido. The base of the Matsumae clan, which prospered through trade with the Ainu.
matsumae_castle.text_en: Matsumae Castle is the only Japanese-style castle in Hokkaido, and the castle tower, which was completed in 1854, still exists (restored). The Matsumae clan was the only domain that ruled Ezo (Hokkaido) throughout the Edo period, and prospered through the ``location contract system'' of trade with the Ainu. It has a unique history where Japanese and Ainu cultures intersect, and it was also a port town that prospered through trade with Kitamaebune ships. At the end of the Edo period, the Hakodate Magistrate's Office was established and it also took on the role of guarding the north. Many temples remain in the castle town of Matsumae, which still maintains Hokkaido's unique castle town culture.

otaru_canal.name: 小樽運河・小樽港
otaru_canal.text: 小樽運河は1923年に完成した全長1,140mの運河で、北海道開拓時代の経済の中心として栄えた小樽の歴史を象徴しています。明治時代に北海道開発の物流拠点として整備された小樽港は、石炭・海産物・木材の積み出し港として本州と北海道を結ぶ大動脈でした。運河沿いには石造倉庫が並び、夜はガス灯の温かい光に照らされてロマンチックな景観を醸し出しています。運河の保存運動は市民主導で行われ、全国の歴史的街並み保存のモデルケースとなりました。
otaru_canal.highlight: 北海道開拓の物流拠点。石造倉庫が並ぶ明治ロマンの運河
otaru_canal.highlight_en: Logistics base for Hokkaido development. Meiji romantic canal lined with stone warehouses
otaru_canal.text_en: The Otaru Canal is a 1,140m long canal that was completed in 1923 and symbolizes the history of Otaru, which flourished as the economic center of Hokkaido's pioneering era. Established during the Meiji era as a logistics base for the development of Hokkaido, Otaru Port was a major artery connecting Honshu and Hokkaido, serving as a shipping port for coal, marine products, and lumber. Stone warehouses line the canal, and at night they are illuminated by the warm light of gas lamps, creating a romantic landscape. The canal preservation movement was led by citizens and became a model case for the preservation of historic townscapes across the country.

sapporo_clock_tower.name: 札幌時計台・北海道開拓の村
sapporo_clock_tower.text: 札幌時計台（旧札幌農学校演武場）は1878年に建設された北海道開拓の象徴的建物です。クラーク博士「Boys be ambitious!」の精神のもと設立された札幌農学校は、北海道の農業・教育・産業の近代化を担いました。新渡戸稲造・内村鑑三ら多くの人材を輩出し、北海道のみならず日本の近代化に大きく貢献しました。郊外の北海道開拓の村には明治・大正時代の建造物52棟が移築・復元され、開拓時代の暮らしを体感できます。現在も時計台は現役で稼働し、毎正時に鐘が鳴り響きます。
sapporo_clock_tower.highlight: クラーク博士の夢が宿る開拓の象徴。明治の北海道を体感する地
sapporo_clock_tower.highlight_en: A symbol of pioneering where Dr. Clark's dreams dwell. A place to experience Meiji Hokkaido
sapporo_clock_tower.text_en: The Sapporo Clock Tower (formerly the Sapporo Agricultural School Demonstration Hall) is a symbolic building built in 1878 and is a symbol of Hokkaido's development. Sapporo Agricultural College, founded under the spirit of Dr. Clark's ``Boys be ambitious!'', was responsible for modernizing Hokkaido's agriculture, education, and industry. It produced many talented people such as Nitobe Inazo and Uchimura Kanzo, and greatly contributed to the modernization of not only Hokkaido but also Japan. In the suburban Hokkaido pioneer village, 52 buildings from the Meiji and Taisho eras have been relocated and restored, allowing you to experience life in the pioneer era. The clock tower is still in operation today, and the bell rings every hour on the hour.

noboribetsu_ainu.name: ウポポイ（民族共生象徴空間）
noboribetsu_ainu.text: ウポポイは2020年に開業したアイヌ文化の復興・発展の拠点です。白老町のポロト湖畔に設けられ、国立アイヌ民族博物館を核として、アイヌの歴史・文化・言語を世界に発信しています。アイヌは北海道・樺太・千島に住む先住民族で、独自の言語・信仰・食文化・工芸を持ちます。和人との交易・対立・同化政策の歴史を経て、近年ようやく先住民族としての権利が認められました。チセ（伝統家屋）の復元や伝統芸能の実演が行われ、カムイ（神）とともに生きる世界観を体験できます。
noboribetsu_ainu.highlight: アイヌ文化の国立拠点。先住民族の知恵と美しさを今に伝える
noboribetsu_ainu.highlight_en: National base of Ainu culture. Conveying the wisdom and beauty of indigenous peoples to the present day
noboribetsu_ainu.text_en: Upopoy is a base for the restoration and development of Ainu culture that opened in 2020. Established on the shores of Lake Poroto in Shiraoi Town, the National Ainu Museum is the core of the museum, which disseminates the history, culture, and language of the Ainu to the world. The Ainu are an indigenous people living in Hokkaido, Sakhalin, and the Kuril Islands, and have their own language, beliefs, food culture, and crafts. After a history of trade, conflict, and assimilation policies with the Japanese people, their rights as indigenous peoples have finally been recognized in recent years. There will be restorations of chise (traditional houses) and demonstrations of traditional performing arts, allowing you to experience the world of living with kamuy (gods).

abashiri_prison.name: 博物館網走監獄
abashiri_prison.kana: はくぶつかんあばしりかんごく
abashiri_prison.text: 網走監獄は1890年に設置された、北海道開拓の最前線を担った刑務所です。明治政府は北海道の道路建設・農地開墾のために全国から囚人を送り込み、過酷な環境下での強制労働を行いました。旭川〜網走間144kmの「中央道路」はわずか8ヶ月で完成しましたが、多くの囚人が命を落としました。現在は博物館として整備され、明治時代の木造監獄建築8棟が国の重要文化財に指定されています。北海道開拓の「光と影」を伝える歴史施設として、年間30万人以上が訪れます。
abashiri_prison.highlight: 開拓を支えた囚人たちの歴史。北海道近代史の光と影
abashiri_prison.highlight_en: The history of the prisoners who supported the development. Light and shadow of modern Hokkaido history
abashiri_prison.text_en: Abashiri Prison was established in 1890 and was at the forefront of the development of Hokkaido. The Meiji government sent prisoners from all over the country to work on Hokkaido's road construction and farmland cultivation, and they were forced to work under harsh conditions. The 144km Chuo Road between Asahikawa and Abashiri was completed in just eight months, but many prisoners lost their lives. Currently, it is maintained as a museum, and eight of the wooden prison buildings from the Meiji era have been designated as important cultural properties of the country. As a historical facility that conveys the "light and shadow" of Hokkaido's development, more than 300,000 people visit each year.

hakodate_bugyosho.name: 箱館奉行所跡・元町
hakodate_bugyosho.kana: はこだてぶぎょうしょあと
hakodate_bugyosho.text: 箱館（函館）は1854年の日米和親条約により下田とともに開港した日本最初の開港地のひとつです。箱館奉行所は幕府が北方警備と対外交渉のために設置した機関で、五稜郭内に復元された建物が公開されています。元町の外国人居留地には当時の洋館・教会・領事館が今も残り、和洋折衷の独特の街並みを形成しています。ロシア正教会・カトリック教会・プロテスタント教会が並ぶ丘は「函館の教会群」として知られ、夜景とともに函館の象徴的風景となっています。
hakodate_bugyosho.highlight: 日本初の開港地。洋館と教会が並ぶ幕末開国の舞台
hakodate_bugyosho.highlight_en: Japan's first port to open. The stage for the opening of the country at the end of the Edo period, lined with Western-style buildings and churches
hakodate_bugyosho.text_en: Hakodate (Hakodate) was one of the first ports in Japan to open, along with Shimoda, in accordance with the Treaty of Peace and Amity between the United States and Japan in 1854. The Hakodate Magistrate's Office is an institution established by the Shogunate for the purpose of guarding the north and conducting foreign negotiations, and the restored building within Goryokaku is open to the public. Western-style buildings, churches, and consulates from that time still remain in the foreign settlement of Motomachi, creating a unique streetscape that blends Japanese and Western styles. The hill where Russian Orthodox, Catholic, and Protestant churches are lined up is known as the ``Hakodate Church Group,'' and together with the night view, it has become a symbolic landscape of Hakodate.

esashi_oiwake.name: 江差・いにしえ街道
esashi_oiwake.kana: えさし・いにしえかいどう
esashi_oiwake.text: 江差は江戸時代にニシン漁と北前船交易で栄えた北海道最古の港町のひとつです。「江差の五月は江戸にもない」と称えられるほど繁栄し、全国から商人・船乗りが集まりました。江差追分は船乗りたちの哀愁を歌った民謡で、全国民謡の中でも最も美しいとも言われます。いにしえ街道には江戸時代の商家・蔵が保存され、国の重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に選定されています。幕末には開陽丸がこの沖で嵐により沈没し、榎本武揚の蝦夷共和国構想にも影を落としました。
esashi_oiwake.highlight: ニシン景気で栄えた北前船の湊。江差追分が生まれた北の港町
esashi_oiwake.highlight_en: The Kitamaebune port flourished due to the herring economy. The northern port town where Esashi Oiwake was born
esashi_oiwake.text_en: Esashi is one of Hokkaido's oldest port towns, flourishing in the Edo period with herring fishing and Kitamaebune trade. It was so prosperous that it was praised as ``Esashi's May is not even in Edo,'' and merchants and sailors gathered from all over the country. Esashi Oiwake is a folk song about the melancholy of sailors, and is said to be the most beautiful of all folk songs. Edo-era merchant houses and storehouses are preserved along Inishie Kaido, and it has been selected as a nationally important preservation district for groups of traditional buildings. At the end of the Edo period, the Kaiyo Maru sank in a storm off this coast, casting a shadow on Takeaki Enomoto's idea of ​​an Ezo Republic.

tokachi_pioneer_village.name: 晩成社入植地・依田勉三記念館
tokachi_pioneer_village.kana: ばんせいしゃにゅうしょくち
tokachi_pioneer_village.text: 1883年、依田勉三は仲間27人と「晩成社」を設立し、十勝の原野に入植しました。当時の十勝は開拓がほとんど進んでいない手つかずの大地で、極寒・食糧難・疫病との過酷な戦いが続きました。依田は「晩成社」の名の通り「大器晩成」を信じ、失敗を重ねながらも大豆・小麦・バターなどの農業を切り開きました。十勝が今日「日本の食料基地」と呼ばれる農業地帯になった礎を築いた先人の苦闘の地として、帯広市に記念碑と展示施設が残されています。
tokachi_pioneer_village.highlight: 「晩成社」が切り拓いた十勝の大地。日本の食料基地の原点
tokachi_pioneer_village.highlight_en: The land of Tokachi was carved out by Banseisha. The origin of Japan's food base
tokachi_pioneer_village.text_en: In 1883, Benzo Yoda established Banseisha with 27 friends and settled in the wilderness of Tokachi. At that time, Tokachi was an untouched land with little development, and the area continued to struggle with extreme cold, food shortages, and epidemics. As the name ``Banseisha'' suggests, Yoda believed in ``great late blooming,'' and despite repeated failures, he pioneered the cultivation of soybeans, wheat, butter, and other crops. A monument and exhibition facility remain in Obihiro City, commemorating the struggle of our ancestors who laid the foundations for Tokachi to become the agricultural region known today as ``Japan's food base.''

shiraoi_ainu_kotan.name: 白老・アイヌ民族資料館（旧ポロトコタン）
shiraoi_ainu_kotan.kana: しらおい・あいぬみんぞくしりょうかん
shiraoi_ainu_kotan.text: 白老は古来よりアイヌ民族が暮らす聖地で、ポロト湖周辺には縄文時代からの居住の痕跡が残ります。江戸時代には松前藩の「白老場所」として和人との交易が行われ、アイヌの生活は徐々に変化していきました。19世紀の同化政策によりアイヌの文化・言語は急速に失われましたが、近年の文化復興運動により伝統が再び輝きを取り戻しています。2020年に開業したウポポイ（民族共生象徴空間）の隣接地として、アイヌ文化体験の拠点となっています。カムイと自然への深い敬意を持つアイヌの世界観は、現代にも多くの示唆を与えます。
shiraoi_ainu_kotan.highlight: 縄文から続くアイヌの聖地。先住民族文化の継承と復興の地
shiraoi_ainu_kotan.highlight_en: A sacred place for the Ainu people since the Jomon period. A place for the inheritance and restoration of indigenous culture
shiraoi_ainu_kotan.text_en: Shiraoi has been a sacred place where the Ainu people have lived since ancient times, and the area around Lake Poroto has traces of habitation from the Jomon period. During the Edo period, the Ainu people's lives gradually changed as the Matsumae clan's Shiraoi area was used for trade with Japanese people. The Ainu culture and language were rapidly lost due to the assimilation policies of the 19th century, but the tradition has regained its luster due to recent cultural revival movements. It is adjacent to Upopoi (a symbolic space for ethnic coexistence), which opened in 2020, and has become a base for experiencing Ainu culture. The Ainu worldview, with its deep respect for kamuy and nature, has many implications for modern times.

kamakura_engakuji.name: 円覚寺（鎌倉）
kamakura_engakuji.text: 円覚寺は1282年、北条時宗が元寇の戦没者を弔うために創建した臨済宗の大寺院です。宋から招いた無学祖元を開山とし、鎌倉五山第二位に列せられました。時宗は二度にわたる元の来襲（文永・弘安の役）を退けた執権で、国家の危機を仏の力で乗り越えようとしたのです。境内の舎利殿は国宝で、鎌倉時代の禅宗建築を代表する貴重な遺構です。夏目漱石・島崎藤村・三島由紀夫なども参禅した歴史があり、近代文学との縁も深い寺院です。
kamakura_engakuji.highlight: 元寇の英雄・北条時宗が創建した鎌倉五山第二位の禅寺
kamakura_engakuji.highlight_en: Founded by the Mongol invasion hero Tokimune Hojo, it is the second-ranked Zen temple in Kamakura's Gozan.
kamakura_engakuji.text_en: Engakuji Temple is a large temple of the Rinzai sect, founded in 1282 by Hojo Tokimune to mourn the dead of the Mongol invasion. It was founded by Mugaku Sogen, who was invited from the Song Dynasty, and was ranked as the second-ranked Kamakura Five Mountains. Tokimune was the regent who defeated two Yuan invasions (Bun'ei and Koan eras), and tried to overcome the national crisis with the power of Buddha. The Shariden in the precincts is a national treasure and is a valuable relic that represents Zen architecture from the Kamakura period. The temple has a history of Zen meditation by Natsume Soseki, Shimazaki Toson, Mishima Yukio, and others, and has a deep connection with modern literature.

odawara_hojo_ruins.name: 小田原城・北条氏政墓所
odawara_hojo_ruins.text: 小田原城は後北条氏（北条早雲が興した戦国大名）の本拠で、100年以上にわたって関東に覇を唱えた名城です。戦国最大規模の総構（そうがまえ）と呼ばれる外郭は全長9kmに及び、城下町ごと城壁で囲む独特の防衛方式でした。1590年、豊臣秀吉は22万の大軍で小田原を包囲し、約100日の籠城戦の末に北条氏は降伏。北条氏政・氏照は切腹し、戦国時代の覇者北条氏は滅亡しました。現在の天守は1960年に復元されたもので、北条氏の歴史資料を展示しています。
odawara_hojo_ruins.highlight: 後北条氏100年の本拠。秀吉の小田原攻めで戦国の幕が下りた城
odawara_hojo_ruins.highlight_en: The home of the Gohojo clan for 100 years. The castle where the Sengoku period ended with Hideyoshi's attack on Odawara
odawara_hojo_ruins.text_en: Odawara Castle is the stronghold of the Gohojo clan (a Sengoku feudal lord founded by Hojo Soun), and is a famous castle that claimed dominance over the Kanto region for over 100 years. The outer wall, called Souga-mae, was the largest in the Sengoku period and was 9 km long, and had a unique defense system in which the entire castle town was surrounded by a wall. In 1590, Toyotomi Hideyoshi besieged Odawara with a large army of 220,000 men, and the Hojo clan surrendered after about 100 days of battle. Ujimasa Hojo and Ujiteru committed seppuku, and the Hojo clan, the rulers of the Sengoku period, fell into ruin. The current castle tower was restored in 1960 and displays historical materials of the Hojo clan.

nikko_shinkyo.name: 日光・神橋と二社一寺
nikko_shinkyo.kana: にっこう・しんきょう
nikko_shinkyo.text: 日光は8世紀に勝道上人が開山した山岳信仰の聖地で、神橋・日光東照宮・日光二荒山神社・輪王寺が世界遺産「日光の社寺」を構成しています。神橋は日光山への入口に架かる朱塗りの橋で、日本三名橋のひとつ。江戸時代には将軍の参詣道として整備され、日光街道は五街道のひとつとして栄えました。杉並木が続く日光街道は今も往時の面影を残し、日本最長の並木道として国の特別史跡・特別天然記念物に指定されています。
nikko_shinkyo.highlight: 世界遺産の山岳霊場への入口。江戸五街道が行き着く聖地
nikko_shinkyo.name_en: Nikko/Shinkyo and two shrines and one temple
nikko_shinkyo.highlight_en: Entrance to a world heritage mountain sacred site. A sacred place where the five roads of Edo reach
nikko_shinkyo.text_en: Nikko is a sacred place for mountain worship founded by Shodo Shonin in the 8th century, and Shinkyo Bridge, Nikko Toshogu Shrine, Nikko Futarasan Shrine, and Rinnoji Temple make up the World Heritage Site ``Shrines and Temples of Nikko.'' Shinkyo Bridge is a vermilion-lacquered bridge that spans the entrance to Mt. Nikko, and is one of Japan's three famous bridges. During the Edo period, it was developed as a pilgrimage route for the shogun, and Nikko Kaido flourished as one of the Five Great Highways. Nikko Kaido, lined with cedar trees, still retains the vestiges of the past, and is Japan's longest tree-lined avenue and has been designated as a national special historic site and special natural monument.

ueno_kaneiji.name: 上野・寛永寺と東叡山
ueno_kaneiji.text: 寛永寺は1625年、天台宗の僧・天海が江戸城の鬼門鎮護のために創建した大寺院です。比叡山（東叡山）になぞらえて「東叡山」と称され、徳川将軍家の菩提寺として絶大な権威を持ちました。境内はかつて現在の上野公園全体に及ぶ広大なもので、六代〜十五代将軍のうち六人がここに葬られています。幕末の戊辰戦争では彰義隊が上野の山に立て籠もり、新政府軍と激突した「上野戦争」の舞台となりました。現在の上野公園には博物館・動物園・美術館が立ち並び、文化の中心地となっています。
ueno_kaneiji.highlight: 徳川家の菩提寺。幕末の上野戦争で彰義隊が散った地
ueno_kaneiji.highlight_en: The Tokugawa family's family temple. The place where Shogitai was scattered during the Ueno War at the end of the Edo period
ueno_kaneiji.text_en: Kan'eiji Temple is a large temple built in 1625 by Tenkai, a monk of the Tendai sect, to protect the demons of Edo Castle. It was called ``Higashieizan'' after comparing it to Mt. Hiei (Higashieizan), and had great authority as the family temple of the Tokugawa shogunate. The precincts were once as vast as the entirety of present-day Ueno Park, and six of the 6th to 15th shoguns are buried here. During the Boshin War at the end of the Edo period, the Shogitai barricaded themselves in the mountains of Ueno and clashed with the new government forces, which became the stage for the Ueno War. Currently, Ueno Park is lined with museums, zoos, and art galleries, and has become a cultural center.

edo_shimbashi_tokaido.name: 新橋・東海道の起点
edo_shimbashi_tokaido.kana: しんばし・とうかいどうのきてん
edo_shimbashi_tokaido.text: 日本橋は1603年に架けられた東海道・中山道など五街道の起点となった橋です。江戸時代の日本橋周辺は全国の物流・商業の中心地で、魚河岸（現在の築地の前身）や問屋街が集中し「天下の台所」を支える商業都市の核でした。隣接する新橋は1872年に日本初の鉄道（新橋〜横浜）の起点となり、近代日本の交通革命の出発点となりました。日本橋に刻まれた「道路元標」は今も日本の道路距離の基点であり、江戸から続く歴史の重みを現代に伝えています。
edo_shimbashi_tokaido.highlight: 五街道の起点・日本橋。日本初の鉄道も走り出した交通の原点
edo_shimbashi_tokaido.highlight_en: Nihonbashi, the starting point of the Five Highways. The origin of transportation, where Japan's first railway began running
edo_shimbashi_tokaido.text_en: Nihonbashi is a bridge that was built in 1603 and served as the starting point for five major roads, including the Tokaido and Nakasendo. During the Edo period, the area around Nihonbashi was the nation's distribution and commercial center, with a concentration of Uogashi (predecessor of today's Tsukiji) and wholesale shops, and was the core of the commercial city that supported the ``nation's kitchen.'' The adjacent Shinbashi became the starting point of Japan's first railway (Shinbashi - Yokohama) in 1872, and became the starting point of modern Japan's transportation revolution. The ``road marker'' engraved on Nihonbashi is still the reference point for measuring road distances in Japan, and conveys the weight of the history that continued from Edo to the present day.

kamakura_kenchoji.name: 建長寺（鎌倉）
kamakura_kenchoji.text: 建長寺は1253年、北条時頼が宋から招いた蘭渓道隆を開山として創建した日本最初の禅道場です。鎌倉五山第一位に列せられ、禅宗を武家社会に広めた最重要の寺院です。中国・南宋の様式を取り入れた伽藍配置は当時の人々に衝撃を与え、禅宗建築の源流となりました。境内の梵鐘は国宝で、鎌倉時代の鋳造技術の粋を示しています。北条氏の滅亡後も足利・徳川幕府の庇護を受け、今日まで禅宗の道場として厳格な修行が続けられています。
kamakura_kenchoji.highlight: 日本初の禅道場・鎌倉五山筆頭。禅宗が武家に広まった聖地
kamakura_kenchoji.highlight_en: Head of Kamakura Gozan, Japan's first Zen dojo. Sacred place where Zen Buddhism spread to samurai families
kamakura_kenchoji.text_en: Kencho-ji Temple was founded in 1253 by Hojo Tokiyori, who invited Doryu Rankei from the Song Dynasty to open the temple, and it was Japan's first Zen dojo. It is ranked as the first of Kamakura's five temples and is the most important temple that spread Zen Buddhism to samurai society. The layout of the temple, which adopted the style of the Southern Song Dynasty in China, shocked the people of the time and became the origin of Zen Buddhism architecture. The temple bell in the temple grounds is a national treasure and shows the best of the casting techniques of the Kamakura period. Even after the fall of the Hojo clan, it received the patronage of the Ashikaga and Tokugawa shogunate, and continues to conduct rigorous training as a Zen dojo to this day.

edo_ryogoku_ edo_museum.name: 両国・江戸東京博物館
edo_ryogoku_ edo_museum.kana: りょうごく・えどとうきょうはくぶつかん
edo_ryogoku_ edo_museum.text: 両国は江戸時代の盛り場として栄えた地区で、回向院・両国橋・相撲などの文化が花開きました。両国橋は1659年に架けられた隅田川最大の橋で、花火や見世物など江戸の娯楽の中心でした。回向院は1657年の明暦の大火の犠牲者を供養するために建てられた寺院で、大相撲の発祥の地でもあります。江戸東京博物館（現在改修中）には江戸城の縮小模型や当時の町並みの復元展示があり、260年の江戸文化を体感できます。徳川の平和が育んだ庶民文化の結晶がここに集まっています。
edo_ryogoku_ edo_museum.highlight: 明暦の大火の記憶と江戸の盛り場文化。相撲発祥の地・両国
edo_ryogoku_ edo_museum.highlight_en: Memories of the Great Fire of Meireki and the culture of Edo entertainment venues. Ryogoku, the birthplace of sumo
edo_ryogoku_ edo_museum.text_en: Ryogoku was a prosperous area during the Edo period, where culture such as Ekoin Temple, Ryogoku Bridge, and sumo wrestling flourished. Built in 1659, Ryogoku Bridge is the largest bridge over the Sumida River, and was the center of Edo entertainment such as fireworks and spectacles. Ekoin is a temple built to commemorate the victims of the Great Meireki Fire of 1657, and is also the birthplace of sumo wrestling. The Edo-Tokyo Museum (currently under renovation) has a scale model of Edo Castle and a restored display of the townscape from that time, allowing you to experience 260 years of Edo culture. The crystallization of common people's culture nurtured by Tokugawa's peace is gathered here.

hachioji_castle_ruins.name: 八王子城跡
hachioji_castle_ruins.kana: はちおうじじょうあと
hachioji_castle_ruins.text: 八王子城は後北条氏の重臣・北条氏照が1571年頃に築いた山城です。当時の関東最大規模の山城で、本丸は標高445mの山頂に置かれた堅固な城でした。1590年の豊臣秀吉による小田原攻めの際、前田利家・上杉景勝の軍勢数万に攻められ、わずか半日で落城。城内に逃れた多くの女性・子供が氏照の妻を先頭に城山川に身を投げたと伝えられます。現在は国の史跡に指定され、豊かな自然の中に石垣・虎口などの遺構が残る関東屈指の山城跡です。
hachioji_castle_ruins.highlight: 小田原攻めで一日で落城。北条の女たちが身を投げた悲劇の山城
hachioji_castle_ruins.highlight_en: The castle fell in one day during the attack on Odawara. The tragic mountain castle where the women of Hojo threw themselves
hachioji_castle_ruins.text_en: Hachioji Castle is a mountain castle built around 1571 by Ujiteru Hojo, a senior vassal of the Gohojo clan. It was the largest mountain castle in the Kanto region at the time, and the main castle was a strong castle located on the top of a mountain at an altitude of 445 meters. When Toyotomi Hideyoshi attacked Odawara in 1590, the castle was attacked by tens of thousands of troops led by Toshiie Maeda and Kagekatsu Uesugi, and the castle fell in just half a day. It is said that many women and children who fled into the castle threw themselves into the Shiroyama River, with Ujiteru's wife leading the way. Currently designated as a national historic site, it is one of the best mountain castle ruins in the Kanto region, with remains of stone walls, tiger mouths, and other structures surrounded by rich nature.

kawagoe_little_edo.name: 川越・蔵造りの町並み
kawagoe_little_edo.kana: かわごえ・くらづくりのまちなみ
kawagoe_little_edo.text: 川越は江戸時代に「小江戸」と呼ばれた城下町で、江戸の北の守りとして重要な役割を果たしました。1893年の大火の後、類焼を防ぐために蔵造りの商家が建てられ、今も一番街に30棟以上が残ります。時の鐘（寛永年間建立）は今も1日4回鐘を鳴らし、川越のシンボルとして親しまれています。喜多院は徳川家光が誕生したとも伝わる由緒ある寺院で、江戸城の書院・客殿が移築されています。菓子屋横丁では昔ながらの駄菓子屋が軒を連ね、レトロな街並みに多くの観光客が訪れます。
kawagoe_little_edo.highlight: 江戸北の守り「小江戸」。蔵造りの町並みと時の鐘が残る城下町
kawagoe_little_edo.highlight_en: “Little Edo” is the protection of northern Edo. A castle town with a warehouse-style townscape and a bell of time.
kawagoe_little_edo.text_en: Kawagoe was a castle town called "Little Edo" during the Edo period, and played an important role as the northern defense of Edo. After the great fire of 1893, warehouse-style merchant houses were built to prevent similar fires, and more than 30 of them still remain on Ichibangai. The Bell of Time (erected in the Kanei era) still rings four times a day and is a familiar symbol of Kawagoe. Kita-in is a historic temple where it is said that Tokugawa Iemitsu was born, and the study hall and reception hall from Edo Castle were relocated there. Kashiya Yokocho is lined with old-fashioned candy shops, and many tourists visit the retro streetscape.

yokohama_foreign_settlement.name: 横浜山手・外国人居留地跡
yokohama_foreign_settlement.text: 横浜は1859年の開港以来、日本の近代化を牽引した国際都市です。山手（ブラフ）地区には英・米・仏など各国の外国人が居留し、西洋文化の窓口として機能しました。現存する外国人墓地・山手西洋館・山手聖公会などが当時の国際的雰囲気を今に伝えます。関内・中華街は日本最大の中華街として発展し、横浜独自の文化を形成しています。明治時代の横浜では野球・競馬・アイスクリームなど多くの西洋文化が日本に初めて紹介され、文明開化の玄関口として日本の近代史を彩りました。
yokohama_foreign_settlement.highlight: 文明開化の玄関口。西洋文化が上陸した開港横浜の山手
yokohama_foreign_settlement.highlight_en: The gateway to civilization and enlightenment. Yamate in Yokohama, the port where Western culture landed
yokohama_foreign_settlement.text_en: Since its opening in 1859, Yokohama has been an international city that has led Japan's modernization. The Yamate (Bluff) area was home to foreigners from Britain, America, France, and other countries, and served as a gateway to Western culture. Existing foreign cemetery, Yamate Western House, Yamate Episcopal Church, etc. still convey the international atmosphere of the time. Kannai Chinatown has developed into Japan's largest Chinatown, forming a unique culture of Yokohama. Many Western cultures such as baseball, horse racing, and ice cream were introduced to Japan for the first time in Yokohama during the Meiji era, and the city became a gateway to civilization and enlightenment, coloring Japan's modern history.

omi_hachiman_town.name: 近江八幡・八幡堀
omi_hachiman_town.kana: おうみはちまん・はちまんぼり
omi_hachiman_town.text: 近江八幡は1585年、豊臣秀次（秀吉の甥）が八幡山城を築いて城下町を開いた商業都市です。八幡堀は琵琶湖と城下町を結ぶ運河で、全国から船荷が集まる物流の要衝でした。ここで育った「近江商人」は「三方よし（売り手よし・買い手よし・世間よし）」の精神のもと全国を行商し、伊藤忠・西武・高島屋など現代の大企業の祖先となりました。白雲館や旧西川家住宅など当時の商家が残る町並みは重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に選定されています。
omi_hachiman_town.highlight: 「三方よし」近江商人の本拠地。八幡堀が結ぶ水辺の商都
omi_hachiman_town.highlight_en: "Sampo Yoshi" is the home base of Omi merchants. A waterside commercial town connected by Hachimanbori
omi_hachiman_town.text_en: Omihachiman is a commercial city where Toyotomi Hidetsugu (Hideyoshi's nephew) built Hachimanyama Castle and opened a castle town in 1585. Hachimanbori is a canal that connects Lake Biwa and the castle town, and was a key logistics hub for shipping cargo from all over the country. The ``Omi merchants'' who grew up here sold their goods all over the country based on the spirit of ``Sampo Yoshi'' (good for the seller, good for the buyer, and good for society), and became the ancestors of today's large companies such as Itochu, Seibu, and Takashimaya. The townscape where merchant houses from that time remain, such as Hakuunkan and the former Nishikawa family residence, has been selected as an important preservation district for groups of traditional buildings.

kyoto_fushimi_castle.name: 伏見城跡・桃山御陵
kyoto_fushimi_castle.text: 伏見城（桃山城）は豊臣秀吉が1592年に建築を始めた壮大な居城です。秀吉はここで晩年を過ごし1598年に没しました。翌1600年の関ヶ原の戦いの前哨戦として「伏見城の戦い」が起こり、鳥居元忠率いる徳川方1,800人が石田三成ら4万の西軍に奮戦して全滅しました。床板の血染めは「血天井」として京都各所の寺院に残されています。桃山時代（安土桃山時代）の名称はこの地（桃山）に由来し、絢爛豪華な文化が花開いた時代を象徴しています。現在は明治天皇陵が置かれ、付近に伏見桃山城（模擬天守）が建ちます。
kyoto_fushimi_castle.highlight: 秀吉終焉の地。関ヶ原前哨戦「血天井」が残る桃山文化の城
kyoto_fushimi_castle.highlight_en: The place where Hideyoshi ended his life. A castle of Momoyama culture where the “blood ceiling” of the Sekigahara pre-war remains.
kyoto_fushimi_castle.text_en: Fushimi Castle (Momoyama Castle) is a magnificent castle built by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1592. Hideyoshi spent his later years here and died in 1598. The following year, in 1600, the Battle of Fushimi Castle took place as a prelude to the Battle of Sekigahara, in which 1,800 Tokugawa troops led by Mototada Torii fought hard against Mitsunari Ishida and 40,000 Western troops and were annihilated. Blood stains on the floorboards remain as ``blood ceilings'' in temples throughout Kyoto. The name Momoyama period (Azuchi-Momoyama period) comes from this place (Momoyama) and symbolizes the era when a gorgeous and luxurious culture flourished. Currently, the Meiji Emperor's tomb is located here, and Fushimi-Momoyama Castle (a mock castle tower) is built nearby.

osaka_tennoji_shitenoji.name: 天王寺・四天王寺周辺
osaka_tennoji_shitenoji.kana: てんのうじ・してんのうじ
osaka_tennoji_shitenoji.text: 四天王寺は593年に聖徳太子が建立した日本最古の官寺のひとつです。太子は物部守屋との戦いに際し「勝利の暁には四天王を祀る寺を建てる」と誓願し、勝利後にこの寺を創建しました。当初の伽藍配置（四天王寺式）は朝鮮半島から伝わった様式で、日本の寺院建築の原型となりました。隣接する天王寺公園（慶沢園）や茶臼山古戦場（大坂冬の陣・夏の陣の古戦場）など歴史の層が重なる地域です。大阪最古の歴史を持つこのエリアは、日本仏教の黎明期を今に伝えています。
osaka_tennoji_shitenoji.highlight: 聖徳太子が建立した日本最古の官寺。大阪の仏教の原点

transit.name: 地下鉄「四天王寺前夕陽ヶ丘」

osaka_tennoji_shitenoji.highlight_en: Japan's oldest official temple built by Prince Shotoku. The origin of Buddhism in Osaka
osaka_tennoji_shitenoji.text_en: Shitennoji is one of the oldest official temples in Japan, built in 593 by Prince Shotoku. At the time of the battle with Moriya Mononobe, the prince vowed, ``When I am victorious, I will build a temple to enshrine the Four Heavenly Kings,'' and he built this temple after his victory. The original layout of the temple (Shitennoji style) was a style introduced from the Korean Peninsula and became the prototype for Japanese temple architecture. It is an area with many layers of history, including the adjacent Tennoji Park (Keitakuen) and the Chausuyama Battlefield (Osaka's Winter and Summer Battlefields). This area, which has the oldest history in Osaka, still tells the story of the dawn of Japanese Buddhism.

kyoto_nijo_ninomaru.name: 二条城・二の丸御殿
kyoto_nijo_ninomaru.kana: にじょうじょう・にのまるごてん
kyoto_nijo_ninomaru.text: 二条城は1603年、徳川家康が京都御所の守護と将軍上洛の際の宿館として建築した城です。二の丸御殿は国宝に指定された唯一の城御殿建築で、狩野派による金地障壁画と「鳴き龍」と呼ばれる音響現象で知られます。1867年、15代将軍・徳川慶喜がここで「大政奉還」を宣言し、265年続いた江戸幕府が終焉を迎えました。幕府の開始（家康入城）と終焉（慶喜の大政奉還）の両方がここで行われた、日本近世史の始まりと終わりを刻む特別な城です。
kyoto_nijo_ninomaru.highlight: 幕府誕生と大政奉還の舞台。江戸265年の始まりと終わりを刻む城

transit.name: 地下鉄東西線「二条城前」

kyoto_nijo_ninomaru.highlight_en: The stage for the birth of the shogunate and the restoration of imperial rule. A castle marking the beginning and end of 265 years of Edo
kyoto_nijo_ninomaru.text_en: Nijo Castle was built in 1603 by Tokugawa Ieyasu to protect the Kyoto Imperial Palace and to serve as an inn for the shogun's visit to Kyoto. Ninomaru Palace is the only castle palace designated as a national treasure, and is known for its gold wall paintings by the Kano school and the acoustic phenomenon called ``Nakiryu.'' In 1867, the 15th shogun, Yoshinobu Tokugawa, declared the restoration of imperial rule here, marking the end of the 265-year-old Edo Shogunate. This is a special castle that marks the beginning and end of Japan's early modern history, as both the beginning (Ieyasu entered the castle) and the end (Yoshinobu's restoration of the imperial government) of the shogunate took place here.

himeji_kofun_area.name: 白鷺城・姫路城西の丸
himeji_kofun_area.kana: はくろじょう・にしのまる
himeji_kofun_area.text: 姫路城は「白鷺城」の別称を持つ世界遺産・国宝で、現存する日本最大の木造城郭建築です。1601年から9年をかけて池田輝政が大改築し、今に見る白漆喰の壮麗な姿が完成しました。西の丸には千姫ゆかりの百間廊下が残り、二代将軍秀忠の娘・千姫が本多忠刻と再婚してここで暮らした歴史が刻まれています。第二次世界大戦の空襲では周囲が焼け野原になる中、奇跡的に焼失を免れました。大天守の修復工事（平成の大修理）を経て、白く輝く美しさを取り戻しています。
himeji_kofun_area.highlight: 現存最大の木造城郭・世界遺産。千姫も暮らした白鷺城の全貌
himeji_kofun_area.highlight_en: The largest existing wooden castle and a world heritage site. The whole story of Shirasagi Castle where Princess Sen also lived
himeji_kofun_area.text_en: Himeji Castle, also known as "White Heron Castle," is a World Heritage Site and National Treasure, and is the largest existing wooden castle in Japan. Starting in 1601, Terumasa Ikeda underwent a major renovation over a period of nine years, creating the magnificent white plaster structure that we see today. In the Nishinomaru, a Hyakken Corridor connected to Senhime remains, and the history of Senhime, the daughter of the second shogun Hidetada, remarried Honda Tadatoki and lived here. Miraculously, it escaped destruction during the air raids of World War II, while the surrounding area was reduced to ashes. After undergoing restoration work on the main tower (Major Repairs of the Heisei Period), it has regained its shining white beauty.

nara_heijokyo.name: 平城宮跡（奈良の都）
nara_heijokyo.kana: へいじょうきゅうあと
nara_heijokyo.text: 平城京は710年に元明天皇が藤原京から遷都した奈良時代の都です。唐の長安を模した碁盤目状の都市は東西4.3km・南北4.8kmの規模を誇り、当時の人口は10万人以上に達したと推定されています。平城宮は都の北部中央に置かれた天皇の宮殿・政府庁舎で、奈良時代の政治の中枢でした。大仏建立・遣唐使・万葉集編纂など、日本文化の基礎が築かれたのがこの時代です。現在は特別史跡として発掘調査が続けられ、朱雀門・大極殿などが復原され往時の壮観を偲ぶことができます。
nara_heijokyo.highlight: 日本最初の本格的都城。奈良時代の政治・文化の中枢
nara_heijokyo.highlight_en: Japan's first full-fledged capital city. The political and cultural center of the Nara period
nara_heijokyo.text_en: Heijo-kyo was the capital of the Nara period, where Emperor Genmei moved the capital from Fujiwara-kyo in 710. The grid-shaped city, modeled after Chang'an in the Tang Dynasty, is 4.3 km from east to west and 4.8 km from north to south, and its population at the time is estimated to have reached over 100,000 people. Heijo Palace was the emperor's palace and government building located in the northern center of the capital, and was the political center of the Nara period. It was during this period that the foundations of Japanese culture were laid, including the construction of the Great Buddha, the envoys to China, and the compilation of the Manyoshu.
