Currently, excavations are continuing as a special historic site, and the Suzakumon gate and Daigokuden hall have been restored, allowing us to remember the grandeur of the past.

kyoto_arashiyama_tenryuji.name: 嵐山・天龍寺と渡月橋
kyoto_arashiyama_tenryuji.kana: あらしやま・てんりゅうじ
kyoto_arashiyama_tenryuji.text: 天龍寺は1339年、足利尊氏が後醍醐天皇の菩提を弔うために創建した臨済宗の大寺院で、京都五山第一位に列せられます。庭園を設計した夢窓疎石は日本庭園史上最高の作庭家とも称され、曹源池を中心とした池泉回遊式庭園は世界遺産に登録されています。渡月橋は嵐山の象徴で、平安時代から貴族の遊覧地として知られてきました。竹林の小径・野宮神社・大河内山荘など周辺は平安文化の薫りを今も漂わせ、四季折々の美しさで国内外から多くの観光客が訪れます。
kyoto_arashiyama_tenryuji.highlight: 室町幕府が建てた京都五山筆頭。夢窓疎石の名庭と嵐山の絶景

transit.name: JR嵯峨嵐山駅・嵐電「嵐山」

kyoto_arashiyama_tenryuji.highlight_en: The first of Kyoto's five mountains built by the Muromachi Shogunate. Muso Soseki's famous garden and spectacular views of Arashiyama
kyoto_arashiyama_tenryuji.text_en: Tenryu-ji Temple is a large temple of the Rinzai sect of Buddhism that was built in 1339 by Takauji Ashikaga to pray for the memory of Emperor Godaigo, and is ranked as the first of Kyoto's five temples. Muso Soseki, who designed the garden, is said to be the greatest garden designer in the history of Japanese gardens, and the pond strolling style garden centered around Sogen Pond is registered as a World Heritage Site. Togetsukyo Bridge is a symbol of Arashiyama and has been known as a pleasure spot for aristocrats since the Heian period. The surrounding area, including the bamboo forest path, Nonomiya Shrine, and Okochi Sanso, still exudes the scent of Heian culture, and attracts many tourists from Japan and abroad due to its seasonal beauty.

osaka_namba_dotonbori.name: 道頓堀・大坂町人文化の地
osaka_namba_dotonbori.text: 道頓堀は1615年、安井道頓が私財を投じて開削した運河で、大坂の商業・芸能の中心地として発展しました。江戸時代には芝居小屋が立ち並ぶ「道頓堀五座」が全盛を誇り、上方歌舞伎・人形浄瑠璃（文楽）の聖地として栄えました。近松門左衛門はここを舞台に数多くの人形浄瑠璃作品を書き、「曽根崎心中」など不朽の名作を生みました。「食い倒れの町」とも称される大阪の食文化もここから発信され、たこ焼き・串カツなど庶民の味が育まれました。
osaka_namba_dotonbori.highlight: 大坂町人文化の中心地。近松の浄瑠璃と食い倒れ文化が生まれた運河
osaka_namba_dotonbori.highlight_en: The center of Osaka merchant culture. The canal where Chikamatsu's joruri and eating culture were born
osaka_namba_dotonbori.text_en: Dotonbori was a canal dug in 1615 by Doton Yasui with his own money, and it developed into Osaka's center of commerce and entertainment. During the Edo period, Dotonbori Goza, a theater lined with theaters, was at its peak, and flourished as a sacred place for Kamigata Kabuki and puppet theater (Bunraku). Chikamatsu Monzaemon wrote many puppet joruri works using this place as a stage, creating timeless masterpieces such as ``Sonezaki Shinju.'' The food culture of Osaka, also known as the "town of foodies," originated here, and the tastes of the common people, such as takoyaki and kushikatsu, were developed here.

kobe_kitano_ijinkan.name: 神戸北野・異人館街
kobe_kitano_ijinkan.kana: こうべきたの・いじんかんがい
kobe_kitano_ijinkan.text: 神戸は1868年の開港以来、横浜と並ぶ日本最大の国際貿易港として発展しました。北野・山本通には明治から大正にかけて居留した外国人が建てた洋館「異人館」が約30棟現存し、異国情緒豊かな街並みを形成しています。風見鶏の館・萌黄の館・英国館など各国様式の洋館が点在し、神戸独自のモダンな文化を今に伝えます。明治政府の殖産興業政策のもと、神戸港を通じて多くの外国技術・文化が日本に流入し、日本の近代化に大きく貢献しました。
kobe_kitano_ijinkan.highlight: 開港場神戸に生まれた異国情緒。明治の西洋館が並ぶ北野
kobe_kitano_ijinkan.highlight_en: An exotic atmosphere born in the open port of Kobe. Kitano, lined with Western-style buildings from the Meiji era
kobe_kitano_ijinkan.text_en: Since its opening in 1868, Kobe has developed into one of Japan's largest international trading ports, along with Yokohama. Approximately 30 Western-style buildings called Ijinkan, built by foreigners who lived in the area between the Meiji and Taisho eras, still exist on Kitano/Yamamoto-dori Street, creating a townscape rich in exoticism. The area is dotted with Western-style buildings from various countries, such as the Weathervane House, the Moegi House, and the British House, which convey Kobe's unique modern culture to this day. Under the Meiji government's industrial promotion policy, many foreign technologies and cultures entered Japan through Kobe Port, greatly contributing to Japan's modernization.

wakayama_kishyu_tokugawa.name: 和歌山城・紀州徳川家の城下町
wakayama_kishyu_tokugawa.text: 和歌山城は1585年に豊臣秀吉の弟・秀長が築城し、その後浅野幸長が天守を建てた城です。徳川家康の十男・頼宣が1619年に入封してからは紀州徳川家（御三家のひとつ）の居城となりました。紀州徳川家からは8代将軍吉宗・14代将軍家茂が出るなど、江戸幕府との関係は特別に深いものでした。連立式の天守群は現存する貴重な構成で、虎伏山に聳える姿から「虎伏城」とも呼ばれます。隣接する西之丸庭園は「紅葉渓庭園」として春夏秋冬の美を楽しめます。
wakayama_kishyu_tokugawa.highlight: 御三家・紀州徳川家の居城。将軍吉宗を生んだ天下の名城
wakayama_kishyu_tokugawa.name_en: Wakayama Castle/Castle town of the Kishu Tokugawa family
wakayama_kishyu_tokugawa.highlight_en: The residence of the Kishu Tokugawa family, one of the three major families. A famous castle in the world where Shogun Yoshimune was born
wakayama_kishyu_tokugawa.text_en: Wakayama Castle was built in 1585 by Toyotomi Hideyoshi's younger brother Hidenaga, and later Yukinaga Asano built the castle tower. After Tokugawa Ieyasu's tenth son Yorinobu entered the castle in 1619, it became the residence of the Kishu Tokugawa family (one of the three imperial families). The Kishu Tokugawa family had a particularly deep relationship with the Edo shogunate, with the 8th Shogun Yoshimune and the 14th Shogun Iemochi coming out of the Kishu Tokugawa family. The group of continuous castle towers is a valuable structure that still exists, and it is also called ``Torabuse Castle'' because of its towering appearance on Mt. Torabuse. The adjacent Nishinomaru Garden is a ``Momiji Valley Garden'' where you can enjoy the beauty of spring, summer, fall, and winter.

tsuwano_castle_ruins.name: 津和野城跡・殿町通り
tsuwano_castle_ruins.text: 津和野は島根県西部の山間に位置する「山陰の小京都」と称される城下町です。津和野城は13世紀に吉見頼行が築いた山城で、後に坂崎直盛・亀井家が城主となりました。殿町通りには白壁の武家屋敷・津和野藩庁跡・西周旧宅・森鷗外旧宅など、江戸〜明治の歴史的建造物が残ります。明治の文豪・森鷗外と西洋哲学者・西周を生んだ知の土地として知られ、小さな町ながら日本近代思想への貢献は絶大です。鯉が泳ぐ掘割と白壁の町並みが織りなす景観は、日本の原風景として多くの訪問者を魅了しています。
tsuwano_castle_ruins.highlight: 森鷗外・西周を生んだ「山陰の小京都」。鯉泳ぐ城下町
tsuwano_castle_ruins.highlight_en: "Little Kyoto in the San'in region" where Mori Ogai and Nishi Amane were born. A castle town where carp swims
tsuwano_castle_ruins.text_en: Tsuwano is a castle town located in the mountains of western Shimane Prefecture and is known as ``Little Kyoto in the San'in area.'' Tsuwano Castle is a mountain castle built by Yoshimi Yoriyuki in the 13th century, and later the castle was owned by Naomori Sakazaki and the Kamei family. On Tonomachi Street, there are historical buildings from the Edo to Meiji eras, such as the white-walled samurai residence, the ruins of the Tsuwano Domain Office, Nishishu's former residence, and Mori Ogai's former residence. It is known as the land of knowledge that gave birth to Meiji literary giant Mori Ogai and Western philosopher Nishi Shu, and although it is a small town, it has made a tremendous contribution to modern Japanese thought. The landscape of the moat where carp swims and the white-walled townscape attracts many visitors as an original Japanese landscape.

shimonoseki_cho_fu.name: 長府・功山寺と長府藩
shimonoseki_cho_fu.kana: ちょうふ・こうざんじ
shimonoseki_cho_fu.text: 長府は下関市の旧長府藩の城下町で、細川氏・毛利氏の支配を経た歴史ある地域です。功山寺は1320年創建の臨済宗の名刹で、室町時代の仏殿は国宝に指定されています。幕末には高杉晋作が1864年にここで奇兵隊など80名を率いて挙兵（功山寺挙兵）し、長州藩の倒幕路線を決定づけました。古江小路の武家屋敷群・城下町の石畳など、江戸時代の面影を残す街並みが重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に指定されています。
shimonoseki_cho_fu.highlight: 高杉晋作が倒幕の狼煙を上げた功山寺。国宝仏殿を持つ城下町
shimonoseki_cho_fu.highlight_en: Kozanji Temple is where Shinsaku Takasugi signaled the overthrow of the Shogunate. A castle town with a National Treasure Buddha Hall
shimonoseki_cho_fu.text_en: Chofu is a castle town of the former Chofu domain in Shimonoseki City, and is a historical area that was ruled by the Hosokawa and Mori clans. Kozanji Temple is a famous temple of the Rinzai sect, founded in 1320, and its Buddhist temple built in the Muromachi period is designated as a national treasure. At the end of the Edo period, in 1864, Shinsaku Takasugi led 80 people, including the Kiheitai, to raise an army (Kozanji Raise of Armies), which determined the Choshu clan's plan to overthrow the Shogunate. The cityscape that retains the vestiges of the Edo period, such as the samurai residences of Furuekoji and the stone pavements of the castle town, has been designated as an important traditional building preservation district.

hiroshima_miyajima_history.name: 宮島・大聖院と戦国の歴史
hiroshima_miyajima_history.kana: みやじま・だいしょういん
hiroshima_miyajima_history.text: 宮島（厳島）は平清盛が篤く信仰し、海上に大鳥居と社殿を建てた神聖な島として知られます。1555年には毛利元就と陶晴賢が島を舞台に戦った「厳島の戦い」が起こり、元就の巧みな奇策により陶軍を壊滅させ中国地方の覇権を確立しました。大聖院は806年、空海が開基したとされる宮島最古の寺院で、弥山の登山口にも近く修験道の聖地でもあります。世界遺産の厳島神社と宮島の自然が一体となった景観は、日本三景のひとつとして古来より人々を魅了してきました。
hiroshima_miyajima_history.highlight: 平清盛が愛した海上の神域。毛利元就が奇策で勝った厳島の戦い
hiroshima_miyajima_history.name_en: Miyajima Daishoin and the history of the Sengoku period
hiroshima_miyajima_history.highlight_en: A sacred area on the sea loved by Taira no Kiyomori. The Battle of Itsukushima, won by Mori Motonari with a clever strategy
hiroshima_miyajima_history.text_en: Miyajima (Itsukushima) is known as a sacred island where Taira no Kiyomori had a strong faith and built a large torii gate and a shrine on the sea. In 1555, the ``Battle of Itsukushima'' was fought on the island between Mori Motonari and Sue Harukata, and Motonari's clever and ingenious strategy destroyed the Sue army and established hegemony over the Chugoku region. Daishoin is the oldest temple on Miyajima, said to have been founded by Kukai in 806, and is also a sacred place for Shugendo, close to the trailhead of Mt. Misen. The scenery that combines the world heritage site Itsukushima Shrine and Miyajima's nature has fascinated people since ancient times as one of Japan's three most scenic views.

okayama_korakuen.name: 後楽園・岡山城
okayama_korakuen.kana: こうらくえん・おかやまじょう
okayama_korakuen.text: 後楽園は1700年、岡山藩主・池田綱政が11年の歳月をかけて造営した日本三名園のひとつです。広大な芝生・沢の池・茶室が調和した池泉回遊式庭園は、大名庭園の傑作として名高く、四季折々の風景が楽しめます。隣接する岡山城は「烏城（うじょう）」と呼ばれる黒い天守が特徴で、宇喜多秀家が1597年に完成させた城です。池田氏が岡山藩を治めた江戸時代、熊沢蕃山・新田開発など農政改革が行われ、備前国は文化・産業ともに栄えました。
okayama_korakuen.highlight: 日本三名園・後楽園と烏城。池田藩が誇る大名文化の粋
okayama_korakuen.highlight_en: Korakuen and Karasu Castle, one of Japan's three most famous gardens. The essence of daimyo culture that the Ikeda clan is proud of
okayama_korakuen.text_en: Korakuen is one of Japan's top three gardens, built in 1700 by Tsunamasa Ikeda, the lord of the Okayama domain, over a period of 11 years. The Ikeizumi Strolling Garden is a harmonious combination of a vast lawn, a stream pond, and a tea room, and is famous as a masterpiece of feudal lord gardens, where you can enjoy the scenery of each season. The adjacent Okayama Castle is characterized by a black castle tower called ``Crow Castle'' and was completed in 1597 by Hideie Ukita. During the Edo period, when the Ikeda clan ruled the Okayama domain, agricultural reforms such as Kumazawa Banzan and new field development were carried out, and Bizen Province prospered in both culture and industry.

yamaguchi_city_history.name: 山口・大内氏館跡と龍福寺
yamaguchi_city_history.kana: やまぐち・おおうちしやかたあと
yamaguchi_city_history.text: 山口は室町時代に大内氏が「西の京都」と呼ばれるほど繁栄させた都市です。大内義隆は京都の公家文化を積極的に取り入れ、朝鮮・明・ポルトガルとの貿易で富を蓄え、応仁の乱を逃れた文化人・学者を保護しました。1551年の「大寧寺の変」で大内義隆が陶晴賢に倒され、栄華は突然終わりを迎えました。龍福寺は大内氏館跡に建てられた寺院で、大内文化の記憶を今に伝えます。フランシスコ・ザビエルが布教のために訪れた地としても知られ、山口市内にはザビエル記念聖堂が建ちます。
yamaguchi_city_history.highlight: 「西の京都」大内氏の栄華の地。ザビエルも訪れた中世山口の都
yamaguchi_city_history.name_en: Yamaguchi/Ouchi Clan Residence and Ryufukuji Temple
yamaguchi_city_history.highlight_en: ``Western Kyoto'', the prosperous land of the Ouchi clan. The capital of medieval Yamaguchi, visited by Xavier
yamaguchi_city_history.text_en: Yamaguchi is a city that was made prosperous by the Ouchi clan during the Muromachi period to the point where it was called the ``Kyoto of the West.'' Yoshitaka Ouchi actively adopted Kyoto's court noble culture, amassed wealth through trade with Korea, the Ming Dynasty, and Portugal, and protected intellectuals and scholars who had escaped the Onin War. In 1551, Yoshitaka Ouchi was defeated by Sue Haruken in the ``Daineiji Incident'', and the prosperity came to an abrupt end. Ryufuku-ji Temple was built on the site of the Ouchi clan mansion, and it preserves the memories of Ouchi culture. It is also known as the place where Francis Xavier visited for missionary work, and the Xavier Memorial Cathedral is built in Yamaguchi City.

tottori_castle_ruins.name: 鳥取城跡と城下町
tottori_castle_ruins.text: 鳥取城は1545年に山名氏が築いた山城で、戦国時代には羽柴秀吉（豊臣秀吉）が「鳥取の渇え殺し」と呼ばれる兵糧攻めで攻略したことで知られます。秀吉は周辺の食料を買い占めて城を孤立させ、約4ヶ月の籠城の末に城将・吉川経家は城兵の命と引き換えに切腹して開城しました。江戸時代は池田家が因幡・伯耆の鳥取藩を治め、城下町として整備されました。天球丸の巻石垣（球形の石垣）は技術的に珍しい遺構で、国の史跡として整備が進んでいます。
tottori_castle_ruins.highlight: 「鳥取の渇え殺し」秀吉の兵糧攻めで有名な因幡の名城
tottori_castle_ruins.name_en: Tottori Castle ruins and castle town
tottori_castle_ruins.highlight_en: ``The Thirst Killer of Tottori'' A famous castle in Inaba famous for Hideyoshi's food raids
tottori_castle_ruins.text_en: Tottori Castle is a mountain castle built by the Yamana clan in 1545, and is known for being conquered by Hashiba Hideyoshi (Toyotomi Hideyoshi) during the Sengoku period with a food raid called the ``Thirst Slayer of Tottori.'' Hideyoshi isolated the castle by buying up all the food in the surrounding area, and after about four months of siege, the castle commander, Tsuneie Yoshikawa, committed seppuku and surrendered the castle in exchange for the lives of the castle's soldiers. During the Edo period, the Ikeda family ruled the Tottori domain of Inaba and Hoki, and developed it into a castle town. The makiishigaki (spherical stone wall) of Tenkyumaru is a technically rare structure, and is being maintained as a national historic site.

iwami_ginzan_world.name: 石見銀山・大森の町並み
iwami_ginzan_world.text: 石見銀山は16世紀に本格採掘が始まり、最盛期には世界の銀産出量の約3分の1を占めたとされる世界有数の銀山です。2007年に「石見銀山遺跡とその文化的景観」として世界遺産に登録されました。産出された銀は博多商人や大内氏・毛利氏を通じて中国・ポルトガルへ輸出され、日本が世界経済に本格的に組み込まれるきっかけとなりました。江戸時代は幕府直轄地（天領）として厳しく管理され、代官所が置かれた大森地区には当時の街並みが残ります。坑道（間歩）の見学や精錬技術の展示で往時の繁栄を体感できます。
iwami_ginzan_world.highlight: 世界遺産の銀山。世界の銀の1/3を産出した中世日本の経済拠点
iwami_ginzan_world.highlight_en: A world heritage silver mine. The economic center of medieval Japan, which produced 1/3 of the world's silver
iwami_ginzan_world.text_en: Iwami Ginzan Silver Mine began full-scale mining in the 16th century, and is one of the world's leading silver mines, accounting for approximately one-third of the world's silver production at its peak. In 2007, it was registered as a World Heritage Site as "Iwami Ginzan Ruins and its Cultural Landscape." The silver produced was exported to China and Portugal through Hakata merchants and the Ouchi and Mori clans, marking the beginning of Japan's full-scale integration into the world economy. During the Edo period, it was strictly controlled as a land under the direct control of the shogunate (Tenryo), and the Omori district, where the magistrate's office was located, still retains the streetscape from that time. You can experience the prosperity of the past by touring the mine shafts and exhibiting smelting techniques.

matsue_lafcadio_hearn.name: 松江・小泉八雲旧居
matsue_lafcadio_hearn.kana: まつえ・こいずみやくもきゅうきょ
matsue_lafcadio_hearn.text: 松江はラフカディオ・ハーン（小泉八雲）が1890〜91年に暮らした城下町です。ハーンはアイルランド系のジャーナリストで、松江で日本人女性と結婚し日本に帰化。「怪談（Kwaidan）」「知られぬ日本の面影」など日本の民話・怪談を英語で世界に紹介し、欧米の日本ブームに火をつけました。武家屋敷が残る城山北麓には旧居と記念館が保存され、ハーンが愛した松江の武家町の静けさが今も漂っています。松江城と宍道湖・塩見縄手が織りなす風景は、日本の城下町の美しさを凝縮しています。
matsue_lafcadio_hearn.highlight: 「怪談」を世界に広めたハーンが愛した城下町。松江の武家屋敷
matsue_lafcadio_hearn.highlight_en: A castle town loved by Hahn, who spread "ghost stories" around the world. Samurai residence in Matsue
matsue_lafcadio_hearn.text_en: Matsue is a castle town where Lafcadio Hearn (Koizumi Yakumo) lived from 1890 to 1891. Hearn is an Irish journalist who married a Japanese woman in Matsue and became a naturalized Japanese citizen. He introduced Japanese folktales and ghost stories in English to the world, such as ``Kwaidan'' and ``Unknown Faces of Japan,'' which ignited a Japanese boom in the West. At the northern foot of Shiroyama, where the samurai residences remain, the former residence and memorial hall have been preserved, and the tranquility of the samurai town of Matsue, beloved by Hahn, still lingers in the air. The scenery created by Matsue Castle, Lake Shinji, and Shiomi Nawate encapsulates the beauty of Japan's castle towns.

fukuyama_tomonoura.name: 鞆の浦・沼名前神社
fukuyama_tomonoura.text: 鞆の浦は瀬戸内海のほぼ中央に位置し、古代から潮待ちの港として栄えた「潮待ちの港」です。万葉集にも詠まれ、江戸時代には北前船・朝鮮通信使が必ず立ち寄った要港でした。江戸時代の雁木（船着場）・常夜燈・波止・焚場・船番所が揃って現存する唯一の港として知られ、江戸時代の港の景観が完全な形で残っています。宮崎駿監督が「崖の上のポニョ」の構想を練った地としても知られ、海と山と古い町並みが調和する絵のような港です。
fukuyama_tomonoura.highlight: 江戸の港施設が完全に残る奇跡の港町。万葉から続く潮待ちの湊
fukuyama_tomonoura.highlight_en: A miraculous port town where Edo port facilities remain intact. A seaport waiting for the tide that continues from Manyo
fukuyama_tomonoura.text_en: Tomonoura is located almost in the center of the Seto Inland Sea and has flourished as a port for waiting for the tide since ancient times. It is written about in the Manyoshu, and was an important port where Kitamaebune and Korean envoys always stopped by during the Edo period. It is known as the only port that still has the Edo period's Gangi (pier), nightlight, wharf, fire pit, and ship guard house, and the landscape of the Edo period port remains intact. It is also known as the place where director Hayao Miyazaki conceived the idea for ``Ponyo on the Cliff'', and is a picturesque port where the sea, mountains, and old townscape harmonize.

hiroshima_hiraga_gennai.name: 三原城跡・浮城
hiroshima_hiraga_gennai.text: 三原城は1567年、毛利元就の三男・小早川隆景が瀬戸内海の小島を本丸として築いた「浮城」です。海水が直接石垣に迫る水城の形式を取り、潮が満ちると城が海に浮かぶように見えたことからこの名が付きました。隆景は毛利氏の水軍を率いる智将として知られ、豊臣秀吉の信任も厚く「豊臣五大老」のひとりに数えられました。現在は石垣の一部と天主台が残るのみですが、JR山陽本線のトンネルが天主台を貫通しているという珍しい構造で知られています。
hiroshima_hiraga_gennai.highlight: 毛利の知将・小早川隆景が築いた水城。海に浮かぶ「浮城」の石垣
hiroshima_hiraga_gennai.highlight_en: A water castle built by Takakage Kobayakawa, a wealthy Mouri general. Stone wall of a floating castle floating on the sea
hiroshima_hiraga_gennai.text_en: Mihara Castle is a floating castle built in 1567 by Takakage Kobayakawa, the third son of Mori Motonari, on a small island in the Seto Inland Sea. It took the form of a water castle, where the seawater directly approaches the stone walls, and it got its name because it looked like it was floating on the sea when the tide was high. Takakage was known as a wise general who led the Mouri clan's navy, and was highly trusted by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who counted him as one of the ``Five Elders of Toyotomi.'' Currently, only part of the stone wall and the church tower remain, but it is known for its unusual structure in that the JR Sanyo Main Line tunnel passes through the church tower.

kochi_katsurahama.name: 桂浜・坂本龍馬像
kochi_katsurahama.text: 桂浜は高知市南部の太平洋に面した景勝地で、弧を描く砂浜と黒松林・岩礁が月見の名所として古来知られてきました。浜の小高い丘には幕末の志士・坂本龍馬の銅像が太平洋を見つめて立ち、高知のシンボルとなっています。龍馬は1835年に土佐藩下士の家に生まれ、脱藩後は薩長同盟の仲介・大政奉還の建白など明治維新の立役者となりました。桂浜水族館・坂本龍馬記念館が隣接し、龍馬の生涯と幕末の歴史を深く知ることができます。
kochi_katsurahama.highlight: 龍馬が太平洋を見つめる高知のシンボル。幕末志士の魂が宿る浜辺
kochi_katsurahama.highlight_en: A symbol of Kochi where Ryoma gazes out at the Pacific Ocean. A beach where the souls of Bakumatsu patriots dwell
kochi_katsurahama.text_en: Katsurahama is a scenic spot facing the Pacific Ocean in the southern part of Kochi City, and has been known since ancient times as a famous moon-viewing spot for its arching sandy beach, black pine forest, and rocky reef. A bronze statue of Sakamoto Ryoma, a patriot at the end of the Edo period, stands on a small hill on the beach, looking out at the Pacific Ocean, and has become a symbol of Kochi. Ryoma was born in 1835 into the family of a samurai of the Tosa domain, and after leaving the domain, he became a leading figure in the Meiji Restoration, mediating the Satsuma-Choshu alliance and campaigning for the restoration of imperial rule. The Katsurahama Aquarium and Sakamoto Ryoma Memorial Museum are adjacent to it, where you can learn more about Ryoma's life and the history of the end of the Edo period.

dogo_onsen_main.name: 道後温泉本館
dogo_onsen_main.kana: どうごおんせんほんかん
dogo_onsen_main.text: 道後温泉は日本最古の温泉のひとつで、3000年以上の歴史を持つとされます。万葉集にも詠まれ、聖徳太子も訪れたと伝えられる霊泉です。1894年に建てられた本館（神の湯本館）は木造3階建ての複雑な構造を持つ温泉建築の傑作で、国の重要文化財に指定されています。夏目漱石は松山中学の英語教師として赴任した際にここで入浴し、小説「坊っちゃん」に道後温泉を描写。宮崎駿の「千と千尋の神隠し」のモデルのひとつとも言われています。
dogo_onsen_main.highlight: 3000年の歴史を誇る日本最古の温泉。「坊っちゃん」の舞台

transit.name: 伊予鉄道市内線「道後温泉」

dogo_onsen_main.highlight_en: Japan's oldest hot spring with a history of 3000 years. "Botchan" stage
dogo_onsen_main.text_en: Dogo Onsen is one of the oldest hot springs in Japan, with a history of over 3000 years. It is a sacred spring that is mentioned in the Manyoshu and is said to have been visited by Prince Shotoku. The main building (Kami no Yu Honkan), built in 1894, is a masterpiece of hot spring architecture with a complex three-story wooden structure, and has been designated as a national important cultural property. Natsume Soseki bathed here when he was appointed as an English teacher at Matsuyama Junior High School, and he described Dogo Onsen in his novel ``Botchan.'' It is said to be one of the models for Hayao Miyazaki's ``Spirited Away''.

kotohira_kompira.name: 金刀比羅宮（こんぴらさん）
kotohira_kompira.text: 金刀比羅宮は琴平山（象頭山）の中腹に鎮座する、航海・農業・医薬の神として知られる神社です。本宮まで785段、奥社まで1,368段の石段が続き、江戸時代から「一生に一度はこんぴらまいり」と庶民の憧れの参詣地でした。参拝できない人の代わりに犬が初穂料を持って旅をする「こんぴら狗」の風習が生まれたほど、こんぴら信仰は全国に広まりました。参道には江戸時代の灯籠・五人百姓の飴屋・書院に残る円山応挙の障壁画など、文化財が豊富に残っています。
kotohira_kompira.highlight: 「一生に一度はこんぴら参り」。1368段を登る四国屈指の聖地
kotohira_kompira.highlight_en: "Visit Konpira once in your life." One of the most sacred places in Shikoku with 1368 steps to climb
kotohira_kompira.text_en: Kotohira Shrine is a shrine known as the god of navigation, agriculture, and medicine, located halfway up Mt. Kotohira (Mt. Zouzu). There are 785 stone steps to the main shrine and 1,368 steps to the inner shrine, and since the Edo period, it has been a place of worship for the common people, who say, ``Visiting Konpira at least once in a lifetime.'' Konpira worship spread across the country to the extent that the custom of ``Konpira Inu'' was born, in which dogs travel with first-fruits money to replace those who cannot visit the shrine. There are a wealth of cultural assets remaining along the approach, including lanterns from the Edo period, the candy store of the five peasants, and Maruyama Okyo's wall paintings that remain in the study hall.

uwajima_castle_ruins.name: 宇和島城・宇和島伊達家
uwajima_castle_ruins.text: 宇和島城は1601年に藤堂高虎が築いた三角形の縄張りが特徴的な城で、現存12天守のひとつです。後に入封した伊達秀宗（伊達政宗の庶長子）が宇和島伊達家を開き、幕末まで存続しました。城下町には伊達家の菩提寺・伊達博物館があり、仙台から持ち込まれた東北の文化と四国の文化が融合した独特の歴史が残されています。幕末には二代藩主・宇和島伊達宗城が開明派の名君として知られ、嘉蔵（前原巧山）に蒸気船の試作を命じた先進的な藩政を行いました。
uwajima_castle_ruins.highlight: 現存12天守の宇和島城。仙台伊達家の支藩として独自の文化を育む
uwajima_castle_ruins.highlight_en: Uwajima Castle has 12 existing castle towers. Cultivating a unique culture as a branch of the Sendai Date clan
uwajima_castle_ruins.text_en: Uwajima Castle was built in 1601 by Todo Takatora, and is one of the 12 castle towers in existence. Date Hidemune (the eldest son of Date Masamune), who later joined the clan, opened the Uwajima Date family, which continued until the end of the Edo period. The castle town is home to the Date Museum, the family temple of the Date clan, and has a unique history that combines the culture of Tohoku and Shikoku brought from Sendai. At the end of the Edo period, the second lord of the Edo period, Date Muneki of Uwajima, was known as a great lord of the Kaimei school, and conducted an advanced domain administration, ordering Kazo (Takuzan Maehara) to prototype a steamship.

naruto_whirlpool.name: 鳴門の渦潮と鳴門海峡
naruto_whirlpool.text: 鳴門海峡は淡路島と四国（徳島県）の間の幅約1.3kmの狭い海峡で、瀬戸内海と太平洋の潮流が激突することで世界最大級の渦潮が発生します。直径最大30mにも達する渦潮は1日4回のサイクルで生まれ、春と秋の大潮の時期が最も壮観です。古来より「鳴門の渦潮」は万葉集にも詠まれた名所で、航海の難所でもありました。第一次世界大戦中にはドイツ人捕虜を収容した板東俘虜収容所がこの地に設けられ、捕虜たちが日本初のベートーヴェン第九を演奏したことでも知られます。
naruto_whirlpool.highlight: 世界最大級の渦潮が発生する絶景の海峡。万葉の昔から有名な難所
naruto_whirlpool.highlight_en: A spectacular strait with one of the world's largest whirlpools. A famous difficult spot from ancient times in Manyo
naruto_whirlpool.text_en: The Naruto Strait is a narrow strait approximately 1.3 km wide between Awaji Island and Shikoku (Tokushima Prefecture), where the world's largest whirlpools are generated when the tidal currents of the Seto Inland Sea and the Pacific Ocean collide. The whirlpools, which can reach up to 30 meters in diameter, are created four times a day, and are most spectacular during the spring tides in spring and autumn. Since ancient times, the ``Naruto whirlpools'' have been a famous place mentioned in the Manyoshu, and were also a difficult place for navigation. During World War I, the Bando POW camp was established here to house German prisoners of war, and it is also known for being the first place in Japan to perform Beethoven's Ninth.

takamatsu_ritsurin.name: 栗林公園（高松）
takamatsu_ritsurin.text: 栗林公園は高松藩・松平家が約100年の歳月をかけて整備した大名庭園で、特別名勝に指定されています。6つの池と13の築山を配した池泉回遊式庭園は、後楽園・兼六園と並ぶ日本三大名園に次ぐ「特別名勝」として高い評価を受けています。ミシュランガイドで三ツ星を獲得したことで海外にも広く知られるようになりました。園内の掬月亭では抹茶を楽しみながら庭園を一望でき、江戸時代の大名文化の雅を体感できます。瀬戸内の温暖な気候の中、四季折々の表情を見せる庭園美は格別です。
takamatsu_ritsurin.highlight: ミシュラン三ツ星の大名庭園。松平家が百年かけて育てた特別名勝
takamatsu_ritsurin.highlight_en: A three-star Michelin daimyo garden. A special scenic spot cultivated by the Matsudaira family over 100 years
takamatsu_ritsurin.text_en: Ritsurin Park is a feudal lord garden that was maintained by the Matsudaira family of the Takamatsu domain over a period of approximately 100 years, and has been designated as a special scenic spot. The Ikeizumi Strolling Garden, which has 6 ponds and 13 artificial hills, has been highly praised as a ``Special Place of Scenic Beauty'', second only to Japan's three great gardens along with Korakuen and Kenrokuen. It became widely known overseas after receiving three stars in the Michelin Guide. At Kikgetsutei in the park, you can enjoy a panoramic view of the garden while enjoying matcha tea, and experience the elegance of the daimyo culture of the Edo period. In the warm climate of the Seto Inland Sea, the beauty of the garden is exceptional as it changes with the seasons.

awa_yoshino_river.name: 阿波・吉野川と三好氏の城跡群
awa_yoshino_river.text: 阿波国（徳島県）吉野川流域は、戦国時代に三好氏が台頭した歴史の地です。三好長慶は1549年に細川氏を排除して京都の実権を握り、織田信長に先駆けて「天下人」となった人物として再評価されています。吉野川沿いには勝瑞城・三好氏の城跡が点在し、徳島城（阿波徳島城）は蜂須賀家が江戸時代を通じて治めた城です。吉野川は「四国三郎」の別称を持つ大河で、流域の藍染め産業（阿波藍）は江戸時代の徳島藩の財政を潤しました。
awa_yoshino_river.highlight: 信長より先に天下を握った三好長慶の本拠地。藍染めで栄えた阿波
awa_yoshino_river.name_en: Awa/Yoshino River and Miyoshi clan castle ruins
awa_yoshino_river.highlight_en: The home base of Miyoshi Nagayoshi, who ruled the country before Nobunaga. Awa flourished with indigo dyeing
awa_yoshino_river.text_en: The Yoshino River basin in Awa Province (Tokushima Prefecture) is a historical place where the Miyoshi clan rose to prominence during the Sengoku period. Miyoshi Nagayoshi took over the real power of Kyoto in 1549 by eliminating the Hosokawa clan, and is now being reevaluated as a man who became a ``national ruler'' ahead of Oda Nobunaga. Along the Yoshino River, there are the ruins of Shozui Castle and Miyoshi clan castles, and Tokushima Castle (Awa Tokushima Castle) was ruled by the Hachisuka family throughout the Edo period. The Yoshinogawa River is a great river that is also known as ``Shikoku Saburo,'' and the indigo dyeing industry (Awa Ai) in its basin enriched the finances of the Tokushima clan during the Edo period.

kochi_shimanto.name: 四万十川・中村城下町
kochi_shimanto.kana: しまんとがわ・なかむらじょうかまち
kochi_shimanto.text: 四万十川は「日本最後の清流」と称される全長196kmの大河で、ダムが一つもない自然のままの川として知られます。中村市（現四万十市）は1468年、関白・一条教房が応仁の乱を逃れてここに下り「土佐の小京都」を築いた城下町です。一条氏は京都の文化をそのまま土佐に持ち込み、公家文化と土佐の土地が融合した独自の文化圏を形成しました。後に長宗我部氏に滅ぼされますが、その文化の記憶は今も中村の街並みに残ります。四万十川の沈下橋と清流は、日本の原風景として多くの人々の心をつかんでいます。
kochi_shimanto.highlight: 「日本最後の清流」四万十川。応仁の乱を逃れた公家が造った小京都
kochi_shimanto.highlight_en: "Japan's last clear stream" Shimanto River. Little Kyoto was built by court nobles who fled the Onin War.
kochi_shimanto.text_en: The Shimanto River is a large river with a total length of 196 km and is known as ``Japan's last clear stream'', and is known as a pristine river with no dams. Nakamura City (currently Shimanto City) is a castle town where Kanpaku Ichijo Norifusa fled the Onin War in 1468 and built the ``Little Kyoto of Tosa.'' The Ichijo clan brought the culture of Kyoto directly to Tosa, creating a unique cultural area that blended the culture of court nobles and the land of Tosa. Although it was later destroyed by the Chosokabe clan, the memories of that culture still remain in the streets of Nakamura. The submerged bridge and clear stream of the Shimanto River capture the hearts of many people as a part of Japan's original scenery.

ehime_ozu_castle.name: 大洲城・肱川の城下町
ehime_ozu_castle.text: 大洲城は肱川の岸辺に築かれた城で、現在の4層4階の天守は2004年に木造で復元されたものです。復元に際しては江戸時代の古写真・雛形（模型）・文書が詳細に分析され、高い精度で当時の姿を再現しています。城下町・大洲は「伊予の小京都」とも呼ばれ、白壁の商家・武家屋敷が残る歴史的な町並みが続きます。肱川の川霧と大洲城の幻想的な風景は「城下町大洲の霧」として知られ、秋から冬にかけて白い霧の中に浮かぶ天守の景観は圧巻です。
ehime_ozu_castle.highlight: 木造復元天守と肱川の霧が織りなす幻想的な景観。伊予の小京都
ehime_ozu_castle.highlight_en: A fantastic landscape created by the restored wooden castle tower and the mist of the Hijikawa River. Iyo's Little Kyoto
ehime_ozu_castle.text_en: Ozu Castle is a castle built on the banks of the Hijikawa River, and its current 4-story, 4-story castle tower was restored in 2004 with a wooden structure. During the restoration, old photographs, models, and documents from the Edo period were analyzed in detail, and the building was recreated with a high degree of accuracy. The castle town of Ozu is also known as ``Iyo's Little Kyoto'' and has a historic townscape with white-walled merchant houses and samurai residences. The fantastic scenery of the river mist of the Hijigawa River and Ozu Castle is known as the "Castle Town Ozu Fog," and the sight of the castle tower floating in the white mist from autumn to winter is a sight to behold.

tokushima_bizan.name: 眉山と阿波おどり会館
tokushima_bizan.text: 眉山は徳島市のシンボルの山で、万葉集にも詠まれた古代からの名山です。山頂からは紀伊水道・淡路島・瀬戸内海を一望でき、徳島の歴史的な景観を楽しめます。阿波おどりは約400年の歴史を持つ日本最大規模の盆踊りで、毎年8月に開催される阿波おどりには全国から100万人以上が訪れます。「踊る阿呆に見る阿呆、同じ阿呆なら踊らにゃ損損」のお囃子のもと、男踊り・女踊りが繰り広げられる熱狂は徳島の誇りです。阿波おどり会館では年間を通じてプロの踊りを鑑賞できます。
tokushima_bizan.highlight: 万葉の山と400年の伝統・阿波おどり。徳島を象徴する文化の地
tokushima_bizan.highlight_en: Mountains of Manyo and 400 years of tradition, Awa Odori. A cultural place that symbolizes Tokushima
tokushima_bizan.text_en: Bizan is the symbol of Tokushima City, and is a famous mountain from ancient times that has been mentioned in the Manyoshu. From the top of the mountain, you can see the Kii Channel, Awaji Island, and the Seto Inland Sea, and enjoy Tokushima's historic scenery. Awa Odori is Japan's largest Bon dance with a history of about 400 years, and more than 1 million people from all over the country visit the Awa Odori festival held every August. Tokushima is proud of the enthusiasm with which the men's and women's dances are performed, accompanied by the melody of ``A fool looks like a fool when he dances, and if he is the same fool, it's a loss to dance.'' At the Awa Odori Kaikan, you can enjoy professional dance performances throughout the year.

osorezan_bodaiji.name: 恐山菩提寺
osorezan_bodaiji.text: 恐山は下北半島の中央にそびえる火山性の山で、比叡山・高野山と並ぶ日本三大霊山の一つです。平安時代の慈覚大師円仁が開山したとされ、死者の魂が集まる「死の山」として古来より信仰されてきました。硫黄の噴気が立ち上る荒涼とした風景の中に宇曽利山湖が広がり、極楽浜と呼ばれる白砂の浜は対照的に清らかな美しさを見せます。夏の大祭では「イタコ」と呼ばれる霊媒師が口寄せを行い、死者の言葉を伝えると言われています。近代に至っても多くの人が故人との対話を求めて訪れる、日本独自の霊場文化が息づく場所です。
osorezan_bodaiji.highlight: 日本三大霊山の一つ。イタコの口寄せで知られる死者の山
osorezan_bodaiji.highlight_en: One of Japan's three major sacred mountains. Mountain of the Dead, known for Itako no Kuchiyose
osorezan_bodaiji.text_en: Osorezan is a volcanic mountain that rises in the center of the Shimokita Peninsula, and is one of Japan's three great sacred mountains, along with Mt. Hiei and Mt. Koya. The mountain is said to have been founded by Jikaku Daishi Ennin during the Heian period, and has been worshiped since ancient times as the ``Mountain of Death'' where the souls of the dead gather. Usoriyama Lake spreads out in a desolate landscape with sulfur fumes rising, and in contrast, the white sand beach called Gokurakuhama shows off its pure beauty. It is said that during the summer festival, a medium called ``Itako'' performs a communion and conveys the words of the dead. Even in modern times, many people visit this place in search of a dialogue with the deceased, and it is a place where Japan's unique sacred culture lives on.

hachinohe_nejo.name: 根城跡（八戸市）
hachinohe_nejo.kana: ねじょあと（はちのへし）
hachinohe_nejo.text: 根城は南北朝時代の1334年、南部師行によって築かれた城で、南部氏の居城として200年以上にわたり東北地方を支配しました。現在の史跡公園には、発掘調査に基づいて中世城館の建物が忠実に復元されており、本丸・中館・東善寺館など当時の姿を間近に体感できます。国の特別史跡に指定されており、復元された主殿では中世武士の暮らしぶりを学ぶことができます。隣接する八戸市博物館とともに、南部氏と中世北東北の歴史を知る絶好の拠点となっています。
hachinohe_nejo.highlight: 南部氏が200年支配した中世城館。復元建物で当時の暮らしを体感
hachinohe_nejo.highlight_en: A medieval castle ruled by the Nanbu clan for 200 years. Experience life at the time in a restored building
hachinohe_nejo.text_en: Nejo was built in 1334 during the Nanbokucho period by Moroyuki Nambu, and ruled the Tohoku region for over 200 years as the residence of the Nambu clan. In the current historic park, the buildings of the medieval castle have been faithfully restored based on excavations, and you can experience up close how they looked at the time, including the Honmaru, Nakadate, and Tozenji Building. It has been designated as a special national historic site, and you can learn about the lifestyle of medieval samurai in the restored main hall. Along with the adjacent Hachinohe City Museum, it is a great base to learn about the history of the Nanbu clan and medieval Tohoku.

aomori_nebuta.name: ねぶたの家ワ・ラッセ
aomori_nebuta.kana: ねぶたのいえわらっせ
aomori_nebuta.text: 青森ねぶた祭は毎年8月初旬に開催される東北を代表する祭りで、国の重要無形民俗文化財に指定されています。巨大な人形型の「ねぶた」は針金と和紙で作られ、内部に照明が灯された芸術作品です。その起源は奈良時代の「七夕の灯籠流し」にあるとも、坂上田村麻呂が蝦夷征伐の際に敵を引きつける囮として使ったとも伝わります。ねぶたの家ワ・ラッセでは一年中実物大のねぶたを展示しており、祭りのハネトダンスの体験もできます。青森駅前に立地し、津軽海峡の景色を背にした印象的な施設です。
aomori_nebuta.highlight: 青森ねぶた祭の常設展示施設。巨大ねぶたと祭り文化を体感
aomori_nebuta.highlight_en: A permanent exhibition facility for the Aomori Nebuta Festival. Experience the giant Nebuta and festival culture
aomori_nebuta.text_en: The Aomori Nebuta Festival is a festival representing Tohoku that is held every year in early August, and has been designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property. The giant doll-shaped ``Nebuta'' is a work of art made of wire and washi paper, and is illuminated inside. It is said that its origin lies in the ``Tanabata lantern float'' of the Nara period, and that Sakanoue Tamuramaro used it as a decoy to attract enemies during his conquest of Ezo. At Wa Rasse, the Nebuta house, life-sized Nebuta are on display all year round, and you can also experience the festival's haneto dance. This is an impressive facility located in front of Aomori Station with a view of the Tsugaru Strait in the background.

towada_oirase.name: 十和田湖・奥入瀬渓流
towada_oirase.kana: とわだこ・おいらせけいりゅう
towada_oirase.text: 十和田湖は約20万年前の火山活動によって形成されたカルデラ湖で、青森・秋田両県にまたがる国立公園の中心にあります。流出する奥入瀬渓流は全長約14kmにわたり、銚子大滝をはじめ大小さまざまな滝と瀑布が連なる日本屈指の渓流美を誇ります。明治末期に文人墨客が訪れ始め、大町桂月が「奥入瀬は日本一の渓流」と称えたことで全国に知られるようになりました。湖畔には彫刻家・高村光太郎の最晩年の大作「乙女の像」が建ち、作家・大町桂月の終焉の地でもあります。
towada_oirase.highlight: 青森・秋田にまたがる絶景カルデラ湖。奥入瀬渓流は日本一の渓流美
towada_oirase.highlight_en: A spectacular caldera lake that straddles Aomori and Akita. Oirase Gorge is the most beautiful mountain stream in Japan
towada_oirase.text_en: Lake Towada is a caldera lake formed by volcanic activity about 200,000 years ago, and is located at the center of a national park that straddles Aomori and Akita prefectures. The Oirase Gorge, which flows out of it, has a total length of approximately 14 km and boasts one of the most beautiful mountain streams in Japan, with waterfalls and waterfalls of various sizes, including Choshi Otaki. At the end of the Meiji period, literary figures and artists began to visit, and Oirase became known throughout the country after Omachi Keigetsu praised it as ``the best mountain stream in Japan.'' On the shore of the lake stands the sculptor Kotaro Takamura's masterpiece "Statue of a Maiden" in his later years, and it is also the final resting place of the writer Keigetsu Omachi.

tsugaru_iwaki_shrine.name: 岩木山神社（津軽のお岩木さん）

transit.name: 弘南バス「岩木山神社前」

tsugaru_iwaki_shrine.text: 岩木山神社は青森県最高峰・岩木山（1625m）の麓に鎮座する古社で、延暦初年（780年代）の創建と伝わります。「お岩木さま」の愛称で津軽の人々に親しまれ、農業・漁業・縁結びの神として広く信仰を集めてきました。楼門や拝殿は江戸時代に津軽藩が造営したもので、日光東照宮を思わせる豪壮な建築が山麓の杉林の中にそびえます。毎年旧暦8月1日（お山参詣）には数千人の信者が白装束で岩木山に登る伝統行事が行われ、東北の山岳信仰を今に伝えています。
tsugaru_iwaki_shrine.highlight: 津軽の守護神「お岩木さま」。日光東照宮に似た豪壮な社殿が残る
tsugaru_iwaki_shrine.highlight_en: Oiwaki-sama, the guardian deity of Tsugaru. A magnificent shrine building similar to Nikko Toshogu Shrine remains.
tsugaru_iwaki_shrine.text_en: Iwakiyama Shrine is an old shrine located at the foot of Aomori Prefecture's highest peak, Mt. Iwaki (1625m), and is said to have been founded in the first year of the Enryaku era (780s). Nicknamed ``Oiwaki-sama'' by the people of Tsugaru, he is widely worshiped as the god of agriculture, fishing, and marriage. The tower gate and worship hall were built by the Tsugaru clan during the Edo period, and the magnificent architecture, reminiscent of Nikko Toshogu Shrine, towers over the cedar forest at the foot of the mountain. Every year on August 1st of the lunar calendar (Oyama Pilgrimage), thousands of believers climb Mt. Iwaki dressed in white in a traditional event that continues to pass down Tohoku's mountain worship.

tono_kappa_buchi.name: 遠野・カッパ淵（遠野物語の里）
tono_kappa_buchi.text: 遠野は岩手県の内陸部に位置する盆地の町で、民俗学者・柳田國男が1910年（明治43年）に著した『遠野物語』の舞台として全国に知られています。カッパ・ザシキワラシ・オシラサマなど日本の妖怪・精霊伝説の宝庫であり、カッパ淵は今もカッパが棲むと伝わる小川です。淵には小祠があり、全国からカッパ捕獲許可証を求める観光客が訪れます。柳田國男は地元の佐々木喜善から103話もの伝承を聞き書きし、それが日本民俗学の礎となりました。遠野市立博物館では遠野の自然と民俗を総合的に学ぶことができます。
tono_kappa_buchi.highlight: 「遠野物語」の舞台。カッパや座敷わらし伝説が息づく民話の里
tono_kappa_buchi.highlight_en: The setting of "Tono Monogatari". A village of folklore where legends of kappa and zashikiwarashi live on.
tono_kappa_buchi.text_en: Tono is a basin town located in the inland area of ​​Iwate Prefecture, and is known throughout the country as the setting for "Tono Monogatari," written in 1910 (Meiji 43) by folklorist Kunio Yanagita. It is a treasure trove of Japanese monsters and spirit legends such as the Kappa, Zashikiwarashi, and Oshirasama, and Kappafuchi is a stream where kappas still live. There is a small shrine at the deep end, and tourists come from all over the country to get a kappa hunting permit. Kunio Yanagida heard and wrote down 103 tales of folklore from a local man, Kiyoshi Sasaki, which became the foundation of Japanese folklore. At the Tono City Museum, you can comprehensively learn about Tono's nature and folklore.

kunohe_castle.name: 九戸城跡
kunohe_castle.text: 九戸城は岩手県北部に位置する戦国時代の山城で、天正19年（1591年）に起きた「九戸政実の乱」の舞台として知られています。九戸政実は南部宗家への反乱を起こし、豊臣秀吉が派遣した6万3000人もの大軍に抵抗しました。わずかな兵力で籠城した政実は23日間奮戦しましたが、開城後に捕らえられ処刑されました。この戦いは豊臣政権による東北仕置きの最後の局面であり、奥羽の戦国時代に終止符を打った歴史的事件です。城跡からは岩手山や馬淵川を見渡す眺望が広がり、石垣の一部が残っています。
kunohe_castle.highlight: 豊臣大軍6万に抵抗した九戸政実の乱の舞台。東北戦国の終幕の地
kunohe_castle.highlight_en: The stage of Kunohe Masazane's rebellion, which resisted Toyotomi's 60,000-strong army. The place where the Tohoku Sengoku period ended
kunohe_castle.text_en: Kunohe Castle is a mountain castle located in the northern part of Iwate Prefecture during the Sengoku period, and is known as the setting for the Kunohe Masazane Rebellion that occurred in 1591. Masazane Kunohe started a rebellion against the Nanbu family and resisted the 63,000-strong army sent by Toyotomi Hideyoshi. Masazane, who was besieged with a small force, fought bravely for 23 days, but was captured and executed after the castle was surrendered. This battle was the final phase of Tohoku's punishment by the Toyotomi government, and is a historical event that brought an end to the Sengoku period in Ou. The castle ruins offer a panoramic view of Mt. Iwate and the Mabuchi River, and some of the stone walls remain.

morioka_hachimangu.name: 盛岡八幡宮（南部氏の守護神）
morioka_hachimangu.kana: もりおかはちまんぐう
morioka_hachimangu.text: 盛岡八幡宮は江戸時代の延宝8年（1680年）、南部26代当主・重信が現在地に遷宮した盛岡の総鎮守です。南部藩の歴代藩主から手厚い保護を受け、城下町盛岡の精神的中心として機能してきました。境内の末社・天満宮には菅原道真が祀られ、受験生の合格祈願でも知られています。毎年9月の例大祭では流鏑馬や神輿行列が行われ、盛岡の秋の風物詩となっています。隣接する八幡公園からは岩手山の雄姿を望むことができ、南部氏が支配した盛岡の歴史を今に伝えています。
morioka_hachimangu.highlight: 南部藩が守護した盛岡の総鎮守。流鏑馬と岩手山の眺望で知られる
morioka_hachimangu.name_en: Morioka Hachimangu Shrine (guardian deity of the Nanbu clan)
morioka_hachimangu.highlight_en: The general guardian of Morioka, protected by the Nanbu domain. Known for Yabusame and the view of Mt. Iwate
morioka_hachimangu.text_en: Morioka Hachimangu Shrine is the general guardian of Morioka, and was moved to its current location by Shigenobu, the 26th head of the Nanbu clan, in 1680 during the Edo period. It received generous protection from successive lords of the Nanbu domain and has functioned as the spiritual center of the castle town of Morioka. The Tenmangu Shrine, a subsidiary shrine within the precincts, is dedicated to Sugawara no Michizane, and is also known for praying for the success of entrance exams. Every year in September, Yabusame and Mikoshi parades are held at the annual festival, which has become a typical autumn tradition in Morioka. From the adjacent Yahata Park, you can see the majestic view of Mt. Iwate, and you can still see the history of Morioka ruled by the Nanbu clan.

kakunodate_bukeyashiki.name: 角館武家屋敷通り
kakunodate_bukeyashiki.kana: かくのだてぶけやしきどおり
kakunodate_bukeyashiki.text: 角館は「みちのくの小京都」と呼ばれる秋田県仙北市の城下町で、江戸時代の武家屋敷が約80棟現存する貴重な歴史的景観地区です。芦名氏によって17世紀初頭に整備された町割りがほぼそのまま保存されており、重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に指定されています。黒板塀が続く内町（武家地）には、青柳家・岩橋家・石黒家などの武家屋敷が公開されており、当時の生活ぶりを体感できます。春には武家屋敷の庭に咲き誇るしだれ桜が有名で、一帯が桜のトンネルに包まれます。また、秋の枝垂れ桜の黄葉も見事です。
kakunodate_bukeyashiki.highlight: 江戸の武家屋敷80棟が現存。みちのくの小京都・春の枝垂れ桜が絶景
kakunodate_bukeyashiki.highlight_en: 80 Edo samurai residences still exist. Michinoku's Little Kyoto: Spectacular view of weeping cherry blossoms in spring
kakunodate_bukeyashiki.text_en: Kakunodate is a castle town in Semboku City, Akita Prefecture, known as ``Little Kyoto of Michinoku,'' and is a valuable historical scenic area with approximately 80 surviving samurai residences from the Edo period. The town layout laid out by the Ashina clan in the early 17th century has been preserved almost exactly as it was, and it has been designated as an Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings. The samurai residences of the Aoyagi family, Iwahashi family, Ishiguro family, and others are open to the public in the inner town (samurai area), which is lined with blackboard walls, and you can experience the lifestyle of the time. In spring, the garden of the samurai residence is famous for the weeping cherry blossoms that bloom in full bloom, and the whole area is covered in a tunnel of cherry blossoms. The yellow leaves of the weeping cherry blossoms in autumn are also spectacular.

oga_namahage.name: 男鹿半島・なまはげ館
oga_namahage.kana: おがはんとう・なまはげかん

transit.name: 男鹿なび「なまはげ館前」

oga_namahage.text: なまはげは男鹿半島に伝わる歳神の行事で、大晦日の夜に「泣く子はいねぇか！」と叫びながら鬼の面をかぶった男たちが各家を訪問し、怠け者や悪い子を戒める伝統です。2018年にはユネスコ無形文化遺産「来訪神：仮面・仮装の神々」の一つとして登録されました。なまはげ館では150面以上の多様ななまはげの面を展示し、地域ごとの違いが楽しめます。隣接する男鹿真山伝承館では実際のなまはげ行事を体験できます。男鹿半島には縄文時代から続く長い歴史があり、日本海に突き出た半島の景色も壮観です。
oga_namahage.highlight: ユネスコ無形文化遺産・なまはげの本場。150面の面を展示し行事を体験
oga_namahage.highlight_en: The home of Namahage, a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. Experience events with 150 masks on display
oga_namahage.text_en: Namahage is an annual festival that has been passed down on the Oga Peninsula, and is a tradition in which men wearing demon masks visit each house on the night of New Year's Eve, shouting, "No child is crying!" and admonishing lazy and bad children. In 2018, it was registered as one of the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage "Visiting Gods: Gods in Masks and Costumes." The Namahage Museum exhibits over 150 different Namahage masks, allowing you to enjoy the differences from region to region. At the adjacent Oga Shinzan Folklore Museum, you can experience an actual Namahage event. The Oga Peninsula has a long history dating back to the Jomon period, and the scenery of the peninsula jutting out into the Sea of ​​Japan is spectacular.

akita_castle_ruins.name: 秋田城跡（城介秋田城）

transit.name: バス「秋田城跡歴史資料館前」

akita_castle_ruins.text: 秋田城は奈良時代（733年頃）に設置された律令制の城柵（じょうさく）で、大和朝廷が蝦夷との境界に設けた北方の軍事・行政拠点でした。発掘調査によって、古代水洗トイレ遺構が日本最古の木製水洗トイレとして確認され、当時の衛生文化の高さを示しています。平安時代まで約200年間機能した秋田城は、その後廃絶しましたが、現在は史跡公園として整備され、当時の建物が復元されています。城の周辺では古代の役人が生活した痕跡が次々と発見されており、東北支配の重要な歴史を物語っています。
akita_castle_ruins.highlight: 奈良時代の北方拠点・律令制城柵。日本最古の水洗トイレ遺構が出土
akita_castle_ruins.highlight_en: Ritsuryo castle fence, a northern base during the Nara period. Japan's oldest flush toilet remains unearthed
akita_castle_ruins.text_en: Akita Castle was a castle fence built in the Nara period (around 733) under the Ritsuryo system, and was a northern military and administrative base established by the Yamato court on the border with Ezo. Through excavations, the remains of an ancient flush toilet were confirmed to be the oldest wooden flush toilet in Japan, demonstrating the high level of sanitary culture at the time. Akita Castle, which functioned for about 200 years until the Heian period, has since been abandoned, but it is now maintained as a historical park, and the buildings from that time have been restored. Traces of ancient officials living there have been discovered one after another around the castle, which tells the story of the important history of Tohoku domination.

oyu_stone_circle.name: 大湯環状列石（縄文遺跡）
oyu_stone_circle.kana: おおゆかんじょうれっせき

transit.name: 鹿角市民バス「大湯環状列石前」

oyu_stone_circle.text: 大湯環状列石は秋田県鹿角市にある縄文時代後期（約4000年前）のストーンサークルで、2021年に「北海道・北東北の縄文遺跡群」の構成資産の一つとしてユネスコ世界文化遺産に登録されました。「万座」と「野中堂」の2つの環状列石があり、中心の日時計状組石が夏至に沈む太陽の方向と一致することから、縄文人が精巧な天文知識を持っていたことが分かります。その配置や規模から、多くの人が集まった祭祀・埋葬の場と考えられ、縄文時代の精神世界を今に伝える貴重な遺跡です。
oyu_stone_circle.highlight: 世界文化遺産・縄文のストーンサークル。夏至の日没と一致する天文遺跡
oyu_stone_circle.highlight_en: Jomon stone circle, a world cultural heritage site. Astronomical ruins that coincide with the summer solstice sunset
oyu_stone_circle.text_en: The Oyu Stone Circles are stone circles from the late Jomon period (approximately 4000 years ago) located in Kazuno City, Akita Prefecture, and were registered as a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site in 2021 as one of the constituent assets of the "Jomon Ruins in Hokkaido and Northern Tohoku." There are two stone rings, ``Manza'' and ``Nonakado.'' The sundial-shaped stones in the center coincide with the direction of the sun setting on the summer solstice, indicating that the Jomon people had sophisticated astronomical knowledge. Due to its layout and size, it is thought to have been a place where many people gathered for rituals and burials, and is a valuable ruin that conveys the spiritual world of the Jomon period.

yokote_castle_akita.name: 横手城跡（かまくらの里）
yokote_castle_akita.text: 横手城は秋田県横手市の中心にある小高い丘の上に築かれた城で、戦国時代に小野寺氏の居城として機能しました。江戸時代には秋田藩の支城となり、城下町横手が整備されました。現在の天守は昭和40年代に再建された展望台で、横手盆地を見渡す眺望が楽しめます。横手市は「かまくら」で有名な町でもあります。毎年2月に行われるかまくら祭りは700年以上の歴史を持ち、雪国の水神信仰と子どもたちの遊びが融合した独特の行事として国の重要無形民俗文化財に指定されています。
yokote_castle_akita.highlight: かまくら発祥の城下町横手。700年以上の雪国の伝統行事を今に伝える
yokote_castle_akita.highlight_en: Yokote is the castle town where Kamakura originated. Passing on the traditional events of the snow country for over 700 years
yokote_castle_akita.text_en: Yokote Castle is a castle built on a small hill in the center of Yokote City, Akita Prefecture, and served as the residence of the Onodera clan during the Sengoku period. During the Edo period, it became a branch castle of the Akita clan, and the castle town of Yokote was developed. The current castle tower is an observation deck that was rebuilt in the 1960s, and you can enjoy a panoramic view of the Yokote Basin. Yokote City is also famous for its Kamakura (Kamakura). The Kamakura Festival, which is held every February, has a history of over 700 years, and has been designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property as a unique event that combines the snowy country's water god belief and children's play.

tazawa_lake.name: 田沢湖・辰子像（秋田の伝説）
tazawa_lake.kana: たざわこ・たつこぞう
tazawa_lake.text: 田沢湖は日本最深の湖（水深423m）で、透明度が高く神秘的なコバルトブルーの水を湛えています。湖畔には「辰子像」と呼ばれる金色の女神像が建ち、田沢湖の美しさを独占しようと龍に変身した伝説の美女・辰子をモデルにしています。辰子伝説は秋田の代表的な民話で、永遠の美しさと引き換えに人間としての生を失った悲話として語り継がれています。戦時中には酸性の玉川水系を引き込む農業政策のためにマス類が絶滅するという悲劇もありましたが、現在は水質改善が進み、魚類の復活が進んでいます。
tazawa_lake.highlight: 日本最深のコバルトブルーの湖。辰子伝説の美女が龍に変身した伝説の地
tazawa_lake.highlight_en: Japan's deepest cobalt blue lake. The legendary place where Tatsuko, the legendary beauty, transformed into a dragon
tazawa_lake.text_en: Lake Tazawa is Japan's deepest lake (423m deep), filled with highly transparent and mysterious cobalt blue water. There is a golden statue of the goddess called ``Tatsuko Statue'' on the shore of the lake, modeled after Tatsuko, the legendary beauty who transformed into a dragon in order to monopolize the beauty of Lake Tazawa. The legend of Tatsuko is a representative folk tale of Akita, and is passed down as a tragic tale of a woman who lost her life as a human in exchange for eternal beauty. During the war, there was a tragedy in which trout species became extinct due to agricultural policies that drew in the acidic Tamagawa water system, but now water quality has improved and fish species are making a comeback.

yuzawa_inaniwa.name: 湯沢・稲庭城跡（稲庭うどんの里）
yuzawa_inaniwa.kana: ゆざわ・いなにわじょうあと
yuzawa_inaniwa.text: 稲庭城は秋田県南部、湯沢市稲庭地区にあった戦国時代の山城で、小野寺氏の支城として機能しました。城跡からは仙北平野を見渡す眺望が広がります。稲庭地区は日本三大うどんの一つ「稲庭うどん」の発祥地として知られており、細く白くつやのある手延べ麺は江戸時代に秋田佐竹藩への献上品として名声を得ました。約400年の伝統を持つ製麺技術は今も職人の手仕事で守られており、地区内の製麺所では製造工程を見学できます。湯沢市は「七夕絵どうろうまつり」でも有名で、江戸時代から続く伝統行事が毎年8月に行われます。
yuzawa_inaniwa.highlight: 日本三大うどん・稲庭うどん400年の発祥地。小野寺氏の稲庭城跡も残る
yuzawa_inaniwa.highlight_en: The birthplace of Japan's three major udon noodles, Inaniwa udon, for 400 years. The ruins of Onodera's Inaniwa Castle also remain.
yuzawa_inaniwa.text_en: Inaniwa Castle is a mountain castle located in the Inaniwa district of Yuzawa City in southern Akita Prefecture during the Sengoku period, and served as a branch castle of the Onodera clan. From the castle ruins, you can enjoy a panoramic view of the Senboku Plain. The Inaniwa area is known as the birthplace of Inaniwa udon, one of Japan's three major types of udon, and its thin, white, glossy, hand-pulled noodles gained fame during the Edo period as a gift to the Akita Satake clan. The noodle-making technique, which has a tradition of about 400 years, is still preserved by the handiwork of craftsmen, and you can observe the manufacturing process at noodle factories in the area. Yuzawa City is also famous for the Tanabata Edorou Festival, a traditional event that has been held since the Edo period every August.

dewa_sanzan_haguro.name: 出羽三山・羽黒山（山岳信仰の聖地）
dewa_sanzan_haguro.kana: でわさんざん・はぐろさん
dewa_sanzan_haguro.text: 出羽三山（羽黒山・月山・湯殿山）は山形県の霊山で、崇峻天皇の皇子・蜂子皇子が推古天皇の時代に開山したと伝わります。羽黒山には樹齢1000年を超える爺杉がそびえ、2446段の石段を上ると江戸時代初期の建築である国宝・五重塔が出迎えます。山伏修行の地として知られ、現在も「秋の峰」「春の峰」と呼ばれる厳しい修行が行われています。松尾芭蕉も『おくのほそ道』の旅で出羽三山を訪れ、「涼しさや ほの三日月の 羽黒山」と詠んでいます。生・死・再生を象徴する三山巡礼は今も多くの修験者が継承しています。
dewa_sanzan_haguro.highlight: 崇峻天皇の皇子が開山した山岳霊場。国宝五重塔と芭蕉ゆかりの古刹
dewa_sanzan_haguro.name_en: Dewa Sanzan/Mt. Haguro (sacred place for mountain worship)
dewa_sanzan_haguro.highlight_en: A sacred mountain site founded by the prince of Emperor Sushun. National Treasure Five-storied Pagoda and Old Temple Associated with Basho
dewa_sanzan_haguro.text_en: The Dewa Sanzan (Mt. Haguro, Mt. Gassan, and Mt. Yudono) are sacred mountains in Yamagata Prefecture, and are said to have been founded by Prince Hachiko, the son of Emperor Suushun, during the reign of Emperor Suiko. Mt. Haguro is dominated by a cedar tree that is over 1,000 years old, and as you climb the 2,446 stone steps, you will be greeted by a national treasure, a five-storied pagoda built in the early Edo period. It is known as a place for Yamabushi training, and even today, severe training is carried out called ``Autumn Mine'' and ``Spring Mine.'' Matsuo Basho also visited Dewa Sanzan on his trip ``Oku no Hosomichi'' and wrote a poem about it as ``Haguro Mountain with its coolness and warm crescent moon.'' The Sanzan pilgrimage, which symbolizes life, death, and rebirth, is still carried on by many ascetic ascetics.

shonai_tsuruoka.name: 荘内神社・鶴岡城跡
shonai_tsuruoka.kana: しょうないじんじゃ・つるおかじょうあと
shonai_tsuruoka.text: 鶴岡城は庄内地方を支配した酒井氏の居城で、江戸時代を通じて酒井家14万石の藩庁として機能しました。明治維新後に廃城となりましたが、本丸跡には藩主酒井家の先祖を祀る荘内神社が建てられ、鶴岡公園として市民に親しまれています。藩学「致道館」は現在も建物が残り、日本最古の学校建築の一つとして重要文化財に指定されています。鶴岡市は「つるおか食文化市場FOODEVER」にも象徴されるように、ユネスコ食文化創造都市に認定された食の都でもあります。出羽三山への玄関口としても重要な拠点です。
shonai_tsuruoka.highlight: 酒井氏14万石の城下町鶴岡。ユネスコ食文化創造都市・出羽三山の拠点
shonai_tsuruoka.highlight_en: Tsuruoka is a castle town where the Sakai clan has 140,000 koku. Base of Dewa Sanzan, UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy
shonai_tsuruoka.text_en: Tsuruoka Castle was the residence of the Sakai clan, who ruled the Shonai region, and throughout the Edo period it functioned as the domain office of the Sakai clan, which was worth 140,000 koku. After the Meiji Restoration, the castle was abandoned, but Shonai Shrine was built on the site of the main enclosure to enshrine the ancestors of the Sakai family, the feudal lord, and is now popular among citizens as Tsuruoka Park. The Chidokan building for domain studies still stands today, and is designated as an important cultural property as one of the oldest school buildings in Japan. Tsuruoka City is also a food capital recognized as a UNESCO Creative City of Food Culture, as symbolized by the Tsuruoka Food Culture Market FOODEVER. It is also an important base as the gateway to the Dewa Sanzan.

shirakawa_komine_castle.name: 白河小峰城
shirakawa_komine_castle.kana: しらかわこみねじょう
shirakawa_komine_castle.text: 白河小峰城は南北朝時代の1340年頃に結城親朝が築いたとされ、江戸時代に丹羽長重が石垣造りの近世城郭に改修しました。城は奥州街道と水戸街道が交わる要衝に位置し、「東北の玄関口」として幕末まで機能し続けました。幕末の1868年（戊辰戦争）には官軍との激戦の末に落城し、奥羽列藩同盟の抵抗拠点として重要な役割を果たしました。現在は三重櫓と前御門が復元されており、東北では数少ない木造復元天守として人気を集めています。白河市の中心にそびえるその姿は、城下町の象徴として市民に愛されています。
shirakawa_komine_castle.highlight: 奥州の玄関口・東北数少ない木造復元天守。戊辰戦争で激戦を経た要衝
shirakawa_komine_castle.highlight_en: The gateway to Oshu and one of the few restored wooden castle towers in the Tohoku region. A strategic point that was the site of a fierce battle during the Boshin War
shirakawa_komine_castle.text_en: Shirakawa Komine Castle is said to have been built by Chikatomo Yuki around 1340 during the Nanbokucho period, and was renovated into an early modern castle built with stone walls by Niwa Nagashige in the Edo period. The castle was located at the strategic point where Oshu Kaido and Mito Kaido intersect, and continued to function as the "gateway to Tohoku" until the end of the Edo period. At the end of the Edo period in 1868 (Boshin War), the castle fell after a fierce battle with the government army, and played an important role as a resistance base for the Ou clan alliance. Currently, the triple turret and front gate have been restored, and it is gaining popularity as one of the few restored wooden castle towers in Tohoku. Its appearance towering over the center of Shirakawa City is loved by the citizens as a symbol of the castle town.

aizu_byakkotai.name: 飯盛山・白虎隊自刃の地
aizu_byakkotai.kana: いいもりやま・びゃっこたいじじんのち
aizu_byakkotai.text: 飯盛山は1868年（戊辰戦争）に、会津藩の少年隊「白虎隊」が集団自刃した悲劇の地として知られています。白虎隊は15〜17歳の少年たちで編成された会津藩の武士集団で、戦場から逃れてきた20名が飯盛山に登り、煙に包まれた会津城（鶴ヶ城）を見て「城が落ちた」と誤認し、藩の滅亡を悲しんで自刃しました（実際には城は健在でした）。うち1名は奇跡的に生還しました。山頂には白虎隊の墓と銅像が並び、イタリアのムッソリーニが贈った記念碑も立っています。今なお多くの学生が修学旅行で訪れ、「忠義と悲劇」の歴史を学びます。
aizu_byakkotai.highlight: 15〜17歳の白虎隊20名が自刃した悲劇の地。城を誤認した少年たちの忠義
aizu_byakkotai.highlight_en: The place of tragedy where 20 Byakkotai members aged 15 to 17 committed suicide. The loyalty of the boys who misidentified the castle
aizu_byakkotai.text_en: Iimoriyama is known as the site of a tragic incident in 1868 (the Boshin War), where the Aizu clan's boys' troop, the Byakkotai, committed mass suicide. The Byakkotai was a samurai group of the Aizu clan made up of boys between the ages of 15 and 17. Twenty of them escaped from the battlefield, climbed Mt. Iimori, saw Aizu Castle (Tsuruga Castle) shrouded in smoke, mistakenly thought that the castle had fallen, and committed suicide out of sadness over the fall of the clan (in reality, the castle was still standing). One of them miraculously survived. At the top of the mountain, there are graves and bronze statues of the Byakkotai, and there is also a monument given by Italy's Mussolini. Many students still visit on school trips to learn about the history of "loyalty and tragedy."

miharu_takizakura.name: 三春滝桜（樹齢1000年超）
miharu_takizakura.text: 三春滝桜は福島県三春町にある樹齢1000年以上のエドヒガンザクラで、日本三大桜の一つに数えられ、国の天然記念物に指定されています。樹高は約13.5m、枝張りは東西22m・南北18mに達し、四方に垂れ下がる枝が滝のように見えることから「滝桜」の名がつきました。推古天皇の時代に植えられたとも、源義家が東征の際に立ち寄ったとも伝わります。毎年4月中旬に見頃を迎え、夜間ライトアップ期間には多くの観光客が訪れます。三春町は戊辰戦争では早期に新政府軍に降伏したことで城下町が守られ、今も古い家並みが残っています。
miharu_takizakura.highlight: 樹齢1000年超・日本三大桜のひとつ。滝のように垂れ咲く国指定天然記念物
miharu_takizakura.highlight_en: Over 1000 years old and one of Japan's three major cherry blossoms. A nationally designated natural monument with waterfall-like blooms
miharu_takizakura.text_en: Miharu Takizakura is an Edohiganzakura tree that is over 1,000 years old and is located in Miharu Town, Fukushima Prefecture.It is counted as one of Japan's three major cherry blossoms and is designated as a national natural monument. The tree is approximately 13.5m tall, and its branches reach 22m from east to west and 18m from north to south.The tree is named ``Takizakura'' because its branches that hang down in all directions look like waterfalls. It is said that it was planted during the reign of Emperor Suiko, and that Minamoto no Yoshiie stopped by during his expedition to the east. The best time to see them is in mid-April every year, and many tourists visit during the night illumination period. Miharu surrendered to the new government forces early in the Boshin War, so the castle town was protected, and many of the old houses still remain.

inawashiro_castle_ruins.name: 猪苗代城跡（亀ヶ城）
inawashiro_castle_ruins.kana: いなわしろじょうあと
inawashiro_castle_ruins.text: 猪苗代城（亀ヶ城）は福島県猪苗代町に位置する中世の山城で、南北朝時代の1340年代に猪苗代氏が築いたとされています。猪苗代氏はその後、伊達氏や蘆名氏の支配下に入り、蒲生氏郷・上杉景勝・加藤嘉明などが代々城主を務めました。江戸時代には会津藩の支城となり、会津盆地の東口を守る要衝として機能しました。城跡からは磐梯山と猪苗代湖を望む眺望が絶景で、現在は史跡公園として整備されています。城の麓には野口英世の出身地・猪苗代町が広がり、野口英世記念館も近くにあります。
inawashiro_castle_ruins.highlight: 磐梯山・猪苗代湖を見下ろす中世の要衝。蒲生氏郷・上杉氏も統治した城
inawashiro_castle_ruins.highlight_en: A medieval strategic point overlooking Mt. Bandai and Lake Inawashiro. A castle that was also ruled by the Ujisato Gamo and Uesugi clans.
inawashiro_castle_ruins.text_en: Inawashiro Castle (Kamegajo) is a medieval mountain castle located in Inawashiro Town, Fukushima Prefecture, and is said to have been built by the Inawashiro clan in the 1340s during the Nanbokucho period. The Inawashiro clan then came under the control of the Date clan and the Ashina clan, and Ujisato Gamo, Kagekatsu Uesugi, Yoshiaki Kato, and others served as the castle's lords for generations. During the Edo period, it became a branch castle of the Aizu clan and functioned as a strategic point protecting the east entrance of the Aizu basin. The castle ruins offer a spectacular view of Mt. Bandai and Lake Inawashiro, and are currently maintained as a historical park. At the foot of the castle lies Inawashiro Town, the birthplace of Hideyo Noguchi, and the Hideyo Noguchi Memorial Museum is also nearby.

sado_kinzan.name: 佐渡金山（世界遺産候補）

transit.name: 両津港からバス「金山前」

sado_kinzan.text: 佐渡金山は江戸時代に日本最大の金銀山として栄えた鉱山で、採掘された金・銀は幕府の財政を長年にわたり支えました。1601年（慶長6年）に本格開採が始まり、最盛期には年間400kgの金を産出しました。過去に流人の地でもあった佐渡には、世阿弥（能楽の大成者）や日蓮（日蓮宗の開祖）なども流刑に処されています。明治以降も近代採掘が続き、1989年の閉山まで約400年間掘り続けられました。現在は観光施設として公開されており、江戸時代の手掘り坑道や近代の機械採掘坑道を見学できます。世界遺産登録も申請されています。
sado_kinzan.highlight: 江戸幕府の財政を支えた日本最大の金銀山。世阿弥・日蓮が流刑された島
sado_kinzan.highlight_en: Japan's largest gold and silver mine, which supported the finances of the Edo Shogunate. The island where Zeami and Nichiren were exiled
sado_kinzan.text_en: Sado Gold Mine was a mine that prospered as Japan's largest gold and silver mine during the Edo period, and the gold and silver mined supported the finances of the Shogunate for many years. Full-scale mining began in 1601 (Keicho 6), and at its peak it produced 400 kg of gold annually. In the past, Sado was also a place of exile, including Zeami (a great Nohgaku master) and Nichiren (founder of the Nichiren sect). Modern mining continued even after the Meiji era, and continued to be mined for about 400 years until the mine was closed in 1989. It is currently open to the public as a tourist facility, and you can tour the hand-dug mines from the Edo period and the modern mechanical mines. It has also been applied for registration as a World Heritage Site.

niigata_old_city.name: 新潟市・旧新潟税関（開港五港の一つ）
niigata_old_city.kana: にいがたし・きゅうにいがたぜいかん

transit.name: JR新潟駅からバス「みなとぴあ前」

niigata_old_city.text: 新潟は1869年（明治2年）に開港した「開港五港」の一つで、日本海側唯一の開港地として対外貿易の窓口となりました。旧新潟税関庁舎は明治初期の洋風建築で、現在は博物館として公開されています。新潟港には幕末の戊辰戦争時に旧幕府軍と新政府軍が激突した歴史もあり、北越戦争の激戦地でもありました。近代には多くの移民が新潟港からブラジル・アメリカへ旅立ち、日本のアメリカへの玄関口として機能しました。みなとぴあ（新潟市歴史博物館）では新潟の水運と商業の歴史を詳しく学ぶことができます。
niigata_old_city.highlight: 日本海側唯一の開港五港。旧幕府・新政府の北越戦争激戦地の要衝
niigata_old_city.name_en: Niigata City/Former Niigata Customs (one of the five opened ports)
niigata_old_city.highlight_en: The only five open ports on the Sea of ​​Japan. A key location of the fierce battle between the former Shogunate and the new government during the Hokuetsu War.
niigata_old_city.text_en: Niigata was one of the "Five Open Ports" that opened in 1869 (Meiji 2), and as the only open port on the Sea of ​​Japan, it became a window for foreign trade. The former Niigata Customs Building is a Western-style building from the early Meiji period, and is currently open to the public as a museum. Niigata Port has a history of clashes between the former shogunate army and the new government army during the Boshin War at the end of the Edo period, and was also the site of a fierce battle during the Hokuetsu War. In modern times, many immigrants departed from Niigata Port to Brazil and America, and it served as the gateway for Japan to America. At Minato Pia (Niigata City History Museum), you can learn more about Niigata's water transport and commercial history.

murakami_castle.name: 村上城跡（臥牛山城）
murakami_castle.text: 村上城は新潟県村上市にそびえる臥牛山（標高135m）の山頂に築かれた山城で、戦国時代から江戸時代にかけて越後北部の要衝として機能しました。本丸石垣は江戸時代初期のもので、現在もほぼ完全な姿で残っており、その技術水準の高さが評価されています。村上藩は松平・内藤などの家が治め、城下町には武家屋敷・町人地が整備されました。村上市は「村上茶」と「塩引き鮭」で有名な城下町で、毎年10月に行われる「城下町村上 町屋の人形さま巡り」では江戸時代の人形が各町屋に飾られます。
murakami_castle.highlight: 越後北部の要衝・臥牛山城。石垣がほぼ完全な姿で残る希少な山城
murakami_castle.highlight_en: Gagyusuyama Castle is a key location in northern Echigo. A rare mountain castle with almost intact stone walls.
murakami_castle.text_en: Murakami Castle is a mountain castle built on the summit of Mt. Gagyu (135m above sea level) in Murakami City, Niigata Prefecture, and served as a strategic point in northern Echigo from the Sengoku period to the Edo period. The Honmaru stone wall dates back to the early Edo period and remains almost intact today, and its high level of technology has been praised. The Murakami clan was ruled by families such as Matsudaira and Naito, and samurai residences and townspeople were established in the castle town. Murakami City is a castle town famous for ``Murakami Tea'' and ``Salted Salmon.'' Edo period dolls are displayed in each townhouse during the ``Castle Town Murakami Machiya Doll Tour'' held every October.

joetsu_kota_jinja.name: 直江津・居多神社（親鸞上人の流刑地）
joetsu_kota_jinja.kana: なおえつ・こたじんじゃ

transit.name: えちごトキめき鉄道「黒井」

joetsu_kota_jinja.text: 居多神社は越後国一宮で、鎌倉時代には流刑に処された親鸞上人がこの地を訪れ、神前で「片葉の葦」の奇跡を起こしたと伝わります。親鸞は1207年（承元の法難）に越後国府（現在の上越市直江津）に流刑となり、約7年間をこの地で過ごしました。流刑中に恵信尼と結婚し、在家仏教の実践者として民衆に接した経験が浄土真宗の思想形成に大きく影響しました。境内には親鸞上人の像が立ち、近くには上人が住んだとされる居多ヶ浜跡もあります。春日山城跡（上杉謙信の城）も近く、越後の歴史を辿るルートの一つになっています。
joetsu_kota_jinja.highlight: 浄土真宗の開祖・親鸞が7年間流刑された越後の地。片葉の葦の奇跡伝説
joetsu_kota_jinja.highlight_en: Echigo is where Shinran, the founder of Jodo Shinshu Buddhism, was exiled for seven years. The legend of the miracle of the single-leafed reed
joetsu_kota_jinja.text_en: Ita Shrine is an Ichinomiya shrine in Echigo Province, and it is said that Shinran Shonin, who was exiled during the Kamakura period, visited this place and performed the miracle of the ``one-leaf reed'' in front of the shrine. Shinran was exiled to Echigo Kokufu (present-day Naoetsu, Joetsu City) in 1207 (Jogen no Nōran), where he spent approximately seven years. During his exile, he married Eshinni, and his experience interacting with the people as a practitioner of lay Buddhism greatly influenced the formation of his thoughts on Jodo Shinshu Buddhism. There is a statue of Shinran Shonin in the precincts, and nearby is the Itagahama ruins where Shonin is said to have lived. The ruins of Kasugayama Castle (Uesugi Kenshin's castle) are also nearby, making it one of the routes to trace Echigo's history.

tochio_castle.name: 栃尾城跡（上杉謙信 初陣の地）
tochio_castle.text: 栃尾城は越後（新潟県）の山城で、上杉謙信（当時は長尾景虎）が14歳のとき初めて戦場に立った「栃尾城の戦い」（1543年）の舞台です。兵力で劣る景虎は夜襲と機転で敵を撃退し、「越後の龍」としての名声を確立する第一歩を踏み出しました。その後も謙信は春日山城を本拠に信濃・関東・北陸へ積極的に遠征し、武田信玄との川中島の戦いで知られる戦国最強の武将の一人となりました。栃尾市街は「栃尾の油揚げ」で有名で、普通の3倍以上の大きさのジャンボ油揚げが名物です。
tochio_castle.highlight: 14歳の上杉謙信が初陣を飾った越後の山城。越後の龍の出発点となった地
tochio_castle.name_en: Tochio Castle ruins (place of Uesugi Kenshin's first battle)
tochio_castle.highlight_en: Echigo Yamashiro, where 14-year-old Uesugi Kenshin made his first appearance. The place where Echigo's dragons started
tochio_castle.text_en: Tochio Castle is a mountain castle in Echigo (Niigata Prefecture), and is the setting for the Battle of Tochio Castle (1543), where Uesugi Kenshin (then known as Kagetora Nagao) fought his first battle at the age of 14. Kagetora, who was inferior in military strength, repelled the enemy with night attacks and quick wits, and took the first step toward establishing his reputation as the ``Dragon of Echigo.'' After that, Kenshin continued to use Kasugayama Castle as his base and actively went on expeditions to Shinano, Kanto, and Hokuriku, and became one of the strongest military commanders of the Sengoku period, known for his battle with Takeda Shingen at Kawanakajima. Tochio city is famous for ``Tochio's fried tofu'', and its specialty is jumbo fried tofu that is more than three times the size of normal tofu.

niigata_rekishi_hakubutsukan.name: 新潟市歴史博物館（みなとぴあ）
niigata_rekishi_hakubutsukan.kana: にいがたしれきしはくぶつかん
niigata_rekishi_hakubutsukan.text: 新潟市歴史博物館（みなとぴあ）は信濃川と日本海の交わる場所に立つ博物館で、港町・新潟の歴史と文化を総合的に紹介しています。隣接する旧新潟税関庁舎と旧第四銀行住吉町支店は明治・大正期の洋風建築として国の重要文化財に指定されています。新潟は古来より北前船の寄港地として大陸・北海道との交易を担い、商人文化が栄えました。幕末開港後は外国人居留地が設けられ、近代化の波が押し寄せました。博物館では縄文時代から現代に至る新潟の歩みを分かりやすく展示しており、港の歴史と先人の知恵を学ぶことができます。
niigata_rekishi_hakubutsukan.highlight: 港町新潟の歴史博物館。旧税関・旧銀行など明治洋風建築群と一体の施設
niigata_rekishi_hakubutsukan.highlight_en: A history museum in the port city of Niigata. Facilities integrated with Meiji Western-style buildings such as the former customs house and old bank
niigata_rekishi_hakubutsukan.text_en: Niigata City History Museum (Minatopia) is a museum located at the intersection of the Shinano River and the Sea of ​​Japan, and comprehensively introduces the history and culture of the port city of Niigata. The adjacent former Niigata Customs Office building and the former Daishi Bank Sumiyoshicho branch are designated as important cultural properties of the country as Western-style buildings from the Meiji and Taisho periods. Since ancient times, Niigata has been a port of call for Kitamaebune ships, responsible for trade with the mainland and Hokkaido, and a flourishing merchant culture. After the port opened at the end of the Edo period, a foreign settlement was established and a wave of modernization swept through. The museum exhibits the history of Niigata from the Jomon period to the present in an easy-to-understand manner, allowing you to learn about the history of the port and the wisdom of our ancestors.

sado_island_exile.name: 佐渡島・順徳天皇配流地（真野御陵）
sado_island_exile.kana: さどしま・じゅんとくてんのうはいるち

transit.name: 新潟交通佐渡バス「真野」

sado_island_exile.text: 佐渡島は日本海に浮かぶ離島で、古来より流刑の地として知られています。鎌倉時代の順徳天皇は1221年の承久の乱で後鳥羽上皇とともに挙兵したものの敗れ、21歳で佐渡に配流されました。島で22年を過ごし43歳で没した天皇の墓・真野御陵が今も残ります。その他にも日蓮（鎌倉時代）・世阿弥（室町時代）など多くの文化人が佐渡に流され、島の文化発展に大きく貢献しました。特に世阿弥が佐渡で完成させたとされる「風姿花伝」は能楽の理論書として現代に伝わっています。
sado_island_exile.highlight: 順徳天皇・日蓮・世阿弥など多くの文化人が流刑された日本海の離島
sado_island_exile.name_en: Sado Island, Emperor Juntoku's exile (Mano Mausoleum)
sado_island_exile.highlight_en: A remote island in the Sea of ​​Japan where many cultural figures such as Emperor Juntoku, Nichiren, and Zeami were exiled.
sado_island_exile.text_en: Sado Island is a remote island in the Sea of ​​Japan, and has been known as a place of exile since ancient times. Emperor Juntoku of the Kamakura period raised an army with the retired Emperor Gotoba during the Jokyu War in 1221, but was defeated and exiled to Sado at the age of 21. The Mano Mausoleum, the tomb of the Emperor who lived on the island for 22 years before dying at the age of 43, still remains. Many other cultural figures, including Nichiren (Kamakura period) and Zeami (Muromachi period), were exiled to Sado and greatly contributed to the island's cultural development. In particular, ``Fushikaden'', which Zeami is said to have completed in Sado, has been handed down to the present day as a theoretical book on Nohgaku.

takaoka_castle.name: 高岡城跡・古城公園
takaoka_castle.kana: たかおかじょうあと・こじょうこうえん

transit.name: あいの風とやま鉄道「高岡」

takaoka_castle.text: 高岡城は1609年（慶長14年）に前田利長が築いた平城で、前田家2代目として加賀藩の実権を握った利長が晩年を過ごした城です。しかし利長の死後わずか2年で廃城となり、以後は「高岡の森」として市民の憩いの場となりました。現在は国の史跡に指定され、土塁と水濠が当時の姿をよく残す古城公園となっています。高岡市は400年の伝統を持つ高岡銅器の産地で、大仏・梵鐘・美術工芸品などが作られています。高岡大仏は奈良・鎌倉と並ぶ「日本三大仏」に数えられることもある銅造の大仏です。
takaoka_castle.highlight: 前田利長が晩年を過ごした城。400年の銅器産地・高岡大仏も近く
takaoka_castle.highlight_en: The castle where Toshinaga Maeda spent his later years. Takaoka Daibutsu, a 400-year-old copper production site, is also nearby.
takaoka_castle.text_en: Takaoka Castle is a flat castle built by Maeda Toshinaga in 1609 (Keicho 14), and is the castle where Toshinaga, the second generation of the Maeda family and in charge of the Kaga clan, spent his later years. However, just two years after Toshinaga's death, the castle was abandoned, and since then it has become a place of relaxation for citizens as the ``Takaoka Forest.'' It is now designated as a national historic site, and is an old castle park where the earthworks and water moat still retain their original appearance. Takaoka City is the production center of Takaoka copperware, which has a 400-year tradition, and produces things such as the Great Buddha, temple bells, and arts and crafts. Takaoka Daibutsu is a large bronze Buddha statue that is sometimes counted as one of Japan's three great Buddhas, along with Nara and Kamakura.

zuiryuji_temple.name: 瑞龍寺（国宝の禅刹・高岡）

transit.name: あいの風とやま鉄道「高岡」

zuiryuji_temple.text: 瑞龍寺は高岡市に位置する曹洞宗の名刹で、加賀藩二代藩主・前田利長の菩提を弔うために三代藩主・光高が20年以上かけて造営した壮大な伽藍です。山門・仏殿・法堂の三棟が国宝に指定され、回廊・大庫裏・禅堂など多くの建物が重要文化財となっています。特に仏殿の鉛瓦は北陸の豪雪に耐えるための工夫であり、江戸初期の建築技術の粋が結集されています。境内は厳かな空気に満ち、参道の石畳・山門・仏殿が整然と並ぶ様子は日本の禅宗建築を代表する景観の一つです。
zuiryuji_temple.highlight: 前田利長の菩提寺。山門・仏殿・法堂が国宝の江戸初期禅宗建築の傑作
zuiryuji_temple.name_en: Zuiryuji Temple (National Treasure Zen Temple, Takaoka)
zuiryuji_temple.highlight_en: Maeda Toshinaga's family temple. A masterpiece of early Edo Zen Buddhism architecture whose main gate, Buddhist hall, and Buddhist hall are national treasures.
zuiryuji_temple.text_en: Zuiryu-ji Temple is a famous temple of the Soto sect located in Takaoka City, and is a magnificent temple built over 20 years by Mitsutaka, the third lord of the Kaga domain, to pray for the memory of Toshinaga Maeda, the second lord of the Kaga domain. The three buildings, the Sanmon, Butsuden, and Dharma Hall, have been designated as national treasures, and many other buildings, including the cloister, the Okuri, and the Zendo, are important cultural properties. In particular, the lead tiles in the Buddhist temple were designed to withstand the heavy snowfall of the Hokuriku region, and are a culmination of the best architectural techniques of the early Edo period. The precincts are filled with a solemn atmosphere, and the stone pavement of the approach, the Sanmon gate, and the Buddha hall are lined up in an orderly manner, making it one of the representative landscapes of Japanese Zen architecture.

gokayama_gasshozukuri.name: 五箇山合掌造り集落（世界遺産）
gokayama_gasshozukuri.kana: ごかやまがっしょうづくりしゅうらく
gokayama_gasshozukuri.text: 五箇山は富山県南砺市の深山にある秘境の集落で、白川郷とともに1995年にユネスコ世界文化遺産に登録されました。急傾斜の茅葺き屋根が特徴の合掌造り建物は、豪雪地帯での生活の知恵から生まれた建築様式で、内部では養蚕・塩硝製造などが行われていました。加賀藩の火薬原料である硝石の一大生産地として、外部との接触を禁じられた閉鎖的な山村でもありました。現在も人々が生活しながら伝統を守り続けており、世界でも珍しい「生きている世界遺産」です。冬の雪に包まれた合掌造りの景観は特に美しく、多くの観光客が訪れます。
gokayama_gasshozukuri.highlight: 世界文化遺産の合掌造り集落。加賀藩の火薬原料・硝石生産の秘境の村
gokayama_gasshozukuri.highlight_en: A gassho-zukuri village designated as a world cultural heritage site. An unexplored village where the Kaga clan produces raw materials for gunpowder and saltpeter.
gokayama_gasshozukuri.text_en: Gokayama is a hidden village in the deep mountains of Nanto City, Toyama Prefecture, and was registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1995 along with Shirakawa-go. The gassho-zukuri building, characterized by its steeply sloping thatched roof, is an architectural style born from the wisdom of living in areas with heavy snowfall, and inside was used for sericulture and salt and salt production. As a major producer of saltpeter, a raw material for gunpowder for the Kaga clan, it was also a closed mountain village where contact with the outside world was prohibited. Today, people continue to preserve their traditions while living here, making it a rare "living world heritage site" in the world. The scenery of the gassho-zukuri houses covered in snow in winter is especially beautiful and attracts many tourists.

tateyama_oyama_shrine.name: 立山・雄山神社（立山信仰の霊峰）
tateyama_oyama_shrine.kana: たてやま・おやまじんじゃ

transit.name: 富山地方鉄道「立山」→ケーブルカー・バス乗継

tateyama_oyama_shrine.text: 立山は北アルプスの最高峰の一つ（雄山3003m）で、富士山・白山と並ぶ「日本三霊山」として古来より篤い信仰を集めてきました。奈良時代の718年に佐伯有頼が白鷹に導かれて登山し開山したとされ、立山信仰は「地獄」と「浄土」の両方が存在する山として発展しました。地獄谷（地獄）と弥陀ヶ原（極楽浄土）は今も噴気が立ち上り、独特の景観を呈しています。雄山山頂には雄山神社峰本社が鎮座し、夏の登山シーズンには多くの登山者が参拝します。立山黒部アルペンルートは現代でも国内随一の山岳観光ルートです。
tateyama_oyama_shrine.highlight: 日本三霊山の一つ・立山。地獄と極楽が共存する山岳信仰3000m峰
tateyama_oyama_shrine.name_en: Tateyama/Oyama Shrine (sacred mountain of Tateyama worship)
tateyama_oyama_shrine.highlight_en: Tateyama, one of Japan's three sacred mountains. A 3000m mountain peak where hell and paradise coexist
tateyama_oyama_shrine.text_en: Tateyama is one of the highest peaks in the Northern Alps (Mt. Oyama, 3003m) and has been worshiped since ancient times as one of Japan's three sacred mountains along with Mt. Fuji and Mt. Hakusan. It is said that Ariyori Saeki climbed the mountain and founded it in 718 during the Nara period when he was guided by a white hawk, and Tateyama worship developed as a mountain where both ``Hell'' and ``Pure Land'' existed. Jigokudani (Hell) and Midagahara (Gokuraku Pure Land) still have fumaroles rising from them, creating a unique landscape. Oyama Shrine Mine Head Office is located at the summit of Mt. Oyama, and many climbers visit the shrine during the summer climbing season. The Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route is Japan's premier mountain sightseeing route even today.

kurobe_unazuki.name: 黒部峡谷・宇奈月温泉
kurobe_unazuki.kana: くろべきょうこく・うなづきおんせん

transit.name: 富山地方鉄道「宇奈月温泉」

kurobe_unazuki.text: 黒部峡谷は富山県東部を流れる黒部川がV字に刻んだ日本有数の秘境で、最大深さ2000mを超える峡谷が続きます。大正時代から続く水力発電開発の歴史があり、昭和38年（1963年）に完成した黒部ダム（黒四ダム）は当時東洋一の規模を誇り、171人もの殉職者を出した難工事として知られています。宇奈月温泉を起点にトロッコ電車（黒部峡谷鉄道）に乗ると、断崖絶壁の峡谷を縫うように走る絶景を楽しめます。黒部川の清流と深山の自然は、電源開発史と自然美が交差する独特の観光地となっています。
kurobe_unazuki.highlight: 171人が犠牲になった黒部ダム建設の舞台。日本有数の秘境峡谷とトロッコ
kurobe_unazuki.highlight_en: The stage for the construction of Kurobe Dam, where 171 people died. One of Japan's most unexplored canyons and trolleys
kurobe_unazuki.text_en: Kurobe Gorge is one of Japan's most unexplored regions, carved in a V-shape by the Kurobe River that flows through eastern Toyama Prefecture, and is a continuous gorge with a maximum depth of over 2,000 meters. The city has a history of hydroelectric power development dating back to the Taisho era, and the Kurobe Dam (Kuro 4 Dam), completed in 1963, was the largest in Asia at the time, and is known for its difficult construction that resulted in 171 people being killed in the line of duty. If you ride the trolley train (Kurobe Gorge Railway) starting at Unazuki Onsen, you can enjoy the spectacular scenery as it weaves through the gorge with sheer cliffs. The clear waters of the Kurobe River and the nature of the deep mountains make it a unique tourist destination where the history of power development and natural beauty intersect.

himi_manyo.name: 氷見市・万葉集ゆかりの地（奈良時代の詩情）
himi_manyo.kana: ひみし・まんようしゅうゆかりのち
himi_manyo.text: 氷見市は富山湾に面した漁師町で、奈良時代の越中国守・大伴家持が5年間赴任した地として知られています。家持はここで四季の自然を詠んだ多くの歌を万葉集に残し、その数は越前国と並ぶ多さです。「春の野にすみれ摘みにと来しわれぞ野をなつかしみ一夜寝にける」など、北陸の豊かな自然を詠んだ歌が市内各地に歌碑として建てられています。また氷見は「氷見の寒ブリ」で有名な漁港でもあり、冬になると全国から一番ブリを求める人々が訪れます。藤子不二雄Aの出身地でもあります。
himi_manyo.highlight: 大伴家持が5年間赴任し万葉集に多数の歌を残した越中の地。寒ブリの港
himi_manyo.name_en: Himi City, a place related to Manyoshu (poetry of the Nara period)
himi_manyo.highlight_en: The Etchu region where Otomo Ieyamochi lived for five years and left many poems in the Manyoshu. Port of Kanburi
himi_manyo.text_en: Himi City is a fishing town facing Toyama Bay, and is known as the place where Otomo Ieyamochi, the governor of Etchu Province during the Nara period, lived for five years. Ieyamochi left behind many poems about the nature of the four seasons in the Manyoshu, the number of which is on par with Echizen Province. Poems depicting the rich nature of Hokuriku, such as ``I came to the spring fields to pick violets, and slept for the night nostalgic for the fields,'' have been erected as monuments throughout the city. Himi is also a fishing port famous for ``Himi's cold yellowtail,'' and in the winter, people from all over the country come here in search of yellowtail. It is also the birthplace of Fujiko Fujio A.

etchu_kokubunji.name: 越中国分寺跡（高岡市）
etchu_kokubunji.kana: えっちゅうこくぶんじあと

transit.name: あいの風とやま鉄道「二塚」

etchu_kokubunji.text: 越中国分寺は聖武天皇の詔（741年）によって全国に設置された国分寺の一つで、越中国（富山県）の国分寺として奈良時代に建立されました。現在は礎石などが残るのみですが、発掘調査によって金堂・七重塔などの規模が明らかになっています。この地には大伴家持も国守として赴任しており、古代から越中の政治・文化の中心地でした。近くには現在も真言宗の寺院「越中国分寺」が法灯を継いでおり、境内には出土した瓦などが展示されています。奈良時代の地方統治の実態を物語る貴重な遺跡です。
etchu_kokubunji.highlight: 聖武天皇の詔で建立された越中の国分寺跡。大伴家持の赴任地に残る古代遺跡
etchu_kokubunji.highlight_en: The ruins of Kokubunji Temple in Etchu, built by Emperor Shomu's edict. Ancient ruins remaining in the place where Otomo Ieyamochi was posted
etchu_kokubunji.text_en: Etchubu Temple is one of the Kokubunji temples established across the country by Emperor Shomu's edict (741), and was built in the Nara period as a Kokubunji temple for Etchuchu Province (Toyama Prefecture). Currently, only the foundation stones remain, but excavations have revealed the scale of the main hall and seven-storied pagoda. Otomo Ieyamochi was also stationed here as a national governor, and it has been the political and cultural center of Etchu since ancient times. Nearby, the Shingon sect temple Etchubu-ji still carries on the lantern, and excavated tiles and other items are on display within the grounds. It is a valuable ruin that shows the reality of local governance during the Nara period.

masuyama_castle.name: 増山城跡（砺波市・戦国の要衝）

transit.name: 砺波市コミュニティバス

masuyama_castle.text: 増山城は富山県砺波市にある中世の山城で、守山城・富山城とともに「越中三大山城」の一つに数えられます。南北朝時代から戦国時代にかけて、越中の支配権をめぐる争いの舞台となり続けました。上杉謙信・武田信玄・織田信長・佐々成政など、戦国時代の名将が次々とこの城と関わりを持ちました。本丸・二の丸・三の丸が尾根に沿って連なる縄張りは、中世山城の典型的な形態を示しており、石垣や土塁がよく保存されています。2008年には国の史跡に指定され、整備が進んでいます。
masuyama_castle.highlight: 越中三大山城の一つ。謙信・信長・佐々成政など戦国名将が次々争った要衝
