masuyama_castle.name_en: Masuyama Castle Ruins (Tonami City, a strategic point during the Sengoku period)
masuyama_castle.highlight_en: One of the three major mountain castles in Etchu. A strategic point where famous Sengoku generals such as Kenshin, Nobunaga, and Narimasa Sasa fought one after another.
masuyama_castle.text_en: Masuyama Castle is a medieval mountain castle located in Tonami City, Toyama Prefecture, and is counted as one of the three major mountain castles in Etchu, along with Moriyama Castle and Toyama Castle. From the Nanbokucho period to the Sengoku period, it continued to be the stage for conflicts over control of Etchu. Famous warlords from the Sengoku period, such as Uesugi Kenshin, Takeda Shingen, Oda Nobunaga, and Sasa Narimasa, had ties to this castle one after another. The territory where Honmaru, Ninomaru, and Sannomaru are connected along the ridge shows the typical form of a medieval mountain castle, and the stone walls and earthworks are well preserved. It was designated as a national historic site in 2008, and maintenance is progressing.

noto_wajima_market.name: 輪島朝市・輪島塗の里
noto_wajima_market.kana: わじまあさいち・わじまぬりのさと
noto_wajima_market.text: 輪島朝市は千年以上の歴史を持つ日本三大朝市の一つで、毎朝200軒以上の露店が並びます。平安時代末期、地元の神社の縁日に物々交換が始まったとされ、能登の新鮮な海産物や農産物、伝統工芸品が並ぶ活気ある市場として全国に知られています。輪島塗は室町時代から始まった漆器で、百回以上の工程を経て完成する堅牢華麗な漆器として国の重要無形文化財に指定されています。2024年の能登半島地震で輪島朝市の建物が大きな被害を受けましたが、地域の人々の力で復興が進められています。
noto_wajima_market.highlight: 千年の歴史・日本三大朝市。国指定の輪島塗と能登の海産物が集まる朝の市
noto_wajima_market.highlight_en: One of Japan's three major morning markets with a thousand years of history. Morning market where nationally designated Wajima lacquerware and Noto seafood gather
noto_wajima_market.text_en: Wajima Morning Market is one of Japan's three major morning markets with a history of over 1,000 years, and there are over 200 stalls lined up every morning. It is said that bartering began at the end of the Heian period during festivals held at local shrines, and is known nationwide as a lively market selling Noto's fresh seafood, agricultural products, and traditional crafts. Wajima lacquerware is a type of lacquerware that began in the Muromachi period, and has been designated as an important intangible cultural property of the country as a sturdy and gorgeous lacquerware that takes over 100 steps to complete. The Wajima Asaichi building suffered major damage in the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake, but reconstruction is progressing with the help of local people.

hakusan_hime_shrine.name: 白山比咩神社（白山信仰の総本宮）
hakusan_hime_shrine.kana: しらやまひめじんじゃ
hakusan_hime_shrine.text: 白山比咩神社は石川県白山市に鎮座し、全国に2700社以上ある白山神社の総本宮です。白山は富士山・立山と並ぶ「日本三霊山」で、8世紀に越前の修行僧・泰澄が開山したとされています。白山を御神体とし、菊理媛神（くくりひめのかみ）・伊弉諾尊・伊弉冉尊を祀るこの神社は、縁結び・家内安全・農業の神として広く信仰されています。境内の杉並木は樹齢数百年に及ぶものが多く、厳かな雰囲気が漂います。毎年7月の「白山登山」シーズンには全国から登山者と参拝者が集まります。
hakusan_hime_shrine.highlight: 全国2700社・白山神社の総本宮。富士山・立山と並ぶ日本三霊山の総社
hakusan_hime_shrine.name_en: Hakusan Hime Shrine (main shrine of Hakusan faith)
hakusan_hime_shrine.highlight_en: The main shrine of 2,700 Hakusan Shrines nationwide. The main shrine of Japan's three sacred mountains along with Mt. Fuji and Mt. Tateyama
hakusan_hime_shrine.text_en: Hakusan Hime Shrine is located in Hakusan City, Ishikawa Prefecture, and is the main shrine of over 2,700 Hakusan Shrines nationwide. Mt. Hakusan is one of Japan's three sacred mountains, along with Mt. Fuji and Mt. Tateyama, and is said to have been founded in the 8th century by Taisumi, an Echizen monk. This shrine, which has Mt. Hakusan as its object of worship and enshrines Kukurihime no Kami, Izanagi no Mikoto, and Izami no Mikoto, is widely worshiped as the god of matchmaking, family safety, and agriculture. Many of the cedar trees on the grounds are hundreds of years old, giving it a solemn atmosphere. Climbers and worshipers gather from all over the country during the "Mt. Hakusan climbing" season in July every year.

nanao_castle.name: 七尾城跡（謙信が攻めた能登の名城）
nanao_castle.text: 七尾城は能登半島の中央部、七尾湾を見下ろす山上に築かれた中世の巨大山城です。室町時代に能登国を支配した畠山氏の居城として栄え、最盛期には日本五大山城の一つに数えられるほどの規模を誇りました。上杉謙信は「なべて思へば 月は今も 昔の七尾の城に似たるかな」と詠み、1577年に落城させました。謙信が詠んだこの歌は、七尾城の絶景を高く評価したものとして知られています。現在は石垣が残る山城跡で、能登の海と里山を見渡す眺望が見事です。
nanao_castle.highlight: 上杉謙信が「月は今も昔の七尾の城に」と詠んだ能登の巨大山城
nanao_castle.name_en: Nanao Castle Ruins (Famous castle in Noto that Kenshin attacked)
nanao_castle.highlight_en: A gigantic mountain castle in Noto where Uesugi Kenshin wrote, ``The moon is still like Nanao Castle''
nanao_castle.text_en: Nanao Castle is a huge medieval mountain castle built on a mountain overlooking Nanao Bay in the central part of the Noto Peninsula. It flourished as the residence of the Hatakeyama clan, which ruled Noto Province during the Muromachi period, and at its peak was so large that it was ranked as one of Japan's five great mountain castles. Uesugi Kenshin wrote a poem saying, ``When I think about it, the moon still resembles the ancient Nanao Castle,'' and the castle was destroyed in 1577. This poem, written by Kenshin, is known to highly praise the spectacular view of Nanao Castle. Currently, the ruins of the mountain castle still have stone walls, and the view overlooking the sea and the countryside of Noto is spectacular.

keta_taisha.name: 気多大社（能登国一宮）
keta_taisha.text: 気多大社は石川県羽咋市に鎮座する能登国の一宮で、大己貴命（おおなむちのみこと）を主祭神とする古社です。『古事記』にも記される格式ある神社で、上杉謙信や前田利家など歴代の武将から厚い崇敬を受けてきました。境内には樹齢数百年の古木が立ち並ぶ「入らずの森」があり、人が足を踏み入れることが禁じられた原生林として厳かな雰囲気を保っています。縁結びの神様としても有名で、全国から良縁を求める参拝者が訪れます。羽咋市は「UFOの里」としても知られており、宇宙科学博物館コスモアイル羽咋も近くにあります。
keta_taisha.highlight: 謙信・利家も崇敬した能登一宮。人立入禁止の原生林「入らずの森」が神秘
keta_taisha.highlight_en: Noto Ichinomiya was revered by Kenshin and Toshiie. The mysterious virgin forest ``Nieruzu no Mori'' that is off-limits to humans
keta_taisha.text_en: Kitada Shrine is a shrine in Noto Province located in Hakui City, Ishikawa Prefecture, and is an old shrine whose main deity is Onamuchi no Mikoto. It is a prestigious shrine that is mentioned in the Kojiki, and has been deeply revered by successive military commanders such as Uesugi Kenshin and Maeda Toshiie. Within the precincts, there is a ``Forest of No Entry'' lined with ancient trees that are hundreds of years old, and it maintains a solemn atmosphere as a primeval forest where humans are forbidden to set foot. It is also famous as the god of matchmaking, and worshipers come from all over the country to find a good match. Hakui City is also known as the "UFO village" and the Space Science Museum Cosmo Isle Hakui is also nearby.

kanazawa_higashi_chayagai.name: 金沢・東茶屋街
kanazawa_higashi_chayagai.kana: かなざわ・ひがしちゃやがい
kanazawa_higashi_chayagai.text: 東茶屋街は金沢市の繁華街の一角に残る江戸時代の茶屋街で、国の重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に指定されています。1820年（文政3年）に加賀藩がお茶屋（芸妓を呼んで遊ぶ料亭）を公認し、一か所に集めたことに始まります。格子戸が連なる2階建ての町家が続く街並みは、江戸時代の情緒をよく残しており、映画やドラマのロケ地にもなっています。現在は茶屋文化を体験できる施設や和菓子店・工芸品店が軒を連ね、金沢観光の定番スポットとなっています。主計町（かずえまち）茶屋街・にし茶屋街とともに「金沢三茶屋街」を形成しています。
kanazawa_higashi_chayagai.highlight: 加賀前田藩が公認した江戸の茶屋街。格子戸の街並みが200年以上残る
kanazawa_higashi_chayagai.highlight_en: Edo's teahouse district officially recognized by the Kaga Maeda clan. The streetscape of lattice doors has remained for over 200 years.
kanazawa_higashi_chayagai.text_en: Higashi Chaya District is a tea house district from the Edo period that remains in a corner of the downtown area of ​​Kanazawa City, and has been designated as a nationally important preservation district for groups of traditional buildings. It all began in 1820 when the Kaga domain authorized teahouses (restaurants that invited geisha to play) and gathered them in one place. The townscape, which is lined with two-story townhouses with lattice doors, retains the atmosphere of the Edo period, and has been used as a filming location for movies and TV dramas. Today, it is lined with facilities where you can experience teahouse culture, Japanese sweets shops, and craft shops, and has become a standard sightseeing spot in Kanazawa. Together with Kazuemachi Chaya District and Nishi Chaya District, it forms the Kanazawa Sanchaya District.

maruoka_castle.name: 丸岡城（現存12天守・霞ヶ城）
maruoka_castle.text: 丸岡城は1576年（天正4年）に柴田勝家の甥・勝豊が築いたとされる城で、現存する天守の中で最古の建築様式を持つ一つです。現存12天守の一つに数えられ、重要文化財に指定されています。石瓦（凝灰岩）を使った屋根が特徴で、北陸の豪雪に対応した造りになっています。城は小高い丘の上に建ち、周辺には春に1,200本の桜が咲き誇り「霞ヶ城」の別名で親しまれています。戊辰戦争では大きな被害を受けませんでしたが、1948年の福井地震で天守が崩壊し、その後古材を用いて復元されました。「一筆啓上 火の用心 お仙泣かすな 馬肥やせ」の手紙で知られる本多重次もゆかりの地です。
maruoka_castle.highlight: 現存最古の建築様式・現存12天守の一つ。石瓦の古天守と千本桜で有名
maruoka_castle.name_en: Maruoka Castle (12 existing castle towers, Kasumigajo)
maruoka_castle.highlight_en: The oldest existing architectural style and one of the 12 existing castle towers. Famous for its old stone tile castle tower and 1000 cherry blossoms
maruoka_castle.text_en: Maruoka Castle is said to have been built in 1576 by Katsutoyo, a nephew of Katsuie Shibata, and is one of the oldest castle towers in existence. It is counted as one of the 12 existing castle towers and is designated as an important cultural property. It is characterized by a roof made of stone tiles (tuff), and is built to withstand the heavy snowfall of Hokuriku. The castle is built on a small hill, and the surrounding area is known for its 1,200 cherry blossom trees that bloom in spring, giving it the nickname "Kasumiga Castle." Although it was not seriously damaged during the Boshin War, the castle tower collapsed during the 1948 Fukui earthquake, and was later rebuilt using old materials. The area is also connected to Shigeji Honda, who is known for his letter, ``Let's take care of the fire, don't let the fairy cry, and let the horse grow fat.''

tsuruga_kehi_shrine.name: 敦賀・気比神宮（源義経ゆかりの地）
tsuruga_kehi_shrine.kana: つるが・けひじんぐう
tsuruga_kehi_shrine.text: 気比神宮は敦賀市に鎮座する越前国一宮で、日本三大鳥居の一つとして知られる大鳥居が境内入口に立っています。祭神は仲哀天皇・神功皇后・応神天皇などで、北陸道総鎮守として古来より皇室・武家から崇敬されてきました。源義経は奥州逃避行の途中、1187年に敦賀に立ち寄り、気比神宮に参拝したとされています。松尾芭蕉も『おくのほそ道』の旅でこの地を訪れ、「月清し 遊行のもてる 砂の上」と詠みました。敦賀は古代から大陸・半島との交流拠点であり、シルクロードの東端を象徴するムゼウム（人道の港・敦賀ムゼウム）も近くにあります。
tsuruga_kehi_shrine.highlight: 日本三大鳥居の気比神宮。源義経・芭蕉が訪れた北陸道総鎮守の大社
tsuruga_kehi_shrine.name_en: Tsuruga/Kehi Shrine (place related to Minamoto no Yoshitsune)
tsuruga_kehi_shrine.highlight_en: Kehi Shrine has one of Japan's three major torii gates. The main shrine of Hokuriku Prefecture visited by Minamoto no Yoshitsune and Basho
tsuruga_kehi_shrine.text_en: Kehi Shrine is a shrine in Echizen Province located in Tsuruga City, and the large torii gate, known as one of Japan's three major torii gates, stands at the entrance to the shrine grounds. The deities enshrined include Emperor Chuai, Empress Jingu, and Emperor Ojin, and it has been revered by the imperial family and samurai families since ancient times as the general guardian of Hokuriku. It is said that Minamoto no Yoshitsune stopped in Tsuruga in 1187 on his escape to Oshu and visited Kehi Shrine. Matsuo Basho also visited this place on his journey ``Oku no Hosomichi'' and wrote a poem, ``Moon clearing, on the sand where you can enjoy a leisurely stroll.'' Tsuruga has been a base for exchange with the continent and peninsula since ancient times, and the Museum (Tsuruga Museum, Port of Humanity), which symbolizes the eastern end of the Silk Road, is also nearby.

kofu_castle.name: 甲府城跡（舞鶴城）
kofu_castle.text: 甲府城は1593年（文禄2年）に豊臣秀吉の命で築かれた近世城郭で、武田氏滅亡後の甲斐国を統治する拠点として機能しました。関ヶ原の戦い後は徳川家の直轄領となり、江戸時代には将軍家の親藩・柳沢氏が治めました。城跡は現在「舞鶴城公園」として整備されており、石垣と稲荷櫓が復元されています。甲府盆地を見下ろす高台に位置し、晴れた日には富士山や南アルプスを一望できます。武田信玄の「風林火山」で知られる甲斐国の歴史的拠点として、武田氏館跡（信玄の居城）とともに甲府の歴史を語る重要な史跡です。
kofu_castle.highlight: 豊臣秀吉が築き徳川家が治めた甲斐の近世城郭。富士山と南アルプスの眺望
kofu_castle.highlight_en: Kai's early modern castle was built by Toyotomi Hideyoshi and ruled by the Tokugawa family. View of Mt. Fuji and the Southern Alps
kofu_castle.text_en: Kofu Castle is an early modern castle built in 1593 (Bunroku 2) by order of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, and served as a base for governing Kai Province after the fall of the Takeda clan. After the Battle of Sekigahara, it became a territory under the direct control of the Tokugawa family, and during the Edo period it was ruled by the Yanagisawa clan, the shogun's family. The castle ruins are currently maintained as Maizuru Castle Park, and the stone walls and Inari turret have been restored. Located on a hill overlooking the Kofu Basin, you can see Mt. Fuji and the Southern Alps on clear days. As a historical base of Kai Province, known for Takeda Shingen's ``Furinkazan'', it is an important historical site that tells the history of Kofu, along with the Takeda clan mansion ruins (Shingen's castle).

erin_ji_temple.name: 恵林寺（武田信玄の菩提寺）
erin_ji_temple.text: 恵林寺は山梨県甲州市（旧塩山市）にある臨済宗妙心寺派の名刹で、武田信玄の菩提寺として知られています。1330年（元弘元年）に夢窓疎石が開山し、武田信玄が火事で焼失した伽藍を再建して菩提寺としました。信玄の位牌と木像が安置されており、境内には信玄の墓所もあります。1582年には信長の甲州征伐によって寺が焼き討ちにあい、住職・快川紹喜が「心頭滅却すれば火もまた涼し」という言葉を残して焼死した悲劇の地としても有名です。国の名勝に指定された庭園も見どころです。
erin_ji_temple.highlight: 武田信玄の菩提寺。「心頭滅却すれば火もまた涼し」の快川が信長に焼かれた地
erin_ji_temple.highlight_en: Takeda Shingen's family temple. The place where Kaigawa, which is said to be ``If you destroy your mind, the fire will also be cool,'' was burned by Nobunaga.
erin_ji_temple.text_en: Erinji Temple is a famous temple of the Myoshinji school of the Rinzai sect located in Koshu City (formerly Enzan City), Yamanashi Prefecture, and is known as Takeda Shingen's family temple. Muso Soseki opened the temple in 1330, and Takeda Shingen rebuilt the temple that had been destroyed by fire and made it his family temple. Shingen's memorial tablet and wooden statue are enshrined here, and there is also Shingen's grave within the precincts. In 1582, during Nobunaga's Koshu conquest, the temple was burnt down, and the temple is famous as the place where the chief priest, Shoki Kaikawa, died after leaving behind the words, ``If the head of the mind is destroyed, the fire is also cool.'' The garden, which has been designated as a national scenic spot, is also a highlight.

minobusan_kuonji.name: 身延山久遠寺（日蓮宗総本山）
minobusan_kuonji.text: 身延山久遠寺は山梨県身延町にある日蓮宗の総本山で、日蓮上人が晩年の9年間を過ごし、1282年（弘安5年）に入滅した霊場です。本堂に至る287段の急階段「菩提梯」は、煩悩を落とし菩提に至る道を象徴しています。境内の樹齢400年を超えるしだれ桜は「見頃桜」と呼ばれ、春の身延山の名物となっています。日蓮が「南無妙法蓮華経」の題目を唱え続けたこの地は、今も全国の日蓮宗信者の巡礼地であり、毎年多くの参詣者が訪れます。本山のケーブルカーで登る奥之院・思親閣からは富士山を望む絶景が広がります。
minobusan_kuonji.highlight: 日蓮上人が晩年を過ごした日蓮宗の総本山。287段の急階段と富士山の眺望
minobusan_kuonji.name_en: Minobuyama Kuonji Temple (head temple of the Nichiren sect)
minobusan_kuonji.highlight_en: The head temple of the Nichiren sect where Nichiren Shonin spent his later years. 287 steep steps and views of Mt. Fuji
minobusan_kuonji.text_en: Minobuzan Kuonji Temple is the head temple of the Nichiren sect in Minobu Town, Yamanashi Prefecture, and is a sacred place where Nichiren Shonin spent nine years of his later years before dying in 1282 (Koan 5th year). The 287-step steep staircase leading to the main hall, the Bodhi Ladder, symbolizes the path to eliminating earthly desires and attaining Bodhi. The weeping cherry trees on the grounds that are over 400 years old are called the ``best cherry blossoms'' and are a specialty of Mt. Minobu in spring. This place, where Nichiren continued to chant the title ``Namu-myoho-renge-kyo,'' is still a pilgrimage site for Nichiren sect believers from all over the country, and many pilgrims visit every year. From Okunoin and Shishinkaku, which you can climb by cable car from the main mountain, you can enjoy a spectacular view of Mt. Fuji.

saruhashi_bridge.name: 猿橋（日本三奇橋のひとつ）
saruhashi_bridge.text: 猿橋は山梨県大月市を流れる桂川（相模川上流）に架かる木造の橋で、錦帯橋・愛本橋とともに「日本三奇橋」の一つに数えられます。橋脚を川中に立てることなく、両岸から張り出した4層の「はね木」だけで橋板を支える構造が奇橋と呼ばれる由縁です。その起源は古く、1638年の記録にも登場し、江戸時代には甲州街道の重要な橋として機能しました。周囲の渓谷美も見事で、江戸時代から多くの文人墨客が訪れました。現在の橋は昭和時代に再建されたものですが、伝統的な工法を忠実に再現しており、国の名勝に指定されています。
saruhashi_bridge.highlight: 橋脚なしで両岸のはね木だけで支える日本三奇橋。甲州街道の名勝
saruhashi_bridge.name_en: Saruhashi (one of Japan's three strange bridges)
saruhashi_bridge.highlight_en: Japan's three strange bridges are supported only by springboards on both sides without piers. Scenic spots of Koshu Kaido
saruhashi_bridge.text_en: Saruhashi is a wooden bridge that spans the Katsura River (upstream of the Sagami River) in Otsuki City, Yamanashi Prefecture, and is considered one of Japan's three strange bridges, along with Kintaikyo Bridge and Aihon Bridge. The reason why it is called a strange bridge is because it has a structure that supports the bridge boards only with four layers of "hanging wood" extending from both banks, without having to erect piers in the river. Its origins are old, and it was recorded in 1638, and during the Edo period it functioned as an important bridge on the Koshu Highway. The beauty of the surrounding valley is also spectacular, and many literary figures and artists have visited since the Edo period. The current bridge was rebuilt during the Showa period, but it faithfully reproduces traditional construction methods, and has been designated as a national scenic spot.

komoro_castle.name: 小諸城跡（懐古園・島崎藤村ゆかりの城）
komoro_castle.text: 小諸城は信濃国（長野県）に位置する平山城で、16世紀に武田信玄が拡張整備した城です。城は千曲川の断崖上に築かれ、天守台は川より低いという珍しい「穴城」の形態を持ちます。仙石氏・松平氏などが城主を務め、参勤交代の宿場として城下町が賑わいました。明治後に廃城となりましたが、懐古園として公開されており、三の門（重要文化財）などが残ります。詩人・島崎藤村はここで教師をしながら「千曲川旅情のうた」を詠み、藤村記念館が近くに建ちます。信州の名城で春の桜と秋の紅葉でも知られています。
komoro_castle.highlight: 「穴城」の小諸城・懐古園。島崎藤村が「千曲川旅情」を詠んだ信州の城
komoro_castle.name_en: Komoro Castle Ruins (Kaikoen/Castle related to Shimazaki Toson)
komoro_castle.highlight_en: Komoro Castle and Kaikoen, the "ana castle". The castle in Shinshu where Toson Shimazaki wrote “Chikuma River Journey”
komoro_castle.text_en: Komoro Castle is a Hirayama castle located in Shinano Province (Nagano Prefecture), which was expanded and maintained by Takeda Shingen in the 16th century. The castle was built on the cliffs of the Chikuma River, and has the unusual structure of an ``hole castle,'' with the castle tower being lower than the river. The Sengoku clan and the Matsudaira clan served as the lords of the castle, and the castle town flourished as a post station for sankin kotai. Although the castle was abandoned after the Meiji period, it is open to the public as a kaikoen garden, and the San-no-mon Gate (an important cultural property) remains. The poet Toson Shimazaki wrote ``Chikuma River Traveling Song'' while teaching here, and the Toson Memorial Museum is built nearby. It is a famous castle in Shinshu and is also known for its cherry blossoms in spring and the autumn leaves.

suwa_taisha_kamisha.name: 諏訪大社（上社本宮・全国最古の大社）
suwa_taisha_kamisha.kana: すわたいしゃ（かみしゃほんみや）

transit.name: JR中央本線「茅野」よりバス

suwa_taisha_kamisha.text: 諏訪大社は長野県諏訪市・諏訪郡にまたがる4社からなる全国最古の神社の一つで、「建御名方神（たけみなかたのかみ）」を主祭神とします。全国に25,000社以上ある諏訪神社の総本社であり、縄文時代から続く狩猟・農業・武の神として古来より信仰されてきました。武田信玄・徳川家康など多くの武将が出陣前に必勝祈願を行ったことで知られています。7年に1度行われる「御柱祭」は、樹齢200年の巨木を山から里へ人力で運ぶ勇壮な祭りで、長野を代表する伝統行事として国の重要無形民俗文化財に指定されています。
suwa_taisha_kamisha.highlight: 全国25000社の諏訪神社の総本社。信玄・家康が祈願した7年に1度の御柱祭
suwa_taisha_kamisha.name_en: Suwa Taisha Shrine (Kamisha Main Shrine, the oldest shrine in Japan)
suwa_taisha_kamisha.highlight_en: Headquarters of 25,000 Suwa Shrines nationwide. Onbashira Festival, held once every seven years, prayed for by Shingen and Ieyasu
suwa_taisha_kamisha.text_en: Suwa Taisha is one of the oldest shrines in Japan, consisting of four shrines spanning Suwa City and Suwa District, Nagano Prefecture, and its main deity is Takeminakata no Kami. It is the headquarters of more than 25,000 Suwa Shrines nationwide, and has been worshiped since ancient times as the god of hunting, agriculture, and martial arts, dating back to the Jomon period. Many military commanders such as Takeda Shingen and Tokugawa Ieyasu are known to have prayed for victory before going into battle. The Onbashira Festival, held once every seven years, is a heroic festival in which a 200-year-old giant tree is carried by hand from the mountain to the village, and is designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property as a representative traditional event of Nagano.

takato_castle.name: 高遠城跡（天下第一の桜）

transit.name: 伊那バス「高遠城址公園」

takato_castle.text: 高遠城は長野県伊那市に位置する山城で、武田信玄が甲斐・信濃統治の重要拠点として整備しました。1572年（元亀3年）、信玄の五男・仁科盛信が城主の時、織田信長の大軍に攻められ、わずかな兵力で壮絶な籠城戦を演じましたが落城しました。この「高遠城の戦い」は歴史的な悲劇として語り継がれています。現在は「天下第一の桜」として名高い高遠城址公園となっており、約1,500本のコヒガンザクラが咲き誇る春は多くの花見客で賑わいます。江戸時代には保科家・内藤家が城主を務め、城下町が整備されました。
takato_castle.highlight: 武田の城・1500本の「天下第一の桜」。仁科盛信が織田軍に壮烈に抵抗した城
takato_castle.name_en: Takato Castle ruins (the best cherry blossoms in the world)
takato_castle.highlight_en: Takeda Castle - 1,500 ``Town's Greatest Cherry Blossoms''. The castle where Morinobu Nishina bravely resisted the Oda army.
takato_castle.text_en: Takato Castle is a mountain castle located in Ina City, Nagano Prefecture, and was built by Takeda Shingen as an important base for his rule over Kai and Shinano. In 1572, when Shingen's fifth son, Morinobu Nishina, was the lord of the castle, the castle was attacked by Oda Nobunaga's large army, and although he fought a fierce battle with a small army, the castle fell. This "Battle of Takato Castle" is handed down as a historical tragedy. Currently, it is Takato Castle Ruins Park, which is famous as ``the best cherry blossoms in the world'', and is crowded with many cherry blossom viewing visitors in spring when approximately 1,500 Kohigan cherry trees are in full bloom. During the Edo period, the Hoshina family and Naito family served as the castle lords, and a castle town was developed.

naraijuku_post_town.name: 奈良井宿（中山道の宿場町）
naraijuku_post_town.text: 奈良井宿は長野県塩尻市に位置する中山道の宿場で、中山道六十九次のうち「難所鳥居峠」を控えた重要な宿場として「奈良井千軒」と呼ばれるほどの繁栄を誇りました。現在も1kmにわたって江戸時代の街並みがほぼそのまま残る稀有な保存地区で、国の重要伝統的建造物群保存地区に指定されています。漆工・曲げ物・木工品などの木工業の町として発展し、「奈良井塗」は江戸時代から知られた漆器です。宿場を挟んで立ち並ぶ格子戸の旅籠・商家・酒蔵などが当時の姿を今日に伝え、映画やドラマのロケ地としても人気を集めています。
naraijuku_post_town.highlight: 1kmにわたり江戸の街並みが現存する中山道の宿場。国の重要伝統的建造物群
naraijuku_post_town.highlight_en: A post station on the Nakasendo route where the Edo townscape still exists for 1km. Group of nationally important traditional buildings
naraijuku_post_town.text_en: Narai-juku is a post station on the Nakasendo Route located in Shiojiri City, Nagano Prefecture, and was so prosperous that it was called ``Narai Sengen'' as it was an important post station near Torii Pass, one of the 69 stages of the Nakasendo Route. Today, it is a rare preservation district where the Edo period townscape remains almost intact for 1km, and has been designated as a nationally important preservation district for groups of traditional buildings. It developed as a town for woodworking, such as lacquerware, bent objects, and woodwork, and ``Narai-nuri'' is a type of lacquerware that has been known since the Edo period. The lattice-doored inns, merchant houses, and sake breweries that line the post are still visible today, and are popular as filming locations for movies and TV dramas.

shizuoka_sengen_shrine.name: 静岡浅間神社（家康が造営した総社）
shizuoka_sengen_shrine.kana: しずおかせんげんじんじゃ

transit.name: JR静岡駅からバス「浅間神社」

shizuoka_sengen_shrine.text: 静岡浅間神社は静岡市の中心部に位置する神社で、富知六所浅間神社・神部神社・浅間神社の三社が一体となった複合社です。徳川家康は幼少期にこの地（今川家のもと）で過ごし、大御所時代（駿府城在城）には境内を大規模に整備しました。現在の社殿群は江戸時代中期〜後期に造営されたもので、楼門・拝殿・本殿など26棟が国の重要文化財に指定されています。神部神社は創建2100年以上と伝わる古社で、「駿河の国の惣社」として歴代の権力者から崇敬を受けてきました。境内の歴史博物館では今川氏・徳川氏ゆかりの史料を展示しています。
shizuoka_sengen_shrine.highlight: 26棟が重要文化財・家康が幼少期を過ごした駿河総社。今川・徳川の要衝
shizuoka_sengen_shrine.name_en: Shizuoka Sengen Shrine (the main shrine built by Ieyasu)
shizuoka_sengen_shrine.highlight_en: 26 buildings are Suruga Soja, which is designated as an important cultural property and where Ieyasu spent his childhood. Key points in Imagawa and Tokugawa
shizuoka_sengen_shrine.text_en: Shizuoka Sengen Shrine is a shrine located in the center of Shizuoka City, and is a complex of three shrines: Tomi Rokusho Sengen Shrine, Kanbe Shrine, and Sengen Shrine. Tokugawa Ieyasu spent his childhood in this area (with the Imagawa family), and during his time as a great mogul (Sunpu Castle), he developed the precincts on a large scale. The current group of shrine buildings was built in the mid to late Edo period, and 26 buildings, including the tower gate, worship hall, and main shrine, have been designated as important cultural properties of the country. Kanbe Shrine is an ancient shrine that is said to have been founded over 2,100 years ago, and has been revered by successive generations of powerful people as the ``Sosha of Suruga Province.'' The history museum on the grounds displays historical materials related to the Imagawa and Tokugawa clans.

okitsu_seiken_ji.name: 興津・清見寺（今川・徳川ゆかりの古刹）
okitsu_seiken_ji.text: 清見寺は静岡県静岡市清水区興津に位置する曹洞宗の古刹で、奈良時代に創建されたと伝わります。東海道の海岸に沿って建ち、今川義元や徳川家康が幼少期に学問を修めた寺として知られています。家康は今川氏の人質として興津に滞在した際、清見寺の禅僧から教育を受けたとされ、その縁で江戸時代には寺領が寄進され厚遇されました。また、江戸後期には頼山陽・伊能忠敬など多くの文人・学者が訪れ、駿河の名所として知られました。境内の池泉回遊式庭園は「清見潟公園」の名で親しまれ、富士山を望む絶景スポットでもあります。
okitsu_seiken_ji.highlight: 今川義元・徳川家康が学んだ古刹。東海道の海岸沿いに立つ富士山の眺望地
okitsu_seiken_ji.name_en: Okitsu/Seikenji Temple (an old temple connected to Imagawa/Tokugawa)
okitsu_seiken_ji.highlight_en: An old temple where Imagawa Yoshimoto and Tokugawa Ieyasu studied. Viewing spot of Mt. Fuji along the coast of Tokaido
okitsu_seiken_ji.text_en: Seikenji Temple is an old temple of the Soto sect located in Okitsu, Shimizu Ward, Shizuoka City, Shizuoka Prefecture, and is said to have been founded during the Nara period. Built along the Tokaido coast, it is known as the temple where Imagawa Yoshimoto and Tokugawa Ieyasu studied during their childhood. When Ieyasu stayed in Okitsu as a hostage of the Imagawa clan, it is said that he received education from the Zen monks of Seikenji Temple, and as a result of this connection, he was given temple territory and was treated well during the Edo period. Also, in the late Edo period, many literary figures and scholars such as Rai Sanyo and Ino Tadataka visited, and it became known as a famous spot in Suruga. The pond strolling garden within the precincts is affectionately known as ``Kiyomigata Park,'' and is also a scenic spot overlooking Mt. Fuji.

shibata_castle.name: 新発田城（菖蒲城・三階櫓）
shibata_castle.text: 新発田城は新潟県北部、加治川流域に位置する平城で、戦国時代に新発田氏が築き、江戸時代には溝口氏が10万石の城下町を整備しました。三階櫓は屋根に3匹の鯱が乗る全国でも珍しい構造で、近代の戊辰戦争では奥羽越列藩同盟に加わるか官軍に付くかで揺れたものの、最終的に新政府軍に与しました。現在は本丸表門と旧二の丸隅櫓が現存（重要文化財）し、平成16年には三階櫓・辰巳櫓が復元されました。菖蒲城の別名通り、城内の堀には毎年初夏に菖蒲が美しく咲きます。
shibata_castle.highlight: 屋根に三匹の鯱を乗せる三階櫓が珍しい溝口氏10万石の城
shibata_castle.highlight_en: Mizoguchi's 100,000 koku castle has a rare three-story turret with three shachi on the roof.
shibata_castle.text_en: Shibata Castle is a flat castle located in the Kaji River basin in northern Niigata Prefecture. It was built by the Shibata clan during the Sengoku period, and the Mizoguchi clan developed a castle town of 100,000 koku in the Edo period. The three-story turret has a unique structure in Japan with three horsetails on the roof, and during the modern Boshin War, the tower was torn between joining the Ou-etsu clan alliance or joining the government army, but ultimately sided with the new government army. Currently, the main main gate and the former Ninomaru corner turret still exist (Important Cultural Properties), and the third floor turret and Tatsumi turret were restored in 2004. As the castle's other name suggests, irises bloom beautifully in the moat in early summer every year.

takada_castle_niigata.name: 高田城跡（松平忠輝・桜の名所）

transit.name: えちごトキめき鉄道「高田」

takada_castle_niigata.text: 高田城は1614年（慶長19年）、徳川家康の六男・松平忠輝の居城として築かれた平城で、伊達政宗が普請総督を務め、わずか4か月で完成させた急造の城です。天守を持たず三重櫓を中心とする質素な縄張りで、堀が深く石垣を持たない土塁の城という特徴があります。城跡は高田公園として桜の名所となり、約4000本の桜が咲き誇る春の夜桜は「日本三大夜桜」の一つに数えられます。市内には旧高田藩士の屋敷や雁木通り（雪国独特の屋根付き歩道）が残り、城下町の風情を伝えています。
takada_castle_niigata.highlight: 家康六男の松平忠輝の居城・伊達政宗が普請。日本三大夜桜の名所
takada_castle_niigata.name_en: Takada Castle Ruins (Tadateru Matsudaira/Famous Cherry Blossom Spot)
takada_castle_niigata.highlight_en: It was constructed by Date Masamune, the residence of Ieyasu's sixth son, Matsudaira Tadateru. Japan's three major night cherry blossom viewing spots
takada_castle_niigata.text_en: Takada Castle is a flat castle built in 1614 (Keicho 19) as the residence of Matsudaira Tadateru, the sixth son of Tokugawa Ieyasu, and was a hastily constructed castle completed in just four months by Date Masamune, who served as the construction governor. It has a simple territory with a triple turret at its center, without a castle tower, and is characterized by an earthwork castle with a deep moat and no stone walls. The castle ruins have become Takada Park, a famous spot for cherry blossom viewing, and the spring night cherry blossoms with approximately 4,000 cherry blossom trees in full bloom are considered one of Japan's top three night cherry blossoms. The mansions of the former Takada samurai and Gangi-dori (covered sidewalks unique to snowy regions) remain in the city, conveying the atmosphere of a castle town.

matsushiro_castle.name: 松代城跡（海津城・真田氏の居城）
matsushiro_castle.text: 松代城は武田信玄が川中島の戦いの前線拠点として築いた「海津城」が前身で、武田家滅亡後は織田・上杉・森氏らが城主を務めました。1622年（元和8年）に真田信之が上田から移封されて以降、真田氏10万石の居城として明治維新まで続きました。城下町には真田邸・文武学校・象山記念館など真田氏ゆかりの史跡が多数残り、佐久間象山の生誕地としても知られています。城は1985年から平成にかけて石垣・櫓門が復元され、現在は国の史跡となっています。川中島古戦場も近く、戦国の歴史を辿る絶好の地です。
matsushiro_castle.highlight: 武田信玄が築いた海津城が前身。真田信之が10万石を治めた城
matsushiro_castle.name_en: Matsushiro Castle ruins (Kaizu Castle, residence of the Sanada clan)
matsushiro_castle.highlight_en: Its predecessor was Kaizu Castle, built by Takeda Shingen. The castle where Nobuyuki Sanada ruled over 100,000 koku
matsushiro_castle.text_en: The predecessor of Matsushiro Castle was Kaizu Castle, which was built by Takeda Shingen as a front-line base during the Battle of Kawanakajima, and after the fall of the Takeda clan, the Oda, Uesugi, and Mori clans served as lords of the castle. After Nobuyuki Sanada was transferred from Ueda in 1622, it continued to be the residence of the Sanada family with a capital of 100,000 koku until the Meiji Restoration. The castle town has many historical sites related to the Sanada clan, such as the Sanada residence, literary and martial arts school, and the Shozan Memorial Hall, and is also known as the birthplace of Sakuma Shozan. The castle's stone walls and turret gate were restored between 1985 and the Heisei era, and it is now a national historic site. The Kawanakajima Battlefield is also nearby, making it a perfect place to trace the history of the Sengoku period.

tatsuoka_castle.name: 龍岡城跡（日本に2つしかない五稜郭）
tatsuoka_castle.text: 龍岡城は信濃国佐久郡（長野県佐久市）に幕末の1864年から建設された星形稜堡式の城郭で、函館の五稜郭と並ぶ日本に2つしかない西洋式城郭です。築城主は奥殿藩主・松平乗謨（後の大給恒）で、フランスのヴォーバン式築城法を学んで設計しました。明治維新により1867年に未完成のまま放棄されましたが、星形の堀と土塁は現在もよく保存されており、隣接する田口小学校の校庭が城内本丸跡となっています。城跡の展望台「五稜郭であいの館」からは星形の全景を望めます。
tatsuoka_castle.highlight: 函館と並ぶ日本に2つしかない星形稜堡式洋式城郭
tatsuoka_castle.name_en: Tatsuoka Castle ruins (one of only two Goryokaku in Japan)
tatsuoka_castle.highlight_en: A Western-style castle with a star-shaped fort, one of only two in Japan along with Hakodate.
tatsuoka_castle.text_en: Tatsuoka Castle is a star-shaped fort-style castle built in 1864 at the end of the Edo period in Saku District, Shinano Province (Saku City, Nagano Prefecture), and is one of only two Western-style castles in Japan, along with Goryokaku in Hakodate. The castle was built by Noriyuki Matsudaira (later Ogachi Tsune), the lord of the Okudono domain, who learned the French Vauban-style castle construction method and designed it. Although it was abandoned unfinished in 1867 due to the Meiji Restoration, the star-shaped moat and earthworks are still well preserved, and the adjacent schoolyard of Taguchi Elementary School serves as the ruins of the main castle enclosure. You can see a star-shaped panoramic view from the observation deck of the castle ruins, Goryokaku Deai no Yakata.

yamanaka_castle.name: 山中城跡（北条氏の障子堀）
yamanaka_castle.text: 山中城は北条氏が東海道の要衝・箱根の西麓に築いた防御拠点で、戦国時代の小田原北条氏五代にわたって整備されました。最大の特徴は「障子堀」と「畝堀」と呼ばれる独特の堀の構造で、堀底に格子状の畝を造ることで敵兵の動きを封じる工夫がなされています。1590年（天正18年）の豊臣秀吉の小田原征伐では、わずか半日で4000の城兵が7万の豊臣軍に攻略され落城しました。現在は国の史跡として復元整備されており、障子堀の幾何学的な美しさは日本の城郭遺構の中でも特に印象的です。
yamanaka_castle.highlight: 格子状の障子堀が美しい北条氏の城。秀吉軍に半日で落城
yamanaka_castle.name_en: Yamanaka Castle ruins (Hojo clan's shoji moat)
yamanaka_castle.highlight_en: A castle owned by the Hojo clan with a beautiful lattice-shaped shoji moat. The castle fell to Hideyoshi's army in half a day.
yamanaka_castle.text_en: Yamanaka Castle is a defensive base built by the Hojo clan at the western foot of Hakone, a key location on the Tokaido.It was maintained over five generations of the Odawara Hojo clan during the Sengoku period. The most distinctive feature is the unique moat structure called ``shoji moat'' and ``unebori,'' which are designed to block the movement of enemy soldiers by creating lattice-like ridges at the bottom of the moat. During Toyotomi Hideyoshi's conquest of Odawara in 1590 (Tensho 18), 4,000 castle soldiers were captured by 70,000 Toyotomi troops and fell in just half a day. It has now been restored and maintained as a national historic site, and the geometric beauty of the shoji moat is one of the most impressive among Japanese castle ruins.

kakegawa_castle.name: 掛川城（山内一豊の城・東海の名城）
kakegawa_castle.text: 掛川城は文明年間（1469-87年）に今川氏家臣の朝比奈氏が築いた城で、戦国時代には今川義元の家臣朝比奈泰朝の居城となりました。1568年（永禄11年）の徳川家康の侵攻を受け、攻城戦の末に開城。その後は徳川氏の支城となり、1590年に山内一豊が5万石で入封して天守を築きました。一豊は関ヶ原の戦いで功を挙げ土佐24万石へと栄転、後に高知城を築きます。掛川城天守は1854年の安政地震で倒壊しましたが、1994年に日本初の木造復元天守として再建され、東海地方の名城として親しまれています。
kakegawa_castle.highlight: 山内一豊が築き土佐藩主への足がかりとした城。木造復元天守が見事
kakegawa_castle.name_en: Kakegawa Castle (Kazutoyo Yamauchi's castle, famous castle in the Tokai region)
kakegawa_castle.highlight_en: A castle built by Kazutoyo Yamauchi and used as a stepping stone to becoming the lord of the Tosa domain. The restored wooden castle tower is stunning
kakegawa_castle.text_en: Kakegawa Castle was built by the Asahina clan, a vassal of the Imagawa clan, during the Bunmei era (1469-87), and during the Sengoku period, it became the residence of Yasutomo Asahina, a vassal of Yoshimoto Imagawa. In 1568 (Eiroku 11), the castle was invaded by Tokugawa Ieyasu, and the castle was surrendered after a siege. After that, it became a branch castle of the Tokugawa clan, and in 1590 Kazutoyo Yamauchi bought it for 50,000 koku and built a castle tower. Kazutoyo achieved great success in the Battle of Sekigahara and was able to earn 240,000 koku in Tosa, and later built Kochi Castle. Kakegawa Castle's castle tower collapsed in the Ansei Earthquake of 1854, but was rebuilt in 1994 as Japan's first restored wooden castle tower, and is now known as a famous castle in the Tokai region.

takatenjin_castle.name: 高天神城跡（武田×徳川の激戦地）
takatenjin_castle.kana: たかてんじんじょうあと

transit.name: 自家用車推奨（バス便少）

takatenjin_castle.text: 高天神城は静岡県掛川市に位置する険峻な山城で、「高天神を制する者は遠州を制す」と言われた戦略上の要衝でした。今川・徳川・武田の三氏が奪い合い、1574年（天正2年）に武田勝頼が攻略、1581年（天正9年）には徳川家康が奪還する激戦の舞台となりました。武田氏滅亡の前兆ともされたこの戦いでは、城兵全員が玉砕する壮絶な攻防が繰り広げられました。現在は国の史跡として整備されており、本丸跡からは遠州灘を一望できます。武田氏の影響を受けた独特の縄張りが今も残り、戦国の生々しい歴史を今に伝えています。
takatenjin_castle.highlight: 「制する者は遠州を制す」の要衝・武田×徳川の激戦地。城兵玉砕の地
takatenjin_castle.name_en: Takatenjin Castle ruins (field of fierce battle between Takeda and Tokugawa)
takatenjin_castle.highlight_en: The battleground between Takeda and Tokugawa, a key point where ``those who control will control Enshu.'' Land of Castle Soldiers Gyokusai
takatenjin_castle.text_en: Takatenjin Castle is a steep mountain castle located in Kakegawa City, Shizuoka Prefecture, and was a strategically important point where it was said that "those who control Takatenjin will control Enshu." It became the scene of a fierce battle between the Imagawa, Tokugawa, and Takeda clans, with Takeda Katsuyori capturing it in 1574 (Tensho 2) and Tokugawa Ieyasu recapturing it in 1581 (Tensho 9). This battle, which was seen as a harbinger of the downfall of the Takeda clan, was a fierce battle in which all of the castle's soldiers were crushed. It is currently maintained as a national historic site, and you can see the Enshu Sea from the main enclosure ruins. The unique territory influenced by the Takeda clan still remains today, conveying the vivid history of the Sengoku period.

naegi_castle.name: 苗木城跡（絶景の岩盤城・天空の城）
naegi_castle.text: 苗木城は岐阜県中津川市の木曽川を見下ろす標高432mの山頂に築かれた山城で、巨岩を取り込んだ独特の縄張りが特徴です。城主は遠山氏一族で、戦国時代に武田氏の侵攻を受けるも返り咲き、江戸時代を通じて1万石の小藩ながら明治維新まで遠山氏12代が続きました。最大の見どころは天守台の巨岩で、岩盤に直接柱穴を彫り込んで懸造（清水寺の舞台と同様）で天守を建てたという稀有な造りでした。現在は石垣のみ残りますが、天守台からは木曽川と恵那山、中央アルプスを望む大パノラマが広がり、近年「天空の城」として人気を集めています。
naegi_castle.highlight: 巨岩を取り込んだ天空の岩盤山城。木曽川と中央アルプスの絶景パノラマ
naegi_castle.name_en: Naegi Castle Ruins (Bedrock Castle with Spectacular View, Castle in the Sky)
naegi_castle.highlight_en: A bedrock mountain castle in the sky that incorporates huge rocks. Spectacular panorama of the Kiso River and the Central Alps
naegi_castle.text_en: Naegi Castle is a mountain castle built on the top of a mountain at an altitude of 432 meters overlooking the Kiso River in Nakatsugawa City, Gifu Prefecture, and is characterized by its unique territory that incorporates huge rocks. The castle was owned by the Toyama clan, which was invaded by the Takeda clan during the Sengoku period, but made a comeback, and continued through the Edo period to the Meiji Restoration, with 12 generations of the Toyama clan, although it was a small domain with an income of 10,000 koku. The main attraction is the huge rock on the castle tower, which is a rare structure in which the castle tower was built using a hanging structure (similar to the stage at Kiyomizu-dera Temple) with postholes carved directly into the bedrock. Currently, only the stone walls remain, but the castle tower offers a panoramic view of the Kiso River, Mt. Ena, and the Central Alps, and has become popular as a ``castle in the sky'' in recent years.

iwamura_castle.name: 岩村城跡（日本三大山城・女城主の城）
iwamura_castle.text: 岩村城は岐阜県恵那市岩村町、標高717mの山頂に築かれた日本三大山城（高取・備中松山と並ぶ）の一つで、別名「霧ヶ城」と呼ばれる中世以来の山城です。戦国時代には織田信長の叔母「おつや」が城主となり、武田氏の城将・秋山虎繁との「政略結婚」で開城した「女城主の悲劇」で有名です。後に信長軍に奪回されると、おつやと虎繁はともに信長に処刑されました。江戸時代には松平・丹羽・大給松平氏らが2万石を治め、明治維新後に廃城。現在は本丸の高石垣が今も天空にそびえ、城下町には武家屋敷や酒蔵が残り「日本一の山城」と呼ばれる景観を保ちます。
iwamura_castle.highlight: 日本三大山城・「女城主の悲劇」で知られる海抜717mの天空城
iwamura_castle.name_en: Iwamura Castle Ruins (Japan's three major mountain castles, castle of female castle lord)
iwamura_castle.highlight_en: A castle in the sky at 717m above sea level, known for Japan's three major mountain castles, ``The Tragedy of the Female Castle Lord''
iwamura_castle.text_en: Iwamura Castle is one of Japan's three major mountain castles (along with Takatori and Bicchu Matsuyama) built on the top of a mountain at an altitude of 717 meters in Iwamura-cho, Ena City, Gifu Prefecture, and is also known as ``Kiriga Castle'' and has been around since the Middle Ages. During the Sengoku period, Oda Nobunaga's aunt ``Otsuya'' became the lord of the castle, and it is famous for the ``tragedy of the female castle lord'', where she surrendered the castle through a ``political marriage'' with the Takeda clan's castle commander, Torashige Akiyama. When it was later recaptured by Nobunaga's forces, both Otsuya and Torashige were executed by Nobunaga. During the Edo period, the Matsudaira, Niwa, and Taikyu Matsudaira clans ruled over 20,000 koku, and the castle was abandoned after the Meiji Restoration. Today, the high stone walls of the main castle tower still tower into the sky, and samurai residences and sake breweries remain in the castle town, preserving the landscape known as ``Japan's best mountain castle.''

gujo_hachiman_castle.name: 郡上八幡城（日本最古の木造復元天守）
gujo_hachiman_castle.kana: ぐじょうはちまんじょう

transit.name: 郡上八幡駅からまめバス「城下町プラザ」

gujo_hachiman_castle.text: 郡上八幡城は岐阜県郡上市の長良川と吉田川の合流点を見下ろす八幡山（標高354m）に築かれた山城で、戦国時代の1559年に遠藤盛数が築城しました。江戸時代を通じて遠藤・井上・金森・青山氏らが治め、4万8千石の城下町・郡上八幡を発展させました。明治の廃城令で建物は取り壊されましたが、1933年（昭和8年）に再建された木造模擬天守は「日本最古の木造再建城」として国の登録有形文化財となっています。日本三大民謡の「郡上おどり」が400年続く城下町で、夏には徹夜踊りで賑わいます。
gujo_hachiman_castle.highlight: 日本最古の木造復元天守。郡上おどりが400年続く城下町
gujo_hachiman_castle.name_en: Gujo Hachiman Castle (Japan's oldest restored wooden castle tower)
gujo_hachiman_castle.highlight_en: Japan's oldest restored wooden castle tower. A castle town where Gujo Odori has continued for 400 years.
gujo_hachiman_castle.text_en: Gujo Hachiman Castle is a mountain castle built on Mt. Hachiman (354 m above sea level) overlooking the confluence of the Nagara River and Yoshida River in Gujo City, Gifu Prefecture, and was built by Morikazu Endo in 1559 during the Sengoku period. Throughout the Edo period, the Endo, Inoue, Kanamori, and Aoyama clans ruled and developed Gujo Hachiman, a castle town with an area of ​​48,000 koku. The building was demolished due to the Meiji Castle Abolition Order, but the wooden mock castle tower was rebuilt in 1933 (Showa 8) and is now a registered tangible cultural property of the country as Japan's oldest wooden reconstructed castle. It is a castle town where the Gujo Odori dance, one of Japan's three major folk songs, has continued for 400 years, and is crowded with people dancing all night long in the summer.

chihaya_castle.name: 千早城跡（楠木正成の悲願の城）
chihaya_castle.text: 千早城は大阪府南河内郡千早赤阪村の金剛山西麓（標高634m）に築かれた山城で、1332年（元弘2年）に楠木正成が後醍醐天皇の倒幕計画を支えるため築きました。翌1333年、鎌倉幕府が派遣した数十万の大軍に対し、わずか1000の兵で100日間籠城を貫き、ついには鎌倉幕府滅亡の引き金となった伝説の籠城戦の舞台です。正成は熱湯・煮糞・大石落としなどの奇策で大軍を翻弄し、「悪党戦法」の極致を見せました。現在は千早神社が建ち、本丸跡には正成を祀る祠があります。金剛山登山道の入口にあり、ハイキングと一緒に訪れる人も多い名所です。
chihaya_castle.highlight: 楠木正成が1000の兵で数十万の幕府軍に100日籠城。鎌倉幕府滅亡の引き金
chihaya_castle.name_en: Chihaya Castle Ruins (Masashige Kusunoki's long-awaited castle)
chihaya_castle.highlight_en: Masashige Kusunoki, with 1,000 soldiers, was besieged by hundreds of thousands of Shogunate troops for 100 days. The trigger for the fall of the Kamakura Shogunate
chihaya_castle.text_en: Chihaya Castle is a mountain castle built at the western foot of Mt. Kongo (634m above sea level) in Chihayaakasaka Village, Minamikawachi District, Osaka Prefecture, and was built in 1332 by Masashige Kusunoki to support Emperor Godaigo's plan to overthrow the shogunate. The following year, in 1333, the Kamakura Shogunate fought against a large army of hundreds of thousands of soldiers with just 1,000 soldiers, holding the castle for 100 days, and it is the setting for the legendary battle that ultimately triggered the downfall of the Kamakura Shogunate. Masashige toyed with the large army using tricks such as boiling water, boiling dung, and dropping large stones, demonstrating the ultimate in ``rogue tactics.'' Currently, Chihaya Shrine is built, and there is a shrine dedicated to Masashige at the site of the main enclosure. Located at the entrance to the Mt. Kongo mountain trail, it is a famous spot that many people visit while hiking.

takatori_castle.name: 高取城跡（日本三大山城・芙蓉城）
takatori_castle.text: 高取城は奈良県高取町、標高583mの高取山山頂に築かれた日本三大山城（岩村・備中松山と並ぶ）の一つで、別名「芙蓉城」と呼ばれます。南北朝時代に越智邦澄が築城し、戦国時代には筒井氏が大改修、江戸時代を通じて植村氏が治めました。山頂までの比高差390mは日本一を誇り、約30万㎡の城域に総石垣で築かれた壮大な縄張りは「巨大山城」の代表です。明治の廃城令で建物は取り壊されましたが、現在も本丸の高石垣・天守台・櫓台などが森の中に残り、「日本最強の城」「もののけ姫の世界」と評される神秘的な景観が広がります。
takatori_castle.highlight: 日本三大山城・標高583m・比高差390mは日本一。総石垣の天空の名城
takatori_castle.name_en: Takatori Castle Ruins (Fuyo Castle, Japan's three major mountain castles)
takatori_castle.highlight_en: One of Japan's three largest mountain castles with an altitude of 583m and a relative height difference of 390m. A famous castle in the sky with all stone walls
takatori_castle.text_en: Takatori Castle is one of Japan's three major mountain castles (along with Iwamura and Bitchu Matsuyama), built on the top of Mt. Takatori at an altitude of 583 meters in Takatori Town, Nara Prefecture, and is also known as ``Fuyo Castle.'' It was built by Kunizumi Ochi during the Nanbokucho period, was extensively renovated by the Tsutsui clan during the Sengoku period, and was ruled by the Uemura clan throughout the Edo period. The relative height difference of 390 meters to the summit is the highest in Japan, and the castle area is approximately 300,000 square meters and is a magnificent castle built entirely of stone walls, making it a representative example of a ``giant mountain castle.'' Although the buildings were demolished under the Meiji era Castle Abolition Order, the main castle's high stone walls, castle tower, turret, and other features still remain in the forest, creating a mystical landscape that has been described as ``Japan's strongest castle'' and ``the world of Princess Mononoke.''

sasayama_castle.name: 篠山城（天下普請の堅城）
sasayama_castle.text: 篠山城は1609年（慶長14年）、徳川家康が大坂城の豊臣秀頼を抑えるため、藤堂高虎の縄張りで普請奉行・池田輝政らに命じて天下普請で築かせた城です。築城開始からわずか半年で完成し、堅固な石垣と幾重もの堀をめぐらせた近世城郭の典型として知られています。家康は実子・松平康重を初代城主に置き、丹波篠山6万石の藩庁となりました。明治後に建物の多くは失われましたが、2000年に大書院が忠実に復元され、見学できます。武家屋敷群・河原町妻入商家群など城下町の景観も豊かに残り、国の重要伝統的建造物群保存地区となっています。
sasayama_castle.highlight: 家康の天下普請・藤堂高虎縄張り。半年で完成した堅城と城下町
sasayama_castle.name_en: Sasayama Castle (Fortification of the nation's construction)
sasayama_castle.highlight_en: Todo Takatora's territory, Ieyasu's territory. Fortress and castle town completed in half a year
sasayama_castle.text_en: Sasayama Castle was a castle built by Tokugawa Ieyasu in 1609 (Keicho 14) in order to suppress Toyotomi Hideyori of Osaka Castle by ordering fusho magistrate Terumasa Ikeda and others to build it on Todo Takatora's territory. It was completed in just six months after construction began, and is known as a typical early modern castle with solid stone walls and multiple moats. Ieyasu made his son, Yasushige Matsudaira, the first lord of the castle, and Tamba Sasayama became the domain of 60,000 koku. Although much of the building was lost after the Meiji period, the Daishoin was faithfully restored in 2000 and can be visited. The castle town's rich scenery remains, including samurai residences and Kawaramachi-Tsumari merchant houses, making it a nationally important preservation district for traditional buildings.

ako_castle.name: 赤穂城跡（忠臣蔵・赤穂浪士の城）
ako_castle.text: 赤穂城は1648年（慶安元年）から13年かけて浅野長直が築いた変形輪郭式の海城で、軍学者・近藤正純の設計による独特の縄張りが特徴です。1701年（元禄14年）、3代藩主・浅野内匠頭長矩が江戸城松之廊下で吉良上野介を斬りつけて切腹となり、お家は断絶。家老・大石内蔵助良雄ら47名の元赤穂藩士が翌年12月14日に吉良邸に討ち入った「赤穂事件（忠臣蔵）」は、日本人なら誰もが知る忠義の物語として今も語り継がれています。城跡には大石内蔵助邸跡や大石神社が建ち、毎年12月14日には「赤穂義士祭」が盛大に開かれます。
ako_castle.highlight: 忠臣蔵の舞台・赤穂浪士47士の本拠。海城ならではの変形輪郭式縄張り
ako_castle.highlight_en: The setting for Chushingura and the base of the 47 Ako Ronin samurai. Deformed contour type territory unique to Kaijo
ako_castle.text_en: Ako Castle is a modified contour-style sea castle built by Asano Naganao over a period of 13 years starting in 1648, and is characterized by its unique territory designed by military scholar Masazumi Kondo. In 1701 (Genroku 14), the third lord of the domain, Asano Takuminokami Naganori, slashed Kira Kaminosuke in the Matsuno Corridor of Edo Castle and committed seppuku, resulting in the end of his family. The Ako Incident (Chushingura), in which 47 former retainers of the Ako domain, including the chief retainer, Yoshio Oishi Kuranosuke, raided the Kira residence on December 14 of the following year is still passed down as a story of loyalty that all Japanese people know. The ruins of the Oishi Kuranosuke residence and Oishi Shrine are built on the castle ruins, and the Ako Gishi Festival is held on December 14th every year.

fukuchiyama_castle.name: 福知山城（明智光秀の丹波経営拠点）
fukuchiyama_castle.text: 福知山城は1579年（天正7年）、織田信長の命を受けて丹波平定に成功した明智光秀が、丹波支配の拠点として築いた城です。光秀は城下町を整備し、由良川の流れを変える治水事業も行い、地元では今も「明智光秀公」と慕われています。本能寺の変の3年後に城主は替わり、江戸時代には朽木氏ら譜代大名が3万2千石の藩庁として治めました。明治の廃城令で建物は取り壊されましたが、1986年に天守が市民の寄付で復元されました。天守内部は郷土資料館となっており、明智光秀の事績や福知山の歴史を学べます。大河ドラマ『麒麟がくる』の舞台地としても注目を集めました。
fukuchiyama_castle.highlight: 明智光秀が丹波経営の拠点とした城。地元では今も「光秀公」と慕われる
fukuchiyama_castle.name_en: Fukuchiyama Castle (Tamba management base of Mitsuhide Akechi)
fukuchiyama_castle.highlight_en: A castle that Mitsuhide Akechi used as his base for managing Tamba. He is still affectionately known as ``Ko Mitsuhide'' by the locals.
fukuchiyama_castle.text_en: Fukuchiyama Castle was built in 1579 (Tensho 7) by Akechi Mitsuhide, who succeeded in conquering Tamba under the orders of Oda Nobunaga, as a base for his control over Tamba. Mitsuhide developed the castle town and carried out flood control projects that changed the flow of the Yura River, and the locals still call him ``Akechi Mitsuhide.'' Three years after the Honnoji Incident, the castle owner changed hands, and during the Edo period, Fudai daimyo such as the Kuchiki clan ruled it as a domain office with a capital of 32,000 koku. The building was demolished under the Meiji Castle Abolition Order, but the castle tower was restored in 1986 with donations from citizens. The inside of the castle tower is a local museum where you can learn about the achievements of Mitsuhide Akechi and the history of Fukuchiyama. It also attracted attention as the setting for the historical drama Kirin ga Kuru.

kishiwada_castle.name: 岸和田城（だんじり祭の城下町）
kishiwada_castle.text: 岸和田城は和泉国（大阪府岸和田市）に位置する平城で、別名「千亀利城（ちきりじょう）」とも呼ばれます。鎌倉時代に和田高家が築き、戦国時代には信長家臣の津田信張、続いて秀吉家臣の中村一氏らが城主となりました。江戸時代に岡部氏が5万3千石で治め、明治の廃城令まで岡部家13代が続きました。1827年（文政10年）、5層の天守が落雷で焼失したものの、1954年に3層の鉄筋天守が市民の寄付で再建されました。岸和田と言えば300年の歴史を持つ「だんじり祭」（重要無形民俗文化財）で全国的に有名で、毎年9月の祭礼は岸和田城を中心に勇壮に繰り広げられます。
kishiwada_castle.highlight: 「だんじり祭」で有名な城下町。岡部氏13代5万3千石の千亀利城
kishiwada_castle.name_en: Kishiwada Castle (castle town of Danjiri Festival)
kishiwada_castle.highlight_en: A castle town famous for the Danjiri Festival. Sengiri Castle, 53,000 koku owned by the 13th generation of the Okabe clan
kishiwada_castle.text_en: Kishiwada Castle is a flat castle located in Izumi Province (Kishiwada City, Osaka Prefecture), and is also known as Chikiri Castle. It was built by Wada Takaie during the Kamakura period, and during the Sengoku period, Nobunaga's vassal Nobuharu Tsuda, followed by Hideyoshi's vassal Kazuuji Nakamura, became the castle's lords. During the Edo period, the Okabe clan ruled with 53,000 koku, and 13 generations of the Okabe family continued until the Meiji era when the castle was abolished. In 1827 (Bunsei 10), the five-story castle tower was destroyed by lightning, but a three-story steel castle tower was rebuilt in 1954 with donations from citizens. Speaking of Kishiwada, it is famous nationwide for the Danjiri Festival (Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property), which has a history of 300 years, and the festival is held every September in a grand manner centered around Kishiwada Castle.

torigoe_castle.name: 鳥越城跡（加賀一向一揆 最後の砦）

transit.name: 加賀白山バス「鳥越城跡前」

torigoe_castle.text: 鳥越城は石川県白山市の手取川と大日川の合流点を見下ろす山城で、加賀一向一揆（本願寺門徒の一揆衆）の最後の砦として知られています。1573年（天正元年）頃に山内衆の鈴木出羽守が築き、織田信長の重臣・柴田勝家、佐久間盛政らが攻め寄せ、激戦の末1580年に陥落しました。さらに翌年に再起した門徒衆300人余りが磔にされた悲劇の地でもあります。1582年の本能寺の変後、一向一揆は事実上終結しました。現在は国の史跡として整備され、本丸・桝形門・後二の丸などが復元されています。「百姓ノ持タル国」と呼ばれた加賀一向一揆の歴史を体感できる貴重な遺跡です。
torigoe_castle.highlight: 加賀一向一揆最後の砦。「百姓ノ持タル国」の終焉を見届けた山城
torigoe_castle.name_en: Torigoe Castle Ruins (last stronghold of the Kaga Ikko Ikki)
torigoe_castle.highlight_en: The last stronghold of the Kaga Ikko Ikki. Yamashiro witnessed the end of the “farmer-no-mochi-taru country”
torigoe_castle.text_en: Torigoe Castle is a mountain castle overlooking the confluence of the Tedori River and the Dainichi River in Hakusan City, Ishikawa Prefecture, and is known as the last stronghold of the Kaga Ikko Ikki (Ikki group of Honganji disciples). It was built around 1573 by Suzuki Dewa no kami of the Yamauchi clan, and was attacked by Oda Nobunaga's senior vassals, Shibata Katsuie and Sakuma Morimasa, and fell in 1580 after a fierce battle. It is also the place of tragedy where over 300 disciples who rose again the following year were crucified. After the Honnoji Incident in 1582, the Ikko Ikki effectively came to an end. Currently, it is maintained as a national historic site, and the main enclosure, Masugata gate, Go-ninomaru, etc. have been restored. This is a valuable ruin where you can experience the history of the Kaga Ikko Ikki, which was known as the ``Farmers' Country''.

echizen_ono_castle.name: 越前大野城（天空の城）
echizen_ono_castle.kana: えちぜんおおのじょう
echizen_ono_castle.text: 越前大野城は1576年（天正4年）、織田信長から越前大野郡3万石を与えられた金森長近が4年の歳月をかけて築いた平山城で、標高249mの亀山山頂にそびえます。長近は京都の都市計画を参考に碁盤目状の城下町を整備し、「北陸の小京都」と呼ばれる風雅な町並みを今に伝えました。江戸時代には松平氏らが治め、明治の廃城令で建物は失われましたが、1968年に天守が市民の寄付で復元されました。雲海に浮かぶ姿が「天空の城」として人気を集め、年に10日ほど条件が揃った日の早朝に幻想的な雲海の中に城が浮かびます。
echizen_ono_castle.highlight: 金森長近が築いた北陸の小京都。雲海に浮かぶ天空の城
echizen_ono_castle.name_en: Echizen Ono Castle (Castle in the Sky)
echizen_ono_castle.highlight_en: Little Kyoto in Hokuriku built by Nagachika Kanamori. Castle in the sky floating in a sea of ​​clouds
echizen_ono_castle.text_en: Echizen Ono Castle is a flat mountain castle built in 1576 by Nagachika Kanamori, who was given 30,000 koku in Echizen Ono District by Oda Nobunaga, over a period of four years, and towers over the top of Mt. Kameyama at an altitude of 249 meters. Nagachika developed a castle town in a grid pattern based on the city plan of Kyoto, and created an elegant townscape that is now known as the ``Little Kyoto of Hokuriku''. During the Edo period, it was ruled by the Matsudaira clan, and the building was lost due to the Meiji era castle abolishment ordinance, but the castle tower was restored in 1968 with donations from citizens. The appearance of the castle floating in a sea of ​​clouds has gained popularity as a ``castle in the sky,'' and on about 10 days a year when the conditions are right, the castle can be seen floating in a fantastic sea of ​​clouds early in the morning.

hachimanyama_castle.name: 八幡山城跡（豊臣秀次の悲劇の城）
hachimanyama_castle.kana: はちまんやまじょうあと
hachimanyama_castle.text: 八幡山城は1585年（天正13年）、豊臣秀吉の甥・豊臣秀次が築いた近江八幡（滋賀県）の山城で、安土城が焼失した後の近江経営の拠点となりました。秀次は城下に楽市楽座を敷き、安土の住民を移住させて八幡商人発祥の地となる近江八幡の町を整備。「八幡堀」と呼ばれる運河を巡らせて琵琶湖水運と直結させ、後の近江商人文化の礎を築きました。1591年に秀次は関白に就任し清洲城に移りましたが、1595年に秀吉から謀反の疑いをかけられ高野山で切腹。城も廃城となりました。現在は山頂までロープウェイで登れ、本丸石垣と村雲御所瑞龍寺門跡があります。
hachimanyama_castle.highlight: 豊臣秀次が築き近江商人文化の礎を築いた城。秀次切腹で10年で廃城
hachimanyama_castle.name_en: Hachimanyama Castle ruins (Toyotomi Hidetsugu's tragic castle)
hachimanyama_castle.highlight_en: This castle was built by Hidetsugu Toyotomi and laid the foundation for Omi merchant culture. The castle was abandoned in 10 years due to Hidetsugu seppuku.
hachimanyama_castle.text_en: Hachimanyama Castle is a mountain castle in Omihachiman (Shiga Prefecture) built in 1585 (Tensho 13) by Toyotomi Hideyoshi's nephew, Toyotomi Hidetsugu, and became the base for Omi management after Azuchi Castle was burnt down. Hidetsugu established Rakuichi Rakuza in the castle town, relocated Azuchi residents, and established the town of Omihachiman, which became the birthplace of Yawata merchants. A canal called ``Hachimanbori'' was built around the area, connecting it directly to Lake Biwa water transportation, and laid the foundation for the later Omi merchant culture. In 1591, Hidetsugu became Kanpaku and moved to Kiyosu Castle, but in 1595, Hideyoshi accused him of rebellion and committed seppuku on Mt. Koya. The castle was also abandoned. Currently, you can take a ropeway to the top of the mountain, where you can see the Honmaru Ishigaki and Murakumo Gosho Zuiryuji Temple Monzeki.

ichinotani_battle.name: 一ノ谷古戦場（鵯越の逆落とし）
ichinotani_battle.kana: いちのたにこせんじょう
ichinotani_battle.text: 一ノ谷の戦いは1184年（寿永3年）に源義経率いる源氏軍と平氏軍が摂津国一ノ谷（神戸市須磨区）で激突した源平合戦の決戦のひとつ。義経は本陣の背後にある急峻な鵯越（ひよどりごえ）の崖を騎馬で駆け下りる「鵯越の逆落とし」の奇襲で平氏を背後から急襲し、混乱に陥った平氏は壊滅。平敦盛が熊谷直実に討たれた悲話の舞台としても知られる。
ichinotani_battle.highlight: 義経が「鵯越の逆落とし」の奇襲で平氏を壊滅させた源平合戦の決戦地
ichinotani_battle.highlight_en: The decisive battle site of the Genpei War, where Yoshitsune annihilated the Taira clan with a surprise attack called ``Gakuotoshi no Gakuotoshi.''
ichinotani_battle.text_en: The Battle of Ichinotani was one of the decisive battles of the Genpei War in 1184 (Juei 3), when the Minamoto clan forces led by Minamoto no Yoshitsune and the Taira clan forces clashed in Ichinotani, Settsu Province (Suma Ward, Kobe City). Yoshitsune attacked the Taira clan from behind in a surprise attack called ``Gakotoshi no Gakuotoshi,'' in which he ran down the steep Hiyodorigoe cliff behind the main camp on horseback, and the Taira clan fell into chaos and was destroyed. It is also known as the setting for the tragic story of Atsumori Taira being killed by Naozane Kumagai.

yashima_battle.name: 屋島古戦場（那須与一の扇の的）
yashima_battle.text: 屋島の戦いは1185年2月、讃岐国屋島（高松市）の平氏本陣を源義経が奇襲で攻略した戦い。少数の精鋭で阿波勝浦に上陸し、強行軍で背後から平氏を急襲。屋島から逃れる平氏船団に向けて、那須与一が揺れる船上の扇を一矢で射落とした「扇の的」の名場面が生まれた。平氏は壇ノ浦へと敗走し、源平合戦は最終局面に向かう。
yashima_battle.highlight: 那須与一の「扇の的」伝説の地。義経の奇襲で平氏が壇ノ浦に追われた地
yashima_battle.highlight_en: The legendary place of Yoichi Nasu's ``Ougi no Tate''. The place where the Taira clan was chased to Dan-no-ura by Yoshitsune's surprise attack.
yashima_battle.text_en: The Battle of Yashima took place in February 1185, when Minamoto no Yoshitsune captured the Taira clan's headquarters in Yashima, Sanuki Province (Takamatsu City) in a surprise attack. A small number of elite troops landed at Awa-Katsuura and used a forced march to attack the Taira clan from behind. The famous scene of ``Target of the Fan'' was created when Yoichi Nasu shot down a swinging fan on board the Heishi fleet fleeing Yashima with a single arrow. The Taira clan was routed to Dan-no-ura, and the Genpei War entered its final phase.

dannoura_battle.name: 壇ノ浦古戦場（平家滅亡の地）
dannoura_battle.kana: だんのうらこせんじょう

transit.name: JR「下関」
transit.walk: バス20分「みもすそ川」下車すぐ

dannoura_battle.text: 壇ノ浦の戦いは1185年3月24日、関門海峡で源義経と平知盛が激突した源平合戦の最終決戦。潮流を読んだ義経が反撃に転じると、平氏は壊滅。二位の尼が幼い安徳天皇を抱いて入水し、三種の神器のうち草薙剣も海底に沈んだ。これにより平家は滅亡し、源氏の天下が確立した。みもすそ川公園には源義経・平知盛の像が向かい合って建つ。
dannoura_battle.highlight: 平家滅亡・安徳天皇入水の地。義経vs平知盛・源平合戦の最終決戦地
dannoura_battle.name_en: Dan-no-ura Battlefield (place of the downfall of the Heike clan)
dannoura_battle.highlight_en: The place where the Heike clan fell and Emperor Antoku entered the water. Yoshitsune vs. Tomomori Taira - Final battle site of the Genpei War
dannoura_battle.text_en: The Battle of Dan-no-ura was the final battle of the Genpei War, fought on March 24, 1185, between Minamoto no Yoshitsune and Taira no Tomomori in the Kanmon Straits. Yoshitsune, who read the current trend, launched a counterattack and the Taira clan was destroyed. The second-rank nun entered the water carrying the young Emperor Antoku, and the Kusanagi sword, one of the three sacred treasures, also sank to the bottom of the sea. As a result, the Heike family was destroyed and the Minamoto clan was established. In Mimosuso River Park, statues of Minamoto no Yoshitsune and Taira Tomomori stand facing each other.

fujikawa_battle.name: 富士川古戦場（水鳥の羽音で平氏敗走）
fujikawa_battle.kana: ふじかわこせんじょう
fujikawa_battle.text: 富士川の戦いは1180年10月、駿河国富士川（静岡県富士市）で源頼朝の関東軍と平維盛率いる平氏追討軍が対峙した戦い。武田信義率いる甲斐源氏が平氏陣の背後に回り込んだ夜、富士沼の水鳥が一斉に飛び立った羽音を源氏の奇襲と勘違いした平氏軍は戦わずして潰走した。頼朝はこれを契機に鎌倉を本拠地として東国独立を進める。
fujikawa_battle.highlight: 水鳥の羽音に怯えた平氏が戦わず敗走。頼朝の鎌倉幕府成立を決定づけた地
fujikawa_battle.name_en: Fujikawa Battlefield (The Taira clan was defeated by the sound of waterfowl)
fujikawa_battle.highlight_en: The Taira clan, frightened by the sound of waterfowl's wings, fled without fighting. The place where Yoritomo decided to establish the Kamakura Shogunate
fujikawa_battle.text_en: The Battle of Fujikawa was a battle that took place in October 1180 in Fujikawa, Suruga Province (Fuji City, Shizuoka Prefecture), where Minamoto no Yoritomo's Kwantung Army and Taira no Korimori's Taira clan hunting force faced off. On the night that Kai-Genji, led by Nobuyoshi Takeda, sneaked behind the Taira clan's camp, the Taira clan's army fled without a fight, mistaking the sound of waterfowl taking off all at once from Fuji Swamp as a surprise attack by the Genji clan. Yoritomo took this opportunity to use Kamakura as his base and promote the independence of eastern Japan.

uji_river_jokyu.name: 宇治川古戦場（承久の乱）
uji_river_jokyu.kana: うじがわこせんじょう
uji_river_jokyu.text: 宇治川は治承4年（1180）の源頼政の挙兵、寿永3年（1184）の佐々木高綱と梶原景季の「先陣争い」、そして承久3年（1221）の承久の乱と、3度の歴史的合戦の舞台となった京の防衛線。承久の乱では後鳥羽上皇の朝廷軍と北条義時の幕府軍が激突し、19万の幕府軍が朝廷軍を圧倒。後鳥羽上皇は隠岐に流され、武家政権の優位が確立した。
uji_river_jokyu.highlight: 承久の乱で19万の幕府軍が朝廷軍を破り武家優位を確立した京の防衛線
uji_river_jokyu.highlight_en: Kyoto's defense line where 190,000 shogunate troops defeated the imperial court army and established samurai dominance during the Jokyu War.
uji_river_jokyu.text_en: The Uji River was the line of defense for Kyoto that was the scene of three historic battles: Minamoto no Yorimasa's raising of an army in 1180, the battle for the lead between Takatsuna Sasaki and Kajiwara Kagetsue in 1184, and the Jokyu War in 1221. In the Jokyu War, the imperial army of Retired Emperor Gotoba and Yoshitoki Hojo clashed, and the 190,000 shogunate army overwhelmed the imperial army. Retired Emperor Gotoba was exiled to Oki, and the samurai government was established.

genko_borui.name: 元寇防塁（蒙古襲来）
genko_borui.text: 元寇防塁は1276年（建治2年）から博多湾沿いに約20km築かれた高さ2mほどの石塁で、文永の役（1274）に続く弘安の役（1281）に備えて鎌倉幕府が築造させた防衛施設。実際に弘安の役ではこの石塁が元軍の上陸を阻み、「神風」と呼ばれた台風到来までの時間稼ぎに成功した。生の松原・西新・今津など博多湾沿いの各所に遺構が残る。
genko_borui.highlight: 蒙古襲来に備えた博多湾20kmの石塁。神風までの時間稼ぎに貢献
genko_borui.highlight_en: A 20km stone fort in Hakata Bay in preparation for the Mongolian invasion. Contributing to buying time until Kamikaze
genko_borui.text_en: The Mongol Invasion Forts are stone forts approximately 2m high that were built along Hakata Bay for approximately 20km from 1276 (Kenji 2nd year), and were defense facilities built by the Kamakura Shogunate in preparation for the Battle of Koan (1281), which followed the Battle of Bunei (1274). In fact, during the Battle of Koan, these stone forts prevented the Yuan army from landing and succeeded in buying time until the arrival of the typhoon, which was nicknamed the ``kamikaze.'' Remains remain in various locations along Hakata Bay, including Nama no Matsubara, Nishishin, and Imazu.

atsukashi_borui.name: 阿津賀志山防塁（奥州合戦古戦場）
atsukashi_borui.kana: あつかしやまぼうるい
atsukashi_borui.text: 阿津賀志山防塁は1189年（文治5年）、奥州藤原氏4代・泰衡が源頼朝率いる関東28万軍の侵攻に備えて築いた全長3.2kmの大規模防塁。福島県国見町から伊達郡桑折町にかけての阿武隈川と阿津賀志山を結ぶ線に二重三重の堀切と土塁を巡らせたが、頼朝軍はこれを突破。藤原氏は滅亡し、奥州が鎌倉幕府の支配下に入った。
atsukashi_borui.highlight: 奥州藤原氏が築いた3.2kmの大防塁。頼朝に攻略され奥州藤原氏滅亡
atsukashi_borui.highlight_en: A large fortification of 3.2km built by the Oshu Fujiwara clan. Conquered by Yoritomo, Oshu Fujiwara clan falls
atsukashi_borui.text_en: Atsukashiyama Fort was a large-scale fortification with a total length of 3.2km built in 1189 (5th year of Bunji) by Yasuhira, the fourth generation of the Oshu Fujiwara clan, in preparation for the invasion of 280,000 Kanto forces led by Minamoto no Yoritomo. Double and triple moats and earthworks were built around the line connecting the Abukuma River and Mt. Atsugashi from Kunimi Town in Fukushima Prefecture to Kuwaori Town in Date District, but Yoritomo's army broke through. The Fujiwara clan fell, and Oshu came under the control of the Kamakura shogunate.

inamuragasaki.name: 稲村ヶ崎（新田義貞 鎌倉攻め）
inamuragasaki.text: 稲村ヶ崎は1333年（元弘3年）、新田義貞が鎌倉攻めの際に黄金の太刀を海に投げ入れて龍神に祈ったところ、潮が引いて干潟ができ、軍勢が鎌倉に突入できたとの伝説が残る景勝地。これにより鎌倉幕府は滅亡し、北条高時以下一族郎党は東勝寺で自害。日本の中世史を大きく転換させた歴史的事件の舞台である。
inamuragasaki.highlight: 新田義貞が太刀を投げ入れ潮が引いた伝説の地。鎌倉幕府滅亡の引き金
inamuragasaki.highlight_en: This is the legendary place where Yoshisada Nitta threw his sword and the tide went out. The trigger for the fall of the Kamakura Shogunate
inamuragasaki.text_en: Inamuragasaki is a scenic spot where legend has it that in 1333, when Yoshisada Nitta was attacking Kamakura, he threw a golden long sword into the sea and prayed to the dragon god, and the tide receded, creating a tidal flat, allowing his army to invade Kamakura. As a result, the Kamakura shogunate collapsed, and Hojo Takatoki and his remaining members committed suicide at Toshoji Temple. It is the stage of a historical event that significantly changed Japan's medieval history.

hojo_grave_tosho.name: 東勝寺跡・北条高時腹切やぐら
hojo_grave_tosho.text: 東勝寺は鎌倉幕府の執権・北条氏の菩提寺で、1333年5月22日、新田義貞の鎌倉攻めにより滅亡寸前となった北条高時以下一族郎党約870名が自害した場所。背後の崖には「腹切やぐら」と呼ばれる岩窟が残り、鎌倉幕府滅亡の象徴的な遺跡として国の史跡に指定されている。鎌倉時代150年の幕引きの地。
hojo_grave_tosho.highlight: 北条高時以下870名が自害し鎌倉幕府が滅亡した「腹切やぐら」の地
hojo_grave_tosho.name_en: Toshoji Temple Ruins/Hojo Takatoki Harakiri Yagura
hojo_grave_tosho.highlight_en: The site of Harakiri Yagura, where 870 people including Takatoki Hojo committed suicide and the Kamakura Shogunate was destroyed.
hojo_grave_tosho.text_en: Toshoji is the family temple of the Hojo clan, the regent of the Kamakura shogunate, and is the place where on May 22, 1333, approximately 870 members of the Hojo clan, including Takatoki Hojo, committed suicide after Yoshisada Nitta's invasion of Kamakura nearly destroyed the temple. A rock cave called ``Harakiri Yagura'' remains on the cliff in the background, and is designated as a national historic site as a symbolic ruin of the fall of the Kamakura Shogunate. The place where the Kamakura period ended 150 years ago.

genpei_oshu_kasenadori.name: 衣川古戦場（藤原泰衡×源義経）
genpei_oshu_kasenadori.kana: ころもがわこせんじょう
genpei_oshu_kasenadori.text: 衣川は1189年（文治5年）、源頼朝の圧力に屈した奥州藤原氏4代・泰衡が源義経を襲撃し、義経が自害した古戦場。義経は北方の館（衣川館・高館義経堂）で武蔵坊弁慶ら忠臣とともに最期を遂げた。「弁慶の立往生」の伝説でも知られ、後に芭蕉が訪れて「夏草や 兵どもが 夢の跡」と詠んだ。
genpei_oshu_kasenadori.highlight: 義経自害・弁慶立往生の地。芭蕉「夏草や兵どもが夢の跡」の舞台
genpei_oshu_kasenadori.name_en: Kinugawa Battlefield (Yasuhiro Fujiwara x Yoshitsune Minamoto)
genpei_oshu_kasenadori.highlight_en: The place where Yoshitsune committed suicide and Benkei died. Stage of Basho's ``Summer Grass and Soldiers are the Traces of Dreams''
genpei_oshu_kasenadori.text_en: Kinugawa is an old battlefield where in 1189 (5th year of Bunji), Yasuhira, the 4th generation of the Oshu Fujiwara clan, succumbed to pressure from Minamoto no Yoritomo, attacked Minamoto Yoshitsune, and Yoshitsune committed suicide. Yoshitsune met his end in the northern mansion (Kirokawa-kan, Takadate Yoshitsune-do) along with Musashibo Benkei and other loyal retainers. It is also known for the legend of ``Benkei's stuck life,'' and Basho later visited and wrote a poem about ``Summer grass and soldiers are the remains of dreams.''

ishibashiyama_battle.name: 石橋山古戦場（頼朝挙兵 最初の戦い）
ishibashiyama_battle.kana: いしばしやまこせんじょう
ishibashiyama_battle.text: 石橋山の戦いは1180年8月23日、源頼朝が以仁王の令旨を受けて挙兵した最初の戦い。伊豆の山木兼隆を討った直後、わずか300の兵で大庭景親率いる3000の平氏方と相模国石橋山で激突。土砂降りの雨の中で大敗し、頼朝は山中に潜伏したのちに安房へ脱出した。再起後の鎌倉幕府成立の原点となる屈辱の敗戦地。
ishibashiyama_battle.highlight: 頼朝挙兵の最初の戦い。300vs3000で大敗し安房に逃れた原点の地
ishibashiyama_battle.highlight_en: The first battle of Yoritomo's army. The place of origin where he fled to Awa after losing 300 vs 3000
ishibashiyama_battle.text_en: The Battle of Ishibashiyama was fought on August 23, 1180, and was the first battle in which Minamoto no Yoritomo raised an army in response to an order from King Mochihito. Immediately after defeating Kanetaka Yamaki of Izu, he clashed with 3,000 Taira clan forces led by Kagechika Oba at Ishibashiyama in Sagami Province with only 300 soldiers. After suffering a crushing defeat in the pouring rain, Yoritomo hid in the mountains before escaping to Awa. The place of humiliating defeat in the war that became the starting point for the establishment of the Kamakura Shogunate after its revival.

munakata_genpei.name: 宗像・蒙古軍上陸地（鷹島）
munakata_genpei.kana: たかしま・もうこぐんじょうりくち
munakata_genpei.text: 鷹島（長崎県松浦市）は弘安の役（1281年）で元軍4400隻・14万人が集結した最終戦の地。台風「神風」の襲来で大半の元艦船が沈没し、上陸していた元軍も日本軍に殲滅された。海底からは元軍の遺物が大量に発見され、現在は「鷹島神崎遺跡」として国の史跡に指定。元寇終焉の地として歴史的価値が高い。
munakata_genpei.highlight: 弘安の役・元軍14万が「神風」で壊滅した最終決戦地。海底に遺物多数
munakata_genpei.highlight_en: The final battleground of the Koan War, where 140,000 former troops were destroyed by kamikaze. Many relics on the ocean floor
munakata_genpei.text_en: Takashima (Matsuura City, Nagasaki Prefecture) was the site of the final battle of the Battle of Koan (1281), where 4,400 former troops and 140,000 soldiers assembled. Most of the Yuan ships were sunk by the typhoon Kamikaze, and the Yuan troops that had landed there were also annihilated by the Japanese army. A large number of former military relics were discovered on the ocean floor, and the site is now designated as a national historic site as the Takashima Kanzaki Ruins. It has great historical value as the place where the Mongol invasion ended.

jisho_yoritomo_kamakura.name: 鶴岡八幡宮（頼朝幕府の中枢）
jisho_yoritomo_kamakura.kana: つるがおかはちまんぐう
jisho_yoritomo_kamakura.text: 鶴岡八幡宮は源頼朝が1180年（治承4年）、鎌倉入りした直後に由比郷から現在地に遷座させた武家社会の中心的神社。源氏の氏神として歴代将軍が崇敬し、流鏑馬・舞楽など武家文化の中心地でもあった。1219年（建保7年）、三代将軍・源実朝が大銀杏の陰から飛び出した甥・公暁に暗殺された悲劇の現場でもある。
jisho_yoritomo_kamakura.highlight: 頼朝が幕府の精神的中枢に置いた武家の総鎮守。源実朝暗殺の地
jisho_yoritomo_kamakura.name_en: Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine (the center of the Yoritomo shogunate)
jisho_yoritomo_kamakura.highlight_en: The general guardian of the samurai clan, which Yoritomo placed at the spiritual center of the shogunate. Place of Minamoto no Sanetomo assassination
jisho_yoritomo_kamakura.text_en: Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine is a central shrine for the samurai society that Minamoto no Yoritomo relocated from Yuigago to its current location in 1180 (Jishō 4), immediately after entering Kamakura. It was revered by successive shoguns as the guardian deity of the Genji clan, and was also the center of samurai culture such as yabusame and bugaku. It is also the site of a tragedy in 1219 (Kenpo 7), when the third shogun, Minamoto no Sanetomo, was assassinated by his nephew, Kimiyo, who jumped out from behind a large ginkgo tree.

minatogawa_battle.name: 湊川古戦場（楠木正成 戦死の地）
minatogawa_battle.kana: みなとがわこせんじょう
minatogawa_battle.text: 湊川の戦いは1336年5月25日、足利尊氏の大軍に対し、後醍醐天皇方の楠木正成と新田義貞が摂津国湊川で迎え撃った南北朝時代の決戦。圧倒的劣勢の中、正成は弟・正季と「七生報国（七度生まれ変わっても朝敵を討つ）」を誓って自害。正成の死後、湊川神社が建立され「大楠公」として崇敬を集める。明治期には吉田松陰・西郷隆盛らがここに参拝し勤皇思想を高めた。
minatogawa_battle.highlight: 楠木正成「七生報国」の自害地。後の勤皇思想の聖地・湊川神社
minatogawa_battle.name_en: Minatogawa Battlefield (place where Masashige Kusunoki died in battle)
minatogawa_battle.highlight_en: The site of Masashige Kusunoki's ``Nanasho Hokoku'' suicide. Minatogawa Shrine, a sacred place for later imperial ideology
minatogawa_battle.text_en: The Battle of Minatogawa was a decisive battle during the Nanbokucho period on May 25, 1336, when Emperor Go-Daigo's forces Masashige Kusunoki and Yoshisada Nitta faced off against Takauji Ashikaga's large army at Minatogawa in Settsu Province. Despite being overwhelmingly outnumbered, Masashige committed suicide with his younger brother, Masaki, vowing to ``Avenge the enemies of the Imperial Court even if we were reborn seven times.'' After Masashige's death, Minatogawa Shrine was built and he was revered as ``Okusunoki.'' During the Meiji period, Shoin Yoshida, Takamori Saigo, and others visited here and promoted the ideology of imperial service.

shijonawate_battle.name: 四條畷古戦場（楠木正行 戦死の地）
shijonawate_battle.kana: しじょうなわてこせんじょう
shijonawate_battle.text: 四條畷の戦いは1348年（正平3年）、楠木正成の嫡男・楠木正行（小楠公）が父の遺志を継ぎ、足利尊氏の執事・高師直率いる大軍と河内国四條畷で激突。正行は弟・正時とともに奮戦するも力尽き、兄弟刺し違えて壮絶な最期を遂げた。享年23歳。四條畷神社には正行が祀られ、忠孝の精神を伝える聖地となっている。
shijonawate_battle.highlight: 楠木正行「小楠公」が父の遺志を継いで戦死した忠孝の聖地
shijonawate_battle.name_en: Shijonawate Battlefield (place where Masayuki Kusunoki died in battle)
shijonawate_battle.highlight_en: A sacred place of loyalty and filial piety where Masayuki Kusunoki ``Ko Kusunoki'' died in battle carrying on his father's will.
shijonawate_battle.text_en: The Battle of Shijonawate took place in 1348 (Shohei 3), when Masashige Kusunoki's eldest son, Masayuki Kusunoki (Kokusunoki), carried on his father's will and clashed with a large army led by Takauji Ashikaga's butler, Taka Moronao, at Shijonawate in Kawachi Province. Although Masayuki fought bravely with his younger brother, Masatoki, they ran out of strength and met a violent end when they stabbed each other. He passed away at the age of 23. Shijonawate Shrine is dedicated to Masayuki and is a sacred place that conveys the spirit of loyalty and filial piety.

tadaragahama_battle.name: 多々良浜古戦場（足利尊氏 西国挽回の地）
tadaragahama_battle.kana: たたらがはまこせんじょう
tadaragahama_battle.text: 多々良浜の戦いは1336年3月、九州に敗走した足利尊氏が筑前国多々良浜（福岡市東区）で南朝方の菊池武敏軍と対決した戦い。500の兵で4万の菊池軍を奇跡的に撃破し、これを足がかりに再び京へ攻め上った尊氏は湊川で楠木正成を破り、室町幕府を開く。九州を制する者は天下を制すの言葉通りの逆転劇の地。
tadaragahama_battle.highlight: 500vs4万の奇跡的勝利。尊氏が西国から逆転して室町幕府を開く起点
tadaragahama_battle.name_en: Tatarahama Battlefield (Takauji Ashikaga's place of recovery in the Saigoku region)
tadaragahama_battle.highlight_en: A miraculous victory of 500 vs 40,000. The starting point for Takauji's reversal from the Saigoku region and the founding of the Muromachi Shogunate.
tadaragahama_battle.text_en: The Battle of Tatarahama took place in March 1336, when Takauji Ashikaga, who had fled to Kyushu, faced off against Taketoshi Kikuchi's army from the Southern Court at Tatarahama, Chikuzen Province (Higashi Ward, Fukuoka City). Takauji miraculously defeated the 40,000-man Kikuchi army with 500 soldiers and used this as a foothold to attack Kyoto again, defeating Masashige Kusunoki at Minatogawa and establishing the Muromachi Shogunate. As the saying goes, "Whoever controls Kyushu will control the world," this is a land of reversals.

fujishima_nitta.name: 藤島古戦場（新田義貞 戦死の地）
fujishima_nitta.kana: ふじしまこせんじょう
fujishima_nitta.text: 藤島の戦いは1338年（暦応元年）、越前国藤島（福井市新田塚町）で新田義貞が斯波高経軍の伏兵に襲われ戦死した古戦場。馬が田の泥にとられた義貞は弓矢で眉間を射抜かれ、自刃した。享年38歳。1656年に農夫が「新田家系図」と義貞の兜・剣を発見し、明治期に藤島神社として整備された。鎌倉幕府を倒した英雄の悲劇の終焉地。
fujishima_nitta.highlight: 鎌倉幕府を倒した新田義貞が38歳で戦死した越前の地。藤島神社で顕彰
fujishima_nitta.name_en: Fujishima Battlefield (place where Yoshisada Nitta died in battle)
fujishima_nitta.highlight_en: Echizen, where Yoshisada Nitta, who overthrew the Kamakura Shogunate, died in battle at the age of 38. Honored at Fujishima Shrine
fujishima_nitta.text_en: The Battle of Fujishima was an old battlefield in 1338 (1st year of the calendar) where Yoshisada Nitta was attacked by an ambush from Takatsune Shiba's army and died in battle on Fujishima in Echizen Province (Nittazuka-cho, Fukui City). Yoshisada, whose horse was trapped in the mud of a rice field, was shot between the eyebrows with a bow and arrow and committed suicide. He passed away at the age of 38. In 1656, a farmer discovered the Nitta family tree and Yoshisada's helmet and sword, and it was established as Fujishima Shrine in the Meiji period. The tragic final place of the hero who defeated the Kamakura Shogunate.

hakone_takenoshita.name: 箱根・竹之下古戦場
hakone_takenoshita.kana: はこね・たけのしたこせんじょう
hakone_takenoshita.text: 箱根・竹之下の戦いは1335年12月、足利尊氏が後醍醐天皇方の新田義貞軍を箱根の峠で迎撃した戦い。竹之下（静岡県小山町）で激戦の末、義貞軍は大敗を喫し、京方へと退却。これが尊氏と後醍醐天皇の決定的対立となり、南北朝の動乱の幕開けとなった。箱根古戦場碑が地元に建つ。
hakone_takenoshita.highlight: 尊氏が後醍醐天皇方を箱根で破り南北朝動乱の幕を開けた決戦地
hakone_takenoshita.highlight_en: The decisive battleground where Takauji defeated Emperor Go-Daigo's forces at Hakone and ushered in the Nanbokucho turmoil.
hakone_takenoshita.text_en: The Battle of Hakone-Takenoshita was fought in December 1335, when Takauji Ashikaga intercepted the army of Yoshisada Nitta on the side of Emperor Godaigo at the pass of Hakone. After a fierce battle at Takenoshita (Oyama Town, Shizuoka Prefecture), Yoshisada's army suffered a crushing defeat and retreated to Kyoto. This became a decisive conflict between Takauji and Emperor Godaigo, and began the turmoil of the Nanbokucho. The Hakone Battlefield Monument is erected locally.

kasagisan.name: 笠置山（後醍醐天皇 倒幕挙兵の地）
kasagisan.text: 笠置山は1331年（元徳3年）、後醍醐天皇が鎌倉幕府打倒の挙兵で行宮を構えた京都府笠置町の山。元弘の乱（元弘元年8月）の発端となり、幕府軍7万に攻められて1か月籠城の末に陥落、後醍醐天皇は隠岐に配流された。これを契機に楠木正成が赤坂城で蜂起、新田義貞・足利尊氏らも加わって鎌倉幕府滅亡へと向かう。
kasagisan.highlight: 後醍醐天皇が倒幕挙兵し1か月籠城した山。元弘の乱の発端の地
kasagisan.name_en: Kasagiyama (place where Emperor Go-Daigo raised an army to overthrow the shogunate)
kasagisan.highlight_en: This is the mountain where Emperor Go-Daigo raised an army to overthrow the shogunate and was confined for a month. The birthplace of the Motoko War
kasagisan.text_en: Mt. Kasagi is a mountain in Kasagi-cho, Kyoto Prefecture, where Emperor Go-Daigo set up his palace in 1331 (3rd year of Gentoku) when he raised an army to overthrow the Kamakura shogunate. This was the beginning of the Genko Rebellion (August 1, 1987), and the castle was attacked by 70,000 bakufu troops and fell after being in siege for a month, and Emperor Go-Daigo was banished to Oki. This triggered an uprising by Masashige Kusunoki at Akasaka Castle, which was joined by Yoshisada Nitta, Takauji Ashikaga, and others, leading to the downfall of the Kamakura shogunate.

akasaka_castle_kusunoki.name: 赤坂城跡（楠木正成 挙兵の城）
akasaka_castle_kusunoki.text: 赤坂城（下赤坂城）は1331年（元弘元年）、後醍醐天皇の倒幕挙兵に呼応して楠木正成が築いた最初の挙兵拠点。河内国赤坂村（大阪府千早赤阪村）にあり、幕府軍数万を「藁人形」「煮糞」「大石落とし」など奇策で翻弄した名籠城戦の舞台。一度は落城したものの、正成は千早城で再起し、鎌倉幕府滅亡への道を切り開いた。
akasaka_castle_kusunoki.highlight: 楠木正成が最初に挙兵した城。藁人形・煮糞など奇策で幕府軍を翻弄
akasaka_castle_kusunoki.name_en: Akasaka Castle ruins (Masashige Kusunoki's castle of raising an army)
akasaka_castle_kusunoki.highlight_en: The castle where Masashige Kusunoki first raised an army. Toyed with the shogunate's army with strange tactics such as straw dolls and boiled feces.
akasaka_castle_kusunoki.text_en: Akasaka Castle (Shimoakasaka Castle) was the first military base built by Masashige Kusunoki in response to Emperor Go-Daigo's army to overthrow the shogunate in 1331. Located in Akasaka Village, Kawachi Province (Chihaya Akasaka Village, Osaka Prefecture), this is the stage of the Battle of Nago Castle, where tens of thousands of Shogunate troops were at the mercy of tricks such as ``straw dolls'', ``boiled dung'', and ``big stone drop''. Although the castle fell once, Masashige made a comeback at Chihaya Castle and paved the way for the fall of the Kamakura Shogunate.

yoshino_chotei.name: 吉野朝廷跡（南朝・後醍醐天皇）
yoshino_chotei.kana: よしのちょうていあと
yoshino_chotei.text: 吉野朝廷は1336年（延元元年）、京を追われた後醍醐天皇が大和国吉野（奈良県吉野町）に開いた南朝の朝廷。後醍醐・後村上・長慶・後亀山と4代57年にわたって続き、1392年（明徳3年）に北朝との合一で終焉した。吉水神社・如意輪寺・吉野水分神社など南朝関連史跡が点在し、桜の名所としても全国的に有名。
yoshino_chotei.highlight: 後醍醐天皇が開き4代57年続いた南朝の朝廷。桜の名所と歴史の宝庫
yoshino_chotei.name_en: Yoshino Imperial Court Ruins (Southern Court, Emperor Godaigo)
yoshino_chotei.highlight_en: The Southern Court was founded by Emperor Go-Daigo and lasted for 57 years over four generations. A famous cherry blossom spot and a treasure trove of history
yoshino_chotei.text_en: The Yoshino Imperial Court was an imperial court of the Southern Court that was established in Yoshino, Yamato Province (Yoshino Town, Nara Prefecture) in 1336 (1st year of the Engen era) by Emperor Go-Daigo, who was forced out of Kyoto. It continued for 57 years through four generations: Go-Daigo, Go-Murakami, Nagayoshi, and Go-Kameyama, and ended with the union with the Northern Court in 1392 (Meitoku 3). It is dotted with historical sites related to the Southern Dynasty, such as Yoshimizu Shrine, Nyoirinji Temple, and Yoshino Mizu Shrine, and is also famous nationwide as a cherry blossom viewing spot.

shichijo_kawara.name: 七条河原（足利尊氏の決戦地）
shichijo_kawara.text: 七条河原は京都・鴨川の七条付近の河原で、南北朝時代の1336年、足利尊氏軍と新田義貞・北畠顕家連合軍が激突した古戦場。京都の市街戦の舞台として有名で、何度も繰り返された南北朝動乱の主戦場の一つ。中世以降は罪人の処刑場・晒し首の場としても使われた。三十三間堂・蓮華王院などの近くに位置する。
shichijo_kawara.highlight: 南北朝の京都市街戦の主戦場。三十三間堂すぐ近くの鴨川河原
shichijo_kawara.highlight_en: The main battlefield of the Kyoto city battle between the Northern and Southern Courts. Kamogawa River near Sanjusangendo Temple
shichijo_kawara.text_en: Shichijo Kawara is a river near Shichijo on the Kamogawa River in Kyoto, and is an old battlefield where Takauji Ashikaga's army and the combined army of Yoshisada Nitta and Akiie Kitabatake clashed in 1336 during the Nanbokucho period. It is famous as the stage for urban battles in Kyoto, and was one of the main battlegrounds during the Nanbokucho Uprising, which was repeated many times. From the Middle Ages onwards, it was also used as a place for the execution and display of heads of criminals. It is located near Sanjusangen-do Temple, Rengeo-in Temple, etc.

chihaya_aka_battle.name: 千早赤阪村（南北朝最大の籠城戦）

transit.name: 金剛バス「金剛山ロープウェイ前」

chihaya_aka_battle.text: 千早赤阪村は楠木正成の本拠地で、千早城・上赤坂城・下赤坂城の3城を中心に1331-1333年に幕府軍と激戦を展開した南北朝動乱の聖地。「楠木氏発祥地」「南朝発祥地」として、村内には楠木正成生誕地碑・楠公誕生地・道の駅ちはやあかさかなど史跡が点在する。日本で唯一の「村」名を持つ単独自治体としても知られる。
chihaya_aka_battle.highlight: 楠木正成の本拠地・南朝発祥地。千早城・赤坂城など多数の南朝史跡
chihaya_aka_battle.name_en: Chihaya Akasaka Village (the largest siege battle of the Northern and Southern Courts)
chihaya_aka_battle.highlight_en: The home of Masashige Kusunoki and the birthplace of the Southern Court. Numerous Southern Court historical sites such as Chihaya Castle and Akasaka Castle
