chihaya_aka_battle.text_en: Chihayaakasaka Village was the home base of Masashige Kusunoki, and was a sacred place during the Nanbokucho turmoil, where fierce battles with the Shogunate army took place between 1331 and 1333, centering around the three castles of Chihaya Castle, Kamiakasaka Castle, and Shimoakasaka Castle. Known as the ``birthplace of the Kusunoki clan'' and ``the birthplace of the Southern Court,'' the village is dotted with historical sites such as the birthplace monument of Masashige Kusunoki, the birthplace of Lord Kusunoki, and the Chihaya Akasaka roadside station. It is also known as the only independent municipality in Japan with the name ``village''.

kamakura_kanaisawa.name: 化粧坂（新田義貞 鎌倉攻めの切通）
kamakura_kanaisawa.text: 化粧坂は鎌倉七口の一つで、1333年5月の新田義貞の鎌倉攻めにおける主戦場の一つ。義貞軍は化粧坂・極楽寺坂・巨福呂坂の3方向から鎌倉へ攻め込み、化粧坂では幕府軍と激戦を交えた。最終的に稲村ヶ崎を突破した義貞軍が鎌倉になだれ込み、北条氏が滅亡した。今も急な切通の地形が中世の戦の姿を伝える。
kamakura_kanaisawa.highlight: 鎌倉七口の要衝・新田義貞 鎌倉攻めの主戦場。今も中世の切通が残る
kamakura_kanaisawa.highlight_en: Yoshisada Nitta, the strategic point of Kamakura Nanakuchi, the main battlefield of the attack on Kamakura. The medieval cutouts still remain.
kamakura_kanaisawa.text_en: Kosekizaka is one of the Seven Entrances of Kamakura, and one of the main battlegrounds during Nitta Yoshisada's attack on Kamakura in May 1333. Yoshisada's army attacked Kamakura from three directions: Kosume-zaka, Gokurakuji-zaka, and Kofukuro-zaka, and engaged in a fierce battle with the shogunate's army on Kosekezaka. Yoshisada's army finally broke through Inamuragasaki and rushed into Kamakura, resulting in the destruction of the Hojo clan. Even today, the steep cut-through terrain gives us a glimpse of medieval warfare.

taiheiki_nawate.name: 住吉浜古戦場（北畠顕家 戦死の地）
taiheiki_nawate.kana: すみよしはまこせんじょう
taiheiki_nawate.text: 住吉浜・阿倍野は1338年（暦応元年）、南朝の若き名将・北畠顕家（21歳）が足利尊氏方の高師直軍と激戦の末、戦死した古戦場。後醍醐天皇に仕えた顕家は、東北から京への二度の遠征で尊氏を破った天才武将だったが、最後はこの地で力尽きた。阿倍野神社には北畠親房・顕家親子が祭神として祀られている。
taiheiki_nawate.highlight: 南朝の若き天才武将・北畠顕家21歳が戦死した古戦場。阿倍野神社で顕彰
taiheiki_nawate.name_en: Sumiyoshihama Battlefield (place where Akiie Kitabatake died in battle)
taiheiki_nawate.highlight_en: The old battlefield where 21-year-old Akiie Kitabatake, a genius young military commander of the Southern Court, died in battle. Honored at Abeno Shrine
taiheiki_nawate.text_en: Sumiyoshihama/Abeno is an old battlefield where in 1338 (the first year of the calendar), Akiie Kitabatake (21 years old), a famous young general of the Southern Court, was killed in a fierce battle with Takashi Takauji's army on Takauji Ashikaga's side. Akiie, who served Emperor Go-Daigo, was a genius military commander who defeated Takauji on two expeditions from Tohoku to Kyoto, but he ultimately ran out of steam here. Abeno Shrine enshrines Chikafusa Kitabatake and his son Akiie as deities.

anegawa_battle.name: 姉川古戦場（信長・家康vs浅井・朝倉）
anegawa_battle.kana: あねがわこせんじょう
anegawa_battle.text: 姉川の戦いは1570年6月28日、織田信長・徳川家康連合軍と浅井長政・朝倉景健連合軍が近江国姉川（滋賀県長浜市）で激突した戦い。徳川家康軍の奮戦と織田家家臣・榊原康政の活躍で連合軍が勝利。浅井・朝倉氏は壊滅的打撃を受け、3年後の小谷城・一乗谷の戦いで滅亡へと向かう。「血川」と呼ばれるほどの激戦だった。
anegawa_battle.highlight: 信長・家康vs浅井・朝倉の決戦。「血川」と呼ばれた戦国屈指の激戦
anegawa_battle.highlight_en: Decisive battle between Nobunaga and Ieyasu vs. Asai and Asakura. One of the fiercest battles in the Sengoku period, known as the “Blood River”
anegawa_battle.text_en: The Battle of Anegawa was a battle that took place on June 28, 1570, when the combined forces of Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu and the combined forces of Asai Nagamasa and Asakura Kageken clashed in Anegawa, Omi Province (Nagahama City, Shiga Prefecture). The Allied forces won thanks to the brave fighting of Tokugawa Ieyasu's army and the efforts of Yasumasa Sakakibara, a vassal of the Oda family. The Asai/Asakura clan suffered a devastating blow, and three years later, at the Battle of Odari Castle and Ichijodani, they headed for extinction. The battle was so fierce that it was called the "River of Blood."

itsukushima_battle.name: 厳島古戦場（毛利元就 奇襲の戦い）
itsukushima_battle.kana: いつくしまこせんじょう
itsukushima_battle.text: 厳島の戦いは1555年10月、安芸の毛利元就が陶晴賢を厳島（広島県廿日市市）に誘い出し奇襲で討ち取った戦い。元就は4000の兵で2万の陶軍を撃破するという「日本三大奇襲」の一つに数えられる戦勝で、これを契機に毛利氏は中国地方の覇者へと躍進した。世界遺産・厳島神社の島が戦国の決戦地となった珍しい事例。
itsukushima_battle.highlight: 毛利元就が4000で陶軍2万を奇襲で破った日本三大奇襲。世界遺産の地
itsukushima_battle.highlight_en: One of Japan's three greatest surprise attacks, in which Motonari Mouri defeated Sue's 20,000 troops with 4,000 troops. world heritage site
itsukushima_battle.text_en: The Battle of Itsukushima took place in October 1555, when Mori Motonari of Aki lured Sue Harukata to Itsukushima (Hatsukaichi City, Hiroshima Prefecture) and defeated him in a surprise attack. Motonari was a victory that was considered one of the ``Three Great Surprise Attacks of Japan,'' in which 4,000 soldiers defeated the 20,000-strong Sue army, and this victory served as an opportunity for the Mori clan to leapfrog to become the hegemon of the Chugoku region. A rare case in which the island of Itsukushima Shrine, a World Heritage Site, became the site of a decisive battle during the Sengoku period.

kawagoe_yasen.name: 河越夜戦古戦場（北条氏康 8000vs8万の奇跡）
kawagoe_yasen.text: 河越夜戦は1546年4月、北条氏康がわずか8000の兵で関東管領・上杉憲政＋古河公方・足利晴氏連合軍8万を夜襲で撃破した戦い。日本三大奇襲・三大夜戦の一つで、これにより北条氏の関東支配が確立した。氏康は地味な装束で敵陣を奇襲し、上杉軍を大混乱に陥れた。河越城（川越城）が舞台。
kawagoe_yasen.highlight: 北条氏康8000vs上杉8万の奇跡的勝利。日本三大奇襲・三大夜戦の一つ
kawagoe_yasen.name_en: Kawagoe Night Battle Battlefield (Ujiyasu Hojo 8000 vs 80,000 Miracle)
kawagoe_yasen.highlight_en: A miraculous victory between Ujiyasu Hojo 8000 and Uesugi 8000. One of Japan's three major surprise attacks and three major night battles
kawagoe_yasen.text_en: The Night Battle of Kawagoe took place in April 1546, when Hojo Ujiyasu defeated 80,000 combined forces of Kanto Kanrei, Norimasa Uesugi, Koga Kubo, and Haruji Ashikaga in a night attack with just 8,000 soldiers. It was one of Japan's three major surprise attacks and three major night battles, and established the Hojo clan's control over the Kanto region. Ujiyasu made a surprise attack on the enemy camp wearing plain clothes, throwing the Uesugi army into chaos. The setting is Kawagoe Castle (Kawagoe Castle).

konodai_battle.name: 国府台古戦場（北条vs里見の関東決戦）
konodai_battle.kana: こうのだいこせんじょう
konodai_battle.text: 国府台合戦は1538年（第一次）と1564年（第二次）に下総国国府台（千葉県市川市）で北条氏綱・氏康と房総の里見義堯・義弘の間で行われた関東支配権をめぐる激戦。特に第二次合戦は北条氏康の謀略により里見軍が大敗、関東での北条氏の覇権が確定した。江戸湾沿岸の最重要戦略拠点。
konodai_battle.highlight: 北条vs里見の関東覇権をかけた2度の決戦。江戸湾沿岸の最重要戦略地
konodai_battle.name_en: Kokufudai Battlefield (Kanto decisive battle between Hojo and Satomi)
konodai_battle.highlight_en: Two decisive battles for Kanto supremacy between Hojo and Satomi. The most important strategic location along the coast of Edo Bay
konodai_battle.text_en: The Battle of Kokufudai was a fierce battle for control of the Kanto region that took place in Kokufudai, Shimousa Province (Ichikawa City, Chiba Prefecture) in 1538 (First Battle) and 1564 (Second Battle) between Hojo Ujitsuna and Ujiyasu and Boso's Yoshiya Satomi and Yoshihiro. In particular, in the second battle, the Satomi army was defeated by Ujiyasu Hojo's strategy, and the Hojo clan's hegemony in the Kanto region was confirmed. The most important strategic base along the coast of Edo Bay.

okitanawate_battle.name: 沖田畷古戦場（島津×龍造寺の九州決戦）
okitanawate_battle.kana: おきたなわてこせんじょう
okitanawate_battle.text: 沖田畷の戦いは1584年3月、肥前国島原半島の湿地帯で、薩摩・島津家久＋有馬晴信連合軍5000が肥前の龍造寺隆信25000を破った九州統一戦の決戦。「九州三強」の一角・龍造寺隆信は討ち取られ、九州の覇権争いは島津氏の独走へと傾いた。湿地と狭路を利用した島津の見事な奇襲戦術が知られる。
okitanawate_battle.highlight: 島津5000が龍造寺25000を破り隆信を討ち取った九州統一の決定戦
okitanawate_battle.name_en: Okitanawate Battlefield (Kyushu decisive battle between Shimazu and Ryuzoji)
okitanawate_battle.highlight_en: The decisive battle for the unification of Kyushu where Shimazu 5000 defeated Ryuzoji 25000 and defeated Takanobu.
okitanawate_battle.text_en: The Battle of Okitanawate was held in March 1584 in the wetlands of the Shimabara Peninsula in Hizen Province, and was the decisive battle for the unification of Kyushu in which the combined forces of Satsuma and Shimazu Iehisa + Arima Harunobu 5,000 troops defeated Hizen's Ryuzoji Takanobu 25,000 troops. Takanobu Ryuzoji, one of the ``Three Powers of Kyushu,'' was defeated, and the battle for supremacy in Kyushu became dominated by the Shimazu clan. Shimadzu's brilliant surprise attack tactics using wetlands and narrow roads are well known.

hetsukigawa_battle.name: 戸次川古戦場（島津×豊臣の九州決戦）
hetsukigawa_battle.kana: へつぎがわこせんじょう
hetsukigawa_battle.text: 戸次川の戦いは1586年12月、豊後国戸次川（大分市）で島津家久が四国軍の仙石秀久・長宗我部信親・十河存保ら豊臣方を撃破した戦い。長宗我部信親（元親の嫡男）・十河存保が討ち死にし、豊臣秀吉の九州征伐の発端となった。長宗我部信親の戦死は、後の長宗我部家衰退の遠因となる悲劇だった。
hetsukigawa_battle.highlight: 島津家久が豊臣方を撃破。長宗我部信親が戦死した九州征伐前夜の決戦
hetsukigawa_battle.name_en: Tojigawa Battlefield (Kyushu decisive battle between Shimazu and Toyotomi)
hetsukigawa_battle.highlight_en: Shimazu Iehisa defeated the Toyotomi army. The decisive battle on the eve of the Kyushu conquest in which Nobuchika Chosokabe was killed in action.
hetsukigawa_battle.text_en: The Battle of Totsugawa was fought in December 1586 at Totsugi River (Oita City), Bungo Province, in which Shimazu Iehisa defeated the Toyotomi forces of the Shikoku Army, including Hidehisa Sengoku, Nobuchika Chosokabe, and Tsunami Sogo. Chosokabe Nobuchika (Motochika's eldest son) and Sogo Nobuyasu died in battle, marking the beginning of Toyotomi Hideyoshi's conquest of Kyushu. The death of Nobuchika Chosokabe in battle was a tragedy that was the cause of the later decline of the Chosokabe family.

suriagehara_battle.name: 摺上原古戦場（伊達政宗 奥州統一戦）
suriagehara_battle.kana: すりあげはらこせんじょう
suriagehara_battle.text: 摺上原の戦いは1589年6月、奥州南部で伊達政宗が芦名義広（佐竹氏一族）を破った戦い。会津若松・磐梯山麓の摺上原（福島県磐梯町）が舞台で、政宗の電撃戦により芦名氏は本拠地・黒川城（後の会津若松城）を失い滅亡した。これにより23歳の政宗は南奥州114万石を支配する大大名となるが、翌年豊臣秀吉に屈する。
suriagehara_battle.highlight: 23歳の伊達政宗が芦名氏を滅ぼし南奥州を統一した決戦地
suriagehara_battle.name_en: Suriuehara Ancient Battlefield (Date Masamune's Oshu Unification Battle)
suriagehara_battle.highlight_en: The decisive battleground where 23-year-old Date Masamune destroyed the Ashina clan and unified southern Oshu.
suriagehara_battle.text_en: The Battle of Suriuehara was a battle in June 1589 in southern Oshu in which Date Masamune defeated Yoshihiro Ashina (of the Satake clan). The story is set in Suriuehara at the foot of Mt. Bandai in Aizuwakamatsu (Bandai Town, Fukushima Prefecture), where the Ashina clan lost its stronghold, Kurokawa Castle (later Aizuwakamatsu Castle), and fell to ruin due to Masamune's blitzkrieg. As a result, Masamune, at the age of 23, became a great daimyo who ruled over 1,140,000 koku in southern Oshu, but he succumbed to Toyotomi Hideyoshi the following year.

mimigawa_battle.name: 耳川古戦場（島津×大友の九州決戦）
mimigawa_battle.kana: みみがわこせんじょう
mimigawa_battle.text: 耳川の戦いは1578年11月、日向国耳川（宮崎県日向市）で島津義久が豊後の大友宗麟を破った戦い。九州六カ国を支配した「九州の覇者」大友氏はこの一戦で大打撃を受け衰退。代わって島津氏が九州統一に大きく前進した。キリシタン大名・大友宗麟の野望挫折の地でもある。
mimigawa_battle.highlight: 島津義久が大友宗麟を破り九州統一に大きく前進した決定戦
mimigawa_battle.name_en: Mimikawa Battlefield (Kyushu decisive battle between Shimazu and Otomo)
mimigawa_battle.highlight_en: Decisive match in which Yoshihisa Shimazu defeated Sorin Otomo and made great progress towards unification of Kyushu.
mimigawa_battle.text_en: The Battle of Mimikawa was fought in November 1578 in Mimikawa, Hyuga Province (Hyuga City, Miyazaki Prefecture), in which Yoshihisa Shimazu defeated Sorin Otomo of Bungo. The Otomo clan, the ``ruler of Kyushu'' who ruled over six countries in Kyushu, suffered a major blow in this battle and declined. In his place, the Shimazu clan made great strides in unifying Kyushu. It is also the place where the ambitions of the Christian daimyo Otomo Sorin were frustrated.

yamazaki_battle.name: 山崎古戦場（明智光秀×秀吉の決戦）
yamazaki_battle.kana: やまざきこせんじょう
yamazaki_battle.text: 山崎の戦いは1582年6月13日、本能寺の変で織田信長を討った明智光秀と、毛利攻めから「中国大返し」で駆けつけた羽柴秀吉が、京と摂津の境・山崎（京都府大山崎町）で激突した決戦。光秀軍1万6千、秀吉軍4万。「天王山を占めた者が勝つ」と言われる戦況の鍵となった天王山。光秀は敗れて落ち武者狩りに討たれ、秀吉が信長後継への足がかりを得た。
yamazaki_battle.highlight: 明智光秀vs秀吉の決戦。「天王山」の語源となった信長後継争いの天下分け目
yamazaki_battle.name_en: Yamazaki Battlefield (Akechi Mitsuhide x Hideyoshi's decisive battle)
yamazaki_battle.highlight_en: The decisive battle between Mitsuhide Akechi and Hideyoshi. The dividing point in the battle for Nobunaga's succession, which is the origin of the word "Tennozan"
yamazaki_battle.text_en: The Battle of Yamazaki was a decisive battle that took place on June 13, 1582, when Mitsuhide Akechi, who had defeated Nobunaga Oda during the Honnoji Incident, and Hideyoshi Hashiba, who had rushed in to attack Mori in a ``Great Return of China,'' clashed at Yamazaki (Oyamazaki Town, Kyoto Prefecture) on the border between Kyoto and Settsu. Mitsuhide's army was 16,000, Hideyoshi's army was 40,000. Tennozan was the key to the outcome of the war, which is said to be ``the one who occupies Tennozan wins.'' Mitsuhide was defeated and killed by warrior hunters, and Hideyoshi gained a foothold to succeed Nobunaga.

nagashima_ikko.name: 長島一向一揆古戦場（信長の苦戦）
nagashima_ikko.kana: ながしまいっこういっき
nagashima_ikko.text: 長島一向一揆は1570-74年、伊勢長島（三重県桑名市）の本願寺門徒が織田信長に対して4年にわたり蜂起した宗教戦争。信長は3度の出兵を重ね、ついに1574年に2万人の門徒を焼き殺すという凄惨な皆殺し戦に出てようやく鎮圧。信長の宗教勢力との苛烈な戦いを象徴する古戦場。
nagashima_ikko.highlight: 信長が4年苦戦の末、門徒2万人を焼殺して鎮圧した宗教戦争の地
nagashima_ikko.name_en: Nagashima Ikko Ikki old battlefield (Nobunaga's struggle)
nagashima_ikko.highlight_en: The site of a religious war in which Nobunaga put down 20,000 of his followers by burning them to death after four years of struggle.
nagashima_ikko.text_en: The Nagashima Ikko Ikki was a four-year religious war that took place between 1570 and 1574, when Honganji followers on Ise Nagashima (Kuwana City, Mie Prefecture) rose up against Oda Nobunaga. Nobunaga dispatched troops three times, and finally put down the war in 1574 in a gruesome battle in which 20,000 of his followers were burned to death. An old battlefield that symbolizes Nobunaga's fierce battle with religious forces.

shigisan_matsunaga.name: 信貴山城跡（松永久秀 爆死の地）

transit.name: 近鉄信貴山口→ケーブル

shigisan_matsunaga.text: 信貴山城は大和国信貴山（奈良県平群町）に築かれた山城で、戦国の梟雄・松永久秀の最後の居城。1577年、織田信長への謀反を起こし籠城した久秀は、信長が所望した名物茶器「平蜘蛛釜」を抱えて天守に火をかけ爆死したと伝わる。「日本初の天守を持つ城」「日本初の爆死」「将軍・主君殺し」など戦国史上の「初めて」が多い梟雄の終焉地。
shigisan_matsunaga.highlight: 戦国の梟雄・松永久秀が平蜘蛛釜を抱えて爆死した山城
shigisan_matsunaga.name_en: Shigiyama Castle ruins (place where Hisashi Matsunaga died)
shigisan_matsunaga.highlight_en: Yamashiro where the Sengoku period owl hero Hisashi Matsunaga died in an explosion while holding a flat spider kettle.
shigisan_matsunaga.text_en: Shigisan Castle is a mountain castle built on Mt. Shigi, Yamato Province (Heigun Town, Nara Prefecture), and was the last residence of Hisashi Matsunaga, the owl hero of the Sengoku period. In 1577, Hisahide rebelled against Oda Nobunaga and became siege, and it is said that he set fire to the castle tower and died in an explosion while holding the famous tea utensil ``Hiragumo Kama'' that Nobunaga had requested. Fukuo's final resting place has many "firsts" in the history of the Sengoku period, such as "Japan's first castle with a castle tower," "Japan's first explosion death," and "killing of a general and lord."

toba_fushimi_battle.name: 鳥羽伏見の戦い古戦場（戊辰戦争の幕開け）
toba_fushimi_battle.kana: とばふしみのたたかい
toba_fushimi_battle.text: 鳥羽・伏見の戦いは1868年1月3日、京都の南郊・鳥羽と伏見で旧幕府軍15000と薩長新政府軍5000が激突した戊辰戦争の幕開けの戦い。装備で劣るものの錦の御旗を掲げた新政府軍が勝利し、将軍・徳川慶喜は大坂城から江戸に逃れた。淀城・鳥羽離宮跡などに古戦場碑が点在し、新政府軍勝利の起点となった。
toba_fushimi_battle.highlight: 戊辰戦争の幕開け・錦の御旗で旧幕府軍15000を破った新政府軍勝利の起点
toba_fushimi_battle.name_en: Battle of Toba-Fushimi (the beginning of the Boshin War)
toba_fushimi_battle.highlight_en: The beginning of the Boshin War, the starting point of the victory of the new government army, which defeated 15,000 former shogunate troops with the Nishiki flag
toba_fushimi_battle.text_en: The Battle of Toba-Fushimi was the opening battle of the Boshin War on January 3, 1868, when 15,000 former Shogunate troops and 5,000 new Satcho government troops clashed in Toba and Fushimi, the southern suburbs of Kyoto. Despite being inferior in equipment, the new government army, flying a brocade flag, was victorious, and the shogun, Yoshinobu Tokugawa, fled from Osaka Castle to Edo. Historic battlefield monuments are dotted around the ruins of Yodo Castle and Toba Imperial Villa, which served as the starting point for the new government's victory.

ueno_shogitai.name: 上野戦争跡（彰義隊 最後の決戦）
ueno_shogitai.text: 上野戦争は1868年5月15日、旧幕臣の彰義隊2000人余りが上野・寛永寺に籠城し、新政府軍と戦った戊辰戦争の戦い。大村益次郎の戦術指揮と佐賀藩のアームストロング砲によって、彰義隊はわずか一日で壊滅した。寛永寺の堂宇の多くが焼失し、上野公園内に彰義隊の墓と西郷隆盛像が建つ。
ueno_shogitai.highlight: 旧幕臣・彰義隊2000人がアームストロング砲で一日で壊滅した戦地
ueno_shogitai.highlight_en: The battlefield where 2,000 former Shogun retainers and Shogi troops were destroyed in one day by Armstrong cannons.
ueno_shogitai.text_en: The Ueno War was a battle of the Boshin War that took place on May 15, 1868, when more than 2,000 Shogi troops, former vassals of the shogunate, holed up at Kan'eiji Temple in Ueno and fought against the new government forces. Thanks to Masujiro Omura's tactical command and the Saga clan's Armstrong cannon, the Shogitai were annihilated in just one day. Many of the halls of Kan'eiji Temple were destroyed by fire, and the grave of the Shogitai and the statue of Takamori Saigo were erected in Ueno Park.

bonari_pass_battle.name: 母成峠古戦場（会津戦争の決戦）
bonari_pass_battle.kana: ぼなりとうげこせんじょう

transit.name: 磐梯熱海より自家用車

bonari_pass_battle.text: 母成峠の戦いは1868年8月21日、会津若松へ向かう新政府軍3000が、会津・大鳥圭介率いる旧幕府連合軍800を母成峠（福島県猪苗代町）で破った戊辰戦争・会津戦争の決戦。これにより会津若松への道が開かれ、9月22日の会津若松城開城、白虎隊の悲劇へとつながった。新選組の土方歳三もこの戦いに参加。
bonari_pass_battle.highlight: 会津戦争の決戦・新政府軍が突破して若松城へ向かった戦地。土方歳三も参戦
bonari_pass_battle.name_en: Moshinari Pass Old Battlefield (decisive battle of the Aizu War)
bonari_pass_battle.highlight_en: The decisive battle of the Aizu War, where the new government forces broke through and headed towards Wakamatsu Castle. Toshizo Hijikata also participated
bonari_pass_battle.text_en: The Battle of Moshinari Pass was the decisive battle of the Boshin War and Aizu War on August 21, 1868, when 3,000 new government troops headed toward Aizuwakamatsu defeated 800 former shogunate allied forces led by Keisuke Otori at Moshinari Pass (Inawashiro Town, Fukushima Prefecture). This opened the way to Aizuwakamatsu, leading to the surrender of Aizuwakamatsu Castle on September 22nd and the tragedy of the Byakkotai. Toshizo Hijikata of the Shinsengumi also participated in this battle.

nagaoka_castle_battle.name: 長岡城の戦い（河井継之助 北越戦争）
nagaoka_castle_battle.kana: ながおかじょうのたたかい
nagaoka_castle_battle.text: 長岡城の戦いは1868年5-7月、越後・長岡藩の家老・河井継之助が新政府軍に抵抗した戊辰戦争・北越戦争の主戦場。継之助は当時最新鋭の機関銃「ガトリング砲」を導入し、長岡藩7万4千石の小藩ながら新政府軍と互角に戦った。5月の落城後、7月25日に奇襲で奪還するも、継之助は被弾し戦死。長岡市民の精神的支柱となった悲劇の名宰相。
nagaoka_castle_battle.highlight: 河井継之助がガトリング砲で新政府軍と互角に戦った北越戦争の主戦場
nagaoka_castle_battle.name_en: Battle of Nagaoka Castle (Tsuginosuke Kawai, Hokuetsu War)
nagaoka_castle_battle.highlight_en: The main battlefield of the Hokuetsu War, where Tsuginosuke Kawai fought on equal terms with the new government army using his Gatling gun.
nagaoka_castle_battle.text_en: The Battle of Nagaoka Castle took place from May to July 1868, and was the main battleground of the Boshin War and Hokuetsu War, in which Tsuginosuke Kawai, a retainer of the Nagaoka domain in Echigo, resisted the new government forces. Tsuginosuke introduced the Gatling gun, the most advanced machine gun at the time, and fought on equal terms with the new government's army, even though the Nagaoka domain was a small domain with a total of 74,000 koku. After the castle fell in May, the castle was recaptured in a surprise attack on July 25, but Tsuginosuke was hit by a bullet and killed in action. A tragic prime minister who became the spiritual pillar of the citizens of Nagaoka.

nihonmatsu_shonentai_battle.name: 大壇口古戦場（二本松少年隊 悲劇の地）
nihonmatsu_shonentai_battle.kana: おおだんぐちこせんじょう
nihonmatsu_shonentai_battle.text: 大壇口は1868年7月29日、戊辰戦争の二本松戦争で12-17歳の少年たち62名「二本松少年隊」が新政府軍と戦った古戦場。年齢を2歳水増しして出陣した少年たちは14名が戦死、二本松城も陥落した。白虎隊と並ぶ幕末の悲劇として知られ、二本松霞ヶ城公園には少年隊群像と隊士の墓が建てられている。
nihonmatsu_shonentai_battle.highlight: 12-17歳の二本松少年隊62名が戦った悲劇の地。14名戦死
nihonmatsu_shonentai_battle.highlight_en: The tragic site where 62 members of the Nihonmatsu boys' group, aged 12 to 17, fought. 14 killed in action
nihonmatsu_shonentai_battle.text_en: Odanguchi is a former battlefield where 62 boys between the ages of 12 and 17 fought against the new government army on July 29, 1868 during the Nihonmatsu War of the Boshin War. Fourteen boys who went to war after increasing their age by two years died in battle, and Nihonmatsu Castle also fell. Along with the Byakkotai, it is known as a tragedy at the end of the Edo period, and a statue of the Shonen-tai group and the graves of the soldiers are erected in Nihonmatsu Kasumigajo Park.

shirakawaguchi_battle.name: 白河口の戦い古戦場（奥羽越列藩同盟の崩壊）
shirakawaguchi_battle.kana: しらかわぐちこせんじょう
shirakawaguchi_battle.text: 白河口の戦いは1868年5月-7月、白河小峰城をめぐって新政府軍と奥羽越列藩同盟が3か月にわたり激戦を繰り広げた戊辰戦争の戦い。会津・仙台・米沢など列藩同盟軍は当初優勢だったが、新政府軍の精強さに最終的に敗北。白河の落城は奥羽越列藩同盟崩壊の始まりとなり、東北戦線の流れを決定づけた。
shirakawaguchi_battle.highlight: 奥羽越列藩同盟が3か月激戦の末敗北した東北戦線の流れを決めた決戦
shirakawaguchi_battle.name_en: Battle of Shirakawaguchi Ancient Battlefield (Collapse of the Ouuetsu clan alliance)
shirakawaguchi_battle.highlight_en: The decisive battle that decided the course of the Tohoku Front, in which the Ouuetsu Domain Alliance was defeated after three months of fierce fighting.
shirakawaguchi_battle.text_en: The Battle of Shirakawaguchi was fought between May and July 1868 during the Boshin War, in which the new government forces and the Ouuetsu feudal alliance fought fiercely over Shirakawa Komine Castle for three months. The allied forces of Aizu, Sendai, and Yonezawa initially had the upper hand, but were ultimately defeated by the strength of the new government forces. The fall of Shirakawa marked the beginning of the collapse of the Ou-etsu clan alliance and determined the course of the Tohoku Front.

ikedaya_jiken.name: 池田屋事件跡（新選組 名を上げた事件）
ikedaya_jiken.text: 池田屋事件は1864年6月5日、京都・三条木屋町の旅館「池田屋」に集まった長州藩・土佐藩などの尊王攘夷派志士20余名を、新選組の近藤勇・沖田総司・永倉新八ら9名が襲撃した事件。志士9名が斬殺・捕縛され、明治維新は1年遅れたとされる。新選組の名声を全国に轟かせるきっかけとなった事件で、現在は跡地碑と居酒屋「池田屋」が建つ。
ikedaya_jiken.highlight: 新選組の名を全国に轟かせた尊攘志士襲撃事件。明治維新を1年遅らせた
ikedaya_jiken.name_en: Ikedaya Incident (The incident that made the Shinsengumi famous)
ikedaya_jiken.highlight_en: The attack on the Sonjo Shishi that made the name of the Shinsengumi famous throughout the country. Delayed the Meiji Restoration by one year
ikedaya_jiken.text_en: The Ikedaya Incident took place on June 5, 1864, when nine members of the Shinsengumi, including Isamu Kondo, Souji Okita, and Shinpachi Nagakura, attacked more than 20 patriots from the Choshu and Tosa clans who were members of the Sonno Joi faction who had gathered at the Ikedaya inn in Sanjo Kiyamachi, Kyoto. Nine patriots were killed and captured, and the Meiji Restoration is said to have been delayed by one year. This incident caused the Shinsengumi to become famous throughout the country, and a monument and a pub called Ikedaya now stand on the site.

hamaguri_gate_war.name: 蛤御門の変跡（禁門の変）
hamaguri_gate_war.kana: はまぐりごもんのへん
hamaguri_gate_war.text: 蛤御門の変（禁門の変）は1864年7月19日、長州藩が京都御所の蛤御門付近で会津・薩摩藩を中心とする幕府方と激突した戦い。長州藩は敗れ、藩士・久坂玄瑞らが自刃。この事件で長州は朝敵とされ、第一次長州征伐の発端となった。京都市内で大火災が発生し約3万戸が焼失、「どんどん焼け」と呼ばれる大火災となった。
hamaguri_gate_war.highlight: 長州が京都御所で会津・薩摩と激突。京都3万戸焼失「どんどん焼け」の地
hamaguri_gate_war.name_en: The Incident of Hamaguri Gomon (Kinmon Incident)
hamaguri_gate_war.highlight_en: Choshu clashes with Aizu and Satsuma at the Kyoto Imperial Palace. Land of Dondon Burns, where 30,000 houses in Kyoto were destroyed by fire
hamaguri_gate_war.text_en: The Hamaguri Gomon Incident (Kinmon Incident) was a battle that took place on July 19, 1864, when the Choshu domain clashed with the Shogunate forces, centered on the Aizu and Satsuma domains, near the Hamaguri Gomon gate of the Kyoto Imperial Palace. The Choshu clan was defeated, and feudal retainers Genzui Kusaka and others committed suicide. This incident made Choshu an enemy of the Imperial Court, and became the beginning of the first Choshu conquest. A huge fire broke out in Kyoto City, destroying approximately 30,000 homes, resulting in a major fire known as the ``Dondon Burn''.

teradaya_jiken.name: 寺田屋（坂本龍馬・伏見奉行所襲撃）
teradaya_jiken.text: 寺田屋は京都・伏見の船宿で、幕末の2つの事件で歴史に名を残した。1862年4月の「寺田屋騒動」では薩摩藩の有馬新七ら過激派9名が同藩士に粛清された。1866年1月には坂本龍馬が伏見奉行所の捕り方に襲撃されるが、お龍の機転と高杉晋作からもらったピストルで脱出に成功した。建物は維新後に再建され、現在も旅館・史跡として公開されている。
teradaya_jiken.highlight: 坂本龍馬が伏見奉行所襲撃を脱出した宿。寺田屋騒動・薩摩粛清の地
teradaya_jiken.name_en: Teradaya (Ryoma Sakamoto and Fushimi Magistrate's Office attack)
teradaya_jiken.highlight_en: The inn where Ryoma Sakamoto escaped from the attack on the Fushimi Magistrate's Office. Place of Teradaya Riot and Satsuma Purge
teradaya_jiken.text_en: Teradaya is a boat inn in Fushimi, Kyoto that left its name in history for two incidents at the end of the Edo period. In April 1862, during the Teradaya Riot, nine extremists from the Satsuma domain, including Shinshichi Arima, were purged by samurai of the same domain. In January 1866, Ryōma Sakamoto was attacked by his captors at the Fushimi Magistrate's Office, but he succeeded in escaping with Oryū's quick thinking and the pistol given to him by Shinsaku Takasugi. The building was rebuilt after the Meiji Restoration and is still open to the public as an inn and historical site.

sakuradamon_gai.name: 桜田門外の変跡（井伊直弼 暗殺地）
sakuradamon_gai.kana: さくらだもんがいのへん
sakuradamon_gai.text: 桜田門外の変は1860年3月3日、江戸城桜田門外で大老・井伊直弼が水戸藩脱藩浪士17名と薩摩藩士1名に暗殺された事件。安政の大獄で吉田松陰ら多数の志士を処刑した井伊への報復で、雪降る朝に駕籠の中で銃撃を受けた直弼は首を取られた。江戸幕府の権威失墜の決定的な事件となり、明治維新への流れを加速させた。
sakuradamon_gai.highlight: 大老・井伊直弼が雪の朝に水戸浪士に暗殺された幕府権威失墜の事件
sakuradamon_gai.name_en: Traces outside Sakuradamon (place of Ii Naosuke's assassination)
sakuradamon_gai.highlight_en: The incident that led to the fall of the authority of the shogunate, in which the elder Ii Naosuke was assassinated by Mito Roshi on a snowy morning.
sakuradamon_gai.text_en: The Sakuradamon Incident took place on March 3, 1860, when Tairo Ii Naosuke was assassinated outside the Sakuradamon Gate of Edo Castle by 17 ronin samurai from the Mito clan and one samurai from the Satsuma clan. In retaliation for Ii, who had executed many patriots, including Shoin Yoshida, in the Great Prison of Ansei, Naosuke was shot in his palanquin on a snowy morning and was beheaded. This was a decisive incident that led to the fall of the authority of the Edo shogunate, and accelerated the trend toward the Meiji Restoration.

shimonoseki_war.name: 下関戦争跡（馬関戦争・四国艦隊砲撃）
shimonoseki_war.kana: しものせきせんそうあと
shimonoseki_war.text: 下関戦争（馬関戦争）は1863-64年、長州藩と英・仏・米・蘭の四国連合艦隊が下関海峡で激突した攘夷戦争。攘夷を実行した長州が外国船を砲撃したことに対する報復で、四国艦隊の圧倒的火力に長州藩は大敗。これにより長州は「攘夷」から「開国・倒幕」へと方針転換し、薩長同盟・明治維新への道を進む契機となった。砲台跡が壇之浦に残る。
shimonoseki_war.highlight: 長州が四国連合艦隊に大敗。攘夷から開国・倒幕への方針転換の契機
shimonoseki_war.name_en: Shimonoseki War Ruins (Baseki War, Shikoku Fleet Bombardment)
shimonoseki_war.highlight_en: Choshu was defeated by the Shikoku Combined Fleet. Opportunity to change policy from Joi to opening up the country and overthrowing the Shogunate
shimonoseki_war.text_en: The Shimonoseki War (Baseki War) was a Joi War in 1863-64 in which the Choshu clan and the Shikoku combined fleet of Britain, France, the United States, and the Netherlands clashed in the Shimonoseki Strait. In retaliation for Choshu's bombardment of foreign ships, which carried out the Joi expulsion, the Choshu clan suffered a crushing defeat due to the overwhelming firepower of the Shikoku fleet. As a result, Choshu changed its policy from ``exterminating Joi'' to ``opening the country and overthrowing the shogunate'' and became an opportunity to move forward on the path to the Satsuma-Choshu alliance and the Meiji Restoration. The remains of a gun battery remain in Dannoura.

satsu_ei_war.name: 薩英戦争跡（鹿児島湾の攘夷戦争）
satsu_ei_war.kana: さつえいせんそうあと
satsu_ei_war.text: 薩英戦争は1863年7月2-4日、生麦事件（1862）の報復として英国艦隊7隻が鹿児島湾に侵入し、薩摩藩と砲撃戦を交えた攘夷戦争。薩摩藩は鹿児島市街を焼かれる大損害を受けたが、英艦も大破。この戦闘で薩摩は西洋の軍事力の凄まじさを実感し、攘夷から開国・倒幕へと方針転換。後の薩長同盟・明治維新の起点となった。
satsu_ei_war.highlight: 生麦事件報復・英国艦隊と薩摩の砲撃戦。薩摩が開国に転じる契機
satsu_ei_war.name_en: Sites of the Satsuma-British War (Kagoshima Bay Joi War)
satsu_ei_war.highlight_en: Retaliation for the Namamugi Incident: Artillery battle between the British fleet and Satsuma. Opportunity for Satsuma to turn to opening up the country
satsu_ei_war.text_en: The Anglo-Satsuma War was a war between July 2 and 4, 1863, when seven British ships invaded Kagoshima Bay in retaliation for the Namamugi Incident (1862) and engaged in artillery battles with the Satsuma Domain. The Satsuma domain suffered heavy damage, with the city of Kagoshima being burned down, but British ships were also severely damaged. In this battle, Satsuma realized the formidable military power of the West, and changed its policy from expelling Joi to opening the country and overthrowing the Shogunate. It became the starting point of the later Satsuma-Choshu Alliance and Meiji Restoration.

abashi_battle.name: 阿波野・天王寺口の戦い（大坂夏の陣）
abashi_battle.kana: てんのうじぐちのたたかい
abashi_battle.text: 天王寺口の戦いは1615年5月7日、大坂夏の陣の最終決戦。豊臣方の真田信繁（幸村）が3500の赤備えで徳川家康の本陣に突撃し、家康をあと一歩のところまで追い詰めた「真田丸最後の輝き」の地。「日本一の兵」と称えられた信繁はこの戦いで戦死。翌日、大坂城は炎上し豊臣秀頼・淀殿が自害、豊臣家が滅亡した。安居神社（信繁戦死地）に碑が建つ。
abashi_battle.highlight: 真田信繁が家康本陣に突撃した「日本一の兵」最期の地。豊臣家滅亡の前夜
abashi_battle.name_en: Battle of Awano/Tennojiguchi (Summer Battle of Osaka)
abashi_battle.highlight_en: The final resting place of Nobushige Sanada, ``Japan's number one soldier,'' who charged into Ieyasu's headquarters. The night before the fall of the Toyotomi family
abashi_battle.text_en: The Battle of Tennojiguchi was fought on May 7, 1615, and was the final battle of the Summer Campaign in Osaka. This is the place where Sanada Nobushige (Yukimura) of Toyotomi's side attacked Tokugawa Ieyasu's main camp with 3,500 red armor and cornered Ieyasu to one step. Nobushige, who was praised as ``Japan's best soldier,'' died in this battle. The next day, Osaka Castle went up in flames, Toyotomi Hideyori and Yodo-dono committed suicide, and the Toyotomi family fell. A monument is erected at Yasui Shrine (the place where Nobushige died in battle).

kiyomizudera.name: 清水寺
kiyomizudera.text: 清水寺は778年、坂上田村麻呂の創建と伝わる北法相宗の寺院で、ユネスコ世界文化遺産「古都京都の文化財」の一つです。崖からせり出した「清水の舞台」は釘を一本も使わない懸造（かけづくり）で、本堂とともに国宝に指定されています。「清水の舞台から飛び降りる」の言葉でも知られ、江戸時代には実際に願掛けで飛び降りる人が後を絶ちませんでした。音羽の滝の霊水、坂上田村麻呂と蝦夷征伐の伝説、幕末には西郷隆盛と僧・月照が密議を交わした成就院など、千年以上の歴史が積み重なっています。
kiyomizudera.highlight: 坂上田村麻呂創建の世界遺産。釘を使わぬ「清水の舞台」は国宝
kiyomizudera.highlight_en: A world heritage site founded by Sakanoue Tamuramaro. The “Shimizu Stage” that does not use nails is a national treasure
kiyomizudera.text_en: Kiyomizu-dera is a temple of the Northern Hosso sect, said to have been founded by Sakanoue Tamuramaro in 778, and is one of the UNESCO World Heritage Sites, ``Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto.'' The Kiyomizu Stage, which juts out from the cliff, was built in a hanging structure without using a single nail, and has been designated as a national treasure along with the main hall. It is also known for the phrase "jumping off the stage of Shimizu," and during the Edo period, there was no end to people who actually jumped off the stage to make a wish. It has more than a thousand years of history, including the sacred waters of Otowa Falls, the legend of Sakanoue Tamuramaro and the Ezo Conquest, and Jojuin Temple, where Saigo Takamori and the monk Gessho had a secret meeting at the end of the Edo period.

yasaka_jinja.name: 八坂神社（祇園さん）
yasaka_jinja.text: 八坂神社は素戔嗚尊（すさのおのみこと）を主祭神とする全国祇園社の総本社で、社伝では656年の創建と伝わります。平安京で疫病が流行した869年、災厄退散を祈願して始まった「祇園御霊会」が、日本三大祭の一つ「祇園祭」の起源です。1か月にわたる祇園祭は山鉾巡行を中心に千年以上続き、ユネスコ無形文化遺産に登録されています。朱塗りの西楼門は東山のシンボルで、円山公園とともに京都随一の桜の名所でもあります。歴代の武将・町衆から篤い崇敬を受けてきました。
yasaka_jinja.highlight: 全国祇園社の総本社。千年続く日本三大祭「祇園祭」発祥の社
yasaka_jinja.highlight_en: Headquarters of Gionsha nationwide. The birthplace of Japan's three major festivals, the Gion Festival, which has been going on for 1,000 years
yasaka_jinja.text_en: Yasaka Shrine is the head office of the National Gion Shrine, whose main deity is Susanoo no Mikoto, and according to the shrine's legend, it was founded in 656. The origin of the Gion Festival, one of Japan's three major festivals, is the Gion Goryo-e, which began in 869 when an epidemic spread in Heiankyo, to pray for the exodus of disaster. The month-long Gion Festival has continued for over 1,000 years, centering on the float parade, and is registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. The vermilion-painted West Tower Gate is a symbol of Higashiyama, and along with Maruyama Park, it is also one of the best cherry blossom viewing spots in Kyoto. It has been deeply revered by successive military commanders and townsfolk.

kitano_tenmangu.name: 北野天満宮（菅原道真を祀る学問の神）
kitano_tenmangu.text: 北野天満宮は947年、無実の罪で大宰府に左遷され失意のうちに没した菅原道真を「天神様」として祀るために創建された神社で、全国約1万2千社の天満宮・天神社の総本社です。道真の死後に都で起きた天変地異や落雷を「道真の祟り」とした朝廷が、その霊を鎮めるために創建しました。学問の神として受験生の信仰を集め、毎月25日の「天神市」は京の風物詩。豊臣秀吉が催した「北野大茶湯」の舞台でもあり、約1500本の梅が咲く梅苑も有名です。
kitano_tenmangu.highlight: 菅原道真を祀る全国天満宮の総本社。学問の神・北野大茶湯の舞台
kitano_tenmangu.name_en: Kitano Tenmangu Shrine (the god of learning that enshrines Michizane Sugawara)
kitano_tenmangu.highlight_en: Headquarters of all the Tenmangu shrines in Japan that enshrines Michizane Sugawara. The stage of Kitano Ochayu, the god of learning
kitano_tenmangu.text_en: Kitano Tenmangu Shrine was built in 947 to enshrine Sugawara no Michizane, who died in despair after being demoted to Dazaifu for a crime he was not guilty of, and is the headquarters of approximately 12,000 Tenmangu shrines and shrines nationwide. The imperial court believed that the natural disasters and lightning strikes that occurred in the capital after Michizane's death were ``the curse of Michizane,'' and it was built to appease his spirit. It is worshiped by students as the god of learning, and the ``Tenjin Market'' held on the 25th of every month is a Kyoto tradition. It was also the setting for the Kitano Grand Tea Ceremony hosted by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, and is also famous for its plum garden, where approximately 1,500 plum trees bloom.

kyoto_gosho.name: 京都御所（幕末まで天皇の住まい）

transit.name: 地下鉄烏丸線「今出川」「丸太町」

kyoto_gosho.text: 京都御所は1331年から1869年（明治2年）の東京遷都まで、歴代天皇が住まいとした宮殿です。現在の建物は1855年の再建で、紫宸殿・清涼殿など平安時代以来の宮廷建築様式を伝えています。幕末には尊王攘夷運動の中心舞台となり、すぐ西の蛤御門では1864年の禁門の変が起き、王政復古の大号令もここで発せられました。和宮の生家でもあり、明治天皇はここで即位しました。広大な京都御苑に囲まれ、紫宸殿前の左近の桜・右近の橘が王朝の雅を今に伝えます。
kyoto_gosho.highlight: 幕末まで天皇が住んだ宮殿。王政復古の大号令が発せられた維新の舞台
kyoto_gosho.name_en: Kyoto Imperial Palace (residence of the Emperor until the end of the Edo period)
kyoto_gosho.highlight_en: The palace where the Emperor lived until the end of the Edo period. The stage of the Meiji Restoration, where the grand edict to restore the monarchy was issued.
kyoto_gosho.text_en: The Kyoto Imperial Palace was the residence of successive emperors from 1331 until the capital was moved to Tokyo in 1869 (Meiji 2). The current building was rebuilt in 1855 and retains the imperial architectural style from the Heian period, including Shishinden and Seiryoden. At the end of the Edo period, it became the center stage of the Sonno-joi movement, and the Kinmon Incident of 1864 took place at Hamaguri Gomon, just to the west, and the great edict for the restoration of the monarchy was also issued here. It is also the birthplace of Kazunomiya, and Emperor Meiji ascended the throne here. Surrounded by the vast Kyoto Gyoen National Garden, the Sakon cherry blossoms and Ukon Tachibana trees in front of Shishinden still convey the elegance of the dynasty.

nanzenji.name: 南禅寺（京都五山の上・別格の禅刹）
nanzenji.text: 南禅寺は1291年、亀山法皇が離宮を禅寺に改めて開いた臨済宗南禅寺派の大本山で、京都五山・鎌倉五山の上に置かれる「五山之上」の別格寺院です。歌舞伎「楼門五三桐」で石川五右衛門が「絶景かな、絶景かな」と見得を切る巨大な三門は日本三大門の一つ。境内を横切る赤レンガのアーチ「水路閣」は、明治期の琵琶湖疏水事業で田辺朔郎が設計したもので、和洋が調和する独特の景観をつくっています。方丈庭園「虎の子渡し」は国の名勝です。
nanzenji.highlight: 京都五山の上の別格禅刹。石川五右衛門の三門と水路閣で名高い
nanzenji.name_en: Nanzenji Temple (a special Zen temple at the top of Kyoto's five mountains)
nanzenji.highlight_en: A special Zen temple on top of Kyoto's five mountains. Famous for Ishikawa Goemon's Sanmon Gate and Suirokaku
nanzenji.text_en: Nanzenji is the head temple of the Nanzenji sect of the Rinzai sect, which was opened in 1291 by Emperor Kameyama, who converted his villa into a Zen temple.It is a special temple of the ``Gozan no Kami'' located above Kyoto Gozan and Kamakura Gozan. In the Kabuki play ``Romon Gosan Kiri,'' Goemon Ishikawa said, ``It's a spectacular view, isn't it?'' The huge Sanmon Gate is one of Japan's three great gates. Suirokaku, a red brick arch that crosses the temple grounds, was designed by Sakuro Tanabe during the Lake Biwa Canal Project during the Meiji period, creating a unique landscape that blends Japanese and Western elements. The Hojo Garden ``Toranoko Watari'' is a national scenic spot.

ryoanji.name: 龍安寺（石庭・枯山水の傑作）
ryoanji.text: 龍安寺は1450年、室町幕府の管領・細川勝元が創建した臨済宗妙心寺派の寺院で、ユネスコ世界文化遺産です。最大の見どころは方丈前の枯山水庭園「石庭」で、白砂に大小15個の石を配した約75坪の空間は作庭者・作庭年代ともに不明の謎多き名園。どの角度から見ても15個すべては見えない構成や、東洋哲学を体現した抽象美は世界中の人々を魅了し、エリザベス女王も絶賛しました。「吾唯足知（われただたるをしる）」の蹲踞（つくばい）でも知られています。
ryoanji.highlight: 細川勝元創建の世界遺産。15の石を配した謎多き枯山水「石庭」
ryoanji.name_en: Ryoanji Temple (a masterpiece of rock garden and dry landscape)
ryoanji.highlight_en: A world heritage site founded by Katsumoto Hosokawa. A mysterious Karesansui ``Ishiwa'' with 15 stones arranged in it.
ryoanji.text_en: Ryoanji is a temple of the Myoshinji sect of the Rinzai sect, founded in 1450 by Katsumoto Hosokawa, Kanrei of the Muromachi Shogunate, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The biggest highlight is the dry landscape garden in front of the Hojo, called the "Ishi-niwa." The approximately 75-tsubo space, made of white sand and 15 large and small stones, is a famous garden full of mysteries, as both the creator and the year of the garden are unknown. The composition, in which all 15 pieces are invisible no matter what angle you look at, and the abstract beauty that embodies Eastern philosophy fascinated people all over the world, and even Queen Elizabeth praised it highly. It is also known for the tsukubai of ``Wataru wo Shiru.''

rokuharamitsuji.name: 六波羅蜜寺（平清盛・空也上人ゆかり）
rokuharamitsuji.text: 六波羅蜜寺は951年、空也上人が疫病退散を祈って創建した真言宗智山派の寺院です。一帯はかつて平家一門の屋敷「六波羅第」が立ち並んだ平家政権の中枢で、平清盛もこの地を拠点としました。後に鎌倉幕府の出先機関「六波羅探題」も置かれました。宝物館には、念仏を唱える口から6体の阿弥陀仏が現れる姿を表した国宝級の「空也上人立像」、運慶作と伝わる「平清盛坐像」が安置され、平安末期の動乱を今に伝える貴重な仏教彫刻の宝庫です。
rokuharamitsuji.highlight: 空也上人創建・平家政権の中枢。空也上人像と平清盛坐像を所蔵
rokuharamitsuji.name_en: Rokuharamitsuji Temple (related to Taira no Kiyomori and Kuya Shonin)
rokuharamitsuji.highlight_en: The center of the Heike government founded by Kuya Shonin. Contains a statue of Kuya Shonin and a seated statue of Taira no Kiyomori
rokuharamitsuji.text_en: Rokuharamitsu-ji Temple is a temple of the Chizan sect of the Shingon sect, founded in 951 by Kuya Shonin to pray for the exodus of epidemics. The area was once the center of the Heike government, with the Rokuharadai residences of the Heike family, and Taira no Kiyomori also made this area his base. Later, the Kamakura Shogunate's branch office, Rokuhara Tandai, was also established. The Treasure Hall houses the National Treasure-class Kuya Shonin Standing Statue, which depicts six Amida Buddhas emerging from the mouth reciting the Nembutsu, and the Taira no Kiyomori Seated Statue, said to have been created by Unkei.It is a treasure trove of valuable Buddhist sculptures that convey the turmoil of the late Heian period.

shimogamo_jinja.name: 下鴨神社（賀茂御祖神社・葵祭）
shimogamo_jinja.text: 下鴨神社（正式名：賀茂御祖神社）は上賀茂神社とともに賀茂氏の氏神を祀る京都最古級の神社で、ユネスコ世界文化遺産です。創建は紀元前と伝わり、平安京遷都の際には都の守護神として国家的崇敬を受けました。上賀茂神社と合同で行う「葵祭」は祇園祭・時代祭と並ぶ京都三大祭の一つで、平安貴族の装束をまとった行列が御所から両社へ向かう王朝絵巻です。社殿を取り囲む原生林「糺の森（ただすのもり）」は太古の山城国の植生を残す貴重な森として知られています。
shimogamo_jinja.highlight: 京都最古級の世界遺産。京都三大祭「葵祭」と原生林「糺の森」
shimogamo_jinja.highlight_en: Kyoto's oldest world heritage site. Kyoto's three major festivals "Aoi Festival" and the primeval forest "Tadasu no Mori"
shimogamo_jinja.text_en: Shimogamo Shrine (official name: Kamo Miso Shrine), along with Kamigamo Shrine, is one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto that enshrines the guardian deity of the Kamo clan, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is said that it was founded in BC, and when the capital was moved to Heiankyo, it received national veneration as the guardian deity of the capital. The Aoi Festival, which is held jointly with Kamigamo Shrine, is one of the three major festivals in Kyoto, along with the Gion Festival and the Jidai Festival, and is a picture scroll of the dynasty in which a procession wearing the costumes of Heian aristocrats heads from the imperial palace to both shrines. The primeval forest "Tadasu no Mori" that surrounds the shrine is known as a valuable forest that retains the vegetation of ancient Yamashiro Province.

ninnaji.name: 仁和寺（御室御所・宇多天皇開基）
ninnaji.text: 仁和寺は888年、宇多天皇が完成させた真言宗御室派の総本山で、ユネスコ世界文化遺産です。宇多天皇は譲位後に出家してこの寺に入り、以後明治維新まで皇族が住職を務める「門跡寺院」の筆頭「御室御所」として格式を誇りました。御所から移築された国宝・金堂、徒然草にも登場する仁和寺の法師の逸話、遅咲きで樹高の低い名物「御室桜」など見どころが多く、応仁の乱で焼失した伽藍は江戸初期に再建されました。皇室と密接に結びついた雅な寺院文化を今に伝えています。
ninnaji.highlight: 宇多天皇開基の世界遺産。皇族が住職を務めた門跡筆頭「御室御所」
ninnaji.name_en: Ninnaji Temple (Omuro Imperial Palace, founded by Emperor Uda)
ninnaji.highlight_en: A world heritage site founded by Emperor Uda. Omuro Gosho, the first monzeki where members of the imperial family served as chief priests
ninnaji.text_en: Ninna-ji Temple is the head temple of the Omuro school of Shingon Buddhism, completed by Emperor Uda in 888, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. After Emperor Uda abdicated the throne, he became a priest and entered this temple, and from then until the Meiji Restoration, it boasted status as the Omuro Gosho, the first of the Monzeki temples where members of the imperial family served as chief priests. There are many attractions to see, such as the Kondo Hall, a national treasure that was relocated from the imperial palace, the anecdote about the priest of Ninnaji Temple, which appears in Tsurezuregusa, and the famous Omurozakura, which blooms late and has a low height.The temple was burnt down during the Onin War, but was rebuilt in the early Edo period. It still preserves the elegant temple culture that is closely connected to the imperial family.

daitokuji.name: 大徳寺（千利休・一休・信長葬儀の禅刹）
daitokuji.text: 大徳寺は1325年に宗峰妙超が開いた臨済宗大徳寺派の大本山で、一休宗純が再興し、戦国時代には茶の湯文化と深く結びついた禅刹です。千利休は山門「金毛閣」の上層を寄進しましたが、そこに自身の木像を置いたことが豊臣秀吉の怒りを買い、切腹の一因となったと伝わります。1582年、本能寺で斃れた織田信長の葬儀を羽柴秀吉がこの寺で盛大に営み、塔頭の総見院に信長の墓があります。多くの塔頭に名園と茶室が点在し、わび茶の精神を伝える日本文化の聖地です。
daitokuji.highlight: 千利休切腹の発端・信長の葬儀の地。茶の湯文化と禅の聖地
daitokuji.name_en: Daitokuji Temple (Zen temple for the funerals of Sen no Rikyu, Ikkyu, and Nobunaga)
daitokuji.highlight_en: The place where Sen no Rikyu's seppuku began and where Nobunaga's funeral took place. Sacred place of tea ceremony culture and Zen
daitokuji.text_en: Daitokuji is the main temple of the Daitokuji school of the Rinzai sect, which was founded by Soho Myochō in 1325, and revived by Ikkyu Sojun, and is a Zen temple that was deeply connected to the tea ceremony culture during the Sengoku period. Sen no Rikyu donated the upper tier of the temple gate ``Konmokaku,'' but it is said that placing a wooden statue of himself there angered Toyotomi Hideyoshi and was one of the reasons for seppuku. In 1582, Hideyoshi Hashiba held a grand funeral for Nobunaga Oda, who died at Honnoji Temple, at this temple, and Nobunaga's grave is located in the Soken-in sub-temple. It is a sacred place for Japanese culture that conveys the spirit of wabicha, with many sub-temples, famous gardens, and tea rooms scattered throughout.

meiji_jingu.name: 明治神宮
meiji_jingu.text: 明治神宮は明治天皇と昭憲皇太后を祀る神社で、1920年（大正9年）に創建されました。明治天皇は江戸を東京と改め、王政復古から文明開化・富国強兵へと日本を近代国家へ導いた天皇です。境内の70万平方メートルに及ぶ「鎮守の森」は、創建時に全国から献木された約10万本を植えて人工的に造成されたもので、100年を経て自然林のような豊かな森に育ちました。初詣の参拝者数は例年日本一を誇り、原宿・表参道に隣接しながら都心の喧騒を忘れさせる荘厳な空間が広がります。
meiji_jingu.highlight: 明治天皇を祀る社。100年かけ人工造成された都心の鎮守の森
meiji_jingu.highlight_en: A shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji. A sacred forest in the city center that was created over 100 years
meiji_jingu.text_en: Meiji Shrine is a shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken, and was built in 1920 (Taisho 9). Emperor Meiji was the emperor who changed Edo to Tokyo and led Japan to become a modern nation, from the restoration of the monarchy to civilization, enlightenment, and a rich country and strong military. The 700,000 square meter ``Chinju no Mori'' within the temple grounds was artificially created by planting approximately 100,000 trees donated from all over the country at the time of its founding, and over 100 years it has grown into a rich forest that resembles a natural forest. The number of visitors to New Year's shrines is the highest in Japan every year, and although it is adjacent to Harajuku and Omotesando, it is a magnificent space where you can forget the hustle and bustle of the city center.

yasukuni_jinja.name: 靖国神社
yasukuni_jinja.text: 靖国神社は1869年（明治2年）、明治天皇の意向により戊辰戦争の戦没者を祀る「東京招魂社」として創建され、1879年に靖国神社と改称されました。幕末の志士から明治維新、西南戦争、日清・日露戦争、先の大戦に至るまでの戦没者約246万6千柱が祀られています。境内には日本初の西洋式銅像である大村益次郎像（近代陸軍の創設者）が立ち、桜の名所として東京の標本木があることでも知られています。日本の近現代史を考えるうえで避けて通れない場所です。
yasukuni_jinja.highlight: 幕末以降の戦没者246万柱を祀る社。大村益次郎像と桜の標本木
yasukuni_jinja.highlight_en: A shrine that enshrines 2.46 million war dead since the end of the Edo period. Statue of Masujiro Omura and specimen cherry tree
yasukuni_jinja.text_en: Yasukuni Shrine was founded in 1869 (Meiji 2) as ``Tokyo Shokonsha'' to enshrine the war dead of the Boshin War at the request of Emperor Meiji, and was renamed Yasukuni Shrine in 1879. Approximately 2,466,000 soldiers are enshrined here, from the patriots of the end of the Edo period to the Meiji Restoration, the Seinan War, the Sino-Japanese and Russo-Japanese Wars, and the last World War. In the precincts stands the statue of Masujiro Omura (founder of the modern army), Japan's first Western-style bronze statue, and it is also known as a famous spot for cherry blossoms, including Tokyo's specimen trees. It is an unavoidable place when thinking about Japan's modern history.

nihonbashi_gokaido.name: 日本橋（五街道の起点）
nihonbashi_gokaido.text: 日本橋は1603年（慶長8年）、徳川家康の命により江戸の中心に架けられた橋で、東海道・中山道・日光街道・奥州街道・甲州街道の「五街道」すべての起点と定められました。橋のたもとには里程の基点「日本国道路元標」が今も埋め込まれ、全国の道路距離はここを起点に測られています。歌川広重の浮世絵「東海道五十三次」の第一図も日本橋から始まります。現在の石造アーチ橋は1911年（明治44年）築の重要文化財で、頭上を首都高速道路が走る景観は近年地下化が進められています。
nihonbashi_gokaido.highlight: 家康が架けた五街道の起点。全国道路の距離基点「道路元標」
nihonbashi_gokaido.highlight_en: The starting point of the Five Roads built by Ieyasu. National road distance reference point “Road Marker”
nihonbashi_gokaido.text_en: Nihonbashi was a bridge built in the center of Edo in 1603 (8th year of Keicho era) by order of Tokugawa Ieyasu, and was designated as the starting point of all ``Five Highways'': Tokaido, Nakasendo, Nikko Kaido, Oshu Kaido, and Koshu Kaido. At the foot of the bridge, the base point for mileage, the ``Japanese National Highway Signpost,'' is still embedded, and road distances across the country are measured from here. The first illustration of Hiroshige Utagawa's ukiyo-e ``Fifty-three Stations of the Tokaido'' also begins in Nihonbashi. The current stone arch bridge was built in 1911 (Meiji 44) and is an important cultural property, and the scenery with the Metropolitan Expressway running overhead has been moved underground in recent years.

yushima_tenmangu.name: 湯島天満宮（学問の神・菅原道真）
yushima_tenmangu.text: 湯島天満宮（湯島天神）は458年の創建と伝わり、1355年に学問の神・菅原道真を勧請しました。江戸時代には徳川家の崇敬を受け、林羅山ら儒学者や多くの学者が集う江戸の文教の中心として栄えました。明治の文豪・泉鏡花の名作『婦系図』の舞台「湯島の白梅」でも知られ、約300本の梅が咲く梅まつりは早春の風物詩です。現代でも合格祈願の受験生が絶えず、奉納された絵馬が鈴なりに掛けられる「学問の神様」として東京を代表する天神様となっています。
yushima_tenmangu.highlight: 菅原道真を祀る江戸の文教中心。泉鏡花「婦系図」の梅の名所
yushima_tenmangu.name_en: Yushima Tenmangu Shrine (God of learning, Michizane Sugawara)
yushima_tenmangu.highlight_en: A cultural center in Edo that enshrines Michizane Sugawara. Famous plum blossom spots in Kyoka Izumi's ``Female Genealogy''
yushima_tenmangu.text_en: Yushima Tenmangu Shrine (Yushima Tenjin) is said to have been founded in 458, and was dedicated to the god of learning, Michizane Sugawara, in 1355. During the Edo period, it was revered by the Tokugawa family and flourished as the center of Edo's culture, where Confucian scholars such as Hayashi Razan and many other scholars gathered. The area is also known as Yushima's White Plum Blossoms, which is the setting for Meiji period literary giant Kyoka Izumi's masterpiece ``Fujinzu'', and the plum festival, where approximately 300 plum trees bloom, is an early spring tradition. Even in modern times, it has become one of Tokyo's most representative Tenjin shrines, and is known as the ``god of learning,'' where many students pray for their success in exams, and dedicated votive tablets are hung around the bell.

ikegami_honmonji.name: 池上本門寺（日蓮聖人 入滅の地）
ikegami_honmonji.text: 池上本門寺は1282年（弘安5年）、日蓮宗の開祖・日蓮聖人が61歳で入滅（臨終）した霊跡に建つ日蓮宗の大本山です。身延山で病んだ日蓮が湯治に向かう途中、池上宗仲の館で生涯を閉じました。その遺徳を慕い、池上氏が約7万坪の土地を寄進して伽藍が築かれました。加藤清正が寄進した石段「此経難持坂（96段）」、関東最古級の五重塔（重要文化財）、力道山の墓など見どころが多く、毎年10月の「お会式」には30万人が集う日蓮宗最大の法要が営まれます。
ikegami_honmonji.highlight: 日蓮聖人入滅の霊跡。加藤清正寄進の石段と関東最古級の五重塔
ikegami_honmonji.name_en: Ikegami Honmonji Temple (place of Nichiren Saint's death)
ikegami_honmonji.highlight_en: The spiritual remains of Nichiren Saint's death. Stone steps donated by Kato Kiyomasa and the oldest five-storied pagoda in Kanto
ikegami_honmonji.text_en: Ikegami Honmonji is the main temple of the Nichiren sect, built on the site of the sacred site where the founder of the Nichiren sect, Nichiren Shonin, passed away at the age of 61 in 1282 (Koan 5). Nichiren, who fell ill on Mt. Minobu, died at Ikegami Munenaka's mansion on his way to the hot springs. Admiring his virtues, the Ikegami clan donated approximately 70,000 tsubo of land to build the temple. There are many sights to see, such as the stone steps ``Konokenanjizaka'' (96 steps) donated by Kiyomasa Kato, one of the oldest five-storied pagodas in the Kanto region (an important cultural property), and the tomb of Rikidozan.Every October, the largest memorial service of the Nichiren sect is held at ``Oishiki'', which attracts 300,000 people.

gotokuji_temple.name: 豪徳寺（井伊直弼の墓・招き猫発祥）
gotokuji_temple.text: 豪徳寺は彦根藩主・井伊家の江戸における菩提寺で、桜田門外の変で暗殺された大老・井伊直弼の墓があります。井伊直弼は日米修好通商条約の調印と安政の大獄で知られ、その墓は国の史跡に指定されています。また当寺は「招き猫」発祥の地として有名で、二代藩主・井伊直孝が白猫に手招きされて寺に立ち寄り雷雨を避けられた逸話から、招福猫児（まねきねこ）が信仰されるようになりました。境内の招き猫奉納所には大小無数の招き猫が並び、世界中から観光客が訪れる名所となっています。
gotokuji_temple.highlight: 井伊直弼が眠る彦根藩井伊家の菩提寺。招き猫発祥の地
gotokuji_temple.name_en: Gotokuji Temple (the grave of Naosuke Ii and the origin of the beckoning cat)
gotokuji_temple.highlight_en: The family temple of the Ii family of the Hikone domain, where Naosuke Ii is buried. The birthplace of the beckoning cat
gotokuji_temple.text_en: Gotokuji is the family temple of the Ii family, the lords of Hikone, in Edo, and contains the grave of Naosuke Ii, an elder statesman who was assassinated during the Sakuradamon Incident. Naosuke Ii is known for the signing of the Japan-US Treaty of Amity and Commerce and for the great prison of Ansei, and his grave is designated as a national historic site. The temple is also famous as the birthplace of the ``beckoning cat'', and the belief in the ``manekineko'' came from an anecdote in which the second lord of the domain, Naotaka Ii, was beckoned by a white cat and stopped at the temple to avoid a thunderstorm. The beckoning cat offering place on the grounds is lined with countless beckoning cats of all sizes, making it a famous place visited by tourists from all over the world.

fukagawa_basho.name: 深川・芭蕉庵跡（おくのほそ道 出発地）
fukagawa_basho.kana: ふかがわ・ばしょうあんあと

transit.name: 都営大江戸線「清澄白河」

fukagawa_basho.text: 深川の芭蕉庵は、俳聖・松尾芭蕉が1680年から没年近くまで暮らした草庵の跡です。門人から贈られた芭蕉（バナナの一種）を植えたことが「芭蕉」の俳号の由来となりました。1689年、芭蕉はこの庵を引き払い、弟子の曽良を伴って『おくのほそ道』の旅へ旅立ちました。「草の戸も住み替はる代ぞ雛の家」はその発句です。隅田川を望む地に芭蕉稲荷神社・芭蕉記念館・芭蕉庵史跡展望庭園が整備され、川面を眺める芭蕉翁の座像が、漂泊の詩人の面影を今に伝えています。
fukagawa_basho.highlight: 松尾芭蕉が「おくのほそ道」へ旅立った草庵跡。俳号「芭蕉」発祥地
fukagawa_basho.name_en: Fukagawa Bashoan Ruins (Oku no Hosomichi starting point)
fukagawa_basho.highlight_en: The remains of the hermitage where Matsuo Basho departed on his ``Oku no Hosomichi'' journey. Birthplace of the haiku name “Basho”
fukagawa_basho.text_en: Basho-an in Fukagawa is the remains of the hermitage where the haiku master Matsuo Basho lived from 1680 until close to the year of his death. The haiku name ``Basho'' was derived from the fact that he planted a basho (a type of banana) given to him by his disciples. In 1689, Basho left this hermitage and set out on a journey along the ``Oku no Hosomichi'' with his disciple Sora. The phrase ``Kusa no Tomo also moved to Haruyo Hina's House'' is the result of this phrase. The Basho Inari Shrine, Basho Memorial Museum, and Basho-an Historical Observatory Garden have been built on a site overlooking the Sumida River, and the seated statue of Basho Old Man looking out over the river still conveys the image of the wandering poet.

takahata_fudoson.name: 高幡不動尊（土方歳三ゆかりの古刹）

transit.name: 京王線・多摩モノレール「高幡不動」

takahata_fudoson.text: 高幡不動尊金剛寺は平安初期に円仁が開いたと伝わる関東三大不動の一つで、新選組副長・土方歳三の菩提寺としても知られています。土方家の菩提寺であった縁から、境内には土方歳三の銅像と、慶応4年に建てられた殉節両雄之碑（近藤勇・土方歳三を顕彰する石碑、勝海舟の書）があります。日野出身の土方歳三は新選組「鬼の副長」として京で活躍し、最後は箱館・五稜郭で戦死しました。重要文化財の不動堂や室町時代の仁王門が残り、初夏のあじさい祭りでも親しまれる多摩の名刹です。
takahata_fudoson.highlight: 新選組副長・土方歳三の菩提寺。土方像と勝海舟筆の殉節両雄之碑
takahata_fudoson.name_en: Takahata Fudoson (An old temple connected to Toshizo Hijikata)
takahata_fudoson.highlight_en: The family temple of Toshizo Hijikata, deputy leader of the Shinsengumi. Statue of Hijikata and monument to the martyred heroes written by Kaishu Katsu
takahata_fudoson.text_en: Takahata Fudoson Kongoji Temple is said to have been founded by Ennin in the early Heian period, and is one of the three major Fudo temples in the Kanto region, and is also known as the family temple of Toshizo Hijikata, vice-commander of the Shinsengumi. Because it was the family temple of the Hijikata family, there is a bronze statue of Toshizo Hijikata on the grounds, as well as a stone monument honoring Isamu Kondo and Toshizo Hijikata (a stone monument honoring Isamu Kondo and Toshizo Hijikata, with calligraphy by Kaishu Katsu) that was built in 4th year of Keio. Toshizo Hijikata, a native of Hino, was active in Kyoto as the Shinsengumi's ``vice leader of demons'' and was finally killed in battle at Hakodate and Goryokaku. It is a famous temple in Tama, with the Fudo-do Hall, an important cultural property, and the Niomon gate from the Muromachi period remaining, and is popular for its hydrangea festival in early summer.

hino_juku_honjin.name: 日野宿本陣（新選組のふるさと）
hino_juku_honjin.text: 日野宿本陣は甲州街道の宿場・日野宿に現存する都内唯一の本陣建築（江戸時代の大名宿）です。本陣を営んだ佐藤彦五郎は土方歳三の義兄で、自宅に天然理心流の道場を開いていました。ここに近藤勇・土方歳三・沖田総司ら後の新選組の主要メンバーが集い剣の腕を磨いた、まさに「新選組のふるさと」です。日野は土方歳三の生誕地でもあり、近くには土方歳三資料館・新選組のふるさと歴史館があります。幕末の動乱に身を投じた多摩の若者たちの原点となった場所です。
hino_juku_honjin.highlight: 近藤勇・土方歳三・沖田総司が剣を磨いた新選組のふるさと
hino_juku_honjin.highlight_en: The hometown of the Shinsengumi where Isamu Kondo, Toshizo Hijikata, and Souji Okita polished their swords.
hino_juku_honjin.text_en: Hino-shuku Honjin is the only honjin building (a feudal lord inn from the Edo period) that still exists in Hino-shuku, a post station on the Koshu Kaido. Hikogoro Sato, who ran the Honjin, was Toshizo Hijikata's brother-in-law and had opened a dojo for Tennen Rishin-ryu in his home. It is truly the ``hometown of the Shinsengumi'' where Isamu Kondo, Toshizo Hijikata, Souji Okita, and other major members of the Shinsengumi gathered here to hone their sword skills. Hino is also the birthplace of Toshizo Hijikata, and the Toshizo Hijikata Museum and Shinsengumi Furusato History Museum are nearby. This was the starting point for the young people of Tama who threw themselves into the turmoil at the end of the Edo period.

tomioka_hachimangu.name: 富岡八幡宮（深川・伊能忠敬と勧進相撲）
tomioka_hachimangu.kana: とみおかはちまんぐう

transit.name: 地下鉄東西線「門前仲町」

tomioka_hachimangu.text: 富岡八幡宮は1627年の創建で、「深川の八幡様」として江戸庶民に親しまれた江戸最大の八幡宮です。1684年に始まった「江戸勧進相撲」発祥の地であり、境内には歴代横綱を刻んだ横綱力士碑が立ち、大相撲とのゆかりが深い社です。また、測量家・伊能忠敬は深川に居を構え、全国測量の旅に出る前には必ず富岡八幡宮に参拝して安全を祈願したことから、境内に伊能忠敬の銅像が建てられています。例年8月の深川八幡祭りは江戸三大祭の一つで、神輿を担ぐ参加者に水をかける勇壮な祭りとして知られます。
tomioka_hachimangu.highlight: 江戸勧進相撲発祥・横綱力士碑の社。伊能忠敬が測量旅の安全を祈願
tomioka_hachimangu.name_en: Tomioka Hachimangu Shrine (Fukagawa/Ino Tadataka and Kanjin Sumo)
tomioka_hachimangu.highlight_en: The shrine of the Yokozuna sumo wrestler monument, the birthplace of Edo Kanjin sumo. Tadataka Ino prays for safety on his surveying trip
tomioka_hachimangu.text_en: Tomioka Hachimangu Shrine was founded in 1627 and is the largest Hachimangu shrine in Edo, which was familiar to the common people of Edo as ``Hachiman-sama of Fukagawa.'' It is the birthplace of Edo Kanjin Sumo, which began in 1684, and there is a yokozuna sumo monument inscribed with past yokozuna wrestlers in the shrine grounds, and it is a shrine with deep connections to sumo wrestling. In addition, the surveyor Ino Tadataka lived in Fukagawa, and before embarking on a nationwide survey trip, he always visited Tomioka Hachimangu Shrine to pray for safety, so a bronze statue of Ino Tadataka was erected in the precincts. The Fukagawa Hachiman Festival, which usually takes place in August, is one of the three major festivals of Edo, and is known as a heroic festival where participants carrying mikoshi (portable shrines) are sprinkled with water.
